declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_twoFibreProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of
`S` which is representable by algebraic spaces, let `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` be any 1-morphism, and assume
`𝒵` is represented by an algebraic space over `S`. Then the 2-fibre product `𝒵 ×_𝒴 𝒳` is
represented by an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace_twoFibreProduct
    (𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v₁, u + 1, w₁} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v₂, u + 1, w₂} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (g : 𝒵.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒴.val) (f : 𝒳.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒴.val)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f)
    (h𝒵 : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS 𝒵) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpace B S hS (twoFibreProduct B S hS 𝒴 𝒵 𝒳 g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two morphisms representable by algebraic spaces is
representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w}
      (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom)
    (hg : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS g.hom) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (f ≫ g).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_twoFibreProductFst
declarations.doc:
If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of
`S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and `g : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒴` is any 1-morphism, then the base
change `𝒵 ×_{g, 𝒴, f} 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵` is representable by algebraic spaces. No relation is assumed
between the universes of the three categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_twoFibreProductFst
    (𝒴 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v, u + 1, w} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒵 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v₁, u + 1, w₁} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, v₂, u + 1, w₂} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (g : 𝒵.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒴.val) (f : 𝒳.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒴.val)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (twoFibreProductFst B S hS 𝒴 𝒵 𝒳 g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_productMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0303.** The product `f₁ × f₂` of two 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids
over the big fppf site of `S`, each representable by algebraic spaces, is representable by
algebraic spaces.

It factors as `(id_{𝒴₁} × f₂) ∘ (f₁ × id_{𝒳₂})`, each factor is representable by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_productMap_id_left` resp.
`…_id_right`, and the composite is representable by Stacks 0301.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_productMap (f₁ : 𝒳₁ ⟶ 𝒴₁) (f₂ : 𝒳₂ ⟶ 𝒴₂)
    (hf₁ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f₁.hom)
    (hf₂ : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f₂.hom) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (productMap f₁ f₂).hom

declarations.name: mvPowerSeries_fin_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
The formal power series ring in `n` variables over a Noetherian commutative ring is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem mvPowerSeries_fin_isNoetherianRing
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (n : ℕ) :
    IsNoetherianRing (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) R)

declarations.name: Stacks.IntegralClosureLocalization.isLocalization_integralClosure
declarations.doc:
Integral closure commutes with localization: if `Rf` is the localization of `R` at `M` and
`Sf` the localization of `S` at the image of `M`, then `integralClosure Rf Sf` is the localization
of `integralClosure R S` at the image of `M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalization_integralClosure (M : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization M Rf]
    [IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S M) Sf] :
    letI := integralClosureAlgebra R S Rf Sf
    IsLocalization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid ↥(integralClosure R S) M)
      ↥(integralClosure Rf Sf)

declarations.name: integral_closure_transitive
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0308 (transitivity of integral closure): the integral closure of
`B'` in `C` equals the integral closure of `A` in `C`, as subrings of `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem integral_closure_transitive (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C) :
    Cprime f g = Dsub f g

declarations.name: isIntegrallyClosed_tfae_of_finite_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030C.** Let `R` be a reduced ring with finitely many minimal primes. Then the
following are equivalent: (1) `R` is a normal ring, i.e. all its localizations at primes are
normal domains; (2) `R` is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions; (3) `R` is a finite
product of normal domains; (4) the canonical map from `R` to the product of the quotients `R/𝔭`
by its minimal primes is bijective and each such quotient is integrally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegrallyClosed_tfae_of_finite_minimalPrimes {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsReduced R] (hR : (minimalPrimes R).Finite) :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
          IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p),
        IsIntegrallyClosed R,
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (A i)),
          (∀ i, IsDomain (A i)) ∧ (∀ i, IsIntegrallyClosed (A i)) ∧
            Nonempty (R ≃+* ∀ i, A i),
        (∀ p ∈ minimalPrimes R, IsIntegrallyClosed (R ⧸ p)) ∧
          Function.Bijective
            (RingHom.pi fun p : minimalPrimes R => Ideal.Quotient.mk (p : Ideal R)) ]

declarations.name: MvRatFunc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 2).
The field of multivariate rational functions in the variables indexed by `σ` over `R`,
defined as the fraction ring of the multivariate polynomial ring `MvPolynomial σ R`.
declarations.statement: abbrev MvRatFunc (σ R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Type _

declarations.name: PurelyTranscendental
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 3).
A field extension `K/k` is *purely transcendental* if there exists a set `s ⊆ K`
that is algebraically independent over `k` and generates `K` as a field over `k`.
Equivalently, `K` is isomorphic to the field of fractions of a polynomial ring
over `k` on the variables indexed by `s`.
declarations.statement: class PurelyTranscendental (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] : Prop

declarations.name: PurelyTranscendental.exists_algEquiv_mvRatFunc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 3, a part of the correctness).
Any purely transcendental extension `K/k` is `k`-isomorphic to a multivariate
field of rational functions `MvRatFunc s k` for some indexing set `s ⊆ K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_mvRatFunc (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [PurelyTranscendental k K] : ∃ s : Set K, Nonempty (MvRatFunc s k ≃ₐ[k] K)

declarations.name: PurelyTranscendental.mvRatFunc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 3, a part of the correctness).
The multivariate field of rational functions `MvRatFunc σ k` is purely transcendental
over `k`, with the variables `X i` (`i : σ`) forming a transcendence basis.
declarations.statement: instance mvRatFunc (k σ : Type*) [Field k] : PurelyTranscendental k (MvRatFunc σ k)

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.purelyTranscendental
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 3, a part of the correctness).
Pure transcendence transports across `k`-algebra isomorphisms: if `F ≃ₐ[k] E` and
`F/k` is purely transcendental, then so is `E/k`.

declarations.name: AlgEquiv.purelyTranscendental'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030E** (part 3, a part of the correctness).
The reverse-direction transport: if `F ≃ₐ[k] E` and `E/k` is purely transcendental,
then so is `F/k`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.purelyTranscendental_of_ringEquiv
declarations.doc:
Pure transcendence transports along a pair of compatible ring isomorphisms of the base
field and of the extension.
declarations.statement:
lemma purelyTranscendental_of_ringEquiv {k K k' K' : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] [Field k']
    [Field K'] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k' K'] (e : k ≃+* k') (E : K ≃+* K')
    (hc : (algebraMap k' K').comp e = E.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap k K))
    [PurelyTranscendental k K] : PurelyTranscendental k' K'

declarations.name: perfectClosure.isGalois
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030N** (second part of 2).
For a normal field extension `E/F`, the extension `E` over the perfect closure of `F`
in `E` is Galois.
declarations.statement: instance perfectClosure.isGalois [Normal F E] : IsGalois (perfectClosure F E) E

declarations.name: separableClosure_sup_perfectClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030N** (second part of 3).
For a normal field extension `E/F`, the separable closure and the perfect closure of
`F` in `E` together generate the whole extension `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem separableClosure_sup_perfectClosure [Normal F E] :
    separableClosure F E ⊔ perfectClosure F E = ⊤

declarations.name: Algebra.IsSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
A field extension `K/k` is *separable* if every subextension `k ⊆ K' ⊆ K` with `K'` finitely
generated over `k` is separably generated over `k`. For algebraic extensions this is Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsSeparable`.
declarations.statement: public class IsSeparableExtension (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] : Prop

registrations.name: Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable
registrations.comment: a subextension of a separable extension is separable

declarations.name: separablyGenerated_fg_exists_primitive_transcendence_basis
declarations.doc:
Stacks 030Q (Lemma 10.42.3). If `K/k` is separably generated and finitely
generated, with transcendence degree `r`, then there are `x_1, ..., x_{r+1} ∈ K`
(here packaged as `x : Fin (r+1) → K`) such that:

1. `x_1, ..., x_r` (the entries `x i.castSucc`) form a transcendence basis of
   `K` over `k`;
2. `K = k(x_1, ..., x_{r+1})` (the adjoin of the whole tuple is `⊤`); and
3. `x_{r+1}` (the entry `x (Fin.last r)`) is separable over the subfield
   `k(x_1, ..., x_r)` generated by the first `r` entries.
declarations.statement:
theorem separablyGenerated_fg_exists_primitive_transcendence_basis
    (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (hsep : SeparablyGenerated k K)
    (hfg : (⊤ : IntermediateField k K).FG)
    (r : ℕ) (hr : Algebra.trdeg k K = r) :
    ∃ x : Fin (r + 1) → K,
      IsTranscendenceBasis k (fun i : Fin r => x i.castSucc) ∧
      IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range x) = ⊤ ∧
      IsSeparable
        (↥(IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun i : Fin r => x i.castSucc))))
        (x (Fin.last r))

declarations.name: exists_isPurelyInseparable_and_isSeparableExtension_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a finitely generated field extension and let `Ω/K` be a perfect field extension.
Then inside `Ω` there is a diagram
```
K  →  K'
↑     ↑
k  →  k'
```
with `k'/k` and `K'/K` finite purely inseparable and `K'/k'` separable in the sense of
[stacks, 030O](2), in which moreover `K'` is the compositum `k'K` and the canonical map
`k' ⊗[k] K → K'` is surjective with kernel the nilradical, i.e. `K' = (k' ⊗[k] K)_red`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_and_isSeparableExtension_of_essFiniteType
    (k K Ω : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Field Ω] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k Ω] [Algebra K Ω]
    [IsScalarTower k K Ω] [PerfectField Ω] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] :
    ∃ (K' : IntermediateField K Ω) (k' : IntermediateField k ↥K'),
      Module.Finite K ↥K' ∧ IsPurelyInseparable K ↥K' ∧
      Module.Finite k ↥k' ∧ IsPurelyInseparable k ↥k' ∧
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension ↥k' ↥K' ∧
      IntermediateField.adjoin K (k' : Set ↥K') = ⊤ ∧
      Function.Surjective (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k ↥k' ↥K') (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K ↥K')) ∧
      RingHom.ker (Algebra.TensorProduct.productMap
        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k ↥k' ↥K') (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K ↥K')) =
        nilradical (↥k' ⊗[k] K)

declarations.name: DirectLimit.instIsGeometricallyReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030T (3).** A directed colimit of geometrically reduced `R`-algebras is geometrically
reduced over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public instance instIsGeometricallyReduced
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type*} [∀ i, Ring (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (G i)]
    {T : ∀ ⦃i j : ι⦄, i ≤ j → Type*} {f : ∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), T h}
    [∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), FunLike (T h) (G i) (G j)]
    [∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), AlgHomClass (T h) R (G i) (G j)]
    [DirectedSystem G (f · · ·)]
    [∀ i, Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced R (G i)] :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced R (DirectLimit G f)
declarations.comment:
Part (3): a directed colimit of geometrically reduced algebras is geometrically
  reduced, stated for `DirectLimit` of a directed system of algebras over a commutative base ring.
  Parts (1) and (2) are `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.of_injective` and
  `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.of_forall_fg`; part (4) is Lemma 04KN.

declarations.name: Algebra.isReduced_tensorProduct_of_isSeparableExtension_or_isSeparablyGenerated
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a reduced `k`-algebra and let `K/k` be a field extension which
is either separable or separably generated. Then `K ⊗[k] S` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isReduced_tensorProduct_of_isSeparableExtension_or_isSeparablyGenerated
    {k K S : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [IsReduced S]
    (hK : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K ∨ Algebra.IsSeparablyGenerated k K) :
    IsReduced (K ⊗[k] S)
declarations.comment:
Stated with the two notions of Definition 030O as a disjunctive hypothesis, as in
  the source: separably generated implies separable is Lemma 030X, whose proof uses this lemma.

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyReduced_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReduced_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (kperf : Type w) [Field kperf] [Algebra k kperf] [ExpChar kperf p] [PerfectRing kperf p]
    [IsPerfectClosure (algebraMap k kperf) p]
    (K : Type w') [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsAlgClosure k K] :
    [∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
        [IsPurelyInseparable k k'], IsReduced (k' ⊗[k] S),
      IsReduced (AdjoinPthRoots k ⊗[k] S),
      IsReduced (kperf ⊗[k] S),
      IsReduced (K ⊗[k] S),
      ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L], IsReduced (L ⊗[k] S),
      IsGeometricallyReduced k S].TFAE
declarations.comment:
The source's five conditions in its order, with its definition of geometric
  reducedness spelled out as item (5), plus item (6), Mathlib's `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced`;
  `k^{1/p}` is `AdjoinPthRoots k`, and the perfect and algebraic closures are taken abstractly, as
  `IsPerfectClosure` and `IsAlgClosure`.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSeparableExtension_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 030W.** Let `k` be a field of exponential characteristic `p` and let `K/k` be a field
extension. The following are equivalent: `K` is separable over `k` (Definition
[Stacks 030O](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/030O)); for every `k`-linearly independent
subset `s` of `K` the set of `p`-th powers of elements of `s` is `k`-linearly independent; the ring
`K ⊗_k k^{1/p}` is reduced; and `K` is geometrically reduced over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSeparableExtension_tfae (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] :
    List.TFAE
      [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K,
        ∀ s : Set K, LinearIndepOn k _root_.id s → LinearIndepOn k (· ^ p) s,
        IsReduced (K ⊗[k] AdjoinPthRoots k),
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k K]
declarations.comment:
Stated for the exponential characteristic, so that characteristic zero is the case
  `p = 1`, where all four conditions hold; the source assumes `p > 0`. Condition (2) quantifies over
  arbitrary, not just finite, linearly independent subsets. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_isSeparable_adjoin_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A separably generated field extension is separable. Let `K/k` be a field extension with a
separating transcendence basis `s`, that is, a transcendence basis of `K/k` such that `K` is
separable algebraic over `k(s)`. Then every subextension `k ⊆ L ⊆ K` which is finitely generated
over `k` again has a separating transcendence basis: there is a finite transcendence basis `t` of
`L/k` such that `L` is separable algebraic over `k(t)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isTranscendenceBasis_and_isSeparable_of_isSeparable_adjoin_of_essFiniteType
    {k K L : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L K]
    [IsScalarTower k L K] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k L] {s : Set K}
    (hs : IsTranscendenceBasis k ((↑) : s → K))
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparable (IntermediateField.adjoin k s) K) :
    ∃ t : Finset L,
      IsTranscendenceBasis k ((↑) : t → L) ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparable (IntermediateField.adjoin k (t : Set L)) L

declarations.name: zero_at_ass_zero
declarations.doc:
Over a Noetherian ring, the canonical map from $M$ into the product of its localizations at
associated primes is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem zero_at_ass_zero (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Function.Injective (assMap R M)

declarations.name: associatedPrimes.tensorProduct_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `R`-module and let `N` be an `S`-module which is flat
as an `R`-module. Then `Ass_S(N ⊗_R M) ⊇ ⋃_{𝔭 ∈ Ass_R(M)} Ass_S(N / 𝔭N)`, and if `R` is
Noetherian this inclusion is an equality. Here `Ass` is the set of primes that *are* the
annihilator of an element, written out as such, and the index set of the equality is
`associatedPrimes R M`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem associatedPrimes.tensorProduct_of_flat {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module R N]
    [IsScalarTower R S N] [Module.Flat R N] :
    (⋃ p ∈ {p : Ideal R | p.IsPrime ∧ ∃ m : M, (⊥ : Submodule R M).colon {m} = p},
        {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧
          ∃ w : N ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)),
            (⊥ : Submodule S (N ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)))).colon {w} =
              q}) ⊆
      {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧ ∃ w : N ⊗[R] M, (⊥ : Submodule S (N ⊗[R] M)).colon {w} = q} ∧
    (IsNoetherianRing R →
      {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧ ∃ w : N ⊗[R] M, (⊥ : Submodule S (N ⊗[R] M)).colon {w} = q} =
        ⋃ p ∈ associatedPrimes R M,
          {q : Ideal S | q.IsPrime ∧
            ∃ w : N ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)),
              (⊥ : Submodule S (N ⧸ (p.map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)))).colon {w} =
                q})

declarations.name: Ideal.symbolicPower
declarations.doc:
The `n`th *symbolic power* `p ^ (n)` of a prime ideal `p` of a commutative semiring `R`: the
kernel of `R → R_p / p ^ n R_p`, realized as the contraction to `R` of the ideal `p ^ n R_p` of the
localization `R_p`.
declarations.statement:
public def symbolicPower {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (n : ℕ) :
    Ideal R

declarations.name: ass_quotient_symbolicPower'
declarations.doc:
For a Noetherian ring `R`, a prime ideal `p`, and `n > 0`, the set of associated primes of
`R / p^{(n)}` is exactly `{p}`.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.map_shortExact_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0315 (3).** If `0 → K → P → M → 0` is a short exact sequence of
`R`-modules and `M` is flat over `R`, then its `I`-adic completion is again short exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_shortExact_of_flat {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) {K : Type v} {P : Type w} {M : Type t} [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K]
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Flat R M]
    {f : K →ₗ[R] P} {g : P →ₗ[R] M} (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g) :
    Function.Injective (map I f) ∧ Function.Exact (map I f) (map I g) ∧
      Function.Surjective (map I g)

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0316.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `I` be an ideal of `R`. The completion
`R^∧ = lim_n R/Iⁿ` of `R` with respect to `I` is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
public instance AdicCompletion.isNoetherianRing {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) : IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion I R)
declarations.comment:
Stated as an instance for `IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion I R)`, Mathlib's
spelling of the completion `R^∧ = lim_n R/Iⁿ`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete_iff_pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0318.** Let `R` be a ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `M` be an `R`-module.
Write `Kₙ = Ker(M^∧ → M/IⁿM)` for the kernel of the `n`-th projection out of the `I`-adic
completion `M^∧` of `M`. Then `M^∧` is `I`-adically complete if and only if `Kₙ = IⁿM^∧` for all
`n ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdicComplete_iff_pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsAdicComplete I (AdicCompletion I M) ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
        I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R (AdicCompletion I M)) = (eval I M n).ker
declarations.comment: The criterion of Lenstra and de Smit; no hypothesis on `I` or `R`.

declarations.name: agreement_of_completions
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses `I^c ⊆ J` and
`J^d ⊆ I` (with `c, d > 0`), for every `R`-module `M` there is a canonical
`R`-linear isomorphism between the `I`-adic and `J`-adic completions of `M`,
compatible with the canonical maps from `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem agreement_of_completions
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I J : Ideal R)
    {c d : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hIJ : I ^ c ≤ J) (hJI : J ^ d ≤ I)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    ∃ e : AdicCompletion I M ≃ₗ[R] AdicCompletion J M,
      e.toLinearMap.comp (AdicCompletion.of I M) = AdicCompletion.of J M

declarations.name: completeness_preserved
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses `I^c ⊆ J` and `J^d ⊆ I` (with `c, d > 0`), an
`R`-module `M` is `I`-adically complete if and only if it is `J`-adically
complete.
declarations.statement:
theorem completeness_preserved
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I J : Ideal R)
    {c d : ℕ} (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hIJ : I ^ c ≤ J) (hJI : J ^ d ≤ I)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsAdicComplete I M ↔ IsAdicComplete J M

declarations.name: main_theorem_031a
declarations.doc:
For an $I$-adically complete module $M$ and a submodule $K$, the equality
$K = \bigcap_n (K + I^n M)$ holds if and only if the quotient $M/K$ is
$I$-adically complete.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_031a {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [IsAdicComplete I M] (K : Submodule R M) :
    (K = ⨅ n : ℕ, (K ⊔ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R M))) ↔ IsAdicComplete I (M ⧸ K)

declarations.name: isAdicComplete_of_iInf_smul_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
A finite module `M` over an `I`-adically complete ring `R` is itself `I`-adically
complete as soon as `⋂ₙ IⁿM = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicComplete_of_iInf_smul_eq_bot
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [IsAdicComplete I R] [Module.Finite R M]
    (h : ⨅ n : ℕ, (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) = ⊥) :
    IsAdicComplete I M

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.instIsAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 031C**, adic completeness. Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `I` an ideal of `R` and `M`
an `R`-module. Then the `I`-adic completion `M^∧` of `M` is `I`-adically complete. This is the
Noetherian form of `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`, stated as an instance: over a Noetherian ring
the finite generation of `I` that the proof needs is automatic, so no side condition has to be
supplied.
declarations.comment:
Adic completeness, as an instance over a Noetherian ring; the general form is
`AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete`. The other two assertions specialise from Lemma 05GG along
`IsNoetherian.noetherian I : I.FG`: `IⁿM^∧ = (IⁿM)^∧` is
`AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval` composed with
`AdicCompletion.restrictScalars_range_ofPowSMul_eq_ker_eval`, and `M^∧/IⁿM^∧ = M/IⁿM` is
`AdicCompletion.quotPowSMulTopEquiv`.

declarations.name: Module.Finite.of_iInf_pow_smul_top_eq_bot_of_finite_quotient_smul_top
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring, let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal and let `M` be an `R`-module. Assume that `R` is
`I`-adically precomplete, that `⋂_{n ≥ 1} IⁿM = 0`, and that `M/IM` is a finite `R/I`-module.
Then `M` is a finite `R`-module. Here `IⁿM` is `I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M)`, so the second
hypothesis is `⨅ n, I ^ n • ⊤ = ⊥`, and `M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` with its canonical `R ⧸ I`-module
structure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Finite.of_iInf_pow_smul_top_eq_bot_of_finite_quotient_smul_top
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [IsPrecomplete I R] (hsep : ⨅ n : ℕ, I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule R M) = ⊥)
    (hfin : Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))) :
    Module.Finite R M

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_of_flat_of_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a local homomorphism of local
Noetherian rings such that:
1. `R` is regular,
2. the closed fibre `S / m_R S` is regular, and
3. `φ : R → S` is flat.
Then `S` is regular.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_flat_of_closedFibre (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    (hR : IsRegularLocalRing R)
    (hfibre : IsRegularLocalRing (ClosedFibre R S))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R S) :
    IsRegularLocalRing S

declarations.name: Ideal.isMaximal_and_finite_primesOver_and_module_finite_quotient
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian domain of Krull dimension at most one with fraction field `K`, let
`L/K` be a finite field extension, and let `S` be a domain with fraction field `L` which is an
`R`-algebra compatibly with `K ⊆ L`. Then, for every maximal ideal `m` of `R`, every prime `n` of
`S` lying over `m` is maximal, only finitely many primes of `S` lie over `m`, each residue field
extension `κ(n)/κ(m)` is finite, and moreover `S/mS` is a finite-dimensional `κ(m)`-vector
space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMaximal_and_finite_primesOver_and_module_finite_quotient
    (R S K L : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Ring.KrullDimLE 1 R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S]
    [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Field L] [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing S L]
    [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsScalarTower R S L] (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal] :
    (∀ (n : Ideal S) [n.IsPrime] [n.LiesOver m], n.IsMaximal) ∧
      (m.primesOver S).Finite ∧
      (∀ (n : Ideal S) [n.IsPrime] [n.LiesOver m], Module.Finite (R ⧸ m) (S ⧸ n)) ∧
      Module.Finite (R ⧸ m) (S ⧸ m.map (algebraMap R S))
declarations.comment:
The three assertions of the tag, for an arbitrary maximal ideal `m` of a Noetherian
domain with `Ring.KrullDimLE 1` rather than for the maximal ideal of a local ring of dimension
one, together with the finite-dimensionality of `S/mS` over `κ(m)` from which the author's proof
deduces them. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.KaehlerDifferential.Colimit.main_theorem_031g
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 031G.** For a system of ring maps over a directed set `I`, the
canonical comparison map `Θ : colim_i Ω[S_i⁄R_i] → Ω[S⁄R]` is bijective (an
isomorphism of abelian groups, equivalently of `S`-modules).
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_031g (hsq : IsCompatible fR fS)
    (hdirS : DirectedSystem S (fun _ _ h => (fS h : S _ → S _))) :
    Function.Bijective (Theta fR fS hsq)

registrations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp
registrations.comment: formal smoothness is stable under composition

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.tfae_of_surjective
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.FormallySmooth.tfae_of_surjective
    {R : Type*} {S : Type*} {P : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing P]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R P] [Algebra P S] [IsScalarTower R P S]
    [Algebra.FormallySmooth R P] (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P S)) :
    List.TFAE
      [ Algebra.FormallySmooth R S,
        ∃ g, (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R P S).kerSquareLift.comp g = AlgHom.id R S,
        Function.Injective (kerCotangentToTensor R P S) ∧
          ∃ σ : Ω[S⁄R] →ₗ[S] S ⊗[P] Ω[P⁄R], mapBaseChange R P S ∘ₗ σ = LinearMap.id,
        Module.Projective S Ω[S⁄R] ∧ Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R S) ]
declarations.comment:
Stated for a variable formally smooth presentation, giving the source's `for some
P` and `for all P` forms at once; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.exists_retraction_mapBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**The sequence of differentials of a tower is split short exact.** Let `R → A → B` be ring
maps with `A → B` formally smooth. Then the canonical injection `B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R}` admits
a `B`-linear retraction, so that `0 → B ⊗_A Ω_{A/R} → Ω_{B/R} → Ω_{B/A} → 0` is a split short
exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem KaehlerDifferential.exists_retraction_mapBaseChange (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Algebra R B]
    [IsScalarTower R A B] [Algebra.FormallySmooth A B] :
    ∃ r : Ω[B⁄R] →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] Ω[A⁄R],
      r ∘ₗ KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange R A B = LinearMap.id
declarations.comment:
Split short exactness, i.e. the two assertions of the tag that are not already in
Mathlib (exactness at `Ω_{C/A}` is `KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map` and surjectivity
is `KaehlerDifferential.map_surjective`), stated as the existence of a retraction of the
injection: that is at once its injectivity and the splitting. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallyEtale.colimit
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `ι` be a directed set, a nonempty preorder in which
every pair has an upper bound. Let `F : ι ⥤ CommAlgCat R` be a directed system of `R`-algebras
over `ι`, the family `S_i = F.obj i` with the transition maps encoded by functoriality. If every
`S_i` is formally étale over `R`, then the colimit `S = colim_i S_i` is formally étale over
`R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FormallyEtale.colimit
    (R : Type) [CommRing R]
    (ι : Type) [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : ι ⥤ CommAlgCat.{0} R)
    (h : ∀ i : ι, Algebra.FormallyEtale R (F.obj i)) :
    Algebra.FormallyEtale R (colimit F : CommAlgCat R)

declarations.name: HasPropertyRk
declarations.doc:
Property `(Rₖ)`: every prime `𝔭` of `A` of height at most `k` has regular localization `A_𝔭`.
As `height 𝔭 = dim A_𝔭`, this is regularity of `A` in codimension at most `k`.
declarations.statement: def HasPropertyRk (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: PropertySkRing
declarations.doc:
Property `(Sₖ)` for a Noetherian commutative ring `R`: at every prime `𝔭` the depth of the
localization `R_𝔭` is at least `min(k, dim R_𝔭)`.
declarations.statement: def PropertySkRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: PropertySkModule
declarations.doc:
Property `(Sₖ)` for a finite module `M` over a Noetherian commutative ring `R`: at every prime
`𝔭` the depth of the localization `M_𝔭` is at least `min(k, dim Supp(M_𝔭))`.
declarations.statement:
def PropertySkModule (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: propertySkRing_of_ringEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Serre's condition `(Sₖ)` is invariant under an isomorphism of rings.** A prime of the
target pulls back along the isomorphism, `Localization.localRingEquiv` identifies the two
localizations, and both the Krull dimension and the depth are invariant under that
isomorphism.

declarations.name: Module.forall_minimal_mem_associatedPrimes_iff_min_one_supportDim_le_depth
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module. Then
`M` has no embedded associated prime — that is, every associated prime of `M` is minimal among
the associated primes of `M` — if and only if `M` has property `(S₁)`: for every prime `𝔭` of
`R` the depth of the `R_𝔭`-module `M_𝔭` along `𝔭R_𝔭` is at least `min{1, dim Supp(M_𝔭)}`, the
inequality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`. Concretely the right-hand side says that
`depth(M_𝔭) ≥ 1` at every prime `𝔭` with `dim Supp(M_𝔭) ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem forall_minimal_mem_associatedPrimes_iff_min_one_supportDim_le_depth
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    (∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R M, Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R M) p) ↔
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
        min 1 (supportDim (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M)) ≤
          (depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
            (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M) : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: Property `(S₁)` is spelled out as the inequality `min{1, dim Supp(M_𝔭)} ≤ depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(M_𝔭)` of Definition 031P at `k = 1` rather than as `PropertySkModule R M 1`, whose depth and dimension truncate the conventions this statement needs; having no embedded associated prime is spelled out with `Minimal`, as in tag 02M6; and the localizations are the canonical models `Localization.AtPrime` and `LocalizedModule`, indexed by `PrimeSpectrum R` as in Definition 0AAH. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isReduced_iff_hasR0_and_hasS1
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 031R (Lemma 10.157.3, Serre's criterion). A Noetherian ring `R`
is reduced if and only if it has both property `(R_0)` and property `(S_1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduced_iff_hasR0_and_hasS1 (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsReduced R ↔ HasR0 R ∧ HasS1 R

declarations.name: isDomain_and_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime_iff_isRegularLocalRing_and_min_two_le_depth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 031S (Serre's criterion for normality).** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring. Then `R`
is a normal ring — every localization `R_𝔭` at a prime is a domain integrally closed in its
fraction field — if and only if `R` has properties `(R_1)` and `(S_2)`: the local ring `R_𝔭` is
regular for every prime `𝔭` of height `≤ 1`, and `depth(R_𝔭) ≥ min{2, dim(R_𝔭)}` for every
prime `𝔭`, the latter inequality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDomain_and_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime_iff_isRegularLocalRing_and_min_two_le_depth
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    (∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) ↔
      (∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], p.height ≤ 1 →
          IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧
        ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
          min 2 (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p)) ≤
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
              (Localization.AtPrime p) : WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: Normality is inlined as `IsDomain` plus `IsIntegrallyClosed` on `Localization.AtPrime 𝔭` for every prime `𝔭`, as in item (1) of tag 030C, Mathlib having no predicate for a normal ring; properties `(R_1)` and `(S_2)` are spelled out from Definition 031P at `k = 1` and `k = 2` with `Ideal.height`, `IsRegularLocalRing`, `ringKrullDim` and `Module.depth` (tag 00LI), the depth inequality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: associatedPrimes_minimal_and_height_eq_one_and_iInf_localization_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field `K`. Then
(1) for every nonzero `a : R` each associated prime of `R/aR` is minimal among the associated
primes of `R/aR` — that is, `R/aR` has no embedded primes — and has height `1`;
(2) `R` is the intersection, inside `K`, of the subalgebras `R_𝔭` over the primes `𝔭` of height
`1`; and (3) the same as (1) for the ideal `R ∩ xR` attached to a nonzero `x : K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem associatedPrimes_minimal_and_height_eq_one_and_iInf_localization_eq_bot
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] :
    (∀ a : R, a ≠ 0 → ∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a}),
        Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {a})) p ∧ p.height = 1) ∧
      ((⨅ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ⨅ _ : p.asIdeal.height = 1,
          Localization.subalgebra.ofField K _ p.asIdeal.primeCompl_le_nonZeroDivisors) = ⊥) ∧
      (∀ x : K, x ≠ 0 →
        ∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R
            (R ⧸ ((Submodule.span R {x}).comap (Algebra.linearMap R K) : Ideal R)),
          Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R
              (R ⧸ ((Submodule.span R {x}).comap (Algebra.linearMap R K) : Ideal R))) p ∧
            p.height = 1)
declarations.comment: A normal domain is `IsDomain` plus `IsIntegrallyClosed`, as in Definition 0309; having no embedded primes is spelled with `Minimal`, as in tags 02M6 and 031Q; item (2) is the equality `⨅ 𝔭, R_𝔭 = ⊥` of `R`-subalgebras of `K`, as in `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.iInf_localization_eq_bot`; and `R ∩ xR` is the pullback of `xR ⊆ K` along `Algebra.linearMap R K`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Polynomial.Separable.exists_pow_eq_of_coeff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 031V** (part 2 — the general statement).
Let `K` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, `L/K` a field extension, and `x ∈ L`.
If `f ∈ K[X]` satisfies
  (a) `x` is a root of `f`,
  (b) `f` is a separable polynomial, and
  (c) every coefficient of `f` is a `p`-th power in `K`,
then `x` is a `p`-th power in `L`.

declarations.name: exists_pow_eq_of_minpoly_coeff_of_separable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 031V** (part 1).
Let `K` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, `L/K` a separable extension, and `x ∈ L`.
If every coefficient of the minimal polynomial of `x` over `K` is a `p`-th power in `K`,
then `x` is a `p`-th power in `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_eq_of_minpoly_coeff_of_separable {p : ℕ}
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharP K p] {L : Type*} [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    {x : L} (h₁ : ∀ i, ∃ b : K, b ^ p = (minpoly K x).coeff i) :
    ∃ y, y ^ p = x

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.D_eq_zero_iff_exists_pow_eq
declarations.doc:
**Vanishing differentials over a perfect field are `p`-th powers.** Let `k` be a perfect
field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `K/k` be a field extension and let `a : K`. Then `d a = 0` in
`Ω[K⁄k]` if and only if `a` is a `p`-th power in `K`. Equivalently, the kernel of the universal
`k`-derivation `d : K → Ω[K⁄k]` is the subfield of `p`-th powers of `K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem KaehlerDifferential.D_eq_zero_iff_exists_pow_eq {k K : Type*} [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] [PerfectField k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (a : K) :
    KaehlerDifferential.D k K a = 0 ↔ ∃ b : K, b ^ p = a
declarations.comment:
The source's `d a = 0 in Ω_{K/k}` is `KaehlerDifferential.D k K a = 0` and `a` is a
`p`-th power is `∃ b, b ^ p = a`; characteristic `p > 0` is `[Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]` on the
base. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSeparableExtension_iff_injective_mapBaseChange
declarations.doc:
A field extension `K/k` is separable in the sense of `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension` if and only
if the canonical map `K ⊗_k Ω_{k/𝐙} → Ω_{K/𝐙}` is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSeparableExtension_iff_injective_mapBaseChange (k K : Type*) [Field k]
    [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K ↔
      Function.Injective (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange ℤ k K)
declarations.comment:
Differentials are taken over `𝐙`, which for a field of characteristic `p` is the
source's `𝐅_p`, and the characteristic hypothesis is dropped: both conditions hold outright in
characteristic zero, and the consumers (Lemmas 031Y, 0321 and Proposition 0322) are stated for all
characteristics. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be an extension of fields. If `K` is formally smooth over `k`, then `K` is a
separable extension of `k`: every subextension of `K/k` finitely generated over `k` has a
separating transcendence basis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.FormallySmooth.isSeparableExtension (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra.FormallySmooth k K] : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K
declarations.comment:
Separability is `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension` (Definition 030O(2)), not Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsSeparable`, which asks the extension to be algebraic and would make the statement false
for purely transcendental extensions. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.formallySmooth_iff_subsingleton_h1Cotangent
declarations.doc:
A field `K` which is an algebra over a commutative ring `R` is formally smooth over `R` if and
only if `H¹(L_{K/R}) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.formallySmooth_iff_subsingleton_h1Cotangent
    (R K : Type*) [CommRing R] [Field K] [Algebra R K] :
    Algebra.FormallySmooth R K ↔ Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R K)
declarations.comment:
Stated for a field `K` over an arbitrary commutative base ring `R`; the source's
base field `k` is the case `R := k`, and no hypothesis on the base is used. `H_1(L_{K/k}) = 0` is
`Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R K)`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_algebraicIndependent_and_of_isSeparable_and_of_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be an extension of fields. Then `K` is formally smooth over `k` in each of the
following three cases: (1) `K` is purely transcendental over `k`, that is, `K` is generated as an
intermediate field by an algebraically independent set; (2) `K` is separable algebraic over `k`;
(3) `K` is separable over `k` in the sense of `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_algebraicIndependent_and_of_isSeparable_and_of_isSeparableExtension
    (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    (∀ s : Set K, AlgebraicIndependent k ((↑) : s → K) → IntermediateField.adjoin k s = ⊤ →
        Algebra.FormallySmooth k K) ∧
      (Algebra.IsSeparable k K → Algebra.FormallySmooth k K) ∧
      (Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K → Algebra.FormallySmooth k K)
declarations.comment:
The source's parts (1), (2), (3) are the conjuncts `.1`, `.2.1`, `.2.2`. Purely
transcendental is `AlgebraicIndependent` together with `IntermediateField.adjoin k s = ⊤`, as in
the Mathlib sibling `Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_algebraicIndependent`; separable algebraic is
`Algebra.IsSeparable`; separable is `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`, Definition 030O(2), which does
not presuppose algebraicity. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
A field extension `K/k` is formally smooth over `k` if and only if it is separable over `k` in
the sense of `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.FormallySmooth.iff_isSeparableExtension (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] : Algebra.FormallySmooth k K ↔ Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K
declarations.comment:
Separability is `Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`, Definition 030O (2), which does not
presuppose algebraicity and so is not `Algebra.IsSeparable`; formal smoothness is
`Algebra.FormallySmooth`, Definition 00TI. The characteristic split is dropped: both implications
hold in every characteristic (the source's proof is `combine Lemmas 031Y and 0320`, neither of
which mentions the characteristic), so part (2) is this equivalence and part (1) is it together
with the characteristic-zero case of Lemma 030Z. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSeparableExtension_of_charZero_and_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a field extension. If the characteristic of `k` is zero then `K` is separable over
`k`; and, in any characteristic, the following are equivalent: `K` is separable over `k`, the ring
`K ⊗_k k^{1/p}` is reduced for the exponential characteristic `p` of `k`, `K` is geometrically
reduced over `k`, the map `K ⊗_k Ω_{k/𝐙} → Ω_{K/𝐙}` is injective, `H_1(L_{K/k}) = 0`, and `K` is
formally smooth over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSeparableExtension_of_charZero_and_tfae (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] :
    (CharZero k → Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K) ∧
      List.TFAE
        [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K,
          IsReduced (K ⊗[k] AdjoinPthRoots k),
          Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k K,
          Function.Injective (KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange ℤ k K),
          Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K),
          Algebra.FormallySmooth k K]
declarations.comment:
The equivalences are stated uniformly in the characteristic: `k^{1/p}` is
`AdjoinPthRoots k` for the exponential characteristic, which in characteristic zero makes the second
condition, hence all of them, automatic, and the source's characteristic-zero list is recovered.
Differentials are taken over `𝐙` in both characteristics. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.isAdicComplete_maximalIdeal_iff_forall_compatible_existsUnique_mk_eq
declarations.doc:
**A local ring is complete exactly when it is the inverse limit of its adic truncations.**

Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local ring. Then `R` is `𝔪`-adically complete if and only if for every
family `f` of residues `f n : R ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ` that is compatible with the truncation maps
`R ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ → R ⧸ 𝔪ᵏ` for `k ≤ n`, there is a *unique* `r : R` whose residue modulo `𝔪ⁿ` is
`f n` for every `n`.

This is the Stacks project's definition of a complete local ring: a compatible family is an
element of `lim_n R / 𝔪ⁿ`, existence of `r` says the canonical map `R → lim_n R / 𝔪ⁿ` is
surjective, and uniqueness says it is injective, so the two together say that this ring map is
an isomorphism. Uniqueness for the zero family is the separatedness `⋂ₙ 𝔪ⁿ = (0)` that the
source's footnote insists on; it corresponds to the `IsHausdorff` half of `IsAdicComplete`,
while existence corresponds to the `IsPrecomplete` half.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.isAdicComplete_maximalIdeal_iff_forall_compatible_existsUnique_mk_eq
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R ↔
      ∀ f : (n : ℕ) → R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n,
        (∀ (k n : ℕ) (h : k ≤ n),
            Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right h) (f n) = f k) →
          ∃! r : R, ∀ n : ℕ, Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal R ^ n) r = f n
declarations.comment: 0323 is the label of the heading `\section{The Cohen structure theorem}`, not of a mathematical statement: it has no hypotheses and no conclusion, so NO single theorem can be a faithful formalization of it, and this attribute is placed under the project's rule that a tag which is not a statement as written is carried in corrected form with the correction recorded. The correction: 0323 is carried here, on the section's OPENING NOTION — the section begins `Here is a fundamental notion in commutative algebra` and then states Definition 0324, the definition of a complete local ring, which is what this declaration characterizes — and the section's remaining eleven labelled items are carried at their own tags elsewhere in this library, not here. Namely: 032A, the Cohen structure theorem itself, on `IsLocalRing.exists_isCoefficientRing_and_exists_surjective_mvPowerSeries` in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.CompleteLocalRing.CohenStructureTheorem`; 032D on `IsLocalRing.exists_injective_finite_mvPowerSeries` in the same module; 0C0S, the power series description of a regular complete local ring, on `IsRegularLocalRing.nonempty_ringEquiv_and_algEquiv_mvPowerSeries` in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.CompleteLocalRing.Regular`; 0325 on `quotient_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing` and `finite_isProduct_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing`, and 032B on `complete_local_ring_noetherian`, all in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.CompleteLocalRing.Noetherian`; 0326 on `LocalSubring.IsCoefficientRing` in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.CompleteLocalRing.CoefficientRing`; 0327 on the class `IsCohenRing`, 0328 on `IsCohenRing.exists_residueField_ringEquiv` and 0329 on `IsCohenRing.formallySmooth_quotient_span_pow`, all in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.CohenRing`; and 032C on `isUniversallyCatenary_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal` in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Catenary.Formal`. With 0324 carried here, every labelled item of the section now has a carrier and only the heading itself had none.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.isAdicComplete_maximalIdeal_iff_forall_compatible_existsUnique_mk_eq
declarations.doc:
**A local ring is complete exactly when it is the inverse limit of its adic truncations.**

Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a local ring. Then `R` is `𝔪`-adically complete if and only if for every
family `f` of residues `f n : R ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ` that is compatible with the truncation maps
`R ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ → R ⧸ 𝔪ᵏ` for `k ≤ n`, there is a *unique* `r : R` whose residue modulo `𝔪ⁿ` is
`f n` for every `n`.

This is the Stacks project's definition of a complete local ring: a compatible family is an
element of `lim_n R / 𝔪ⁿ`, existence of `r` says the canonical map `R → lim_n R / 𝔪ⁿ` is
surjective, and uniqueness says it is injective, so the two together say that this ring map is
an isomorphism. Uniqueness for the zero family is the separatedness `⋂ₙ 𝔪ⁿ = (0)` that the
source's footnote insists on; it corresponds to the `IsHausdorff` half of `IsAdicComplete`,
while existence corresponds to the `IsPrecomplete` half.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.isAdicComplete_maximalIdeal_iff_forall_compatible_existsUnique_mk_eq
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] :
    IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R ↔
      ∀ f : (n : ℕ) → R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n,
        (∀ (k n : ℕ) (h : k ≤ n),
            Ideal.Quotient.factor (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right h) (f n) = f k) →
          ∃! r : R, ∀ n : ℕ, Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal R ^ n) r = f n
declarations.comment: The source defines `(R, 𝔪)` to be a *complete local ring* when the canonical map `R ⟶ lim_n R / 𝔪ⁿ` is an isomorphism. This library has no definition of its own for that: completeness of a local ring is spelled `IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R` everywhere downstream (for instance in 032A, 032D and 0C0S), and introducing a second name for it would shadow canonical Mathlib API. So the definition is carried as the CHARACTERIZATION theorem that identifies the library's spelling with the source's: `IsAdicComplete` holds iff every compatible family of residues modulo `𝔪ⁿ` comes from a unique element of `R`, i.e. iff the canonical ring map into the inverse limit is bijective, hence an isomorphism. `lim_n R/𝔪ⁿ` is not named as an object; it is spelled by its universal property, with the source's own truncations `Ideal.Quotient.mk (𝔪ⁿ)` and transition maps `Ideal.Quotient.factor`, so the statement does not depend on a model of the limit. The source's footnote — that this includes `⋂ 𝔪ⁿ = (0)`, `R` complete AND separated — is the uniqueness half of the `∃!`, applied to the zero family; it matches the `IsHausdorff` component of `IsAdicComplete`, existence matching `IsPrecomplete`. The footnote's three cross-references (05JC, 05GG, 05GH) are remarks on when the completion is itself complete and Noetherian; they are separate tags and are not claimed here.

declarations.name: quotient_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a Noetherian complete local ring and `J` is a proper ideal of `R`, then the
quotient `R / J` is again a Noetherian complete local ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotient_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (hR : IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing R)
    (J : Ideal R) (hJ : J ≠ ⊤) :
    IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing (R ⧸ J)

declarations.name: finite_isProduct_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a Noetherian complete local ring and `R → S` is a finite ring map, then `S` is a
finite product of Noetherian complete local rings: there exist finitely many rings
`T 0, ..., T (m-1)`, each a Noetherian complete local ring, together with a ring isomorphism
`S ≃+* Π i, T i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_isProduct_isNoetherianCompleteLocalRing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (hR : IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing R)
    {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S] :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (T : Fin m → Type v) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (T i)),
      (∀ i, IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing (T i)) ∧
      Nonempty (S ≃+* (Π i, T i))

declarations.name: LocalSubring.IsCoefficientRing
declarations.doc:
A *coefficient ring* of a local ring `(R, 𝔪)` is a local subring `Λ ⊆ R` such that `Λ` is
complete with maximal ideal `Λ ∩ 𝔪`, the residue field of `Λ` maps isomorphically onto the
residue field of `R`, and `Λ ∩ 𝔪 = pΛ`, where `p` is the characteristic of the residue field
of `R`.
declarations.statement: public structure LocalSubring.IsCoefficientRing (Λ : LocalSubring R) : Prop

declarations.name: IsCohenRing
declarations.doc:
A *Cohen ring* is a complete discrete valuation ring whose uniformizer is
a (rational) prime number `p`. Concretely, `R` is a domain, it is a discrete
valuation ring, it is complete for the maximal-ideal-adic topology, and there
is a prime number `p ∈ ℕ` such that the maximal ideal of `R` is generated by
the image of `p` in `R`.

This is a class extending `IsDiscreteValuationRing` and `IsAdicComplete` for the maximal ideal, so
that both the valuation-theoretic and the completeness API of a Cohen ring are available to
instance search without unfolding the definition, and only the arithmetic condition on the
uniformizer is a field of its own.
declarations.statement:
class IsCohenRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] : Prop extends
    IsDiscreteValuationRing R, IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R

declarations.name: IsCohenRing.exists_residueField_ringEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Cohen rings exist** (Stacks 0328). Let `p` be a prime number and let `k` be a field of
characteristic `p`. Then there is a Cohen ring `Λ` whose uniformizer is `p`, i.e. with
`maximalIdeal Λ = pΛ`, and whose residue field `Λ/pΛ` is isomorphic to `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCohenRing.exists_residueField_ringEquiv (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (k : Type u)
    [Field k] [CharP k p] :
    ∃ (Λ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Λ) (_ : IsDomain Λ) (_ : IsCohenRing Λ),
      maximalIdeal Λ = Ideal.span {(p : Λ)} ∧ Nonempty (ResidueField Λ ≃+* k)
declarations.comment: The source's `Λ/pΛ ≅ k` is the conjunction of `maximalIdeal Λ = pΛ`, pinning the uniformizer to the prime `p` that `IsCohenRing` (Stacks 0327) only asserts to exist, with a ring isomorphism `ResidueField Λ ≃+* k`, `ResidueField Λ` being `Λ ⧸ maximalIdeal Λ`. The ring `Λ` is asked for in the universe of `k`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsCohenRing.formallySmooth_quotient_span_pow
declarations.doc:
Let `Λ` be a Cohen ring whose residue field has characteristic `p`, so that `p` is a
uniformizer of `Λ`. For every `n` the ring map `ℤ/pⁿℤ → Λ/pⁿΛ` is formally smooth
(Stacks 0329).
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCohenRing.formallySmooth_quotient_span_pow (p n : ℕ) (Λ : Type*) [CommRing Λ]
    [IsDomain Λ] [IsCohenRing Λ] [CharP (ResidueField Λ) p]
    [Algebra (ZMod (p ^ n)) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ n})] :
    Algebra.FormallySmooth (ZMod (p ^ n)) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ) ^ n})
declarations.comment: The source's `p > 0` prime and `p` a uniformizer are consequences of `CharP (ResidueField Λ) p` for a Cohen ring, so only the latter is assumed, and `n ≥ 1` is dropped because `n = 0` gives the zero ring on both sides. The `ZMod (p ^ n)`-algebra structure is assumed rather than synthesized; it is unique where it exists, so this pins the source's map `ℤ/pⁿℤ → Λ/pⁿΛ`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_isCoefficientRing_and_exists_surjective_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
**Cohen structure theorem** (Stacks 032A). Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a complete local ring.
1. `R` has a coefficient ring: a local subring `Λ ⊆ R` which is complete with maximal ideal
   `Λ ∩ 𝔪`, whose residue field maps isomorphically onto that of `R`, and with `Λ ∩ 𝔪 = pΛ` for
   `p` the residue characteristic of `R`.
2. If `𝔪` is a finitely generated ideal, then `R` is isomorphic to a quotient
   `Λ[[x_1, …, x_n]]/I` where `Λ` is either a field or a Cohen ring; equivalently, there is a
   surjective ring homomorphism `Λ[[x_1, …, x_n]] → R`, whose kernel is `I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_isCoefficientRing_and_exists_surjective_mvPowerSeries
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    (∃ Λ : LocalSubring R, Λ.IsCoefficientRing) ∧
      ((maximalIdeal R).FG →
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Λ) (_ : IsDomain Λ),
          (IsField Λ ∨ IsCohenRing Λ) ∧
            ∃ f : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ →+* R, Function.Surjective f)
declarations.comment: Completeness of `R` is `IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R`, the source's `R ≅ lim_n R/𝔪ⁿ`. The two parts are the two conjuncts, the second guarded by its own hypothesis so that part (1) keeps the source's generality, and its `R ≅ Λ[[x_1, …, x_n]]/I` is stated as the existence of a surjection `MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ →+* R` with kernel `I`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: complete_local_ring_noetherian
declarations.doc:
A local ring `R` that is complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology and whose maximal
ideal is finitely generated is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem complete_local_ring_noetherian
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R)
    (hfg : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).FG) :
    IsNoetherianRing R

declarations.name: isUniversallyCatenary_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 032C.** A Noetherian complete local ring is universally catenary.

By the Cohen structure theorem it is a quotient of a power series ring over a field or over a
Cohen ring, hence of a regular local ring; a regular local ring is Cohen-Macaulay with full
support, so [Stacks, Tag 00NM] applies, and universal catenarity passes to quotients.

Completeness is asked for as precompleteness for the maximal ideal, as in [Stacks, Tag 07PJ]; the
Hausdorff half is automatic for a Noetherian local ring, so a ring carrying
`IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R` satisfies the hypothesis by inference.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] : Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary R

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_injective_finite_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian complete local domain. Then there is a subring `R₀ ⊆ R` which is
a regular complete local ring, over which `R` is finite, which induces an isomorphism on residue
fields, and which is a power series ring `Λ[[X_1, …, X_d]]` over a field or over a Cohen ring `Λ`.
The subring is presented as the image of an injective ring homomorphism
`f : Λ[[X_1, …, X_d]] → R`, finite and with `R/𝔪` generated by the image of `f`. (Stacks 032D)
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_injective_finite_mvPowerSeries (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Λ) (_ : IsDomain Λ),
      (IsField Λ ∨ IsCohenRing Λ) ∧
        ∃ _ : IsRegularLocalRing (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ),
          IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ)) (MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ) ∧
            ∃ f : MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ →+* R,
              Function.Injective f ∧ f.Finite ∧ Function.Surjective ((residue R).comp f)
declarations.comment: The subring `R₀ ⊆ R` is presented as an injective ring homomorphism `f` from the power series ring it is isomorphic to, so that items (1) and (3) are statements about `MvPowerSeries (Fin d) Λ` and item (2) is one about `f`: `f.Finite` for finiteness and `Function.Surjective ((residue R).comp f)` for the isomorphism on residue fields. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsN1
declarations.doc:
A domain `R` is **N-1** if the integral closure of `R` in its field of fractions is a finite
`R`-module.

The field of fractions is `FractionRing R`; see the module docstring for the formulation with an
arbitrary field of fractions. As with `IsIntegrallyClosed`, `R` is not required to be a domain:
for a general commutative ring `FractionRing R` is the total ring of fractions, and the condition
reads the same.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsN1 (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: IsJapaneseRing
declarations.doc:
A domain `R` is **N-2**, or **Japanese**, if for every finite field extension `L` of its
field of fractions `K = Frac(R)`, the integral closure of `R` in `L` is a finite `R`-module.

The extension is presented as a field `L` that is a `K`-algebra, finite dimensional over `K`,
whose `R`-algebra structure is the composite of `R → K` with `K → L`.
declarations.statement: class IsJapaneseRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] : Prop

declarations.name: isN1_and_isJapaneseRing_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**N-1 and N-2 pass to a localization.** Stacks Tag 032G: if a domain `R` is N-1 then so is
every localization of `R` which is again a domain, and the same for N-2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isN1_and_isJapaneseRing_of_isLocalization {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (M : Submonoid R) (Rₛ : Type u) [CommRing Rₛ] [IsDomain Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ]
    [IsLocalization M Rₛ] :
    (IsN1 R → IsN1 Rₛ) ∧ (IsJapaneseRing R → IsJapaneseRing Rₛ)

declarations.name: isN1_and_isJapaneseRing_of_localizationSpan
declarations.doc:
**N-1 and N-2 descend along a principal open cover.** Stacks Tag 032H: let `R` be a domain and
let `t ⊆ R` generate the unit ideal. If the localization `R_g` is N-1 for every `g ∈ t` then so is
`R`, and the same for N-2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isN1_and_isJapaneseRing_of_localizationSpan {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (t : Set R) (ht : Ideal.span t = ⊤)
    {Rₚ : ∀ _ : t, Type u} [∀ g, CommRing (Rₚ g)] [∀ g, IsDomain (Rₚ g)]
    [∀ g, Algebra R (Rₚ g)] [∀ g, IsLocalization.Away g.val (Rₚ g)] :
    ((∀ g, IsN1 (Rₚ g)) → IsN1 R) ∧
      ((∀ g, IsJapaneseRing (Rₚ g)) → IsJapaneseRing R)

declarations.name: isJapaneseRing_of_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**N-2 ascends along a quasi-finite extension of domains.** Stacks Tag 032I: let `R ⊆ S` be a
quasi-finite extension of domains with `R` Noetherian and N-2. Then `S` is N-2.

Zariski's main theorem covers `Spec S` by principal opens on which `S` agrees with a subalgebra
module-finite over `R`; N-2 ascends to such a subalgebra, passes to its localizations (Tag 032G),
and descends from the cover (Tag 032H).
declarations.statement:
theorem isJapaneseRing_of_quasiFinite {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [CommRing S]
    [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S] (hR : IsJapaneseRing R) : IsJapaneseRing S

declarations.name: main_theorem_032j
declarations.doc:
Theorem (Stacks Tag 032J). Let `R` be a Noetherian domain. If the Laurent
polynomial ring `R[z, z^{-1}]` is N-1, then `R` is N-1.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_032j (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (h : IsN1 (LaurentPolynomial R)) : IsN1 R

declarations.name: isN1_of_finite_of_isN1
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (N-1 descends, part of Stacks Tag 032K).**
Let `R` be a Noetherian domain and `R ⊂ S` a finite extension of domains
(modelled by an injective algebra map `R → S` with `S` finite over `R`).
If `S` is N-1, then `R` is N-1.
declarations.statement:
theorem isN1_of_finite_of_isN1
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (hfin : Module.Finite R S)
    (hS : IsN1 S) : IsN1 R

declarations.name: isN2_of_finite_of_isN2
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (N-2 descends, part of Stacks Tag 032K).**
Let `R` be a Noetherian domain and `R ⊂ S` a finite extension of domains
(modelled by an injective algebra map `R → S` with `S` finite over `R`).
If `S` is N-2, then `R` is N-2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isN2_of_finite_of_isN2
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (hfin : Module.Finite R S)
    (hS : IsN2_032k S) : IsN2_032k R

declarations.name: Noetherian_normal_domain_finite_separable_extension
declarations.doc:
The integral closure of a Noetherian normal domain in a finite separable
extension is finite over the base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem Noetherian_normal_domain_finite_separable_extension
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L] :
    Module.Finite R (integralClosure R L)

declarations.name: N1_iff_N2
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 032M, Lemma 10.161.11. For a Noetherian domain `R` whose fraction
field `K` has characteristic zero, `R` is N-1 if and only if `R` is N-2 (Japanese).
declarations.statement:
theorem N1_iff_N2 (R K : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] [CharZero K] :
    IsN1_032m R K ↔ IsN2_032m R K

declarations.name: isJapaneseRing_iff_finite_integralClosure_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**N-2 is tested on purely inseparable extensions.** Stacks Tag 032N: a Noetherian domain `R`
is N-2 if and only if the integral closure of `R` in every finite purely inseparable extension of
its field of fractions is a finite `R`-module.

The source states this for a field of fractions of characteristic `p > 0`; the characteristic
plays no role in the argument, which factors a finite normal extension of `K` as a purely
inseparable extension followed by a separable one (Tag 030M) and is vacuously about `L = K` in
characteristic zero, so no characteristic hypothesis is imposed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isJapaneseRing_iff_finite_integralClosure_isPurelyInseparable (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsJapaneseRing R ↔
      ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra R L] [Algebra (FractionRing R) L]
        [IsScalarTower R (FractionRing R) L] [FiniteDimensional (FractionRing R) L]
        [IsPurelyInseparable (FractionRing R) L],
        Module.Finite R (integralClosure R L)

declarations.name: Polynomial.isN1_and_isJapaneseRing
declarations.doc:
**N-1 and N-2 ascend to a polynomial ring.** Let `R` be a domain. If the integral closure of
`R` in `Frac(R)` is a finite `R`-module, then the integral closure of `R[x]` in `Frac(R[x])` is a
finite `R[x]`-module; and if `R` is Noetherian and N-2 (Japanese), then `R[x]` is N-2.

The Noetherian hypothesis of Tag 032O is attached to the N-2 conjunct only, the N-1 conjunct not
using it; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsJapaneseRing.of_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Tate's theorem.** Let `R` be a Noetherian integrally closed (i.e. normal) domain and let
`x ∈ R` generate a prime ideal, so that `R ⧸ xR` is a domain. If `R ⧸ xR` is N-2 (Japanese) and
`R` is `x`-adically complete, then `R` is N-2.

Completeness is asked for as `IsPrecomplete (Ideal.span {x}) R`; the Hausdorff half of
`IsAdicComplete` is automatic here, see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsJapaneseRing.of_quotient_span_singleton {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R] (x : R) [(Ideal.span {x}).IsPrime]
    [IsPrecomplete (Ideal.span {x}) R] (h : IsJapaneseRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x})) :
    IsJapaneseRing R

declarations.name: PowerSeries.isJapaneseRing
declarations.doc:
**Tag 032Q.** If `R` is a Noetherian N-2 (Japanese) domain, then so is the formal power
series ring `R⟦X⟧`: the integral closure of `R⟦X⟧` in every finite extension of `Frac R⟦X⟧` is
a finite `R⟦X⟧`-module.

Together with `PowerSeries.instIsNoetherianRing` and `PowerSeries.instIsDomain` this says that
`R⟦X⟧` is a Noetherian N-2 domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJapaneseRing {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (hR : IsJapaneseRing R) : IsJapaneseRing R⟦X⟧

declarations.name: IsUniversallyJapaneseRing
declarations.doc:
A ring `R` is **universally Japanese** if for every finite-type ring map `R → S` with `S` a
domain, the domain `S` is N-2 (Japanese), i.e. satisfies `IsJapaneseRing`.
declarations.statement: class IsUniversallyJapaneseRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: IsNagataRing
declarations.doc:
A ring `R` is a **Nagata ring** if `R` is Noetherian and for every prime ideal `p ⊆ R` the
quotient domain `R ⧸ p` is N-2 (Japanese), i.e. satisfies `IsJapaneseRing`.
declarations.statement: class IsNagataRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: isUniversallyJapanese_of_isEssentiallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
(Stacks Tag 032S, Lemma 10.162.4) If `R` is universally Japanese then any
`R`-algebra `A` essentially of finite type over `R` is universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyJapanese_of_isEssentiallyOfFiniteType (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (hR : IsUniversallyJapanese R)
    (hA : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType R A (algebraMap R A)) : IsUniversallyJapanese A

declarations.name: isNagataRing_of_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**A quasi-finite algebra over a Nagata ring is a Nagata ring.** If `R` is a Nagata ring —
Noetherian, with every quotient `R ⧸ p` by a prime N-2 — and `R → S` is quasi-finite, that is of
finite type with finite-dimensional fibres (for example module-finite), then `S` is a Nagata ring.

Quasi-finiteness in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 00PL] is the conjunction
`[Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S]`, Mathlib's `Algebra.QuasiFinite` omitting the
finite type condition. No injectivity is required: the map `R → S` is arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataRing_of_quasiFinite {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.QuasiFinite R S] (hR : IsNagataRing R) :
    IsNagataRing S

declarations.name: isNagata_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
(Stacks Tag 032U) A localization of a Nagata ring is a Nagata ring.

Here `T` is an arbitrary `R`-algebra realizing `T = M⁻¹R` for a submonoid `M ⊆ R`
(`IsLocalization M T`), which is exactly Definition 4 of a localization. The single-element
case `R_f` (`M = {1, f, f², …}`) and the prime case `R_p` (`M = R ∖ p`) are special cases.

Proof structure (Stacks: "clear from Tag 032G"):
* Noetherianity of `T` is `IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing M T hR.isNoetherianRing`.
* For a prime `q ⊆ T`, set `p := q.comap (R → T)` (prime by `Ideal.comap_isPrime`). Then
  `R/p` is N-2 (`hR.isJapaneseRing_quotient p`), and `T/q ≅ M̄⁻¹(R/p)` is a localization of the
  domain `R/p` at the image `M̄` of `M`, which lies in the nonzerodivisors of `R/p`. By
  `isN2_of_isLocalization_domain`, `T/q` is N-2. Hence `T` is Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagata_of_isLocalization (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : Submonoid R) (T : Type u)
    [CommRing T] [Algebra R T] [IsLocalization M T] (hR : IsNagataRing R) :
    IsNagataRing T

declarations.name: isUniversallyJapaneseRing_and_isNagataRing_of_localizationSpan
declarations.doc:
**Universally Japanese and Nagata descend along a principal open cover.** Let `t ⊆ R`
generate the unit ideal and for `g ∈ t` let `Rₚ g` be a localization of `R` away from `g`. If
every `Rₚ g` is universally Japanese then so is `R`, and if every `Rₚ g` is a Nagata ring then so
is `R`.

The source states the two parts for finitely many `f₁, …, f_n`; they are the two conjuncts
here, and an arbitrary spanning set is the same hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isUniversallyJapaneseRing_and_isNagataRing_of_localizationSpan {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] (t : Set R) (ht : Ideal.span t = ⊤) (Rₚ : ∀ _ : t, Type u)
    [∀ g, CommRing (Rₚ g)] [∀ g, Algebra R (Rₚ g)] [∀ g, IsLocalization.Away g.val (Rₚ g)] :
    ((∀ g, IsUniversallyJapaneseRing (Rₚ g)) → IsUniversallyJapaneseRing R) ∧
      ((∀ g, IsNagataRing (Rₚ g)) → IsNagataRing R)

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**A Noetherian complete local ring is a Nagata ring.** If `R` is Noetherian, local, and
complete for the topology defined by its maximal ideal `m`, then `R` is a Nagata ring: for every
prime `p ⊆ R` the quotient domain `R ⧸ p` is N-2 (Japanese).

Completeness is asked for as `IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R`; the Hausdorff half
of `IsAdicComplete` is automatic for a Noetherian local ring, so a ring with
`IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R` satisfies the hypothesis by inference.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsNagataRing.of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] :
    IsNagataRing R

declarations.name: IsAnalyticallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
A local ring `R` with maximal ideal `m` is **analytically unramified** if its completion
`R^ = lim_n R ⧸ mⁿ` is reduced.

The source asks for `R` Noetherian; that hypothesis is not needed to state the condition and is
carried by the lemmas about it. A prime ideal `p ⊂ R` is analytically unramified when the local
ring `R ⧸ p` is, i.e. when `IsAnalyticallyUnramified (R ⧸ p)` holds.
declarations.statement: public def IsAnalyticallyUnramified (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: isAnalyticallyUnramified_iff_minimalPrimes_and_isN1
declarations.doc:
**Tag 032Y.** Let `(R, m)` be a Noetherian local ring. Then `R` is analytically unramified if
and only if `R` is reduced and each of its minimal primes `q` is analytically unramified, i.e.
each local ring `R ⧸ q` is; and an analytically unramified `R` is N-1, i.e. the integral closure
of `R` in its total ring of fractions `Q(R)` is a finite `R`-module.

The first conjunct is parts (1), (2) and (3) of the source, the forward direction being (1) and
(2) and the converse being (3); the second conjunct is part (4), and part (5) is that conjunct
with `[IsDomain R]` adjoined.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAnalyticallyUnramified_iff_minimalPrimes_and_isN1 (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    (IsAnalyticallyUnramified R ↔
        IsReduced R ∧
          ∀ q ∈ minimalPrimes R, ∀ [IsLocalRing (R ⧸ q)], IsAnalyticallyUnramified (R ⧸ q)) ∧
      (IsAnalyticallyUnramified R → IsN1 R)

declarations.name: exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime_of_analyticallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 032Z.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and `p ⊂ R` a prime
ideal such that the localization `R_p` is a discrete valuation ring and `p` is
analytically unramified (`R^ / p R^` is reduced). Then for every associated prime
`q` of the `R^`-module `R^ / p R^`, the local ring `(R^)_q` is a discrete
valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime_of_analyticallyUnramified {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
  [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (p : Ideal R)
    [p.IsPrime]
    -- (1) `R_p` is a discrete valuation ring (hence a domain).
    [IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p)] (hdvr : IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p))
    -- (2) `p` is analytically unramified: `R^ / p R^` is reduced.
    (hunr : AnalyticallyUnramifiedPrime p)
    -- `q` is an associated prime of the `R^`-module `R^ / p R^`.
    (q : Ideal (mCompletion R)) (hq : IsAssociatedPrime q (mCompletion R ⧸ pCompletion p)) :
    -- Conclusion: `(R^)_q` is a discrete valuation ring (in particular a domain).
    ∃ (_ : q.IsPrime) (_ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q)),
      IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime q)

declarations.name: IsAnalyticallyUnramified.of_associatedPrimes_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0330.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `x ∈ 𝔪` be a
nonzerodivisor. If `R ⧸ xR` has no embedded primes — every associated prime of the module `R ⧸ xR`
is minimal over `xR` — and every associated prime `𝔭` of `R ⧸ xR` has `R_𝔭` regular and is
analytically unramified, then `R` is analytically unramified.

The source assumes `R` a domain and `x ≠ 0`; only `x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R` is used, and it is what
those two amount to.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsAnalyticallyUnramified.of_associatedPrimes_quotient_span_singleton {R : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {x : R} (hx : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors R)
    (hxm : x ∈ maximalIdeal R)
    (hemb : associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) ⊆ (Ideal.span {x}).minimalPrimes)
    (hp :
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] [IsLocalRing (R ⧸ p)],
        p ∈ associatedPrimes R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {x}) →
          IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsAnalyticallyUnramified (R ⧸ p)) :
    IsAnalyticallyUnramified R
declarations.comment: The source's `R` a domain with `x ≠ 0` is generalized to `x` a nonzerodivisor, which is all the proof uses; `R ⧸ xR` having no embedded primes is spelled as every associated prime of `R ⧸ xR` being minimal over `xR`, there being no predicate for it in this library.

declarations.name: IsAnalyticallyUnramified.of_isNagataRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0331.** A local ring `(R, 𝔪)` which is a domain and a Nagata ring is
analytically unramified: its completion `R^ = lim_n R ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ` is reduced.

The source also assumes `R` Noetherian; that is the first conjunct of `IsNagataRing R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsAnalyticallyUnramified.of_isNagataRing {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsDomain R] (hR : IsNagataRing R) : IsAnalyticallyUnramified R
declarations.comment: Nagata is `IsNagataRing` of Definition 032R(2), whose first conjunct is `IsNoetherianRing R`, so the source's Noetherian hypothesis is absorbed rather than restated; analytically unramified is the predicate of Tag 032X, reducedness of the `𝔪`-adic completion.

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_setOf_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime
declarations.doc:
