**Stacks Tag 0332.** Let `R` be a Noetherian domain. If there is a nonzero `f ∈ R` such that
`R_f` is normal, then the set of primes `𝔭` of `R` with `R_𝔭` a normal domain is open in
`Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_setOf_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {f : R} (hf : f ≠ 0)
    (hf' : IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.Away f)) :
    IsOpen {p : PrimeSpectrum R | IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)}
declarations.comment: Normality of a localization is spelled `IsIntegrallyClosed`, Mathlib having no predicate for a normal ring; the `IsDomain` conjunct of the spelling used for tags 030C (1) and 031S is automatic here because `R` is a domain. `R_f` is the canonical model `Localization.Away f`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isN1_iff_exists_isIntegrallyClosed_away_and_forall_isN1_atPrime
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian domain `R` is **N-1** — its integral closure in `Frac R` is a finite `R`-module —
if and only if `R_f` is normal for some nonzero `f ∈ R` and `R_𝔪` is N-1 for every maximal ideal
`𝔪 ⊆ R`.

Normality of the domain `R_f` is `IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.Away f)`; see the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isN1_iff_exists_isIntegrallyClosed_away_and_forall_isN1_atPrime
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsN1 R ↔
      (∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.Away f)) ∧
        ∀ (𝔪 : Ideal R) [𝔪.IsMaximal], IsN1 (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪)
declarations.comment:
`R_f` normal is `IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.Away f)`, normality of a domain
being integral closedness in its field of fractions; the localizations are the concrete models
`Localization.Away f` and `Localization.AtPrime 𝔪`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isNagataRing_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Nagata's theorem.** For a ring `R` the following are equivalent: `R` is a Nagata ring;
every finite-type `R`-algebra is a Nagata ring; `R` is universally Japanese and Noetherian.

In particular an algebra of finite type over a Nagata ring is a Nagata ring. Nagata is
`IsNagataRing` and universally Japanese is `IsUniversallyJapaneseRing`, the two conditions of
Definition 032R.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataRing_tfae {R : Type u} [CommRing R] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsNagataRing R,
        ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S], IsNagataRing S,
        IsUniversallyJapaneseRing R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R ]
declarations.comment: Items (1)-(3) as a `List.TFAE`. Nagata is `IsNagataRing` (032R(2)) and universally Japanese is `IsUniversallyJapaneseRing` (032R(1)); item (2), the condition the source's proof calls universally Nagata, is stated as the quantification over finite-type `R`-algebras rather than through a predicate of its own. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isNagataRing_field_and_int_and_isDedekindDomain
declarations.doc:
**Fields, `ℤ` and Dedekind domains whose fraction field has characteristic zero are Nagata
rings**, hence in particular universally Japanese. These are items (1), (3) and (4) of the source,
in its order; they share the one argument that inspects `R ⧸ 𝔭` for each prime `𝔭`.

The three classes on their own are `IsNagataRing.of_field`, `Int.isNagataRing` and
`IsNagataRing.of_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero`, which is how they are applied; see the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataRing_field_and_int_and_isDedekindDomain :
    (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K], IsNagataRing K) ∧
    IsNagataRing ℤ ∧
    ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero R], IsNagataRing R
declarations.comment: Items (1), (3) and (4) as one conjunction, since they share one proof; each is available separately as `IsNagataRing.of_field`, `Int.isNagataRing` and `IsNagataRing.of_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero`. Item (2) is Tag 032W and item (5) with the closing clause "and in particular universally Japanese" is Tag 0334, both tagged 0335 below. Nagata is `IsNagataRing` (032R(2)) and universally Japanese is `IsUniversallyJapaneseRing` (032R(1)). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.of_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0335 (1).** A field is a Nagata ring, hence in particular universally Japanese: the
only prime of a field `K` is `0`, and `K ⧸ 0 = K` is N-2 because the integral closure of `K` in a
finite extension `L` of `K` is `L` itself, a finite `K`-module.
declarations.statement: public theorem IsNagataRing.of_field {K : Type u} [Field K] : IsNagataRing K

declarations.name: Int.isNagataRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0335 (3).** The ring `ℤ` is a Nagata ring, hence in particular universally Japanese.
This is the case `R = ℤ` of `IsNagataRing.of_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero`.
declarations.statement: public theorem Int.isNagataRing : IsNagataRing ℤ

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.of_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0335 (4).** A Dedekind domain whose fraction field has characteristic zero is a
Nagata ring, hence in particular universally Japanese. For a prime `𝔭 ≠ 0` the quotient `R ⧸ 𝔭` is
a field and so is N-2; for `𝔭 = 0` the quotient is `R` itself, which is N-1 because it is
integrally closed, and N-1 implies N-2 in characteristic zero (Tag 032M).

The condition on the fraction field is stated as `CharZero R`, which for a domain `R` is
equivalent since `R → Frac R` is injective. It cannot be dropped: a one-dimensional Noetherian
integrally closed domain in characteristic `p` need not be N-2.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsNagataRing.of_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero R] : IsNagataRing R
declarations.comment: (4) Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero, the latter read as `CharZero R`.

registrations.name: IsNagataRing.of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
registrations.comment: (2) Noetherian complete local rings, which is Tag 032W.

registrations.name: isNagataRing_tfae
registrations.comment: (5) Finite type ring extensions of any of the above, which is the implication (1) ⇒ (2) of Tag 0334, and the closing clause "and in particular universally Japanese", which is its implication (1) ⇒ (3).

declarations.name: Module.depth_self_eq_depth_self_add_depth_quotient_map_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Depth is additive along a flat local homomorphism.** Let `R → S` be a flat local
homomorphism of local rings with `S` Noetherian, with maximal ideals `𝔪_R` and `𝔪_S`. Then
`depth_{𝔪_S}(S) = depth_{𝔪_R}(R) + depth_{𝔪_S}(S/𝔪_R S)`, where `𝔪_R S` is the ideal of `S`
generated by the image of `𝔪_R`. The depth of the fibre `S/𝔪_R S` is taken over `S` along `𝔪_S`,
which is its depth as a local ring in its own right.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_self_eq_depth_self_add_depth_quotient_map_maximalIdeal (R S : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [Module.Flat R S] :
    depth S (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S =
      depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R +
        depth S (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S)
          (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
declarations.comment: Stated for `Module.depth` along the maximal ideals (Tag 00LI), with the fibre ring spelled as the `S`-module `S ⧸ 𝔪_R S`, of the same depth as the local ring `S/𝔪_R S`, and with `IsNoetherianRing R` dropped, being a consequence of faithful flatness. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.depth_tensorProduct_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Depth is additive along a flat local homomorphism.** Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism
of Noetherian local rings, let `M` be a finite `R`-module and let `N` be a finite `S`-module
flat over `R`. Then `depth_S(N ⊗_R M) = depth_R(M) + depth_S(N/𝔪_R N)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_tensorProduct_of_flat {R S M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] [Module.Finite S N]
    [Module.Flat R N] :
    depth S (maximalIdeal S) (N ⊗[R] M) = depth R (maximalIdeal R) M +
      depth S (maximalIdeal S)
        (N ⧸ ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S) • (⊤ : Submodule S N)))
declarations.comment: The fibre `N/𝔪_R N` has its depth taken over `S` along `𝔪_S` rather than over `S/𝔪_R S`, which is the same value, and the tensor product is written with `N` on the left.

declarations.name: min_le_depth_atPrime_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0339.** Let `R → S` be a flat ring map of Noetherian rings. If every fibre ring
`κ(𝔭) ⊗_R S` has Serre's property `(S_k)` and `R` has `(S_k)`, then `S` has `(S_k)`, property
`(S_k)` of a ring meaning that the depth of its localization at any prime is at least the minimum
of `k` and the dimension of that localization. The inequalities are read in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem min_le_depth_atPrime_of_flat {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Flat R S] {k : ℕ}
    (hfibre : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (Q : Ideal (p.Fiber S)) [Q.IsPrime],
      min (k : WithBot ℕ∞) (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime Q)) ≤
        (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime Q)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime Q)) (Localization.AtPrime Q) :
            WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hR : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
      min (k : WithBot ℕ∞) (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p)) ≤
        (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (Localization.AtPrime p) :
            WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
      min (k : WithBot ℕ∞) (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q)) ≤
        (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime q)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Localization.AtPrime q) :
            WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: Property `(S_k)` is spelled out from Definition 031P as the inequality `min{k, dim(A_𝔮)} ≤ depth(A_𝔮)` at every prime, with `Module.depth` (Tag 00LI) along the maximal ideal of `Localization.AtPrime 𝔮` and `ringKrullDim` for the dimension, as in Tags 031Q, 031S and 0352, the inequality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`; the fibre ring `S ⊗_R κ(𝔭)` is `Ideal.Fiber 𝔭 S`, and the ring map is an `Algebra R S` instance with `Module.Flat R S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: property_Rk_of_flat_of_fibre_of_base
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a flat ring map between Noetherian rings and fix `k ≥ 0`. If every
fibre ring `S ⊗[R] κ(p)` has property `(R_k)` and `R` has property `(R_k)`, then `S` has
property `(R_k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_Rk_of_flat_of_fibre_of_base
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Module.Flat R S]
    (k : ℕ)
    (hfib : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], HasPropertyRk (fibreRing R S p) k)
    (hR : HasPropertyRk R k) :
    HasPropertyRk S k

declarations.name: Algebra.isReduced_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 033B.** Let `R → S` be a smooth ring map. If `R` is reduced, then `S` is
reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isReduced_of_smooth (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.Smooth R S] [IsReduced R] : IsReduced S
declarations.comment: The ring map is an `Algebra R S` instance and smoothness of it is Mathlib's `Algebra.Smooth R S` (equivalently `(algebraMap R S).Smooth`, by `RingHom.smooth_algebraMap`); reducedness is `IsReduced`. No Noetherian hypothesis, so this is not an instance of Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced.isReduced_of_flat_of_isLocallyNoetherian`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isNormalRing_of_smooth
declarations.doc: **Stacks 033C.** A smooth algebra over a normal ring is a normal ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.isNormalRing_of_smooth (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.Smooth R S] (hR : IsNormalRing R) : IsNormalRing S

declarations.name: descent_noetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 033E**. If `φ : R → S` is faithfully flat and `S` is Noetherian, then `R` is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem descent_noetherian {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S)
    (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat) (hS : IsNoetherianRing S) : IsNoetherianRing R

declarations.name: RingHom.FaithfullyFlat.isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 033F**. If `φ : R → S` is a faithfully flat ring map and `S` is reduced,
then `R` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.FaithfullyFlat.isReduced {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] {φ : R →+* S}
    (hφ : φ.FaithfullyFlat) [IsReduced S] : IsReduced R

declarations.name: isDomain_and_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 033G.** Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map. If `S` is a normal ring, i.e. all
its localizations at primes are normal domains, then so is `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDomain_and_isIntegrallyClosed_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S]
    (hS : ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
      IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime q)) :
    ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
      IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)
declarations.comment: Normality is inlined as `IsDomain` plus `IsIntegrallyClosed` on `Localization.AtPrime 𝔭` for every prime `𝔭`, as in item (1) of tag 030C and in tag 031S, Mathlib having no predicate for a normal ring; the ring map `R → S` is an `Algebra R S` instance and its faithful flatness is `Module.FaithfullyFlat R S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsNormal
declarations.doc: A scheme is normal if each stalk of its structure sheaf is a normal domain.
declarations.statement: class IsNormal (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033J.** Normality of a scheme is equivalent to normality of the
section ring on every affine open, on one affine open covering, or to the existence of an
open covering by normal open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsNormal X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsNormalRing Γ(X, U),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : X.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, IsNormalRing Γ(X, U i),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, IsNormal (U i).toScheme]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_open
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 033J.** Every open subscheme of a normal scheme is normal.
declarations.statement:
public instance isNormal_open {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNormal X]
    (U : X.Opens) : IsNormal U.toScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_of_isNormal
declarations.doc: A normal scheme is reduced.
declarations.statement: instance isReduced_of_isNormal (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNormal X] : IsReduced X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_iff_forall_affineOpen_normal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033L.** An integral scheme is normal if and only if the ring of
sections on every nonempty affine open is a normal domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_iff_forall_affineOpen_normal (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] :
    IsNormal X ↔
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ _hU : Nonempty U.1,
        letI : IsDomain Γ(X, U.1) := IsIntegral.component_integral U.1
        IsIntegrallyClosed Γ(X, U.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_iff_exists_iso_finite_coproduct_integral_normal
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is isomorphic to a finite coproduct of normal
integral schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_iff_exists_iso_finite_coproduct_integral_normal
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    IsNormal X ↔
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
          (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Y i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsIntegral (Y i)),
        Nonempty (X ≅ ∐ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_iff_exists_iso_coproduct_integral_normal
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is isomorphic to a coproduct of normal
integral schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_iff_exists_iso_coproduct_integral_normal
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsNormal X ↔
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
          (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Y i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsIntegral (Y i)),
        Nonempty (X ≅ ∐ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularInCodimension
declarations.doc:
A scheme is regular in codimension `k` (has property `(R_k)`) if each of its local rings of
Krull dimension at most `k` is regular.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsRegularInCodimension (X : Scheme) (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.HasPropertySk
declarations.doc:
Serre's property `(Sₖ)` for a locally Noetherian scheme: at every point, the depth of the
local ring is at least the minimum of `k` and the dimension of that local ring.
declarations.statement: def HasPropertySk (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme
declarations.doc:
A scheme is **universally Japanese** if every point has an affine open neighbourhood whose
ring of sections is universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
public def IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme
    (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop

declarations.name: isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme
declarations.doc: A scheme is Nagata if and only if it is locally Noetherian and universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme
    (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsNagataScheme X ↔
      (IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧
        IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme X)
declarations.comment: the forward implication: a Nagata scheme is locally Noetherian

declarations.name: isJapaneseScheme_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033V.** For an integral scheme, Japanese-ness is equivalent to
Japanese-ness of the section ring of every nonempty affine open, to the existence of an affine
open cover with Japanese section rings, and to the existence of an open cover by Japanese
schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJapaneseScheme_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsJapaneseScheme X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, ∀ _hU : Nonempty U.1,
        letI : IsDomain Γ(X, U.1) := IsIntegral.component_integral U.1
        IsJapaneseRing Γ(X, U.1),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i).1) ∧
          ∀ i, ∃ _hU : Nonempty (U i).1,
            letI : IsDomain Γ(X, (U i).1) := IsIntegral.component_integral (U i).1
            IsJapaneseRing Γ(X, (U i).1),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover U ∧
        ∀ i, ∃ hU : IsIntegral (U i).toScheme,
            @IsJapaneseScheme (U i).toScheme hU]

declarations.name: isJapaneseScheme_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033V.** Every nonempty open subscheme of a Japanese integral scheme is
Japanese.

declarations.name: isUniversallyJapaneseScheme_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033W.** For a scheme `X`, being universally Japanese is equivalent to
the section ring of every affine open being universally Japanese, to this holding on some affine
open covering, and to admitting an open covering by universally Japanese open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyJapaneseScheme_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsUniversallyJapaneseRing Γ(X, (U : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : X.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, IsUniversallyJapaneseRing Γ(X, (U i : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme (U i).toScheme]

declarations.name: isUniversallyJapaneseScheme_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033W.** Every open subscheme of a universally Japanese scheme is
universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyJapaneseScheme_open {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme X)
    (U : X.Opens) : IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme U.toScheme

declarations.name: isNagataScheme_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 033X.** For a scheme `X`, being Nagata is equivalent to the section
ring of every affine open being Nagata, to this holding on some affine open covering, and to
admitting an open covering by Nagata open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagataScheme_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsNagataScheme X,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, IsNagataRing Γ(X, (U : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        IsOpenCover (fun i ↦ (U i : X.Opens)) ∧
          ∀ i, IsNagataRing Γ(X, (U i : X.Opens)),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        IsOpenCover U ∧ ∀ i, IsNagataScheme (U i).toScheme]

declarations.name: isNagataScheme_open
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 033X.** Every open subscheme of a Nagata scheme is Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagataScheme_open {X : Scheme.{u}} (hX : IsNagataScheme X) (U : X.Opens) :
    IsNagataScheme U.toScheme

declarations.name: isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme
declarations.doc: A scheme is Nagata if and only if it is locally Noetherian and universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme
    (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    IsNagataScheme X ↔
      (IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧
        IsUniversallyJapaneseScheme X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafHasDepthAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0341.** A sheaf of modules has depth `k` at `x` when its stalk has
depth `k` over the local ring at `x`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SheafHasDepthAt (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing
      X.toRingedSpace)) (x : X)
    (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SchemeHasDepthAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0341.** A scheme has depth `k` at `x` when its local ring at `x` has
depth `k` over itself.
declarations.statement: abbrev SchemeHasDepthAt (X : Scheme.{u}) (x : X) (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafHasPropertySk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0341.** Serre's condition `(Sₖ)` for a sheaf of modules: at every
point its depth is at least the minimum of `k` and the dimension of the support of its
stalk.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SheafHasPropertySk (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing
      X.toRingedSpace))
    (k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_iff_forall_hasPropertySk
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if it satisfies Serre's condition
`(Sₖ)` for every nonnegative integer `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_iff_forall_hasPropertySk
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsCohenMacaulay X ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, HasPropertySk X k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafIsCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0343.** A sheaf of modules is Cohen–Macaulay when it satisfies
Serre's condition `(Sₖ)` for every `k`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SheafIsCohenMacaulay (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing
      X.toRingedSpace)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_iff_hasPropertyS1_and_isRegularInCodimension_zero
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is reduced if and only if it satisfies Serre's conditions `(S₁)`
and `(R₀)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_iff_hasPropertyS1_and_isRegularInCodimension_zero
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    IsReduced X ↔
      HasPropertySk X 1 ∧ IsRegularInCodimension X 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_iff_hasPropertySk_two_and_isRegularInCodimension_one
declarations.doc:
**Serre's criterion for normality, Stacks Project, Tag 0345.** A locally Noetherian scheme is
normal if and only if it satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)` and is regular in codimension one.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints_iff_hasPropertySk_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0346.** A coherent sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme has no
embedded associated points if and only if it satisfies Serre's condition `(S₁)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints_iff_hasPropertySk_one (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F ↔ SheafHasPropertySk X F 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0349.** A Zariski-local property of schemes which ascends along
flat morphisms of affine schemes and descends along the surjective ones is fpqc local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocal_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affine (P : ObjectProperty Scheme.{u})
    [ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage]
    (ascends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Flat f → P S → P X)
    (descends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Flat f → Surjective f → P X → P S) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_fppfPrecoverage_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0349.** A Zariski-local property of schemes which ascends along
flat morphisms of finite presentation of affine schemes and descends along the surjective
ones is fppf local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocal_fppfPrecoverage_of_affine (P : ObjectProperty Scheme.{u})
    [ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage]
    (ascends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Flat f → FinitePresentation f → P S → P X)
    (descends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Flat f → FinitePresentation f → Surjective f → P X → P S) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_etalePrecoverage_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0349.** A Zariski-local property of schemes which ascends along
étale morphisms of affine schemes and descends along the surjective ones is étale local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocal_etalePrecoverage_of_affine (P : ObjectProperty Scheme.{u})
    [ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage]
    (ascends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Etale f → P S → P X)
    (descends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Etale f → Surjective f → P X → P S) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.etalePrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_smoothPrecoverage_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0349.** A Zariski-local property of schemes which ascends along
smooth morphisms of affine schemes and descends along the surjective ones is smooth
local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocal_smoothPrecoverage_of_affine (P : ObjectProperty Scheme.{u})
    [ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage]
    (ascends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Smooth f → P S → P X)
    (descends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Smooth f → Surjective f → P X → P S) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal P (Scheme.precoverage @Smooth)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_syntomicPrecoverage_of_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0349.** A Zariski-local property of schemes which ascends along
syntomic morphisms of affine schemes and descends along the surjective ones is syntomic
local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocal_syntomicPrecoverage_of_affine (P : ObjectProperty Scheme.{u})
    [ObjectProperty.IsLocal P Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage]
    (ascends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Syntomic f → P S → P X)
    (descends : ∀ {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S),
      Syntomic f → Surjective f → P X → P S) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal P (Scheme.precoverage @Syntomic)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_isLocal_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 034C.** Being locally Noetherian is local for fppf coverings of
schemes.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyNoetherian_isLocal_fppf :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X)
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_isLocal_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 034E.** Reducedness of schemes is local for the smooth
precoverage.
declarations.statement:
instance isReduced_isLocal_smooth :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced X)
      (Scheme.precoverage @Smooth)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocal_isNormal_etalePrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 034F for the étale precoverage.** Normality of a scheme is a local object property
for `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etalePrecoverage`: a scheme étale over a normal scheme is normal,
and a scheme covered by normal schemes étale over it is normal.

The source states Lemma 034F for the smooth topology; the étale precoverage is what the
algebraic-spaces layer consumes, and both affine inputs — Stacks 033C for ascent and Stacks 033G
for descent — are the smooth ones, so nothing is lost by restricting.

This is item (7) of Remark 03E7: it is the instance that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_atlas_iff_forall_etale` needs in order to turn
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNormal` — Definition 03E6 at normality — from a some-chart condition

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.diagonalPullbackEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The comparison functor `Φ : I_{S/S'} ⥤ Δ ⊡ Δ` is an equivalence of categories, with explicit
quasi-inverse `Ψ`, unit coming from the equality `Ψ ∘ Φ = 𝟭` and counit the isomorphism with
component `(id, κ)`.
declarations.statement:
def diagonalPullbackEquivalence (F : S ⥤ S') :
    RelativeInertia F ≌ CategoricalPullback (diagonal F) (diagonal F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 034I.** An object of the relative inertia category `I_{S/S'}` for a
functor `F : S ⥤ S'`: a pair `(x, α)` with `α : Aut x` such that `F(α) = id_{F(x)}`.
The relative inertia `I_{S/S'}` (and the absolute inertia `I_S = I_{S/C}`) is the
fibred category built from this structure.
declarations.statement: structure RelativeInertia (F : S ⥤ S')

declarations.name: exists_prime_vCapD_singleton_isField_of_not_isJacobsonRing
declarations.doc:
(Non-Jacobson direction, Stacks 034J (1).) If `R` is not a Jacobson ring, then
there exist a prime ideal `p` and an element `f` such that `p` is not maximal,
`f ∉ p`, `V(p) ∩ D(f) = {p}`, and `(R/p)_f` is a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_prime_vCapD_singleton_isField_of_not_isJacobsonRing {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (hR : ¬ IsJacobsonRing R) :
    ∃ (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (f : R),
      (¬ p.asIdeal.IsMaximal) ∧
      (f ∉ p.asIdeal) ∧
      (vCapD p f = {p}) ∧
      IsField (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk p.asIdeal f))

declarations.name: vCapD_infinite_of_isJacobsonRing
declarations.doc:
(Jacobson direction, Stacks 034J (2).) If `R` is a Jacobson ring, then for every
prime ideal `p` that is not maximal and every element `f ∉ p`, the set
`V(p) ∩ D(f)` is infinite.
declarations.statement:
theorem vCapD_infinite_of_isJacobsonRing {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (hR : IsJacobsonRing R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (f : R)
    (hp : ¬ p.asIdeal.IsMaximal) (hf : f ∉ p.asIdeal) :
    (vCapD p f).Infinite

declarations.name: isIntegral_iff_isIntegral_localization_atPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 034K.** Let `φ : R → S` be a ring map and `x ∈ S`. Then `x` is integral
over `R` if and only if, for every maximal ideal `p ⊆ R`, the image `x_p` of `x` in `S_p`
is integral over `R_p` (where `R_p`, `S_p` are the localizations at `p` as above, and `S_p`
is regarded as an `R_p`-algebra via the induced map `φ_p : R_p → S_p`). Only the maximal
ideals are needed; for the all-primes equivalence as the tag states it, which this
implies, see `isIntegral_iff_forall_isPrime`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_iff_isIntegral_localization_atPrime
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (x : S) :
    IsIntegral R x ↔
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsMaximal], IsIntegral (Localization.AtPrime p)
        (algebraMap S (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S p.primeCompl)) x)

declarations.name: isIntegral_iff_forall_isPrime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 034K**, as the tag states it. Let `φ : R → S` be a ring map and `x ∈ S`.
Then `x` is integral over `R` if and only if, for *every* prime ideal `p ⊆ R`, the image
`x_p` of `x` in `S_p` is integral over `R_p`.

The substantive direction is `isIntegral_iff_isIntegral_localization_atPrime`, which needs
the hypothesis only at the maximal ideals; integrality at an arbitrary prime follows from
integrality over `R` by base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_iff_forall_isPrime (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (x : S) :
    IsIntegral R x ↔ ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsIntegral (Localization.AtPrime p)
      (algebraMap S (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid S p.primeCompl)) x)

declarations.name: integralClosure_isNormalDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 034L.** If `S` is a normal domain, then the integral closure of
`R` in `S` is a normal domain.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_isNormalDomain
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hS : IsNormalDomain S) :
    IsNormalDomain (integralClosure R S)

declarations.name: IsNormalRing.isIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
A normal ring `R` is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions
`Q(R) = FractionRing R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsNormalRing.isIntegrallyClosed
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (hR : IsNormalRing R) :
    IsIntegrallyClosed R

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.isReduced_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
The tensor product of a reduced `k`-algebra `R` with a geometrically reduced `k`-algebra `S`

declarations.statement:
public instance Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced.isReduced_tensorProduct
    (k R S : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsReduced R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k S] :
    IsReduced (R ⊗[k] S)
declarations.comment:
Stated with Mathlib's `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced` in place of the source's
  Definition 030S, the two being equivalent by Lemma 030V; as an instance, since both hypotheses
  are classes.

declarations.name: HasUniquePrimeIdealFactorization
declarations.doc:
The property that every nonzero ideal of `R` can be written as a product
of nonzero prime ideals, uniquely up to permutation.
declarations.statement: def HasUniquePrimeIdealFactorization (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.hasUniquePrimeIdealFactorization_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 034X**. For a ring `R` the following are equivalent:
1. `R` is a Dedekind domain in the sense of tag 034W: a domain in which every nonzero ideal is a
   product of nonzero prime ideals, uniquely up to permutation;
2. `R` is a Noetherian domain and `R_𝔪` is a discrete valuation ring for every nonzero maximal
   ideal `𝔪`;
3. `R` is a Noetherian normal domain of Krull dimension at most one.

In (2) the domain hypothesis is an existential binder, so that it is available as an instance
when stating that the localizations are discrete valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniquePrimeIdealFactorization_tfae (R : Type*) [CommRing R] :
    [IsDomain R ∧ HasUniquePrimeIdealFactorization R,
      ∃ _ : IsDomain R, IsNoetherianRing R ∧
        ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal], m ≠ ⊥ → IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime m),
      IsDomain R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed R ∧ ringKrullDim R ≤ 1].TFAE

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_faithfullyFlat_finitePresentation_model
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 034Y.** Let `R → A → B` be ring maps with `A → B` faithfully flat of finite
presentation. Then there are an `R`-algebra `A₀` of finite presentation and a faithfully flat
`A₀`-algebra `B₀` of finite presentation, with maps `A₀ → A` of `R`-algebras and `B₀ → B`
compatible with `A₀ → B₀` and `A → B`, such that `B = A ⊗_{A₀} B₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_faithfullyFlat_finitePresentation_model {R : Type v} {A B : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B] :
    ∃ (A₀ B₀ : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing A₀) (_ : CommRing B₀) (_ : Algebra R A₀)
      (_ : Algebra A₀ B₀) (_ : Algebra A₀ A) (_ : IsScalarTower R A₀ A) (_ : Algebra B₀ B)
      (_ : Algebra A₀ B) (_ : IsScalarTower A₀ A B) (_ : IsScalarTower A₀ B₀ B),
      Algebra.FinitePresentation R A₀ ∧ Module.FaithfullyFlat A₀ B₀ ∧
        Algebra.FinitePresentation A₀ B₀ ∧ Algebra.IsPushout A₀ A B₀ B
declarations.comment:
The diagram is the data `R → A₀ → A` with `IsScalarTower R A₀ A` (the left square)
and `A₀ → B₀ → B`, `A₀ → A → B` through a common `A₀ → B` (the right square); `B = A ⊗_{A₀} B₀` is
`Algebra.IsPushout A₀ A B₀ B`. The rings `A₀`, `B₀` live in the universe of `R`, `A` and `B`.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_faithfullyFlat_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 034Z.** Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map of finite presentation. Then there
is an `S`-algebra `S'` such that `R → S'` is quasi-finite, faithfully flat and of finite
presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_faithfullyFlat_finitePresentation
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S] :
    ∃ (S' : Type u) (_ : CommRing S') (_ : Algebra R S') (_ : Algebra S S')
      (_ : IsScalarTower R S S'), Algebra.QuasiFinite R S' ∧ Module.FaithfullyFlat R S' ∧
        Algebra.FinitePresentation R S'
declarations.comment:
The commutative triangle is the data `R → S → S'` with `IsScalarTower R S S'`;
quasi-finiteness (Definition 00PL) is `Algebra.QuasiFinite`, which omits the finite type clause of
the source's definition, supplied here by `Algebra.FinitePresentation`. `S'` lives in the universe
of `R` and `S`.

declarations.name: isUniversallyJapanese_of_finiteType_isN1
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0351.** Let `R` be a ring such that for every finite type ring map
`R → S` with `S` a domain, the domain `S` is N-1. Then `R` is universally Japanese.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyJapanese_of_finiteType_isN1 (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (H : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S], IsN1 S) :
    IsUniversallyJapaneseRing R

declarations.name: isNoetherianRing_and_min_le_depth_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0352.** Let `R → S` be a ring map. If it is faithfully flat and `S` is Noetherian
with property `(S_k)` — the depth of `S_𝔮` is at least `min{k, dim(S_𝔮)}` for every prime `𝔮` —
then `R` is Noetherian and has property `(S_k)`. The depth inequalities are read in
`WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNoetherianRing_and_min_le_depth_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] [IsNoetherianRing S] {k : ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime],
      min (k : WithBot ℕ∞) (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q)) ≤
        (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime q)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Localization.AtPrime q) :
            WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    IsNoetherianRing R ∧
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        min (k : WithBot ℕ∞) (ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p)) ≤
          (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p)) (Localization.AtPrime p) :
              WithBot ℕ∞)
declarations.comment: Property `(S_k)` is spelled out from Definition 031P as the inequality `min{k, dim(R_𝔭)} ≤ depth(R_𝔭)` at every prime, with `Module.depth` (tag 00LI) along the maximal ideal of `Localization.AtPrime 𝔭` and `ringKrullDim` for the dimension, as in tags 031Q and 031S, the inequality being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`; the ring map `R → S` is an `Algebra R S` instance and its faithful flatness is `Module.FaithfullyFlat R S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isNoetherianRing_and_isRegularLocalRing_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0353.** Let `R → S` be a ring map. If it is faithfully flat and `S` is Noetherian
with property `(R_k)` — the local ring `S_𝔮` is regular for every prime `𝔮` of height at most `k`
— then `R` is Noetherian and has property `(R_k)`. The bound `k` ranges over `ℕ∞`, the value `⊤`
giving the descent of regularity itself (tag 07NG).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNoetherianRing_and_isRegularLocalRing_atPrime_of_faithfullyFlat
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] [IsNoetherianRing S] {k : ℕ∞}
    (hS : ∀ (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime], q.height ≤ k →
      IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)) :
    IsNoetherianRing R ∧
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], p.height ≤ k →
        IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)
declarations.comment: Property `(R_k)` is spelled out from Definition 031P as the implication `height 𝔭 ≤ k → IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime 𝔭)`, with `Ideal.height` and `IsRegularLocalRing`, as in tag 031S; the source's `dim(R_𝔭) ≤ k` is `Ideal.height 𝔭 ≤ k` by `IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height`. The bound `k` is generalized from a non-negative integer to an element of `ℕ∞`, whose top value recovers tag 07NG. The ring map `R → S` is an `Algebra R S` instance and its faithful flatness is `Module.FaithfullyFlat R S`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.of_smooth_of_comap_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0354.** Let `R → S` be a ring map. If it is smooth and the induced map
`Spec S → Spec R` is surjective, and `S` is a Nagata ring — Noetherian, with every quotient
`S ⧸ q` by a prime N-2 — then `R` is a Nagata ring.

Smoothness is `Algebra.Smooth` (Definition 00T2), and together with surjectivity on spectra it is
equivalent to `R → S` being smooth and faithfully flat, by `Algebra.Smooth.flat` and
`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsNagataRing.of_smooth_of_comap_surjective {R S : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.Smooth R S]
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S)))
    (hS : IsNagataRing S) : IsNagataRing R
declarations.comment: Smoothness of the ring map `R → S` is `Algebra.Smooth R S` (Definition 00T2) for an `Algebra R S` instance, and surjectivity on spectra is surjectivity of `PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S)`; the pair is equivalent to smooth plus `Module.FaithfullyFlat R S`. Nagata is `IsNagataRing` of Definition 032R(2), whose Noetherian clause is part of the conclusion rather than a hypothesis on `R`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.exists_lift_subschemeι_iff_range_subset_support
declarations.doc:
A map from a reduced scheme factors through a closed subscheme precisely when its
set-theoretic image lies in the support of that subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_subschemeι_iff_range_subset_support {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsReduced Y] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    (∃ g : Y ⟶ I.subscheme, g ≫ I.subschemeι = f) ↔
      Set.range f ⊆ (I.support : Set X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.existsUnique_lift_nilradical_subschemeι
declarations.doc: Every map from a reduced scheme factors uniquely through the reduction of its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.existsUnique_lift_nilradical_subschemeι {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced Y]
    (f : Y ⟶ X) :
    ∃! g : Y ⟶ X.nilradical.subscheme, g ≫ X.nilradical.subschemeι = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNormal_iff_exists_iso_coproduct
declarations.doc:
A scheme whose quasi-compact open subspaces have finitely many irreducible components is
normal if and only if it is isomorphic to a coproduct of normal integral schemes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_iff_exists_iso_coproduct
    {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (hX : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    IsNormal X ↔
      ∃ (ι : Type u) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
          (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Y i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsIntegral (Y i)),
        Nonempty (X ≅ ∐ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNagataScheme_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_isPrecomplete

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isNagataScheme_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035B (4).** A scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind domain
whose fraction field has characteristic zero is a Nagata scheme: such a ring is Nagata by
Tag 0335 (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem isNagataScheme_of_locallyOfFiniteType_over_isDedekindDomain_of_charZero (R : Type u)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_totalQuotientSheaf_iso_pushforward
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible
components, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be the canonical morphism from the coproduct of the spectra of the
residue fields at the generic points of `X`. Then the sheaf of meromorphic functions of `X` is
`f_* 𝒪_Y`, as a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_totalQuotientSheaf_iso_pushforward [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃ e : X.totalQuotientSheaf.presheaf ≅
        (fromGenericPointResidueFields X).base _* (genericPointResidueSpectrum X).presheaf,
      X.toTotalQuotientSheaf.hom ≫ e.hom = (fromGenericPointResidueFields X).c
declarations.comment: K_X = f_* O_Y for X reduced

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.mem_range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_iff
declarations.doc:
A section of `A` over `U` lies in the integral closure of the structure sheaf exactly when
its germ at every point of `U` is integral over the local ring of `X` at that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_iff {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (A : X.QuasicoherentAlgebra) (U : Opens X) (s : A.right.presheaf.obj (.op U)) :
    s ∈ Set.range ((integralClosureAlgebraι A).right.hom.app (.op U)) ↔
      ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U),
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map A.hom.hom).hom.IsIntegralElem
          (A.right.presheaf.germ U x hx s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.isQuasicoherent_integralClosureAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The integral closure of the structure sheaf in a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras is
itself a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_X`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_integralClosureAlgebra {X : Scheme.{u}} (A : X.QuasicoherentAlgebra)
    [(underlyingModule A).IsQuasicoherent] :
    (underlyingModule (integralClosureAlgebra A)).IsQuasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.range_stalkFunctor_map_integralClosureAlgebraι
declarations.doc:
The stalk at `x` of the integral closure of the structure sheaf in `A` is the integral
closure of the local ring `𝒪_{X,x}` in the stalk `A_x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_stalkFunctor_map_integralClosureAlgebraι {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (A : X.QuasicoherentAlgebra) (x : X) :
    letI : Algebra ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).obj X.presheaf)
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).obj A.right.presheaf) :=
      ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map A.hom.hom).hom.toAlgebra
    Set.range (((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map
        (integralClosureAlgebraι A).right.hom).hom) =
      (integralClosure ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).obj X.presheaf)
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).obj A.right.presheaf) : Set _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuasicoherentAlgebra.range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
Over an affine open `U`, the sections of the integral closure of the structure sheaf in a
quasi-coherent `A` form the integral closure of `𝒪_X(U)` in `A(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_integralClosureAlgebraι_app_of_isAffineOpen {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (A : X.QuasicoherentAlgebra) [(underlyingModule A).IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : Opens X) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    letI : Algebra (X.presheaf.obj (.op U)) (A.right.presheaf.obj (.op U)) :=
      (A.hom.hom.app (.op U)).hom.toAlgebra
    Set.range ((integralClosureAlgebraι A).right.hom.app (.op U)) =
      (integralClosure (X.presheaf.obj (.op U)) (A.right.presheaf.obj (.op U)) : Set _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization_universalProperty_iff_existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
An integral factorization of a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism has the
universal property of relative normalization if and only if it is uniquely isomorphic
to the relative normalization, compatibly with both maps of the factorization.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalization_universalProperty_iff_existsUnique_iso
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (i : Y ⟶ Z) (p : Z ⟶ X) [IsIntegralHom p] (hip : i ≫ p = f) :
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (j : Y ⟶ T) (q : T ⟶ X),
      IsIntegralHom q → j ≫ q = f →
        ∃! k : Z ⟶ T, i ≫ k = j ∧ k ≫ q = p) ↔
      ∃! e : Z ≅ f.normalization,
        i ≫ e.hom = f.toNormalization ∧ e.hom ≫ f.fromNormalization = p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationDesc_universalProperty
declarations.doc:
Relative normalization is unchanged after replacing the target by an
intermediate scheme integral over it.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationDesc_universalProperty
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (p : Z ⟶ X) [IsIntegralHom p] (H : f = g ≫ p) :
    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (j : Y ⟶ T) (q : T ⟶ Z),
      IsIntegralHom q → j ≫ q = g →
        ∃! k : f.normalization ⟶ T,
          f.toNormalization ≫ k = j ∧
            k ≫ q = f.normalizationDesc g p H

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationMap
declarations.doc: The canonical morphism between relative normalizations induced by a commutative square.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def normalizationMap : f₂.normalization ⟶ f₁.normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toNormalization_normalizationMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism between normalizations commutes with the maps from the source
schemes.
declarations.statement:
lemma toNormalization_normalizationMap :
    f₂.toNormalization ≫ normalizationMap f₁ f₂ gY gX sq =
      gY ≫ f₁.toNormalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationMap_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
The canonical morphism between normalizations commutes with the maps to the target
schemes.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalizationMap_fromNormalization :
    normalizationMap f₁ f₂ gY gX sq ≫ f₁.fromNormalization =
      f₂.fromNormalization ≫ gX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationMap_unique
declarations.doc:
A morphism between the relative normalizations that makes both squares commute is the
canonical morphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma normalizationMap_unique (h : f₂.normalization ⟶ f₁.normalization)
    (h_source : f₂.toNormalization ≫ h = gY ≫ f₁.toNormalization)
    (h_target : h ≫ f₁.fromNormalization = f₂.fromNormalization ≫ gX) :
    h = normalizationMap f₁ f₂ gY gX sq

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationPullback
registrations.comment: the comparison morphism from the normalization of the base change to the base change of the normalization, for `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.instIsIsoNormalizationPullbackOfSmooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_sigma_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035L.** The normalization of `Y` in a normal scheme `X` whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components is a disjoint union of integral
normal schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_sigma_normalization [IsNormal X]
    (hX : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (Z : ι → Scheme.{u}) (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Z i))
        (_ : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral (Z i)), Nonempty (f.normalization ≅ ∐ Z)
declarations.comment: disjoint union of integral normal schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijOn_irreducibleComponents_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035L.** The dominant morphism from `X` to the normalization of `Y` in
`X` carries irreducible components to irreducible components bijectively.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijOn_irreducibleComponents_toNormalization [IsNormal X]
    (hX : ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    Set.BijOn (fun C ↦ closure (f.toNormalization.base '' C))
      (irreducibleComponents X) (irreducibleComponents f.normalization)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.genericPointResidueSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035M.** The coproduct of the spectra of the residue fields at the
generic points of the irreducible components of `X`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def genericPointResidueSpectrum (X : Scheme.{u}) : Scheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.fromGenericPointResidueFields
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035M.** The canonical morphism from the spectra of the residue fields
at the generic points of `X` to `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fromGenericPointResidueFields (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    genericPointResidueSpectrum X ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035N.** The normalization morphism of a scheme whose quasi-compact
opens have finitely many irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev normalization (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    normalizationScheme X hX ⟶ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationToReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035O.** The canonical factor of the normalization morphism of `X`
through the reduction of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalizationToReduction (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    X.normalizationScheme hX ⟶ X.nilradical.subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationToReduction_subschemeι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035O.** The normalization morphism of `X` is the composite of its
canonical factor through the reduction with the closed immersion of the reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationToReduction_subschemeι (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    X.normalizationToReduction hX ≫ X.nilradical.subschemeι = X.normalization hX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.existsUnique_iso_normalizationScheme_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035O.** The normalization of `X` is the normalization of the reduction
of `X`: the canonical factor of the normalization morphism of `X` through the reduction is
uniquely isomorphic, over the reduction, to the normalization morphism of the reduction,
compatibly with the morphisms from the generic-point residue spectra.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_normalizationScheme_reduction (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃! e : X.normalizationScheme hX ≅
        X.nilradical.subscheme.normalizationScheme
          (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reduction hX),
      (X.genericPointResidueSpectrumReductionIso.hom ≫ X.toNormalizationScheme hX) ≫ e.hom =
          X.nilradical.subscheme.toNormalizationScheme
            (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reduction hX) ∧
        e.hom ≫ X.nilradical.subscheme.normalization
            (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reduction hX) =
          X.normalizationToReduction hX
declarations.comment: an iso over the reduction with the normalization of the reduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationReductionIso_hom_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035O.** The isomorphism of the normalization of `X` with the
normalization of the reduction of `X` is an isomorphism over the reduction: it carries the
normalization morphism of the reduction to the canonical factor of the normalization morphism of
`X` through the reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationReductionIso_hom_normalization (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    (X.normalizationReductionIso hX).hom ≫
        X.nilradical.subscheme.normalization
          (X.finite_irreducibleComponents_reduction hX) =
      X.normalizationToReduction hX
declarations.comment: the iso of X^nu with (X_red)^nu is over X_red

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.preimageNormalizationIsoSpecIntegralClosure_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
Under `AlgebraicGeometry.preimageNormalizationIsoSpecIntegralClosure`, the restriction of the
normalization morphism is the spectrum map induced by the inclusion into the integral closure.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimageNormalizationIsoSpecIntegralClosure_hom_comp
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ V : X.Opens,
      IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (U : X.Opens)
    (e : Spec (.of A) ≅ U.toScheme) :
    (preimageNormalizationIsoSpecIntegralClosure hX U e).hom ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A (integralClosure A (FractionRing A)))) =
      (Scheme.normalization X hX ∣_ U) ≫ e.inv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_minimalPrimes_of_affine_open
declarations.doc:
If every quasi-compact open of a scheme has finitely many irreducible components,
then a ring presenting an affine open of that scheme has finitely many minimal primes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_minimalPrimes_of_affine_open
    {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (hX : ∀ (V : X.Opens), IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (U : X.Opens) (e : Spec (.of A) ≅ (U : Scheme)) :
    (minimalPrimes A).Finite

declarations.name: minimalPrimes.totalFractionRing_algEquiv_pi_fractionRing_quotient
declarations.doc:
The total ring of fractions of a reduced ring with finitely many minimal primes is the
product of the fraction fields of its minimal-prime quotients.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalFractionRing_algEquiv_pi_fractionRing_quotient
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (hA : (minimalPrimes A).Finite) :
    letI : (p : minimalPrimes A) → Algebra A (FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A))) :=
      fun p => ((algebraMap (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)) (FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)))).comp
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (p : Ideal A))).toAlgebra
    Nonempty (FractionRing A ≃ₐ[A]
      (∀ p : minimalPrimes A, FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A))))

declarations.name: minimalPrimes.integralClosure_fractionRing_algEquiv_pi_quotient
declarations.doc:
The integral closure of a reduced ring in its total fraction ring is the product of the
integral closures of its minimal-prime quotients in their fraction fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_fractionRing_algEquiv_pi_quotient
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (hA : (minimalPrimes A).Finite) :
    letI : (p : minimalPrimes A) →
        Algebra A
          (integralClosure (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)) (FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)))) :=
      fun p =>
        ((algebraMap (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A))
          (integralClosure (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A))
            (FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A))))).comp
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (p : Ideal A))).toAlgebra
    Nonempty
      (integralClosure A (FractionRing A) ≃ₐ[A]
        (∀ p : minimalPrimes A,
          integralClosure (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)) (FractionRing (A ⧸ (p : Ideal A)))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_iso_sigma_isIntegral_isNormal_normalizationScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035Q.** The normalization of a scheme whose quasi-compact opens have
finitely many irreducible components is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes: it is
isomorphic to the coproduct of the normalizations of its reduced irreducible components, and
each of those is integral and normal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_sigma_isIntegral_isNormal_normalizationScheme
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
        (_ : ∀ i, IsNormal (Y i)) (_ : ∀ i, IsIntegral (Y i)),
      Nonempty (X.normalizationScheme hX ≅ ∐ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_normalizationFactorization_of_integral_of_birational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035Q.** An integral morphism which is birational over every
quasi-compact open does not change the normalization.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizationFactorization_of_integral_of_birational
    {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) →
      (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) (α : X' ⟶ X) [IsIntegralHom α]
    (hcomponents : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) →
      (irreducibleComponents (α ⁻¹ᵁ U)).Finite)
    (hbirational : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) →
      IsBirational (α ∣_ U)) :
    ∃ (hX' : ∀ V : X'.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X') →
        (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
      (g : Scheme.normalizationScheme X hX ⟶ X')
      (e : Scheme.normalizationScheme X hX ≅
        Scheme.normalizationScheme X' hX'),
      g ≫ α = Scheme.normalization X hX ∧
        e.hom ≫ Scheme.normalization X' hX' = g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIntegralHom_surjective_bijOn_irreducibleComponents_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035Q.** Part (2). Let `X` be a scheme such that every quasi-compact
open of `X` has finitely many irreducible components. Then the normalization morphism
`ν : X^ν ⟶ X` is integral, it is surjective, and it induces a bijection on irreducible
components: sending an irreducible component of `X^ν` to the closure of its image under `ν` is a
bijection onto the set of irreducible components of `X`.

Integrality is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIntegralHom_normalization` (Tag 035I), surjectivity
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.surjective_normalization`, and the bijection on components is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.bijOn_irreducibleComponents_normalization`, which rests on Tags 035O
and 0BXC.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_surjective_bijOn_irreducibleComponents_normalization
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    IsIntegralHom (X.normalization hX) ∧ Surjective (X.normalization hX) ∧
      Set.BijOn (fun D ↦ closure ((X.normalization hX).base '' D))
        (irreducibleComponents (X.normalizationScheme hX)) (irreducibleComponents X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.existsUnique_lift_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035Q part (4).** A morphism to `X` from a normal scheme each of whose
irreducible components dominates an irreducible component of `X` factors uniquely through the
normalization of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_normalization {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (f : Z ⟶ X) [IsNormal Z]
    (hgeneric : ∀ η : genericPoints Z, f η.1 ∈ genericPoints X) :
    ∃! g : Z ⟶ X.normalizationScheme hX, g ≫ X.normalization hX = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalization_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035R.** The normalization morphism of an integral Japanese scheme is
finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalization_isFinite (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    (hX : IsJapaneseScheme X) :
    let hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens,
        IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite := by
      intro U _
      cases isEmpty_or_nonempty U with
      | inl hU =>
          rw [Set.finite_def]
          let : IsEmpty U := hU
          exact ⟨⟨∅, fun C ↦ isEmptyElim (C.2.1.nonempty.some)⟩⟩
      | inr hU =>
          let : Nonempty U := hU
          rw [irreducibleComponents_eq_singleton]
          exact Set.finite_singleton _
    IsFinite (Scheme.normalization X hfinite)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isFinite_normalization_of_isNagataScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035S.** The normalization morphism `ν : X^ν ⟶ X` of a Nagata scheme
`X` is finite.

A Nagata scheme is locally Noetherian, so each of its quasi-compact opens is a Noetherian space
and has finitely many irreducible components; the Nagata hypothesis therefore both forms the
normalization morphism and makes it finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_normalization_of_isNagataScheme {X : Scheme.{u}} (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X) :
    IsFinite (X.normalization (finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNagataScheme X hNagata))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationGluedSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035T.** The normalization of a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact
opens have finitely many irreducible components, carrying the charts that present it as a
relative spectrum of the integral closure of `𝒪_X` in the sheaf of meromorphic functions.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationGluedSpectrum (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    GluedSpectrum (X.meromorphicIntegralClosureSituation hfinite)
declarations.comment: the normalization carries the charts of the relative spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationIsoMeromorphicSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035T.** For a reduced scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely
many irreducible components, the normalization is the relative spectrum of the integral closure
`𝒪'` of `𝒪_X` in the sheaf of meromorphic functions.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationIsoMeromorphicSpectrum (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    X.normalizationScheme hfinite ≅
      (gluedSpectrum (X.meromorphicIntegralClosureSituation hfinite)).scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.normalizationIsoMeromorphicSpectrum_hom_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035T.** The comparison isomorphism lies over `X`: the normalization
morphism `ν : X^ν ⟶ X` is the structure morphism of the relative spectrum of `𝒪'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationIsoMeromorphicSpectrum_hom_toBase (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (hfinite : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    (normalizationIsoMeromorphicSpectrum X hfinite).hom ≫
        (gluedSpectrum (X.meromorphicIntegralClosureSituation hfinite)).toBase =
      X.normalization hfinite
declarations.comment: the normalization is the structure morphism of the relative spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyReducedOver
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 035V].** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a scheme over `k`, given by its
structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`.

1. `X` is *geometrically reduced at* a point `x ∈ X` if for any field extension `k'/k` and any
   point `x'` of `X_{k'}` lying over `x` the local ring `𝒪_{X_{k'}, x'}` is reduced. That
   pointwise condition is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x`, the body of this
   definition under its quantifier: the base change `X_{k'}` is the pullback of `f` along
   `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`, and `x'` lies over `x` when the first projection sends it to `x`.
2. `X` is *geometrically reduced over `k`* if it is geometrically reduced at every point of
   `X`, which is exactly what this definition says.

Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyReduced` is the notion of part (2) for an arbitrary
base, defined by reducedness of every field-valued base change rather than pointwise; over a
field the two agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_iff_forall_isGeometricallyReducedAt`, so the results
stated for it — such as `AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced` over a perfect
field — apply to this predicate as well.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGeometricallyReducedOver {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_isGeometricallyReduced_stalk
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is geometrically reduced at a point if and only if its local ring at
that point is geometrically reduced over the field.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_isGeometricallyReduced_stalk
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x ↔
      let : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
        let : Algebra k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)) :=
          StructureSheaf.stalkAlgebra k (f.base x)
        ((f.stalkMap x).hom.comp
          (algebraMap k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)))).toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k (X.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035X.** The seven standard characterizations of geometric reducedness
for a scheme over a field are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (kperf : Type u) [Field kperf] [Algebra k kperf] [ExpChar kperf p]
    [PerfectRing kperf p] [IsPerfectClosure (algebraMap k kperf) p]
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsAlgClosure k K] :
    let isReducedAfterBaseChange := fun (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] ↦
      IsReduced (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))
    let geometricallyReducedSections := fun U : X.Opens ↦
      letI : Algebra k Γ(X, U) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced k Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE
      [ GeometricallyReduced f,
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'], isReducedAfterBaseChange k',
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
          [IsPurelyInseparable k k'], isReducedAfterBaseChange k',
        isReducedAfterBaseChange (AdjoinPthRoots k),
        isReducedAfterBaseChange kperf,
        isReducedAfterBaseChange K,
        ∀ U : X.affineOpens, geometricallyReducedSections U.1 ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 035Y.** For a scheme over a field of positive characteristic,
geometric reducedness at a point is equivalent to reducedness of the local rings above that
point after every finite purely inseparable extension, after adjoining all `p`-th roots, or
after passing to a perfect closure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_tfae
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : p ≠ 0)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) :
    [IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x,
      ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
          [IsPurelyInseparable k k'],
        let g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
        ∀ x' : (pullback f g : Scheme), pullback.fst f g x' = x →
          _root_.IsReduced ((pullback f g).presheaf.stalk x'),
      let g : Spec (.of (AdjoinPthRoots k)) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AdjoinPthRoots k)))
      ∀ x' : (pullback f g : Scheme), pullback.fst f g x' = x →
        _root_.IsReduced ((pullback f g).presheaf.stalk x'),
      let g : Spec (.of (perfectClosure k (AlgebraicClosure k))) ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap k (perfectClosure k (AlgebraicClosure k))))
      ∀ x' : (pullback f g : Scheme), pullback.fst f g x' = x →
        _root_.IsReduced ((pullback f g).presheaf.stalk x')].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_stalk_pullback_of_isGeometricallyReducedAt
declarations.doc:
A product with a reduced scheme is reduced at every point above a geometrically reduced
point of the other factor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_stalk_pullback_of_isGeometricallyReducedAt
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X)
    (hX : IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x) [IsReduced Y]
    (z : (pullback f g : Scheme)) (hz : pullback.fst f g z = x) :
    _root_.IsReduced ((pullback f g).presheaf.stalk z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_pullback
declarations.doc:
The fibre product of a geometrically reduced scheme and a reduced scheme over a field is
reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_pullback
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [IsReduced Y] :
    IsReduced (pullback f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_pullback_over_field
declarations.doc:
The fibre product over a field of two geometrically reduced schemes is geometrically
reduced.
declarations.statement:

    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyReduced f] [GeometricallyReduced g] :
    GeometricallyReduced (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReduced_pullback_over_perfectField

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_open_geometricallyReduced_of_isGeometricallyReducedAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0360.** A locally Noetherian scheme that is geometrically reduced at a

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_fpqc_of_affine_descent
declarations.doc:
A property of morphisms of schemes which is Zariski local on the source and on the target,
which is preserved by precomposition with flat morphisms, and which descends along surjective
flat morphisms of affine schemes, is fpqc local on the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtSource_fpqc_of_affine_descent (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    [P.RespectsLeft (@Flat.{u})] [IsZariskiLocalAtSource P] [IsZariskiLocalAtTarget P]
    (hAffine : ∀ {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
      (g : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y), Surjective g → Flat g → P (g ≫ f) → P f) :
    P.IsLocalAtSource Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.statement:

    (hAffine : ∀ {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
      (g : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y), Surjective g → Syntomic g → P (g ≫ f) → P f) :
    P.IsLocalAtSource (Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic.{u}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_of_standard_descent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 036I.** In condition (4) of Tag 036H one may assume that the morphism
is a (surjective) *standard smooth* morphism when `τ = smooth`, a (surjective) *standard
syntomic* morphism when `τ = syntomic`, and a (surjective) *standard étale* morphism when
`τ = étale`.

The three conjuncts are the statements of the smooth, syntomic and étale cases of Tag 036H with
condition (4) so strengthened; they are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_smooth_of_standard_descent`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_syntomic_of_standard_descent` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalAtSource_etale_of_standard_descent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalAtSource_of_standard_descent :
    (∀ (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) [P.RespectsLeft (@Smooth.{u})]
        [IsZariskiLocalAtSource P] [IsZariskiLocalAtTarget P],
        (∀ {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
          (g : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y), Surjective g → IsStandardSmooth g → P (g ≫ f) → P f) →
        P.IsLocalAtSource (Scheme.precoverage (@Smooth.{u}))) ∧
      (∀ (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) [P.RespectsLeft (@Syntomic.{u})]
        [IsZariskiLocalAtSource P] [IsZariskiLocalAtTarget P],
        (∀ {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
          (g : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y), Surjective g → IsStandardSyntomic g → P (g ≫ f) → P f) →
        P.IsLocalAtSource (Scheme.precoverage (@Syntomic.{u}))) ∧
      ∀ (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) [P.RespectsLeft (@Etale.{u})]
        [IsZariskiLocalAtSource P] [IsZariskiLocalAtTarget P],
        (∀ {X' X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X'] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y]
          (g : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y), Surjective g → IsStandardEtale g → P (g ≫ f) → P f) →
        P.IsLocalAtSource Scheme.etalePrecoverage

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.isStack
declarations.doc:
The relative inertia `I_{𝒮/𝒮'}` of a 1-morphism `F` of stacks over the site `(𝒞, J)`, with its
structure functor `π ⋙ p`, is a stack over `𝒞`; taking `F = p` and `p' = 𝟭 𝒞`, so is the absolute
inertia `I_𝒮`.

Only the fibredness half of the conclusion is proved, from Stacks 034H (2); the descent of
morphisms and the effectivity of descent for the inertia are the hypotheses `hmor` and
`heff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack (hp : p.IsStack J) (_hp' : p'.IsStack J) (hF : p.IsFibredOneMorphism p' F)
    (hmor : haveI : (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p).IsFibered :=
        RelativeInertia.isFibered F p p' hp.isFibered hF
      ∀ (U : 𝒞) (x y : (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p).Fiber U),
        Functor.IsMorSheaf (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J U x y)
    (heff : haveI : (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p).IsFibered :=
        RelativeInertia.isFibered F p p' hp.isFibered hF
      Functor.HasEffectiveDescent (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J) :
    Functor.IsStack (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.isStack_and_fiber_isGroupoid
declarations.doc:
If `𝒮` and `𝒮'` are stacks in groupoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`, then so is the relative inertia
`I_{𝒮/𝒮'}`; taking `F = p` and `p' = 𝟭 𝒞`, so is the absolute inertia `I_𝒮`.

Being a stack in groupoids is written out as being a stack with groupoid fibres; the stack
condition on the inertia is the hypothesis `hst`, which is part (1), and what is proved here is
the remaining content, that the fibres of the inertia are groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_and_fiber_isGroupoid (_hp : p.IsStack J) (hgp : ∀ U, IsGroupoid (p.Fiber U))
    (_hp' : p'.IsStack J) (_hgp' : ∀ U, IsGroupoid (p'.Fiber U))
