    (hst : Functor.IsStack (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J) :
    Functor.IsStack (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J ∧
      ∀ U, IsGroupoid ((RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p).Fiber U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.RelativeInertia.isStackInSetoids
declarations.doc:
If `𝒮` and `𝒮'` are stacks in setoids over the site `(𝒞, J)`, then so is the relative inertia
`I_{𝒮/𝒮'}`; taking `F = p` and `p' = 𝟭 𝒞`, so is the absolute inertia `I_𝒮`.

The stack condition on the inertia is the hypothesis `hst`, which is part (1); what is proved
here is the remaining content, that the fibres of the inertia are setoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStackInSetoids (hp : p.IsStackInSetoids J) (_hp' : p'.IsStackInSetoids J)
    (hst : Functor.IsStack (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p) J) :
    (RelativeInertia.π F ⋙ p).IsStackInSetoids J

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.TorsorWithMap.projection_isStackInGroupoids_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0370**: in Situation 04WL the projection `p : [[X/G]] ⟶ (Sch/S)_fppf` is a stack
in groupoids for the fppf topology.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.TorsorWithMap.projection_isStackInGroupoids_unconditional` with
`hB` and `G` explicit. The argument `hX` is part of Situation 04WL: `[[X/G]]` is formed for an
arbitrary object `X` of `Over B`, and the situation asks that it be an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isStackInGroupoids_of_isAlgebraicSpace (X : Over B) [ModObj G.obj.X X]
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) :
    Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (projection hB G X) (BigFppfOver.topology 𝒞 S hS)
declarations.comment: in Situation 04WL: the projection of [[X/G]] is a stack in groupoids for the fppf topology, with hB and G explicit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.TorsorWithMap.projection_isStackInGroupoids_unconditional
declarations.doc:
In Situation 04WL the projection `p : [[X/G]] ⟶ (Sch/S)_fppf` is a stack in groupoids for the
fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isStackInGroupoids_unconditional
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace 𝒞 S hS X.left) :
    Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{w} (projection hB G X) (BigFppfOver.topology 𝒞 S hS)
declarations.comment: in Situation 04WL: the projection of [[X/G]] is a stack in groupoids for the fppf topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0371.** An object of the quotient `[[X/G]]` of a sheaf `X` by an abstract group
`G`: an object `U` of `(Sch/S)_fppf`, a torsor on `(Sch/U)_fppf` under the constant sheaf of
groups with value `G`, and a `G`-equivariant map of sheaves from it to `X`.
declarations.statement: structure AbstractGroupQuotientStack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.Hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0371.** A morphism `(U, P, φ) ⟶ (U', P', φ')` of the quotient `[[X/G]]`: a
morphism `f : U ⟶ U'` of `(Sch/S)_fppf` together with a `G`-equivariant isomorphism
`g : P → f^{-1}P'` of torsors under the constant sheaf of groups with value `G`, compatible
with `φ` and `φ'`. The isomorphism is recorded on total spaces: `g` is a map of sheaves on
`(Sch/S)_fppf` over `f` restricting to a bijection from the fibre of `P` over each
`a : V ⟶ U` to the fibre of `P'` over `a ≫ f`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (A A' : AbstractGroupQuotientStack B S hS G X ρ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.instCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0371.** The quotient `[[X/G]]` of a sheaf `X` by an abstract group `G` is a
category: morphisms compose by composing `f` and `g`.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category (AbstractGroupQuotientStack B S hS G X ρ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0371.** The functor `[[X/G]] ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` sending a triple `(U, P, φ)` to
`U`, which is how `[[X/G]]` is regarded as a category over the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
def projection :
    AbstractGroupQuotientStack B S hS G X ρ ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS
declarations.comment: the functor to the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_abstractGroupQuotientStack
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be an abstract group whose constant group scheme `G_S` lies in the big fppf site,
`X` an algebraic space over `S` and `ρ : G →* Aut X` an action. Then the stack `[[X/G]]` of
triples `(U, P, φ)`, `P` a torsor under the constant sheaf `G` on `(Sch/U)_fppf` and
`φ : P → X` equivariant, is equivalent over `(Sch/S)_fppf` to the stack `[[X/G_S]]`, for `G_S`
the constant group algebraic space `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.constantGroupSpace` acting on `X`
through `ρ` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.constGSModObj`, whose constant sections act as `ρ` does by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.constGS_isCompatibleAction`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_isEquivalenceOver_abstractGroupQuotientStack :
    letI : ModObj (constantGroupSpace 𝒞 S hS G (baseS 𝒞 S hS) (isAlgebraicSpace_baseS 𝒞 S hS)
        hG).obj.X (overBaseS X₀) := constGSModObj hG hX.isSheaf ρ₀
    ∃ F : TorsorWithMap (isAlgebraicSpace_baseS 𝒞 S hS)
        (constantGroupSpace 𝒞 S hS G (baseS 𝒞 S hS) (isAlgebraicSpace_baseS 𝒞 S hS) hG)
        (overBaseS X₀) ⥤
      AbstractGroupQuotientStack.{max t (u + 1)} 𝒞 S hS G (X₀ ⋙ uliftFunctor.{max t (u + 1)})
        (uliftAction.{max t (u + 1)} ρ₀),
      Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver
        (TorsorWithMap.projection (isAlgebraicSpace_baseS 𝒞 S hS)
          (constantGroupSpace 𝒞 S hS G (baseS 𝒞 S hS) (isAlgebraicSpace_baseS 𝒞 S hS) hG)
          (overBaseS X₀))
        AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection_isStackInGroupoids
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0371.** For an algebraic space `X` over `S` with an action `ρ : G →* Aut X` of an
abstract group `G`, the functor `[[X/G]] ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection` turns `[[X/G]]` into a stack in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`.

This is the assertion of the remark, under exactly its standing hypothesis that `X` is an
algebraic space over `S`: nothing beyond the sheaf condition for `X` is used, and the three
conditions of Stacks 02ZI are proved outright, with the stack property of the torsors under
the constant sheaf of groups supplied by Stacks 04UK rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem projection_isStackInGroupoids
    (hX : Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{max t (u + 1)} B S hS X) :
    Functor.IsStackInGroupoids.{w}
      (projection : AbstractGroupQuotientStack.{max t (u + 1)} B S hS G X ρ ⥤
        BigFppfOver B S hS) (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
declarations.comment: [[X/G]] is a stack in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantGroupSheafRepresentedByConstantGroupScheme_bigFppf
registrations.comment: the constant sheaf G is representable by G_S on (Sch/S)_fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardObject
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the objects of `Picardstack_{X/B}`.**  A triple `(U, b, L)`: a scheme `U` of
the site with a morphism `b : U ⟶ B` to the base, and an invertible module `L` on the base
change `X_U`.
declarations.statement: structure PicardObject (s : PicardSituation B S hS)
declarations.comment: the objects of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the morphisms of `Picardstack_{X/B}`.**  A pair `(f, g)`: a morphism
`f : U ⟶ U'` of schemes over the base, and an isomorphism `g : f^*L' ⟶ L` of modules on
`X_U`.
declarations.statement: structure PicardHom {s : PicardSituation B S hS} (A C : PicardObject s)
declarations.comment: the morphisms of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom.id
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the identity of an object.**  The identity of its pair `(U, b)`, with the
unit law `(X_{𝟙 U})^* ≅ 𝟭` of Stacks 03LU as its comparison of modules.
declarations.statement: def id (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) (A : PicardObject s) : PicardHom A A
declarations.comment: the identity, conditional on the pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom.comp
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the composition `(f, g)` with `(f', g')` is `(f' ∘ f, g ∘ f^*(g'))`.**  The
composite of the base maps, with the inverse image of the second comparison followed by the
first, read through the comparison of Stacks 03LU for the composite.
declarations.statement: def comp (m : PicardHom A C) (n : PicardHom C D) : PicardHom A D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom.id_comp
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the identity law at the source.**  Composing a morphism of
`Picardstack_{X/B}` with the identity of its source returns it.
declarations.statement:
theorem id_comp (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) {A C : PicardObject s}
    (m : PicardHom A C) : PicardHom.comp (PicardHom.id hc A) m = m
declarations.comment: the identity law at the source for the composition of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom.comp_id
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the identity law at the target.**  Composing a morphism of
`Picardstack_{X/B}` with the identity of its target returns it.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_id (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) {A C : PicardObject s}
    (m : PicardHom A C) : PicardHom.comp m (PicardHom.id hc C) = m
declarations.comment: the identity law at the target for the composition of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardHom.comp_assoc
declarations.doc: **Section 0372, associativity.**  The composition of `Picardstack_{X/B}` is associative.
declarations.comment: associativity of the composition of the Picard stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardCategory
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the category `Picardstack_{X/B}`.**  The objects are the triples `(U, b, L)`,
the morphisms are the pairs `(f, g)` of a morphism of test schemes over the base and an
isomorphism `f^*L' ≅ L`, and the identities and the composition are the ones of Section 0372.
declarations.statement:
def picardCategory (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) (s : PicardSituation B S hS) :
    Category.{u + 1} (PicardObject s)
declarations.comment: the category Picardstack_{X/B}, conditional on the pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU that its identity already needs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardProjection
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372, the functor `p`.**  The projection of `Picardstack_{X/B}` to the test schemes
over the base, forgetting the invertible module.
declarations.comment: the projection of the Picard stack to the test schemes over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.picardCategoryData
declarations.doc:
**Section 0372.**  The category `Picardstack_{X/B}` together with its projection satisfies
the specification `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardCategoryData`: its hom-sets, identities,
composition and projection are the ones of Section 0372.
declarations.statement:
def picardCategoryData (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS)
    (s : PicardSituation B S hS) : PicardCategoryData hc s
declarations.comment: a value of the specification of the category Picardstack_{X/B} with its projection, conditional on the pseudofunctoriality of the direct images of Stacks 03LU

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The fixed-point scheme `Y^g = {y ∈ Y | g(y) = y}` of the automorphism
of `Y` attached to a group element `g`, as the fibre product
`Y^g = Y ×_{(1, 1), Y ×_S Y, (g, 1)} Y` displayed in the source.
declarations.statement: def fixedScheme (Y : Over S) (a : G →* Aut Y) (g : G) : Over S
declarations.comment: the fixed-point scheme X^g as the displayed fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedSchemeHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The fibre product `Y ×_{(1, 1), Y ×_S Y, (g, 1)} Y` is the locus
`Y^g = {y ∈ Y | g(y) = y}`: its `T`-points are exactly the `T`-points of `Y` fixed by the
automorphism attached to `g`.
declarations.statement:
def fixedSchemeHomEquiv (Y : Over S) (a : G →* Aut Y) (g : G) (T : Over S) :
    (T ⟶ fixedScheme S G Y a g) ≃ {x : T ⟶ Y // x ≫ (a g).asIso.hom = x}
declarations.comment: X^g = {x ∈ X | g(x) = x} as a functor of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedSchemeAut
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The action of `G` on the fixed-point scheme `Y^g` induced by the action
on `Y`. It is here that commutativity of `G` enters: for `h ∈ G` the automorphism of `Y`
attached to `h` commutes with the one attached to `g`, hence preserves `Y^g`.
declarations.statement:
def fixedSchemeAut (Y : Over S) (a : G →* Aut Y) (g : G) :
    G →* Aut (fixedScheme S G Y a g)
declarations.comment: the induced action of G on X^g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.totalToTarget_factorsThroughFixedScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The source's sentence "the condition that `φ ∘ α = φ` means that `φ`
factors through the inclusion of `Y^g` in `Y`": for an object of `[Y/G]` whose equivariant
map is fixed by `g`, every value of that map factors uniquely through `Y^g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem totalToTarget_factorsThroughFixedScheme (g : G)
    (A : schemeQuotient.{t} B S hS G Y a)
    (hA : ∀ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ) (p : A.Total V),
      (schemePointsAut B S hS G Y a g).asIso.hom.app V (A.totalToTarget V p) =
        A.totalToTarget V p)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ) (p : A.Total V) :
    ∃! y : (Over.post B.inclusion).obj V.unop ⟶ fixedScheme S G Y a g,
      y ≫ fixedSchemeIncl S G Y a g = A.totalToTarget V p
declarations.comment: φ ∘ α = φ makes φ factor through the inclusion of X^g in X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedQuotientToInertia
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The morphism `[Y^g/G] → I_{[Y/G]}` of the source: a torsor `P` with a
`G`-equivariant map `ψ : P → Y^g` goes to the triple `(P, ι ∘ ψ)` together with the
automorphism given by multiplication by `g` on `P`.
declarations.comment: the g-th summand of the morphism to the inertia stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.inertiaComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The morphism `∐_{g ∈ G} [Y^g/G] → I_{[Y/G]}` of the source, assembled
from its summands. On `T`-points it is the source's recipe: a `G`-torsor `P → T` with a
`G`-equivariant `ψ : P → Y^g` is sent to `(P, ι ∘ ψ, α)` with `α` multiplication by `g`.
declarations.comment: the morphism from the disjoint union of the [X^g/G] to the inertia stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AbstractGroupQuotientStack.inertiaComparison_comp_struct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The comparison morphism is a morphism *over* `(Sch/S)_fppf`: on each
summand, composing it with the structure functor of the inertia gives back the projection of
`[Y^g/G]` to the site, since neither the inclusion `Y^g → Y` nor remembering the
automorphism `α` changes the object of the site attached to a triple.
declarations.statement:
lemma inertiaComparison_comp_struct (g : G) :
    Sigma.incl g ⋙ inertiaComparison.{t} B S hS G Y a ⋙
        relativeInertiaStruct (schemeQuotientProjection.{t} B S hS G Y a)
          (schemeQuotientProjection.{t} B S hS G Y a) =
      schemeQuotientProjection.{t} B S hS G (fixedScheme S G Y a g)
        (fixedSchemeAut Y a g)
declarations.comment: the comparison is a morphism over the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertia_equivalence_stackCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** Let `S` be a scheme, `G` a commutative group, `Y → S` a scheme over `S` and
`a : G →* Aut_S(Y)` an action of `G` on `Y`. Then the inertia stack of `[Y/G]` is the coproduct of
stacks `I_{[Y/G]} = ∐_{g ∈ G} [Y^g/G]`, where `Y^g = Y ×_{(1, 1), Y ×_S Y, (g, 1)} Y` is the
fixed-point scheme of `g` (`AlgebraicGeometry.fixedScheme`) with the action of `G` induced by
`a`: there is an equivalence of categories over `(Sch/S)_fppf` (a quasi-inverse over
`(Sch/S)_fppf` with unit and counit lying over identities) from the coproduct of stacks
`∐_{g ∈ G} [Y^g/G]` to `I_{[Y/G]}`, whose restriction to the `g`-th summand `[Y^g/G]` is the
canonical functor of the source, sending a torsor `P` with an equivariant map `P → Y^g` to `P`
with the composite map to `Y` and the automorphism given by multiplication by `g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertia_equivalence_stackCoproduct :
    ∃ H : Functor.StackCoproduct
        (fun g : G => schemeQuotientProjection.{max (u + 1) t} B S hS G (fixedScheme S G Y a g)
          (fixedSchemeAut Y a g))
        (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (fun _ => projection_isFiberedInGroupoids) ⥤
        AbsoluteInertia (schemeQuotientProjection.{max (u + 1) t} B S hS G Y a),
      Nonempty (Functor.IsEquivalenceOver (Functor.stackCoproductProj _ _ _)
        (schemeInertiaProj.{max (u + 1) t} B S hS G Y a) H) ∧
      ∀ g : G, Nonempty (Functor.stackCoproductι _ _ _ g ⋙ H ≅
        fixedQuotientToInertia.{max (u + 1) t} B S hS G Y a g)
declarations.comment: I_{[X/G]} = ∐_{g ∈ G} [X^g/G]: an equivalence over (Sch/S)_fppf from the coproduct of stacks to the inertia stack, restricting on each summand to the canonical functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_fixedPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The fixed subpresheaf `X^σ` is the fibre product
`X ×_{(1,1), X × X, (σ,1)} X` displayed in the source. On presheaves over the big fppf site
of `S` the binary product is the fibre product over `S`, as `S` is the terminal object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_fixedPresheaf (σ : X ⟶ X) :
    IsPullback (fixedPresheafIncl σ) (fixedPresheafIncl σ)
      (prod.lift (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)) (prod.lift σ (𝟙 X))
declarations.comment: the fixed locus as a fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedPresheafAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** Because `G` is commutative, its action on `X` restricts to an action
on the fixed locus `X^g`. This is what makes the quotient `[X^g/G]` of the source's formula
meaningful.
declarations.statement: def fixedPresheafAction (ρ : G →* Aut X) (g : G) : G →* Aut (fixedPresheaf (ρ g).asIso.hom)
declarations.comment: the induced action on the fixed locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixedQuotientStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The quotient `[X^g/G]` of the fixed locus `X^g` by `G`, formed by the
construction of Stacks 0371 applied to `X^g` with its induced action.
declarations.statement: abbrev fixedQuotientStack (g : G) : Type _
declarations.comment: the quotient of the fixed locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaSummand
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The canonical functor `[X^g/G] ⥤ I_{[X/G]}`: a torsor with an
equivariant map to `X^g` is sent to the same torsor, mapping to `X`, together with the
automorphism given by translation by `g`.
declarations.statement:
def inertiaSummand (g : G) :
    fixedQuotientStack B S hS G X ρ g ⥤ quotientInertia B S hS G X ρ
declarations.comment: the canonical functor to the inertia stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaSummandLift_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** `I_{[X/G]} = ∐_{g ∈ G} [X^g/G]`, summand by summand: for each `g ∈ G`
the canonical functor is an equivalence from the quotient `[X^g/G]` of the fixed locus onto
the part of the inertia stack of `[[X/G]]` on which the automorphism is translation by `g`.
Objects correspond because `φ ∘ α = φ` says that `φ` factors through `X^g → X`, and
morphisms correspond because a morphism of `[[X/G]]` is `G`-equivariant.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaSummandLift_isEquivalence (g : G) :
    (inertiaSummandLift (ρ := ρ) g).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the g-summand of the inertia stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaSummandLift_comp_structure
declarations.doc:
The equivalence of Stacks 0374 is an equivalence over `(Sch/S)_fppf`: it carries the
projection of `[X^g/G]` to the structure functor of the inertia stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem inertiaSummandLift_comp_structure (g : G) :
    inertiaSummandLift (ρ := ρ) g ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (IsTranslationBy (ρ := ρ) g) ⋙
        relativeInertiaStruct
          (AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
            (X := X) (ρ := ρ))
          (AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
            (X := X) (ρ := ρ)) =
      AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
        (X := fixedPresheaf (ρ g).asIso.hom) (ρ := fixedPresheafAction ρ g)
declarations.comment: the g-summand is an equivalence over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaCoproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** The disjoint union `∐_{g ∈ G} [X^g/G]` of the quotients of the fixed
loci, mapping to the inertia stack of `[[X/G]]`; on the `g`-summand this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaSummand`.
declarations.statement:
def inertiaCoproduct :
    (Σ g : G, fixedQuotientStack B S hS G X ρ g) ⥤ quotientInertia B S hS G X ρ
declarations.comment: the disjoint union of the quotients of the fixed loci

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.incl_comp_inertiaCoproduct_comp_structure
declarations.doc:
The coproduct of Stacks 0374 maps to the inertia stack over `(Sch/S)_fppf`: on each
summand it carries the projection of `[X^g/G]` to the structure functor of the inertia.
declarations.statement:
theorem incl_comp_inertiaCoproduct_comp_structure (g : G) :
    Sigma.incl g ⋙ inertiaCoproduct (ρ := ρ) ⋙
        relativeInertiaStruct
          (AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
            (X := X) (ρ := ρ))
          (AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
            (X := X) (ρ := ρ)) =
      AbstractGroupQuotientStack.projection (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) (G := G)
        (X := fixedPresheaf (ρ g).asIso.hom) (ρ := fixedPresheafAction ρ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_auto_eq_totalSmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0374.** Conversely to `AlgebraicGeometry.inertiaSummand`: the automorphism `α`
of an object `(P/T, φ, α)` of `I_{[X/G]}` is, at every section of its torsor, translation by
a *unique* section of the constant sheaf of groups with value `G`. Commutativity of `G` is
not needed for this step; what it buys is that the section is independent of the chosen
point, which is why the summands of the formula are indexed by `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_auto_eq_totalSmul (Z : quotientInertia B S hS G X ρ)
    (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ) (p : Z.obj.Total V) :
    ∃! γ : (constantSheafOfGroups (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) G).presheaf.obj V,
      Z.obj.totalSmul γ p = Z.auto.asIso.hom.map V p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.verticalEquivAut
declarations.doc:
**The data `α` of a point `(L, α)` of the inertia stack of `Picardstack_{X/B}` is an
automorphism of the invertible module `L`.**

A morphism of `Picardstack_{X/B}` from `(U, b, L)` to itself consists of a base map and an
isomorphism `(X_{base})^*L ⟶ L`; when the base map is the identity the unit comparison
`(X_{𝟙 U})^* ≅ 𝟭` of Stacks 03LU turns that isomorphism into an automorphism of `L`, and every
automorphism of `L` arises from exactly one such morphism.
declarations.statement:
def verticalEquivAut (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) {s : PicardSituation B S hS}
    (A : PicardObject s) : A.Vertical ≃ (A.lineBundle ≅ A.lineBundle)
declarations.comment: the points of the inertia stack of the Picard stack over a test scheme are the pairs of an invertible module on the base change and an automorphism of it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.autLineBundleMulEquivAutStructure
declarations.doc:
**The automorphism group of the invertible module of an object of `Picardstack_{X/B}` is the
automorphism group of the structure sheaf of the base change.**
declarations.statement:
def autLineBundleMulEquivAutStructure {s : PicardSituation B S hS} (A : PicardObject s) :
    Aut A.lineBundle ≃* Aut (structureModule (s.baseChange A.T))
declarations.comment: an automorphism of an invertible module on the base change is an invertible global function on the base change, so the automorphism group is independent of the module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardObject.autMulEquivMultiplicativeGroupPoints
declarations.doc:
**The `𝐆_m` factor of the inertia stack, as an explicit isomorphism of groups.** When
`𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an isomorphism for every test scheme `T`, the automorphism group of the
invertible module of an object of `Picardstack_{X/B}` over `T` is `𝐆_{m, S}(T)`: an automorphism
is multiplication by a unique invertible regular function on `T`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardObject.bijective_unitsToAut`), and `H^0(T, 𝒪_T^*)` is
`𝐆_{m, S}(T)` by Stacks 022U.
declarations.statement:
def autMulEquivMultiplicativeGroupPoints (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (A : PicardObject s) :
    Aut A.lineBundle ≃* multiplicativeGroupPointsAt B S hS A.T.left
declarations.comment: the 𝐆_m factor of the inertia stack: when 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every test scheme T, the automorphism group of the invertible module of an object of the Picard stack over T is 𝐆_{m,S}(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardObject.verticalEquivMultiplicativeGroupPoints
declarations.doc:
**The points of the inertia stack.** When `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` is an
isomorphism for every test scheme `T`, the endomorphisms of an object `(T, b, L)` of
`Picardstack_{X/B}` lying over the identity of `T` — the points `(L, α)` of the inertia stack above
it — are the points `𝐆_{m, S}(T)` of the multiplicative group: `α` is an automorphism of `L`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.verticalEquivAut`, for the comparisons of Stacks 03LU of the library,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence`), which is multiplication by a unique
invertible function on `T`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.PicardObject.autMulEquivMultiplicativeGroupPoints`).
declarations.statement:
def verticalEquivMultiplicativeGroupPoints (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (A : PicardObject s) :
    A.Vertical ≃ multiplicativeGroupPointsAt B S hS A.T.left
declarations.comment: the points of the inertia stack above an object of the Picard stack over T are 𝐆_{m,S}(T), when 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every test scheme T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_autLineBundle_mulEquiv_multiplicativeGroupPoints_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**The `𝐆_m` factor of the inertia stack.**  Assume that for every test scheme `T`
over the base the structure map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` of the base change is an isomorphism.
Then for every object `(U, b, L)` of `Picardstack_{X/B}` the automorphism group of `L` is the
group `𝐆_{m, S}(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_autLineBundle_mulEquiv_multiplicativeGroupPoints_of_iso
    (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (A : PicardObject s) :
    Nonempty (Aut A.lineBundle ≃* multiplicativeGroupPointsAt B S hS A.T.left)
declarations.comment: the 𝐆_m factor of the inertia stack: under the hypothesis that 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every test scheme T, the automorphism group of the invertible module of an object of the Picard stack over T is 𝐆_{m,S}(T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_vertical_equiv_multiplicativeGroupPoints_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**The points of the inertia stack.**  Assume that for every test scheme `T` over the base the
structure map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` of the base change is an isomorphism.  Then the
endomorphisms of an object `(U, b, L)` of `Picardstack_{X/B}` lying over the identity of `U` — the
points of the inertia stack above it — are the points `𝐆_{m, S}(U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_vertical_equiv_multiplicativeGroupPoints_of_iso
    (hc : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) (A : PicardObject s) :
    Nonempty (A.Vertical ≃ multiplicativeGroupPointsAt B S hS A.T.left)
declarations.comment: the points of the inertia stack above an object of the Picard stack over T are 𝐆_{m,S}(T), under the hypothesis that 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every test scheme T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_equivalenceOver_picardInertia_multiplicativeGroupProduct_of_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ B` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` such that for
every scheme `T` over `B` the structure map `𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T, *}𝒪_{X_T}` of the base change
`f_T : X_T ⟶ T` is an isomorphism.  Then the inertia stack of the Picard stack
`Picardstack_{X/B}` of Section 0372 is

`I_{Picardstack_{X/B}} = 𝐆_{m, S} ×_S Picardstack_{X/B}`

as a category over `(Sch/S)_fppf`: the two are equivalent over the big fppf site, by an
equivalence which is the identity on the `Picardstack_{X/B}`-factor and sends a point `(L, α)` of
the inertia over `T` to the point of `𝐆_{m, S}(T) = H^0(T, 𝒪_T^*)` that the automorphism `α` of
`L` is multiplication by.

In Stacks 0375 `f` is a morphism of schemes; here it is a morphism of algebraic spaces, which
contains that case.  "Equal" is read as an equivalence over the site
(`CategoryTheory.StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver`), and the product is the 2-fibre product
`CategoryTheory.inertiaPresheafProduct` of the category of elements of `𝐆_{m, S}` with
`Picardstack_{X/B}` over the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_equivalenceOver_picardInertia_multiplicativeGroupProduct_of_iso
    (s : PicardSituation B S hS) (h : s.StructureSheafMapIso) :
    letI : Category.{u + 1} (PicardObject s) :=
      (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).category
    Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      (relativeInertiaStruct
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection)
      (inertiaPresheafProductStruct
        (picardCategoryData (modulePushforwardCoherence B S hS) s).siteProjection
        (multiplicativeGroupPresheaf B S hS)))
declarations.comment: the inertia stack of the Picard stack is 𝐆_{m,S} ×_S Picardstack_{X/B}, as categories over (Sch/S)_fppf, when 𝒪_T ⟶ f_{T,*}𝒪_{X_T} is an isomorphism for every test scheme T

registrations.name: IsConnected.image
registrations.comment: the image of a connected set under a continuous map is connected

declarations.name: connectedComponentsMap_bijective_of_isClosed_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0377.** Let `f : X → Y` be a map of topological spaces such that all fibres of `f` are
connected and a subset `T ⊆ Y` is closed if and only if `f ⁻¹' T` is closed. Then `f` induces a
bijection between the sets of connected components of `X` and `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectedComponentsMap_bijective_of_isClosed_iff
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
    (hfib : ∀ y, IsConnected (f ⁻¹' {y}))
    (hcl : ∀ T : Set Y, IsClosed (f ⁻¹' T) ↔ IsClosed T) :
    Function.Bijective
      ((Topology.isCoinducing_iff_isClosed.mpr hcl).continuous.connectedComponentsMap)

declarations.name: bijective_connectedComponentsMap_of_isOpenMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0378.** A continuous open map with connected fibres induces a bijection between the
sets of connected components.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_connectedComponentsMap_of_isOpenMap
    (f : X → Y) (hf_cont : Continuous f) (hf_open : IsOpenMap f)
    (hf_fib : ∀ y : Y, IsConnected (f ⁻¹' {y})) :
    Function.Bijective (hf_cont.connectedComponentsMap)

declarations.name: IsNormalRing.isLocalization
declarations.doc: A localization of a normal ring is a normal ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsNormalRing.isLocalization {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (h : IsNormalRing R)
    (M : Submonoid R) (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalization M S] :
    IsNormalRing S

declarations.name: directLimit_isNormalRing
declarations.doc:
Let `(ι, ≤)` be a directed nonempty preorder, let `(G_i)` be a family of commutative rings,
and let `φ_{ij} : G_i →+* G_j` (for `i ≤ j`) be ring homomorphisms forming a directed system of
rings. If every `G_i` is a normal ring, then the directed colimit `Ring.DirectLimit G φ` is a
normal ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem directLimit_isNormalRing
    (hdir : DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => φ i j h))
    (hnormal : ∀ i, IsNormalRing (G i)) :
    IsNormalRing (Ring.DirectLimit G (fun i j h => φ i j h))

declarations.name: Stacks.TensorProductSpecImage.images_eq
declarations.doc:
The images in `Spec(R)` of the two diagonal maps coincide:
`im(Spec(α)) = im(Spec(α'))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem images_eq (hι : Function.Injective ι) :
    Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (R := R)
        (S := Localization.Away (baseChangeIncl k R S S' ι f)) (alphaMap k R S S' ι f)) =
      Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (R := R) (S := Localization.Away f) (alphaPrime k R S'
          f))

declarations.name: IsAlgClosedIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 037I** (part 2).
A field extension `E/F` is *algebraically closed in `E`* if every element of `E` that is
algebraic over `F` already lies in `F`, i.e. the relative algebraic closure of `F` in `E`
is trivial.
declarations.statement: def IsAlgClosedIn (F E : Type*) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] : Prop

declarations.name: finiteDimensional_algebraicClosure_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 037J**.
If `K/k` is an essentially finite type field extension, then the relative algebraic
closure of `k` in `K` is finite over `k`.
declarations.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_algebraicClosure_of_essFiniteType
    (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] :
    FiniteDimensional k (algebraicClosure k K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae (k R : Type u) [Field k]
    [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (ksep kbar : Type u) [Field ksep] [Algebra k ksep]
    [IsSepClosure k ksep] [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar] [IsAlgClosure k kbar] :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'], IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] k')),
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
          [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'], IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] k')),
        IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] ksep)),
        IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] kbar)),
        GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k R)))]

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
A `k`-algebra `S` is **geometrically irreducible over `k`** if every base change of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec k` along a field-valued point of `Spec k` is an irreducible space, equivalently
if for every field extension `k'/k` the spectrum of `S ⊗[k] k'` is irreducible
(`Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct`). An
irreducible space is nonempty, so this forces every such `S ⊗[k] k'` to be nonzero.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible (k S : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 037M.** Let `k` be a separably algebraically closed field and let `R` be a
`k`-algebra. Then `R` is geometrically irreducible over `k` if and only if the spectrum of `R`
is irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_iff_irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum
    (k R : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k R ↔ IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)

declarations.name: isGeometricallyIrreducible_of_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1 (Subalgebras).** If `S` is geometrically irreducible over `k`, then
every `k`-subalgebra `S' ⊆ S` is geometrically irreducible over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_of_subalgebra
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (hS : Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S)
    (S' : Subalgebra k S) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S'

declarations.name: isGeometricallyIrreducible_of_forall_fg
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2 (Detection by finitely generated subalgebras).** If every finitely
generated `k`-subalgebra of `S` is geometrically irreducible over `k`, then `S` is
geometrically irreducible over `k`.

Proof outline: for each field extension `k'/k`, reduce
`IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (S ⊗[k] k'))` to `(nilradical (S ⊗[k] k')).IsPrime`
via `irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_iff_nilradical_isPrime`, then build `IsPrime` from
its two pieces: `ne_top` (from `nontrivial_tensorProduct_of_forall_fg`) and `mem_or_mem`
(from `nilradical_tensorProduct_mem_or_mem_of_forall_fg`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_of_forall_fg
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (hS : ∀ (S' : Subalgebra k S), S'.FG →
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S') :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S

declarations.name: isGeometricallyIrreducible_directLimit
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3 (Directed colimits).** A directed colimit of geometrically
irreducible `k`-algebras is geometrically irreducible over `k`.

The directed system is given by a directed preorder `ι`, `k`-algebras `G i`, and
transition ring homomorphisms `f i j : G i →+* G j` (for `i ≤ j`) that commute with
the structure maps from `k` (`hf`) and form a `DirectedSystem`.  The colimit is
`Ring.DirectLimit G f`, equipped with the `k`-algebra structure `dlAlg k G f`.

Proof outline: for each field extension `k'/k`, reduce to
`(nilradical (DirectLimit ⊗ k')).IsPrime` via
`irreducibleSpace_primeSpectrum_iff_nilradical_isPrime`, then assemble `IsPrime` from
`nontrivial_directLimit_tensorProduct` (nontriviality ⇒ `ne_top`) and
`nilradical_directLimit_tensorProduct_mem_or_mem` (the prime implication).
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_directLimit
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {ι : Type u} [Preorder ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (G i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (G i)]
    (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →+* G j)
    (hf : ∀ (i j : ι) (h : i ≤ j) (x : k),
      f i j h (algebraMap k (G i) x) = algebraMap k (G j) x)
    [DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => (f i j h : G i → G j))]
    (hG : ∀ i, Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k (G i)) :
    letI := dlAlg k G (fun i j h => (f i j h : G i → G j))
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k
      (Ring.DirectLimit G (fun i j h => (f i j h : G i → G j)))

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.bijOn_irreducibleComponents_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 037O.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a geometrically irreducible `k`-algebra and
let `R` be any `k`-algebra. Then the map `Spec (R ⊗[k] S) → Spec R` induced by `r ↦ r ⊗ₜ 1`
induces a bijection on irreducible components: taking images along it is a bijection from the
irreducible components of `Spec (R ⊗[k] S)` onto the irreducible components of `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.bijOn_irreducibleComponents_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct
    (k R S : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S] :
    Set.BijOn (fun Z ↦ PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R (R ⊗[k] S)) '' Z)
      (irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] S)))
      (irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum R))

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.of_algebraicClosure_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a field extension. If `k` is algebraically closed in `K`, that is, if the relative
algebraic closure `algebraicClosure k K` is trivial, then `K` is geometrically irreducible over
`k`.

declarations.name: part2
declarations.doc:
Statement 2 (Finiteness of `[k' : k]`). If `K/k` is a finitely generated field extension
(Definition 4 — finite generation as a field, encoded by `(⊤ : IntermediateField k K).FG`),
then `k'` is finite over `k`, i.e. `Module.Finite k k'` (equivalently `[k' : k] < ∞`).
declarations.statement:
theorem part2 (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (hfg : (⊤ : IntermediateField k K).FG) :
    Module.Finite k (separableClosure k K)

declarations.name: part1
declarations.doc:
Statement 1 (Geometric irreducibility over `k'`). `K` is geometrically irreducible over `k' =
separableClosure k K`: for every field extension `L/k'` the spectrum `Spec(K ⊗_{k'} L)` is
irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem part1 (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    ∀ (L : Type) [Field L] [Algebra (separableClosure k K) L],
      IrreducibleSpace (PrimeSpectrum (K ⊗[separableClosure k K] L))

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.connectedSpace_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Connectedness of the spectrum of a tensor product over a separably closed field.** Let `k`
be a separably algebraically closed field and let `R` and `S` be `k`-algebras. If `Spec R` and
`Spec S` are connected, then so is `Spec (R ⊗[k] S)`.
declarations.statement:
public instance connectedSpace_primeSpectrum (k : Type u) (R : Type v) (S : Type w) [Field k]
    [IsSepClosed k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)] [ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum S)] :
    ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum (R ⊗[k] S))
declarations.comment:
Connectedness of the spectra of two `k`-algebras over a separably closed field `k`
  is inherited by the spectrum of their tensor product over `k`. Stated as an instance, with
  `Spec` read as `PrimeSpectrum` and `connected` as `ConnectedSpace`, which includes
  nonemptiness as the source's notion of a connected space does.

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_forall_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
**Geometric connectedness is detected by the finite separable extensions.** Let `k` be a
field and let `R` be a `k`-algebra. Then `R` is geometrically connected over `k`, that is,
`Spec (K ⊗[k] R)` is connected for every field extension `K/k`, if and only if `Spec (K ⊗[k] R)`
is connected for every finite separable field extension `K/k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyConnected_iff_forall_finite_separable (k : Type u) (R : Type v)
    [Field k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
    IsGeometricallyConnected k R ↔
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [FiniteDimensional k K] [Algebra.IsSeparable k K],
        ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum (K ⊗[k] R))
declarations.comment:
Geometric connectedness of a `k`-algebra need only be tested on the finite
  separable extensions of `k`. Condition (1) of the lemma is `Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected`
  (Stacks 037T), which is that condition verbatim; `Spec` is `PrimeSpectrum` and `connected` is
  `ConnectedSpace`, which includes nonemptiness as the source's notion does.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
A `k`-algebra `S` over a field `k` is *geometrically connected over `k`* if for every field
extension `K/k` the spectrum of `K ⊗[k] S` is connected.
declarations.statement:
public class IsGeometricallyConnected (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] : Prop

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Geometric connectedness over a separably closed field.** Let `k` be a separably
algebraically closed field and let `R` be a `k`-algebra. Then `R` is geometrically connected
over `k` if and only if `Spec R` is connected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_primeSpectrum
    (k : Type u) (R : Type v) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k R ↔ ConnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum R)

declarations.name: geometricallyConnected_of_subalgebra
declarations.doc:
If `S` is geometrically connected over `k`, then every `k`-subalgebra `R ⊆ S` is
geometrically connected over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyConnected_of_subalgebra
    (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (hS : Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k S) (R : Subalgebra k S) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k R

declarations.name: geometricallyConnected_of_forall_fg
declarations.doc:
If every finitely generated `k`-subalgebra of `S` is geometrically connected over `k`,
then `S` is geometrically connected over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyConnected_of_forall_fg
    (k : Type u) (S : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (h : ∀ R : Subalgebra k S, R.FG → Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k R) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k S

declarations.name: geometricallyConnected_of_directedColimit
declarations.doc:
A directed colimit of geometrically connected `k`-algebras is geometrically connected
over `k`. The colimit `S` of the directed system `(S_i, φ_{ij})` with cocone maps
`ψ_i : S_i →ₐ[k] S` is presented by its elementary universal property: the `ψ_i` are jointly
surjective, and `ψ_i y = ψ_i z` holds only if `y` and `z` become equal after some transition map
`φ_{ij}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyConnected_of_directedColimit
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (ι : Type w) [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (Sfun : ι → Type v) [(i : ι) → CommRing (Sfun i)] [(i : ι) → Algebra k (Sfun i)]
    (φ : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → (Sfun i →ₐ[k] Sfun j))
    (hφcomp : ∀ (i j l : ι) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjl : j ≤ l),
      (φ j l hjl).comp (φ i j hij) = φ i l (le_trans hij hjl))
    (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (ψ : (i : ι) → (Sfun i →ₐ[k] S))
    (hψ : ∀ (i j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j), (ψ j).comp (φ i j hij) = ψ i)
    (hsurj : ∀ x : S, ∃ (i : ι) (y : Sfun i), ψ i y = x)
    (hsep : ∀ (i : ι) (y z : Sfun i), ψ i y = ψ i z →
      ∃ (j : ι) (hij : i ≤ j), φ i j hij y = φ i j hij z)
    (hgc : ∀ i, Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k (Sfun i)) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k S

declarations.name: Algebra.TensorProduct.bijOn_isIdempotentElem_and_bijective_connectedComponentsMap
declarations.doc:
**Base change along a geometrically connected algebra.** Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a
geometrically connected `k`-algebra and let `R` be any `k`-algebra. Then `R → R ⊗[k] S`,
`r ↦ r ⊗ 1`, restricts to a bijection from the idempotents of `R` onto the idempotents of
`R ⊗[k] S`, and the induced map `Spec (R ⊗[k] S) → Spec R` is a bijection on connected
components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijOn_isIdempotentElem_and_bijective_connectedComponentsMap
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [IsGeometricallyConnected k S] (R : Type w) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] :
    Set.BijOn (algebraMap R (R ⊗[k] S)) {e | IsIdempotentElem e} {e | IsIdempotentElem e} ∧
      Function.Bijective (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap
        (algebraMap R (R ⊗[k] S))).connectedComponentsMap
declarations.comment:
Base change of an arbitrary `k`-algebra `R` along a geometrically connected
  `k`-algebra `S` induces a bijection on idempotents and a bijection on connected components of
  the spectra. Both assertions of the lemma; the second is stated as a bijection, as in the
  source, rather than as the homeomorphism of Varieties, Lemma 0385.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsSeparableExtension.tfae_exists_smooth
declarations.doc:
**A finitely generated field extension is separable if and only if it is the localization of a
smooth algebra.** For a finitely generated field extension `K/k` the following are equivalent:
`K/k` is separable; some smooth `k`-subalgebra of `K` has `K` as its fraction field; some smooth
`k`-algebra has `K` as a localization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsSeparableExtension.tfae_exists_smooth
    (k : Type*) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] :
    List.TFAE
      [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K,
        ∃ R : Subalgebra k K, Algebra.Smooth k R ∧ IsFractionRing R K,
        ∃ (R : Type v) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : Algebra k R) (_ : Algebra R K)
          (_ : IsScalarTower k R K) (S : Submonoid R),
          Algebra.Smooth k R ∧ IsLocalization S K]

declarations.name: Algebra.isNormalRing_tensorProduct_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormalRing_tensorProduct_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [ExpChar k p] (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (kperf : Type w) [Field kperf] [Algebra k kperf] [ExpChar kperf p] [PerfectRing kperf p]
    [IsPerfectClosure (algebraMap k kperf) p] :
    [∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'], IsNormalRing (k' ⊗[k] A),
      ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [EssFiniteType k k'],
        IsNormalRing (k' ⊗[k] A),
      ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
        [IsPurelyInseparable k k'], IsNormalRing (k' ⊗[k] A),
      IsNormalRing (kperf ⊗[k] A)].TFAE
declarations.comment:
The source's four conditions in its order, with a normal ring spelled by the
  library's `IsNormalRing` (Definition 00GV), a finitely generated field extension by
  `Algebra.EssFiniteType`, and the perfect closure taken abstractly, as `IsPerfectClosure`.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyNormal
declarations.doc:
A commutative algebra `A` over a field `k` is *geometrically normal* over `k` if the base
change `k' ⊗[k] A` is a normal ring for every field extension `k'/k`. By Lemma 037Z it is enough
to ask this for the finitely generated extensions, or for the finite purely inseparable ones, or
for a single perfect closure of `k`.
declarations.statement:
public class IsGeometricallyNormal (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] : Prop
declarations.comment:
The first of the four equivalent conditions of Lemma 037Z, a normal ring being
  spelled by the library's `IsNormalRing` (Definition 00GV); the other three are criteria for it,
  through `Algebra.isNormalRing_tensorProduct_tfae`.

declarations.name: Algebra.forall_isRegularRing_tensorProduct_essFiniteType_iff_finite_isPurelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Regularity of all base changes to finitely generated field extensions is detected by the
finite purely inseparable ones.** Let `k` be a field and `A` a `k`-algebra. Then `K ⊗[k] A` is a
regular ring (Definition 00OD) for every finitely generated field extension `K/k` if and only if
`k' ⊗[k] A` is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable extension `k'/k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem forall_isRegularRing_tensorProduct_essFiniteType_iff_finite_isPurelyInseparable
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
    (∀ (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K],
        IsRegularRing (K ⊗[k] A)) ↔
      ∀ (K : Type w) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Module.Finite k K] [IsPurelyInseparable k K],
        IsRegularRing (K ⊗[k] A)
declarations.comment:
Regular ring is Definition 00OD, that is Mathlib's `IsRegularRing`, which already
contains Noetherianness; a finitely generated field extension is `Algebra.EssFiniteType`
(`IntermediateField.fg_top_iff`) and a finite purely inseparable one is `Module.Finite` together
with `IsPurelyInseparable`. The source's hypothesis that `A` be Noetherian is not assumed: it is
implied by either side, since `A ≃ₐ[k] k ⊗[k] A`. The extension fields range over a single free
universe, `w := u` giving the source's statement in full. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular
declarations.doc:
A `k`-algebra `R` over a field `k` is *geometrically regular over `k`* if `K ⊗[k] R` is a
regular ring (Definition 00OD) for every finitely generated field extension `K/k`. By Lemma 0381
it is enough to require this for the finite purely inseparable extensions `k'/k`.
declarations.statement:
public class IsGeometricallyRegular (k : Type u) (R : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] : Prop
declarations.comment:
Stated as condition (1) of Lemma 0381; condition (2) follows by instance
resolution and the converse is that lemma. Regular ring is Definition 00OD, that is Mathlib's
`IsRegularRing`, which already contains Noetherianness, so the source's hypothesis that `R` be
Noetherian is not assumed but implied (take `K := k`). A finitely generated field extension is
`Algebra.EssFiniteType` (`IntermediateField.essFiniteType_iff`), and the test field ranges over the
universe of `k`, which is the source's condition for extensions in every universe. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyOpen_of_field
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a scheme over `k`. The structure morphism `X ⟶ Spec k` is
universally open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyOpen_of_field (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : UniversallyOpen f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0384, pointwise statement.** Geometric reducedness at a point is
preserved and reflected after extending the base field and choosing a point above it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyReducedAt_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X)
    (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) : Scheme))
    (hx' : pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) x' = x) :
    IsGeometricallyReducedAt f x ↔
      IsGeometricallyReducedAt
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyReduced_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0384, global statement.** A scheme over a field is geometrically
reduced if and only if its base change along a field extension is geometrically reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyReduced_iff_baseChange_fieldExtension
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyReduced f ↔
      GeometricallyReduced
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_snd_connectedComponentsMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0385.** Let `k` be a field and let `X`, `Y` be schemes over `k`, presented by
their structure maps `f : X ⟶ Spec k` and `g : Y ⟶ Spec k`. If `X` is geometrically connected
over `k`, then the projection `X ×_k Y ⟶ Y` induces a bijection between the connected components
of `X ×_k Y` and the connected components of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pullback_snd_connectedComponentsMap_bijective
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    Function.Bijective (pullback.snd f g).continuous.connectedComponentsMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_spec_iff
declarations.doc:
An affine scheme is geometrically connected over a field if and only if its coordinate
algebra is geometrically connected over that field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_spec_iff (k A : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] :
    GeometricallyConnected (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k A))) ↔
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyConnected k A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is geometrically connected if and only if its base change to a
separable algebraic closure is connected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_baseChange
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (ksep : Type u) [Field ksep] [Algebra k ksep]
    [IsSepClosure k ksep] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyConnected f ↔
      ConnectedSpace
        (CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback f
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k ksep))) : Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fg_subalgebra_descending_isCompact_open
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0388].** Let `X` be a scheme over a commutative ring `k` and let `A` be a
`k`-algebra. A quasi-compact open `V` of the base change `X_A` is the inverse image of a
quasi-compact open `V'` of `X_{A'}` for some finitely generated `k`-subalgebra `A' ⊆ A`.

The morphism `X_A ⟶ X_{A'}` along which `V'` is pulled back is characterised by its two
projections: it covers the morphism `Spec A ⟶ Spec A'` induced by the inclusion `A' ⊆ A` and it
commutes with the projection to `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_subalgebra_descending_isCompact_open
    {k A : Type u} [CommRing k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (V : (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f).Opens)
    (hV : IsCompact V.1) :
    ∃ (A' : Subalgebra k A) (_ : A'.FG)
      (V' : (pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A'))) f).Opens),
      IsCompact V'.1 ∧
        ∃ p : pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f ⟶
              pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A'))) f,
          p ≫ pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A'))) f =
              pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f ≫
                Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Subalgebra.val A').toRingHom) ∧
            p ≫ pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A'))) f =
              pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))) f ∧
            V = p ⁻¹ᵁ V'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_iff_forall_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is geometrically connected if and only if its base change to every
finite separable extension is connected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_iff_forall_finite_separable
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    GeometricallyConnected f ↔
      ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
        [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'],
        ConnectedSpace ↥(pullback f
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnBaseChange
registrations.comment:
For a Galois extension `kbar/k` the group `kbar ≃ₐ[k] kbar` is `Gal(kbar/k)`,
  and `galoisActionOnBaseChange` is the canonical action of its opposite group on `X_kbar`,
  induced by the automorphisms `Spec σ` of `Spec kbar` through the defining fibre product.
  The opposite group appears because `Spec σ ≫ Spec τ = Spec (τ ∘ σ)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_closed_subset_with_preimage_eq_of_galois_invariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038B.** A closed subset of a scheme after base change by a
Galois field extension descends if it is invariant under the Galois group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_closed_subset_with_preimage_eq_of_galois_invariant
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsGalois k K]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (Tbar : Set (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme))
    (hTbar : IsClosed Tbar)
    (hstable : ∀ σ : K ≃ₐ[k] K,
      (galoisBaseChangeMap k K X f σ) ⁻¹' Tbar = Tbar) :
    ∃ T : Set X, IsClosed T ∧
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) ⁻¹' T = Tbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_connectedSpace_of_galois_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `kbar/k` be a possibly infinite Galois extension and let `T → X` be a morphism of
schemes over `k`. If `T_kbar` is connected and `X_kbar` is disconnected, then `X` is
disconnected.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_connectedSpace_of_galois_baseChange
    (k kbar : Type u) [Field k] [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar] [IsGalois k kbar]
    {T X : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ X) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (hT : ConnectedSpace
      ((pullback (f ≫ p) (Spec.map <| ofHom <| algebraMap k kbar)) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hX : ¬ ConnectedSpace
      ((pullback p (Spec.map <| ofHom <| algebraMap k kbar)) : Scheme.{u})) :
    ¬ ConnectedSpace X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc:
The canonical action of the opposite Galois group on the connected components of a scheme
after base change. A component is sent to its image under the corresponding automorphism of the
base-changed scheme.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents
    (X : Over (Spec (.of R))) :
    Action (Type u) (MulOpposite (S ≃ₐ[R] S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Restriction of Galois automorphisms commutes with the canonical map on the connected
components of the two geometric base changes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents_baseChange
    (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k' kbar']
    [IsScalarTower k k' kbar'] [Normal k kbar]
    (p : pullback X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar') ⟶ pullback X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar))
    (hp₁ : p ≫ pullback.fst X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar) =
      pullback.fst X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar'))
    (hp₂ : p ≫ pullback.snd X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar) =
      pullback.snd X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar') ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar kbar')))
    (σ : kbar' ≃ₐ[k'] kbar')
    (C : ConnectedComponents (galoisActionOnBaseChange k kbar' X).V) :
    p.continuous.connectedComponentsMap
        (ConcreteCategory.hom
          ((galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents k kbar' X).ρ
            (MulOpposite.op (σ.restrictScalars k))).asHom C) =
      ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents k kbar X).ρ
          (MulOpposite.op ((σ.restrictScalars k).restrictNormal kbar))).asHom
        (p.continuous.connectedComponentsMap C)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseChangeComparison_connectedComponents_bijective
declarations.doc: The canonical base-extension map is bijective on geometric connected components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChangeComparison_connectedComponents_bijective
    [IsSepClosed kbar]
    (p : pullback X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar') ⟶ pullback X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar))
    (hp₁ : p ≫ pullback.fst X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar) =
      pullback.fst X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar'))
    (hp₂ : p ≫ pullback.snd X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar) =
      pullback.snd X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar') ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar kbar'))) :
    Function.Bijective p.continuous.connectedComponentsMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents_fixed_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038D.** A connected component of the base change of `X` to a separable
algebraic closure `kbar` of `k` is fixed by the Galois action if and only if it is the inverse
image of a connected component of `X` which is geometrically connected over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents_fixed_iff
    (k kbar : Type u) [Field k] [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar] [IsSepClosure k kbar]
    (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (C : ConnectedComponents (galoisActionOnBaseChange k kbar X).V) :
    (∀ σ : MulOpposite (kbar ≃ₐ[k] kbar),
        ConcreteCategory.hom
          ((galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents k kbar X).ρ σ).asHom C = C) ↔
      ∃ T : Set X.left, (∃ x : X.left, T = connectedComponent x) ∧
        IsGeometricallyConnectedSubset X.hom T ∧
        ⇑(pullback.fst X.hom (spectrumMap k kbar)) ⁻¹' T =
          ConnectedComponents.mk ⁻¹' {C}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_geometricConnectedComponents_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
Open connected components of the geometric base change of a quasi-compact scheme are
finite in number.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_geometricConnectedComponents_of_isOpen
    [CompactSpace X.left]
    (hopen : ∀ x : (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V,
      IsOpen (connectedComponent x)) :
    Finite (ConnectedComponents (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.continuous_galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents
declarations.doc:
The absolute Galois action on open geometric connected components of a quasi-compact
scheme is continuous for the Krull topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem continuous_galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents
    [CompactSpace X.left]
    (hopen : ∀ x : (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V,
      IsOpen (connectedComponent x)) :
    let : TopologicalSpace (galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents k ksep X).V :=
      (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace
        (ConnectedComponents (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V))
    Continuous (fun p : MulOpposite (ksep ≃ₐ[k] ksep) ×
        ConnectedComponents (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V =>
      ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((galoisActionOnGeometricConnectedComponents k ksep X).ρ p.1).asHom p.2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_geometricConnectedComponent_of_finiteType
declarations.doc: The geometric connected components of a scheme of finite type over a field are open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_geometricConnectedComponent_of_finiteType
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    (x : (galoisActionOnBaseChange k ksep X).V) :
    IsOpen (connectedComponent x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijOn_image_irreducibleComponents_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 038F.** Let `k` be a field and let `X`, `Y` be schemes over `k`, presented by
their structure maps `f : X ⟶ Spec k` and `g : Y ⟶ Spec k`. If `X` is geometrically
irreducible over `k`, then `X ×_k Y ⟶ Y` induces a bijection between irreducible components:
taking images along it is a bijection from the irreducible components of `X ×_k Y` onto the
irreducible components of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijOn_image_irreducibleComponents_pullback_snd
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] :
    Set.BijOn (fun Z ↦ (pullback.snd f g).base '' Z)
      (irreducibleComponents (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f g))
      (irreducibleComponents Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_local
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038G.** For a scheme over a field, geometric irreducibility is
equivalent to each of the three stated local criteria.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_local
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    let geometricallyIrreducibleSections := fun U : X.Opens ↦
      let : Algebra k Γ(X, U) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE
      [ GeometricallyIrreducible f,
        Nonempty X ∧ ∀ U : X.affineOpens,
          Nonempty (U : Set X) → geometricallyIrreducibleSections U.1,
        IrreducibleSpace X ∧
          ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
            (⨆ i, (U i).1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, geometricallyIrreducibleSections (U i).1,
        ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Nonempty I) (U : I → X.Opens),
          (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧
            (∀ i, GeometricallyIrreducible ((U i).ι ≫ f)) ∧
            ∀ i j, U i ⊓ U j ≠ ⊥ ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038G.** Every nonempty open subscheme of a geometrically irreducible
scheme over a field is geometrically irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyIrreducible_open
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] (U : X.Opens) (hU : Nonempty U) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible (U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijOn_irreducibleComponents_baseChange_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038H.** If `k` is separably algebraically closed, `k' / k` is a field
extension, and `X` is a scheme over `k`, then the projection `X_{k'} ⟶ X` induces a bijection
on irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijOn_irreducibleComponents_baseChange_of_isSepClosed
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (of k)) :
    Set.BijOn
      (fun Z ↦
        (pullback.fst (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).base '' Z)
      (irreducibleComponents
        (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))))
      (irreducibleComponents X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_of_isSepClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038I.** Geometric irreducibility of a scheme over a field can be tested
after every finite separable extension, or after base change to any separable algebraic
closure.
declarations.statement:
public lemma geometricallyIrreducible_tfae_of_isSepClosure
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (ksep : Type u) [Field ksep] [Algebra k ksep] [IsSepClosure k ksep] :
    List.TFAE
      [GeometricallyIrreducible f,
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [FiniteDimensional k k']
          [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'],
          IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
    IrreducibleSpace ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k ksep))))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fixed_geometricComponent_iff_exists_geometricallyIrreducible_component
declarations.doc:
A geometric irreducible component is fixed by the Galois action exactly when it descends
to a geometrically irreducible component of the original scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem fixed_geometricComponent_iff_exists_geometricallyIrreducible_component
    (k ksep : Type u) [Field k] [Field ksep] [Algebra k ksep]
    [IsSepClosure k ksep]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (Tbar : (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep (Over.mk f)).V) :
    (∀ σ : MulOpposite (ksep ≃ₐ[k] ksep),
      ConcreteCategory.hom
        ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep (Over.mk f)).ρ σ).asHom Tbar =
        Tbar) ↔
      ∃ T : irreducibleComponents X,
        GeometricallyIrreducible
          ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
              ⟨(T : Set X), isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents T.1 T.2⟩).subschemeι ≫ f) ∧
        (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k ksep)))).base ⁻¹'
          (T : Set X) = Tbar.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
The canonical action of the opposite Galois group on the irreducible components of a scheme
after base change. A component is sent to its image under the corresponding automorphism of the
base-changed scheme.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents
    (X : Over (Spec (.of R))) :
    Action (Type u) (MulOpposite (S ≃ₐ[R] S))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents_fixed_iff_and_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038J.** Let `k` be a field with separable algebraic closure `ksep` and
let `X` be a scheme over `k`. The canonical action of `Gal(ksep/k)ᵐᵒᵖ` on the irreducible
components of `X_{ksep}` has the following properties.

1. A component `Tbar` is fixed by the action if and only if there is an irreducible component
   `T` of `X`, geometrically irreducible over `k`, with `T_{ksep} = Tbar`.
2. For every field extension `k'/k` with separable algebraic closure `ksep'`, and every embedding
   `ksep → ksep'` over `k`, taking images along `X_{ksep'} ⟶ X_{ksep}` is a bijection on
   irreducible components (Tag 038H), and it intertwines the action of `Gal(ksep'/k')` with
   the action of `Gal(ksep/k)` through restriction of automorphisms.

Geometric irreducibility of `T` is that of its reduced induced closed subscheme over `k`, and
`T_{ksep}` is the inverse image of `T` in `X_{ksep}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents_fixed_iff_and_compatible
    (k ksep : Type u) [Field k] [Field ksep] [Algebra k ksep] [IsSepClosure k ksep]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    (∀ Tbar : (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep (Over.mk f)).V,
      (∀ σ : MulOpposite (ksep ≃ₐ[k] ksep),
        ConcreteCategory.hom
          ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep (Over.mk f)).ρ σ).asHom Tbar = Tbar) ↔
        ∃ T : irreducibleComponents X,
          GeometricallyIrreducible
            ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                ⟨(T : Set X), isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents T.1 T.2⟩).subschemeι ≫ f) ∧
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k ksep)))).base ⁻¹'
            (T : Set X) = Tbar.1) ∧
    ∀ (k' ksep' : Type u) [Field k'] [Field ksep']
      [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k' ksep'] [Algebra k ksep'] [Algebra ksep ksep']
      [IsScalarTower k k' ksep'] [IsScalarTower k ksep ksep'] [IsSepClosure k' ksep'],
      Set.BijOn (fun Z ↦ (baseChangeComparison k ksep ksep' X f).base '' Z)
          (irreducibleComponents
            (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k ksep')))))
          (irreducibleComponents
            (pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k ksep))))) ∧
        ∀ (σ : MulOpposite (ksep' ≃ₐ[k'] ksep'))
          (Z : (galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep' (Over.mk f)).V),
          irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeComparisonEquiv k ksep ksep' (hsep :=
              IsSepClosure.sep_closed k) X f
            (ConcreteCategory.hom
              ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep' (Over.mk f)).ρ
                (MulOpposite.op (AlgEquiv.restrictScalars k σ.unop))).asHom Z) =
          ConcreteCategory.hom
            ((galoisActionOnGeometricIrreducibleComponents k ksep (Over.mk f)).ρ
              (MulOpposite.op
                ((AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom ksep) (AlgEquiv.restrictScalars k σ.unop)))).asHom
            (irreducibleComponentsBaseChangeComparisonEquiv k ksep ksep' (hsep :=
              IsSepClosure.sep_closed k) X f Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyNormalAt
declarations.doc:
A scheme `X ⟶ Spec k` is geometrically normal at `x` if, after every field extension
`K / k`, the local ring at every point of the base change lying over `x` is normal.
declarations.statement: public def IsGeometricallyNormalAt (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyNormal
declarations.doc: A scheme over `k` is geometrically normal if it is geometrically normal at every point.
declarations.statement: public def IsGeometricallyNormal (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyNormalAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
Geometric normality at a point is equivalent both to normality at every point above it after
every finite purely inseparable field extension and to geometric normality of its local ring over
the ground field.
declarations.statement:
lemma geometricallyNormalAt_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsGeometricallyNormalAt f x,
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Module.Finite k K]
        [IsPurelyInseparable k K],
        ∀ (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u})),
          pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) x' = x →
            IsNormalRing
              ((pullback f
                (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk x'),
      letI : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
        letI : Algebra k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)) :=
          StructureSheaf.stalkAlgebra k (f.base x)
        ((f.stalkMap x).hom.comp
          (algebraMap k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)))).toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyNormal k (X.presheaf.stalk x)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyNormal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038O.** The six standard characterizations of geometric normality for
a scheme over a field are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyNormal_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    let geometricallyNormalSections := fun U : X.Opens ↦
      letI : Algebra k Γ(X, U) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyNormal k Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE
      [ IsGeometricallyNormal f,
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'],
          IsNormal (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k'],
          IsNormal (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
          [IsPurelyInseparable k k'],
          IsNormal (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
        ∀ U : X.affineOpens, geometricallyNormalSections U.1,
        IsNormal (pullback f (Spec.map
          (ofHom (algebraMap k (perfectClosure k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyNormal_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038P.** Geometric normality of a scheme over a field is invariant
under extension of the ground field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyNormal_iff_baseChange (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsGeometricallyNormal f ↔
      IsGeometricallyNormal (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyNormalAt_iff_baseChange
declarations.doc: Geometric normality at a point is invariant under extension of the base field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyNormalAt_iff_baseChange
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (x : X) (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hx' : (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).base x' = x) :
    IsGeometricallyNormalAt f x ↔
      IsGeometricallyNormalAt
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyNormal_iff_baseChange_of_isGeometricallyNormalAt
declarations.doc: A scheme is geometrically normal exactly when any base field extension is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyNormal_iff_baseChange_of_isGeometricallyNormalAt
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    IsGeometricallyNormal f ↔
      IsGeometricallyNormal
        (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
Extending the base field by a finitely generated field extension preserves and reflects
the property that a scheme is locally Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyNoetherian_baseChange_iff
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian X ↔
      IsLocallyNoetherian
