        (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyRegularAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038T, part (1).** A scheme `X` over a field `k` is geometrically
regular at `x` if, after every finitely generated field extension `K/k`, every point above `x`
has a regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGeometricallyRegularAt {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGeometricallyRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038T, part (2).** A scheme over a field is geometrically regular if it
is geometrically regular at every point.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsGeometricallyRegular {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyRegularAt_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a locally Noetherian scheme over a field, geometric regularity at a point is equivalent
both to regularity at every point above it after every finite purely inseparable field extension,
and to geometric regularity of its local ring over the ground field.
declarations.statement:
public lemma geometricallyRegularAt_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (x : X) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsGeometricallyRegularAt f x,
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Module.Finite k K]
        [IsPurelyInseparable k K],
        ∀ (x' : (pullback f
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u})),
          pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) x' = x →
            IsRegularLocalRing
              ((pullback f
                (Spec.map
                  (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk x'),
      let : Algebra k (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
        let : Algebra k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)) :=
          StructureSheaf.stalkAlgebra k (f.base x)
        ((f.stalkMap x).hom.comp
          (algebraMap k ((Spec (.of k)).presheaf.stalk (f.base x)))).toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k (X.presheaf.stalk x)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyRegular_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038V.** The five standard characterizations of geometric regularity
for a locally Noetherian scheme over a field are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyRegular_tfae
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    let geometricallyRegularSections := fun U : X.Opens ↦
      letI : Algebra k Γ(X, U) :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ U (by simp)).hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Γ(X, U)
    List.TFAE
      [ IsGeometricallyRegular f,
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k'],
          IsRegular
            (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
        ∀ (k' : Type u) [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Module.Finite k k']
          [IsPurelyInseparable k k'],
          IsRegular
            (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))),
        ∀ U : X.affineOpens, geometricallyRegularSections U.1,
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
          (⨆ i, (U i).1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, geometricallyRegularSections (U i).1 ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyRegularAt_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038W, pointwise assertion.** Geometric regularity at a point
is equivalent to geometric regularity at any point above it after a finitely generated
extension of the ground field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyRegularAt_baseChange_iff
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X) :
    let g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
      Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
    ∀ (x' : (pullback f g : Scheme.{u})),
      pullback.fst f g x' = x →
        (IsGeometricallyRegularAt f x ↔
          IsGeometricallyRegularAt (pullback.snd f g) x')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyRegular_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038W, global assertion.** Geometric regularity is invariant
under finitely generated extension of the ground field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyRegular_baseChange_iff
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    let g : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
      Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))
    IsGeometricallyRegular f ↔
      IsGeometricallyRegular (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyRegularAt_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038W, the equivalence.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a scheme over `k`,
`k'/k` a finitely generated field extension, `x ∈ X`, and `x' ∈ X_{k'}` a point lying over `x`.
Then `X` is geometrically regular at `x` over `k` if and only if `X_{k'}` is geometrically
regular at `x'` over `k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyRegularAt_baseChange_iff
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (x : X)
    (x' : (pullback f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hx' : pullback.fst f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))) x' = x) :
    IsGeometricallyRegularAt f x ↔
      IsGeometricallyRegularAt (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) x'
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2), for any scheme over k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyRegular_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038W, the consequence for schemes.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a scheme
over `k` and `k'/k` a finitely generated field extension. Then `X` is geometrically regular
over `k` if and only if `X_{k'}` is geometrically regular over `k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyRegular_baseChange_iff
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k']
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    IsGeometricallyRegular f ↔
      IsGeometricallyRegular (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))
declarations.comment: in particular: X geometrically regular over k iff X_{k'} is over k'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGeometricallyRegularAt_iff_smoothAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 038X.** For a scheme locally of finite type over a field, geometric
regularity at a point is equivalent to smoothness of the structure morphism at that point.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isGeometricallyRegularAt_iff_smoothAt
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    IsGeometricallyRegularAt f x ↔ InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsNormalAt
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is normal at `x` if it is flat at `x` and its fibre over the image
of `x` is geometrically normal at the point induced by `x`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsNormalAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsNormal
declarations.doc: A morphism of schemes is normal if it is normal at every point of its source.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsNormal {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isNormal_iff
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is normal exactly when it is flat and each of its fibres is a
geometrically normal scheme over the residue field of its base point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_iff {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsNormal f ↔ Flat f ∧ ∀ s : Y, IsGeometricallyNormal (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)
declarations.comment: stated without the source's standing hypothesis that all fibres are locally Noetherian, which neither implication uses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isNormal_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0391.** For a morphism of schemes all of whose fibres are locally
Noetherian, being normal is equivalent to being flat with geometrically normal fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormal_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hfib : locallyNoetherianFibers f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsNormal f, Flat f ∧ ∀ s : Y, IsGeometricallyNormal (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)]

Having locally Noetherian fibres and being normal is local on

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.nonempty_algEquiv_map_and_finite
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a local homomorphism of local rings `(R, m)` and `(S, n)` with `m` finitely
generated, and assume that the fibre `S/mS` is a finite `R`-module, i.e. `dim_{κ(m)} S/mS < ∞`.
Then the completion `S^∧ = lim S/nᵏ` is, as an `S`-algebra, the `m`-adic completion `lim S/mᵏS`
of `S`, and the latter is a finite module over `R^∧ = lim R/mᵏ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AdicCompletion.nonempty_algEquiv_map_and_finite
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (hm : (maximalIdeal R).FG)
    [Module.Finite R (S ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))] :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal S) S ≃ₐ[S]
        AdicCompletion ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) S) ∧
      Module.Finite (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) S)
declarations.comment: Stated without the source's finite generation of `n`, which no step needs; the `m`-adic completion of `S` appears as a completion along the ideal `mS` of `S` in the first conjunct and along `m` in the second. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_hasStandardEtaleSurjectionOn_of_exists_unramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0395.** Let `R → S` be a ring map and `q ⊂ S` a prime. If `R → S` is unramified at
`q` — that is, if `R → S_g` is unramified for some `g ∈ S`, `g ∉ q` — then there are a `g ∈ S`,
`g ∉ q`, a standard étale ring map `R → S'` and a surjective `R`-algebra map `S' → S_g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.exists_hasStandardEtaleSurjectionOn_of_exists_unramified {R : Type u}
    {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (Q : Ideal S) [Q.IsPrime]
    (hQ : ∃ g ∉ Q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)) :
    ∃ g ∉ Q, HasStandardEtaleSurjectionOn R g
declarations.comment:
The conclusion's three items are Mathlib's `HasStandardEtaleSurjectionOn R g`,
namely `∃ (P : StandardEtalePair R) (φ : P.Ring →ₐ[R] Localization.Away g), Surjective φ`. The
hypothesis "unramified at `q`" is Definition 00UT (3) verbatim,
`∃ g ∉ Q, Algebra.Unramified R (Localization.Away g)`, rather than Mathlib's hypothesis pair
`[Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt R Q]`, which implies it but is not implied by it;
so this is strictly more general than Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt.exists_hasStandardEtaleSurjectionOn` and implies it. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_of_fiberDimensionAt_le_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type is quasi-finite at a point whose fibre has local dimension
at most zero there: local dimensions are nonnegative, so the bound makes the dimension zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFiniteAt_of_fiberDimensionAt_le_zero {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X)
    (hx : topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) ≤ 0) :
    f.QuasiFiniteAt x
declarations.comment: a zero-dimensional fibre point is a quasi-finite point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_of_relativeDimensionLE_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type of relative dimension at most zero is locally
quasi-finite.
declarations.comment: relative dimension at most zero implies locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_iff_fiberDimensionAt_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type is quasi-finite at a point if and only if the local
dimension of its fibre at that point is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFiniteAt_iff_fiberDimensionAt_eq_zero
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    quasiFiniteAt f x ↔
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.fiber (f x)) (f.asFiber x) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_relativeDimension_zero
declarations.doc:
A morphism locally of finite type is locally quasi-finite if and only if it has relative
dimension zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyQuasiFinite_iff_relativeDimension_zero
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    LocallyQuasiFinite f ↔ RelativeDimension f 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_setOf_flatOverAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0399.** The locus where a finitely presented quasi-coherent module is
flat over the target of a locally finitely presented morphism is open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_flatOverAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    IsOpen {x : X | IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F x}

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt_iff_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
For morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S` of locally Noetherian schemes and a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` with nonzero stalk at `x`, flatness over the base together with flatness on the
fibre is equivalent to flatness of `Y` over the base at `f x` together with flatness of `F` over
`Y` at `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt_iff_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (x : X)
    (hx : ∃ a : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) F.val.presheaf x,
      a ≠ 0) :
    IsFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt f g F x ↔ IsFlatOverIntermediateAt f g F x

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt_iff
declarations.doc:
At a point where a quasi-coherent module of finite presentation has nonzero stalk, flatness
over the base together with flatness on the fibre is equivalent to flatness of the intermediate
scheme over the base together with flatness over the intermediate scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt_iff {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ g)] [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (x : X)
    (hx : ∃ a : TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) F.val.presheaf x,
      a ≠ 0) :
    IsFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt f g F x ↔ IsFlatOverIntermediateAt f g F x

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.isOpen_isFlatOverBaseAndFiberAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039C.** The set of points of the support of a quasi-coherent module of
finite presentation at which the two equivalent conditions of the fibrewise criterion for
flatness hold is open in the support.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_flat_fiberHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039D.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes over a base `S`, given
by `g : Y ⟶ S`. If `S`, `X`, `Y` are locally Noetherian, `X` is flat over `S` and every induced
morphism of fibres `X_s ⟶ Y_s` is flat, then `f` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_flat_fiberHom {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat (f ≫ g)]
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, Flat (Stacks.Flatness.fiberHom f g s)) :
    Flat f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_flat_fiberHom_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039D.** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.flat_of_flat_fiberHom`, if `f` is in addition surjective then `Y` is flat over
the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_flat_fiberHom_of_surjective {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] [Flat (f ≫ g)]
    [Surjective f] (hfib : ∀ s : S, Flat (Stacks.Flatness.fiberHom f g s)) :
    Flat g
declarations.comment: flatness of the intermediate scheme over the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.flat_of_flat_fiberHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039E.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes with
`X` locally of finite presentation and flat over `S`, with `Y` locally of finite type over `S`,
and with the morphism `X_s ⟶ Y_s` of fibres flat for every point `s` of `S`. Then `f` is
flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_flat_fiberHom {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ g)] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (f ≫ g)]
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (fiberHom f g s)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Flat f

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.flat_of_flat_fiberHom_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039E.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Flatness.flat_of_flat_fiberHom`, if `f` is moreover surjective then `Y` is flat
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_flat_fiberHom_of_surjective {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (f ≫ g)] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (f ≫ g)] [AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective f]
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (fiberHom f g s)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Flat g
declarations.comment: flatness of the target over the base

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_unramified_away_iff_isUnramifiedLocalHom_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 039G.** Let `A → B` be of finite type and let `q` be a prime of `B` lying over the
prime `p` of `A`. Then `A → B` is unramified at `q` (there is `g ∉ q` with `A → B_g` unramified)
if and only if `A_p → B_q` is an unramified homomorphism of local rings. The source assumes `A`
Noetherian, which is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unramified_away_iff_isUnramifiedLocalHom_algebraMap {A B : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B)
    [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] [Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Localization.AtPrime.IsLiesOverAlgebra p q] :
    (∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Unramified A (Localization.Away g)) ↔
      (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q)).IsUnramifiedLocalHom
declarations.comment:
Without the Noetherian hypothesis on `A`, which is used in the source only to
make Definition 024M applicable to `A_p → B_q`; `RingHom.IsUnramifiedLocalHom` is defined for
all local rings. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: RingHom.moduleFinite_adicCompletion_of_formallyUnramified
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039H**, part (1). The completion of the target of an unramified local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings is a finite module over the completion of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleFinite_adicCompletion_of_formallyUnramified
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hfu : f.FormallyUnramified) (hft : f.EssFiniteType) :
    letI := (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
      (map_maximalIdeal_le f)).toAlgebra
    Module.Finite (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B)

declarations.name: RingHom.surjective_adicCompletionMap_of_bijective_residueFieldMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039H**, part (2). An unramified local homomorphism inducing a
bijection on residue fields induces a surjection on completions.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_adicCompletionMap_of_bijective_residueFieldMap
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hfu : f.FormallyUnramified) (hft : f.EssFiniteType)
    (hκ : Function.Bijective (ResidueField.map f)) :
    Function.Surjective
      (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B) (map_maximalIdeal_le f))

declarations.name: RingHom.surjective_adicCompletionMap_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039H**, part (3). An unramified local homomorphism whose source has
separably closed residue field induces a surjection on completions.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_adicCompletionMap_of_isSepClosed
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hfu : f.FormallyUnramified) (hft : f.EssFiniteType)
    [IsSepClosed (ResidueField A)] :
    Function.Surjective
      (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B) (map_maximalIdeal_le f))

declarations.name: RingHom.unramified_iff_uniformizer_and_residueField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039H**, part (4). A local homomorphism of complete discrete valuation
rings is unramified exactly when it carries a uniformizer to a uniformizer, its residue field
extension is finite and separable, and it is essentially of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem unramified_iff_uniformizer_and_residueField
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal B) B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (ϖ : A) (hϖ : Irreducible ϖ) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    (Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType A B) ↔
      (Irreducible (f ϖ) ∧ Module.Finite (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B) ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparable (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B) ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType A B)

declarations.name: RingHom.formallyUnramified_iff_formallyUnramified_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039I**, parts (1) and (2). An essentially finite type local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings is formally unramified if and only if the induced
homomorphism of completions is.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyUnramified_iff_formallyUnramified_adicCompletion
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hft : f.EssFiniteType) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B ↔
      (letI := (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
        (map_maximalIdeal_le f)).toAlgebra
       Algebra.FormallyUnramified
         (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B))

declarations.name: RingHom.formallyUnramified_adicCompletion_iff_unramified_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039I**, parts (2) and (3). For the completion of an essentially finite
type local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, formal unramifiedness and unramifiedness
agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyUnramified_adicCompletion_iff_unramified_adicCompletion
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hft : f.EssFiniteType) :
    letI := (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
      (map_maximalIdeal_le f)).toAlgebra
    Algebra.FormallyUnramified
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B) ↔
      Algebra.Unramified
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.unramifiedAt_iff_morphisms_unramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
For a locally finite type morphism to a locally Noetherian scheme, the stalk-theoretic
definition of unramifiedness at a point agrees with the affine-neighbourhood definition.
declarations.statement:
lemma unramifiedAt_iff_morphisms_unramifiedAt
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (x : X) :
    StalkwiseUnramifiedAt f x ↔ UnramifiedAt f x

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyOpen.of_flat
registrations.comment: flat and locally of finite presentation implies universally open

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation.iff_locallyOfFiniteType
registrations.comment: over a locally Noetherian base, locally of finite type is locally of finite presentation

declarations.name: Algebra.isEtaleAt_iff_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
A finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is étale at a prime if and only if the induced
map between the local rings at the corresponding primes is an étale local homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleAt_iff_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p] :
    Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q ↔
      letI : IsNoetherianRing B := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing A B
      letI : IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime p) :=
        IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing p.primeCompl _ inferInstance
      letI : IsNoetherianRing (Localization.AtPrime q) :=
        IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing q.primeCompl _ inferInstance
      RingHom.IsEtaleLocalHom
        (Localization.localRingHom p q (algebraMap A B) Ideal.LiesOver.over)

declarations.name: RingHom.isEtaleLocalHom_iff_isEtaleLocalHom_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039M**, parts (1) and (2). An essentially finite type local
homomorphism of Noetherian local rings is étale if and only if the induced homomorphism of
completions is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocalHom_iff_isEtaleLocalHom_adicCompletion
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hft : f.EssFiniteType) :
    letI := AdicCompletion.isLocalHom_adicCompletionMap f
    IsEtaleLocalHom f ↔
      IsEtaleLocalHom
        (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B) (map_maximalIdeal_le f))

declarations.name: RingHom.isEtaleLocalHom_adicCompletion_iff_etale_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039M**, parts (2) and (3). For the completion of an essentially finite
type local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, étaleness as a homomorphism of local rings
agrees with étaleness as an algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleLocalHom_adicCompletion_iff_etale_adicCompletion
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hft : f.EssFiniteType) :
    letI := AdicCompletion.isLocalHom_adicCompletionMap f
    IsEtaleLocalHom
        (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B) (map_maximalIdeal_le f)) ↔
      (letI := (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
        (map_maximalIdeal_le f)).toAlgebra
       Algebra.Etale
         (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B))

declarations.name: RingHom.exists_linearEquiv_fin_adicCompletion_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039M.** The completion of the target of an étale local homomorphism of
Noetherian local rings is a finite free module of positive rank over the completion of the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_linearEquiv_fin_adicCompletion_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    letI := (adicCompletionMap f (maximalIdeal A) (maximalIdeal B)
      (map_maximalIdeal_le f)).toAlgebra
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal B) B ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A]
        (Fin n → AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEtaleAt_iff_etaleAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 039N.** For a morphism locally of finite type over a locally
Noetherian scheme, étaleness of the induced map of local rings at `x` is equivalent to
étaleness on suitable affine neighbourhoods of `x` and its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleAt_iff_etaleAt {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] :
    IsEtaleAt f x ↔ EtaleAt f x

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_standardEtalePair_localization_surjection
declarations.doc:
An unramified local algebra over a local ring is a quotient of the localization at a prime of
a standard étale algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_standardEtalePair_localization_surjection
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B] :
    ∃ (P : StandardEtalePair A) (q : Ideal P.Ring) (hq : q.IsPrime),
      letI := hq
      ∃ φ : Localization.AtPrime q →ₐ[A] B, Function.Surjective φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affine_open_etale_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes which is smooth at a point is, over any affine open neighbourhood `V`
of the image of that point, étale-locally an affine space over `V`: there is an affine open
neighbourhood `U` of the point mapping into `V` and an étale morphism from `U` to an affine
space over `V` commuting with the morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_open_etale_affineSpace {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X)
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hxV : x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x) :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (_ : x ∈ U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V)
      (π : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.toScheme),
      Etale π ∧
        π ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V.toScheme ↘ V.toScheme) =
          f.resLE V U hUV
declarations.comment: smooth at a point is étale-locally an affine space

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.etalePullback_isEquivalence_of_surjective_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Une équivalence remarquable de catégories.** Let `S₀ ⊆ S` be a closed subscheme with the same
underlying topological space. Base change along the closed immersion is an equivalence from the
category of schemes étale over `S` to the category of schemes étale over `S₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etalePullback_isEquivalence_of_surjective_isClosedImmersion (i : S₀ ⟶ S)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : Function.Surjective i.base) :
    letI : MorphismProperty.HasPullbacksAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) i := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ inferInstance⟩
    letI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChangeAlong
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) i :=
      ⟨fun pb hg ↦ MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback pb hg⟩
    (show S.Etale ⥤ S₀.Etale from
      MorphismProperty.Over.pullback
        (@Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊤ i).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: RingHom.ringKrullDim_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
An étale homomorphism of Noetherian local rings preserves the
Krull dimension: the dimension of the source equals the dimension of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringKrullDim_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    ringKrullDim A = ringKrullDim B

declarations.name: RingHom.depth_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
declarations.doc:
An étale local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings
preserves depth.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_eq_of_isEtaleLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : IsEtaleLocalHom f) :
    Module.depth A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A =
      Module.depth B (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.NilpotentFibreCriterion.flat_of_flat_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: ModuleCat.descentDataEquivCartesianCechModule
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an `R`-algebra.  Descent data for `A / R` correspond to cartesian
`(A / R)_•`-modules: the functor `(N, φ) ↦ N_•`, sending a descent datum to its cosimplicial
module over the Čech algebra `(A / R)_•` (`N_n = N_{n, n}`, `N_•(β) = φᵐ_{β(n), m} ∘ N_{β, n}`),
is an equivalence of categories between descent data and cartesian `(A / R)_•`-modules.  Its
inverse sends a cartesian module `M` to `M_0` with the transition `M_0 ⊗_R A ≅ M_1 ≅ A ⊗_R M_0`
read off from the cartesian isomorphisms along the two cofaces `⦋0⦌ ⟶ ⦋1⦌`
(`ModuleCat.cartesianDescentDataFunctor`).  No flatness is assumed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def descentDataEquivCartesianCechModule :
    DescentData.{u, u, max u w} R A ≌ CartesianCechModule.{u, u, max u w} R A
declarations.comment: (2): descent data for `A / R` correspond to cartesian `(A / R)_•`-modules, through the cosimplicial module of a descent datum of Stacks 023H

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Arrow.cechConerve_homotopyEquivalent_const_of_section
declarations.doc:
A split Čech conerve is homotopy equivalent to the constant cosimplicial object on the base.
For commutative `R`-algebras this is the split Čech algebra `(A/R)•` and the constant algebra
`R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechConerve_homotopyEquivalent_const_of_section
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (f : Arrow C)
    [∀ n : ℕ, HasWidePushout f.left (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => f.right) fun _ => f.hom]
    (h : ∃ s : f.right ⟶ f.left, f.hom ≫ s = 𝟙 f.left) :
    ∃ a : f.cechConerve.op ⟶ ((CosimplicialObject.const C).obj f.left).op,
      SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences Cᵒᵖ a

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialModule.Cartesian

declarations.statement: abbrev Cartesian (M : CosimplicialModule A) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CosimplicialModule.isEquivalence_cartesianBaseChange_of_homotopyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 039Y (4).**  If `α : A_• ⟶ B_•` is a homotopy equivalence of cosimplicial
`R`-algebras, then the functor `M_• ↦ M_• ⊗_{A_•} B_•` is an equivalence of categories between
the cartesian `A_•`-modules and the cartesian `B_•`-modules.

A homotopy equivalence is taken in the sense of Simplicial, Definition 019N, through the opposite
category (cosimplicial homotopies being simplicial homotopies of the opposite objects,
Simplicial, Lemma 019X), exactly as in Stacks 039Y (3) here
(`CategoryTheory.Arrow.cechConerve_homotopyEquivalent_const_of_section`).  The proof is the
source's "triviality": base change along homotopic morphisms gives isomorphic functors
(`CategoryTheory.CosimplicialModule.nonempty_iso_cartesianBaseChange_of_homotopic`), so a homotopy
inverse `β` makes base change along `α ≫ β` and along `β ≫ α` isomorphic to the identities, and
base change is functorial (`CategoryTheory.CosimplicialModule.cartesianBaseChangeCompIso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_cartesianBaseChange_of_homotopyEquivalence (α : A ⟶ B)
    (hα : SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (CommAlgCat.{v, u} R)ᵒᵖ (NatTrans.op α)) :
    (cartesianBaseChange.{u, v, w} α).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: (4): base change along a homotopy equivalence of cosimplicial algebras is an equivalence of the categories of cartesian modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.exists_isDenseSubsite_subcanonical
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `ι : C' ⥤ Sh(C)` be a full subcategory of the
category of sheaves of sets on `C`, with a set of objects, which is closed under fibre products
and contains the sheafified representables: `v : C ⥤ C'` is a functor with `v ⋙ ι ≅ h_{-}^#`.
Declare a covering of `C'` to be a family `{F_i ⟶ F}` of morphisms with `∐ F_i ⟶ F` a surjection
of sheaves. Then

1. these coverings are the coverings of a Grothendieck topology `K` on `C'`, i.e. `C'` is a site;
2. `K` is subcanonical, i.e. representable presheaves on `C'` are sheaves;
3. `v` is a special cocontinuous functor, i.e. `v.IsDenseSubsite J K`, hence the induced morphism
   of topoi `g : Sh(C) ⟶ Sh(C')` is an equivalence;
4. `g⁻¹ h_F = F` for every object `F` of `C'`; and
5. `g_* F = h_F` for every object `F` of `C'`; along `v` this is
   `g_* h_U^# = h_{v U} = h_{h_U^#}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDenseSubsite_subcanonical {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {D : Type max u v} [SmallCategory D]
    (ι : D ⥤ Sheaf J (Type max u v)) [ι.Full] [ι.Faithful] [HasPullbacks D]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan ι] (v : C ⥤ D) (e : v ⋙ ι ≅ Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J) :
    ∃ K : GrothendieckTopology D,
      (∀ {X : D} {α : Type max u v} (Y : α → D) (p : ∀ a, Y a ⟶ X) {c : Cofan fun a ↦ ι.obj (Y a)}
          (hc : IsColimit c),
          Sieve.ofArrows Y p ∈ K X ↔ Epi (Cofan.IsColimit.desc hc fun a ↦ ι.map (p a))) ∧
        ∃ (_ : K.Subcanonical) (_ : v.IsDenseSubsite J K),
          Nonempty (K.yoneda ⋙ v.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type max u v) J K ≅ ι) ∧
            Nonempty (ι ⋙ v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type max u v) J K ≅ K.yoneda)
declarations.comment:
A full subcategory of `Sh(C)` with a set of objects which contains the sheafified
  representables and is closed under fibre products is a site, for the coverings whose coproduct
  is a surjection of sheaves; that site is subcanonical, `U ↦ h_U^#` is a special cocontinuous
  functor, and the induced equivalence of topoi matches the representables of the two sides. This
  is all five conclusions, with (5) stated for every object of the subcategory.

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.exists_isDenseSubsite_isMorphismOfSites_pushforward_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `f : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` be a morphism
of topoi. Then there are a site `(C', J')` and functors `v : C ⥤ C'` and `u : D ⥤ C'` such that

1. `v` is a special cocontinuous functor, i.e. exhibits `(C, J)` as a dense subsite of
   `(C', J')`, so that the morphism of topoi `g : Sh(C) → Sh(C')` it induces is an equivalence;
2. `u` commutes with fibre products *and with the final object*, is continuous, and defines a
   morphism of sites `C' → D`, hence a morphism of topoi `h : Sh(C') → Sh(D)`; and
3. `f` agrees with `h ∘ g`, in the sense that `f_*` is isomorphic to the composition of the
   pushforwards `g_* = v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous` and `h_* = u.sheafPushforwardContinuous`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDenseSubsite_isMorphismOfSites_pushforward_iso {C : Type u₁}
    [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type max u₁ v₁)) (Sheaf K (Type max u₁ v₁))) :
    ∃ (C' : Type max u₁ v₁) (_ : SmallCategory C') (J' : GrothendieckTopology C') (v : C ⥤ C') (u :
      D ⥤ C') (_ : v.IsDenseSubsite J J') (_ : _root_.IsMorphismOfSites.{max u₁ v₁} u K J'),
      PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u ∧
        PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete PEmpty.{1}) u ∧
          Nonempty
            (f.pushforward ≅
              v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type max u₁ v₁) J J' ⋙
                u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type max u₁ v₁) K J')
declarations.comment:
Every morphism of topoi is the composition of the equivalence induced by a special
  cocontinuous functor with the morphism of topoi induced by a morphism of sites. The conclusion
  also records, from Stacks 03CJ, that `u` preserves the final object.

registrations.comment: the trivial torsor is a torsor

declarations.name: isTrivial_iff_nonempty_globalSections
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a sheaf of (possibly non-commutative) groups on a site `C` and `F` a `G`-torsor.
Then `F` is trivial if and only if it has a global section, i.e. `Γ(C, F)` is nonempty
(Stacks, Tag 03AI, Lemma 21.4.2).
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_iff_nonempty_globalSections
    (F : PseudoTorsor (C := C) G) (hF : F.IsTorsor) :
    F.IsTrivial ↔ Nonempty (GlobalSections F.presheaf)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AJ.** Isomorphism classes of torsors under an
abelian sheaf are canonically in bijection with its first cohomology group.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def torsorIsoClassesEquivH1
    (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}) :
    torsorIsoClasses H ≃ Sheaf.H H 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_eq_boundary_iff
declarations.doc:
The class of a torsor is the boundary of a global section precisely when
the torsor is equivariantly isomorphic to its fiber in the middle sheaf of
the short exact sequence. The embedding is required to be injective on
sections and to have exactly that fiber as its image.
declarations.statement:
public lemma torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_eq_boundary_iff
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t})) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (q : (Functor.const Cᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{t} ℤ)) ⟶ S.X₃.obj)
    (F : AbelianTorsor S.X₁) :
    torsorIsoClassesEquivH1 S.X₁ (Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid S.X₁) F) =
        (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ (((sheafificationAdjunction J AddCommGrpCat).homEquiv _ _).symm q)).comp
          hS.extClass (zero_add 1) ↔
      ∃ i : F.1.presheaf ⟶ S.X₂.obj ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat,
        (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (h : S.X₁.obj.obj U) (s : F.1.presheaf.obj U),
          let iU : F.1.presheaf.obj U → S.X₂.obj.obj U := i.app U
          iU (F.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd h) s) = S.f.hom.app U h + iU s) ∧
        (∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (i.app U)) ∧
        (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : S.X₂.obj.obj U),
          S.g.hom.app U x = q.app U ⟨1⟩ ↔ ∃ s, i.app U s = x)
declarations.comment: characterization by the boundary map and fiber torsor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_trivial
declarations.doc: The trivial torsor corresponds to zero in first cohomology.
declarations.statement:
public lemma torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_trivial (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}) :
    torsorIsoClassesEquivH1 H
      (Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H)
        ⟨trivialTorsor (abelianSheafAsGroupSheaf H),
          trivialTorsor_isTorsor (abelianSheafAsGroupSheaf H)⟩) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_naturality
declarations.statement:
public lemma torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_naturality
    {H H' : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}} (φ : H ⟶ H')
    (F : AbelianTorsor H) (F' : AbelianTorsor H')
    (f : F.1.presheaf ⟶ F'.1.presheaf)
    (hf : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (h : H.obj.obj U) (s : F.1.presheaf.obj U),
      f.app U (F.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd h) s) =
        F'.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd (φ.hom.app U h)) (f.app U s)) :
    Sheaf.H.map φ 1 (torsorIsoClassesEquivH1 H (Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H) F)) =
      torsorIsoClassesEquivH1 H' (Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H') F')

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.instAddCommGroupTorsorIsoClasses
declarations.doc:
**The isomorphism classes of torsors under an abelian sheaf form an abelian group.**  The
addition is the contracted product and the zero is the trivial torsor, by
`Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClasses_mk_add_of_equivariant` and
`Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClasses_trivial_eq_zero`; the group laws themselves are
those of `Ext¹`, carried across the bijection of Tag 03AJ.
declarations.statement:
public instance instAddCommGroupTorsorIsoClasses (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}) :
    AddCommGroup (torsorIsoClasses H)
declarations.comment: the abelian-group structure on the isomorphism classes of torsors, with addition the contracted product and zero the trivial torsor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesAddEquivH1
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AJ as an isomorphism of abelian groups.**  The canonical bijection
between the isomorphism classes of torsors under an abelian sheaf and its first cohomology group
carries the contracted product of torsors to the addition of `Ext¹`.
declarations.statement:
public def torsorIsoClassesAddEquivH1 (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}) :
    torsorIsoClasses H ≃+ Sheaf.H H 1
declarations.comment: the canonical bijection as a group isomorphism, for the contracted product of torsors

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClasses_trivial_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The zero of the group of torsor classes is the class of the trivial torsor.**  One of the
two laws pinning the group structure of
`Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.instAddCommGroupTorsorIsoClasses`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsorIsoClasses_trivial_eq_zero (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t}) :
    (by exact (Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H)
        ⟨trivialTorsor (abelianSheafAsGroupSheaf H),
          trivialTorsor_isTorsor (abelianSheafAsGroupSheaf H)⟩) : torsorIsoClasses H) = 0
declarations.comment: the zero of the group of torsor classes is the trivial torsor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClasses_mk_add_of_equivariant
declarations.doc:
**The sum of two torsor classes is the class of their contracted product.**  A torsor `T`
receiving a morphism out of the product of the presheaves of `F` and `G` which adds the two
acting sections is precisely a torsor identified with the contracted product `F ∧_H G`, and its
class is the sum of the two classes.  This is the second of the two laws pinning the group
structure of `Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.instAddCommGroupTorsorIsoClasses`, and together with
`Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClasses_trivial_eq_zero` it determines the addition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsorIsoClasses_mk_add_of_equivariant (H : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{t})
    (F G T : AbelianTorsor H)
    (f : Generators.productPresheaf' F.1.presheaf G.1.presheaf ⟶ T.1.presheaf)
    (hf : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : H.obj.obj U) (s : F.1.presheaf.obj U) (t : G.1.presheaf.obj U),
      f.app U (F.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd a) s,
          G.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd b) t) =
        T.1.act U (Multiplicative.ofAdd (a + b)) (f.app U (s, t))) :
    (by exact Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H) F : torsorIsoClasses H) +
        (by exact Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H) G : torsorIsoClasses H) =
      Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid H) T
declarations.comment: the addition of torsor classes is the contracted product of torsors

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechRestrictionToCohomology_bijective_iff
declarations.doc:
For an individual family whose Čech complex exists, bijectivity into degree-zero
Čech homology is equivalent to bijectivity into matching families.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cechRestrictionToCohomology_bijective_iff {X : C}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} X)
    [HasProducts.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{a}]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀), HasProduct (fun j ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i j)))]
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{a}) :
    Function.Bijective (cechRestrictionToCohomology E F) ↔
      Function.Bijective (cechRestriction E F)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.isSheaf_iff_bijective_cechRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AN.** An abelian presheaf is a sheaf if and only if restriction to the
degree-zero Čech cohomology of every covering family is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_iff_bijective_cechRestriction
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{a}) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf J F ↔
      ∀ {X : C} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{max u v} X), E.sieve₀ ∈ J X →
        Function.Bijective (cechRestriction E F)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexPlusFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AP.** The Čech complex as a functor of the coefficient presheaf, with its
nonnegative grading regarded canonically as a bounded-below integer grading.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cechComplexPlusFunctor {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A]
    [HasProducts.{w} A] [Preadditive A] [HasZeroObject A]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀), HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    CategoryTheory.Functor (CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ A) (CochainComplex.Plus A)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexPlusFunctor_exact
declarations.doc: Taking the bounded-below Čech complex of a presheaf of abelian groups is an exact functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechComplexPlusFunctor_exact
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    exactFunctor
      (CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb})
      (CochainComplex.Plus AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb})
      (cechComplexPlusFunctor (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb}) E)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyDeltaFunctor
declarations.doc:
The Čech cohomology functors of a family of morphisms with fixed target
form a cohomological delta functor on abelian presheaves, whose `n`-th functor is the `n`-th
Čech cohomology functor of Stacks 03AM.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def cechCohomologyDeltaFunctor
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun b ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i b)))] :
    { F : DeltaFunctor
        (CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max w a}) AddCommGrpCat.{max w a} //
      ∀ n : ℕ, F.functor n = cechComplexFunctor E ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max w a} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n }

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplex
declarations.doc:
The canonical integral Čech chain complex. Its degree `n` term is
`\bigoplus_{i : Fin (n+1) → E.I₀} ℤ[U_i]`, with `U_i` the corresponding fibre
product over `X`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def integralCechComplex
    [HasCoproducts.{w} (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a})]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    ChainComplex (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a}) ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplex_X
declarations.doc:
The degree-`n` term of the integral Čech complex is the indicated direct sum of
free abelian representable presheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplex_X
    [HasCoproducts.{w} (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a})]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] (n : ℕ) :
    (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E).X n =
      ∐ fun i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀ ↦
      freeAbelianYoneda.{v, u, a}.obj ((∏ᶜ (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))).left)
declarations.comment: the terms of the integral Čech complex

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplex_d
declarations.doc:
The differential of the integral Čech complex is the alternating sum of the canonical maps
which omit one factor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplex_d
    [HasCoproducts.{w} (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a})]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] (n : ℕ) :
    (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E).d (n + 1) n =
      ∑ j : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) •
      (integralCechSimplicialObject.{w, v, u, a} E).δ j
declarations.comment: the differential of the integral Čech complex

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.homIntegralCechComplexIso
declarations.doc:
Mapping the integral Čech chain complex into an abelian presheaf is naturally isomorphic, as a
cochain complex, to its Čech complex.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homIntegralCechComplexIso
    [HasCoproducts.{w} (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a})]
    [HasProducts.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{max u v a}]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    homComplexFunctor (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E) ≅
      liftedCechComplexFunctor.{w, v, u, a} E

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplex_homology_isZero
declarations.doc:
The homology presheaves of the integral Čech chain complex vanish in every positive degree:
the complex of abelian presheaves is exact in all degrees except `0`. The degree-`0` term of
`integralCechComplex` is `⊕_{i₀} Z_{U_{i₀}}`, so the hypothesis `0 < n` is exactly "all degrees
except `0`", and nothing is asserted at `n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplex_homology_isZero (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E).homology n)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.existsUnique_cechCohomologyIsoRightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AU.** The Čech cohomology functors `Ȟ^p(E, -)` of a family of
morphisms with fixed target are canonically isomorphic, as a cohomological `δ`-functor on
abelian presheaves, to the right derived functors `R^p Ȟ⁰(E, -)` of degree-zero Čech cohomology.

"Canonically" is the uniqueness clause: there is exactly one isomorphism of `δ`-functors whose
degree-zero component is the canonical comparison `Ȟ⁰(E, -) ⟶ R⁰ Ȟ⁰(E, -)` of Stacks 05TD, and
it is `Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyDeltaFunctorIsoRightDerived`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_cechCohomologyIsoRightDerived :
    ∃! e : (cechCohomologyDeltaFunctor.{w, v, max u v a, u} E).1 ≅
        cechH0RightDerivedDeltaFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E,
      e.hom.app 0 = (cechH0IsoRightDerivedZero.{w, v, a, u} E).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexIsoRightDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AU**, the functorial quasi-isomorphism. For any right derived
functor `RȞ⁰(E, -) : D⁺(PAb(C)) ⥤ D⁺(Ab)` of degree-zero Čech cohomology, the Čech complex is
isomorphic, functorially in the abelian presheaf, to `RȞ⁰(E, -)` applied to the presheaf placed
in degree zero.

The isomorphism is the span of [Stacks, Tag 03AU]: for an injective resolution `F → I^•`, both
`Č^•(E, F) ⟶ Tot(Č^•(E, I^•))` and `Ȟ⁰(E, I^•) ⟶ Tot(Č^•(E, I^•))` are quasi-isomorphisms,
the first because the Čech complex functor is exact (Stacks 03AQ) and the second because the
higher Čech cohomology of an injective presheaf vanishes (Stacks 03OR).
declarations.statement:
def cechComplexIsoRightDerivedFunctor
    (RF : DerivedCategory.Plus (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a})
    (α : (cechH0Functor.{w, v, a, u} E).mapHomotopyCategoryPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.Plus.quasiIso (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a}))] :
    cechComplexPlusFunctor (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a}) E ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.Q (C := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a}) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w a}) 0 ⋙ RF

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechH0IsoRightDerivedPlusZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AU.** The degree-zero Čech cohomology functor is its own zeroth right derived
functor, normalized by `H ⁰` of the unit of the right derived functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechH0IsoRightDerivedPlusZero :
    { e : cechCohomologyZeroFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E ≅
        cechCohomologyRightDerivedPlus.{w, v, a, u} E 0 //
      e.hom = (cechH0RightDerivedPlusZeroIso.{w, v, a, u} E).inv }

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AU.** The higher right derived functors of degree-zero Čech cohomology, equipped
with their universal cohomological δ-functor structure.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor :
    { R : DeltaFunctor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v a}) AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v a} //
      (∀ n : ℕ, R.functor n = cechCohomologyRightDerivedPlus.{w, v, a, u} E n) ∧
      R.IsUniversal }
declarations.comment: the delta functor of higher right derived functors

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.existsUnique_cechCohomologyDeltaFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AU.** Čech cohomology is canonically isomorphic, as a cohomological δ-functor, to
the higher right derived functors of degree-zero Čech cohomology. The isomorphism is unique with
its prescribed degree-zero component.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_cechCohomologyDeltaFunctorIso :
    ∃! e : (cechCohomologyDeltaFunctor.{w, v, max u v a, u} E).1 ≅
        (rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E).1,
      e.hom.app 0 = (cechH0IsoRightDerivedPlusZero.{w, v, a, u} E).1.hom ≫
        eqToHom ((rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E).2.1 0).symm

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology_isZero_of_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AW (positive degrees).** The Čech cohomology of an injective abelian sheaf for a
covering family vanishes in positive degrees.

Stated before `include hE` because the covering property plays no part: the vanishing is pure
injectivity, and carrying `hE` would make this strictly weaker than the source statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechCohomology_isZero_of_injective [Injective I] (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology E I.obj p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology_zero_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AW (degree zero).** The degree-zero Čech cohomology of an abelian sheaf for a
covering family is its group of sections over the covered object.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechCohomology_zero_iso :
    Nonempty (cechCohomology E I.obj 0 ≅ I.obj.obj (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechToDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AX (derived transformation).** The Čech complex of a covering
family maps naturally to derived sections over the covered object.
declarations.statement:
def cechToDerivedSections :
    cechDerivedFunctor.{a} K E ⟶ derivedSectionsFunctor.{max a u v w} K U

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyToCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AX (cohomology maps).** Taking homology of the Čech-to-derived
comparison gives maps from Čech cohomology to sheaf cohomology, natural in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def cechCohomologyToCohomology (p : ℤ) :
    (cechDerivedFunctor.{a} K E ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor Ab.{max a u v w} p) ⟶
      (derivedSectionsFunctor.{max a u v w} K U ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor Ab.{max a u v w} p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.nonempty_cechResolutionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03AX (the injective-resolution specification).** For every injective
resolution, the Čech-to-derived-sections transformation is the map induced by the two canonical
augmentations into the total Čech complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_cechResolutionComparison (F : Sheaf K Ab.{max a u v w})
    (J : InjectiveResolution F) :
    Nonempty (CechResolutionComparison.{a} K E hE F J)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.rightDerivedSheafToPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AY, right derived functors.** The `p`-th right derived functor of the inclusion of
abelian sheaves into abelian presheaves on a small site is naturally isomorphic to the functor
sending an abelian sheaf to its degree-`p` cohomology presheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def rightDerivedSheafToPresheafIso (p : ℕ) :
    (sheafToPresheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightDerived p ≅
      Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor J p

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_sheafCohomologyAbutment
declarations.doc:
**The Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence of a covering family, for a single abelian
sheaf.** For a family `𝒰 = E` generating a covering sieve on `U` and an abelian sheaf `F` there
is a cohomological spectral sequence with second page

```
E₂^{p,q} ≅ Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F))
```

abutting to a graded family whose value in degree `n : ℕ` is the sheaf cohomology `H^n(U, F)`.

This is `Stacks.CechSite.exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_cohomologyAbutment` with its
abutment read through `Stacks.CechSite.rightDerivedPlus_sheafIncl_obj_obj_iso`; the abutment is
indexed by `ℤ`, as `CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo` requires, and the identification is
stated in the nonnegative degrees, which are the ones a first-quadrant spectral sequence
contributes to. Functoriality of the spectral sequence in `F` is not asserted; see the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_sheafCohomologyAbutment
    (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U) (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    ∃ (S : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0) (H : ℤ → AddCommGrpCat.{u}),
      (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty ((S.page 2 zero_le_two).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅
        cechCohomology E (F.cohomologyPresheaf q) p)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty (H (n : ℤ) ≅ (F.cohomologyPresheaf n).obj (op U))) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S H
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence, its second page and its convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologySheafCohomologyAbutment
declarations.doc:
**The abutment clause of [Stacks, Tag 03AZ]**: the functorial Čech-to-cohomology spectral
sequence of a covering family `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` abuts, through a finite decreasing filtration whose
graded pieces are its infinity terms, to the sheaf cohomology `H^{p+q}(U, F)` — all of it
naturally in the abelian sheaf `F`.

Together with `Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor` and
`Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyPageTwoIso` this is the whole of [Stacks, Tag 03AZ] in functorial
form: a functor from abelian sheaves to first-quadrant `E₂` cohomological spectral sequences, a
natural identification of its second page with `Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F))` and a functorial filtered
abutment to `H^{p+q}(U, F)`.

It is `Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyFunctorialAbutment` with its abutment transported along
`Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyAbutmentIso`;
`Stacks.Cohomology.Leray.FunctorialFirstQuadrantAbutsTo.ofIsoAbutment` touches no other field --
the asserted abutment is mentioned in `abutmentIso` alone, so the filtration, its finiteness, its
top and bottom steps and the graded identification are the ones already proved.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechToCohomologySheafCohomologyAbutment (hE : E.presieve₀ ∈ J U) :
    FunctorialFirstQuadrantAbutsTo
      (cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor J.toGrothendieck E)
      (fun n ↦ Sheaf.cohomologyPresheafFunctor J.toGrothendieck n ⋙
        (evaluation Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj (op U))
declarations.comment: the abutment of the functorial spectral sequence is `H^{p+q}(U, F)`

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence of a family of morphisms, as a functor of the
abelian sheaf.** This is the last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 03AZ]: the spectral sequence whose
second page is `Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F))` is functorial in `F`.

It is the first-quadrant `E₂` cohomological spectral sequence of the double complex
`A^{i,j}(F) = Č^j(𝒰, I^i(F))` of the Čech complexes of a functorial injective resolution of `F`,
obtained by restricting the two-variable spectral sequence of clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 01GY]
along `Stacks.CechSite.sheafToCechPair`. Its second page is
`Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyPageTwoIso` and its functorial filtered abutment is
`Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyFunctorialAbutment`; that abutment is the cohomology of the
total complex and is *not* identified with `H^n(U, F)` here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v} ⥤
    E₂CohomologicalSpectralSequenceNat AddCommGrpCat.{v}
declarations.comment: functoriality of the spectral sequence in the sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologyPageTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**The second page of the functorial Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence is
`Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F))`, naturally in the sheaf `F`.** Together with
`Stacks.CechSite.cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor` this is the functoriality asserted by
the last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 03AZ]: not merely that each sheaf has such a spectral sequence,
but that the assignment is a functor and that the second-page identification is a natural
isomorphism.

It is `Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.Functorial.hypercoverPageTwoIso` restricted along
`Stacks.CechSite.sheafToCechPair`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechToCohomologyPageTwoIso (p q : ℕ) :
    cechToCohomologySpectralSequenceFunctor J E ⋙
        CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.pageFunctor _ _ 2 2 ⋙
          HomologicalComplex.eval _ _ (p, q) ≅
      cechPageTwoFunctor J E p q
declarations.comment: functoriality of the second page in the sheaf

registrations.name: exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_cohomologyAbutment
registrations.comment: the spectral sequence and its second page

declarations.name: ModuleCat.flat_iff_restrictScalars_preservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03B8.**  Every injective `S`-module remains injective after
restriction of scalars along `f : R →+* S` if and only if `f` is flat.

The forward implication uses that extension of scalars along a flat map is exact.  Conversely,
if restriction of scalars preserves injectives, its left adjoint preserves monomorphisms; since
extension of scalars already preserves colimits, it is exact, and hence `S` is flat over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ModuleCat.flat_iff_restrictScalars_preservesInjectiveObjects
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) :
    f.Flat ↔ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u} f).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
A closed subscheme of the objects of a groupoid scheme is invariant when its
scheme-theoretic inverse images along source and target agree.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsInvariantClosedSubscheme {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (Z : G.objects.left.IdealSheafData) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantMonomorphism
declarations.doc:
A monomorphism of schemes into the objects of a groupoid scheme is invariant when its
source and target pullbacks define the same subobject of the arrow scheme.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsInvariantMonomorphism {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : T ⟶ G.objects.left) [Mono i] : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BC, part (1).**  A subset of the objects of a groupoid scheme is
invariant if every arrow starting in it also ends in it.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsInvariantSet {S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (W : Set G.objects.left) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BC, part (2).**  An open subscheme of the objects of a groupoid
scheme is invariant if its underlying set is.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsInvariantOpen {S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    (W : G.objects.left.Opens) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation.HasRepresentableQuotient
declarations.doc:
A pre-relation has a *representable quotient* when its quotient sheaf `U/R` is represented by
an object of the site.

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.HasRepresentableQuotient
declarations.doc:
A groupoid scheme has a *representable quotient* when the quotient sheaf `U/R` of its
pre-relation `(t, s)` is represented by an object of the site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev GroupoidScheme.HasRepresentableQuotient (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J (Type u)] (F : C ⥤ Over S) (G : GroupoidScheme S) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.det_lmul_targetMap_mem_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BH.** For a groupoid scheme with affine object scheme and finite
locally free source map, the norm along the source map of a function pulled back along the
target map is an invariant function.
declarations.statement:
theorem det_lmul_targetMap_mem_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] (f : Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤)) :
    letI := (sourceMap G).toAlgebra
    ∃ (hfinite : Module.Finite Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤))
      (hprojective : Module.Projective Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤)),
      letI := hfinite
      letI := hprojective
      ProjectiveDeterminant.det
          (Algebra.lmul Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤) (targetMap G f)) ∈
        invariantRing G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.norm_targetMap_mem_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
For a groupoid scheme with affine object scheme and finite locally free source map, the
arrow ring is a finite projective module over the object ring along the source map, and the
norm along the source map of a function pulled back along the target map is an invariant
function.
declarations.statement:
theorem norm_targetMap_mem_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left]
    (f : Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤)) :
    letI := (sourceMap G).toAlgebra
    ∃ (hfinite : Module.Finite Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤))
      (hprojective : Module.Projective Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤)),
      letI := hfinite
      letI := hprojective
      ProjectiveDeterminant.det
        (Algebra.lmul Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤) (targetMap G f)) ∈
          invariantRing G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_disjoint_invariant_rank_decomposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BI.** A groupoid scheme whose source map is finite locally free
decomposes by the rank into invariant opens. On each restricted groupoid, both the source and
the target map are finite locally free of that rank, and the rank-zero piece is empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_disjoint_invariant_rank_decomposition {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] :
    ∃ U : ℕ → G.objects.left.Opens,
      U 0 = ⊥ ∧
      (∀ r, IsClosed (U r : Set G.objects.left)) ∧
      Pairwise (Disjoint on U) ∧
      (⨆ r, U r) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ r, IsInvariantOpen G (U r) ∧
        let g : Over.mk ((U r).ι ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk (U r).ι
        let H := GroupoidScheme.restrict G g
        IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank H.groupoid.source.left r ∧
          IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank H.groupoid.target.left r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isIntegral_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
For an affine groupoid scheme with finite locally free source and target, the ring of global
functions on the object scheme is integral over its subring of invariant functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] :
    (Subring.subtype (invariantRing G)).IsIntegral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_over_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
For an affine groupoid scheme with finite locally free source and target, the ring of global
functions on the object scheme is integral over its subring of invariant functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_over_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] :
    (invariantRing G).subtype.IsIntegral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions_bijective_of_flat
declarations.doc:
For a flat extension of the invariant ring of an affine groupoid scheme, the canonical map
from the new base ring to the invariant functions of the base-changed groupoid is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions_bijective_of_flat {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {G : GroupoidScheme S} {C' : Type u} [CommRing C'] [Algebra (invariantRing G) C']
    [Module.Flat (invariantRing G) C'] (G' : AffineInvariantBaseChange G C') :
    Function.Bijective G'.canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_affineInvariantBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BK.** Extending the coordinate rings of an affine groupoid scheme
from its invariant ring produces the indicated groupoid scheme, with finite locally free source
and target.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affineInvariantBaseChange {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    (C' : Type u) [CommRing C'] [Algebra (invariantRing G) C'] :
    Nonempty (AffineInvariantBaseChange G C')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isNilpotent_of_mem_ker_canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions
declarations.doc:
Each element killed by the canonical map from the base ring to the invariant functions of the
base-changed groupoid is nilpotent.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_polynomial_map_eq_pow_X_sub_C
declarations.doc:
A positive power of the linear polynomial of an invariant function after base change comes
from the new base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_polynomial_map_eq_pow_X_sub_C {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    {C' : Type u} [CommRing C'] [Algebra (invariantRing G) C']
    (G' : AffineInvariantBaseChange G C') (f : G'.invariantFunctions) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (P : Polynomial C'),
      P.map G'.canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions = (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C f) ^ n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions_bijective_of_flat
declarations.doc:
For a flat extension of the invariant ring, the canonical map from the extension ring to the
invariant functions of the base-changed groupoid scheme is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions_bijective_of_flat
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {G : GroupoidScheme S}
    {C' : Type u} [CommRing C'] [Algebra (invariantRing G) C']
    [Module.Flat (invariantRing G) C']
    (G' : AffineInvariantBaseChange G C') :
    Function.Bijective G'.canonicalMapToInvariantFunctions
declarations.comment: part (3), flat extensions of the invariant ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.surjective_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BL.** The morphism from the object scheme to the spectrum of the
invariant functions is surjective on underlying topological points.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_objectsToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] :
    Function.Surjective (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G).base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.surjective_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BL.** Over an algebraically closed field, every point of the
spectrum of the invariant functions lifts to the object scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] :
    Function.Surjective
      fun x : Spec (.of k) ⟶ G.objects.left ↦ x ≫ objectsToInvariantSpectrum G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BL.** Over an algebraically closed field, two points of the object
scheme have the same image in the spectrum of the invariant functions exactly when they are
the target and the source of a common arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_objectsToInvariantSpectrum_eq_iff {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (u₀ u₁ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ G.objects.left) :
    u₀ ≫ objectsToInvariantSpectrum G = u₁ ≫ objectsToInvariantSpectrum G ↔
      ∃ r : Spec (.of k) ⟶ G.arrows.left,
        r ≫ G.target.left = u₀ ∧ r ≫ G.source.left = u₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.base_objectsToInvariantSpectrum_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BL.** Two topological points of the object scheme have the same
image in the spectrum of the invariant functions exactly when they are the target and the
source of a common arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem base_objectsToInvariantSpectrum_eq_iff {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    (u₀ u₁ : G.objects.left) :
    (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G).base u₀ = (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G).base u₁ ↔
      ∃ r : G.arrows.left,
        G.target.left.base r = u₀ ∧ G.source.left.base r = u₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isFiniteLocallyFree_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The morphism from the object scheme to the spectrum of the invariant functions is finite
locally free.
declarations.statement:
instance isFiniteLocallyFree_objectsToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source] :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isPullback_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The source and target maps exhibit the arrow scheme as the kernel pair of the morphism to
the spectrum of the invariant functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_objectsToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source] :
    IsPullback G.target.left G.source.left (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)
      (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)
declarations.comment: the relation is the kernel pair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.invariantSpectrumBaseMap
declarations.doc:
The structure morphism of the object scheme descends along the morphism to the spectrum of
the invariant functions.
declarations.statement:
def invariantSpectrumBaseMap {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsAffine G.objects.left]
    [IsAffine G.arrows.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source] :
    { f : Spec (.of (invariantRing G)) ⟶ S //
      objectsToInvariantSpectrum G ≫ f = G.objects.hom }
declarations.comment: descent of the quotient over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isIso_quotientSheafToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc:
