The spectrum of the invariant functions represents the fppf quotient sheaf of the
relation, and the representing isomorphism is compatible with the canonical projection from the
object scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_quotientSheafToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left] [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source]
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)] :
    ∃ hM : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (points (Over.post B.inclusion) (invariantSpectrumOver G)),
      IsIso (quotientSheafToPoints (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Over.post B.inclusion)
        (prod.lift G.target G.source : PreRelation G.arrows G.objects)
        (toInvariantSpectrumOver G)
        (target_comp_toInvariantSpectrumOver G) hM)
declarations.comment: representation of the fppf quotient sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isField_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03BM.** The ring of invariant functions of an affine groupoid scheme
with finite locally free source and target is a field as soon as the ring of functions on the
object scheme is one.  The ring of functions on the object scheme is integral over the invariant
ring by **Stacks 03BJ**, and the invariant ring is a subring, so the extension is injective; an
injective integral extension of a field comes from a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isField_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    (h : IsField Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤)) : IsField (invariantRing G)
declarations.comment: the ring of invariants of a groupoid on the spectrum of a field is a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.objectsToInvariantSpectrum_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc: The canonical map to the spectrum of invariant functions is finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
public instance objectsToInvariantSpectrum_isFiniteLocallyFree {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source] :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_objectsToInvariantSpectrum
declarations.doc: The source and target maps exhibit the arrow scheme as the kernel pair of the quotient.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPullback_objectsToInvariantSpectrum {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source] :
    IsPullback G.target.left G.source.left (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)
      (objectsToInvariantSpectrum G)
declarations.comment: the relation is the kernel pair

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quotientBaseMap
declarations.doc:
The map from the affine invariant quotient to the base scheme, specified by descent of
the original structure map.
declarations.comment: descent of the quotient over the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quotientSheaf_isRepresented
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of invariant functions represents the fppf quotient sheaf, with the
representing isomorphism compatible with the canonical projection from the objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotientSheaf_isRepresented {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.source.left] [IsFiniteLocallyFree G.target.left]
    [IsEquivalenceRelation G.target G.source]
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [HasSheafify (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u)] :
    let F : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS ⥤ Over S := Over.post B.inclusion
    let J := AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
    let j : Stacks.Groupoids.PreRelation G.arrows G.objects := prod.lift G.target G.source
    ∃ hM : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.Groupoids.points F (quotientOver G)),
      ∃ q : Stacks.Groupoids.quotientSheaf J F j ⟶
          (⟨Stacks.Groupoids.points F (quotientOver G), hM⟩ : Sheaf J (Type u)),
        IsIso q ∧
          Stacks.Groupoids.toQuotientSheaf J F j ≫ q.hom =
            F.op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map (quotientProjection G))
declarations.comment: representation of the fppf quotient sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BN.** A morphism between algebraic spaces over `S` is representable by
algebraic spaces: its base change along a scheme-valued point of its target is a fibre
product of three algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_isAlgebraicSpace
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07S4 for a presentation.** An algebraic space presented by a chart whose
underlying space is quasi-separated, with quasi-compact source projection, is
quasi-separated.

The relation of the presentation is the kernel pair of the chart, so
`presheaf_quasiCompact_pullback_snd_of_presentation` supplies the hypothesis of Stacks
07S4.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_presentation (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hseparated : QuasiSeparatedSpace ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U))
    (hsource : QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map P.source)) :
    IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space is *separated* when it is separated over the terminal scheme, that is,
when its absolute diagonal is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAbsolutelySeparated (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space is *locally separated* when it is locally separated over the terminal
scheme, that is, when its absolute diagonal is an immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAbsolutelyLocallySeparated (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space is *quasi-separated* when it is quasi-separated over the terminal
scheme, that is, when its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelyZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space is *Zariski locally quasi-separated* when its absolute form admits a
Zariski covering by quasi-separated open subspaces.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsAbsolutelyZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparated
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BU.** Points of an algebraic space are equivalence classes of its
field-valued points.
declarations.statement: abbrev points : Type (u + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint.hasCommonExtension_trans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BU.** Common extension is transitive: two extensions of a field-valued point
can be amalgamated over that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem FieldValuedPoint.hasCommonExtension_trans
    {p q r : FieldValuedPoint B S hS F}
    (hpq : FieldValuedPoint.HasCommonExtension B S hS F p q)
    (hqr : FieldValuedPoint.HasCommonExtension B S hS F q r) :
    FieldValuedPoint.HasCommonExtension B S hS F p r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FieldValuedPoint.class_eq_class_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BU.** Two field-valued representatives define the same point exactly when
they admit a common field-valued extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem FieldValuedPoint.class_eq_class_iff
    (p q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS F) :
    p.class B S hS F = q.class B S hS F ↔
      FieldValuedPoint.HasCommonExtension B S hS F p q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_pointsToScheme
declarations.doc:
The points of a scheme, viewed as an algebraic space through its functor
of points, are in canonical one-to-one correspondence with the points of the representing
scheme, the correspondence being `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsToScheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_pointsToScheme (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) :
    Function.Bijective (pointsToScheme B S hS U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation.pointsRelation_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BW.** Two points of the presenting scheme are related by the relation scheme
exactly when they have the same image in the algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointsRelation_iff (P : Presentation B S hS F hF)
    (x y : points B S hS (yoneda.obj P.U)) :
    P.pointsRelation x y ↔
      pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj P.U) P.toSpace x =
        pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj P.U) P.toSpace y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation.pointsMap_surjective
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03BW.** The atlas of a presentation is surjective on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointsMap_surjective (P : Presentation B S hS F hF) :
    Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj P.U) P.toSpace)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_pointTopologyFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03BX.** There is a unique family of topologies on the points of the algebraic
spaces over `S` which is the scheme topology on a scheme, makes every morphism of algebraic
spaces continuous on points, and makes an étale morphism from a scheme open on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_pointTopologyFamily :
    ∃! _t : PointTopologyFamily B S hS, True

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointTopology
declarations.doc:
The topology on the points of a presheaf on the big fppf site of `S`: a set of points
is open when its preimage under every scheme-valued point is scheme open.
declarations.statement:
def pointTopology (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    TopologicalSpace (points B S hS F)
declarations.comment: the underlying topological space of an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubspacesOrderIso
declarations.doc:
The order isomorphism from the open subspaces of an algebraic space over `S` to the open
subsets of its space of points, sending an open subspace to the image of its point set.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def openSubspacesOrderIso (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G} ≃o
      TopologicalSpace.Opens (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubspacesOrderIso_apply
declarations.doc: The open subset of points attached to an open subspace is the image of its points.
declarations.statement:
theorem openSubspacesOrderIso_apply (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (G : {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G}) :
    (openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS F hF G).1 =
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.1.toFunctor G.1.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_openSubspacesOrderIso
declarations.doc:
Taking the image of the points of an open subspace is an inclusion-preserving bijection
from the open subspaces of an algebraic space over `S` to the open subsets of its space of
points, and it is the unique order isomorphism doing so.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_openSubspacesOrderIso (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    ∃! e : {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G} ≃o
      TopologicalSpace.Opens (points B S hS F),
      ∀ G, (e G).1 = Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.1.toFunctor G.1.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.openSubspacesOrderIso_and_isZariskiCover_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 03BZ.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`.

Part (1): taking the image of the point set is an inclusion-preserving bijection from the open
subspaces of `X` to the open subsets of `|X|`; it is the unique order isomorphism doing so.

Part (2): a family of open subspaces of `X` is a Zariski covering exactly when the images of
the point sets of its members cover `|X|`.

Together these identify the small Zariski site of `X` with the site attached to the topological
space `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem openSubspacesOrderIso_and_isZariskiCover_iff
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (∃! e : {G : Subfunctor F // IsOpenSubspace B S hS G} ≃o
        TopologicalSpace.Opens (points B S hS F),
        ∀ G, (e G).1 = Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.1.toFunctor G.1.ι)) ∧
      ∀ (I : Type u) (X : I → Subfunctor F), (∀ i, IsOpenSubspace B S hS (X i)) →
        (IsZariskiCover B S hS I X ↔
          (⋃ i, Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (X i).toFunctor (X i).ι)) = Set.univ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZariskiCover_iff_iUnion_points
declarations.doc:
Open subspaces cover an algebraic space in the Zariski topology if and only
if their images on the space of points cover all points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZariskiCover_iff_iUnion_points
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (I : Type u)
    (U : I → Subfunctor F)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsOpenSubspace B S hS (U i)) :
    IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ↔
      (⋃ i, Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (U i).toFunctor (U i).ι)) =
        Set.univ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCovering_iff_iSup_openSubspacesOrderIso
declarations.doc:
Via the canonical identification with open subsets of the point space,
covering families of the small Zariski site are precisely open covers.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCovering_iff_iSup_openSubspacesOrderIso
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (E : Covering.{u + 1, u + 1, u} (OpenSubspaces B S hS F)) :
    let : TopologicalSpace (points B S hS F) :=
      pointTopology B S hS F
    OpenSubspaces.IsCovering B S hS F E ↔
      (⨆ i, openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS F hF
        (E.2.X i)) =
        openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS F hF E.1

declarations.name: contains_sBasis_of_generates
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a local ring with maximal ideal `m` and infinite residue field.
Let `R → S` be a ring map, `M` an `S`-module, and `N ⊆ M` an `R`-submodule.
If `S` is semi-local with `m S ⊆ Jac(S)`, `M` is finite free over `S`, and
`N` generates `M` as an `S`-module, then `N` contains an `S`-basis of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem contains_sBasis_of_generates
    {R S M : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module S M] [Module R M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [IsLocalRing R] [Infinite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)]
    (hSsemilocal : Finite (MaximalSpectrum S))
    (hmS : Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) ≤ Ring.jacobson S)
    [Module.Free S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (N : Submodule R M)
    (hN : GeneratesAsSModule S N) :
    ContainsSBasis S N

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_flat_residueField_algEquiv
declarations.doc:
**A residue field extension is realized by a flat local ring map** (Stacks 03C3). Let
`(R, 𝔪, k)` be a local ring and let `K` be a field extension of `k`. Then there is a local ring
`(R', 𝔪', k')` and a local ring map `R → R'` such that `R'` is flat over `R`, `𝔪' = 𝔪 R'`, and
`k'` is isomorphic to `K` as an extension of `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.exists_flat_residueField_algEquiv (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra (ResidueField R) K] :
    ∃ (R' : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : IsLocalRing R')
      (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')),
      Module.Flat R R' ∧
      (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R R') = maximalIdeal R' ∧
      Nonempty (ResidueField R' ≃ₐ[ResidueField R] K)
declarations.comment:
The lemma's preamble, a local ring `R'` and a local ring map `R → R'`, is the
`Algebra R R'`, `IsLocalRing R'` and `IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')` binders; the conjuncts are
flatness, `𝔪' = 𝔪 R'` as `Ideal.map`, and `k' ≅ K` as an extension of `k` as an
`≃ₐ[ResidueField R]`. `K` is allowed to live in a universe of its own, the source's case being
`v = u`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.FinitePresentation.of_isBaseChange_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03C4** (part 2). Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map, let `M` be an `R`-module
and let `f : M →ₗ[R] N` exhibit the `S`-module `N` as the base change of `M` along `R → S`. If `N`
is a finitely presented `S`-module, then `M` is a finitely presented `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem FinitePresentation.of_isBaseChange_of_faithfullyFlat {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (h : IsBaseChange S f) [Module.FinitePresentation S N] :
    Module.FinitePresentation R M
declarations.comment:
Part (2). Part (1) is `Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`
and part (3) is `Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`, both in Mathlib.

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.isIso_quotientSheafToPoints_baseOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03C5.** Let `τ` be one of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf
topologies, let `j : R ⟶ U ×_S U` be a pre-relation of `S`-schemes, and let `f : U ⟶ M` be a
morphism of `S`-schemes equalizing its source and its target. If `f` induces a surjection of
`τ`-sheaves on the functors of points, and if `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_M U` induces one too, then `M`
represents the quotient sheaf `U/R`: the canonical map `U/R ⟶ h_M` is an isomorphism.

The source's three hypotheses are `hf`, `hU` and `hR`, in that order. Nothing is assumed about
the functor of points of `M`: it is a `τ`-sheaf by
`Stacks.Groupoids.isSheaf_points_baseOver`, and neither `M` nor `R` is assumed to be an object
of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_quotientSheafToPoints_baseOver {R U M : Over S} (j : PreRelation R U) (f : U ⟶ M)
    (hf : j.target ≫ f = j.source ≫ f)
    (hU : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B S hS τ)
      ((Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft (yoneda.map f)))
    (hR : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B S hS τ)
      ((Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion).op.whiskerLeft
        (yoneda.map (pullback.lift j.target j.source hf)))) :
    IsIso (quotientSheafToPoints (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B S hS τ)
      (Over.post (X := B.obj hS) B.inclusion) j f hf
      (isSheaf_points_baseOver B S hS τ M))

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.comp_source_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square formed by composition, the second projection, and two copies of the source map
is a pullback square: a composable pair of arrows is determined by its first member together
with its composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_source_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback G.comp (pullback.snd G.source G.target) G.source G.source
declarations.comment: the lower composition square of the diagram: top map the composition, verticals the second projection and the source, bottom map the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable
declarations.doc:
The vertical map in the top left of the diagram: it sends a pair `(α, β)` with equal
targets to the composable pair `(α, α⁻¹ ∘ β)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.fst_source_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The square formed by the two projections of the scheme of composable pairs together with
the source and the target maps is a pullback square.  This is the lower-left square of the
diagram taken with the lower horizontal maps, and it is cartesian because the scheme of
composable pairs is by definition the fibre product of the source and the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem fst_source_isPullback {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    IsPullback (pullback.fst G.source G.target) (pullback.snd G.source G.target)
      G.source G.target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.id_target_comm
declarations.doc:
The upper-right square of the diagram commutes.  Both of its vertical maps are
identities, of the arrow scheme and of the object scheme respectively, and both of its
horizontal maps are the target map.
declarations.statement:
theorem id_target_comm {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    𝟙 G.arrows ≫ G.target = G.target ≫ 𝟙 G.objects
declarations.comment: commutativity of the upper right square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_fst
declarations.doc:
The comparison map preserves the first projection.  This is the lower of the two
commutative triangles in the top left of the diagram.
declarations.statement:
theorem targetPullbackToComposable_fst {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) :
    targetPullbackToComposable G ≫ pullback.fst G.source G.target =
      pullback.fst G.target G.target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a pair after the change of coordinates recovers its second member.  This is
the upper of the two commutative triangles in the top left of the diagram.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.targetPullbackToComposable_isIso
declarations.doc:
The vertical comparison between pairs with the same target and composable pairs is an
isomorphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.basis_over_invariantRing
declarations.doc:
A basis of the arrow ring over the object ring pulled back along the source descends to a
basis of the object ring over the invariant ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem basis_over_invariantRing {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    {I : Type v} (x : I → Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤))
    (h : letI := (sourceMap G).toAlgebra
      ∃ b : Module.Basis I Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤),
        ∀ i, b i = targetMap G (x i)) :
    ∃ b : Module.Basis I (invariantRing G) Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤), ∀ i, b i = x i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.tensorProduct_equiv_arrowRing
declarations.doc:
Under the same basis hypothesis, the canonical map from the tensor square of the object
ring over its invariant ring to the arrow ring is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_equiv_arrowRing {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    {I : Type v} (x : I → Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤))
    (h : letI := (sourceMap G).toAlgebra
      ∃ b : Module.Basis I Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤),
        ∀ i, b i = targetMap G (x i)) :
    let A := Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤)
    let B := Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤)
    let C := invariantRing G
    ∃ e : RingEquiv (A ⊗[C] A) B,
      ∀ a a', e (a ⊗ₜ[C] a') = sourceMap G a * targetMap G a'

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.shortExact_map_lim_of_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CA.** Let `R` be a ring and let `S` be a short complex of towers of `R`-modules,
that is of functors `ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat R`, which is short exact at every index: for each `i` the
sequence `0 → S.X₁ i → S.X₂ i → S.X₃ i → 0` is short exact. If the tower `S.X₁` satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition, that is for every `i` there is a `c ≥ i` with
`Im(S.X₁ c → S.X₁ i) = Im(S.X₁ j → S.X₁ i)` for all `j ≥ c`, then the sequence of inverse limits
`0 → lim S.X₁ → lim S.X₂ → lim S.X₃ → 0` is short exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem shortExact_map_lim_of_isMittagLeffler {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (S : ShortComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hS : ∀ n : ℕᵒᵖ, (S.map ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj n)).ShortExact)
    (hML : (S.X₁ ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{v} R)).IsMittagLeffler) :
    (S.map (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R)).ShortExact

declarations.name: isMorphismOfSites_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CB.** If `v : C₃ ⥤ C₂` and `u : C₂ ⥤ C₁` are continuous functors defining
morphisms of sites, then so is `v ⋙ u`: the left adjoints compose, and a composition of left
exact functors is left exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_comp
    {C₁ C₂ C₃ : Type*} [Category C₁] [Category C₂] [Category C₃]
    (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C₁) (J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C₂)
    (J₃ : GrothendieckTopology C₃)
    (v : C₃ ⥤ C₂) (u : C₂ ⥤ C₁)
    [IsMorphismOfSites.{w} v J₃ J₂] [IsMorphismOfSites.{w} u J₂ J₁] :
    IsMorphismOfSites.{w} (v ⋙ u) J₃ J₁

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMorphismOfSites.comp
declarations.doc:
The *composition* of morphisms of sites. If `f : D → C` is a morphism of sites given by
`u : C ⥤ D` and `g : E → D` is one given by `u' : D ⥤ E`, then the composite functor
`u ⋙ u' : C ⥤ E` is again continuous with exact induced functor on sheaves of sets, so it defines
a morphism of sites `E → C`, the composition `f ∘ g`.
declarations.comment:
The composition of two morphisms of sites is a morphism of sites, given by
  the composite of the two underlying continuous functors; this is what makes the
  composition of Stacks 03CC well defined.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.overShriek_sheafify_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CD**, packaged as the existence of the isomorphism
`j_{U!}(G^#) ≅ (∐_{φ : V ⟶ U} G(V →φ U))^#`.
declarations.statement:
theorem overShriek_sheafify_iso :
    Nonempty
      (((Over.forget U).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over U) J).obj
          ((presheafToSheaf (J.over U) (Type v)).obj G) ≅
        (presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).obj (presheaf G))

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationProducts.bijective_left_comp_prodSnd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CE(1).** The right adjoint of the localization functor
`j_U = Over.forget U : C/U ⥤ C` is `v : X ↦ X × U / U`: for `Y/U` in `C/U` and `X` in `C` the
map sending a morphism `Y ⟶ X × U / U` over `U` to its underlying morphism followed by the
projection to `X` is a bijection `Mor_{C/U}(Y/U, X × U/U) ≃ Mor_C(Y, X)`.

This is the counit description `Over.forgetAdjStar_counit_app` of Mathlib's adjunction
`Over.forgetAdjStar U : Over.forget U ⊣ Over.star U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_left_comp_prodSnd (Y : Over U) (X : C) :
    Function.Bijective fun g : Y ⟶ (Over.star U).obj X => g.left ≫ prod.snd

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationProducts.isMorphismOfSites_star
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CE(2), first half.** The functor `v = Over.star U : C ⥤ C/U` defines a morphism of
sites `C/U → C`: it is continuous, and the induced pullback on sheaves of sets is exact.

Exactness holds because `v` is a right adjoint, hence representably flat, so this is the criterion
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_representablyFlat` (Stacks 00X5).
declarations.statement: theorem isMorphismOfSites_star : (Over.star U).IsMorphismOfSites J (J.over U)

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationProducts.sheafPushforwardOverForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CE(2), second half.** The pushforward `j_{U*}` of the morphism of topoi attached to
the continuous and cocontinuous functor `j_U` agrees with the pushforward `v^s` of the morphism of
sites given by `v = Over.star U`; that is, the two morphisms of topoi coincide.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardOverForgetIso :
    (Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (J.over U) J ≅
      (Over.star U).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) J (J.over U)

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationProducts.sheafPullbackStarIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CE(2), second half.** Dually, the pullback `v_s = f⁻¹` of the morphism of sites
given by `v = Over.star U` is the restriction functor `j_U⁻¹` along `j_U = Over.forget U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackStarIso :
    (Over.star U).sheafPullback (Type u) J (J.over U) ≅
      (Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) (J.over U) J

declarations.name: StacksLocalizationProducts.sheafPushforwardObjEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CE(3).** For a sheaf `F` on `C/U` the sections of `j_{U*}F` over an object `X` of
`C` are the sections of `F` over `X × U / U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardObjEquiv (F : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type u)) (X : C) :
    (((Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (J.over U) J).obj F).obj.obj (op X) ≃
      F.obj.obj (op ((Over.star U).obj X))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc:
Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor of sites, let `C` have pullbacks and let `u` preserve
them. Then `Over.post u : Over V ⥤ Over (u.obj V)` is continuous for the localized topologies
`J.over V` and `K.over (u.obj V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_overPost_of_preservesPullbacks [HasPullbacks C] (u : C ⥤ D)
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan u] [u.IsContinuous J K] (V : C) :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).IsContinuous (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
declarations.comment:
Continuity of the functor `u' : D/V ⥤ C/U`, `V'/V ↦ u(V')/U`, which the proof of
  03CF asserts without argument and which is the input to every other clause. Proved here for `u`
  continuous with fibre products which `u` preserves, i.e. for Stacks' notion of continuity on
  sites with fibre products; see `Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_flat` for the flat version and
  the module docstring for why bare `Functor.IsContinuous` is not known to suffice.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF, continuity of `u'`, in the generality of 03CF.** If `u : C ⥤ D` is continuous
then so is the localized functor `Over.post u : Over V ⥤ Over (u.obj V)`.

By Stacks 00Y1 every sheaf on `D/U` is the fibre sheaf of a `K`-sheaf over `h_U^#`
(`OverShriek.sheafUnit`), and the restriction of such a fibre sheaf along `Over.post u` is the
fibre presheaf cut out on `C/V` by the restrictions along `u`, which is a sheaf by
`OverShriek.isSheaf_fiber_overPost`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_isContinuous {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {D : Type u}
    [SmallCategory D] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (u : C ⥤ D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K] (V : C) :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).IsContinuous (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
declarations.comment:
Clause (a), continuity half: `u' = Over.post u` is continuous whenever `u` is, with
  no finite-limit or flatness hypothesis. This supersedes the flatness-based
  `Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_flat`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF, clause (a), in the generality of 03CF.** If `u : C ⥤ D` defines a morphism of
sites `f : D → C` and `V : C`, then the localized functor `u' = Over.post u : Over V ⥤ Over (u V)`
defines a morphism of sites `f' : D/u(V) → C/V`.

Continuity is `Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_isContinuous`.  Exactness of `u'_s` is checked on
the terminal object and on fibre products: the former by
`Functor.preservesTerminal_sheafPullback_of_isTerminal`, since `Over.post u` carries `𝟙_V` to
`𝟙_{u V}`; the latter by `sheafPullbackOverPostIso`, `u'_s ⋙ j_{U!} ≅ j_{V!} ⋙ u_s`, together
with the fact that `j_{V!}` preserves and `j_{U!}` reflects connected limits (Stacks 00Y1) and
that `u_s` is left exact by hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (u : C ⥤ D) (V : C) (h : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).IsMorphismOfSites (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
declarations.comment:
Clause (a): the localized functor `u' = Over.post u` defines a morphism of sites
  `D/u(V) → C/V`, assuming only that `u` does. This is the clause Stacks derives from clause (c)
  via 00Y1, and which `Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost` covers only under 03EF's finite-limit
  and left-exactness hypotheses.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF, last assertion**: `f'_* j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1} f_*`, as a strict equality of
functors `Sheaf K A ⥤ Sheaf (J.over V) A` for an arbitrary target category `A`.

In Lean's left-to-right composition order the left-hand side below is `f'_* ∘ j_U^{-1}` and the
right-hand side is `j_V^{-1} ∘ f_*`.  Both are precomposition with the opposite of a functor
`Over V ⥤ D`, and the two functors agree on the nose by `Over.post_forget_eq_forget_comp`; this is
Stacks' remark that the identity "holds even for presheaves".

Clause (a) of Stacks 03CF, that `f'` is a morphism of sites, is
`Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites` in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/SlicePost/MorphismOfSitesGeneral.lean`, in the generality of
03CF.  Clauses (b) and (c) are proved in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/SliceTopos/InverseImage.lean`, also in 03CF's own generality.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq :
    (Over.forget (u.obj V)).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (K.over (u.obj V)) K ⋙
        (Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) =
      u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K ⋙
        (Over.forget V).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) J
declarations.comment:
Clause (d): the identity `f'_* j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1} f_*`, for sheaves valued in any
  category; also the last sentence of 03EF. Clause (a) is in
  Sites/SlicePost/MorphismOfSitesGeneral.lean and clauses (b) and (c) are in
  Sites/SliceTopos/InverseImage.lean, all three in 03CF's own generality.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.sheafPullbackOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
**The lower-shriek form of Stacks 03CF's computation**: `(f')^{-1} j_{U!} ≅ j_{V!} f^{-1}`.

This is the isomorphism `j_{U!}(f')^{-1}H ≅ f^{-1}j_{V!}H` displayed in the proof of Stacks 03CF,
obtained here not from Stacks 00WY but by taking left adjoints in
`sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq`: `(f')^{-1} ⋙ j_{U!}` is left adjoint to
`j_U^{-1} ⋙ f'_*` and `j_{V!} ⋙ f^{-1}` is left adjoint to `f_* ⋙ j_V^{-1}`, and those two right
adjoints are equal.  Uniqueness of left adjoints does the rest.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPullbackOverPostIso :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback A (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) ⋙
        (Over.forget (u.obj V)).sheafPullback A (K.over (u.obj V)) K ≅
      (Over.forget V).sheafPullback A (J.over V) J ⋙ u.sheafPullback A J K
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism `j_{U!}(f')^{-1} ≅ f^{-1}j_{V!}` of the proof of 03CF, deduced from
  clause (d) by uniqueness of left adjoints. As in the clause note on
  `sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq`, clauses (b) and (c) of 03CF are not covered; they
  are in Sites/SliceTopos/InverseImage.lean.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SliceTopos.sheafFunctorToOverCompOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF, clause (c).**  Under the identifications `Sh(C/V) = Sh(C)/h_V^#` and
`Sh(D/U) = Sh(D)/h_U^#` of Stacks 00Y1, the inverse image `(f')⁻¹` is "apply `f⁻¹` to the sheaf and
to its structure map":
```
  (f')⁻¹ (H ⟶ h_V^#) = (f⁻¹H ⟶ f⁻¹h_V^# ≅ h_U^#) .
```
The two sides agree after `Over.forget` by `underlyingIso`, and by `Over.comp_hom_of_terminal` the
remaining triangle need only be checked at the terminal sheaf, where `yonedaIso` was defined to
make it commute.
declarations.statement:
def sheafFunctorToOverCompOverPostIso (hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) ⋙
        sheafFunctorToOver (U := u.obj V) K ≅
      sheafFunctorToOver (U := V) J ⋙ Over.post (u.sheafPullback (Type u) J K) ⋙
        Over.map (yonedaIso J K u V hu).hom
declarations.comment:
Clause (c): under 00Y1's identifications `(f')⁻¹` sends `(H ⟶ h_V^#)` to
  `(f⁻¹H ⟶ h_U^#)`. Proved in 03CF's own generality, from `u.IsMorphismOfSites` alone, and with
  the identification `f⁻¹h_V^# ≅ h_U^#` given by `yonedaIso`, which is NOT proved equal to 04D3's
  `sheafPullbackSheafifyYonedaIso`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SliceTopos.overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF, clause (b): the square of topoi commutes.**
```
  (f')⁻¹ j_V⁻¹ = j_U⁻¹ f⁻¹ .
```
Unlike clause (d) this pairs *two inverse images*, so it is not a statement about right adjoints
and does not follow from `sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq`. It follows from clause (c)
instead: `Φ_U` is fully faithful, so it is enough to prove the square after applying it, and there
Stacks 04IQ (`OverShriek.overPullbackCompSheafFunctorToOverIso`) turns both `j_V⁻¹ Φ_V` and
`j_U⁻¹ Φ_U` into `toOver`, i.e. into "product with `h_V^#`" and "product with `h_U^#`". What is
left is `toOverCompOverPostIso`, that `f⁻¹` carries one product to the other.

The statement does not mention the identification `f⁻¹h_V^# ≅ h_U^#`, so — unlike clause (c) — it
does not depend on which identification is used.
declarations.statement:
def overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso (hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) :
    J.overPullback (Type u) V ⋙
        (Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback (Type u) (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) ≅
      u.sheafPullback (Type u) J K ⋙ K.overPullback (Type u) (u.obj V)
declarations.comment:
Clause (b): the square of topoi commutes, `(f')⁻¹ j_V⁻¹ ≅ j_U⁻¹ f⁻¹`. Proved in
  03CF's own generality, from `u.IsMorphismOfSites` alone. Clause (a) is
  `Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites`; clause (d) is
  `sheafPushforwardContinuous_overPost_eq`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SliceTopos.overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CF's clause (b) is the Beck–Chevalley mate of its clause (d).**

The comparison `(f')^{-1}j_V^{-1} ≅ j_U^{-1}f^{-1}` built from Stacks 00Y1 coincides with the mate
of the strict identity `f'_*j_U^{-1} = j_V^{-1}f_*`.  Since `j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^{-1}` is a bijection the
two transformations may be compared through their adjuncts, and those agree by
`shriek_overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso_hom_app_comp_counit` and
`overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostMate_comp_counit`.

This is what gives clause (b) computable components: every statement about the comparison can now
be read off the unit and counit composite defining the mate.
declarations.statement:
theorem overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso_hom (hu : u.IsMorphismOfSites J K) :
    (overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostIso J K u V hu).hom =
      overPullbackCompSheafPullbackOverPostMate J K u V
declarations.comment:
Clause (b) is the Beck-Chevalley mate of clause (d), which is what makes its
  components computable.

declarations.name: IsSpecialCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
A functor `u : C ⥤ D` from a site `(C, J)` to a site `(D, K)` is a *special cocontinuous
functor* if it is cocontinuous and makes `(C, J)` a dense subsite of `(D, K)`.
declarations.statement:
def IsSpecialCocontinuous {C : Type*} [Category C] {D : Type*} [Category D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (u : C ⥤ D) : Prop

declarations.name: DenseSubsiteOverSheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CH.**

Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `u : C ⥤ D` be a *special
cocontinuous functor*, formalized in Mathlib as
`Functor.IsDenseSubsite J K u`.  Fix an object `U : C`.  Then:

1. The square of underlying site functors commutes:
   `Over.post u ⋙ Over.forget (u.obj U) = Over.forget U ⋙ u`.

2. The induced functor `Over.post u : Over U ⥤ Over (u.obj U)` is again
   a special cocontinuous functor for the localized topologies
   `J.over U` and `K.over (u.obj U)`.

3. Hence, for any target category `A` with the appropriate limits,
   both vertical arrows in the induced commutative diagram of sheaf
   categories are equivalences:
     `Sheaf J A ≌ Sheaf K A` (right vertical), and
     `Sheaf (J.over U) A ≌ Sheaf (K.over (u.obj U)) A` (left vertical).

The Prop below packages all three conclusions.
declarations.statement:
def DenseSubsiteOverSheafEquivalence
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] (D : Type u') [Category.{v'} D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (u : C ⥤ D) (U : C)
    (A : Type w) [Category.{w'} A] : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.exists_isDenseSubsite_subcanonical_hasFiniteLimits_representable
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isDenseSubsite_subcanonical_hasFiniteLimits_representable {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {ι : Type max u v}
    (F : ι → Sheaf J (Type max u v)) :
    ∃ (D : Type max u v) (_ : SmallCategory D) (K : GrothendieckTopology D) (G : C ⥤ D) (_ :
      G.IsDenseSubsite J K) (_ : K.Subcanonical) (_ : HasFiniteLimits D)
      (_ : PreservesFiniteLimits G),
      (∀ (V : D) (ℱ : Sheaf K (Type max u v)) (i : ℱ ⟶ K.yoneda.obj V),
          Mono i → ℱ.obj.IsRepresentable) ∧
        (∀ i,
          ((G.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type max u v) J K).obj
              (F i)).obj.IsRepresentable)
declarations.comment:
Any topos is equivalent, by a special cocontinuous functor, to the topos of
  sheaves on a site which is subcanonical, has all finite limits, has all subsheaves of
  representables representable, and on which a prescribed set of sheaves becomes representable.
  This is conclusions (1), (3), (4) and (5); conclusion (2) holds for every topology and is
  `ofArrows_mem_iff_isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_uliftYoneda_map`. The functor is also recorded
  to preserve all finite limits that exist in the given site.

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.exists_twoSided_isDenseSubsite_representablyFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` be sites and let `f : Sh(C) → Sh(D)` be a morphism of topoi. Then
there are sites `(C', J')` and `(D', K')`, special cocontinuous functors `v : C ⥤ C'` and
`w : D ⥤ D'`, and a functor `u : D' ⥤ C'` such that

1. `v` and `w` exhibit `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` as dense subsites, so the morphisms of topoi
   `g : Sh(C) → Sh(C')` and `e : Sh(D) → Sh(D')` they induce are equivalences (Stacks 03A0);
2. `J'` and `K'` are subcanonical and `C'` and `D'` have all finite limits;
3. `u` is continuous, preserves all finite limits, is representably flat and defines a morphism
   of sites `C' → D'` — in other words Stacks 00X6 applies to `u`;
4. each `g_*(F i)` is a representable sheaf on `C'` and each `e_*(G j)` is a representable sheaf
   on `D'`, for prescribed families of sheaves `F` on `C` and `G` on `D`; and
5. the square commutes: `f_* ⋙ e_*` is isomorphic to `g_* ⋙ h_*`, where `h : Sh(C') → Sh(D')`
   is the morphism of topoi attached to the morphism of sites `u`.

Conclusions (1)-(4) are the source's conclusions (1)-(4) and (5) is the commutativity of the
square the source's remark is about.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_twoSided_isDenseSubsite_representablyFlat {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    {D : Type u} [SmallCategory D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type u)) (Sheaf K (Type u))) {ι : Type u}
    (F : ι → Sheaf J (Type u)) {κ : Type u} (G : κ → Sheaf K (Type u)) :
    ∃ (C' : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory C') (J' : GrothendieckTopology C') (D' : Type u)
      (_ : SmallCategory D') (K' : GrothendieckTopology D') (v : C ⥤ C') (w : D ⥤ D')
      (u : D' ⥤ C') (_ : v.IsDenseSubsite J J') (_ : w.IsDenseSubsite K K')
      (_ : HasFiniteLimits C') (_ : HasFiniteLimits D') (_ : J'.Subcanonical)
      (_ : K'.Subcanonical) (_ : u.IsContinuous K' J') (_ : PreservesFiniteLimits u)
      (_ : RepresentablyFlat u) (_ : u.IsMorphismOfSites K' J'),
      (∀ i, ((v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J J').obj (F i)).obj.IsRepresentable) ∧
      (∀ j, ((w.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) K K').obj (G j)).obj.IsRepresentable) ∧
      Nonempty
        (f.pushforward ⋙ w.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) K K' ≅
          v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J J' ⋙
            u.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u) K' J')
declarations.comment:
Any morphism of topoi fits into a commutative square with two equivalences given
  by special cocontinuous functors and a morphism of topoi coming from a functor `u : D' ⥤ C'`
  to which Stacks 00X6 applies, with both `C'` and `D'` having all finite limits and subcanonical
  topologies, and with prescribed families of sheaves on `C` and on `D` becoming representable on
  `C'` and on `D'`.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.kernelObjIso
declarations.doc:
**The kernel of a morphism of abelian sheaves is its kernel as a morphism of presheaves.**
The underlying presheaf of `kernel φ` is the presheaf kernel of `φ.hom`; the identification is
compatible with the two canonical inclusions, see `kernelObjIso_hom_ι`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kernelObjIso : (kernel φ).obj ≅ kernel φ.hom
declarations.comment:
(2) The kernel of a morphism of abelian sheaves is the kernel of the induced
  morphism of underlying presheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.mono_iff_presheaf_mono
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of abelian sheaves is a monomorphism exactly when the induced morphism of
presheaves is one.**
declarations.statement: theorem mono_iff_presheaf_mono : Mono φ ↔ Mono φ.hom
declarations.comment:
(3) A morphism of abelian sheaves is injective in the sense of Homology, i.e.
  a monomorphism, exactly when it is a monomorphism of presheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.mono_iff_injective
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of abelian sheaves is a monomorphism exactly when it is injective on the
sections over every object of the site**, that is, exactly when it is injective as a map of
presheaves.
declarations.statement: theorem mono_iff_injective : Mono φ ↔ ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (φ.hom.app U)
declarations.comment:
(3) A morphism of abelian sheaves is injective in the sense of Homology, i.e.
  a monomorphism, exactly when it is injective as a map of presheaves: injective on the
  sections over every object of the site.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.mono_iff_isLocallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of abelian sheaves is a monomorphism exactly when it is injective as a map of
sheaves.** Injectivity of a map of sheaves is Mathlib's
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsLocallyInjective`.
declarations.statement: theorem mono_iff_isLocallyInjective : Mono φ ↔ Sheaf.IsLocallyInjective φ
declarations.comment:
(3) A morphism of abelian sheaves is injective in the sense of Homology, i.e.
  a monomorphism, exactly when it is injective as a map of sheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.cokernelSheafifyIso
declarations.doc:
**The cokernel of a morphism of abelian sheaves is the sheafification of its cokernel as a
morphism of presheaves.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cokernelSheafifyIso :
    (presheafToSheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}).obj (cokernel φ.hom) ≅ cokernel φ
declarations.comment:
(4) The cokernel of a morphism of abelian sheaves is the sheafification of the
  cokernel of the induced morphism of underlying presheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.epi_iff_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of abelian sheaves is an epimorphism exactly when it is surjective as a map
of sheaves**, i.e. locally surjective: every section of the target is, on the members of some
covering, in the image.
declarations.statement: theorem epi_iff_isLocallySurjective : Epi φ ↔ Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective φ
declarations.comment:
(5) A morphism of abelian sheaves is surjective in the sense of Homology, i.e.
  an epimorphism, exactly when it is surjective as a map of sheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.AbelianSheaves.exact_iff_locallyLiftable
declarations.doc:
**A complex of abelian sheaves is exact at its middle term exactly when the sections of
that term killed by the second map lift locally through the first map.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_locallyLiftable (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w})) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ ⦃V : C⦄ (z : S.X₂.obj.obj (op V)), S.g.hom.app (op V) z = 0 →
      ∃ T : Sieve V, T ∈ J V ∧ ∀ ⦃W : C⦄ (p : W ⟶ V), T p →
        ∃ x : S.X₁.obj.obj (op W), S.f.hom.app (op W) x = S.X₂.obj.map p.op z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.exists_twoSided_isDenseSubsite_morphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CR.** Let `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) → (Sh(D), O_D)` be a morphism of ringed topoi.
Then there are sites `(C', J')` and `(D', K')`, special cocontinuous functors `v : C ⥤ C'` and
`w : D ⥤ D'`, and a functor `u : D' ⥤ C'` such that

1. `v` and `w` exhibit `(C, J)` and `(D, K)` as dense subsites and the morphisms of topoi
   `g : Sh(C) → Sh(C')` and `e : Sh(D) → Sh(D')` they induce are equivalences (Stacks 03A0);
2. the replacement structure sheaves are `O_{C'} = g_*O_C` and `O_{D'} = e_*O_D`, and the structure
   maps `g♯` and `e♯` are the identity;
3. `J'` and `K'` are subcanonical and `C'` and `D'` have all finite limits;
4. `u` is continuous, preserves all finite limits, is representably flat and defines a morphism of
   sites — in other words Stacks 00X6 applies to `u`;
5. each `g_*(F i)` is a representable sheaf on `C'` and each `e_*(G j)` is a representable sheaf on
   `D'`, for prescribed families of sheaves `F` on `C` and `G` on `D`; and
6. there is a morphism of ringed topoi `(h, h♯) : (Sh(C'), O_{C'}) → (Sh(D'), O_{D'})` whose
   underlying morphism of topoi is the one Stacks 00XC attaches to the morphism of sites `u`, and
   for which the square `(h, h♯) ∘ (g, g♯) ≅ (e, e♯) ∘ (f, f♯)` 2-commutes.

The source's addendum, on the case of an equivalence, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.exists_oneSided_isDenseSubsite_of_isEquivalence`.
declarations.comment:
Every morphism of ringed topoi fits into a commutative square whose two vertical
  arrows are the equivalences induced by special cocontinuous functors, with the replacement
  structure sheaves the direct images of the given ones and the two structure maps the identity,
  and whose bottom arrow comes from a continuous functor `u : D' ⥤ C'` preserving all finite
  limits, with both replacement sites having all finite limits and subcanonical topologies and
  with prescribed families of sheaves becoming representable on them. Conclusions (1)-(7); the
  addendum on an equivalence is `exists_oneSided_isDenseSubsite_of_isEquivalence`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.exists_oneSided_isDenseSubsite_of_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CR, the addendum.** If `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) → (Sh(D), O_D)` is an *equivalence*
of ringed topoi — that is, `f` is an equivalence of topoi and `f♯` is an isomorphism — then the
factorization of Stacks 03CR may be chosen with the two replacement sites equal, the two
replacement structure sheaves identified, and `(h, h♯)` the identity. Concretely there are a single
site `(C', J')` with all finite limits and a subcanonical topology and special cocontinuous
functors `v : C ⥤ C'` and `w : D ⥤ C'` such that, writing `g` and `e` for the equivalences of
ringed topoi they induce as in Stacks 03CR,

1. prescribed families of sheaves `F` on `C` and `G` on `D` become representable on `C'`; and
2. the middle morphism `(h, h♯)` is the identity: its underlying morphism of topoi is
   `MorphismOfTopoi.id`, its structure map `h♯ : e_*O_D ⟶ g_*O_C` is an isomorphism — this is the
   agreement of the two replacement structure sheaves — and the square
   `(h, h♯) ∘ (g, g♯) ≅ (e, e♯) ∘ (f, f♯)` 2-commutes.
declarations.comment:
the addendum: an equivalence of ringed topoi is factored over a *single*
  replacement site `C' = D'`, with the middle morphism of ringed topoi the identity — the
  identity morphism of topoi together with an isomorphism `e_*O_D ≅ g_*O_C` of the two
  replacement structure sheaves, which is the agreement of the structure sheaves the source
  asserts. See the module's implementation notes for why that isomorphism cannot be an equality.

registrations.comment: (2) and (3) morphisms of presheaves of O-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.ChangeOfRings.homEquivCore
declarations.doc:
**The canonical bijection of Tag 03CU.**

For `θ : O₁ ⟶ O₂` a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings, `G` a presheaf of
`O₁`-modules and `F` a presheaf of `O₂`-modules, the bijection
`Hom_{O₂}(O₂ ⊗_{p,O₁} G, F) ≃ Hom_{O₁}(G, F_{O₁})`.

It sends `ψ` to `x ↦ ψ_X(1 ⊗ x)` and its inverse sends `φ` to `a ⊗ x ↦ a • φ_X(x)`;
objectwise these are the two directions of the ring-theoretic extension/restriction of
scalars bijection `ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homEquivCore (θ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (G : PMod O₁) (F : PMod O₂) :
    ((changeOfRings θ).obj G ⟶ F) ≃ (G ⟶ (restrictScalars θ).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.ChangeOfRings.changeOfRingsAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Main statement of Tag 03CU.**

The change-of-rings functor is left adjoint to restriction of scalars,
`changeOfRings θ ⊣ restrictScalars θ`.  It is obtained from the bijection
`homEquivCore`, which it exhibits as natural in both variables.

The unit is `unitHom θ (𝟙 _)`, so it is `x ↦ 1 ⊗ x` on sections; see
`changeOfRingsAdjunction_unit_app_apply`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def changeOfRingsAdjunction (θ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) :
    changeOfRings θ ⊣ restrictScalars θ
declarations.comment: the adjunction: restriction and change of rings are adjoint
