declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.ChangeOfRings.extendRestrictScalarsAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03CZ**: extension of scalars along a morphism `α : R ⟶ R'` of sheaves of rings
is left adjoint to restriction of scalars along `α`. Concretely, for a sheaf of `R`-modules
`G` and a sheaf of `R'`-modules `F` there is a bijection
`Hom_{R'}(R' ⊗_R G, F) = Hom_R(G, F_R)`, natural in `G` and `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extendRestrictScalarsAdjunction :
    extendScalars.{v} α ⊣ SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{v} α

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ToposPushforward.pushforwardModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D1.** The direct image of a sheaf of `O`-modules under a morphism of topoi is
naturally a sheaf of modules over the direct-image ring, with scalar multiplication the direct
image of the original scalar multiplication read through the product comparison, and this
construction is functorial in the module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardModule
    (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type ww)) (Sheaf K (Type ww')))
    (O : Sheaf J RingCat.{ww}) : PushforwardModuleData J K f O

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ToposPullback.pullbackModule
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of a sheaf of `O`-modules under a morphism of topoi is naturally a sheaf of
modules over the inverse-image ring, and this construction is functorial in the module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackModule
    (f : MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf J (Type ww)) (Sheaf K (Type ww')))
    (O : Sheaf K RingCat.{ww'}) : PullbackModuleData J K f O

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.toposModulesHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D3**: the canonical bijection between morphisms out of an inverse-image sheaf
of modules and morphisms into the direct image, the latter read as a sheaf of `O`-modules by
restriction of scalars along the unit `O ⟶ f_*f⁻¹O`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposModulesHomEquiv (G : SheafOfModules.{w'} O)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (inverseImageRingSheaf f O)) :
    ((inverseImageModules f O).obj G ⟶ F) ≃ (G ⟶ (directImageModules f O).obj F)
declarations.comment: the canonical bijection `Hom_{f⁻¹O}(f⁻¹G, F) = Hom_O(G, f_*F)` itself

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.inverseImageAdjDirectImageModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D3** as an adjunction: the inverse image of sheaves of modules along a
morphism of topoi is left adjoint to the direct image, read as a sheaf of `O`-modules by
restriction of scalars along the unit `O ⟶ f_*f⁻¹O`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageAdjDirectImageModules :
    inverseImageModules f O ⊣ directImageModules f O
declarations.comment: the bijection as an adjunction, hence natural in both variables

registrations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.inverseImageAdjDirectImageModules
registrations.comment: inverse image left adjoint to direct image

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.tensorInverseImageAdjDirectImageModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D4** as an adjunction: for a morphism of topoi `f : Sh(C) ⟶ Sh(D)` and a sheaf
of rings `O` on `C`, the functor `G ↦ O ⊗_{f⁻¹f_*O} f⁻¹G` from sheaves of `f_*O`-modules to
sheaves of `O`-modules is left adjoint to the direct image `F ↦ f_*F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorInverseImageAdjDirectImageModules :
    tensorInverseImageModules f O ⊣ directImageModulesOverPushforwardRing f O

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.adjointPullPushModulesHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D4** as the displayed bijection
`Mor_{Mod(O)}(O ⊗_{f⁻¹f_*O} f⁻¹G, F) = Mor_{Mod(f_*O)}(G, f_*F)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointPullPushModulesHomEquiv
    (G : SheafOfModules.{w'} (pushforwardRingSheaf f O)) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} O) :
    ((tensorInverseImageModules f O).obj G ⟶ F) ≃
      (G ⟶ (directImageModulesOverPushforwardRing f O).obj F)

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.isRightAdjoint_pushforward_of_univLE
declarations.doc:
**The pushforward of presheaves of modules is a right adjoint**, with the universes of the
two sites, of their morphisms, of the presheaves of rings and of the module sections
independent. Instance, so that `PresheafOfModules.pullback φ` and
`PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ` are available with no adjointness
hypothesis; this is what Mathlib supplies only for small sites in a single universe.
declarations.statement:
instance isRightAdjoint_pushforward_of_univLE :
    (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: part (2), presheaves of modules at independent universes

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.isRightAdjoint_pushforward_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**The pushforward of presheaves of modules is a right adjoint** as soon as the source site is
essentially small in the universe of the rings and of the module sections, the target site being
locally small in that universe. Instance, so that `PresheafOfModules.pullback φ` and
`PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction φ` are available with no adjointness
hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
instance isRightAdjoint_pushforward_of_essentiallySmall :
    (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: part (2), presheaves of modules over an essentially small site

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.pushforward_isRightAdjoint_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Pushforward of sheaves of modules along a continuous functor of sites has a left adjoint**
as soon as the source site is essentially small in the universe of the sheaves of rings and of
the module sections. This is the existence half of the lower shriek for modules.
declarations.statement:
instance pushforward_isRightAdjoint_of_essentiallySmall :
    (pushforward.{v} φ).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of modules over an essentially small site

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pushforwardModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (1)**: the pushforward of a sheaf of `O_C`-modules along a morphism
of ringed topoi. As a sheaf of abelian groups it is the direct image `f_*F`
(`moduleSheaf_pushforwardModules`), and its scalar action is the restriction along the
direct-image form `f♯ : O_D ⟶ f_*O_C` of the structure map of the direct-image action of
Stacks 03D1 (`pushforwardModules_smul`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardModules :
    SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (2)**: the pullback of a sheaf of `O_D`-modules along a morphism of
ringed topoi: `O_C ⊗_{f⁻¹O_D} f⁻¹G`, i.e. the inverse image of Stacks 03D2 followed by
extension of scalars along the inverse-image form of the structure map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackModules :
    SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u', v', w'} Y.O) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, v, w} X.O)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (2)**: the pullback of a sheaf of `O_D`-modules along a morphism of
ringed topoi: `O_C ⊗_{f⁻¹O_D} f⁻¹G`, i.e. the inverse image of Stacks 03D2 followed by
extension of scalars along the inverse-image form of the structure map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackModules :
    SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u', v', w'} Y.O) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, v, w} X.O)
declarations.comment: part (2), for the two-field morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModulesCompIso
declarations.doc:
**The pullback of sheaves of modules along a composite of morphisms of ringed topoi is the
composite of the pullbacks**, `(g ∘ f)^* ≅ g^* ⋙ f^*`.

Both sides are left adjoint to `f_* ⋙ g_*`: the left-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModulesCompIso` transported across its adjunction,
the right-hand side because adjunctions compose. So they agree by uniqueness of left
adjoints.
declarations.comment:
part (2), pseudo-functoriality: the pullback of a composite of morphisms of
ringed topoi is the composite of the pullbacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePushforwardModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6 part (1) for the small étale sites of schemes.** The pushforward
`f_{small,*} : Mod(𝒪_{X_étale}) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_{Y_étale})` of sheaves of modules along the morphism of
small étale ringed sites of a morphism of schemes: the underlying sheaf of abelian groups is the
direct image, and the module structure is restriction of scalars along `f_{small}^♯`.
declarations.comment:
part (1): pushforward of sheaves of modules along the morphism of small étale
ringed sites of a morphism of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6 part (2) for the small étale sites of schemes.** The pullback
`f_{small}^* : Mod(𝒪_{Y_étale}) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_{X_étale})` of sheaves of modules along the morphism of
small étale ringed sites of a morphism of schemes, characterised as the left adjoint of the
pushforward.

The small étale site is not small in the universe of its structure rings, only essentially so,
which is why this is not an instance of Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.pullback` with its
`SmallCategory` hypothesis.
declarations.comment:
part (2): pullback of sheaves of modules along the morphism of small étale ringed
sites of a morphism of schemes, whose site is essentially small rather than small in the universe
of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.pushforwardTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (1).** The pushforward of sheaves of modules along a morphism of
ringed topoi: the underlying sheaf of abelian groups is the direct image `f_* F`, and the
module structure is restriction of scalars along `f^♯ : O_Y ⟶ f_* O_X`.
declarations.comment:
part (1): pushforward of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed topoi,
presented by a morphism of the underlying sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (2).** The pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed
topoi, characterised as the left adjoint of the pushforward. By `pullbackToposIso` it is the
sheafification of `O_X ⊗_{f⁻¹ O_Y} f⁻¹ G`, which is the formula of the source.
declarations.comment:
part (2): pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed topoi,
presented by a morphism of the underlying sites, both of which are small in the universe of
the sections of the structure sheaves; characterised as the left adjoint of the pushforward
and identified with the sheafification of `O_X ⊗_{f⁻¹ O_Y} f⁻¹ G` in `pullbackToposIso`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.pullbackToposGeneral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (2), at independent universes.** The pullback of sheaves of modules
along a morphism of ringed topoi, characterised as the left adjoint of the pushforward, with the
objects and the morphisms of the two underlying sites in universes independent of each other and
of the universe of the sections of the structure sheaves.  By `pullbackToposGeneralIso` it is
the sheafification of `O_X ⊗_{f⁻¹ O_Y} f⁻¹ G`, which is the formula of the source.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackToposGeneral (f : RingedToposSiteHom X Y) :
    SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
declarations.comment:
part (2): pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed topoi,
presented by a morphism of the underlying sites, with the object and morphism universes of the
two sites independent of each other and of the universe of the sections of the structure
sheaves; the source site is asked to be essentially small in that universe rather than small

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionUnivLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7**, with the universes of the two sites, of their morphisms, of the sheaves
of rings and of the module sections independent: for a continuous functor of sites and a
morphism of sheaves of rings, pullback of sheaves of modules is left adjoint to pushforward.
The adjunction supplies the natural bijection between morphisms out of a pullback and
morphisms into a pushforward.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionUnivLE :
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{v} φ ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pullbackAdjPushforwardModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7**, the ringed-topoi case: for a morphism of ringed topoi
`(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)`, pullback of sheaves of modules is left adjoint to
pushforward. The adjunction supplies the canonical bijection
`Hom_{O_C}(f^*G, F) = Hom_{O_D}(G, f_*F)`, naturally in both variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackAdjPushforwardModules :
    f.pullbackModules ⊣ pushforwardModules f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackAdjPushforwardModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7** for a morphism of ringed topoi in the sense of Stacks 01D3: pullback of
sheaves of modules is left adjoint to pushforward. The adjunction supplies the canonical
bijection `Hom_{O_C}(f^*G, F) = Hom_{O_D}(G, f_*F)`, naturally in both variables.

It is the adjunction of the modules development for the four-field morphism `toModulesHom`,
with the right adjoint transported along `toModulesPushforwardIso`.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackAdjPushforwardModules (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    f.toModulesHom.pullbackModules ⊣ pushforwardModules f
declarations.comment: for the two-field morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ModuleAdjunction.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7**, the ringed-site case: for a continuous functor of sites and a morphism
of sheaves of rings, pullback of sheaves of modules is left adjoint to pushforward. The
adjunction supplies the natural bijection between morphisms out of a pullback and morphisms
into a pushforward.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction :
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} φ ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleModulePullbackAdjunction
declarations.doc:
On sheaves of `𝒪`-modules on the small étale sites of schemes, at the module universe of
Stacks 0DDH, `f_small^*` is left adjoint to `f_{small,*}`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleModulePullbackAdjunction :
    smallEtaleModulePullbackLarge B T S f ⊣ smallEtaleModulePushforward B T S f
declarations.comment: the small étale sites of schemes, at the module universe `u + 1` of the étale cohomology comparisons of Stacks 0DDH rather than at the universe `u` of the sections of the structure sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleModuleInverseImageAdjunction
declarations.doc:
On the big étale sites of schemes, the inverse image `f_big^* = f_big^{-1}` of sheaves of
`𝒪`-modules of Stacks 04CC part (2) is left adjoint to the direct image `f_{big,*}`.
declarations.statement:
public def bigEtaleModuleInverseImageAdjunction :
    bigEtaleInverseImageModules B T S f ⊣ bigEtaleModulePushforward B T S f
declarations.comment: the big étale sites of schemes, where the pullback of sheaves of modules is the inverse image of Stacks 04CC part (2), at the module universe `u + 1`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackAdjPushforwardModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7 for the small étale sites of schemes.** The pullback of sheaves of modules
along `f_small` is left adjoint to the pushforward.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtalePullbackAdjPushforwardModules (a : X ⟶ Y) :
    smallEtalePullbackModules B a ⊣ smallEtalePushforwardModules B a
declarations.comment: the small étale sites of schemes

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.pointModuleAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7 at the point of a chaotic site**: lower shriek of sheaves of modules along
the point functor is left adjoint to restriction, at independent universes. The adjunction
supplies the natural bijection between morphisms out of `p_! M` and morphisms into `p^* N`.
declarations.statement:
def pointModuleAdjunction :
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{v} (F := Functor.star C) (R := R)
        (S := pointInverseImageRing C R)
        (𝟙 (pointInverseImageRing C R) :
          pointInverseImageRing C R ⟶ pointInverseImageRing C R) ⊣
      SheafOfModules.pushforward.{v} (F := Functor.star C) (R := R)
        (S := pointInverseImageRing C R)
        (𝟙 (pointInverseImageRing C R) :
          pointInverseImageRing C R ⟶ pointInverseImageRing C R)
declarations.comment: chaotic site over its point, at independent universes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.pullbackAdjPushforwardMapHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7 on unbounded homotopy categories**: degreewise pullback is left adjoint to
degreewise direct image, with the degreewise unit and counit. Both functors are additive, so
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategory` applies to the adjunction
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackAdjPushforwardModules` of Stacks 03D7.

This is the adjunction that Stacks 09T5 derives.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackAdjPushforwardMapHomotopy (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    pullbackMapHomotopy f ⊣ pushforwardMapHomotopy f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionTopos
declarations.doc: The pullback of sheaves of modules is left adjoint to the pushforward.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionTopos (f : RingedToposSiteHom X Y) :
    f.pullbackTopos ⊣ f.pushforwardTopos
declarations.comment:
ringed topoi, with the geometric morphism presented by a continuous functor
between the underlying sites and the two structure sheaves sharing the universe of their
sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.homEquivModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7**, the displayed bijection. For a sheaf `G` of `O_Y`-modules and a sheaf
`F` of `O_X`-modules, morphisms `f^* G ⟶ F` of `O_X`-modules correspond bijectively to
morphisms `G ⟶ f_* F` of `O_Y`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homEquivModules (f : RingedToposSiteHom X Y)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (f.pullbackTopos.obj G ⟶ F) ≃ (G ⟶ f.pushforwardTopos.obj F)
declarations.comment: the canonical bijection `Hom_{O_X}(f^* G, F) = Hom_{O_Y}(G, f_* F)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom.pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionToposGeneral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D7 at independent universes.** The pullback of sheaves of modules is left adjoint
to the pushforward.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackPushforwardAdjunctionToposGeneral (f : RingedToposSiteHom X Y) :
    f.pullbackToposGeneral ⊣ f.pushforwardTopos
declarations.comment:
ringed topoi, with the geometric morphism presented by a morphism of the
underlying sites and the object and morphism universes of the two sites independent of each
other and of the universe of the sections of the structure sheaves

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
registrations.comment: ringed sites: the adjunction attached to a continuous functor of sites together with a morphism of sheaves of rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.conjugateEquiv_pullbackModulesCompIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D8.** The comparison `(g ∘ f)^* ≅ g^* ⋙ f^*` of pullbacks of sheaves of modules
is the *canonical* one: its mate under the adjunctions `f^* ⊣ f_*` and `g^* ⊣ g_*` of
Stacks 03D7 is the inverse of the comparison `(g ∘ f)_* ≅ f_* ⋙ g_*` of direct images. This is
what pins down the normalization of the inverse-image comparison, the direct-image one being
normalized by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModulesCompIso_underlying`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conjugateEquiv_pullbackModulesCompIso_hom (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (g : RingedToposHom Y Z) :
    conjugateEquiv ((pullbackAdjPushforwardModules g).comp (pullbackAdjPushforwardModules f))
        (pullbackAdjPushforwardModules (g.comp f)) (pullbackModulesCompIso f g).hom =
      (pushforwardModulesCompIso f g).inv

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.instPreservesFiniteColimitsToSheaf
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor from sheaves of modules to abelian sheaves preserves finite colimits,
including cokernels. Together with its finite-limit preservation this says the functor is
exact.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance instPreservesFiniteColimitsToSheaf
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{v} R)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.toSheafKernelIso
declarations.doc:
Kernels of sheaves of modules correspond to kernels of abelian sheaves: the forgetful
functor carries the kernel of a morphism `f` of sheaves of modules to the kernel of the
underlying morphism of abelian sheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.toSheafCokernelIso
declarations.doc:
Cokernels of sheaves of modules correspond to cokernels of abelian sheaves: the forgetful
functor carries the cokernel of a morphism `f` of sheaves of modules to the cokernel of the
underlying morphism of abelian sheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exact_iff_toSheaf_exact
declarations.doc:
Exactness of sheaves of modules corresponds to exactness of abelian sheaves: a short
complex of sheaves of `R`-modules is exact if and only if the underlying short complex of
abelian sheaves is.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_iff_toSheaf_exact (S : ShortComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{v} R)) :
    (S.map (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{v} R)).Exact ↔ S.Exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.instAB5SheafOfModules
declarations.doc: Filtered colimits of sheaves of modules are exact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instAB5SheafOfModules (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) :
    AB5OfSize.{v, v} (_root_.SheafOfModules.{v} R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.toSheaf_preservesLimits
declarations.doc:
Forgetting a sheaf of modules to an abelian sheaf preserves all limits
indexed by diagram objects in the module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem toSheaf_preservesLimits :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{max u' v, v} (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{v} R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.toSheaf_preservesColimits
declarations.doc: Forgetting a sheaf of modules to an abelian sheaf preserves all colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem toSheaf_preservesColimits
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{v}] :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{max u' v, v} (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{v} R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules_preservesLimitsOfSize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DC, part (1).** The direct image of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed
topoi commutes with all limits, of every diagram size: it is a right adjoint, the left adjoint
being the pullback `f^*` of Stacks 03D6.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardModules_preservesLimitsOfSize (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    PreservesLimitsOfSize.{t, t'} (pushforwardModules f)
declarations.comment: part (1): the direct image commutes with all limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DC, part (1).** The direct image of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed
topoi is left exact. This is the finite case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules_preservesLimitsOfSize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardModules_preservesFiniteLimits (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (pushforwardModules f)
declarations.comment: part (1): the direct image is left exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules_preservesColimitsOfSize
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DC, part (2).** The pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed
topoi commutes with all colimits, of every diagram size: it is a left adjoint, the right adjoint
being the direct image `f_*` of Stacks 03D6.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackModules_preservesColimitsOfSize (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{t, t'} (f.toModulesHom.pullbackModules)
declarations.comment: part (2): the pullback commutes with all colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DC, part (2).** The pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed
topoi is right exact. This is the finite case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules_preservesColimitsOfSize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackModules_preservesFiniteColimits (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (f.toModulesHom.pullbackModules)
declarations.comment: part (2): the pullback is right exact

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsFree
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is **free** when it is a coproduct of copies of the structure sheaf,
that is, when some family of global sections exhibits it as such a coproduct.  The coproduct
is specified by its universal property, so no sheafification instance is needed.  This is
Stacks 03DE (1).
declarations.statement: def IsFree (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) : Prop

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsPresentedByGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules **has a global presentation** when it is a cokernel of a map between two
coproducts of copies of the structure sheaf, that is, when it is the right-hand term of an exact
sequence `⊕_{j ∈ K} O ⟶ ⊕_{i ∈ I} O ⟶ F ⟶ 0`.  The coproducts and the cokernel are specified by
their universal properties, so no sheafification instance is needed.  This is Stacks 03DE (6).
declarations.statement: def IsPresentedByGlobalSections (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) : Prop
declarations.comment: global presentation, at a single universe of sections

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules **has a finite global presentation** when it is a cokernel of a map
between two *finite* coproducts of copies of the structure sheaf, that is, when it is the
right-hand term of an exact sequence `O^{⊕k} ⟶ O^{⊕n} ⟶ F ⟶ 0`.  This is Stacks 03DE (7).
declarations.statement: def IsFinitelyPresentedByGlobalSections (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite global presentation, at a single universe of sections

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsGeneratedByGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is **generated by global sections** when some family of global sections
generates it, that is, when it admits a surjection from a free module.  This is
Stacks 03DE (3).
declarations.statement: def IsGeneratedByGlobalSections (F : SheafOfModules.{w} R) : Prop

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.IsGeneratedByGlobalSectionsOfCard
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is **generated by `r` global sections** when some family of global
sections indexed by a type with `r` elements generates it, that is, when it admits a surjection
from the free module on such a type.  This is Stacks 03DE (4).

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.localizedPullbackMapData
declarations.doc:
**The localized pullback datum of Section 03DG, for the quasi-coherent property.** Let
`(f, f♯) : (C, O) ⟶ (D, O')` be a morphism of ringed sites whose underlying functor `u : D ⥤ C`
is left exact, and let `q` be quasi-coherent data for a sheaf of `O'`-modules `M`: a family
`{W_i}` covering the final object of `D` together with a global presentation of `M|_{W_i}` for
each `i`.  Then the family `{u(W_i)}` covers the final object of `C`, and pullback along the
localized morphism of ringed topoi `(Sh(C/u(W_i)), O_{u(W_i)}) ⟶ (Sh(D/W_i), O'_{W_i})` of
Stacks 04J0 carries `M|_{W_i}` to `(f^*M)|_{u(W_i)}` and the structure sheaf to the structure
sheaf, and preserves colimits.

Section 03DG's method for defining an intrinsic property of modules asks, in its condition (3),
that the property be preserved by pullback along a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left
exact continuous functor; the functor that verification needs is the pullback along the
localized morphism of ringed topoi, and this is that datum for quasi-coherence.  The three
properties of it required are exactly the fields of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.QuasicoherentData.MapData`, and each is one of the property-agnostic
pieces above: colimit preservation is
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.preservesColimitsOfSize_localizedPullbackTopos`, the unit
isomorphism is `.localizedPullbackUnitIso`, and the identification of the transported module is
`.localizedPullbackOverIso`.
declarations.comment:
condition (3) of the method, for the quasi-coherent property: the datum needed to
  carry a global presentation along a pullback is the pullback along the localized morphism of
  ringed topoi of 04J0, and this constructs it

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackTopos_of_quasicoherentData
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-coherent clause of Stacks 03DO for a morphism of ringed sites presented by a
left exact continuous functor.** The pullback of a sheaf of `O'`-modules admitting quasi-coherent
data is quasi-coherent on the site.

The data is transported by `Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.localizedPullbackMapData` and the
transported presentations assemble into quasi-coherence on the site by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_mapData`.

This is the case to which Stacks 03DO's own proof reduces its quasi-coherent clause through
Section 03DG; the general statement, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackModules`, which transports this
one along the two equivalences of ringed topoi that Stacks 03CR produces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackTopos_of_quasicoherentData
    (q : M.QuasicoherentData.{ww}) :
    (f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment:
condition (3) verified for the quasi-coherent property: the pullback of a
  quasi-coherent module along a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left exact continuous
  functor is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-coherent clause of Stacks 03DO for a morphism of ringed sites, with the
hypothesis in the form the clause states it.** If a sheaf of `O'`-modules is quasi-coherent on
the site, so is its pullback along a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left exact
continuous functor.

Quasi-coherence may be tested on a single family covering the final object, by Stacks 03DN in the
form `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_exists_cover_hasGlobalPresentation`.  Such
a family `{W_i}` for `M` is carried to the family `{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.coversTop_mapObj`, and the global presentation of `M|_{W_i}` to
one of `(f^*M)|_{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.hasGlobalPresentation_over_pullbackTopos`.  No smallness
hypothesis on the slices of the target site is needed, for the reason recorded there.

This is the case to which Stacks 03DO's own proof reduces its quasi-coherent clause through
Section 03DG; the general statement, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackModules`, which transports this
one along the two equivalences of ringed topoi that Stacks 03CR produces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_pullbackTopos (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment:
condition (3) verified for the quasi-coherent property, with the hypothesis in the
  form 03DO states it: the pullback of a quasi-coherent module along a morphism of ringed sites
  presented by a left exact continuous functor is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFiniteFree_over_pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The localized pullback datum of Section 03DG, for the finite locally free property.** Let
`(f, f♯) : (C, O) ⟶ (D, O')` be a morphism of ringed sites whose underlying functor `u : D ⥤ C`
is left exact, let `M` be a sheaf of `O'`-modules and let `W` be an object of `D` on which `M`
is finite free, that is, on which `M|_W` is a coproduct of finitely many copies of `O'_W`.  Then
`(f^*M)|_{u(W)}` is a coproduct of as many copies of `O_{u(W)}`.

The three pieces of the localized pullback datum are what the transport consumes: pullback along
the localized morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 04J0 preserves colimits, carries `O'_W` to
`O_{u(W)}`, and carries `M|_W` to `(f^*M)|_{u(W)}`.  None of them mentions a property of
modules; the property enters only through
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFiniteFree_map`, which is the statement that finite freeness
is expressed by a colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteFree_over_pullbackTopos (W : Y.C)
    (h : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O).over W)
      (M.over W)) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteFree
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over (f.u.obj W))
      ((f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M).over (f.u.obj W))
declarations.comment:
condition (3) of the method, for the finite locally free property: the datum
  needed to carry a finite free cofan along a pullback is the pullback along the localized
  morphism of ringed topoi of 04J0, and this is that transport

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The finite locally free clause of Stacks 03DO for a morphism of ringed sites presented by
a left exact continuous functor.** If a sheaf of `O'`-modules is finite locally free on the
site, so is its pullback along a morphism of ringed sites whose underlying functor is left
exact.  This is the clause of Stacks 03DO for Stacks 03DL (2).

Finite local freeness may be tested on a single family covering the final object, by Stacks 03DN
in the form `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_iff_exists_cover_isFiniteFree`.
Such a family `{W_i}` for `M` is carried to the family `{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.coversTop_mapObj`, and the finite freeness of `M|_{W_i}` is
carried to that of `(f^*M)|_{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFiniteFree_over_pullbackTopos`.

This is the case to which Stacks 03DO's own proof reduces the clause through Section 03DG; the
general statement, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackModules`, which transports
this one along the two equivalences of ringed topoi that Stacks 03CR produces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackTopos
    (hM : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite M) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
      (f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M)
declarations.comment:
condition (3) verified for the finite locally free property: the pullback of a
  finite locally free module along a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left exact
  continuous functor is finite locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFree_over_pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The localized pullback datum of Section 03DG, for the locally free property.** Let
`(f, f♯) : (C, O) ⟶ (D, O')` be a morphism of ringed sites whose underlying functor `u : D ⥤ C`
is left exact, let `M` be a sheaf of `O'`-modules and let `W` be an object of `D` on which `M`
is free, that is, on which `M|_W` is a coproduct of copies of `O'_W`.  Then `(f^*M)|_{u(W)}` is
a coproduct of copies of `O_{u(W)}` indexed by the same type.

As for finite freeness, the three pieces of the localized pullback datum are what the transport
consumes, and the property enters only through
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFree_map`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFree_over_pullbackTopos (W : Y.C)
    (h : (M.over W).IsFree) :
    ((f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M).over (f.u.obj W)).IsFree
declarations.comment:
condition (3) of the method, for the locally free property: the datum needed to
  carry a free cofan along a pullback is the pullback along the localized morphism of ringed
  topoi of 04J0, and this is that transport

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The locally free clause of Stacks 03DO for a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left
exact continuous functor.** If a sheaf of `O'`-modules is locally free on the site, so is its
pullback along a morphism of ringed sites whose underlying functor is left exact.  This is the
clause of Stacks 03DO for Stacks 03DL (1).

Local freeness may be tested on a single family covering the final object, by Stacks 03DN in the
form `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isLocallyFreeOnSite_iff_exists_cover_isFree`.  Such a family `{W_i}`
for `M` is carried to the family `{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.coversTop_mapObj`, and the freeness of `M|_{W_i}` is carried to
that of `(f^*M)|_{u(W_i)}` by `Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isFree_over_pullbackTopos`.

This is the case to which Stacks 03DO's own proof reduces the clause through Section 03DG; the
general statement, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackModules`, which transports this
one along the two equivalences of ringed topoi that Stacks 03CR produces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyFreeOnSite_pullbackTopos (hM : SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOnSite M) :
    SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFreeOnSite
      (f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M)
declarations.comment:
condition (3) verified for the locally free property: the pullback of a locally
  free module along a morphism of ringed sites presented by a left exact continuous functor is

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.generatingSectionsPullbackTopos
declarations.doc:
**The localized pullback datum of Section 03DG, for the locally generated property.**
Generating global sections of `M|_W` are carried by the pullback along the localized morphism of
ringed topoi of Stacks 04J0 to generating global sections of `(f^*M)|_{u(W)}`, indexed by the
same type.

The transport is Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.GeneratingSections.map`, whose two hypotheses are
again pieces of the localized pullback datum: colimit preservation and the identification of the
two structure sheaves.  The identification of the transported module with `(f^*M)|_{u(W)}` is
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.localizedPullbackOverIso`.
declarations.statement:
def generatingSectionsPullbackTopos (W : Y.C) (σ : (M.over W).GeneratingSections) :
    ((f.toRingedToposSiteHom.pullbackTopos.obj M).over (f.u.obj W)).GeneratingSections
declarations.comment:
condition (3) of the method, for the locally generated property: the datum needed
  to carry a generating family of global sections along a pullback is the pullback along the
  localized morphism of ringed topoi of 04J0, and this is that transport

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.isLocallyGeneratedBySectionsOnSite_pullbackTopos

left exact continuous functor.** If a sheaf of `O'`-modules is locally generated by sections, so

Local generation by sections may be tested on a single family covering the final object, by

Such a family `{W_i}` for `M` is carried to the family `{u(W_i)}` by
`Stacks.Sheaves.LocalizedPullback.coversTop_mapObj`, and the generating sections of `M|_{W_i}`
to those of `(f^*M)|_{u(W_i)}` by

This is the case to which Stacks 03DO's own proof reduces the clause through Section 03DG; the

declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyGeneratedBySectionsOnSite_pullbackTopos

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.OverElements.extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
declarations.doc:
The presheaf whose sheafification is extension by zero has over `V` the direct sum of the
sections of `G` at the objects `(V, t)` of the site of elements, over all sections `t` of `K`
over `V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R)) (V : C) :
    ((PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := proj K) (R := R.obj)
      (S := (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R).obj)
      (𝟙 (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R) :
        (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R) ⟶ (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R)).hom).obj
          G.val).obj (op V) ≅
      (∐ extensionByZeroSummands K J JD R G V)
declarations.comment: for the site of elements of a presheaf of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
declarations.doc:
The presheaf whose sheafification is extension by zero has over `V` the direct sum of
the sections over all maps from `V` to `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (R.over U)) (V : C) :
    ((PresheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U) (R := R.obj)
      (S := (R.over U).obj)
      (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U)).hom).obj G.val).obj (op V) ≅
      (∐ extensionByZeroSummands J R U G V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso_inv_ι
declarations.doc:
The direct-sum comparison is the canonical one: on the summand indexed by
`φ : V ⟶ U`, its inverse is the unit of the presheaf adjunction at `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso_inv_ι
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (R.over U)) (V : C) (φ : V ⟶ U) :
    HEq (Limits.Sigma.ι (extensionByZeroSummands J R U G V) φ ≫
      (extensionByZeroPresheafSectionIso J R U G V).inv)
    (((PresheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{u}
      (F := Over.forget U) (R := R.obj) (S := (R.over U).obj)
      (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U)).hom).unit.app G.val).app
        (op (Over.mk φ)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DI**, the displayed bijection: morphisms of sheaves of `O_U`-modules
`G ⟶ j_U^* F` correspond to morphisms of sheaves of `O`-modules `j_{U!} G ⟶ F`.

This is the transpose of the adjunction `j_{U!} ⊣ j_U^*`, which is available with no
adjointness hypothesis because `sheafRestrictionIsRightAdjoint` discharges it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroHomEquiv (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (R.over U))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} R) :
    (G ⟶ (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U))).obj F) ≃
      ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U))).obj G ⟶ F)
declarations.comment: Mor(G, j_U^* F) = Mor(j_{U!} G, F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.extensionByZeroIsoSheafifyDirectSum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DI**, the direct-sum formula: the extension by zero `j_{U!} G` of a sheaf of
`O_U`-modules `G` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf whose sections over `V` are
`⨁_{φ ∈ Mor_C(V, U)} G(V →φ U)`.

That presheaf is `directSumPresheaf U R.obj G.val`; its sections over `V` are the displayed
direct sum by `directSumPresheaf_obj`, and its restriction maps are the restriction maps of `G`
between the summands by `presheafRestriction_ι_apply`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionByZeroIsoSheafifyDirectSum (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (R.over U)) :
    (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U))).obj G ≅
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R₀ := R.obj) (𝟙 R.obj)).obj
        (directSumPresheaf U R.obj G.val)
declarations.comment: j_{U!} G is the sheaf associated to V ↦ ⨁_{φ : V ⟶ U} G(φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.overMap_isRightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DI for a relocalization.** Restriction of sheaves of modules along
`Over.map f : C/V ⥤ C/U` has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement: instance overMap_isRightAdjoint : (SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} R f).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: extension by zero along a relocalization C/V ⥤ C/U

registrations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.sheafRestrictionIsRightAdjoint
registrations.comment: restriction to C/U has a left adjoint
