declarations.doc: The structure sheaf of the small étale site of `S`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def structureSheaf : Sheaf (topology B S hS) RingCat.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isSheaf_associatedPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf condition of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) at `τ = Zariski`.**  The presheaf
`T ↦ Γ(T, f^* F)` of [Stacks, Tag 03DS] satisfies the sheaf condition on the small Zariski site
of `S`: it is an fpqc sheaf on all schemes over `S` by [Stacks, Tag 03DT], and the presenting
functor of the small Zariski site is continuous.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_associatedPresheaf :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (topology B S hS)
      (Stacks.Sites.associatedPresheaf S F
        (inclusion B S hS ⋙ Over.post (X := (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Schemes)) B.inclusion))
declarations.comment: part (4) at τ = Zariski, the sheaf condition for `Fᵃ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) at `τ = Zariski`.**  The associated module `Fᵃ` of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `F` on the small Zariski site `S_Zar`, as a sheaf of modules over the structure
sheaf of clause (2).  Its sections over an open `T ⊆ S` are the global sections of the pullback
of `F` to `T`, and no sheafification occurs.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleOfSections :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isSheaf_associatedPresheaf'
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf condition of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) at `τ = étale`, with no hypothesis.**
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isSheaf_associatedPresheaf` with its argument discharged: the fpqc
sheaf condition it asks for is [Stacks, Tag 03DT], which
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCoherentPresheaf_isSheaf_fpqc'` proves unconditionally.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_associatedPresheaf' :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (topology B S hS)
      (Stacks.Sites.associatedPresheaf S F
        (inclusion B S hS ⋙ Over.post (X := B.obj S hS) B.inclusion))
declarations.comment: part (4) at τ = étale, the sheaf condition for `Fᵃ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleOfSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) at `τ = étale`.**  The associated module `Fᵃ` of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module `F` on the small étale site `S_étale`, as a sheaf of modules over the structure
sheaf of clause (2).  Its sections over an object `T` of the site are the global sections of the
pullback of `F` to `T`, and no sheafification occurs.

This is the construction [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) performs.  It is not
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, which is the pullback of sheaves of modules
along the morphism of ringed sites `(S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`; the two agree by
[Stacks, Remark 03FH], which for quasi-coherent `F` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoSectionsSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleOfSections :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
For every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}` the associated module `𝓕^a` of a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ`, in
the sense of Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (6).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
The associated module `𝓕^a` of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-module on the small étale site `S_étale`, in the sense of Modules on Sites,
Definition 03DL (6).

The corresponding statement for the small Zariski site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DV, clause (2), at `τ = Zariski`.**  The associated module `𝓕^a` of a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module on the small Zariski site `S_Zar`,
in the sense of Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (6).

The clause string records exactly the scope proved.  Clause (2) of the source
quantifies over `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}` — the two topologies for which Definition 03DU (4) defines
the functor at all — and this is the `τ = Zariski` half, for an arbitrary quasi-coherent `𝓕`; the
`τ = étale` half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`, so with
this declaration clause (2) is complete.  Clause (1) of the source, at all five `τ`, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModuleOfSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DV] (2) at `τ = Zariski`, for the sheaf the source constructs.**  The
associated module `𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) — the sheaf on `S_Zar` whose sections over an
object `f : T → S` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections` — is a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module in
the sense of [Stacks, Tag 03DL] (6).

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent` is the
same clause for the *pullback*-defined `𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; this is it read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`, which identifies the two, and
quasi-coherence on a site is invariant under isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModuleOfSections (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] : (associatedModuleOfSections B S hS F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2) at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections, whose sections over f : T → S are Γ(T, f^*𝓕). The same clause for the pullback-defined 𝓕ᵃ of Remark 03FH is isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent; the two sheaves are identified by associatedModuleIsoOfSections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hZeroBaseAssociatedModuleAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DW], clause (1), in the case `q = 0`.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `𝓕` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module and let `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.  There is a
canonical isomorphism

```
H^0(S, 𝓕)  =  H^0((Sch/S)_τ, 𝓕^a).
```

Cohomology of a site in degree zero is the group of global sections, that is the sections over a
terminal object; the open `⊤` of `S` is terminal both in the small Zariski site of `S` and, as an
object of the big site, in `(Sch/S)_τ`.  So the isomorphism is the identification
`Γ(S, 𝓕) = Γ(S, 𝓕^a)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleSectionsIso`, which is the unit of the
associated-module adjunction at a quasi-coherent module.

Only `q = 0` is asserted *by this declaration*, and only on this site: the big site here is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology`, five topologies on the one underlying
category of a chosen big fppf site.  Every degree `q`, on
`AlgebraicGeometry.overTopology`, is `AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`,
and clause (2) in its small étale half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`; both carry the tag.  For
`τ ≠ fppf` those two sites are topologies on different categories, so this declaration is not
subsumed by them and stays part of the covering set.  The small Zariski half of clause (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Topologies/Zariski/SmallZariskiQuasiCoherentCohomology.lean`),
which carries the tag as well.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def hZeroBaseAssociatedModuleAddEquiv (τ : SiteKind) (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ↥S) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (baseOverTopology B S hS τ) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
    Sheaf.H.{w} ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 ≃+
      Sheaf.H.{w} ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf B S hS τ)).obj
        ((baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj F)) 0
declarations.comment: the case q = 0 of clause (1), for every one of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DW], clause (1).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module and let `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.  In every degree `q` there
is a canonical isomorphism

```
H^q(S, ℱ)  ≅  H^q((Sch/S)_τ, ℱᵃ),
```

the right-hand side being the cohomology of the localized big `τ`-site of `S` with values in the
associated module of [Stacks, Tag 03DU].

`τ` is a bound variable, so this one declaration is all five topologies.  It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso` — the same comparison stated for
cohomology over the object of the site that `⊤` becomes — read through the identification of
cohomology over a terminal object with cohomology of the site, on both sides.
declarations.comment: clause (1), in EVERY degree q and for all five τ at once (τ is a bound variable), in the source's own shape: both sides are the cohomology of a SITE, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H, and not cohomology over an object of it. The Sheaf.H' carrier bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso states the same comparison over the object of the big site that ⊤ becomes; this is that statement composed with the terminal-object identification Stacks.Cohomology.TerminalCohomology.h'AddEquivH on both sides, the two objects being terminal by topIsTerminal and isTerminal_opensBelowToOver_top. Clause (2) is smallZariskiQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv together with smallEtaleQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DW], clause (2), the small Zariski link.**  For a scheme `S` in a big
Zariski site, a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `ℱ` and a degree `q` there is a canonical
isomorphism

```
H^q(S, ℱ)  ≅  H^q(S_Zar, ℱᵃ),
```

the right-hand side being the cohomology of the small Zariski site of [Stacks, Tag 020T] (2)
with values in the associated module of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) at `τ = Zariski`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso` read through the
identification of cohomology over a terminal object with cohomology of the site.
declarations.comment: clause (2), the small ZARISKI link H^q(S, F) = H^q(S_Zar, Fᵃ), in EVERY degree q, in the source's own shape: both sides are the cohomology of a SITE, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H. The Sheaf.H' carrier smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso states the same comparison over the object of S_Zar that ⊤ becomes; this is that statement composed with Stacks.Cohomology.TerminalCohomology.h'AddEquivH on both sides, the two objects being terminal by topIsTerminal and isTerminal_opensToSmallZariski_top. The other link of clause (2) is smallEtaleQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv and clause (1) is bigOverQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DW], clause (2), the small étale link.**  For a scheme `S`, a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `ℱ` and a degree `q` there is a canonical isomorphism

```
H^q(S, ℱ)  ≅  H^q(S_étale, ℱᵃ),
```

the right-hand side being the cohomology of the small étale site of `S` with values in the
associated module of [Stacks, Tag 03DU].

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso` read through the
identification of cohomology over a terminal object with cohomology of the site.
declarations.comment: clause (2), the small ÉTALE link H^q(S, F) = H^q(S_étale, Fᵃ), in EVERY degree q, in the source's own shape: both sides are the cohomology of a SITE, CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H. The Sheaf.H' carrier smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso states the same comparison over the object of S_étale that ⊤ becomes; this is that statement composed with Stacks.Cohomology.TerminalCohomology.h'AddEquivH on both sides, the two objects being terminal by topIsTerminal and isTerminal_opensToEtale_top. The other link of clause (2) is smallZariskiQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv and clause (1) is bigOverQuasiCoherentSiteCohomologyAddEquiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**Zariski cohomology of a quasi-coherent module agrees with its big `τ`-site cohomology**:
for a quasi-coherent module `F` on a scheme `S` and a degree `p`,

  `H^p(S, ℱ) ≅ H^p_τ(S, Fᵃ)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIso` at the whole scheme.  The object it
is taken over on the right, `(opensBelowToOver hS).obj ⊤`, is a final object of the big site by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_opensBelowToOver_top`, so the right-hand side is `τ`-cohomology of
`S` itself.

**This is [Stacks, Tag 03P2] in the case `𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ`**, for all five `τ` at once.  Together
with `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`, which is the case
`𝒞 = S_étale`, it is the covering set of the tag: the source lets `𝒞` be either of the two, and
these are one declaration per case.
declarations.statement:
public def bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj F) p ⊤ ≅
      Sheaf.H' (bigOverAssociatedSheaf S F τ B hS) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff τ B) hS).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (1), in EVERY degree q and for all five τ at once (τ is a bound variable) — the same statement as Tag 03P2 at 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ, Descent Proposition 35.9.3 and Étale Cohomology Theorem 59.22.4 being the same assertion in two chapters. In particular this is the POSITIVE-DEGREE case, which the q = 0 carrier BigFppfOver.hZeroBaseAssociatedModuleAddEquiv does not claim; the affine vanishing H^p(U, Fᵃ) = 0 that the source's proof passes through is isZero_sheafCohomology_succ_overAffine. The site here is overTopology on Over (base B S hS), not the BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology that the q = 0 carrier uses; the two are topologies on different categories for τ ≠ fppf and no bridge is claimed. Clause (2) is covered by smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso (the small étale half) together with smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso (the small Zariski half)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-coherent module `F` on a scheme `S` and a degree `p`, Zariski cohomology of `F`
agrees with small étale cohomology of its associated module:

  `H^p(S, ℱ) ≅ H^p(S_étale, Fᵃ)`.

The right-hand side is taken over `(opensToEtale S).obj ⊤`, a final object of the small étale
site, so it is étale cohomology of `S` itself.
declarations.comment: clause (2), the small étale half, in EVERY degree q — the same statement as Tag 03P2 at 𝒞 = S_étale, Descent Proposition 35.9.3 and Étale Cohomology Theorem 59.22.4 being the same assertion in two chapters. In particular this is the POSITIVE-DEGREE case, which the q = 0 carrier BigFppfOver.hZeroBaseAssociatedModuleAddEquiv does not claim; the affine vanishing H^p(U, Fᵃ) = 0 that the source's proof passes through is isZero_sheafCohomology_succ_smallEtaleAffine. NOT covered here: the small ZARISKI half of clause (2), which is smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso; clause (1) is bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**Zariski cohomology of a quasi-coherent module agrees with the cohomology of its associated
module on the small Zariski site**: for a quasi-coherent module `F` on a scheme `S` and a degree
`p`,

  `H^p(S, ℱ) ≅ H^p(S_Zar, Fᵃ)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiQuasiCoherentCohomologyIso` at the whole scheme.  The
object it is taken over on the right, `(opensToSmallZariski B S hS).obj ⊤`, is a final object of
the small Zariski site by `AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_opensToSmallZariski_top`, so the
right-hand side is the cohomology of `S_Zar` itself.

**This is the small Zariski half of clause (2) of [Stacks, Tag 03DW]**, in every degree.
Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`, the small étale
half, it is the covering set of that clause.
declarations.statement:
public def smallZariskiQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj F) p ⊤ ≅
      Sheaf.H' (smallZariskiAssociatedSheaf B S hS F) p
        ((opensToSmallZariski B S hS).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: clause (2), the small ZARISKI half H^q(S, F) = H^q(S_Zar, Fᵃ), in EVERY degree q. S_Zar is the small Zariski site of Tag 020T (2) and Fᵃ the associated module of Tag 03DU (4) at τ = Zariski, SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections. The object the right-hand side is taken over, (opensToSmallZariski B S hS).obj ⊤, is a final object of the site by isTerminal_opensToSmallZariski_top, so that side is the cohomology of S_Zar itself. The other half of clause (2), H^q(S, F) = H^q(S_étale, Fᵃ), is smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso; clause (1) is bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso. No 03P2 attribute: that tag lets 𝒞 be a big τ-site or S_étale and does not include S_Zar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DX (1) for `τ = fppf`: `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is an equivalence.**  The functor
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)` is fully faithful unconditionally
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite'`, Stacks 0GN7) and
essentially surjective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.quasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite_fppf :
    (associatedModuleQcohOnSite' B S hS).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: clause (1) at τ = fppf: 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a is an equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleEquivalence_fppf
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories of Stacks 03DX (1) for `τ = fppf`**,
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`, with `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` as its functor.
declarations.comment: clause (1) at τ = fppf: the equivalence of categories QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.bijective_restrictionBaseChange_affineChartModule
declarations.doc:
**A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on the small étale site of a scheme is cartesian over
every arrow of the small affine étale site**, for the chart rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_restrictionBaseChange_affineChartModule
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {X Y : (SmallAffineEtale B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (a : X ⟶ Y) :
    Function.Bijective (restrictionBaseChange.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (R := affineChartRings B S hS) (affineChartPresheaf B S hS G) a)
declarations.comment: quasi-coherent implies cartesian over the small affine étale site of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.bijective_restrictionBaseChange_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent sheaf of modules on the small étale site of a scheme is cartesian between
affine objects: for a morphism `f : T ⟶ T'` of objects of `S_étale` whose underlying schemes are
affine, the base-change comparison `Γ(T) ⊗_{Γ(T')} 𝒢(T') ⟶ 𝒢(T)` is bijective.

This is a step of Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = étale`, whose statement as an equivalence of categories
is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_restrictionBaseChange_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {T T' : SmallEtale B S hS}
    (hT : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine ((toScheme B S hS).obj T))
    (hT' : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine ((toScheme B S hS).obj T'))
    (f : T ⟶ T') :
    Function.Bijective
      (restrictionBaseChange (R := commStructurePresheaf B S hS) G.val f.op)
declarations.comment: quasi-coherent implies cartesian between affine objects of the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DX clause (2) at `τ = Zariski`**: `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is an equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)`.

`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsEquivalence` is fullness, faithfulness and essential surjectivity
together, which is the decomposition the source's proof uses: Stacks 03DV (2) for the functor,
Stacks 0GN7 for full faithfulness, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherent_restrictModule` for essential surjectivity.
Clause (2) also ranges over `τ = étale`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite'`; clause (1), over the
big sites, is untouched here.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohOnSite B S hS).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: clause (2) at τ = Zariski: 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a is an equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories of Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = Zariski`**,
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, with `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` as its functor.

The source states the clause as an equivalence rather than as the three properties of the
functor, and this is that statement; its `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohOnSite` by definition.
declarations.comment: clause (2) at τ = Zariski: the equivalence of categories QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isEquivalence_associatedSheafFunctorOnSite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03DX] clause (2) at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source defines**: the
sections-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) is an equivalence
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite` is the same clause for
the pullback-defined functor of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; this is it read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor`.  The
decomposition is the source's own: [Stacks, Tag 03DV] (2) for the functor,
[Stacks, Tag 0GN7] for full faithfulness, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherent_restrictModule` for essential surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_associatedSheafFunctorOnSite :
    (associatedSheafFunctorOnSite B S hS).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: clause (2) at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor corestricted to QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪) — is an equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪). The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is isEquivalence_associatedModuleQcohOnSite; the two functors are identified by associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctorEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of categories of [Stacks, Tag 03DX] (2) at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor
the source defines**: `QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, with the sections-defined `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` as its
functor.

The source states the clause as an equivalence rather than as the three properties of the
functor, and this is that statement; its `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctorOnSite` by definition.  Its
pullback-defined counterpart is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleEquivalence`.
declarations.comment: clause (2) at τ = Zariski, the equivalence of categories QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪) whose functor is the SECTIONS-defined 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4), SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor corestricted to QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪). The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is associatedModuleEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleEquivalenceOnSite'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DX (1) at every `τ`, as an equivalence of categories**:
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, with `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` as its functor and with no hypothesis.
declarations.comment: clause (1) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}: 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ is an equivalence QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePresentation.hasGlobalPresentation_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DX, the presentation step, on the Zariski site.**  A quasi-coherent
`𝒪_T`-module on an affine scheme `T` has a *global* presentation: it is the module associated
with a module over the coordinate ring `Γ(T, ⊤)`, and a presentation of that module by
generators and relations transports to a presentation of the sheaf over the whole of `T`.

Quasi-coherence here is `SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite`, Stacks 03DL(6), which asks only
for a presentation *locally*; the content of the step is that on an affine no covering is
needed.  The two quasi-coherence predicates agree on the Zariski site by
`SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, whose size hypothesis is automatic
there.

The clause string records exactly this much: a quasi-coherent module on an affine has a global
presentation.  Stacks 03DX states its clauses as equivalences of categories, and those are
carried by the declarations named in the module docstring, whose descent arguments consume what
is proved here; the same statement at an affine object of the big fppf site is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hasGlobalPresentation_over_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasGlobalPresentation_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T]
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} T.ringCatSheaf) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    M.HasGlobalPresentation
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent module on an affine has a global presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The forward half of the chart criterion for quasi-coherence on the small étale site of an
algebraic space**: a quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-module, with sections in the universe of the schemes, is
cartesian on affine charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsCartesianOnAffineCharts G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts
declarations.doc:
**The chart criterion for quasi-coherence on the small étale site of an algebraic space**: an
`𝒪_F`-module, with sections in the universe of the schemes, is quasi-coherent if and only if it
is cartesian on affine charts.  The base `F` is an algebraic space, and the statement is a
criterion on a single module rather than the equivalence of categories
`QCoh(𝒪_S) ⥤ QCoh(S_étale, 𝒪)` for a scheme `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔ IsCartesianOnAffineCharts G

registrations.name: baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_yoneda_spec_of_surjective_etale_fieldSpec
declarations.doc:
A quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` admitting a surjective étale morphism from the
spectrum of a field `k` is the spectrum of a field `k'`, and `k` is a finite separable extension
of `k'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_yoneda_spec_of_surjective_etale_fieldSpec
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal F)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {U : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (eU : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U ≅ Spec (.of k)) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hetale : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k' k) (_ : Module.Finite k' k)
      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k' k) (U' : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (eU' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U' ≅ Spec (.of k'))
      (m : U ⟶ U') (e : F ≅ yoneda.obj U'),
      f ≫ e.hom = yoneda.map m ∧
        eU.inv ≫ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map m ≫ eU'.hom =
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' k))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_field_spectrum_of_surjective_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03DZ.** Let `S` be a scheme, `k` a field and `X` an algebraic space over `S`
admitting a surjective étale morphism `Spec(k) ⟶ X`. If `X` is quasi-separated — Stacks 03BS
part (3), that is, quasi-separated over `Spec(ℤ)` — then `X` is isomorphic to `Spec(k')` for a
field `k'` with `k/k'` finite separable, the isomorphism carrying the given atlas to the
morphism induced by the field extension.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_field_spectrum_of_surjective_etale_of_isQuasiSeparatedOver`,
which asks only for quasi-separatedness over `S` and is therefore stronger, together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparatedOver_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated`.
Surjectivity is taken in the sense of Stacks 03ME, that the induced map on points is
surjective, which is the source's reading; the engine asks instead that every represented base
change be a surjective morphism of schemes, and the two agree for a morphism into an algebraic
space by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafSurjective_of_isSurjective`, whose representability
hypothesis is supplied by the representable diagonal of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_field_spectrum_of_surjective_etale
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ S)
    (f : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b⟩ : B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hS)) ⟶ F)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hetale : (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k' k)
      (_ : Module.Finite k' k) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k' k)
      (hk' : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')))
      (b' : Spec (CommRingCat.of k') ⟶ S),
      ∃ (hbase : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' k)) ≫ b' = b)
        (e : F ≅ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (⟨b'⟩ : B.obj hk' ⟶ B.obj hS))),
        f ≫ e.hom = yoneda.map (Over.homMk
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' k))) :
            B.obj hk ⟶ B.obj hk') (by
              apply ObjectProperty.hom_ext
              exact hbase))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.iso_of_mono_of_point_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E1.** Monomorphic field-valued representatives of the same point are
isomorphic over the algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem iso_of_mono_of_point_eq
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (p q : FieldValuedPoint B S hS F)
    [Mono (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)] [Mono (yonedaEquiv.symm q.value)]
    (heq : p.class B S hS F = q.class B S hS F) :
    ∃ e : p.siteObject B S hS F ≅ q.siteObject B S hS F,
      F.map e.hom.op q.value = p.value

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E3.** An algebraic space over `S` is *quasi-compact* when it admits a
surjective étale morphism from a representable presheaf whose underlying scheme is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiCompactSpace (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompactSpaceULift_iff_compactSpace_pointsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E4** for a value universe `max w u` independent of the universe `u` of the
schemes: an algebraic space over `S` is quasi-compact if and only if its space of points is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactSpaceULift_iff_compactSpace_pointsULift
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{w} B S hS F) :
    IsQuasiCompactSpaceULift.{w} B S hS F ↔ CompactSpace (pointsULift.{w} B S hS F)
declarations.comment: for a value universe independent of the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompactSpace_iff_compactSpace_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E4.** An algebraic space over `S` is quasi-compact if and only if its space of
points is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactSpace_iff_compactSpace_points
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS F ↔ CompactSpace (points B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E6.** An algebraic space has an étale-local property of schemes if it has a
surjective étale atlas by a scheme with that property.
declarations.statement: abbrev HasEtaleLocalProperty : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jacobsonSpace_isLocal_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03E7, item (2).** Being a Jacobson scheme is local for étale
coverings of schemes: a scheme is Jacobson if and only if the members of an étale covering
family are.

This is Stacks 0368, which gives the fppf case, read through the inclusion of the étale
precoverage in the fppf one.
declarations.statement:
instance jacobsonSpace_isLocal_etale :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal (fun X : Scheme.{u} => JacobsonSpace X) Scheme.etalePrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_and_hasPropertySk_isLocal_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03E7, item (3).** Being locally Noetherian and satisfying Serre's
condition `(S_k)` is local for étale coverings of schemes.

This is Stacks 036A, which gives the syntomic case, read through the inclusion of the étale
precoverage in the syntomic one.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyNoetherian_and_hasPropertySk_isLocal_etale (k : ℕ) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} => ∃ h : IsLocallyNoetherian X, @HasPropertySk X h k)
      Scheme.etalePrecoverage
declarations.comment: item (3): locally Noetherian and (S_k), by Stacks 036A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCohenMacaulay_isLocal_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03E7, item (4).** Being a Cohen-Macaulay scheme is local for étale
coverings of schemes.

This is Stacks 036B, which gives the syntomic case, read through the inclusion of the étale
precoverage in the syntomic one.
declarations.statement:
instance isCohenMacaulay_isLocal_etale :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsCohenMacaulay X) Scheme.etalePrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_isLocal_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03E7, item (5).** Being a Gorenstein scheme is local for étale
coverings of schemes: a scheme is Gorenstein if and only if the members of an étale covering
family are.

The source cites Stacks 0C01, which states the syntomic case; only the étale case is proved
here. Ascent is `AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_of_etale`. For descent, local Noetherianity
of the base is item (1), and the Gorenstein condition on the stalk at a point of the base is
transported from a point of a member of the family above it.
declarations.statement:
instance isGorenstein_isLocal_etale :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsGorenstein X) Scheme.etalePrecoverage
declarations.comment: item (5): Gorenstein, the étale case of Stacks 0C01

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_and_isRegularInCodimension_isLocal_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03E7, item (8).** Being locally Noetherian and regular in
codimension `k` is local for étale coverings of schemes.

This is Stacks 036C, which gives the smooth case, read through the inclusion of the étale
precoverage in the smooth one.
declarations.statement:
instance isLocallyNoetherian_and_isRegularInCodimension_isLocal_etale (k : ℕ) :
    ObjectProperty.IsLocal
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X ∧ IsRegularInCodimension X k)
      Scheme.etalePrecoverage
declarations.comment: item (8): locally Noetherian and (R_k), by Stacks 036C

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_atlas_iff_forall_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E8.** An étale-local property holds on some surjective étale atlas exactly
when it holds on every étale scheme over the algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_atlas_iff_forall_etale (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F P ↔
    (∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g →
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_atlas_iff_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03E8.** For a represented algebraic space, the atlas condition is equivalent
to the property of its representing scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_atlas_iff_of_representable
    (X : BigFppfOver B S hS) (e : F ≅ yoneda.obj X) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F P ↔ P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsNoetherian
declarations.doc:
An algebraic space over `S` is *Noetherian* when it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and
locally Noetherian. Quasi-separatedness is the absolute notion of Stacks 03BS, part (3), which
is why the containment `hZ` of the terminal scheme in the site is required; local
Noetherianity is the étale-local scheme property `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsNoetherian (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etale_comp_of_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EC.** An étale morphism of the big fppf site of `S` followed by an étale chart
of an algebraic space is again an étale chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_comp_of_scheme {U U' : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : U ⟶ U') (g : yoneda.obj U' ⟶ F)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f))
    (hg : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf g) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etale_of_etale_charts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EC.** A morphism of the big fppf site of `S` between two étale charts of a
presheaf is an étale morphism of schemes.

The ambient presheaf need not be an algebraic space, so the statement covers the source one:
the second chart is étale and hence relatively representable, which is all that is used. The
morphism factors through the fibre product of the two charts, as a section of one projection
followed by the other. Both projections are étale by cancellation against the étale charts,
and a section of an étale morphism is étale by
`CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.of_postcomp`, so no descent along an atlas is required.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_of_etale_charts {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {U U' : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F) (φ' : yoneda.obj U' ⟶ F)
    (hφ : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf φ)
    (hφ' : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf φ')
    (χ : U ⟶ U') (hχ : yoneda.map χ ≫ φ' = φ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map χ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etale_of_comp_surjective_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EC.** Étaleness of a chart of an algebraic space descends along a surjective
étale morphism of the big fppf site of `S`: if `χ : U ⟶ U'` is surjective étale and
`yoneda.map χ ≫ φ'` is an étale chart, then so is `φ'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_of_comp_surjective_etale {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {U U' : BigFppfOver B S hS} (χ : U ⟶ U')
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map χ)]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map χ)]
    (φ' : yoneda.obj U' ⟶ X)
    (hφ : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (yoneda.map χ ≫ φ')) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf φ'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03ED, parts (1) and (2).** The *small étale site* of a presheaf `F` on the big
fppf site of `S`, as a category: its objects are the étale charts of `F`, and its morphisms
are the morphisms of the big fppf site of `S` whose triangle over `F` commutes.
declarations.statement: abbrev SmallEtale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03ED, part (3).** A family of étale charts of `F` is a covering family exactly
when its family of underlying objects of `Sch_κ` is a chosen étale covering family of the
big étale site carried by `B`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCovering (E : Covering (SmallEtale B S hS F)) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.overShriek_overPullback_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EE**, packaged as the existence of the isomorphism
`j_{U!}j_U^{-1}F ≅ F × h_U^#`.
declarations.statement:
theorem overShriek_overPullback_iso (F : Sheaf J (Type v)) :
    Nonempty
      (((Over.forget U).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over U) J).obj
          ((J.overPullback (Type v) U).obj F) ≅
        F ⨯ (presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).obj (yoneda.obj U))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_overPost_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `u : C ⥤ D` be a continuous functor of sites such that
`Over.post u : Over V ⥤ Over (u.obj V)` is representably flat. Then `Over.post u` is continuous for
the localized topologies `J.over V` and `K.over (u.obj V)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_overPost_of_flat (u : C ⥤ D) [u.IsContinuous J K] (V : C)
    [RepresentablyFlat (Over.post (X := V) u)] :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).IsContinuous (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
declarations.comment:
Continuity of `u' : D/V ⥤ C/U` under 03EF's hypotheses: 03EF assumes `u` left exact
  between sites with all finite limits, whence `Over.post u` is flat and this lemma applies. This
  is the continuity half of `Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.starCompOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
For a functor `u : C ⥤ D` preserving binary products and `V : C`, the isomorphism
`Over.star V ⋙ Over.post u ≅ u ⋙ Over.star (u.obj V)` of functors `C ⥤ Over (u.obj V)`, whose
component at `X` is `Limits.prodComparison u V X : u.obj (V ⨯ X) ⟶ u.obj V ⨯ u.obj X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def starCompOverPostIso [HasBinaryProducts C] [HasBinaryProducts D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) u] (V : C) :
    Over.star V ⋙ Over.post (X := V) u ≅ u ⋙ Over.star (u.obj V)
declarations.comment:
Commutativity of the diagram of 03EF: the two composites `C ⥤ Over (u.obj V)` of
  continuous functors around the square are isomorphic, which since morphisms of sites compose by
  composing their continuous functors (03CC) is what it means for the square of morphisms of sites
  to commute. The final clause of 03EF, that the induced diagram of topoi equals the diagram of
  03CF, is NOT covered — see the module docstring.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost
declarations.doc:
If `C` and `D` have all finite limits and `u : C ⥤ D` is continuous and commutes with finite
limits, then for `V : C` the localized functor `Over.post u : Over V ⥤ Over (u.obj V)` defines a
morphism of sites `D/U → C/V`, where `U = u.obj V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_overPost [HasFiniteLimits C] [HasFiniteLimits D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    [u.IsContinuous J K] [PreservesFiniteLimits u] (V : C) :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).IsMorphismOfSites (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
declarations.comment:
The left vertical arrow of 03EF's diagram: `u' = Over.post u` is a morphism of
  sites `D/U → C/V` under 03EF's hypotheses. This is 03CF's clause (a) in the special case where
  03EF's hypotheses hold; clause (a) in the generality of 03CF is
  `Functor.isMorphismOfSites_overPost_of_isMorphismOfSites` in
  Sites/SlicePost/MorphismOfSitesGeneral.lean, proved there through 00Y1 as Stacks does.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_star
declarations.doc:
On a site with binary products, the localization functor `Over.star X : C ⥤ Over X`,
`Y ↦ (Y ⨯ X ⟶ X)`, defines a morphism of sites `C/X → C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_star [HasBinaryProducts C] (X : C) :
    (Over.star X).IsMorphismOfSites J (J.over X)
declarations.comment:
The two horizontal arrows `j_U` and `j_V` of 03EF's diagram: the localization
  functors `X ↦ X ⨯ U` of 03CE are morphisms of sites. Stated once, for an arbitrary site and
  object; the diagram of 03EF instantiates it at `(C, J, V)` and at `(D, K, u.obj V)`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.sheafPushforwardContinuousStarOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism

```
  (Over.post u)_* ⋙ (Over.star V)_* ≅ (Over.star U)_* ⋙ u_* ,
```

of functors `Sheaf (K.over U) A ⥤ Sheaf J A`, for `U = u.obj V` and any category `A`, induced by
`starCompOverPostIso`: the square of pushforwards on sheaves commutes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardContinuousStarOverPostIso [HasBinaryProducts C]
    [HasBinaryProducts D] (u : C ⥤ D) [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) u] (V : C)
    [u.IsContinuous J K]
    [(Over.post (X := V) u).IsContinuous (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))]
    (A : Type*) [Category A] :
    (Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V)) ⋙
        (Over.star V).sheafPushforwardContinuous A J (J.over V) ≅
      (Over.star (u.obj V)).sheafPushforwardContinuous A K (K.over (u.obj V)) ⋙
        u.sheafPushforwardContinuous A J K
declarations.comment:
The induced diagram of morphisms of topoi commutes, on the pushforward side, for
  sheaves valued in any category. 03EF's final clause — that this diagram is EQUAL to 03CF's
  diagram of topoi — is NOT covered; 03CF's clause (b) is now proved in
  Sites/SliceTopos/InverseImage.lean, leaving one equation.

declarations.name: overPost_comp_forget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EG**, the square of categories.  With `V = u(U)`, the localized functor
`u' = Over.post u : C/U ⥤ D/V` and the localization functors `j_U = Over.forget U` and
`j_V = Over.forget V` form a commutative square, `u' ⋙ j_V = j_U ⋙ u`.  Stacks calls this
"clear"; in Lean the two composites are equal by `rfl`.
declarations.statement:
theorem overPost_comp_forget :
    (Over.post u : Over U ⥤ Over (u.obj U)) ⋙ Over.forget (u.obj U) = Over.forget U ⋙ u
declarations.comment: the square of categories commutes: `u' ⋙ j_V = j_U ⋙ u`

declarations.name: isCocontinuous_overPost
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EG**, the mathematical content.  If `u : C ⥤ D` is cocontinuous then so is the
localized functor `u' = Over.post u : C/U ⥤ D/u(U)`, for the localized topologies `J.over U` and
`K.over (u.obj U)`.

Stacks proves this by transferring refinement data verbatim: a covering of `u(U')/u(U)` in
`D/u(U)` is in particular a covering of `u(U')` in `D`, cocontinuity of `u` refines its
`u`-image by a covering `{U'_i → U'}` of `C`, and the very same index map and comparison
morphisms exhibit the refinement after every object is viewed over `U`, resp. over `u(U)`.  In
Mathlib's sieve-theoretic formulation this is
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.instIsCocontinuousOverObjPostOver`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_overPost :
    (Over.post u : Over U ⥤ Over (u.obj U)).IsCocontinuous (J.over U) (K.over (u.obj U))
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow `u'` is cocontinuous

declarations.name: sheafPushforwardCocontinuousOverPostIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EG**, the square of topoi.  Let `f : Sh(C) ⟶ Sh(D)` and
`f' : Sh(C/U) ⟶ Sh(D/u(U))` be the morphisms of topoi attached to `u` and to
`u' = Over.post u` by Stacks 00XO, and let `j_U : Sh(C/U) ⟶ Sh(C)` and
`j_V : Sh(D/u(U)) ⟶ Sh(D)` be those attached to the localization functors.  Then the square of
topoi commutes: there is a natural isomorphism `f'_* ⋙ j_{V*} ≅ j_{U*} ⋙ f_*` of functors
`Sh(C/U) ⥤ Sh(D)`.

Both composites compute the direct image of one and the same functor `C/U ⥤ D`, since
`u' ⋙ j_V = j_U ⋙ u` by `overPost_comp_forget`; the isomorphism is therefore obtained by
comparing each side with that direct image using Stacks 03L5.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardCocontinuousOverPostIso :
    (Over.post u : Over U ⥤ Over (u.obj U)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u)
          (J.over U) (K.over (u.obj U)) ⋙
        (Over.forget (u.obj U)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (K.over (u.obj U)) K ≅
      (Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) (J.over U) J ⋙
        u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J K
declarations.comment: the square of topoi commutes: `f'_* ⋙ j_{V*} ≅ j_{U*} ⋙ f_*`

declarations.name: comp_forget_eq_forget
declarations.doc:
Commutativity of the relocalization triangle: `j_U ∘ j = j_V`, i.e.
`Over.map f ⋙ Over.forget U = Over.forget V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_forget_eq_forget :
    Over.map f ⋙ Over.forget U = Over.forget V

declarations.name: map_eq_forget_iteratedSlice
declarations.doc:
Under the identification `(C/U)/(V/U) ≅ C/V` given by
`Over.iteratedSliceEquiv (Over.mk f)`, the relocalization functor
`j = Over.map f` agrees with the localization functor
`j_{V/U} = Over.forget (Over.mk f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_eq_forget_iteratedSlice :
    (Over.iteratedSliceEquiv (Over.mk f)).functor ⋙ Over.map f =
      Over.forget (Over.mk f)

declarations.name: inverseImage_eq
declarations.doc:
(Inverse image, strict equality.)
`j_V^{-1} = j^{-1} ∘ j_U^{-1}` as functors `Sheaf J A ⟶ Sheaf (J.over V) A`.

This is the strict equality of `sheafPushforwardContinuous` functors, valid
because the underlying functors satisfy `Over.map f ⋙ Over.forget U =
Over.forget V` strictly.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseImage_eq :
    (Over.forget V).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) J =
      (Over.forget U).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over U) J ⋙
        (Over.map f).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) (J.over U)

declarations.name: leftAdjointIso
declarations.doc:
(Lower-shriek, natural isomorphism.)
`j_{V!} ≅ j_{U!} ∘ j_!` as functors `Sheaf (J.over V) A ⟶ Sheaf J A`.

Constructed from `inverseImage_eq` via uniqueness of left adjoints: each of
`sheafPullback` is a chosen left adjoint to the corresponding
`sheafPushforwardContinuous`, and the composition `j_!  ∘ j_U_!` is left
adjoint to `j_U^{-1} ∘ j^{-1} = j_V^{-1}` by `inverseImage_eq`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def leftAdjointIso :
    (Over.forget V).sheafPullback A (J.over V) J ≅
      (Over.map f).sheafPullback A (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙
        (Over.forget U).sheafPullback A (J.over U) J

declarations.name: leftAdjointIso_hom_app_comp_map_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EH carries one transpose to the other.**  A morphism `u : T ⟶ j_V^{-1}Z`
transposes across `j_{V!} ⊣ j_V^{-1}` on the one hand and across `(j_! ∘ j_{U!}) ⊣ j_V^{-1}` on
the other, and the two transposes differ by `leftAdjointIso`.

This is what `leftAdjointIso` *means*: it is a `Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq`, so on its own it is
only an isomorphism of two chosen left adjoints, and the statement that identifies it is the
agreement of the transposes it induces.  It is also the only form in which the triangle can be
used inside an equation of morphisms out of a lower shriek, where one side is written with
`j_{V!}` and the other with `j_{U!} ∘ j_!`.

`Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq_hom_app_counit` is the case `u = 𝟙`; the general case is that one
followed by the naturality of `leftAdjointIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftAdjointIso_hom_app_comp_map_comp_counit {T : Sheaf (J.over V) A} {Z : Sheaf J A}
    (u : T ⟶ ((Over.forget V).sheafPushforwardContinuous A (J.over V) J).obj Z) :
    ((Over.forget V).sheafPullback A (J.over V) J).map u ≫
        ((Over.forget V).sheafAdjunctionContinuous A (J.over V) J).counit.app Z =
      (leftAdjointIso J f A).hom.app T ≫
        ((Over.map f).sheafPullback A (J.over V) (J.over U) ⋙
            (Over.forget U).sheafPullback A (J.over U) J).map u ≫
          (((Over.map f).sheafAdjunctionContinuous A (J.over V) (J.over U)).comp
            ((Over.forget U).sheafAdjunctionContinuous A (J.over U) J)).counit.app Z
declarations.comment: j_{V!} = j_{U!} ∘ j_! carries one transpose to the other

registrations.name: PresheafOfModules.instPreservesFiniteLimitsSheafOfModulesSheafification
registrations.comment: left exact: sheafification preserves finite limits

registrations.name: PresheafOfModules.instIsLeftAdjointSheafOfModulesSheafification
registrations.comment: right exact: sheafification is a left adjoint, so it preserves colimits

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.restrictionFunctor
declarations.doc: Restriction of presheaves of modules along `Over.forget U`, i.e. `j_U^*`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev restrictionFunctor (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{w}) (U : C) :
    PresheafOfModules.{a, v, u, w} O ⥤
      PresheafOfModules.{a, v, max u v, w} (overRingPresheaf O U)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.extensionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Extension of presheaves of modules from the slice category over `U`, as a functor: the
functor `j_{U!}` whose value at `M` is the direct-sum presheaf `extensionPresheaf O U M` and
whose action on morphisms is forced by the hom-set bijection `extensionHomEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionFunctor :
    PresheafOfModules.{a, v, max u v, w} (overRingPresheaf O U) ⥤
      PresheafOfModules.{a, v, u, w} O

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.extensionFunctorAdjunction
declarations.doc: Extension from the slice category is left adjoint to restriction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionFunctorAdjunction :
    extensionFunctor.{v, u, w, a} O U ⊣ restrictionFunctor O U

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.directImage
declarations.doc: The direct-image functor `j_{U*}` on presheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def directImage :
    PresheafOfModules.{a, v, max u v, w} (overRingPresheaf O U) ⥤
      PresheafOfModules.{a, v, u, w} O

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.restrictionDirectImageAdjunction
declarations.doc: Restriction along `Over.forget U` is left adjoint to the direct image.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictionDirectImageAdjunction :
    restrictionFunctor O U ⊣ directImage O U

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.presheafModuleAdjunctionsOver
declarations.doc:
Restriction of presheaves of modules to `C/U` has both an extension left adjoint and a
direct-image right adjoint: the coproduct construction `extensionFunctor` and the limit
construction `directImage`, with their adjunctions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafModuleAdjunctionsOver (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{w}) (U : C) :
    PresheafModuleAdjunctionsOver.{v, u, w, m} O U

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.extension_exact
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03EJ.** Extension of presheaves of modules from a slice category is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem extension_exact (A : PresheafModuleAdjunctionsOver.{v, u, w, m} O U) :
    exactFunctor
      (PresheafOfModules.{max u v m} (overRingPresheaf O U))
      (PresheafOfModules.{max u v m} O) A.extension

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.extensionObjLinearEquivDirectSum
declarations.doc:
Extension of a presheaf of modules from `C/U` has, at `V`, the direct sum of its values
on all arrows `V ⟶ U`. These identifications commute with every restriction map.
declarations.statement:
theorem extensionObjLinearEquivDirectSum (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{w}) (U : C)
    (A : PresheafModuleAdjunctionsOver.{v, u, w, m} O U)
    (G : PresheafOfModules.{max u v m} (overRingPresheaf O U)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ V : C,
        (A.extension.obj G).obj (op V) ≃ₗ[O.obj (op V)]
          extensionFormula.{v, u, w, max u m} O U V G,
      ∀ {V W : C} (f : V ⟶ W) (x : (A.extension.obj G).obj (op W)),
        e V ((A.extension.obj G).map f.op x) =
          extensionFormulaMap.{v, u, w, max u m} O U G f (e W x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.OverModules.extensionSheafificationIso
declarations.doc:
Extension by zero of a sheaf of modules is naturally the sheafification of its extension
as a presheaf of modules from the slice category over `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def extensionSheafificationIso :
    SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
        (F := Over.forget U) (𝟙 (R.over U) : (R.over U) ⟶ (R.over U)) ≅
      SheafOfModules.forget.{u} (R.over U) ⋙ A.extension ⋙
        PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 R.obj)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EL.** For a morphism of ringed topoi
`(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)`, the pullback of a tensor product of sheaves of
`O_D`-modules is the tensor product of their pullbacks,

`f^*(F ⊗_{O_D} G) ≅ f^*F ⊗_{O_C} f^*G`,

naturally in `F` and in `G`. The comparison is the one determined by the chain of bijections
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorHomEquiv`, whose naturality in the sheaf of values turns it
into a morphism of sheaves of modules and whose naturality in `F` and `G` makes that morphism a
natural transformation.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackTensorIso :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u', v', w', w', w'} Y.O)) ⋙
        f.pullbackModules ≅
      Functor.prod (f.pullbackModules) (f.pullbackModules) ⋙
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} X.O))

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedPoint.RingedPointSituation.stalkTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**The stalk commutes with the tensor product of sheaves of modules.** At a point `p` of a
ringed topos `(Sh(C), O)` the module-valued stalk carries a tensor product of sheaves of
`O`-modules to the tensor product of the stalks over `O_p`,

`(F ⊗_O G)_p ≅ F_p ⊗_{O_p} G_p`,

naturally in `F` and in `G`. This is Tag 03EL — the compatibility of pullback with the tensor
product along a morphism of ringed topoi — read along the morphism out of the ringed point of
Section 18.37, whose pullback on modules is the stalk
(`RingedPointSituation.pullbackStalkIso`).
declarations.statement:
def stalkTensorIso :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O)) ⋙ s.stalkModules ≅
      Functor.prod s.stalkModules s.stalkModules ⋙
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor s.point.O))
declarations.comment: the stalk at a point of a ringed topos commutes with the tensor product

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.RingedToposPullback.pullbackCoherence
declarations.doc:
**The coherence of Tag 03EL, proved.** The comparison
`f^*(F ⊗_{O_D} G) ≅ f^*F ⊗_{O_C} f^*G` is compatible with the associator and with both unitors,
the unit object being matched by `ν : f^*O_D ≅ O_C`. The three fields are
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.RingedToposPullback.associativity`, `leftUnitality` and `rightUnitality`;
there is no hypothesis, and the four universes of the two ringed topoi stay independent.
declarations.statement: theorem pullbackCoherence : PullbackCoherence f
declarations.comment: the comparison of the pullback with the tensor product is a monoidal structure: the three coherences

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.componentRestrictionTensorTotalIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EL on total complexes, at the component inclusion.** Restriction to the degree-`n`
component commutes with the total tensor complex:
`g_n^*Tot(K ⊗_O L) ≅ Tot(g_n^*K ⊗_{O_n} g_n^*L)`, the comparison on the summand of bidegree
`(p, q)` being `g_n^*(K^p ⊗_O L^q) ≅ g_n^*K^p ⊗_{O_n} g_n^*L^q`.
declarations.statement:
def componentRestrictionTensorTotalIso
    (K L : CochainComplex (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules ℤ) :
    (S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n).obj
        (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor K L
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (S.totalRingedTopos O).O)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ≅
      HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor ((S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n).obj K)
        ((S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n).obj L)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (S.componentRingedTopos O n).O)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
declarations.comment: on total complexes, for restriction to a simplicial component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EL for a morphism of algebraic spaces.** The inverse image of a tensor product of
`𝒪_Y`-modules along `f : X ⟶ Y` is the tensor product of the inverse images,
`f^*(G ⊗_{𝒪_Y} G') ≅ f^*G ⊗_{𝒪_X} f^*G'`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback` is the inverse image of modules of the morphism of small
étale ringed topoi of Stacks 03G8, so this is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorIso` at that
morphism, with the tensor product sheaf matched with the monoidal product by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulesTensorObjIso` on each side.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackTensorIso (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (G G' : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    (modulePullback B S hS f).obj (G ⊗ G') ≅
      (modulePullback B S hS f).obj G ⊗ (modulePullback B S hS f).obj G'
declarations.comment: for the small étale ringed topoi of a morphism of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: internalHom_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `O` be a presheaf of commutative rings on a site `C`, let `F` be a presheaf of
`O`-modules and let `G` be a sheaf of `O`-modules. Then the internal hom presheaf
`𝓗om_O(F, G) = internalHom O F G` is a sheaf of `O`-modules, i.e. its underlying abelian
presheaf is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHom_isSheaf
    (hG : Presheaf.IsSheaf J G.presheaf) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf J (internalHom O F G).presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.internalHomFunctor_preservesColimitsOfShape
declarations.doc:
For a fixed target `G`, internal Hom in the first variable sends arbitrary colimits of
presheaves of `O`-modules to limits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance internalHomFunctor_preservesColimitsOfShape
    (G : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v} (Oforget O)) (I : Type w) [Category.{w} I] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape I (internalHomFunctor O G)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesLimits
declarations.doc: Internal Hom with fixed first variable commutes with arbitrary limits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesLimits :
    PreservesLimits (internalHomSecondFunctor.{v, u, w, m} O F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EN, sheaf case, second variable.** Internal Hom from a fixed sheaf of modules
commutes with arbitrary limits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesLimits
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Tensor.ringSheaf O)) :
    PreservesLimits (internalHomSecondFunctor.{v, u, w, m} J O F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafInternalHomFunctor_preservesColimitsOfShape
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EN, sheaf case, first variable.** For a fixed target `G`, the internal Hom of
sheaves of modules takes colimits in the first variable to limits.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance sheafInternalHomFunctor_preservesColimitsOfShape
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (I : Type*) [Category I] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape I (sheafInternalHomFunctor J O G)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.preservesFiniteColimits_internalHomFirstMate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EN in the first variable, for the mate.** Internal Hom into a fixed sheaf of
modules, contravariant in its source, carries finite colimits of sheaves of modules to finite
limits of internal Hom sheaves.

This is the continuity that the proof of Stacks 0GN2 uses to pass from the structure sheaf to a
finitely presented source, and it holds with no hypothesis: `internalHomFirstMate` is a left
adjoint, by `internalHomFirstMateAdjunction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteColimits_internalHomFirstMate :
    Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits (internalHomFirstMate O G)
declarations.comment: sheaf case, first variable, for the mate of the tensor comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafInternalHomTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** The canonical currying isomorphism from internal Hom out of a tensor
product to iterated internal Hom.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafInternalHomTensorIso :
    internalHom O (F ⊗ G) H ≅ internalHom O F (internalHom O G H)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafInternalHomTensorIso_hom_app
declarations.doc:
On sections, the currying isomorphism is tensor currying: after restricting `x`, it
evaluates the original morphism on `x ⊗ y`. This pins the isomorphism down, rather than merely
asserting that some isomorphism exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafInternalHomTensorIso_hom_app (a : (restrFun O U).obj (F ⊗ G) ⟶ (restrFun O U).obj H)
    {S : C} (p : S ⟶ U) (x : F.obj (op S)) {T : C} (q : T ⟶ S) (y : G.obj (op T)) :
    sectionOfRestr O H S q
        (((((((presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G H).hom.app (op U)).hom a).app
            (op (Over.mk p))).hom (restrSection O F U p x)).app
              (op (Over.mk q))).hom (restrSection O G S q y)) =
      restrTensorHom O F G H U a (q ≫ p) (F.restrictₛₗ q.op x ⊗ₜ y)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** The currying isomorphism is natural contravariantly in its first tensor
factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_left
    {F' : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Oforget O)} (f : F' ⟶ F) :
    (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G H).hom ≫
        internalHomMapLeft O f =
      internalHomMapLeft O (f ⊗ₘ 𝟙 G) ≫
        (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F' G H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_middle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** The currying isomorphism is natural contravariantly in its second tensor
factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_middle
    {G' : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Oforget O)} (g : G' ⟶ G) :
    (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G H).hom ≫
        internalHomMapRight O F
          (internalHomMapLeft O g) =
      internalHomMapLeft O (𝟙 F ⊗ₘ g) ≫
        (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G' H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_right
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03EO.** The currying isomorphism is natural covariantly in its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafInternalHomTensorIso_natural_right
    {H' : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Oforget O)} (hh : H ⟶ H') :
    internalHomMapRight O (F ⊗ G) hh ≫
        (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G H').hom =
      (presheafInternalHomTensorIso O F G H).hom ≫
        internalHomMapRight O F
          (internalHomMapRight O G hh)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafTensorHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** Tensoring on the right by `G` is left adjoint to the internal-Hom functor
with source `G`. Packaging the canonical correspondence as an adjunction records its
naturality in both remaining variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafTensorHomAdjunction :
    (tensoringRight (_root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Oforget O))).obj G ⊣
      internalHomSecondFunctor.{v, u, max u v w, u} O G

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.presheafTensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** The hom-equivalence of `presheafTensorHomAdjunction` is the canonical
currying map: on sections it sends `b` to the map taking `x` and `y` to `b (x ⊗ y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafTensorHomEquiv_apply (b : F ⊗ G ⟶ H) (U : C) (x : F.obj (op U))
    {T : C} (q : T ⟶ U) (y : G.obj (op T)) :
    sectionOfRestr O H U q
        (((((presheafTensorHomEquiv O F G H b).app (op U)).hom x).app
          (op (Over.mk q))).hom (restrSection O G U q y)) =
      globalTensorHom O F G H b T (F.restrictₛₗ q.op x ⊗ₜ y)

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.FreeUniverse.presheafTensorHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** Tensoring on the right by `G` is left adjoint to the internal-Hom functor
with source `G`. Packaging the canonical correspondence as an adjunction records its
naturality in both remaining variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def presheafTensorHomAdjunction :
    (_root_.PresheafOfModules.tensorBifunctor O).flip.obj G ⊣
      internalHomSecondFunctor.{v, u, w, w} O G
declarations.comment: presheaf_tensor_hom_adjunction, with the universe of the sections of the structure presheaf independent of the universes of the site

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.FreeUniverse.presheafTensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO.** The hom-equivalence of `presheafTensorHomAdjunction` is the canonical
currying map: on sections it sends `b` to the map taking `x` and `y` to `b (x ⊗ y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafTensorHomEquiv_apply (b : F.tensorObj G ⟶ H) (U : C) (x : F.obj (op U))
    {T : C} (q : T ⟶ U) (y : G.obj (op T)) :
    sectionOfRestr O H U q
        (((((presheafTensorHomEquiv O F G H b).app (op U)).hom x).app
          (op (Over.mk q))).hom (restrSection O G U q y)) =
      globalTensorHom O F G H b T (F.restrictₛₗ q.op x ⊗ₜ y)
declarations.comment: presheaf_tensor_hom_adjunction, with the universe of the sections of the structure presheaf independent of the universes of the site

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafCurryIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case.** The canonical currying isomorphism for the sheafified tensor
product and the internal Hom sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafCurryIso :
    siteSheafInternalHom J O (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).obj F).obj G) H ≅
      siteSheafInternalHom J O F (siteSheafInternalHom J O G H)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafCurryIso_hom_app_tmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case.** The canonical isomorphism is tensor currying on every local
pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafCurryIso_hom_app_tmul (U : C)
    (s : (siteSheafInternalHom J O
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor O).obj F).obj G) H).val.obj (op U))
    (f : F.val.obj (op U)) (g : G.val.obj (op U)) :
    ((((((sheafCurryIso O F G H).hom.val.app (op U)).hom s).app
        (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom f).app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom g =
      (s.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom
        (toSheafTensorSection O F G U (f ⊗ₜ[O.obj.obj (op U)] g))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafCurryIso_natural_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case.** Currying is contravariantly natural in the first tensor
factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafCurryIso_natural_left
    {F F' :
      _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) O)}
    (f : F' ⟶ F) :
    (sheafCurryIso O F G H).hom ≫ sheafInternalHomMapLeft J O f =
      sheafInternalHomMapLeft J O (sheafTensorMap O f (𝟙 G)) ≫
        (sheafCurryIso O F' G H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafCurryIso_natural_middle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case.** Currying is contravariantly natural in the second tensor
factor.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafCurryIso_natural_middle
    {G G' :
      _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) O)}
    (g : G' ⟶ G) :
    (sheafCurryIso O F G H).hom ≫
        sheafInternalHomMapRight O (sheafInternalHomMapLeft J O g) =
      sheafInternalHomMapLeft J O (sheafTensorMap O (𝟙 F) g) ≫
        (sheafCurryIso O F G' H).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.sheafCurryIso_natural_right
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03EO, sheaf case.** Currying is covariantly natural in the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafCurryIso_natural_right
    {H H' :
      _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) O)}
    (h : H ⟶ H') :
    sheafInternalHomMapRight O h ≫ (sheafCurryIso O F G H').hom =
      (sheafCurryIso O F G H).hom ≫
        sheafInternalHomMapRight O (sheafInternalHomMapRight O h)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.FreeUniverse.sheafTensorRightHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case, at a free ring universe.**  Tensoring on the right by `G` is left
adjoint to the internal-Hom functor with source `G`, for a sheaf of rings whose sections lie in
a universe independent of those of the site.

The presheaf clause
`Stacks.PresheafOfModules.InternalHom.FreeUniverse.presheafTensorHomAdjunction` is composed
with the sheafification adjunction and the result restricted along the fully faithful forgetful
functor; this is legitimate because the right adjoint of the composite already takes values in
sheaves, the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM being a sheaf as soon as its target is.
declarations.comment: sheaf_tensor_hom_adjunction, with the universe of the sections of the structure sheaf independent of the universes of the site

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.FreeUniverse.sheafTensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EO, sheaf case, at a free ring universe, on sections.**  The correspondence is
the canonical currying map: a morphism `b` out of the sheafified tensor product is sent to the
map taking a section `x` of `F` over `U` and a section `y` of `G` over `T ⟶ U` to the value of
`b` on the image of the pure tensor `x|_T ⊗ y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensorHomEquiv_apply
    (b : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, max u v w, max u v w} R).obj
      F).obj G ⟶ H) (U : C)
    (x : F.val.obj (Opposite.op U)) {T : C} (q : T ⟶ U)
    (y : G.val.obj (Opposite.op T)) :
    FreeUniverse.sectionOfRestr R.obj H.val U q
        (((((sheafTensorHomEquiv R F G H b).val.app (Opposite.op U)).hom x).app
          (Opposite.op (Over.mk q))).hom (FreeUniverse.restrSection R.obj G.val U q y)) =
      FreeUniverse.globalTensorHom R.obj F.val G.val H.val
        ((sheafifyForgetAdjunction R).homEquiv (F.val.tensorObj G.val) H b) T
        (F.val.restrictₛₗ q.op x ⊗ₜ y)
declarations.comment: sheaf_tensor_hom_adjunction, with the universe of the sections of the structure sheaf independent of the universes of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.tensorLeft_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
Tensoring presheaves of modules on the left by a fixed presheaf of modules preserves all
colimits indexed in the module universe: at each object it is a left adjoint.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.sheafTensorLeft_preservesColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 05NB.** Tensoring with a fixed sheaf of modules commutes with
all small colimits, independently of the ring universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensorLeft_preservesColimits (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{a, z} (sheafTensorLeft J R F)

declarations.name: Stacks.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
A presheaf of modules is flat when tensoring on the right with it is an exact
endofunctor.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFlat (F : PresheafOfModules.{z} (ringPresheaf O)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1), for the objectwise tensor product Stacks.tensorRight of this file, whose two module universes are independent of each other and of the ring universe. The tree carries a second objectwise tensor product, and part (1) for that one is AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.IsFlat, which is also where parts (2) and (4) of the tag are registered

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is flat when tensoring on the right with it is an exact endofunctor
on sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
A presheaf of modules is flat when tensoring on the right with it is an
exact endofunctor.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlat {O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w}}

Part (1) for the other objectwise tensor product in the tree, Stacks.tensorRight of StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.TensorExactness, is Stacks.IsFlat

viewed as a module over the source by restriction of scalars, is flat.

declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules is flat when tensoring on the right with it is an exact
endofunctor on sheaves of modules.

This is part (3) of tag 03ER for the native tensor bifunctor, and part (4) just below
is stated in terms of it. `Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat` uses the same native tensor

declarations.statement:
