declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMap
declarations.doc:
A morphism of sheaves of rings is flat when its target ring sheaf, viewed
as a module over the source by restriction of scalars, is flat.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFlatMap {O O' : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} (f : O ⟶ O') : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.isFlat_of_objectwise_flat
declarations.doc:
**A presheaf of modules whose sections over every object are flat is flat.** Finite limits
and finite colimits of presheaves of modules are computed objectwise, so exactness of the
objectwise tensor endofunctor is an objectwise condition, and over each object it is exactness
of tensoring modules by the sections there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_objectwise_flat {O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w}}
    (F : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{z} (ringPresheaf O))
    (hF : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Module.Flat ((ringPresheaf O).obj U) (F.obj U)) :
    IsFlat F

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatSheafification.isFlat_sheafification
declarations.doc:
The sheaf associated to a flat presheaf of modules is flat over the associated sheaf of
rings.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFlat_sheafification
    {O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w}} {Osharp : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}

    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J a]

    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.IsFlat F) :

        (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp) a).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.isFlat_coproduct
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03EU, direct sums.** A coproduct of flat presheaves of modules is flat.

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EU, filtered colimits.** A filtered colimit of flat presheaves of modules is
flat.
declarations.statement:

    {J : Type ju} [Category.{jv} J] [IsFiltered J] [UnivLE.{ju, z}]

**Stacks Project, Tag 03EU part (2), filtered colimits.** A filtered colimit of flat
sheaves of modules is flat.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatColimits.isFlat_coproduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03EU part (2), direct sums.** An arbitrary direct sum of flat sheaves
of modules is flat. An arbitrary coproduct is the filtered colimit of its finite subcoproducts,
so this follows from the finite case `isFlat_coproduct_finite` and the filtered-colimit case
`isFlat_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_coproduct {O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} {ι : Type z}
    (F : ι → _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsFlat (F i)) :
    IsFlat (∐ F)

    (F : ι → _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsFlat (F i)) :
    IsFlat (∐ F)

The extension from the slice category over `U` of the rank-one module is a flat presheaf of

The extension by zero from the localized site of the structure sheaf is a flat sheaf of
modules.

    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]

    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]

    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O).over U) :
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O).over U) ⟶
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O).over U))).obj

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.exists_epi_isFlat_simplicial
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03EW] part (4) at the simplicial site of [Stacks, Tag 09D0].** Every
simplicial `A_•`-module — that is, every sheaf of modules over the sheaf of rings on `Δ × C`
associated to a simplicial sheaf of commutative rings `A_•`, as in [Stacks, Tag 09D1] — receives
an epimorphism from a flat one.
declarations.comment: part (4) at the simplicial site Δ × C of 09D0

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.exists_epi_from_coproduct_extensionByZero
declarations.doc:
**Every sheaf of `O`-modules is a quotient of a direct sum of extensions by zero
`j_{U!}O_U` of the structure sheaves of slices.** The sum is indexed by the sections of `M`,
the summand attached to a section over `U` being `j_{U!}O_U`, and the map sends the
tautological generating section of that summand to the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_coproduct_extensionByZero (M : SheafOfModules.{u} O) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → C)
      (π : (∐ fun i ↦ (extensionByZero.{u, u, u, u} O (U i)).obj (unit (O.over (U i)))) ⟶ M),
        Epi π

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.exists_epi_from_coproduct_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EW, part (1).** Every presheaf of modules is a quotient of a direct sum of
extensions from slice categories of the rank-one module. The sum is indexed by all pairs
`(U, s)` with `s` a section of `F` over `U`, and the component at `(U, s)` is the morphism
adjoint to `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_coproduct_extension (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{w})
    (F : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w z} O) :
    ∃ (ι : Type (max u v w z)) (U : ι → C),
      ∃ (p : (∐ fun i : ι =>
        ((presheafModuleAdjunctionsOver.{v, u, w, max w z} O (U i)).extension.obj
          (uliftUnit.{max u v w z} (overRingPresheaf O (U i))))) ⟶ F), Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.exists_epi_from_flat_presheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EW, part (2).** Every presheaf of modules over a presheaf of commutative rings
is a quotient of a flat presheaf of modules: the direct sum produced by part (1) is a direct
sum of slice extensions of the rank-one module, each of which is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_flat_presheaf (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (ringPresheaf O)) :
    ∃ P : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (ringPresheaf O),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.PresheafOfModules.IsFlat P ∧
        ∃ (p : P ⟶ F), Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.exists_epi_from_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EW, part (4).** Every sheaf of modules over a sheaf of commutative rings is a
quotient of a flat sheaf of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_from_flat (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)) :
    ∃ P : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O),
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat P ∧ ∃ (p : P ⟶ F), Epi p

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatCover.exists_epi_from_isFlat
registrations.comment: part (4): every sheaf of modules is a quotient of a flat one

declarations.name: Stacks.sheafTensorRight_shortExact_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03EX, sheaf case.** If the final term of a short exact sequence of
sheaves of modules is flat, then tensoring the sequence with any sheaf of modules gives a
short exact sequence of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafTensorRight_shortExact_of_flat
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{max t w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)))
    (G : SheafOfModules.{max t w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (hflat : SheafOfModules.IsFlat S.X₃) :
    ∃ h : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, max t w, max t w} O).flip.obj
          G).map S.f ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, max t w, max t w} O).flip.obj
          G).map S.g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, max t w, max t w} O).flip.obj
          G).map S.f)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, max t w, max t w} O).flip.obj
          G).map S.g) h).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.shortExact_map_sheafTensorObj
declarations.doc:
Tensoring a short exact sequence of sheaves of modules whose third term is flat with any sheaf
of modules gives a short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_sheafTensorObj
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) S.X₃)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (S.map ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).obj M)).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.Presheaf.shortExact_map_tensorRight
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EX, part (1).** If the third term of a short exact sequence of presheaves of
modules is flat, then tensoring the sequence with an arbitrary presheaf of modules gives a
short exact sequence.

The proof is the source's.  Right exactness of the objectwise tensor product gives exactness in
the middle and an epimorphism on the right, so the content is injectivity on the left.  For
that, resolve the second tensor factor `G` by a flat presheaf of modules `P` (Stacks 03EW part
(2)), let `K` be the kernel of `P ⟶ G`, and chase the 3-by-3 diagram whose columns are the
sequence tensored with `K`, `P` and `G` and whose rows are `K ⟶ P ⟶ G` tensored with the three
terms of the sequence: the first column and the second row are exact because tensoring is right
exact in each variable, the second column is left exact because `P` is flat, and the bottom row
is left exact because the third term of the sequence is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_tensorRight
    {S : ShortComplex (_root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (ringPresheaf O))}
    (hS : S.ShortExact) (h₃ : PresheafOfModules.IsFlat S.X₃)
    (G : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{max u v w z} (ringPresheaf O)) :
    (S.map (PresheafOfModules.tensorRight G)).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatTwoOutOfThree.isFlat_middle_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03EY, part (1) for sheaves.** In a short exact sequence of sheaves of modules whose
outer terms are flat, the middle term is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_middle_of_shortExact
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) S.X₁)

    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) S.X₂

declarations.doc:

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.acyclic_map_sheafTensorRight_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EZ, sheaf case.** An exact `ℕ`-indexed complex of sheaves of modules all of
whose terms are flat stays exact after tensoring with an arbitrary sheaf of modules.

This is also **Stacks 05NL**, the same statement for a ringed space: a ringed space is the
ringed site of its lattice of opens, its `O_X`-modules are the sheaves of modules over the
structure ring sheaf of that site, and the tensor product is `sheafTensorRight`.  The
site-level statement is recorded against the ringed-space tag for the same reason that the
site-level flatness of Stacks 03ER(3) is recorded against Stacks 05ND in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Modules/Flat.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_map_sheafTensorRight_of_isFlat
    (K : ChainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) ℕ)
    (hK : K.Acyclic)
    (hflat : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (K.X i))
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf R)) :
    ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplex
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} R).flip.obj G)
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj K).Acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatResolution.Presheaf.acyclic_map_tensorRight_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03EZ, presheaf case.** An exact `ℕ`-indexed complex of presheaves of modules all
of whose terms are flat stays exact after tensoring with an arbitrary presheaf of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_map_tensorRight_of_isFlat
    (K : ChainComplex (_root_.PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringPresheaf O)) ℕ)
    (hK : K.Acyclic)
    (hflat : ∀ i, PresheafOfModules.IsFlat (K.X i))
    (G : _root_.PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringPresheaf O)) :
    (((PresheafOfModules.tensorRight G).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.down ℕ)).obj K).Acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F1.** For a ringed site `(C, O)` and a sheaf of `O`-modules `M`, first
extensions of the structure sheaf by `M` are canonically first cohomology.
declarations.statement:
def extOneEquivFirstCohomology (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) :
    Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1 ≃+ (cohomologyFunctor R 1).obj M

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomology_extClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F1.** The class of the extension `0 → M → E → O → 0` goes to the image of the
unit global section under the connecting morphism of the extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomology_extClass (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u})
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (E : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (f : M ⟶ E)
    (g : E ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit R) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact) :
    extOneEquivFirstCohomology R M hS.extClass =
      (eqToHom (universalCohomologyDeltaFunctor_functor R 1)).app M
        ((universalCohomologyDeltaFunctor R).δ hS 0
        ((cohomologyZeroMap R).app (SheafOfModules.unit R)
            (SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv (SheafOfModules.unit R) (𝟙 _))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomology_unique
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03F1.** The connecting-image formula determines the identification uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomology_unique (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u})
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} R)
    (e : Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1 ≃+ (cohomologyFunctor R 1).obj M)
    (he : ∀ (E : SheafOfModules.{u} R) (f : M ⟶ E)
      (g : E ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit R) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
      (hS : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact),
      e hS.extClass =
        (eqToHom (universalCohomologyDeltaFunctor_functor R 1)).app M
          ((universalCohomologyDeltaFunctor R).δ hS 0
            ((cohomologyZeroMap R).app (SheafOfModules.unit R)
              (SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv (SheafOfModules.unit R) (𝟙 _))))) :
    e = extOneEquivFirstCohomology R M

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SiteModules.extOneEquivFirstCohomology_naturality
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03F1.** The identification is natural in the coefficient module sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem extOneEquivFirstCohomology_naturality (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u})
    {M N : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (f : M ⟶ N) (e : Ext (SheafOfModules.unit R) M 1) :
    extOneEquivFirstCohomology R N
        ((Ext.mk₀ f).postcomp (SheafOfModules.unit R) (Nat.add_zero 1) e) =
      (cohomologyFunctor R 1).map f (extOneEquivFirstCohomology R M e)

declarations.name: ModuleSheafCohomology.moduleSheafCohomologyIsoUnderlying
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FD.** For a sheaf of rings `R` on a site, deriving sections in the category of
`R`-module sheaves and then forgetting to abelian groups gives the same cohomology as first
forgetting to an abelian sheaf and deriving there. The comparison is natural in the module
sheaf, holds globally and over every object of the site, and is compatible in degree zero with
the canonical maps to right-derived functors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleSheafCohomologyIsoUnderlying (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) :
    ∃ eSite : ∀ i : ℕ,
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).rightDerived i ≅
          SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ (Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).rightDerived i,
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).toRightDerivedZero ≫
          (eSite 0).hom =
        Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R)
          (Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).toRightDerivedZero ∧
      ∀ U : C,
        ∃ eU : ∀ i : ℕ,
            (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                (sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).rightDerived i ≅
              SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                ((sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).rightDerived i,
          (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                (sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).toRightDerivedZero ≫
              (eU 0).hom =
            Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R)
              ((sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).toRightDerivedZero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesInjectiveObjects_etaleModulePullback_chartToSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F3, part (1), at the small étale site of an algebraic space.** Pullback of
`𝒪_X`-modules along the structure morphism of an étale scheme chart `W` of an algebraic space
`X` carries injective `𝒪_X`-modules to injective `𝒪_W`-modules.

Indeed that pullback is restriction to the localization of the small étale site of `X` at `W`,
which preserves injectives because its left adjoint, extension by zero, preserves
monomorphisms, followed by the equivalence of Stacks 04M0 on sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_etaleModulePullback_chartToSpace
    (W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (chartToSpace B S hS X W)
      (isEtale_chartToSpace B S hS X W)).PreservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.comment: part (1), at the small étale site of an algebraic space

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.cohomologyOverObjectIsoSlice
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F3 (2).** For a ringed site `(C, O)` and an object `U` of `C`, the cohomology
`H^p(U, F)` of a sheaf of `O`-modules over `U` is the cohomology `H^p(C/U, F|_U)` of its
restriction on the site localized at `U`. Both sides place the module in degree zero and take
the `p`-th homology of the corresponding derived sections; the isomorphism is natural in the
module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cohomologyOverObjectIsoSlice (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C) (p : ℤ) :
    DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0 ⋙
        derivedSectionsOverObject X U ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p ≅
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U ⋙
        DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) 0 ⋙
          derivedSectionsOnSlice X U ⋙
            DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.cohomologyOverObjectIsoSliceOfModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F3 (2)**, for one module: the cohomology of `F` over `U` is the cohomology of
`F|_U` on the site localized at `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cohomologyOverObjectIsoSliceOfModule (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C)
    (p : ℤ) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p).obj
        ((derivedSectionsOverObject X U).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj F)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} p).obj
        ((derivedSectionsOnSlice X U).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) 0).obj
            (F.over U)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.preservesInjectiveObjects_overFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F3 (1).** Restriction of sheaves of modules to the site localized at an object
preserves injective objects: its left adjoint, extension by zero, is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_overFunctor :
    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} R U).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.injective_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03F3 (1)**, for one module: the restriction `I|_U` of an injective sheaf of
`R`-modules is an injective sheaf of `R_U`-modules.
declarations.statement: theorem injective_over (I : SheafOfModules.{u} R) [Injective I] : Injective (I.over U)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.OverElements.preservesInjectiveObjects_pushforward_proj
declarations.doc:
Restriction of sheaves of modules along the projection of the site of elements preserves
injective objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesInjectiveObjects_pushforward_proj :
    (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (F := proj K)
      (𝟙 (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R) :
        (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R) ⟶
          (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R))).PreservesInjectiveObjects

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.OverElements.injective_pushforward_proj_obj
declarations.doc:
The restriction of an injective sheaf of `R`-modules to the site of elements of `K` is
injective.
declarations.statement:

        (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R) ⟶ (restrictedRingSheaf K J JD R))).obj I)
declarations.comment: part (1), for one module, at the site of elements of a presheaf of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexMap
declarations.doc:
The map of Čech complexes induced by a morphism of families of morphisms with fixed target,
from the Čech complex of the refined family `G` to that of the refining family `E`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechComplexMap
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {U V : C}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (G : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} V) {f : U ⟶ V}
    (φ : E.HomOver G f)
    {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [Preadditive A]
    [HasProducts.{w} A] [HasProducts.{w'} A]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀), HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → G.I₀), HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (G.f (i a)))]
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) :
    cechComplex G F ⟶ cechComplex E F

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplexTensor
declarations.doc:
The presheaf-of-`O`-modules complex obtained by tensoring the integral Čech
complex with `O` over the constant integer presheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def integralCechComplexTensor

    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    IntegralCechComplexTensorSpec E O

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplexTensor_homology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F5.** Tensoring the integral Čech complex with a
presheaf of rings leaves it exact in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplexTensor_homology_isZero

    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((integralCechComplexTensor E O).K.homology n)

declarations.doc:
The presheaf-of-`R`-modules complex obtained by tensoring the integral Čech

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplexTensorRing_homology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F5.** Tensoring the integral Čech complex with a

declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplexTensorRing_homology_isZero

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.injective_obj
declarations.doc: An injective sheaf is injective as a presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sheaf.injective_obj {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [HasSheafify J A]
    (I : Sheaf J A) [Injective I] : Injective I.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.Acyclic.isIso_cechCohomologyToCohomology_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F7.** Let `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` be a covering family of an object of a
site and let `F` be an abelian sheaf whose higher cohomology vanishes on every nonempty finite
fibre product `U_{i_0} ×_U ⋯ ×_U U_{i_r}` of members of the family. Then the canonical
comparison of [Stacks, Tag 03AX]

```
Ȟ^p(𝒰, F) ⟶ H^p(U, F)
```

is an isomorphism in every degree `p`: the Čech cohomology of such a family computes the sheaf
cohomology of the covered object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cechCohomologyToCohomology_app (F : Sheaf K Ab.{max u v})
    (hacyclic : ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : Fin (r + 1) → E.I₀) (q : ℕ), 0 < q →
      IsZero (((tupleSections K E s).rightDerived q).obj F))
    (p : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((cechCohomologyToCohomology.{max u v} K E hE p).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.Acyclic.cechCohomologyIsoRightDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` be a covering family of an object of a site and let `F` be an abelian
sheaf whose higher cohomology vanishes on every nonempty finite fibre product
`U_{i_0} ×_U ⋯ ×_U U_{i_r}` of members of the family. Then

`Ȟ^j(𝒰, F) ≅ H^j(U, F)`

in every degree, the right hand side being the `j`-th right derived functor of sections over `U`.
The isomorphism is induced by `cechCohomologyToCohomology`.
declarations.statement:
def cechCohomologyIsoRightDerivedSections (F : Sheaf K Ab.{max u v})
    (hacyclic : ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : Fin (r + 1) → E.I₀) (q : ℕ), 0 < q →
      IsZero (((tupleSections K E s).rightDerived q).obj F))
    (j : ℕ) :
    cechCohomology E F.obj j ≅
      (((sheafSections K Ab.{max u v}).obj (op U)).rightDerived j).obj F
declarations.comment: the conclusion read as an isomorphism between the Cech cohomology group of the family and the j-th right derived sections over the covered object, which is the definition of H^j(U, F) that the acyclicity hypothesis of the tag is stated with

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.surjective_on_sections_of_isZero_cechCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F8.** For a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves, vanishing
of first Čech cohomology of the first sheaf on a cofinal system of coverings makes the last
map surjective on sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_on_sections_of_isZero_cechCohomology
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J (AddCommGrpCat.{max a w})]
    (S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (AddCommGrpCat.{max a w}))) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (U : C) (Cov : Set (PreZeroHypercover.{w} U))
    (hCov : ∀ E ∈ Cov, E.sieve₀ ∈ J U)
    (hcofinal : ∀ R ∈ J U, ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U,
      E ∈ Cov ∧ E.sieve₀ ≤ R)
    (hproducts : ∀ (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U), E ∈ Cov →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
        HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a))))
    (hH1 : ∀ (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U) (hE : E ∈ Cov),
      letI := hproducts E hE
      IsZero (cechCohomology E
        ((sheafToPresheaf J (AddCommGrpCat.{max a w})).obj S.X₁) 1)) :
    Function.Surjective
      (((sheafToPresheaf J (AddCommGrpCat.{max a w})).map S.g).app (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.subsingleton_ext_of_cechCohomology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F9, with the morphism universe of the site free.** If a cofinal
collection of coverings of a collection of objects has all its nonempty finite fibre products in
that collection, then vanishing of positive-degree Čech cohomology on those coverings implies
vanishing of positive-degree cohomology over every object in the collection.

Cohomology over `U` is `Ext` out of the sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on the
representable presheaf of `U`, lifted to the coefficient universe. The coefficient universe
contains the object universe of the site, which is what makes Stacks 03OR available for an
injective abelian presheaf and what replaces the hypothesis that the site be small.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_ext_of_cechCohomology_isZero
    (hCovObjects : ∀ {U : C}
      (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }) (hE : E ∈ Cov U),
      U ∈ B ∧ (∀ i, E.1.X i ∈ B) ∧
        ∀ (p : ℕ) (i : Fin (p + 1) → E.1.I₀),
          letI : ∀ (q : ℕ) (j : Fin (q + 1) → E.1.I₀),
            HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (j a))) := hProducts E hE
          (∏ᶜ (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (i a)))).left ∈ B)
    (hCovCofinal : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ R ∈ J U,
      ∃ (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }),
        E ∈ Cov U ∧ E.1.sieve₀ ≤ R)
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w})
    (hCech : ∀ {U : C}
      (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }) (hE : E ∈ Cov U)
      (p : ℕ), 0 < p →
        letI : ∀ (q : ℕ) (i : Fin (q + 1) → E.1.I₀),
          HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (i a))) := hProducts E hE
        IsZero (cechCohomology E.1 F.obj p))
    (U : C) (hU : U ∈ B) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    Subsingleton (Ext ((presheafToSheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}).obj
      (uliftYoneda.{max a u v w}.obj U ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.free)) F p)
declarations.comment: the coefficient universe contains the objects of the site, which replaces the hypothesis that the site be small with morphisms in the coefficient universe

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.sheafCohomology_isZero_of_cechCohomology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03F9.** If a cofinal collection of coverings of a collection of
objects has all its nonempty finite fibre products in that collection, then vanishing of
positive-degree Čech cohomology on those coverings implies vanishing of positive-degree sheaf
cohomology on every object in the collection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafCohomology_isZero_of_cechCohomology_isZero
    {C : Type u} [Category.{max v w} C] [Small.{max v w} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max v w}]
    [HasExt.{x} (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max v w})]
    (B : Set C)
    (Cov : ∀ U : C,
      Set { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U })
    (hProducts : ∀ {U : C}
      (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }),
      E ∈ Cov U → ∀ (p : ℕ) (i : Fin (p + 1) → E.1.I₀),
        HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (i a))))
    (hCovObjects : ∀ {U : C}
      (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }) (hE : E ∈ Cov U),
      U ∈ B ∧ (∀ i, E.1.X i ∈ B) ∧
        ∀ (p : ℕ) (i : Fin (p + 1) → E.1.I₀),
          letI : ∀ (q : ℕ) (j : Fin (q + 1) → E.1.I₀),
            HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (j a))) := hProducts E hE
          (∏ᶜ (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (i a)))).left ∈ B)
    (hCovCofinal : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ R ∈ J U,
      ∃ (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }),
        E ∈ Cov U ∧ E.1.sieve₀ ≤ R)
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{max v w})
    (hCech : ∀ {U : C}
      (E : { E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U // E.sieve₀ ∈ J U }) (hE : E ∈ Cov U)
      (p : ℕ), 0 < p →
        letI : ∀ (q : ℕ) (i : Fin (q + 1) → E.1.I₀),
          HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.1.f (i a))) := hProducts E hE
        IsZero (cechCohomology E.1 F.obj p))
    (U : C) (hU : U ∈ B) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (Sheaf.H' F p U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleCohomologyForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FD on the small étale site of an algebraic space.**  The cohomology of an
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, computed in `𝒪_X`-modules and read in abelian groups, is the cohomology of its
underlying abelian sheaf (with sections raised to `u + 1`), naturally in `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def moduleCohomologyForgetIso (n : ℕ) :
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
    (globalSectionsFunctor.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)).rightDerived n ⋙
        forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ≅
      moduleToAbelianSheaf B S hS X ⋙
        (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).rightDerived n
declarations.comment: on the small étale site of an algebraic space

declarations.name: ModuleSheafCohomology.moduleSheafCohomologyIsoUnderlying
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FD.** For a sheaf of rings `R` on a site, deriving sections in the category of
`R`-module sheaves and then forgetting to abelian groups gives the same cohomology as first
forgetting to an abelian sheaf and deriving there. The comparison is natural in the module
sheaf, holds globally and over every object of the site, and is compatible in degree zero with
the canonical maps to right-derived functors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleSheafCohomologyIsoUnderlying (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) :
    ∃ eSite : ∀ i : ℕ,
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).rightDerived i ≅
          SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ (Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).rightDerived i,
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙ Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).toRightDerivedZero ≫
          (eSite 0).hom =
        Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R)
          (Sheaf.Γ J Ab.{u}).toRightDerivedZero ∧
      ∀ U : C,
        ∃ eU : ∀ i : ℕ,
            (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                (sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).rightDerived i ≅
              SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                ((sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).rightDerived i,
          (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R ⋙
                (sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).toRightDerivedZero ≫
              (eU 0).hom =
            Functor.whiskerLeft (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} R)
              ((sheafSections J Ab.{u}).obj (op U)).toRightDerivedZero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The associated module of a pullback is the pullback of the associated module.**  For
`a : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of schemes of the big étale site, with `r` the underlying morphism of
schemes and `ε_a` the morphism of ringed sites of Stacks 070R (2),

`(r^*𝓕)^a ≅ ε_a^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_Y`-module `𝓕`, with no quasi-coherence hypothesis.  This **is Stacks 03LC
part (1) at `τ = étale`**, for the small étale sites of two schemes and a morphism between them:
the equivalence of Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = étale` is compatible with pullback.  It is proved
here for arbitrary modules, not only quasi-coherent ones.

Each side is a composite of two pullbacks of sheaves of modules round the square of ringed sites
whose geometric half is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.baseChangeOpensIso` and whose ring half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.structureMap_comp_baseChangeOpensIso`, so the two agree because a
left adjoint is determined by its right adjoint.

**This also carries Stacks 03FH (2)** for the morphism `f_{small} : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale` of
Remark 070R (2): that clause asserts `(f^*𝓕)^a = f_{sites}^*𝓕^a` for every `f_{sites}` of
Remark 070R, and this is the small étale one.  The big fppf one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBigPullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigFppf.lean`); the big Zariski,
étale, smooth and syntomic ones are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigSites.lean`), and the small
Zariski one is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiPushforwardSquare.lean:458`).
(It was formerly cited as `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso`, which
states the commutation over the *identity reading* of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` and is a tautology about `𝟭`;
that declaration is untagged, and naming it here made this enumeration a false completeness
claim.)
Those are every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R lists; the mixed-topology entries
`(Sch/X)_τ ⟶ (Sch/Y)_{τ'}` with `τ ≠ τ'` of the Topologies, Section 03FE list that the remark's
opening sentence also covers are not claimed.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBaseChangeIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback (schemeHom B a) ⋙ associatedModule B X.obj X.property ≅
      associatedModule B Y.obj Y.property ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (smallEtaleStructureMapRing B a)
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism f_small : X_étale → Y_étale of Stacks 070R (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoOfSections
declarations.doc:
**The two constructions of `𝓕^a` on the small étale site agree**: the pullback of `𝓕` along
the morphism of ringed sites `id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, is the sheaf
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleOfSections` whose sections over an object
`f : T → S` of `S_étale` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`.

This is the content of [Stacks, Remark 03FH] (1) on the small étale site: [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4)
defines `𝓕^a` by its sections, and the remark observes that it is the pullback along
`id_{small, étale, Zar}`.  It is [Stacks, Tag 070S] (2) in the object form
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoSections`, followed by the removal of the
sheafification, `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.sheafificationIsoAssociatedModuleOfSections`.

**This carries [Stacks, Remark 03FH] (1) for the second of the two morphisms that clause
offers**, `id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`.  Its `τ = Zariski` counterpart
is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`.  The first morphism of the
clause, `id_{τ, Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪)`, is carried at all five `τ` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSectionsSheaf`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/QuasiCoherentTopologiesTwo/TopologyIndependence.lean`),
which identifies the pullback with the sections-defined `𝓕^a` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (3), the
big-site sheafification being removed by [Stacks, Tag 03DT] exactly as it is removed here;
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/SectionsPullbackComparison/Comparison.lean`) is its
[Stacks, Tag 070S] (1) half, before that removal.  The two morphisms together are the whole of
clause (1).

The quasi-coherence hypothesis is not an addition to 03FH: the construction `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` whose two
descriptions the remark identifies is [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4), which is stated for a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleIsoOfSections :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj F ≅ associatedModuleOfSections B S hS F
declarations.comment: part (1), for the morphism id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (1) at `τ = Zariski`, for the small Zariski sites.**  The equivalence of
Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = Zariski` is compatible with pullback: for `f : T ⟶ S` a morphism of
schemes of the big Zariski site, with `f_small : (T_Zar, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪)` the morphism of ringed
sites of Stacks 070R (2) and `𝓖` an `𝒪_S`-module,

    `(f^*𝓖)^a ≅ f_small^*(𝓖^a)`,

naturally in `𝓖` and with no quasi-coherence hypothesis.

Here `𝓖 ↦ 𝓖^a` is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModule`, the functor of
Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` over the structure sheaf `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` of the small
Zariski site — not the identity reading introduced in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.AssociatedModule.SmallZariskiFullyFaithful`.  That
distinction is what gives this declaration its content.
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso` states the corresponding
commutation over the identity reading, and it does **not** state this clause: the identity
reading is pullback along the identity morphism of ringed sites, isomorphic to `𝟭`, so that
statement reads `f_small^* ⋙ 𝟭 ≅ 𝟭 ⋙ f_small^*` and is proved by whiskering the two unit
isomorphisms and applying the two unitors, never touching the coefficient sheaf
`T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` that clause (2) is about.  It is accordingly untagged.

The proof is `SheafOfModules.pullbackSquareIso`, Stacks 03D8 for a square: the geometric half of
the square is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcBaseChangeOpensIso`, that the base change of the
object chosen over an open `V` of `S` is the object chosen over `f⁻¹(V)`, and the ring half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcStructureMap_comp_baseChangeOpensIso`.

**This is also Stacks 03FH part (2)** for the small Zariski `f_small` of Remark 070R (2).  That
clause asserts `(f^*𝓕)^a = f_sites^*𝓕^a` for every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R
lists, and the two clauses coincide at this `f_sites`: both are the statement that the
associated-module functor of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` commutes with pullback along
the morphism of ringed small Zariski sites of Stacks 070R (2).  The companions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso` — which carries the same two
clauses on one declaration — for the big site at each of the five topologies, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso` for the small étale `f_small`.
Those are every `f_sites` of the enumeration; the mixed-topology entries
`(Sch/X)_τ ⟶ (Sch/Y)_{τ'}` with `τ ≠ τ'` of Topologies, Section 03FE are not claimed.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback (lcSchemeHom B f) ⋙ associatedModule B T.1 T.property ≅
      associatedModule B S.1 S.property ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism f_small : (T_Zar, 𝒪_T) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S) of Stacks 070R (2), for the associated-module functor of Definition 03DU (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleObjPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH part (2) at one module**, and equally **Stacks 03LC part (1) at `τ = Zariski`
at one module**: `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_small^*(𝓕^a)` for the morphism `f_small` of the small Zariski
sites of Stacks 070R (2) and the associated-module functor of Definition 03DU (4).  This is the
form in which Stacks 03FH states its clause, read off from
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def lcAssociatedModuleObjPullbackIso (𝓖 : (S.1).Modules) :
    (associatedModule B T.1 T.property).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (lcSchemeHom B f)).obj 𝓖) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)).obj
        ((associatedModule B S.1 S.property).obj 𝓖)
declarations.comment: part (2) at one module, for the morphism f_small of the small Zariski sites and the associated-module functor of Definition 03DU (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoOfSections
declarations.doc:
**The two constructions of `𝓕ᵃ` on the small Zariski site agree**: the pullback of `𝓕` along
the morphism of ringed sites `(S_Zar, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModule`, is the sheaf
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections` whose sections over an object
`f : T → S` of `S_Zar` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`.

This is the content of [Stacks, Remark 03FH] (1) on the small Zariski site: [Stacks, Tag 03DU]
(4) defines `𝓕ᵃ` by its sections, and the remark observes that it is the pullback along
`id_{small, Zar, Zar}`.  At `τ = Zariski` that morphism of ringed sites is an equivalence, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.restrictModule` is fully faithful and the identification follows
from the two isomorphisms `𝓕 ≅ f_*f^*𝓕`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.restrictAssociatedModuleIso`) and `𝓕 ≅ f_*(𝓕ᵃ)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.sectionsUnitIso`); no sheafification argument is needed, where
`τ = étale` needs [Stacks, Tag 070S] (2).

**This carries [Stacks, Remark 03FH] (1) at `τ = Zariski` for the second of the two morphisms
that clause offers**, `id_{small, Zar, Zar} : (S_Zar, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`.  Its `τ = étale`
counterpart is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`, and the first
morphism of the clause, `id_{τ, Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪)`, is carried at all five `τ`
by `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections`.

The quasi-coherence hypothesis is not an added hypothesis of 03FH: the construction `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ`
whose two descriptions the remark identifies is [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4), which is stated for a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleIsoOfSections :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj F ≅ associatedModuleOfSections B S hS F
declarations.comment: part (1), for the morphism id_{small, Zariski, Zar} : (S_Zar, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBigPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphism of big fppf sites
`f_big : ((Sch/X)_fppf, 𝒪_X) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_fppf, 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 070R.**  The associated module of
a pullback is the pullback of the associated module, `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_{big}^*(𝓕^a)`.

No hypothesis: the morphism of ringed sites is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseChange` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.structureComparison`, both available, and the two provisos of
`SheafOfModules.pullbackSquareIso` are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.opensBaseChangeIso` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.comparisonComp_opensBaseChangeIso`.

Only the fppf `f_big` is claimed here.  Stacks 03FH (2) ranges over every morphism of ringed
sites `f_{sites}` of Remark 070R; the other morphisms that remark enumerates are claimed
elsewhere — `f_big` at the other four topologies by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigSites.lean`, which is this
construction read at a variable topology), the small étale `f_small` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso` and the small Zariski `f_small` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiPushforwardSquare.lean:458`).
(The last was formerly cited as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso`, which states the commutation over
the *identity reading* of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` and is a tautology about `𝟭`; it is untagged, and naming it
here made this enumeration a false completeness claim.)
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBigPullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f ⋙ associatedModule B X hX ≅
      associatedModule B Y hY ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (structureComparison B hX hY f)
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism of big fppf sites f_big of Stacks 070R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBigObjPullbackIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03FH, part (2), at one module**: `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_{big}^*(𝓕^a)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBigObjPullbackIso (𝓕 : Y.Modules) :
    (associatedModule B X hX).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (structureComparison B hX hY f)).obj
        ((associatedModule B Y hY).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (2) at one module, for the morphism of big fppf sites f_big

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphism of big sites
`f_big : ((Sch/X)_τ, 𝒪_X) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_τ, 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 070R (1), at each of the five
topologies `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  The associated module of a
pullback is the pullback of the associated module, `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a)`, naturally in the
`𝒪_Y`-module `𝓕`.

No hypothesis: the morphism of ringed sites is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseChange`
together with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseStructureComparison`, and the two provisos of
`SheafOfModules.pullbackSquareIso` are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.opensBaseChangeIso`, which is topology-free, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.comparisonComp_baseOpensBaseChangeIso`.

Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso` (the small étale `f_small`) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso` (the small Zariski `f_small`,
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiPushforwardSquare.lean:458`)
this is every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R lists: clause (1) of that remark gives
the big site at each of these five topologies, and clause (2) the small site at the two
topologies that have one.  (The small Zariski entry was formerly cited as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso`, which states the commutation over
the *identity reading* of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` and is a tautology about `𝟭`; it is untagged, and naming it
here made this enumeration a false completeness claim.)
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBasePullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f ⋙ baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ ≅
      baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ)
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism of big sites f_big : ((Sch/X)_τ, 𝒪_X) → ((Sch/Y)_τ, 𝒪_Y) of Stacks 070R (1), at each of τ = Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBaseObjPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), at one module**: `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a)` for the morphism of big
sites `f_big` at each of the five topologies, read off from
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBaseObjPullbackIso (𝓕 : Y.Modules) :
    (baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ)).obj
        ((baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (2) at one module, for the morphism of big sites f_big at each of τ = Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigBaseChangeRingedSiteHomPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphism of ringed sites
`f_big : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 070R** — entries (1), (6), (10), (13),
(15) of the Topologies, Section 03FE list — at its registered form
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigBaseChangeRingedSiteHom`, for each of the five topologies:

`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, where `f_big^*` is the pullback along that single morphism
and `(-)^a` is the pullback along `id_{τ, Zar}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom`), as in clause (1).  Nothing
is assumed of `𝓕`.

The proof is the source's: by Lemma 03D8 both sides are pullbacks along a composite morphism
`(Sch/T)_τ ⟶ S_Zar`, namely `f_small ∘ id_{τ, Zar}` and `id_{τ, Zar} ∘ f_big`, and these have
isomorphic functors, `V ↦ f⁻¹(V)` and `V ↦ T ×_S V`, compatibly with the structure maps.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBigBaseChangeRingedSiteHomPullbackIso (τ : CoveringTopology)
    (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f.hom ⋙
        (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom T hT τ).pullbackModulesGeneral ≅
      (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom S hS τ).pullbackModulesGeneral ⋙
        (B.bigBaseChangeRingedSiteHom τ f).pullbackModulesGeneral
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism of ringed sites f_big : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) → ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪_S) of Stacks 070R (entries (1), (6), (10), (13), (15) of Stacks 03FE), at the registered morphism bigBaseChangeRingedSiteHom, for each of the five topologies: (f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a), naturally in 𝓕

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigRingedSiteHomPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites
`f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_{τ'}, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 070R** — entries (1)–(15) of the
Topologies, Section 03FE list, one for each pair with `τ` finer than `τ'` — at their registered
form `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigRingedSiteHom`:

`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, where `f_sites^*` is the pullback along that single morphism
and `(-)^a` is the pullback along `id_{τ, Zar}`, as in clause (1).  The hypothesis is Section
03FE's own condition for the entry to be on its list; nothing is assumed of `𝓕`.

The registered morphism is `id_{τ, τ'} ∘ f_big`, so by Lemma 03D8 its pullback is
`id_{τ, τ'}^*` followed by `f_big^*`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigBaseChangeRingedSiteHomPullbackIso` together
with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.idRingedSiteHomPullbackIso` finishes.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBigRingedSiteHomPullbackIso {τ τ' : CoveringTopology} (h : τ.IsFiner τ')
    (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f.hom ⋙
        (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom T hT τ).pullbackModulesGeneral ≅
      (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom S hS τ').pullbackModulesGeneral ⋙
        (B.bigRingedSiteHom h f).pullbackModulesGeneral
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) → ((Sch/S)_τ', 𝒪_S) of Stacks 070R, entries (1)-(15) of the Stacks 03FE list (τ finer than τ'), at the registered morphism bigRingedSiteHom: (f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a), naturally in 𝓕

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHomPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites
`f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 070R** — entries (16)–(19) of the
Topologies, Section 03FE list, `τ ∈ {étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}` — at their registered form
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHom`:

`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, with `𝓕^a` the associated module of the small étale site of
`S` and `(f^*𝓕)^a` that of the big `τ`-site of `T`.  The hypothesis, `τ` finer than the étale
topology, is Section 03FE's condition for the entry to be on its list.

The registered morphism is `π_S ∘ f_sites` with `f_sites : (Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (Sch/S)_étale`; Lemma 03D8
reduces the clause to that for `f_sites`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigRingedSiteHomPullbackIso`, and to
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.smallEtalePiRingedSiteHomPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHomPullbackIso {τ : CoveringTopology}
    (h : τ.IsFiner .etale) (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f.hom ⋙
        (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom T hT τ).pullbackModulesGeneral ≅
      SmallEtale.associatedModule B.toBigEtaleSite S hS ⋙
        (B.bigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHom h f).pullbackModulesGeneral
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) → (S_étale, 𝒪_S) of Stacks 070R, entries (16)-(19) of the Stacks 03FE list, at the registered morphism bigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHom: (f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a), naturally in 𝓕

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHomPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites
`f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 070R** — entries (20)–(24) of the
Topologies, Section 03FE list, one for each of the five topologies — at their registered form
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom`:

`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕`, with `𝓕^a` the associated module of the small Zariski site
of `S` and `(f^*𝓕)^a` that of the big `τ`-site of `T`.  The hypothesis holds at every `τ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.isFiner_zariski`).

The registered morphism is `π_S ∘ f_sites` with `f_sites : (Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (Sch/S)_Zar`; Lemma 03D8
reduces the clause to that for `f_sites`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.associatedModuleBigRingedSiteHomPullbackIso`, and to
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.smallZariskiPiRingedSiteHomPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHomPullbackIso {τ : CoveringTopology}
    (h : τ.IsFiner .zariski) (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f.hom ⋙
        (B.carriedOverToZariskiRingedSiteHom T hT τ).pullbackModulesGeneral ≅
      SmallZariski.associatedModule B.toBigZariskiSite S hS ⋙
        (B.bigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom h f).pullbackModulesGeneral
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphisms of ringed sites f_sites : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S) of Stacks 070R, entries (20)-(24) of the Stacks 03FE list, at the registered morphism bigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom: (f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*(𝓕^a), naturally in 𝓕

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallEtaleToSmallZariskiPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphism of ringed sites
`f_sites : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y)` of Remark 070R** — entry (26) of the list of
Topologies, Section 03FE, the one mixed pair of small sites.  The associated module of a pullback
is the pullback of the associated module,

`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*𝓕`,

naturally in the `𝒪_Y`-module `𝓕`, with `(f^*𝓕)^a` the associated module on the small étale site
of `X`.  As for entries (20) to (24) the target of `f_sites` is `(Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y)` itself, so the
`𝓕^a` of the source's formulation is `𝓕`.

There is no hypothesis: the étale topology is finer than the Zariski one, which is Section 03FE's
condition for this entry to be on its list.  Nothing is assumed of `𝓕`, and nothing of the
morphism beyond `X` and `Y` lying in the chosen big étale site.

`f_sites` is the registered
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom`, Section 03FE's factorization

`X_étale --f_small--> Y_étale --id_{small,étale,Zar}--> Y_Zar`,

and `f_sites^*` is the pullback of sheaves of modules along that single morphism of ringed sites.
The proof is the source's: Lemma 03D8 splits it as `f_small^*` followed by
`id_{small,étale,Zar}^*`, the second of which is the associated-module functor of the small étale
site by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.pullbackToposGeneral_toZariskiRingedToposHom`, and the
clause for `f_small` on the small étale sites — entry (25) —
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso`, finishes.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleSmallEtaleToSmallZariskiPullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a) ⋙
        SmallEtale.associatedModule B X.obj X.property ≅
      (smallEtaleToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom B a).pullbackModulesGeneral
declarations.comment: part (2), for the morphism of ringed sites f_sites : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) → (Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y) of Stacks 070R — entry (26) of the Stacks 03FE list: (f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*𝓕, naturally in 𝓕, the 𝓕^a of the target being 𝓕 because the target is (Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y) itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallEtaleToSmallZariskiObjPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), at one module**, for the morphism of ringed sites
`f_sites : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y)` of Remark 070R — entry (26) of the Section 03FE list:
`(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_sites^*𝓕`, read off from
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallEtaleToSmallZariskiPullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleSmallEtaleToSmallZariskiObjPullbackIso (𝓕 : Y.obj.Modules) :
    (SmallEtale.associatedModule B X.obj X.property).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a)).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (smallEtaleToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom B a).pullbackModulesGeneral.obj 𝓕
declarations.comment: part (2) at one module, for the morphism of ringed sites f_sites : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) → (Y_Zar, 𝒪_Y) of Stacks 070R — entry (26) of the Stacks 03FE list

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSectionsSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH (1) on the big sites.**  The construction `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (3) —
the sheaf on `(Sch/S)_τ` whose value at `f : T → S` is `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)` — **is** the pullback of
`𝓕` under the morphism of ringed sites
`id_{τ, Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪)`, at each of the five
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.

**No sheafification is left in the statement.**  Two inputs compose.  Stacks 070S (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections`, presents the pullback as the
`τ`-sheafification of the pullback-sections presheaf of modules of Stacks 03DS; and Stacks 03DT
on the five big sites,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isSheaf_sectionsPresheafOfModules_baseOverTopology`, says that for
a quasi-coherent `𝓕` that presheaf is **already** a `τ`-sheaf — it is what
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsSheafOfModules` packages.  So the counit of
`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction` is invertible there and removes the
sheafification, which is the step that turns 070S (1) into the remark's own identification with
`𝓕^a` itself.

**The right-hand side is `𝓕^a` as Definition 03DU (3) defines it**, by its sections: the
underlying presheaf of modules of `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsSheafOfModules` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsPresheafOfModules`, the presheaf of Stacks 03DS, and at
`τ = fppf` the packaging is the tagged clause-(3) definition
`AlgebraicGeometry.overAssociatedModule` on the nose —
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.overAssociatedModule_fppf`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/OverAssociatedModuleIso.lean`, which is
`rfl`.

**What the other 03FH registrations carry.**  Clause (1) of the remark offers two morphisms.
This is the first of them, `id_{τ, Zar}`, on the big site, at all five `τ`; the second,
`id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪)`, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleSectionsIso.lean`), with the
small Zariski reading in
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleIsoOfSections`.  The two together are the whole
of clause (1).  `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections` is the same
comparison read before the sheafification is removed, where it is Stacks 070S (1).

**Quasi-coherence is not an added hypothesis.**  The construction whose two descriptions the
remark identifies is `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (3), which is made for a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module; the sheafified form above, which is 070S's own statement, needs nothing of `𝓕`.

The declaration is also what reads the comparison of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopologyAssociatedModuleIso` below off the sections
description, and so is **the key to Stacks 0GNE**: both of the modules compared there are this
one sheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseAssociatedModuleIsoSectionsSheaf (τ : SiteKind) (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj F ≅ sectionsSheafOfModules B S hS τ F
declarations.comment: part (1) for the first of the two morphisms of ringed sites that clause offers, id_{τ, Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪), on the big site (Sch/S)_τ at each of the five τ: the construction 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a of Definition 03DU (3), the sheaf of sections (f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f^*𝓕), is the pullback under that morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections
declarations.doc:
For each of the five topologies `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, the
associated module of a quasi-coherent module `F` on `S` — the pullback along the morphism of
ringed sites `id_{τ,Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` — is the `τ`-sheafification of the
pullback-sections presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺F)` of Stacks 03DS.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleSheafificationIso` at `F`, which
presents the associated module as the `τ`-sheafification of the presheaf-level pullback, followed
by the `τ`-sheafification of `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsComparison`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.coproductCechComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03FI] (3) on a chosen big site.** For an `𝒪`-module `F` on a chosen big
`τ`-site over `S`, a finite family `E` of morphisms of the site and a morphism `f` of the site
whose image in the schemes over `S` is the morphism from the disjoint union of the image of
`E`, the Čech cohomology of `E` with coefficients in the abelian sheaf underlying `F` is the
Čech cohomology of the one-member family `{f}`, in every degree. This discharges
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.CoproductCechComparison`.
declarations.comment:
part (3), on a chosen big site over a scheme: the Čech complex of a finite
family and of the one-member family of the morphism from its disjoint union agree, for an
abelian sheaf on the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.singleton_sigmaDesc_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
The morphism from the disjoint union of a standard covering is an fpqc covering of the
target, for each of the five topologies.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.singleton_sigmaDesc_mem_fpqcPrecoverage (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] {I : Type w} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ U f) :
    letI : Finite I := h.finite_index
    Presieve.singleton (Sigma.desc f) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.singleton_sigmaDesc_mem_precoverage
declarations.doc:
Outside the Zariski topology, the morphism from the disjoint union of a standard covering is
itself a covering family for the topology the covering is standard for.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.singleton_sigmaDesc_mem_precoverage (τ : CoveringTopology)
    (hτ : τ ≠ .zariski) {T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] {I : Type w} (U : I → Scheme.{u})
    (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T) (h : IsStandardCovering τ U f) :
    letI : Finite I := h.finite_index
    Presieve.singleton (Sigma.desc f) ∈ Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ) T
declarations.comment: part (1), covering in the original topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.sieve_sigmaDesc_mem_topology
declarations.doc:
In every one of the five topologies, the sieve generated by the morphism from the disjoint
union of a standard covering is a covering sieve of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.sieve_sigmaDesc_mem_topology (τ : CoveringTopology) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine T] {I : Type w} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ U f) :
    letI : Finite I := h.finite_index
    Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton (Sigma.desc f)) ∈
      (Scheme.precoverage (coveringMorphismProperty τ)).toGrothendieck T
declarations.comment: part (1), covering sieve in every topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_over
declarations.doc:
For an abelian sheaf on a topology on `Over S` refining the big Zariski topology, the
canonical refinement of a finite family by the morphism from its disjoint union induces an
isomorphism of Čech complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_over (S : Scheme.{u})
    (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S)) (hJ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) {T : Over S}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T) [Finite E.I₀] (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{v})
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf J F) :
    IsIso (Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexMap E
      (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} (Sigma.desc E.f))
      (Stacks.CechSite.coproductRefinement E) (F ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{w, v}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
For an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `S`, the canonical refinement of a finite
family by the morphism from its disjoint union induces an isomorphism of Čech complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_smallEtale (S : Scheme.{u}) {T : S.Etale}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T) [Finite E.I₀] (F : (S.Etale)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{v})
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology S) F) :
    IsIso (Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexMap E
      (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} (Sigma.desc E.f))
      (Stacks.CechSite.coproductRefinement E) (F ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{w, v}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.sieve_sigmaDesc_mem_smallEtaleTopology
declarations.doc:
The morphism from the disjoint union of a standard étale covering of an object of the small
étale site of `S` generates a covering sieve of that object.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.sieve_sigmaDesc_mem_smallEtaleTopology (S : Scheme.{u})
    {T : S.Etale} [IsAffine T.left] (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T) [HasCoproduct E.X]
    (h : IsStandardCovering .etale (fun i : E.I₀ ↦ (E.X i).left) (fun i ↦ (E.f i).left)) :
    Sieve.ofArrows (fun _ : PUnit ↦ ∐ E.X) (fun _ : PUnit ↦ Sigma.desc E.f) ∈
      Scheme.smallEtaleTopology S T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_smallZariski
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03FI part (3), case (c).** For an abelian sheaf on the small Zariski
site of a scheme, read on the big Zariski site through its extension, the refinement of a finite
family of morphisms by the single morphism from the coproduct of its members induces an
isomorphism of Čech complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_smallZariski (S : Scheme.{u})
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology S) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    {T : Over S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T) [Finite E.I₀] :
    IsIso (Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexMap E
      (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} (Sigma.desc E.f))
      (Stacks.CechSite.coproductRefinement E)
      ((SmallZariski.extension.{u, v} S F).obj ⋙
        AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{w, max (u + 1) v}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.extension_sections
declarations.doc:
The value of the small-to-big Zariski extension on a scheme `T` over `S`
is the global sections on `T` of the inverse image of the sheaf along its
structure morphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.extension_sections_naturality
declarations.doc:
The valuewise geometric comparison respects every morphism over `S`.
Thus the small-to-big extension is identified with the presheaf of sections
of the geometric inverse image, not merely with its values at each object.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extension_sections_naturality
    (S : Scheme.{u}) {T T' : Over S} (g : T' ⟶ T)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology S)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (extension_sections.{u, v} S T).hom.app F ≫
      pullbackSectionsRestriction.{u, v} S g F =
      ((extension.{u, v} S F).obj.map g.op) ≫
        (extension_sections.{u, v} S T').hom.app F
declarations.comment: case (c), naturality of the geometric extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isIso_extension_unit
declarations.doc:
Restricting the extension of an abelian sheaf on the small Zariski site back
to the open subschemes returns the sheaf itself: the unit of the adjunction is an
isomorphism. This pins `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.extension` as an extension of the
given sheaf.
declarations.comment: case (c), the extension restricts to the given sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.coproductRefinement
declarations.doc:
The component inclusions of a coproduct exhibit a family of morphisms with fixed target as
a refinement of the singleton family given by the induced morphism from the coproduct.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coproductRefinement {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {T : C} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T) [HasCoproduct E.X] :
    E.HomOver (PreZeroHypercover.singleton (Sigma.desc E.f)) (𝟙 T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isZero_cechCohomology_succ_associatedPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Vanishing of Čech cohomology on the cardinality-bounded small étale site of `S`.** The Čech
cohomology of the sections of `Fᵃ` on a standard covering of an object of
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale B S hS` vanishes in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cechCohomology_succ_associatedPresheaf (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] {T : SmallEtale B S hS} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T)
    (h : IsBoundedStandardCovering B S hS E) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology E
      ((toOver B S hS).op ⋙ quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) p)
declarations.comment: the `Cech^p = 0 for p >= 1` clause on the cardinality-bounded small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cechComplexIsoAmitsurQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
For `U` an object of `Over S` with affine total space and `f : W ⟶ U` with `W.left` affine,
the Čech complex of the presheaf `Fᵃ` on the one-member covering `{W → U}` is the complex
`s((A/R)_• ⊗_R M)`, where `R = Γ(U.left, 𝒪)`, `A = Γ(W.left, 𝒪)` and `M = Fᵃ(U)`, with its
`R`-module structure forgotten.
declarations.statement:
public def cechComplexIsoAmitsurQuasiCoherent (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    {W : Over S} (f : W ⟶ U) [IsAffine W.left] :
    letI := overAffineSliceAlgebra U f
    cechComplex (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{u} f) (quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) ≅
      ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(U.left, ⊤) : Type u)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (amitsurCochainComplex (Γ(U.left, ⊤) : Type u) (Γ(W.left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Stacks.Sites.coeffModule S F (𝟭 (Over S)) U))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of complexes, for the one-member covering 03FI reduces to

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cechComplexIsoAmitsurStandardCovering
declarations.doc:
For a standard `τ`-covering `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an object of `Over S` with affine total
space, the Čech complex of `Fᵃ` is `s((A/R)_• ⊗_R M)`, where `R = Γ(U.left, 𝒪)`,
`A = Γ((∐ U_i).left, 𝒪)` and `M = Fᵃ(U)`.
declarations.statement:
public def cechComplexIsoAmitsurStandardCovering (τ : CoveringTopology) (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} U)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ (fun i ↦ (𝒱.X i).left) (fun i ↦ (𝒱.f i).left)) :
    letI : Finite 𝒱.I₀ := h.finite_index
    letI : IsAffine (∐ 𝒱.X).left := h.isAffine_left_sigmaObj τ S 𝒱
    letI := overAffineSliceAlgebra U (Sigma.desc 𝒱.f)
    cechComplex 𝒱 (quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) ≅
      ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(U.left, ⊤) : Type u))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (amitsurCochainComplex (Γ(U.left, ⊤) : Type u) (Γ((∐ 𝒱.X).left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Stacks.Sites.coeffModule S F (𝟭 (Over S)) U))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of complexes, for an arbitrary standard covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cechComplexIsoAmitsurSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
For a small-étale-standard covering `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an object of `S_étale`, the Čech
complex of the presheaf `Fᵃ` is the complex `s((A/R)_• ⊗_R M)`, where `R = Γ(U, 𝒪)`,
`A = Γ(∐ U_i, 𝒪)` and `M = Fᵃ(U)`.
declarations.statement:
public def cechComplexIsoAmitsurSmallEtale (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] {T : S.Etale}
    (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T) (h : IsSmallEtaleStandardCovering S 𝒱) :
    letI : IsAffine ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj T).left :=
      (IsSmallEtaleStandardCovering.isAffine S h).1
    letI : Finite (𝒱.map (Scheme.Etale.forget S)).I₀ :=
      IsSmallEtaleStandardCovering.finite S h
    letI := overAffineSliceAlgebra ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj T)
      (Sigma.desc (𝒱.map (Scheme.Etale.forget S)).f)
    cechComplex 𝒱 ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).op ⋙ quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) ≅
      ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ(((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj T).left, ⊤) : Type u))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (amitsurCochainComplex (Γ(((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj T).left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Γ((∐ (𝒱.map (Scheme.Etale.forget S)).X).left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Stacks.Sites.coeffModule S F (𝟭 (Over S)) ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).obj T)))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of complexes, case (b), the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cechCohomology_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
The Čech cohomology of `Fᵃ` on a small-étale-standard covering vanishes in every positive
degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cechCohomology_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf_smallEtale (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] {T : S.Etale} (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T)
    (h : IsSmallEtaleStandardCovering S 𝒱) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology 𝒱
      ((Scheme.Etale.forget S).op ⋙ quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) p)
declarations.comment: the `Cech^p = 0 for p >= 1` clause, case (b), the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cechComplexIsoAmitsurSmallZariski
declarations.doc:
For a standard Zariski covering `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an affine open `U` of `S`, the Čech
complex in `S_Zar` of the presheaf `Fᵃ`, which on the small Zariski site is `V ↦ Γ(V, F|_V)`,
is the complex `s((A/R)_• ⊗_R M)`, where `R = Γ(U, 𝒪)`, `A = Γ(∐ U_i, 𝒪)` with the coproduct
taken in `Over S`, and `M = Fᵃ(U)`.
declarations.statement:
public def cechComplexIsoAmitsurSmallZariski (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    {T : S.Opens} [IsAffine (S.restrictFunctor.obj T).left]
    (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T)
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → 𝒱.I₀), HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (𝒱.f (i a)))]
    (h : IsStandardCovering .zariski
      (fun i ↦ ((𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).X i).left)
      (fun i ↦ ((𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).f i).left)) :
    letI : Finite (𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).I₀ := h.finite_index
    letI := overAffineSliceAlgebra (S.restrictFunctor.obj T)
      (Sigma.desc (𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).f)
    cechComplex 𝒱 (S.restrictFunctor.op ⋙ quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) ≅
      ((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Γ((S.restrictFunctor.obj T).left, ⊤) : Type u))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (amitsurCochainComplex (Γ((S.restrictFunctor.obj T).left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Γ((∐ (𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).X).left, ⊤) : Type u)
          (Stacks.Sites.coeffModule S F (𝟭 (Over S)) (S.restrictFunctor.obj T)))
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of complexes, case (c), the small Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cechCohomology_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf_smallZariski
declarations.doc:
The Čech cohomology of `Fᵃ` on a standard Zariski covering of an affine open of `S` vanishes
in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cechCohomology_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf_smallZariski (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] {T : S.Opens} [IsAffine (S.restrictFunctor.obj T).left]
    (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} T)
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → 𝒱.I₀), HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (𝒱.f (i a)))]
    (h : IsStandardCovering .zariski
      (fun i ↦ ((𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).X i).left)
      (fun i ↦ ((𝒱.map S.restrictFunctor).f i).left)) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology 𝒱
      (S.restrictFunctor.op ⋙ quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) p)
declarations.comment: the `Cech^p = 0 for p >= 1` clause, case (c), the small Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cechCohomology_singleton_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf
declarations.doc:
Čech vanishing in positive degrees for the one-member covering of an affine object of
`Over S` by an affine object whose coordinate ring is faithfully flat over that of the target,
with the presheaf `Fᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DS] as coefficients.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cechCohomology_singleton_succ_quasiCoherentPresheaf
    (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] {W : Over S} (f : W ⟶ U) [IsAffine W.left]
    (hff : letI := overAffineSliceAlgebra U f
      Module.FaithfullyFlat (Γ(U.left, ⊤) : Type u) (Γ(W.left, ⊤) : Type u))
    (p : ℕ) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{u} f)
      (quasiCoherentPresheafFunctor S F) (p + 1))
