declarations.comment: the canonical morphism of modules of an isomorphism is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentSheaves
declarations.doc:
The category `QCoh(𝒪_F)` of quasi-coherent sheaves on the algebraic space `F`: the full
subcategory of the `𝒪_F`-modules cut out by quasi-coherence on the small étale ringed site.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev QuasicoherentSheaves (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.**  The inverse image `i^*F` of a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module along a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` is quasi-coherent.

Quasi-coherence is local on `Z`, the base changes of the affine étale charts of `X` cover `Z`,
and over such a chart the composite to `X` factors through an affine chart, which is the case of
Stacks 03GA already available.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isClosedImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS i).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the inverse image along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03GA].**  The pullback `f^*F` of Stacks 03LU of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_Y`-module along an arbitrary morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is quasi-coherent.

On the chart space of a chart of `X` carrying an affine chart diagram over `f` the pullback of
`F` along the composite with `f` is quasi-coherent, because that composite factors through the
structure morphism of an affine étale chart of `Y`; the composition comparison of Stacks 03LU
turns that into quasi-coherence of the pullback of `f^*F` to the chart space, and those charts
cover the final object of the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentPullbackFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03GA], in the form the source states it.**  The pullback of Stacks 03LU
along an arbitrary morphism of algebraic spaces restricts to a functor
`QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` between the categories of quasi-coherent modules of Stacks 03G9.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentPullbackFunctor (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ⥤
      QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the induced functor on quasi-coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA for a module with a global presentation.**  If an `𝒪_Y`-module `F` admits a
`SheafOfModules.Presentation` then its pullback `f^*F` of Stacks 03LU along an arbitrary
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is quasi-coherent.

The inverse image of Stacks 03D2 is a left adjoint carrying `𝒪_Y` to `f⁻¹𝒪_Y`, so it carries
the presentation along; extension of scalars to `𝒪_X` carries it further.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_presentation (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (P : F.Presentation) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the pullback of a module with a global presentation is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA for a module of finite presentation.**  The pullback `f^*F` of Stacks 03LU of
an `𝒪_Y`-module of finite presentation along an arbitrary morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces is quasi-coherent.

Unlike the globally presented case this assumes only *local* presentations, which transport
along `f⁻¹` because a finite presentation over an object is a point of a sheaf of sets indexed
by `ℕ × ℕ`.  The clause 03DL (7) of Stacks 03DO therefore holds outright, and a module of
finite presentation is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isFinitePresentation (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the pullback of a module of finite presentation is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA along an étale morphism.**  The pullback functor
`f^* : Mod(𝒪_Y) ⟶ Mod(𝒪_X)` of Stacks 03LU along an étale morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces preserves quasi-coherence, with no hypothesis on the module beyond quasi-coherence.

Along an étale morphism the pullback of Stacks 03LU is restriction of sections along
postcomposition of étale charts, by Stacks' Equation 03LW, and quasi-coherence is inherited by
that restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_isEtale (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the pullback functor preserves quasi-coherence along an étale morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentPullbackOfIsEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA along an étale morphism, in the form the source states it**: the pullback of
Stacks 03LU along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces restricts to a functor
`QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)` between the categories of quasi-coherent modules of Stacks 03G9.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentPullbackOfIsEtale (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ⥤
      QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the induced functor on quasi-coherent modules, along an étale morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_affineChartFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA along a morphism factoring through an affine étale chart of the target.**  If
`f : X ⟶ Y` factors as `k ≫ φ` with `φ` the structure morphism of an étale chart of `Y` whose
underlying scheme is affine, then `f^*` carries quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-modules to quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules, with no hypothesis on `k` and none on the module beyond quasi-coherence.

This is the general case of Stacks 03GA localized at one chart of the target; see the
implementation notes for what the general case still needs.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_affineChartFactorization (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)
    (hV : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1).obj V)))
    (k : X ⟶ chartSpace B S hS Y V) (hk : f = k ≫ chartToSpace B S hS Y V)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the pullback along a morphism factoring through an affine chart of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentPullbackOfAffineChartFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GA along a morphism factoring through an affine étale chart of the target, in the
form the source states it**: the pullback of Stacks 03LU along `k ≫ φ`, with `φ` the structure
morphism of an affine étale chart of `Y`, restricts to a functor `QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_X)`
between the categories of quasi-coherent modules of Stacks 03G9.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentPullbackOfAffineChartFactorization (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1)
    (hV : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS Y.1).obj V)))
    (k : X ⟶ chartSpace B S hS Y V) :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ⥤
      QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the induced functor on quasi-coherent modules, through an affine chart

declarations.name: vandermondeProd_isUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03GF.** For every `d < p`, the element `Δ_d = ∏_{0 ≤ i < j < d}
(α_i - α_j)` is a unit in `R' = Z[1/p][x]/(Phi(x))`.

Δ_d is a double product of the differences `αᵢ - αⱼ`; each such difference (for
`i < j < d ≤ p-1`) is a unit by `alpha_sub_isUnit`, and a product of units is a
unit (`Finset.prod_induction` with `IsUnit.mul`, `isUnit_one`).
declarations.statement: theorem vandermondeProd_isUnit (d : ℕ) (hd : d < p) : IsUnit (vandermondeProd p d)

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.toIntegralClosure_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a smooth ring map, let `R → B` be any ring map, let
`A = integralClosure R B` be the integral closure of `R` in `B` and let
`A' = integralClosure S (S ⊗[R] B)` be the integral closure of `S` in `S ⊗[R] B`. Then the
canonical map `S ⊗[R] A → A'`, `s ⊗ a ↦ s ⊗ a`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem toIntegralClosure_bijective {R S B : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.Smooth R S] :
    Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure R S B)
declarations.comment:
The isomorphism of the tag is bijectivity of Mathlib's canonical map
`TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure`, whose `AlgEquiv` form is `AlgEquiv.ofBijective` applied to it.
This is Mathlib's `TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_smooth`, which carries no
`@[stacks]` tag upstream. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**A Nagata ring has finite integral closure in a reduced algebra essentially of finite type.**

Let `R` be a Nagata ring, that is, a Noetherian ring such that `R ⧸ p` is N-2 (Japanese) for
every prime `p`, and let `S` be a reduced `R`-algebra essentially of finite type. Then the
integral closure `A` of `R` in `S` is a finite `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsIntegralClosure.finite_of_essFiniteType_of_isReduced
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S] [IsReduced S]
    {A : Type v} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra A S] [IsScalarTower R A S]
    [IsIntegralClosure A R S]
    (hR : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsJapaneseRing (R ⧸ p)) :
    Module.Finite R A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistSheafMultiplicationMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical multiplication map `𝒪_X(n) ⊗ ℱ(m) ⟶ ℱ(n + m)`** on `X = Proj S`, for a
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules `ℱ`: reassociate, braid `𝒪(n)` past `ℱ`, reassociate again, and
multiply the two twists of the structure sheaf together.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def twistSheafMultiplicationMap
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology (ProjectiveSpectrum.top 𝒮))
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
        (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.structureSheaf 𝒮))) (n m : ℤ) :
    (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, u, u, u, u}
        (ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.structureSheaf 𝒮)).obj ((twistingSheaf 𝒮 n))).obj
        ((twistSheafOfModules 𝒮 F m))) ⟶
      twistSheafOfModules 𝒮 F (n + m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsPairing
declarations.doc:
**The pairing `(⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, 𝒪_X(n))) × (⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} Γ(X, ℱ(m))) ⟶ ⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} Γ(X, ℱ(m))`**
on `X = Proj 𝒮`: the biadditive extension of the canonical multiplication of a global section of
`𝒪_X(n)` with a global section of `ℱ(m)`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.globalSectionsPairing_of_of
declarations.doc:
The pairing of a global section of `𝒪(n)` with a global section of `ℱ(m)` is their canonical
product, a global section of `ℱ(n + m)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem globalSectionsPairing_of_of (n : ℕ) (m : ℤ) (s : twistGlobalSections 𝒮 n)
    (t : (twistSheafOfModules 𝒮 F m).val.obj (op ⊤)) :
    globalSectionsPairing 𝒮 F (DirectSum.of _ n s) (DirectSum.of _ m t) =
      DirectSum.of _ ((n : ℤ) + m) (multiplyHomogeneousSections 𝒮 F n m s t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpectrum.Proj.twistedGlobalSectionsModule
declarations.doc:
**The module `⨁_{m ∈ ℤ} Γ(X, ℱ(m))` over the graded ring `⨁_{n ≥ 0} Γ(X, 𝒪_X(n))`** on
`X = Proj 𝒮`, for the pairing that multiplies a global section of `𝒪_X(n)` with a global
section of `ℱ(m)` through the canonical morphism `𝒪_X(n) ⊗ ℱ(m) ⟶ ℱ(n + m)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance twistedGlobalSectionsModule :
    Module (⨁ n : ℕ, twistGlobalSections 𝒮 n) (twistedGlobalSections 𝒮 F)
declarations.comment: the module structure on the twisted global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjectiveSpace.closedSubscheme_iso_projQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 03GL, third assertion: `Z = Proj(R[T₀, …, Tₙ]/I)`.** Let `R` be an arbitrary
commutative ring and let `i : Z ⟶ ℙⁿ_R` be a closed subscheme of projective `n`-space over `R`.
Let `I ⊆ R[T₀, …, Tₙ]` be the homogeneous ideal generated by the homogeneous polynomials whose
twisted global section pulls back to zero on `Z` — the ideal whose degree-`d` part is
`Ker(R[T₀, …, Tₙ]_d ⟶ Γ(Z, 𝒪(d)|_Z))`, by the two assertions of the tag registered on
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealOfClosedSubscheme.mem_idealOfClosedSubscheme_iff` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealOfClosedSubscheme.idealOfClosedSubscheme_isHomogeneous`.

Then `Z` is isomorphic to `Proj(R[T₀, …, Tₙ]/I)`, compatibly with the two morphisms into `ℙⁿ_R`:
the closed immersion `i` itself, and the canonical morphism
`Stacks.ClosedSubschemeProjQuotient.ambientHom` read through the comparison. So the two are equal
as closed subschemes of projective space.

No hypothesis is placed on `R`; in particular it need not be Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedSubscheme_iso_projQuotient {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.projectiveSpaceOverRing n (CommRingCat.of R))
    [IsClosedImmersion i] :
    ∃ e : Z ≅ projQuotient (polyGrading R n) (i ≫ (comparisonIso R n).hom),
      e.hom ≫ ambientHom (polyGrading R n) (i ≫ (comparisonIso R n).hom) ≫
        (comparisonIso R n).inv = i
declarations.comment: the closed subscheme is the Proj of the quotient

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistComparisonIso.gradedModule_and_isIso_comparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03GM].** Let `R` be a ring and let `ℱ` be a quasi-coherent sheaf on
`ℙᵐ_R`. For `d ≥ 0` put `M_d = Γ(ℙᵐ_R, ℱ(d))`. Then `M = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} M_d` is a graded
`R[T₀, …, Tₘ]`-module and there is a canonical isomorphism `ℱ = M̃`.

The first conjunct is the graded-module assertion, in three parts: the integer grading
decomposes `M` internally, the grading of `R[T₀, …, Tₘ]` acts on that grading, and the action of
a homogeneous element is the multiplication map of the twists of Equation 03GK. The second and
third are the canonical isomorphism: the comparison `M̃ ⟶ ℱ` is the unique morphism restricting
on each positive-degree standard open `D₊(f)` to `x / f ^ n ↦ x|_{D₊(f)} ⊗ f ^ (-n)`, and it is
invertible.

The source's omitted injectivity and surjectivity arguments are
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistChartBijective.exists_pow_smul_eq_zero_of_numerSection_eq_zero`
and `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistChartBijective.exists_numerSection_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gradedModule_and_isIso_comparison
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (projRingSheaf (projectiveGrading m R)))
    (hqc : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent
      (R := (AlgebraicGeometry.Proj (projectiveGrading m R)).ringCatSheaf) F) :
    (DirectSum.IsInternal (moduleGrading (projectiveGrading m R) F) ∧
        SetLike.GradedSMul (projectiveGrading m R)
          (moduleGrading (projectiveGrading m R) F) ∧
        ∀ (e k : ℕ) (a : projectiveGrading m R e)
          (s : twistSections (projectiveGrading m R) F k),
          (a : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + 1)) R) •
              DirectSum.of (twistSections (projectiveGrading m R) F) k s =
            DirectSum.of (twistSections (projectiveGrading m R) F) (e + k)
              (gsmul (projectiveGrading m R) F a.2 k (e + k) rfl s)) ∧
      (∃! φ : associatedTwistSectionSheaf (projectiveGrading m R) F ⟶ F,
          ∀ p : PositiveElem (projectiveGrading m R),
            φ.val.app (op (positiveBasicOpen (projectiveGrading m R) p)) =
              positiveChartHom (projectiveGrading m R) F p) ∧
      IsIso (comparison (projectiveGrading m R) F)
declarations.comment:
both assertions of the tag in one statement, for a quasi-coherent `ℱ` on `ℙᵐ_R`:
the twisted global sections `M = ⨁_{d ≥ 0} Γ(ℙᵐ_R, ℱ(d))` form a graded `R[T₀, …, Tₘ]`-module --
internally graded, with the grading of the ring acting on the grading of `M`, the action being
the multiplication map of the twists of Equation 03GK -- and the canonical comparison `M̃ ⟶ ℱ`,
the unique morphism restricting on each positive-degree standard open `D₊(f)` to
`x / f ^ n ↦ x|_{D₊(f)} ⊗ f ^ (-n)`, is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyClosed_of_universallyClosed_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03GN], the universally closed half.** Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` be a commutative
triangle with `X ⟶ Y` surjective. If `X ⟶ S` is universally closed, then so is `Y ⟶ S`: a map is
closed as soon as its precomposition with a continuous surjection is, and surjectivity is stable
under base change.
declarations.statement:
lemma universallyClosed_of_universallyClosed_of_surjective (h : g ≫ q = p) [Surjective g]
    [UniversallyClosed p] : UniversallyClosed q
declarations.comment: the universally closed half, in the triangle form of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_of_isProper_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03GN].** The image of a proper scheme is proper: in a commutative triangle
`X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` with `X ⟶ Y` surjective and `X` proper over `S`, the morphism `Y ⟶ S` is proper as
soon as it is separated and locally of finite type.

Universal closedness is the previous lemma; separatedness and locally-of-finite-typeness are
hypotheses, exactly as in the source, since neither descends along a bare surjection.
declarations.statement:
lemma isProper_of_isProper_of_surjective (h : g ≫ q = p) [Surjective g] [IsProper p]
    [IsSeparated q] [LocallyOfFiniteType q] : IsProper q
declarations.comment: the image of a proper scheme is proper, in the triangle form of the source: separatedness and locally-of-finite-typeness of the image are hypotheses, as they are there

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationCoprodIso_inv_coprodDesc_fromNormalization
registrations.comment: compatibility with the morphisms to the base

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toNormalization_inl_normalizationCoprodIso_hom
registrations.comment: compatibility with the dominant morphism from the first summand

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toNormalization_inr_normalizationCoprodIso_hom
registrations.comment: compatibility with the dominant morphism from the second summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_app_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GQ.** For a universally closed morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and
an affine open `U` of `S`, the ring map `Γ(S, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f⁻¹(U))` on sections is integral. This
is the assertion that `f_* 𝒪_X` is integral over `𝒪_S`.

Only universal closedness is needed; the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of Tag 03GQ
are what make `f_* 𝒪_X` a quasi-coherent algebra, not what make it integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_app_of_universallyClosed (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : S.Opens}
    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : RingHom.IsIntegral (f.app U).hom
declarations.comment: integrality of the pushed-forward structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegralHom_toBase_pushforwardSpectrum
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-separated, universally closed morphism `f : X ⟶ S` the sheaf of algebras
`f_* 𝒪_X` is integral over `𝒪_S`: the structure morphism `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X) ⟶ S` of its relative
spectrum is an integral morphism.

An affine morphism is integral as soon as it is universally closed, and universal closedness is
checked on the affine opens of `S`, where the structure morphism is the spectrum of the integral
ring map `Γ(S, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f⁻¹U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_toBase_pushforwardSpectrum :
    IsIntegralHom (pushforwardSpectrum f).toBase

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-separated, universally closed morphism `f : X ⟶ S` the normalization of `S` in
`X` is isomorphic to the relative spectrum `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum :
    f.normalization ≅ (pushforwardSpectrum f).scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.toNormalization_normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom
declarations.doc:
Under the identification of the normalization of `S` in `X` with `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, the
canonical morphism `X ⟶ f.normalization` becomes the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toNormalization_normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom :
    f.toNormalization ≫ (normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum f).hom = canonicalMorphism f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_comp_toBase
declarations.doc:
Under the identification of the normalization of `S` in `X` with `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, the
structure morphism `f.normalization ⟶ S` becomes the structure morphism `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X) ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_comp_toBase :
    (normalizationIsoPushforwardSpectrum f).hom ≫ (pushforwardSpectrum f).toBase =
      f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.normalizationIsoRelativeSpec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GQ.** For a quasi-separated and universally closed morphism
`f : X ⟶ S`, the relative normalization of `S` in `X` is the relative spectrum of `f_* 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalizationIsoRelativeSpec :
    f.normalization ≅ (gluedSpectrum (pushforwardSituation f)).scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.normalizationIsoRelativeSpec_hom_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GQ.** The comparison of the relative normalization with the relative
spectrum of `f_* 𝒪_X` is an isomorphism over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem normalizationIsoRelativeSpec_hom_toBase :
    (normalizationIsoRelativeSpec f).hom ≫
        (gluedSpectrum (pushforwardSituation f)).toBase = f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeSpec.toNormalization_normalizationIsoRelativeSpec_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GQ.** The comparison of the relative normalization with the relative
spectrum of `f_* 𝒪_X` carries the canonical morphism to the relative normalization to the
canonical morphism of [Stacks, Tag 01LY]. Together with
`Stacks.RelativeSpec.normalizationIsoRelativeSpec_hom_toBase` this says that the relative
normalization of `S` in `X` *is* the factorization `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X) ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toNormalization_normalizationIsoRelativeSpec_hom :
    f.toNormalization ≫ (normalizationIsoRelativeSpec f).hom = toRelativeSpec f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GR.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite type with `X` reduced and `S`
Nagata. Then the normalization of `S` in `X` is finite over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hS : IsNagataScheme S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsReduced X] :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian S :=
      ((isNagataScheme_iff_isLocallyNoetherian_and_isUniversallyJapaneseScheme S).mp hS).1
    IsFinite f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GU.** A quasi-finite morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of affine schemes factors
as `j ≫ π` with `Z` affine, `j : Y ⟶ Z` an open immersion and `π : Z ⟶ X` finite.

Quasi-compactness of `f` is not assumed: it is automatic for an affine source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_factorization {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine Z) (j : Y ⟶ Z) (π : Z ⟶ X),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsFinite π ∧ j ≫ π = f

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S`
factors as `f = f' ≫ π`, where `S'` is the normalization of `S` in `X`, where `f'` is the
canonical map to `S'` and where `π` is the structure morphism of `S'`.

A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this also supplies the factorization
of [Stacks Project, Tag 03H2].
declarations.statement:
public theorem toNormalization_fromNormalization :
    f.toNormalization ≫ f.fromNormalization = f

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.quasiCompact_toNormalization
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The first map of the factorization is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: public theorem quasiCompact_toNormalization : QuasiCompact f.toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.quasiSeparated_toNormalization
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The first map of the factorization is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: public theorem quasiSeparated_toNormalization : QuasiSeparated f.toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIntegralHom_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The second map of the factorization, the structure morphism
of the normalization of `S` in `X`, is integral.

A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this also supplies the integrality of
the second factor in [Stacks Project, Tag 03H2].
declarations.statement: public theorem isIntegralHom_fromNormalization : IsIntegralHom f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.universallyClosed_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The first map of the factorization of a universally closed,
quasi-separated morphism is universally closed.
declarations.statement: public theorem universallyClosed_toNormalization : UniversallyClosed f.toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.surjective_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The first map of the factorization of a universally closed,
quasi-separated morphism is surjective: it is universally closed and dominant.
declarations.statement: public theorem surjective_toNormalization : Surjective f.toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_normalizationPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY (flat_base_change).**  Formation of the factorization
`f = π ∘ f'` of a universally closed, quasi-separated morphism commutes with flat base change:
the comparison morphism from the normalization of the base change `f_T : X ×_S T ⟶ T` to the
base change `T ×_S S'` of the normalization of `S` in `X` is an isomorphism.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalizationPullback_snd` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.toNormalization_normalizationPullback_fst`, which say that the
comparison morphism matches the two factors, this is the assertion that the whole factorization
is obtained from that of `f` by base change.
declarations.statement: public instance isIso_normalizationPullback : IsIso (f.normalizationPullback g)

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.normalizationPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY (flat_base_change).**  The identification, over `T`, of the
intermediate scheme of the factorization of the base change `f_T : X ×_S T ⟶ T` with the base
change `T ×_S S'` of the intermediate scheme of the factorization of `f`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_normalizationPullbackIso_hom_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY (flat_base_change).**  Under that identification the first
factor of the factorization of `f_T` becomes the base change of the first factor of `f`.

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.overIsoPushforwardSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY (relative_spectrum).**  Clause (4) of the factorization of a
universally closed, quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S`: the intermediate scheme `S'` of the
factorization is, as a scheme over `S`, the relative spectrum `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of the
pushed-forward structure sheaf.  Being an isomorphism over `S` is the statement that the second
factor `π : S' ⟶ S` becomes the structure morphism of the relative spectrum.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def overIsoPushforwardSpectrum :
    Over.mk f.fromNormalization ≅ Over.mk (pushforwardSpectrum f).toBase

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY (relative_spectrum).**  Under the identification of the
intermediate scheme of the factorization with `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, the first factor
`f' : X ⟶ S'` becomes the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 01LY].
declarations.statement:
public theorem toNormalization_overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_left :
    f.toNormalization ≫ (overIsoPushforwardSpectrum f).hom.left = canonicalMorphism f

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_c_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  Clause (3) of the factorization of a universally closed,
quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S`: the canonical map from the structure sheaf of the
normalization `S'` of `S` in `X` to the pushforward of the structure sheaf of `X` along the
first map `f' : X ⟶ S'` is an isomorphism, that is, `f'_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}`.
declarations.statement: public theorem isIso_c_toNormalization : IsIso f.toNormalization.c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyConnected_fiber_iff_forall_etaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GZ.** The fibre of a morphism at a point is geometrically connected
if and only if the fibre at the distinguished point after pullback to every étale neighborhood
is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem geometricallyConnected_fiber_iff_forall_etaleNeighborhood
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (s : S) :
    GeometricallyConnected (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ↔
      ∀ U : EtaleNeighborhood S s,
        ConnectedSpace ((pullback.snd f U.toBase).fiber U.point)

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isFinite_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (2).**  For a proper morphism `f : X ⟶ S` onto a locally
Noetherian scheme, the second factor `π : S' ⟶ S` of the Stein factorization — the structure
morphism of the normalization of `S` in `X` — is **finite**.  **No hypothesis.**

This is the one clause of Tag 03H0 that is not already a clause of the general Tag 03H2, where
`π` is only asserted to be integral, and it is where local Noetherianness of `S` is used.  The
proof is the source's: `f_* 𝒪_X` is coherent by [Stacks, Tag 02O5], so `Γ(S, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)`
is finite for `U ⊆ S` affine open (`Stacks.SteinFactorization.finite_app_of_isProper`); that map
is `Γ(S, U) ⟶ Γ(S', π ⁻¹ᵁ U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)` and the second map is an isomorphism by
[Stacks, Tag 03GY] (`Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_app_toNormalization`), so the first is
finite;  and `π` is affine, being integral.
declarations.statement: public theorem isFinite_fromNormalization : IsFinite f.fromNormalization
declarations.comment:
clause (2): the second factor of the Stein factorization of a proper morphism
over a locally Noetherian base is finite.  Proved from [Stacks, Tag 02O5]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ProperCoherenceWitness.isCoherent_pushforward`), with no carried
hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (1), the geometric connectedness conjunct.**  For `f`
proper onto a locally Noetherian scheme `S`, the first factor `f' : X ⟶ S'` of the Stein
factorization — `S'` the normalization of `S` in `X` and `f' = f.toNormalization` — has
geometrically connected fibres.

Unconditional, at the hypotheses of the tag.  It is the reading of
`Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization_of_isProper`, clause (1) of the
general [Stacks, Tag 03H2], at the stronger hypotheses of this tag;  the local Noetherianness of
`S` is not used.

The properness conjunct of the same clause is
`Stacks.SteinFactorization.isProper_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian` below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_toNormalization (f : X ⟶ S) [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [IsProper f] : GeometricallyConnected f.toNormalization
declarations.comment: clause (1), the geometric connectedness conjunct: the first factor of the Stein factorization of a proper morphism onto a locally Noetherian base has geometrically connected fibres. The properness conjunct of the same clause is isProper_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_fromNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0: the factorization, together with clause (5).**  A proper morphism
`f : X ⟶ S` onto a locally Noetherian scheme factors as `X --f'--> S' --π--> S` *through the
normalization of `S` in `X`* ([Stacks, Tag 035H],
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization`), with `f' = f.toNormalization` and
`π = f.fromNormalization`.  That the intermediate scheme of the factorization is the
normalization of `S` in `X` is clause (5), and since the intermediate scheme produced here *is*
`f.normalization` the whole content of that clause is the displayed equation.

Local Noetherianness is not needed: this is the general factorization of [Stacks, Tag 03H2],
which holds for any proper morphism, specialized to the hypotheses of Tag 03H0.
declarations.statement:
public theorem toNormalization_fromNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian :
    f.toNormalization ≫ f.fromNormalization = f
declarations.comment:
the factorization itself together with clause (5): f factors as
X --f'--> S' --π--> S with S' the normalization of S in X (Stacks 035H), f' = f.toNormalization
and π = f.fromNormalization.  No carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isProper_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (1), properness half.**  The first factor
`f' : X ⟶ S'` of the Stein factorization of a proper morphism onto a locally Noetherian scheme is
proper.  Local Noetherianness is not needed: `f'` is universally closed because `f` is, and
separated and locally of finite type by cancellation along `π`, which is the general
[Stacks, Tag 03H2] specialized to the hypotheses of Tag 03H0.
declarations.statement: public theorem isProper_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian : IsProper f.toNormalization
declarations.comment:
clause (1), the properness half: the first factor of the Stein factorization is
proper.  No carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_c_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (3).**  `f'_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}` for the first factor of the
Stein factorization of a proper morphism onto a locally Noetherian scheme:  the canonical map
`𝒪_{S'} ⟶ f'_* 𝒪_X` is an isomorphism.  Local Noetherianness is not needed; this is
[Stacks, Tag 03H2] clause (3), which holds for any proper morphism, specialized to the hypotheses
of Tag 03H0.
declarations.statement: public theorem isIso_c_toNormalization_of_isLocallyNoetherian : IsIso f.toNormalization.c
declarations.comment:
clause (3): f'_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}, i.e. the canonical map 𝒪_{S'} ⟶ f'_* 𝒪_X is an
isomorphism.  No carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (4).**  The intermediate scheme `S'` of the Stein
factorization of a proper morphism onto a locally Noetherian scheme is the relative spectrum
`Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, as a scheme over `S`.  Being an isomorphism in `CategoryTheory.Over S` is what
makes this an identification of *factorizations*:  it says that `π` is carried to the structure
morphism of the relative spectrum.  Local Noetherianness is not needed; this is
[Stacks, Tag 03H2] clause (4) specialized to the hypotheses of Tag 03H0.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_of_isLocallyNoetherian :
    Over.mk f.fromNormalization ≅ Over.mk (pushforwardSpectrum f).toBase
declarations.comment:
clause (4): S' = Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X), as an isomorphism in Over S, so that π is
carried to the structure morphism of the relative spectrum.  No carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_left_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0, clause (4), continued.**  The identification of clause (4) carries
the first factor `f'` to the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 01LY];  this
is what makes clause (4) an identification of the factorization `f = f' ≫ π` with the
factorization of `f` through its relative spectrum.
declarations.comment:
clause (4), continued: the identification of clause (4) carries f' to the canonical
morphism X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X) of Stacks 01LY.  No carried hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.exists_isSteinFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H0 (Stein factorization, Noetherian case).**  Let `S` be a locally
Noetherian scheme and let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper.  Then `f` factors as `X --f'--> S' --π--> S`
with all five properties of the tag:  `f'` proper with geometrically connected fibres, `π`
finite, `f'_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}`, `S' = Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, and `S'` the normalization of `S` in `X`.

The witnesses are the ones the source names:  `S'` is the normalization of `S` in `X`, `f'` is
`f.toNormalization` and `π` is `f.fromNormalization`.

Unconditional.  Each of the five clauses is a theorem of its own above;  the last of them to be
proved was the connectedness conjunct of clause (1),
`Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization`, which rests on
[Stacks, Tag 0G7X] at a locally Noetherian base and through it on the theorem on formal
functions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isSteinFactorization
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsProper f] :
    ∃ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (f' : X ⟶ S') (π : S' ⟶ S), Nonempty (IsSteinFactorization f f' π)

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ S`
factors as `f = f' ≫ π`, where `S'` is the normalization of `S` in `X`, where `f'` is the
canonical map to `S'` and where `π` is the structure morphism of `S'`.

A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this also supplies the factorization
of [Stacks Project, Tag 03H2].
declarations.statement:
public theorem toNormalization_fromNormalization :
    f.toNormalization ≫ f.fromNormalization = f

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIntegralHom_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03GY.**  The second map of the factorization, the structure morphism
of the normalization of `S` in `X`, is integral.

A proper morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this also supplies the integrality of
the second factor in [Stacks Project, Tag 03H2].
declarations.statement: public theorem isIntegralHom_fromNormalization : IsIntegralHom f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H2, clause (1), the geometric connectedness conjunct.**  For `f`
proper onto an arbitrary scheme `S`, the first factor `f' : X ⟶ S'` of the Stein factorization —
`S'` the normalization of `S` in `X` and `f' = f.toNormalization` — has geometrically connected
fibres.

Unconditional, at the hypotheses of the tag:  nothing is assumed of `S`.  The two inputs are the
reduction above, which is the source's — [Stacks, Tag 03GZ] together with degree-zero flat base
change and `f'_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}` — and [Stacks, Tag 0G7X] for the base changes of `f'` to étale
neighbourhoods of `S'`, which is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Fibres.extendsOverNeighbourhood_of_isProper`.

The same statement covers the connectedness conjunct of clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 03H0], whose
hypotheses are strictly stronger;
`Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization` in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.MoreMorphisms.SteinFactorization.Noetherian` is that reading of it.
The properness conjunct of clause (1) is `Stacks.SteinFactorization.isProper_toNormalization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_toNormalization_of_isProper :
    GeometricallyConnected f.toNormalization
declarations.comment: clause (1), the geometric connectedness conjunct: the first factor of the Stein factorization of a proper morphism has geometrically connected fibres, over an arbitrary base. The properness conjunct of the same clause is isProper_toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isProper_toNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H2.**  The first map of the factorization of a proper morphism is
proper.  It is universally closed because `f` is, separated and locally of finite type by
cancellation along the second map.
declarations.statement: public theorem isProper_toNormalization : IsProper f.toNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H2 (relative_spectrum).**  Clause (4) of the factorization of a
proper morphism `f : X ⟶ S`: the intermediate scheme `S'` of the factorization is, as a scheme
over `S`, the relative spectrum `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of the pushed-forward structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_of_isProper :
    Over.mk f.fromNormalization ≅ Over.mk (pushforwardSpectrum f).toBase

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.toNormalization_overIsoPushforwardSpectrum_hom_left_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H2 (relative_spectrum).**  Under the identification of the
intermediate scheme of the factorization of a proper morphism with `Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)`, the first
factor `f' : X ⟶ S'` becomes the canonical morphism `X ⟶ Spec_S(f_* 𝒪_X)` of
[Stacks, Tag 01LY].

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_c_toNormalization_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03H2.**  Clause (3) of the factorization of a proper morphism
`f : X ⟶ S`: the pushforward of the structure sheaf of `X` along the first map
`f' : X ⟶ f.normalization` is the structure sheaf of `f.normalization`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_c_toNormalization_of_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] :
    IsIso f.toNormalization.c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_pointsULift_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03H4** for presheaves with values in a universe `max w u` independent of the
universe `u` of the schemes: a point of one middle term of a cartesian square and a point of
the other with the same image in the base are the images of a common point of the fibre
product. This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_of_isPullbackULift` with the two
middle terms in the order of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_points_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pointsULift_of_isPullback
    {W X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)}
    {p : W ⟶ X} {q : W ⟶ Z} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Z ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q f g)
    (a : pointsULift.{w} B S hS X) (b : pointsULift.{w} B S hS Z)
    (hab : pointsMapULift B S hS X f a = pointsMapULift B S hS Z g b) :
    ∃ v : pointsULift.{w} B S hS W,
      pointsMapULift B S hS W p v = a ∧ pointsMapULift B S hS W q v = b
declarations.comment: for a value universe independent of the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_points_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The comparison map from the points of a fibre product of presheaves to the fibre product
of the point sets is surjective: a point of `X` and a point of `Z` with the same image in `Y`
are the images of a common point of a presheaf `W` sitting in a cartesian square over them.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_points_of_isPullback {p : W ⟶ X} {q : W ⟶ Z} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Z ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q f g) (a : points B S hS X) (b : points B S hS Z)
    (hab : pointsMap B S hS X f a = pointsMap B S hS Z g b) :
    ∃ w : points B S hS W,
      pointsMap B S hS W p w = a ∧ pointsMap B S hS W q w = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_of_isPullback_presheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03H4.** Compatible points of the two middle terms of a cartesian square of
presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` lift to a point of its upper left corner.

This is surjectivity of `|Z ×_Y X| → |Z| ×_{|Y|} |X|`, stated elementwise for an arbitrary
cartesian square of presheaves. The companion statement for a cartesian square in the category
of algebraic spaces is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_point_of_isPullback_presheaf
    {W Z X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (z : points B S hS Z) (x : points B S hS X)
    (h : pointsMap B S hS Z g z = pointsMap B S hS X f x) :
    ∃ w : points B S hS W,
      pointsMap B S hS W p w = z ∧ pointsMap B S hS W q w = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S`, a point of `Z` and a
point of `X` with the same image in `Y` are the two images of a point of `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_point_of_isPullback (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {W Z X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (z : points B S hS Z.1) (x : points B S hS X.1)
    (h : pointsMap B S hS Z.1 g.hom z = pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) :
    ∃ w : points B S hS W.1,
      pointsMap B S hS W.1 p.hom w = z ∧ pointsMap B S hS W.1 q.hom w = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafSurjective_iff_isSurjective_yoneda
declarations.doc:
A morphism from a scheme over `S` to an algebraic space over `S` is surjective, in the sense
that every represented base change of it is a surjective morphism of schemes, if and only if the
induced map on points is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafSurjective_iff_isSurjective_yoneda (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ↔ IsSurjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_chart_of_isQuasiCompactSpaceULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03H6**, the forward implication, for a presheaf with values in a universe
`max w u` independent of the universe `u` of the schemes: a quasi-compact algebraic space over
`S` admits a surjective étale chart whose source is an object of the site with *affine*
underlying scheme, not merely a quasi-compact one.

The presheaf is isomorphic to the universe lift of a presheaf of `Type u`, which is a
quasi-compact algebraic space; Tag 03H6 supplies an affine surjective étale chart of it, and
the universe lift of that chart composed with the isomorphism is the required one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_chart_of_isQuasiCompactSpaceULift
    {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{w} B S hS F) (h : IsQuasiCompactSpaceULift.{w} B S hS F) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : (uliftYoneda.{w}).obj U ⟶ F),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative (uliftYoneda.{w}) a ∧
      IsEtaleULift.{w} B S hS a
declarations.comment: the affine chart of a quasi-compact algebraic space, in a value universe independent of the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompactSpace_iff_exists_affine_etale_surjective_cover
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact algebraic space has an affine, étale, surjective cover, and any algebraic
space with such a cover is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactSpace_iff_exists_affine_etale_surjective_cover
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (_hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS F ↔
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
          (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
            (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ∧
          IsEtale B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChart_singleton_covering
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be an algebraic space étale over `X`. There is an étale scheme chart `V` of `X`
and a morphism `V → U` of the spaces-étale site which is étale and surjective, and the
one-element family `{V → U}` is a covering family of the spaces-étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleChart_singleton_covering (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) :
    ∃ (V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U),
      IsEtale B S hS ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).map f).hom ∧
      IsSurjective B S hS ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).map f).hom ∧
      SpacesEtale.IsCovering B S hS X ⟨U, PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{u + 1} f⟩
declarations.comment: the one-element covering by a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_etaleChart_isPullback_self
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be an algebraic space étale over `X`, let `V` be an étale scheme chart of `X` and
let `f : V → U` be a morphism of the spaces-étale site. Then there is an étale scheme chart `W`
of `X` and a pair of morphisms `p, q : W → V` of the *small* étale site whose images under the
comparison functor exhibit `W` as the fibre product `V ×_U V` in the spaces-étale site.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleChart_isPullback_self (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U) :
    ∃ (W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (p q : W ⟶ V),
      IsPullback ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map p)
        ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map q) f f
declarations.comment: the fibre product is a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_fork_of_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `P` be a sheaf on the spaces-étale site of
`X`, and write `F = (comparisonFunctor).op ⋙ P` for its restriction to the small étale site of
`X`. Then for every algebraic space `U` étale over `X` there are an étale scheme chart `V` of
`X`, a surjective étale morphism `f : V → U` of the spaces-étale site whose one-element family
is a covering, and a second étale scheme chart `W` with morphisms `p, q : W → V` of the small
étale site exhibiting `W` as `V ×_U V`, such that

`P(U) → F(V) ⇉ F(W)`

is an equalizer diagram, the two parallel arrows being restriction along `p` and along `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_fork_of_isSheaf (P : (SpacesEtale B S hS X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A)
    (hP : Presheaf.IsSheaf (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X) P) (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) :
    ∃ (V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U)
      (W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (p q : W ⟶ V)
      (_ : IsPullback ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map p)
        ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map q) f f)
      (w : P.map f.op ≫ ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).op ⋙ P).map p.op =
        P.map f.op ≫
          ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).op ⋙ P).map q.op),
      IsEtale B S hS ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).map f).hom ∧
      IsSurjective B S hS ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS X).map f).hom ∧
      SpacesEtale.IsCovering B S hS X ⟨U, PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{u + 1} f⟩ ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι (P.map f.op) w))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_scheme_chart_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03H7.** Every algebraic space étale over `X` is covered, in the spaces-étale site
of `X`, by a single étale *scheme* chart of `X`, namely a chosen atlas of it composed with its
structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_chart_cover (U : SpacesEtale B S hS X) :
    ∃ (V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U),
      Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton f) ∈ SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X U
declarations.comment: a scheme chart covering the étale space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_smallEtaleDirectImageChartEqualizerEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03H7 for the direct image on the small étale sites.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of algebraic spaces, let `P` be a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X`, and let `V` be
an étale scheme chart of `Y`.  Then there are étale scheme charts `W`, `W'` of `X` and two
morphisms `a, b : W' ⟶ W` such that

`(f_{small,*}P)(V) ⟶ P(W) ⇉ P(W')`

is an equalizer: the sections of the direct image over `V` are in bijection with the sections of
`P` over `W` on which restriction along `a` and restriction along `b` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smallEtaleDirectImageChartEqualizerEquiv (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (P : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type u)) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) :
    ∃ (W W' : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) (a b : W' ⟶ W),
      Nonempty (((smallEtaleDirectImage B S hS f).obj P).obj.obj (op V) ≃
        {y : P.obj.obj (op W) // P.obj.map a.op y = P.obj.map b.op y})
declarations.comment: the equalizer diagram, for the direct image on the small etale sites: the sections of f_{small,*}P over an etale scheme chart V of Y are the equalizer of the sections of P over an etale scheme chart W covering X x_Y V and over a chart W' presenting the self-fibre product of W over X x_Y V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_scheme_chart_self_intersection
declarations.doc:
The self-intersection of a scheme chart over an object of the spaces-étale site of `X` is
again an étale scheme chart of `X`, with its canonical pullback projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_scheme_chart_self_intersection {U : SpacesEtale B S hS X}
    {V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U) :
    ∃ (W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
      (p q : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj W ⟶ (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V),
      IsPullback p q f f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sections_equalizer_of_scheme_chart
declarations.doc:
The sections of a sheaf on the spaces-étale site of `X` over an object `U` are the equalizer
of the two restriction maps from a scheme chart covering `U` to the scheme self-intersection of
that chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem sections_equalizer_of_scheme_chart {U : SpacesEtale B S hS X}
    {V W : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V ⟶ U)
    (p q : (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj W ⟶ (comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj V)
    (hcover : Sieve.generate (Presieve.singleton f) ∈ SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X U)
    (hpullback : IsPullback p q f f)
    (G : Sheaf (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS X) (Type w)) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι (G.obj.map f.op) (f := G.obj.map p.op) (g := G.obj.map q.op)
      (by simp [← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, hpullback.w])))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_quasiCompact_iff_isQuasiCompact
registrations.comment: agreement with the notion for representable morphisms

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
registrations.comment:
a morphism from a quasi-compact space to a quasi-separated one is
  quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_quasiCompact_iff_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
For a representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` the two readings of
quasi-compactness agree: every represented base change of it is a quasi-compact morphism of
schemes exactly when every base change of it along a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic
space has quasi-compact source.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_quasiCompact_iff_isQuasiCompact {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {f : F ⟶ G} (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ↔
      IsQuasiCompact B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_presheaf_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
A morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` which is representable and
quasi-compact after every representable base change is quasi-compact: every base change of it
along a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic space has quasi-compact source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_of_presheaf_quasiCompact
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HE.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *quasi-compact* when every
base change of it along a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic space has quasi-compact
source.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiCompact (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
Quasi-compactness of a morphism of algebraic spaces is stable under base change: in a
cartesian square, the base change `b` of a quasi-compact `p` is quasi-compact.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompact.comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of a pair of quasi-compact morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is
quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompact.comp
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hg : IsQuasiCompact B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedMorphism
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *closed* when the map it induces on points is a
closed map for the topology detected by scheme-valued points.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClosedMorphism (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.UniversallyClosed
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *universally closed* when its base change along
every morphism to its target from an algebraic space over `S` is closed.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversallyClosed (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separationProperties_of_relativelyRepresentable
registrations.comment: agreement with the notions for representable morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyRepresentable_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, part (1).** The relative diagonal of a morphism out of an algebraic space
over `S` is relatively representable. The target need not be an algebraic space: the relative
diagonal is a base change of the absolute diagonal of the source, which is representable by
the second defining clause of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_pullbackDiagonal (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_locallyOfFiniteType_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, part (2).** The relative diagonal of a morphism out of an algebraic space
over `S` is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_locallyOfFiniteType_pullbackDiagonal (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_monomorphisms_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, part (3).** Every represented base change of the relative diagonal of a
morphism out of an algebraic space over `S` is a monomorphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_monomorphisms_pullbackDiagonal (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_isSeparated_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, part (4).** The relative diagonal of a morphism out of an algebraic space
over `S` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_isSeparated_pullbackDiagonal (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@IsSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presheaf_locallyQuasiFinite_pullbackDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, part (5).** The relative diagonal of a morphism out of an algebraic space
over `S` is locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheaf_locallyQuasiFinite_pullbackDiagonal (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      ((@LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊓
        (@LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.monomorphisms_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, representability and the monomorphism condition.** The relative diagonal of
a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is representable and a monomorphism after every
represented base change.

It is the base change of the absolute diagonal of the source along `X ×_Y X ⟶ X ⨯ X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pullbackDiagonal_diag`), and for the absolute diagonal this is
part (2) of [Stacks Project, Tag 02X4]. Algebraicity of the target is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem monomorphisms_diagonal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyOfFiniteType_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, local finite type.** Every represented base change of the relative diagonal
of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite
type. This is part (1) of [Stacks Project, Tag 02X4] transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pullbackDiagonal_diag`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFiniteType_diagonal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, separatedness.** Every represented base change of the relative diagonal of a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a separated morphism of schemes. This is part (3) of
[Stacks Project, Tag 02X4] transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pullbackDiagonal_diag`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_diagonal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.locallyQuasiFinite_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HK, local quasi-finiteness.** Every represented base change of the relative
diagonal of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a morphism of schemes which is locally
of finite type and locally quasi-finite. This is part (4) of [Stacks Project, Tag 02X4]
transported along `AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_pullbackDiagonal_diag`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyQuasiFinite_diagonal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      ((@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊓
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (pullback.diagonal f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HL, part (1).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *separated* when
its relative diagonal is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSeparated (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallySeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HL, part (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *locally
separated* when its relative diagonal is an immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallySeparated (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HL, part (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
*quasi-separated* when its relative diagonal is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiSeparated (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: StacksLemmaCompactSubsetSpectral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HO**. The union of a finite collection of nowhere dense subsets of a topological
space is nowhere dense, stated for a binary union, for a `Finset`-indexed family, and for the
union of a `Set.Finite` family of subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem StacksLemmaCompactSubsetSpectral :
    (∀ {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {A B : Set X},
        IsNowhereDense A → IsNowhereDense B → IsNowhereDense (A ∪ B)) ∧
    (∀ {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (A : ι → Set X),
        (∀ i ∈ s, IsNowhereDense (A i)) → IsNowhereDense (⋃ i ∈ s, A i)) ∧
    (∀ {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {S : Set (Set X)},
        S.Finite → (∀ A ∈ S, IsNowhereDense A) → IsNowhereDense (⋃₀ S))

declarations.name: nowhere_dense_local
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HP.** Nowhere density is local on open covers: if `{U i}` is an open cover of `X`
and `T ∩ U i` (encoded as the preimage of `T` under the inclusion `U i → X`) is nowhere dense in
the subspace `U i` for every `i`, then `T` is nowhere dense in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nowhere_dense_local
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {ι : Type*} (U : ι → Set X)
    (hU_open : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hU_cover : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ)
    (T : Set X)
    (hT_local : ∀ i, IsNowhereDense ((Subtype.val : U i → X) ⁻¹' T)) :
    IsNowhereDense T

declarations.name: isClosedNowhereDense_preimage_of_isOpenMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HR** (part 1). If `f : X → Y` is a continuous open map and `T ⊆ Y` is closed
nowhere dense, then `f⁻¹(T)` is closed nowhere dense in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedNowhereDense_preimage_of_isOpenMap
    (f : X → Y) (hfc : Continuous f) (hfo : IsOpenMap f)
    (T : Set Y) (hT_closed : IsClosed T) (hT : IsNowhereDense T) :
    IsClosed (f ⁻¹' T) ∧ IsNowhereDense (f ⁻¹' T)

declarations.name: isClosedNowhereDense_preimage_iff_of_surjective_isOpenMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HR** (part 2). If `f : X → Y` is a surjective continuous open map, then `T ⊆ Y` is
closed nowhere dense if and only if `f⁻¹(T)` is closed nowhere dense in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedNowhereDense_preimage_iff_of_surjective_isOpenMap
    (f : X → Y) (hfc : Continuous f) (hfo : IsOpenMap f) (hfs : Function.Surjective f)
    (T : Set Y) :
    (IsClosed T ∧ IsNowhereDense T) ↔
      (IsClosed (f ⁻¹' T) ∧ IsNowhereDense (f ⁻¹' T))

declarations.name: Polynomial.Monic.exists_finite_free_faithfullyFlat_syntomic_map_eq_prod_X_sub_C
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HS.** Let `A` be a ring and let `P ∈ A[x]` be monic. There is a finite free,
faithfully flat, syntomic extension `A ⊂ A'` and elements `β_1, …, β_n ∈ A'`, `n = deg P`, with
`P = ∏ (x - β_i)` in `A'[x]`. The inclusion `A ⊂ A'` is the faithful flatness: it gives
`FaithfulSMul A A'`, hence `algebraMap A A'` injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Polynomial.Monic.exists_finite_free_faithfullyFlat_syntomic_map_eq_prod_X_sub_C
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {P : A[X]} (hP : P.Monic) :
    ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : Algebra A A') (_ : Module.Finite A A')
      (_ : Module.Free A A') (_ : Module.FaithfullyFlat A A') (_ : Algebra.Syntomic A A')
      (β : Fin P.natDegree → A'), P.map (algebraMap A A') = ∏ i, (X - C (β i))
declarations.comment:
The source's finite free faithfully flat *extension* `A ⊂ A'`: the injectivity of
`algebraMap A A'` is not a conjunct, being `FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective` applied to
`Module.FaithfullyFlat A A'`. The splitting is the explicit product over `Fin P.natDegree`, which
names the roots the consumers use and is stronger than `Polynomial.Splits`. Unlike the Mathlib
sibling `Polynomial.Monic.exists_splits_map`, no `Nontrivial A` is assumed and the extension is
also faithfully flat and syntomic (Definition 00SL). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.OverShriek.isIso_ofRestricted_unit
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site, let `U` be an object of `C` whose representable presheaf `h_U` is a sheaf
(for instance because the topology is subcanonical), and let `G` be a sheaf of sets on `C/U`. Let
`L` be a left adjoint of the restriction functor `j_U^{-1} = J.overPullback : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh(C/U)`,
i.e. let `L` be `j_{U!}`. Then the canonical map from the coproduct presheaf
`V ↦ ∐_{φ : V ⟶ U} G(V →φ U)` to the presheaf underlying `j_{U!}G`, which over `V` sends a pair
`(φ, s)` to the section `s` of `j_{U!}G`, is an isomorphism:
`j_{U!}G(V) = ∐_{φ ∈ Hom_C(V, U)} G(V →φ U)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_ofRestricted_unit {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (U : C) (hU : Presieve.IsSheaf J (yoneda.obj U))
    {L : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v) ⥤ Sheaf J (Type v)} (adj : L ⊣ J.overPullback (Type v) U)
    (G : Sheaf (J.over U) (Type v)) :
    IsIso (ofRestricted G.obj (F := (L.obj G).obj) (adj.unit.app G).hom)
declarations.comment: j_{U!}G(V) = ∐_{φ : V ⟶ U} G(V →φ U) for a subcanonical topology.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.overShriekSheafifyYonedaIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03HU.** For an object `X/U` of the localized site `C/U`, the lower shriek
`j_{U!} = (Over.forget U).sheafPullback` of the sheaf `h_{X/U}^#` associated to the presheaf on
`C/U` represented by `X/U` is the sheaf `h_X^#` associated to the presheaf on `C` represented by
the underlying object `X = j_U(X/U)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def overShriekSheafifyYonedaIso (X : Over U) :
    ((Over.forget U).sheafPullback (Type v) (J.over U) J).obj
        ((presheafToSheaf (J.over U) (Type v)).obj (yoneda.obj X)) ≅
      (presheafToSheaf J (Type v)).obj (yoneda.obj X.left)

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.exists_finiteLocallyFree_cover_closedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03HW.** After a surjective finite locally free base change,
a finite morphism to an affine scheme embeds into a finite locally free scheme covered
set-theoretically by finitely many closed sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteLocallyFree_cover_closedImmersion
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] [IsAffine X] :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : X' ⟶ X),
      Surjective g ∧ IsFiniteLocallyFree g ∧
      Surjective (pullback.fst f g) ∧
      IsFiniteLocallyFree (pullback.fst f g) ∧
      ∃ (Z' : Scheme.{u}) (p : Z' ⟶ X')
        (i : pullback f g ⟶ Z'),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧
        i ≫ p = pullback.snd f g ∧
        IsFiniteLocallyFree p ∧
        ∃ (m : ℕ) (s : Fin m → (X' ⟶ Z')),
          (∀ j, IsClosedImmersion (s j) ∧ s j ≫ p = 𝟙 X') ∧
          (∀ z : Z', ∃ j : Fin m, ∃ x : X', (s j).base x = z)

declarations.name: Stacks.Morphisms.isNowhereDense_image_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03HX.** The image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a finite
morphism of schemes is nowhere dense.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNowhereDense_image_of_isFinite {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f]
    {T : Set Y} (hT_closed : IsClosed T) (hT : IsNowhereDense T) :
    IsNowhereDense (f.base '' T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coordinatePoint_injective
declarations.doc:
Distinct coordinate projections induce distinct points of the spectrum of a countable product
of copies of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem coordinatePoint_injective (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    Function.Injective fun n : ℕ ↦ (coordinate k n).base (default : base k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of `∏ n : ℕ, 𝔽₂` with a closed, non-open point doubled, together with its
canonical projection and chart identifications.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def doubledPoint : DoubledPoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_genericPoint
declarations.doc: The doubled point is the generic point of an irreducible component of the spectrum.
declarations.statement:
theorem doubledPoint_genericPoint :
    doubledPoint.point ∈ genericPoints (space (ZMod 2))
declarations.comment: generic point of an irreducible component

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_quasiCompact
declarations.doc: The canonical projection is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: theorem doubledPoint_quasiCompact : QuasiCompact doubledPoint.projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_locallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc: The canonical projection is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement: theorem doubledPoint_locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType doubledPoint.projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_finiteFibres
declarations.doc: Every fibre of the canonical projection is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem doubledPoint_finiteFibres (y : space (ZMod 2)) :
    (doubledPoint.projection ⁻¹' {y}).Finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_noAffinePreimage
declarations.doc: The inverse image of every open neighbourhood of the doubled point is non-affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem doubledPoint_noAffinePreimage (U : (space (ZMod 2)).Opens)
    (hU : doubledPoint.point ∈ U) :
    ¬ IsAffine ((doubledPoint.projection ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)
declarations.comment: failure of conditions (3) and (4) of Tag 02NW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_notQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc: The canonical projection is not quasi-separated.
declarations.statement: theorem doubledPoint_notQuasiSeparated : ¬ QuasiSeparated doubledPoint.projection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_noAffineOpenContainingFibre
declarations.doc:
There is no affine open neighbourhood `V` of the doubled point together with an affine open
`U` over `V` containing the whole fibre over the doubled point such that the restriction
`U ⟶ V` of the canonical projection is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem doubledPoint_noAffineOpenContainingFibre :
    ¬ ∃ (V : (space (ZMod 2)).affineOpens) (U : doubledPoint.source.affineOpens)
      (hUV : U.1 ≤ doubledPoint.projection ⁻¹ᵁ V.1),
        doubledPoint.point ∈ V.1 ∧
        doubledPoint.projection ⁻¹' {doubledPoint.point} ⊆ U.1 ∧
        IsFinite (doubledPoint.projection.resLE V.1 U.1 hUV)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.doubledPoint_noFiniteRestriction
declarations.doc:
There is no affine open neighbourhood of the doubled point above which the canonical
projection is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem doubledPoint_noFiniteRestriction :
    ¬ ∃ V : (space (ZMod 2)).affineOpens, doubledPoint.point ∈ V.1 ∧
      IsFinite (doubledPoint.projection ∣_ V.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_isFinite_of_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03I1.** A quasi-finite morphism of schemes is finite over a dense open
subscheme of its target. This is also the statement of [Stacks Project, Tag 03HZ], the remark
offering it as an alternative to [Stacks Project, Tag 02NW] and deferring its proof to here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_isFinite_of_quasiFinite {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ U)
declarations.comment:
the whole content of the remark: the alternative to Tag 02NW that it
states, namely that a quasi-finite morphism is finite over a dense open of the target, whose proof
the remark defers to Tag 03I1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**A descent datum relative to an fpqc covering whose components are closed immersions is
effective.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be an fpqc covering and let `D` be a descent
datum relative to it whose structure morphism over each `X i` is a closed immersion. Then `D` is
isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.

A closed immersion is affine, so this is effective descent for affine morphisms along an fpqc
covering, Stacks 0245, at a smaller class of morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_isClosedImmersion {I : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S) (D : DescentData f)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_dense_open_isFinite_of_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03I1.** A quasi-finite morphism of schemes is finite over a dense open
subscheme of its target. This is also the statement of [Stacks Project, Tag 03HZ], the remark
offering it as an alternative to [Stacks Project, Tag 02NW] and deferring its proof to here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dense_open_isFinite_of_quasiFinite {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, Dense (U : Set X) ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_and_presheaf_of_surjectiveEtaleChart
declarations.doc:
