declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separationAxioms_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KR.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in the big fppf site `B` and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`. Then:

1. if `f ≫ g` is separated, so is `f`;
2. if `f ≫ g` is locally separated, so is `f`; and
3. if `f ≫ g` is quasi-separated, so is `f`.

Each of the three separation axioms is a condition on the relative diagonal which is stable
under base change, and the relative diagonal of `f` is a base change of that of `f ≫ g` along
the comparison map `X ×_Y X ⟶ X ×_Z X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem separationAxioms_of_comp (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (IsSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g) → IsSeparated B S hS f) ∧
      (IsLocallySeparated B S hS (f ≫ g) → IsLocallySeparated B S hS f) ∧
      (IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (f ≫ g) → IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
If a composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is quasi-compact and its second
factor is quasi-separated, then its first factor is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hH : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS H) (hgf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hg : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterion_uniqueness_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KU.** A separated morphism of algebraic spaces satisfies the uniqueness part
of the valuative criterion.

Two lifts of a valuative square assemble into a morphism `Spec R ⟶ X ×_Y X`; the base change
of the relative diagonal along it is a closed immersion of schemes which is surjective on
global sections, because the generic point of `Spec R` lifts through it, hence an
isomorphism. The two lifts therefore agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterion_uniqueness_of_isSeparated (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsSeparated B S hS f) : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_valuativeCriterion_uniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KV.** A quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which satisfies
the uniqueness part of the valuative criterion is separated.

Quasi-separatedness is quasi-compactness of the relative diagonal, and the diagonal satisfies
the existence part of the criterion, so by Stacks 03KA it is universally closed. Being also
separated, locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite (Stacks 03HK), every represented
base change of it is a proper locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes, hence finite; being in
addition a monomorphism, it is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_valuativeCriterion_uniqueness
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hu : ValuativeCriterion.Uniqueness f) :
    IsSeparated B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_of_etale_over_field
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KX.** An algebraic space over `S` admitting an étale morphism to an object of the
big fppf site over `S` whose underlying scheme is the spectrum of a field is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_of_etale_over_field
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (eV : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V ≅ Spec (.of k))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (f : F ⟶ yoneda.obj V) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f) :
    F.IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.separationProperties_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KY.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a representable morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`.  Then:

1. `f` is locally separated; and
2. `f` is separated in the sense of Stacks 03HL if and only if it is separated in the sense
   of Stacks 03HA, that is, if and only if every represented base change of `f` is a
   separated morphism of schemes, and likewise for quasi-separatedness.

In particular, a morphism `m` of schemes over `S` is (quasi-)separated in the sense of
Stacks 03HL, as the morphism of algebraic spaces `yoneda.map m`, if and only if it is
(quasi-)separated as a morphism of schemes.

Part (1) holds because the relative diagonal of a morphism of schemes is an immersion, by
Stacks 01KJ, and local separatedness of a morphism with algebraic source is tested on its
represented base changes, by Stacks 03KM, each of which is the Yoneda image of a morphism of
the site.  Part (2) is the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 03KM for
separatedness and for quasi-separatedness, taken together with the fact that separatedness
and quasi-separatedness of the Yoneda image of a morphism of the site are those properties of
the underlying morphism of schemes; that last fact, stated for every morphism of the site, is
also the concluding assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem separationProperties_of_relativelyRepresentable
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    IsLocallySeparated B S hS f ∧
      (IsSeparated B S hS f ↔
          (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
            (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) ∧
      (IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f ↔
          (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
            (@_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) ∧
      ∀ (a b : BigFppfOver B S hS) (m : a ⟶ b),
        (IsSeparated B S hS (yoneda.map m) ↔
            _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map m)) ∧
          (IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (yoneda.map m) ↔
            _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map m))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KZ, property `(β)` for an algebraic space.** This is property `(β)` of
Stacks 03JX: every point of `F` satisfies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 03JU, taken
here in the form of condition (1), finiteness of one relation fibre in some étale chart.
declarations.statement: abbrev HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint : Prop
declarations.comment: property beta for an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasPropertyBeta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KZ, property `(β)` for a morphism.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
has property `(β)` when every base change of it along a morphism from a representable
presheaf into its target has property `(β)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev HasPropertyBeta (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KZ, decent morphism.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *decent*
when every base change of it along a morphism from a representable presheaf into its target
is a decent algebraic space.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDecent (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsReasonable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KZ, reasonable morphism.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
*reasonable* when every base change of it along a morphism from a representable presheaf
into its target is a reasonable algebraic space.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsReasonable (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsVeryReasonable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03KZ, very reasonable morphism.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
*very reasonable* when every base change of it along a morphism from a representable
presheaf into its target is a very reasonable algebraic space.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsVeryReasonable (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPropertyBeta_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L0, property `(β)`.** Property `(β)` of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is preserved by arbitrary base change: a base change of the base change of `f : X ⟶ Y` along
`g : Y' ⟶ Y` is a base change of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyBeta_baseChange (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hf : HasPropertyBeta B S hS f) : HasPropertyBeta B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L0, decent.** Decency of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is preserved
by arbitrary base change: a base change of the base change of `f : X ⟶ Y` along `g : Y' ⟶ Y`
is a base change of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_baseChange (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (hf : IsDecent B S hS f) :
    IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonable_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L0, reasonable.** Reasonableness of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
preserved by arbitrary base change: a base change of the base change of `f : X ⟶ Y` along
`g : Y' ⟶ Y` is a base change of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReasonable_baseChange (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (hf : IsReasonable B S hS f) :
    IsReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPropertyBeta_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L1, property `(β)`.** Property `(β)` of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
is preserved by composition.

The base change of `f ≫ g` along `k : T ⟶ Z` is the base change of `f` along the projection
`T ×_Z Y ⟶ Y`, viewed over `T ×_Z Y`; that projection has property `(β)` by Stacks 03L0 and
`T ×_Z Y` has it because `g` does, so Stacks 0ABY applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyBeta_comp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : HasPropertyBeta B S hS f) (hg : HasPropertyBeta B S hS g) :
    HasPropertyBeta B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L1, decent.** Decency of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is preserved by
composition.

The base change of `f ≫ g` along `k : T ⟶ Z` is the base change of `f` along the projection
`T ×_Z Y ⟶ Y`, viewed over `T ×_Z Y`; that projection is decent by Stacks 03L0 and `T ×_Z Y`
is decent because `g` is, so Stacks 0ABY applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_comp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsDecent B S hS f) (hg : IsDecent B S hS g) :
    IsDecent B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonable_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L1, reasonable.** Reasonableness of a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is
preserved by composition.

The base change of `f ≫ g` along `k : T ⟶ Z` is the base change of `f` along the projection
`T ×_Z Y ⟶ Y`, viewed over `T ×_Z Y`; that projection is reasonable by Stacks 03L0 and
`T ×_Z Y` is reasonable because `g` is, so Stacks 0ABY applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReasonable_comp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsReasonable B S hS f) (hg : IsReasonable B S hS g) :
    IsReasonable B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint_of_surjective_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L2, property `(β)`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact étale morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is surjective on points. If `X` has property `(β)` of
Stacks 03JX — every point has a field-valued representative with a finite relation fibre —
then so does `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint_of_surjective_isEtale
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hq : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (he : IsEtale B S hS f) (hs : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS X f))
    (hβ : HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint B S hS X) :
    HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint B S hS Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_surjective_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L2, reasonable.** Let `f` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` which is surjective on points. If its source is reasonable, then so is its target.

An affine étale chart of the target is dominated, after base change along `f`, by an affine
étale chart of the source, and the bound reasonableness of the source gives the latter bounds
the degrees of the fibres of the former. Étaleness of `f`, which Stacks 03L2 also assumes, is
not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReasonableSpace_of_surjective_isQuasiCompact
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS X f))
    (hXr : IsReasonableSpace B S hS X) :
    IsReasonableSpace B S hS Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasQuasiCompactFieldRepresentative_of_isDecentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L2, condition (5) of Stacks 03JV at every point of the target.** Let `f` be a
quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is surjective on points. If the
source is decent, then every point of the target has a quasi-compact field-valued
representative.

A point of the target is the image of a point of the source, which decency of the source
presents by a quasi-compact morphism from the spectrum of a field; composing it with `f` again
gives a quasi-compact morphism, and it presents the chosen point of the target.

Decency of the target asks for a representative which is in addition a monomorphism, and
obtaining one from this is the equivalence of conditions (4) and (5) of Stacks 03JV. Étaleness
of `f`, which Stacks 03L2 also assumes, is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasQuasiCompactFieldRepresentative_of_isDecentSpace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS X f))
    (hXdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (y : points B S hS Y) :
    HasQuasiCompactFieldRepresentative B S hS Y y
declarations.comment: condition (5) of Stacks 03JV at every point of the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_of_surjective_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L2, decent.** Let `f` be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is surjective on points. If its source is decent, then so is its target.

Every point of the target acquires a quasi-compact field-valued representative by pushing one
forward along `f`, and the implication from condition (5) to condition (4) of Stacks 03JV
makes that representative a monomorphism. Étaleness of `f`, which Stacks 03L2 also assumes,
is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentSpace_of_surjective_isQuasiCompact (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS X f))
    (hXdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    IsDecentSpace B S hS Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPropertyBeta_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyBeta_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [HasPropertyBeta B S hS f,
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            HasPropertyBeta B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint B S hS (pullback g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (Yᵢ : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yᵢ ∧
          ∀ i, HasPropertyBeta B S hS (pullback.fst (Yᵢ i).ι f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y), IsSurjective B S hS g ∧
          IsEtale B S hS g ∧ HasPropertyBeta B S hS (pullback.fst g f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isVeryReasonable_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isVeryReasonable_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsVeryReasonable B S hS f,
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsVeryReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsVeryReasonableSpace B S hS (pullback g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (Yᵢ : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yᵢ ∧
          ∀ i, IsVeryReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst (Yᵢ i).ι f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsDecent B S hS f,
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsDecentSpace B S hS (pullback g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (Yᵢ : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yᵢ ∧
          ∀ i, IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst (Yᵢ i).ι f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_tfae_etale
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` the four conditions of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_tfae` are also equivalent to
`(5)` there is a scheme of the site with a surjective étale morphism `V ⟶ Y` such that
`V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_tfae_etale (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsDecent B S hS f,
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsDecentSpace B S hS (pullback g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (Yᵢ : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yᵢ ∧
          ∀ i, IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst (Yᵢ i).ι f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y), IsSurjective B S hS g ∧
          IsEtale B S hS g ∧ IsDecent B S hS (pullback.fst g f)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonable_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isReasonable_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsReasonable B S hS f,
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
        ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
            IsReasonableSpace B S hS (pullback g f),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (Yᵢ : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yᵢ ∧
          ∀ i, IsReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst (Yᵢ i).ι f),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y), IsSurjective B S hS g ∧
          IsEtale B S hS g ∧ IsReasonable B S hS (pullback.fst g f)]

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_of_isReasonable
registrations.comment:
Remark 68.17.10, which states no proposition of its own: its comparative
  sentence, that being reasonable is a bit stronger than being decent, is sharp only as the
  implication `reasonable ⇒ decent` of Stacks 03M5, which is this theorem.

declarations.name: sheafPushforwardCocontinuousCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03L5**, second half. The canonical natural isomorphism between the direct image
functor of the morphism of topoi attached to `u ⋙ v` and the composition of the direct image
functors attached to `u` and to `v`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafPushforwardCocontinuousCompIso (u : C ⥤ D) (v : D ⥤ E)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [v.IsCocontinuous K L] :
    haveI : (u ⋙ v).IsCocontinuous J L := CategoryTheory.isCocontinuous_comp u v J K
    (u ⋙ v).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J L ≅
      u.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) J K ⋙
        v.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u) K L

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.isCocontinuous_comp
registrations.comment: (1), the composition of two cocontinuous site functors is cocontinuous. Mathlib states it for arbitrary, independent object and hom universes; the statement this replaced fixed all three categories to a single universe `u` with `SmallCategory`, and its proof was a call to this declaration.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheaf_isCoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03L6, coherent case.**  The tensor product of two coherent sheaves of
modules on a ringed site is coherent.

Following the source: a coherent sheaf of modules is of finite presentation, so the mixed
finite-presentation/coherence clause applies.  The argument is run at the universe lift of the
ringed site, where the presentation machinery of Stacks 01BW(1) is available, and transported
back along `Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentLift.isCoherentOnSite_liftModule_iff` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoherentLift.tensorLiftIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheaf_isCoherentOnSite (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    [hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite F]
    [hG : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G] :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).obj F).obj G)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheaf_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03L6, finite presentation case.** The tensor product of two sheaves of
modules of finite presentation on a ringed site is of finite presentation.

Following the source: `F` has a finite presentation over each member of a covering family and so
does `G`; the objects admitting an arrow into a member of each family again cover, and over such
an object the two restricted presentations are still finite and their tensor presentation
presents the restriction of `F ⊗ G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheaf_isFinitePresentation
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation F] [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation G] :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).obj F).obj G)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheaf_isCoherent_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03L6, finite presentation against coherence.**  The tensor product of
a sheaf of modules of finite presentation with a coherent sheaf of modules on a ringed site is
coherent.

Following the source: `F` admits a finite presentation over each member of a covering family,
the restriction of `G` to such a member is still coherent, and the tensor product formed on the
slice site is the restriction of the global one by
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorOverIso`; so
`isCoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf_of_presentation` applies on each member, and coherence is local on
the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorSheaf_isCoherent_of_isFinitePresentation
    (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    [X.J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation F]
    [hG : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G] :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.O).obj F).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_affine_finite_support
declarations.doc:
A family is an fpqc covering if and only if
every member is flat and every affine open of the target is the union of the images of
quasi-compact opens in the sources, all but finitely many of which are empty.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_affine_finite_support :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, Flat (f i)) ∧
        (∀ U : T.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
            ∃ V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens,
              ((∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set (X i))) ∧
                ({i | V i ≠ ⊥} : Set I).Finite ∧
                ⋃ i, f i '' (V i : Set (X i)) = (U : Set T))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_exists_affine_open_cover
declarations.doc:
A family is an fpqc covering if and only if its
members are flat and some affine open covering of the target is, member by member, the union of
images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the sources.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_exists_affine_open_cover :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, Flat (f i)) ∧
        ∃ (A : Type u) (U : A → T.Opens),
          ((∀ a, IsAffineOpen (U a)) ∧
            (⋃ a, (U a : Set T)) = Set.univ ∧
            ∀ a, ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (X (i j)).Opens),
              ((∀ j, IsCompact (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∧
                ⋃ j, f (i j) '' (V j : Set (X (i j))) = (U a : Set T))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_pointwise_compact_open_neighborhood
declarations.doc:
If the target is quasi-separated, a family is an
fpqc covering if and only if its members are flat and every point has a neighborhood which is
the union of the images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the sources. The neighborhood
itself is not required to be open.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_pointwise_compact_open_neighborhood
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, Flat (f i)) ∧
        ∀ t : T, ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (X (i j)).Opens),
          ((∀ j, IsCompact (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∧
            (⋃ j, f (i j) '' (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∈ nhds t))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_of_fpqc_locally
declarations.doc:
Being an fpqc covering is local on an fpqc covering of the base. If every
member of a family `f i : X i ⟶ T` is flat and there is an fpqc covering `g j : S j ⟶ T` of the
target such that for every `j` the base-changed family `S j ×[T] X i ⟶ S j` is an fpqc covering
of `S j`, then `f` is an fpqc covering of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma ofArrows_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_of_fpqc_locally
    {J : Type w} {S : J → Scheme.{u}} (g : ∀ j, S j ⟶ T)
    (hflat : ∀ i, Flat (f i))
    (hg : Presieve.ofArrows S g ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T)
    (hbc : ∀ j, Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ pullback (g j) (f i))
      (fun i ↦ pullback.fst (g j) (f i)) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (S j)) :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isStandardFpqcCovering_of_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LA (1).** If `T' ⟶ T` is an isomorphism onto an affine scheme, then the one-member
family `{T' ⟶ T}` is a standard fpqc covering: the source is affine because it is isomorphic to
the affine target, and an isomorphism is flat and surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStandardFpqcCovering_of_isIso {T T' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T] (f : T' ⟶ T)
    [IsIso f] : IsStandardFpqcCovering (fun _ : PUnit.{v + 1} ↦ T') (fun _ ↦ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardFpqcCovering.bind
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LA (2).** If `{T_i ⟶ T}_{i ∈ I}` is a standard fpqc covering and
`{T_ij ⟶ T_i}_{j ∈ J i}` is a standard fpqc covering for every `i`, then the family of composites
`{T_ij ⟶ T}_{⟨i, j⟩ ∈ Σ i, J i}` is a standard fpqc covering.  Its index is the sigma type of the
indices, finite because each of its factors is; its members are composites of flat morphisms,
hence flat; and a point of `T` is hit through some member of the outer family and then through
some member of the inner family above it.  The inner and the outer index types may lie in
different universes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardFpqcCovering.pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LA (3).** If `{T_i ⟶ T}_{i ∈ I}` is a standard fpqc covering and `T' ⟶ T` is a
morphism of affine schemes, then the family of first projections `{T' ×_T T_i ⟶ T'}_{i ∈ I}` is a
standard fpqc covering.  The index is unchanged, flatness is preserved by base change, each fibre
product is affine because it is a fibre product of affine schemes over an affine base, Stacks
01JQ, and a point of `T'` lies under a point of the fibre product over any point of `T_i` with the
same image in `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsStandardFpqcCovering.pullback {T : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type v} {U : I → Scheme.{u}}
    {f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T} (hf : IsStandardFpqcCovering U f) {T' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine T']
    (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    IsStandardFpqcCovering (fun i ↦ Limits.pullback g (f i))
      (fun i ↦ Limits.pullback.fst g (f i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presieve₀_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affine_refinements
declarations.doc:
A flat family which admits a standard fpqc refinement after every affine base change
is an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
public lemma presieve₀_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_of_affine_refinements
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (U : PreZeroHypercover.{v} T)
    (hflat : ∀ i, Flat (U.f i))
    (hrefine : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine Z] (h : Z ⟶ T),
      ∃ (V : Z.AffineCover.{0} @Flat), Finite V.I₀ ∧
        Nonempty (V.cover.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom (U.pullback₂ h))) :
    U.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LC part (1), at `τ = fppf`.**  The equivalence of Stacks 03DX is
compatible with pullback: for `f : X ⟶ S` the structure morphism of an object `T` of the big fppf
category over `S`, with `f_big` the induced morphism of ringed big fppf sites of Stacks 021W, and
`𝓕` a quasi-coherent module on `S`,

    `f_big^*(𝓕^a) ≅ (f^*𝓕)^a`,

naturally in `𝓕`.  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleObjRestrictNatIso` with the restriction functor
replaced by the inverse image of `f_big` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.objInverseImageIso`.

The same clause for an arbitrary morphism of schemes rather than an object of the big site, and
at all five `τ` rather than at `fppf` alone, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigSites.lean`); what this
declaration adds over it is the identification of `f_big^*` with restriction to the big fppf site
of the scheme of `T`, which is what the proof of Stacks 03DX (1) consumes.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBaseChangeIso :
    associatedModule B S hS ⋙ SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (objBaseChangeSharp B S hS T) ≅
      Scheme.Modules.pullback (objHom B S hS T) ⋙
        associatedModule B (objScheme B S hS T) (contains_objScheme B S hS T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedModule_pullback_compatible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LC part (1).**  The equivalences of Proposition 03DX are compatible
with pullback: for every morphism of schemes `f` and every module `𝓖` on the target,
`f_sites^*(𝓖^a) ≅ (f^*𝓖)^a`, naturally in `𝓖`, where `f_sites` is the induced morphism of ringed
sites of Stacks 070R —

* on the big sites, `f_big : ((Sch/X)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_τ, 𝒪)` at each of
  `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`);
* on the small étale sites, `f_small : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale`
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso`);
* on the small Zariski sites, `f_small : T_Zar ⟶ S_Zar`
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso`).

The source states it for quasi-coherent `𝓖`; it holds for every module.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedModule_pullback_compatible :
    (∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hY : B.Contains Y)
        (f : X ⟶ Y) (τ : SiteKind),
      Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.pullback f ⋙ BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ ≅
        BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ ⋙
          SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (BigFppfOver.baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ))) ∧
    (∀ (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (a : X ⟶ Y),
      Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.pullback (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a) ⋙
          SmallEtale.associatedModule B X.obj X.property ≅
        SmallEtale.associatedModule B Y.obj Y.property ⋙
          SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (SmallEtale.smallEtaleStructureMapRing B a))) ∧
    (∀ (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) {S T : B.Schemes} (f : T ⟶ S),
      Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.pullback (SmallZariski.lcSchemeHom B f) ⋙
          SmallZariski.associatedModule B T.1 T.property ≅
        SmallZariski.associatedModule B S.1 S.property ⋙
          SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (SmallZariski.lcStructureMapRing B f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.associatedModule_pushforward_compatible_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LC part (3).**  Let `f` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`.  Then `f_*` preserves quasi-coherent modules (Stacks 01LC,
`AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_isQuasicoherent`), `f_{small, *}` preserves quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the small `τ`-sites, and the square of the two associated-module functors commutes,
`f_{small, *}(𝓕^a) ≅ (f_*𝓕)^a` for every quasi-coherent `𝓕`.

At `τ = étale` the last two conjuncts are
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallPushforwardIsoOfQcqs`; at `τ = Zariski` they
are `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcIsQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedModule_pushforward_compatible_of_qcqs :
    (∀ (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (a : X ⟶ Y)
        [QuasiCompact (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a)] [QuasiSeparated (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a)],
      (∀ 𝓕 : X.obj.Modules, 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent →
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a)).obj 𝓕).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      (∀ 𝓖 : SheafOfModules.{u} (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B X.obj X.property),
        𝓖.IsQuasicoherentOnSite → ((SmallEtale.smallPushforward B a).obj 𝓖).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
      (∀ 𝓕 : X.obj.Modules, 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent →
        Nonempty ((SmallEtale.associatedModule B Y.obj Y.property).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (SmallEtale.schemeHom B a)).obj 𝓕) ≅
          (SmallEtale.smallPushforward B a).obj
            ((SmallEtale.associatedModule B X.obj X.property).obj 𝓕)))) ∧
    (∀ (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) {S T : B.Schemes} (f : T ⟶ S)
        [QuasiCompact (SmallZariski.lcSchemeHom B f)]
        [QuasiSeparated (SmallZariski.lcSchemeHom B f)],
      (∀ 𝓕 : (T.1).Modules, 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent →
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (SmallZariski.lcSchemeHom B f)).obj 𝓕).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      (∀ 𝓖 : SheafOfModules.{u} (SmallZariski.structureSheaf B T.1 T.property),
        𝓖.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
          ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (SmallZariski.lcStructureMapRing B f)).obj
            𝓖).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
      (∀ 𝓕 : (T.1).Modules, 𝓕.IsQuasicoherent →
        Nonempty ((SmallZariski.associatedModule B S.1 S.property).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (SmallZariski.lcSchemeHom B f)).obj 𝓕) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (SmallZariski.lcStructureMapRing B f)).obj
            ((SmallZariski.associatedModule B T.1 T.property).obj 𝓕))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The associated module of a pullback is the pullback of the associated module.**  For
`a : X ⟶ Y` a morphism of schemes of the big étale site, with `r` the underlying morphism of
schemes and `ε_a` the morphism of ringed sites of Stacks 070R (2),

`(r^*𝓕)^a ≅ ε_a^*(𝓕^a)`,

naturally in the `𝒪_Y`-module `𝓕`, with no quasi-coherence hypothesis.  This **is Stacks 03LC
part (1) at `τ = étale`**, for the small étale sites of two schemes and a morphism between them:
the equivalence of Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = étale` is compatible with pullback.  It is proved
here for arbitrary modules, not only quasi-coherent ones.

Each side is a composite of two pullbacks of sheaves of modules round the square of ringed sites
whose geometric half is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.baseChangeOpensIso` and whose ring half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.structureMap_comp_baseChangeOpensIso`, so the two agree because a
left adjoint is determined by its right adjoint.

**This also carries Stacks 03FH (2)** for the morphism `f_{small} : X_étale ⟶ Y_étale` of
Remark 070R (2): that clause asserts `(f^*𝓕)^a = f_{sites}^*𝓕^a` for every `f_{sites}` of
Remark 070R, and this is the small étale one.  The big fppf one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBigPullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigFppf.lean`); the big Zariski,
étale, smooth and syntomic ones are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigSites.lean`), and the small
Zariski one is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiPushforwardSquare.lean:458`).
(It was formerly cited as `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso`, which
states the commutation over the *identity reading* of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` and is a tautology about `𝟭`;
that declaration is untagged, and naming it here made this enumeration a false completeness
claim.)
Those are every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R lists; the mixed-topology entries
`(Sch/X)_τ ⟶ (Sch/Y)_{τ'}` with `τ ≠ τ'` of the Topologies, Section 03FE list that the remark's
opening sentence also covers are not claimed.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleBaseChangeIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback (schemeHom B a) ⋙ associatedModule B X.obj X.property ≅
      associatedModule B Y.obj Y.property ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (smallEtaleStructureMapRing B a)
declarations.comment: part (1) at τ = étale, for the small étale sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (3) at `τ = étale`, the second conjunct.**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, the direct image `f_{small, *}` along the morphism of ringed small étale
sites of Stacks 070R (2) carries a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module on `X_étale` to a quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-module on `Y_étale`.

The reduction to the previous statement is Descent, Proposition 03DX (2) at `τ = étale`, which
this development has unconditionally:  a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module `𝓖` on `X_étale` restricts to
a quasi-coherent module on the affine objects by Stacks 0GZX (3) ⇒ (2), so the counit of the
associated-module adjunction of `X_étale` is an isomorphism at `𝓖` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isIso_counit_of_affineRestriction`, exhibiting `𝓖` as the
associated module of the quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ε_{X,*}𝓖`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward
    [QuasiCompact (schemeHom B a)] [QuasiSeparated (schemeHom B a)]
    (𝓖 : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B X.obj X.property))
    (h𝓖 : 𝓖.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((smallPushforward B a).obj 𝓖).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (3) at τ = étale, the second conjunct: f_{small, *} carries quasi-coherent 𝒪-modules on the small étale site of X to quasi-coherent 𝒪-modules on the small étale site of Y, for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallPushforwardIsoOfQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (3) at `τ = étale`, the commuting square**, at one module and with no
hypothesis beyond quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` and quasi-coherence of `𝓕`:

    `(f_*𝓕)^a ≅ f_{small, *}(𝓕^a)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSmallPushwardIso` with its hypothesis
discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward_associatedModule`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedModuleSmallPushforwardIsoOfQcqs
    [QuasiCompact (schemeHom B a)] [QuasiSeparated (schemeHom B a)] :
    (associatedModule B Y.obj Y.property).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (schemeHom B a)).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (smallPushforward B a).obj ((associatedModule B X.obj X.property).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (3) at τ = étale, the commuting square f_{small, *}(𝓕^a) ≅ (f_*𝓕)^a, at one module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (1) at `τ = Zariski`, for the small Zariski sites.**  The equivalence of
Stacks 03DX (2) at `τ = Zariski` is compatible with pullback: for `f : T ⟶ S` a morphism of
schemes of the big Zariski site, with `f_small : (T_Zar, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪)` the morphism of ringed
sites of Stacks 070R (2) and `𝓖` an `𝒪_S`-module,

    `(f^*𝓖)^a ≅ f_small^*(𝓖^a)`,

naturally in `𝓖` and with no quasi-coherence hypothesis.

Here `𝓖 ↦ 𝓖^a` is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModule`, the functor of
Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` over the structure sheaf `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` of the small
Zariski site — not the identity reading introduced in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Descent.AssociatedModule.SmallZariskiFullyFaithful`.  That
distinction is what gives this declaration its content.
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso` states the corresponding
commutation over the identity reading, and it does **not** state this clause: the identity
reading is pullback along the identity morphism of ringed sites, isomorphic to `𝟭`, so that
statement reads `f_small^* ⋙ 𝟭 ≅ 𝟭 ⋙ f_small^*` and is proved by whiskering the two unit
isomorphisms and applying the two unitors, never touching the coefficient sheaf
`T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` that clause (2) is about.  It is accordingly untagged.

The proof is `SheafOfModules.pullbackSquareIso`, Stacks 03D8 for a square: the geometric half of
the square is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcBaseChangeOpensIso`, that the base change of the
object chosen over an open `V` of `S` is the object chosen over `f⁻¹(V)`, and the ring half is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcStructureMap_comp_baseChangeOpensIso`.

**This is also Stacks 03FH part (2)** for the small Zariski `f_small` of Remark 070R (2).  That
clause asserts `(f^*𝓕)^a = f_sites^*𝓕^a` for every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R
lists, and the two clauses coincide at this `f_sites`: both are the statement that the
associated-module functor of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` commutes with pullback along
the morphism of ringed small Zariski sites of Stacks 070R (2).  The companions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso` — which carries the same two
clauses on one declaration — for the big site at each of the five topologies, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso` for the small étale `f_small`.
Those are every `f_sites` of the enumeration; the mixed-topology entries
`(Sch/X)_τ ⟶ (Sch/Y)_{τ'}` with `τ ≠ τ'` of Topologies, Section 03FE are not claimed.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback (lcSchemeHom B f) ⋙ associatedModule B T.1 T.property ≅
      associatedModule B S.1 S.property ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)
declarations.comment: part (1) at τ = Zariski, for the small Zariski sites: (f^*𝓖)^a ≅ f_small^*(𝓖^a), for an arbitrary morphism of schemes of the site and arbitrary modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (3) at `τ = Zariski`, the commuting square**, at one module and with no
hypothesis on `f`: for every `𝒪_T`-module `𝓕`,

    `(f_*𝓕)^a ≅ f_{small, *}(𝓕^a)`.

The isomorphism is the counit of the associated-module adjunction of the small Zariski site of
`S` at `f_{small, *}(𝓕^a)`, which is an isomorphism at every module by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_counit_smallZariskiAssociatedModuleAdjunction`, precomposed with the
associated module of the identification
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcRestrictModuleSmallPushforwardAssociatedModuleIso` of its
restriction with `f_*𝓕`.

The source states the square for `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, where it is a square of
the categories of *quasi-coherent* modules; the isomorphism of modules holds without those
hypotheses, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcIsQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward` supplies the
quasi-coherence of the two corners under them.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardIso (𝓕 : (T.1).Modules) :
    (associatedModule B S.1 S.property).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (lcSchemeHom B f)).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)).obj
        ((associatedModule B T.1 T.property).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (3) at τ = Zariski, the commuting square f_{small,*}(𝓕^a) ≅ (f_*𝓕)^a, at one module and with no hypothesis on f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (3) at `τ = Zariski`, the commuting square as an isomorphism of
functors.**  The square

```
  Mod(𝒪_T) ------ f_* ------> Mod(𝒪_S)
      |                          |
   𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a                   𝓖 ↦ 𝓖^a
      v                          v
  Mod(T_Zar, 𝒪) - f_{small,*} -> Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)
```

commutes up to the canonical natural isomorphism, with no hypothesis on `f` and on all modules.
Its components are `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardIso`; the
proof is the same three steps, read as isomorphisms of functors: the unit of the
associated-module adjunction of `T_Zar`, the mate square
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcRestrictModuleBaseChangeIso`, and the counit of the
associated-module adjunction of `S_Zar`, which is an isomorphism of functors because
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.restrictModule` is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardNatIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pushforward (lcSchemeHom B f) ⋙ associatedModule B S.1 S.property ≅
      associatedModule B T.1 T.property ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)
declarations.comment: part (3) at τ = Zariski, the commuting square of the part, as an isomorphism of functors Mod(𝒪_T) ⥤ Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪) and with no hypothesis on f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcIsQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LC part (3) at `τ = Zariski`, the preservation of quasi-coherence by
`f_{small, *}`.**  For `f : T ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the direct image along
`f_small : (T_Zar, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪)` of a module quasi-coherent on the small Zariski site of `T`
is quasi-coherent on the small Zariski site of `S`.

Every such module is an associated module: its restriction to the opens of `T` is quasi-coherent
by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherent_restrictModule` and the counit exhibits the
module as the associated module of that restriction.  Its direct image is then
`(f_*𝓕)^a` by `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModuleSmallPushforwardIso`, and
`f_*𝓕` is quasi-coherent by Stacks 01LC, so that associated module is quasi-coherent on the site
by Stacks 03DV (2).
declarations.statement:
public theorem lcIsQuasicoherentOnSite_smallPushforward
    [QuasiCompact (lcSchemeHom B f)] [QuasiSeparated (lcSchemeHom B f)]
    (𝒢 : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B T.1 T.property))
    (h𝒢 : 𝒢.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u} (lcStructureMapRing B f)).obj 𝒢).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (3) at τ = Zariski, f_{small,*} carries quasi-coherent 𝒪-modules on the small Zariski site to quasi-coherent 𝒪-modules on the small Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), for the morphism of big sites
`f_big : ((Sch/X)_τ, 𝒪_X) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_τ, 𝒪_Y)` of Stacks 070R (1), at each of the five
topologies `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  The associated module of a
pullback is the pullback of the associated module, `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a)`, naturally in the
`𝒪_Y`-module `𝓕`.

No hypothesis: the morphism of ringed sites is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseChange`
together with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseStructureComparison`, and the two provisos of
`SheafOfModules.pullbackSquareIso` are
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.opensBaseChangeIso`, which is topology-free, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.comparisonComp_baseOpensBaseChangeIso`.

Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleBaseChangeIso` (the small étale `f_small`) and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.lcAssociatedModulePullbackIso` (the small Zariski `f_small`,
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiPushforwardSquare.lean:458`)
this is every `f_sites` the enumeration of Remark 070R lists: clause (1) of that remark gives
the big site at each of these five topologies, and clause (2) the small site at the two
topologies that have one.  (The small Zariski entry was formerly cited as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModulePullbackIso`, which states the commutation over
the *identity reading* of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` and is a tautology about `𝟭`; it is untagged, and naming it
here made this enumeration a false completeness claim.)
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBasePullbackIso :
    Scheme.Modules.pullback f ⋙ baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ ≅
      baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ ⋙
        SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ)
declarations.comment: part (1) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, for the big sites: (f^*𝓖)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓖^a), for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and arbitrary modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBaseObjPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03FH, part (2), at one module**: `(f^*𝓕)^a ≅ f_big^*(𝓕^a)` for the morphism of big
sites `f_big` at each of the five topologies, read off from
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.associatedModuleBasePullbackIso`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleBaseObjPullbackIso (𝓕 : Y.Modules) :
    (baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ).obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj 𝓕) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ)).obj
        ((baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (1) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, for the big sites, at one module: f_big^*(𝓖^a) ≅ (f^*𝓖)^a

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.QcohPushforward.exists_isEmpty_iso_bigPushforward_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LC part (2).**  The equivalences `𝓖 ↦ 𝓖^a` of Proposition 03DX part
(1) are **not** compatible with pushforward in general: there are a morphism of schemes
`f : X ⟶ Y`, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` — so
that `f_*𝓕` is quasi-coherent and `(f_*𝓕)^a` is defined — such that on every big site (both
schemes lie in every one) and at every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`

    `f_{big, *}(𝓕^a) ≇ (f_*𝓕)^a`

as `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/Y)_τ`, where `f_{big, *}` is the pushforward along the morphism of
ringed big sites `f_big : ((Sch/X)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_τ, 𝒪)` of Stacks 070R (1).

The witness is the source's: the punctured plane `U = Spec k[t][X] ∖ V(X, t)` over
`Spec k[t][X]`, with `k = ULift ℚ`, and `𝓕 = 𝒪_U`; the two sides differ over the origin
`Spec k ⟶ Spec k[t][X]`, which is where the base-change map of
`Stacks.Examples.QcohPushforward.exists_not_isIso_baseChangeNatTrans` fails.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isEmpty_iso_bigPushforward_associatedModule :
    ∃ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (F : X.Modules),
      QuasiCompact f ∧ QuasiSeparated f ∧ F.IsQuasicoherent ∧
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F).IsQuasicoherent ∧
        (∀ B : BigFppfSite.{u}, B.Contains X ∧ B.Contains Y) ∧
        ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X) (hY : B.Contains Y) (τ : SiteKind),
          IsEmpty ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u}
              (BigFppfOver.baseStructureComparison B hX hY f τ)).obj
              ((BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule B X hX τ).obj F) ≅
            (BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule B Y hY τ).obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EquivariantModule
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on `X` equivariant for a given action of `G`, written directly in
terms of the action map and the projection.
declarations.statement: structure EquivariantModule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantGroupoidMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LG.** An equivariant morphism induces the specified morphism of
action groupoids.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivariantGroupoidMorphism (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsModHom G f] :
    EquivariantGroupoidMorphism B G X Y f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LG.** Pullback of equivariant quasi-coherent modules along an
equivariant morphism `f`. Its action on modules, on equivariant structures and on morphisms is
that of the pullback functor along the induced morphism of action groupoids.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivariantPullback (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsModHom G f] :
    Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.QuasicoherentModule (actionGroupoid B G X) ⥤
      Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.QuasicoherentModule (actionGroupoid B G Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.QuasicoherentModule
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on a groupoid scheme, with its descent morphism, cocycle law, and
normalization along the identity section.
declarations.statement: structure QuasicoherentModule {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pullbackFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LJ.** Pullback along a morphism of groupoid schemes, as a functor on
quasi-coherent modules equipped with groupoid descent data.  On objects it sends `(F, α)` to
`(f⁺F, f⁺α)`, using the canonical comparison isomorphisms for pullback along composites; on
morphisms it is the usual pullback of morphisms of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackFunctor (f : Hom G H) :
    QuasicoherentModule H ⥤ QuasicoherentModule G

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pullbackFunctor_obj_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LJ.** Pullback along a morphism of groupoid schemes pulls back the
underlying module along the map on objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_obj_module (f : Hom G H) (M : QuasicoherentModule H) :
    ((pullbackFunctor f).obj M).module =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f.mapObjects.left).obj M.module

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pullbackFunctor_obj_alpha
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LJ.** The descent morphism of a pulled-back module is the canonical
pullback of the original descent morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_obj_alpha (f : Hom G H) (M : QuasicoherentModule H) :
    Eq.ndrec (motive := fun X =>
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj X ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.source.left).obj X)
      ((pullbackFunctor f).obj M).alpha (pullbackFunctor_obj_module f M) =
      pullbackDescent f M

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pullbackFunctor_map_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LJ.** Pullback of a morphism of quasi-coherent modules on a groupoid
scheme is the usual pullback of morphisms of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackFunctor_map_hom (f : Hom G H) {M N : QuasicoherentModule H} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (pullbackFunctor_obj_module f M) ▸
      (pullbackFunctor_obj_module f N) ▸
        (QuasicoherentModule.Hom.hom ((pullbackFunctor f).map g)) =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback f.mapObjects.left).map g.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantModuleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LL.** Equivariant quasi-coherent modules for an action of a group
scheme are the same as quasi-coherent modules on the associated action groupoid scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivariantModuleEquivalence :
    EquivariantModule Y G X ≌
      GroupoidScheme.QuasicoherentModule (groupoidSchemeOfAction Y G X).groupoid

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantModuleEquivalence_functor_obj_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LL.** The canonical comparison leaves the underlying quasi-coherent
module unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivariantModuleEquivalence_functor_obj_module (M : EquivariantModule Y G X) :
    ((toActionGroupoidModule Y G X).obj M).module = M.module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantModuleEquivalence_functor_obj_alpha
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LL.** The canonical comparison leaves the descent morphism
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem equivariantModuleEquivalence_functor_obj_alpha (M : EquivariantModule Y G X) :
    ((toActionGroupoidModule Y G X).obj M).alpha = M.alpha

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.equivariantModuleEquivalence_functor_map_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LL.** On morphisms the canonical comparison is the identity on the
underlying morphism of modules.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isInvariantSet_target_image_source_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LO (1).** The saturation of any subset by the arrows of a groupoid
scheme is invariant.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.isOpen_target_image_source_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LO (2).** The saturation of an open set is open when the target map
is an open map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_target_image_source_preimage {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    (ht : IsOpenMap G.target.left.base)
    (W : G.objects.left.Opens) :
    IsOpen (G.target.left.base '' (G.source.left.base ⁻¹' (W : Set G.objects.left)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_invariant_compact_open_neighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LO (3).** If the target map is open and the source map is
quasi-compact, every point of the object scheme has an invariant quasi-compact open
neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invariant_compact_open_neighborhood {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    (ht : IsOpenMap G.target.left.base)
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left]
    (x : G.objects.left) :
    ∃ V : G.objects.left.Opens,
      x ∈ (V : Set G.objects.left) ∧
        IsInvariantOpen G V ∧ IsCompact (V : Set G.objects.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_isInvariantOpen_eq_target_image_source_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LO, part (2).** If the target map of a groupoid scheme is open then
the saturation `t(s⁻¹(W))` of an open subscheme `W` of the object scheme is an invariant open
subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvariantOpen_eq_target_image_source_preimage
    (ht : IsOpenMap G.target.left.base) (W : G.objects.left.Opens) :
    ∃ V : G.objects.left.Opens,
      (V : Set G.objects.left) =
        G.target.left.base '' (G.source.left.base ⁻¹' (W : Set G.objects.left)) ∧
      (W : Set G.objects.left) ⊆ (V : Set G.objects.left) ∧ IsInvariantOpen G V
declarations.comment: (2) t(s⁻¹(W)) is an invariant open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_isInvariantOpen_isCompact_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03LO, part (3).** If the target map of a groupoid scheme is open and
its source map is quasi-compact, then the object scheme has an open covering consisting of
invariant quasi-compact open subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvariantOpen_isCompact_cover [QuasiCompact G.source.left]
    (ht : IsOpenMap G.target.left.base) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (V : ι → G.objects.left.Opens),
      (∀ i, IsInvariantOpen G (V i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set G.objects.left)) ∧
      ⨆ i, V i = ⊤

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.abelianEtaleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Restriction of abelian étale sheaves** along an étale morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces: restriction along postcomposition with `f`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_abelianInverseImage_obj_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LP, the displayed formula for the inverse image, at abelian coefficients.** The
sections of `h_{small}^{-1}G` over an étale chart `W` of `U` are the sections of `G` over the
composite chart `jW`, as abelian groups.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_abelianInverseImageIso` evaluated at `G` and
at `W`; on the right-hand side the sections of a restricted sheaf are the asserted ones by
definition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_abelianInverseImage_obj_obj (h : U ⟶ V)
    (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom)
    (G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS V.1) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (W : SmallEtale B S hS U.1) :
    (((Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS h)).obj G).obj.obj (.op W)) ≅
      G.obj.obj (.op ((smallEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).obj W))
declarations.comment: the displayed formula for the inverse image, at abelian coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp
declarations.doc:
Postcomposition of an étale scheme chart with an étale morphism of algebraic spaces, as a
functor between the small étale sites.  Its underlying scheme and scheme morphisms are
unchanged.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtalePostcomp (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    SmallEtale B S hS X.1 ⥤ SmallEtale B S hS Y.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp_obj_hom
declarations.doc: On charts, postcomposition replaces `U ⟶ X` by its composite with `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtalePostcomp_obj_hom (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    ((smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).obj U).1.hom = U.1.hom ≫ f.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp_map_left
declarations.doc: On chart morphisms, postcomposition leaves the underlying scheme map unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtalePostcomp_map_left (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
    {U V : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (g : U ⟶ V) :
    ((smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).map g).hom.left = g.hom.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
Postcomposition along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces is continuous for the small
étale topologies, so that restriction along it carries sheaves on the small étale site of `Y`
to sheaves on that of `X`.
declarations.statement:
instance smallEtalePostcomp_isContinuous (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).IsContinuous
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LP.** Postcomposition along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces is
cocontinuous for the small étale topologies: a covering sieve of the composite chart `jU` pulls
back to a covering sieve of `U`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale.smallEtalePostcomp_cover_lift`, which in turn comes
from the comparison of the slice of the small étale site of `X` at `U` with the slice of that of
`Y` at `jU` — Stacks' remark that a covering of `jU` in `Y_étale` is the same thing as a
covering of `U` in `X_étale`.
declarations.statement:
instance smallEtalePostcomp_isCocontinuous (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).IsCocontinuous
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
For an étale morphism of algebraic spaces the small étale direct image is the direct image
attached to the cocontinuous postcomposition functor on charts.
declarations.statement:
def smallToposMorphism_pushforwardIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).pushforward ≅
      (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso
declarations.doc:
Sections of the small étale inverse image along an étale morphism over a chart `U ⟶ X` are
the sections of the original sheaf over the composite chart `U ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
def smallToposMorphism_inverseImageObjObjIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
    (G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (Type (u + 1)))
    (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    ((smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage.obj G).obj.obj (Opposite.op U) ≅
      G.obj.obj (Opposite.op ((smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf).obj U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LQ**, and the remaining assertion of **Stacks 03LP**: for an étale morphism
`h : U ⟶ V` of algebraic spaces, the inverse image of the morphism of *small* étale topoi
`h_{small}` of Stacks 03G2, part (3) is restriction along the postcomposition functor `j` of
Stacks 03LP, i.e. `G|_{U_étale} = h_{small}^{-1}G`.

The small étale morphism of topoi is the transport of the spaces-étale one along the comparison
equivalences of Stacks 03G1, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesToposMorphism_inverseImageIso` conjugated by those
equivalences, the comparison with small étale postcomposition being the identity.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso (h : U ⟶ V) (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS h).inverseImage ≅
      (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS U.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS V.1)
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi attached to j is f_small

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImage_obj_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LP, the displayed formula for the inverse image.** The sections of
`h_{small}^{-1}G` over an étale chart `W` of `U` are the sections of `G` over the composite
chart `jW`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso` evaluated at `G` and at
`W`, the sections of a restricted sheaf being the asserted ones by definition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_inverseImage_obj_obj (h : U ⟶ V)
    (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom)
    (G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS V.1) (Type (u + 1)))
    (W : SmallEtale B S hS U.1) :
    (((smallToposMorphism B S hS h).inverseImage.obj G).obj.obj (.op W)) ≅
      G.obj.obj (.op ((smallEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).obj W))
declarations.comment: the displayed formula for the inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_abelianInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LQ at abelian coefficients.** For an étale morphism `h : U ⟶ V` of algebraic
spaces, the inverse image of *abelian* sheaves along the morphism of small étale topoi
`h_{small}` of Stacks 03G2, part (3) is restriction along the postcomposition functor `j` of
Stacks 03LP, i.e. `G|_{U_étale} = h_{small}^{-1}G` for `G` an abelian sheaf.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso` is the same statement for sheaves
of sets, which is the form the source states it in.  The right-hand side is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleAbelianRestriction`.

Both sides are the conjugate, by the identification of abelian sheaves with commutative group
objects of the topos, of `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCommGrp` of the corresponding set-level
functor: for the inverse image that is the definition of
`CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage`, and for restriction along `j` it is
`Stacks.Sites.AbelianPullback.abelianSheafPushforwardIso`.  So the set-level isomorphism is
carried across by `CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCommGrpNatIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_abelianInverseImageIso (h : U ⟶ V)
    (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom) :
    Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS h) ≅
      (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS U.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS V.1)
declarations.comment: at abelian coefficients: h_small^{-1} of an abelian sheaf is restriction along j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesToposMorphism_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LQ on the spaces-étale topoi.** The inverse image of the morphism of
spaces-étale topoi attached to an étale morphism `h : U ⟶ V` is restriction along
postcomposition with `h`.

Its direct image is restriction along base change along `h`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesEtalePostcompSheafAdjunction` exhibits restriction along
postcomposition as another left adjoint of that functor, so the two agree by uniqueness of
left adjoints.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spacesToposMorphism_inverseImageIso (h : U ⟶ V)
    (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom) :
    ((spacesBaseChange_isMorphismOfSites B S hS h).morphismOfTopoi).inverseImage ≅
      (spacesEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS U) (SpacesEtale.topology B S hS V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LQ**, and the remaining assertion of **Stacks 03LP**: for an étale morphism
`h : U ⟶ V` of algebraic spaces, the inverse image of the morphism of *small* étale topoi
`h_{small}` of Stacks 03G2, part (3) is restriction along the postcomposition functor `j` of
Stacks 03LP, i.e. `G|_{U_étale} = h_{small}^{-1}G`.

The small étale morphism of topoi is the transport of the spaces-étale one along the comparison
equivalences of Stacks 03G1, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesToposMorphism_inverseImageIso` conjugated by those
equivalences, the comparison with small étale postcomposition being the identity.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposMorphism_inverseImageIso (h : U ⟶ V) (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS h).inverseImage ≅
      (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS h hh).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS U.1) (SmallEtale.topology B S hS V.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleAbelianInverseImageSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LR's inverse-image footnote, at abelian coefficients.**  For a cartesian square
of algebraic spaces, the inverse image of *abelian* sheaves on the small étale sites may be
taken around the square either way:
`(f')_{small}^{-1}(G|_{Y'}) = (f_{small}^{-1}G)|_{X'}`, naturally in the abelian sheaf `G`.

As at `Type` coefficients the hypothesis is only that the square commute, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleAbelianInverseImageSquareIsoOfComm`; the identity is pure
functoriality.

Like `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImageSquareIso`, which is the same statement for
sheaves of sets, this is the datum of which the inverse of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleAbelianPushforwardBaseChangeIso` is *expected* to be the
adjunction mate; that identification is not proved here either.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleAbelianInverseImageSquareIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS g) ⋙
        Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS f') ≅
      Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS f) ⋙
        Sites.abelianInverseImage (smallToposMorphism B S hS i)
declarations.comment: the inverse-image footnote, at abelian coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePushforwardBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LR, part (1).** For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces whose bottom arrow
`g` is étale, direct image of sheaves of sets on the small étale sites commutes with
restriction: `f'_{small,*}(F|_{X'}) = (f_{small,*}F)|_{Y'}`, naturally in the sheaf `F`.

Restriction is the inverse image of the small étale morphism of topoi, by Stacks 03LQ.  Each of
the four functors is the conjugate by the comparison equivalences of Stacks 03G1 of a
restriction functor on the spaces-étale sites, where the statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.spacesPushforwardBaseChangeIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallEtalePushforwardBaseChangeIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS i).inverseImage ⋙
        (smallToposMorphism B S hS f').pushforward ≅
      (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).pushforward ⋙
        (smallToposMorphism B S hS g).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImageSquareIso
declarations.doc:
The inverse-image identification around a cartesian square, built from the inverse-image
composition isomorphism of Stacks 03G2, part (3) and the commutativity of the square.

It is the datum of which the inverse of `smallEtalePushforwardBaseChangeIso` is expected to be
the adjunction mate; that identification is not proved here.

This is the parenthetical assertion of Stacks 03LR — "Also `(f')^{-1}_{small}(G|_{Y'}) =
(f_{small}^{-1}G)|_{X'}` because of commutativity of the diagram and (03LQ)" — which is why the
hypothesis is only `sq` and not the étaleness of `g`: the identity is pure functoriality.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallEtaleInverseImageSquareIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    (smallToposMorphism B S hS g).inverseImage ⋙
        (smallToposMorphism B S hS f').inverseImage ≅
      (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage ⋙
        (smallToposMorphism B S hS i).inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtaleAbelianHigherBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Étale base change for higher direct images.**  For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces
over `S`

```
X' --i--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --g--> Y
```

with `g` étale, and for every `n`, the canonical comparison of higher direct images of abelian
sheaves on the small étale sites is an isomorphism: `R^n f'_{small,*}(ℱ|_{X'})` and
`(R^n f_{small,*} ℱ)|_{Y'}` are identified by it, naturally in the abelian sheaf `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleAbelianHigherBaseChangeMap (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (smallEtaleAbelianHigherBaseChangeMap B S hS i f' f g sq hg n)
declarations.comment:
part (2): for every abelian sheaf and every degree n, the canonical comparison
(R^n f_{small,*} F)|_{Y'} ⟶ R^n f'_{small,*}(F|_{X'}) of higher direct images is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePushforwardEtaleBaseChange_allParts
declarations.doc:
**Étale base change on the small étale sites.**  For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces
over `S`

```
X' --i--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --g--> Y
```

with `g` étale, the following three assertions hold. First, the canonical base-change 2-cell
`f_{small,*} ∘ g_{small}^{-1} ⟶ i_{small}^{-1} ∘ f'_{small,*}` of sheaves of sets is invertible,
which is `f'_{small,*}(ℱ|_{X'}) = (f_{small,*}ℱ)|_{Y'}` naturally in `ℱ`. Second,
`(f')_{small}^{-1}(𝒢|_{Y'}) = (f_{small}^{-1}𝒢)|_{X'}`. Third, in every degree `n` the canonical
comparison `(R^n f_{small,*} ℱ)|_{Y'} ⟶ R^n f'_{small,*}(ℱ|_{X'})` of higher direct images of
abelian sheaves is invertible.

The second conjunct is stated as `Nonempty` of an isomorphism of functors; the canonical one is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInverseImageSquareIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtalePushforwardEtaleBaseChange_allParts (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    IsIso (properBaseChangeMap B S hS f g f' i sq) ∧
      Nonempty ((smallToposMorphism B S hS g).inverseImage ⋙
            (smallToposMorphism B S hS f').inverseImage ≅
          (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage ⋙
            (smallToposMorphism B S hS i).inverseImage) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (smallEtaleAbelianHigherBaseChangeMap B S hS i f' f g sq hg n)
declarations.comment: the whole statement as one conjunction, in the source's order: part (1), that the canonical base-change 2-cell of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism, i.e. f'_* (F|_X') = (f_* F)|_Y'; its inverse-image footnote, (f')^{-1}(G|_Y') = (f^{-1} G)|_X'; and part (2), that for every degree n the canonical comparison (R^n f_* F)|_Y' -> R^n f'_* (F|_X') of higher direct images of abelian sheaves is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_properBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces whose bottom arrow `g` is étale, the base-change
2-cell `f_{small,*} ∘ g_{small}^{-1} ⟶ i_{small}^{-1} ∘ f'_{small,*}` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_properBaseChangeMap (sq : IsPullback i f' f g) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    IsIso (properBaseChangeMap B S hS f g f' i sq)
declarations.comment: part (1), invertibility of the canonical base-change 2-cell

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartRestrictionComp_cocycle
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle condition of Stacks 03LS for the restrictions of a sheaf to the étale scheme
charts of `X`**: restricting to a chart `U`, then to a chart `V` over it, then to a chart `W` over
that, is the same whether the last two steps are taken one at a time or the two morphisms of
charts are composed first.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphism_comp_inverseImage_cocycle` at the represented
