morphisms of the charts, where the three equalities of morphisms of algebraic spaces are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartMap_comp_chartToSpace` twice and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartMap_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartRestrictionComp_cocycle {W V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U) (g : W ⟶ V) :
    Functor.whiskerRight (chartRestrictionComp B S hS X f).hom
        (chartInverseImage B S hS X g) ≫ (chartRestrictionComp B S hS X g).hom =
    Functor.whiskerLeft (chartRestriction B S hS X U)
        (chartInverseImageComp B S hS X f g).hom ≫
      (chartRestrictionComp B S hS X (g ≫ f)).hom
declarations.comment: the cocycle condition for the chartwise restrictions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartGlueingEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LS.**  A sheaf of sets on the small étale site of an algebraic space `X` is the
same thing as a family of sheaves `F_U` on the small étale sites of the étale scheme charts `U`
of `X`, together with isomorphisms `c_f : f^{-1}F_U ≅ F_V` for the morphisms `f : V ⟶ U` of
charts satisfying the cocycle condition `c_g ∘ g^{-1}c_f = c_{g ≫ f}` — an *equivalence of
categories*, given by sending a sheaf to the family of its restrictions to the charts.

The proof is the one the source gives: the chartwise inverse image is restriction along
postcomposition (Stacks 03LQ, through Stacks 03LP), so the chartwise data are the slice-indexed
data of Stacks 0GWK read through the comparison equivalence of Stacks 04M0
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sliceToChartFunctor`, an equivalence), and the chartwise description is
the slice-indexed one read through it
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartGlueingFunctorIso`).
declarations.statement:
def chartGlueingEquivalence :
    Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1) (Type (u + 1)) ≌ ChartGlueingData B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartInverseImageComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LS.** The canonical comparison of successive chartwise inverse images with the
inverse image along the composite morphism of charts: it is the adjoint-mate composition
isomorphism of Stacks 03G2, part (3), read through the equality `chartMap g ≫ chartMap f =
chartMap (g ≫ f)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartInverseImageComp {W V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (g : W ⟶ V) :
    chartInverseImage B S hS X f ⋙ chartInverseImage B S hS X g ≅
      chartInverseImage B S hS X (g ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartRestrictionComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LS.** Restriction to a chart commutes canonically with further restriction along
a morphism of charts: the composite of the structure morphism of the larger chart with the
morphism of charts is the structure morphism of the smaller chart.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartRestrictionComp {V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    chartRestriction B S hS X U ⋙ chartInverseImage B S hS X f ≅
      chartRestriction B S hS X V
declarations.comment: compatibility of chart restriction with inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward_additive
declarations.doc:
The direct image of `𝒪`-modules along a morphism of algebraic spaces is an additive
functor.
declarations.statement:
instance modulePushforward_additive (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (modulePushforward B S hS f).Additive

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleSheafFunctor_map_compIsoCongr_hom_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LU.**  The comparison `f_* ∘ g_* ≅ (f ≫ g)_*` of direct images of `𝒪`-modules is
the geometric comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphismTypeU_comp` of Stacks 03G2,
part (3), on underlying sheaves of sets.  The comparison appears in the transported form that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso_eq_compIsoCongr` identifies it with, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso_hom_app_eq` is that identification at a
single module.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleSheafFunctor_map_compIsoCongr_hom_app (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z)).map
        ((CategoryTheory.Functor.compIsoCongr
          (pushforwardModules_eq_modulePushforward B S hS f)
          (pushforwardModules_eq_modulePushforward B S hS g)
          (pushforwardModules_eq_modulePushforward B S hS (f ≫ g))
          (pushforwardModulesCompAt B S hS f g)).hom.app F) =
      (smallToposMorphismTypeU_comp B S hS f g).hom.app
        ((Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).obj F)
declarations.comment: the composition comparison for direct images is the geometric comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LU, the composition comparison for the direct image of modules.**  The composite of
the direct images of `𝒪`-modules along `f : X ⟶ Y` and then `g : Y ⟶ Z` is canonically isomorphic
to the direct image along `f ≫ g`.

The comparison is the composition law for the direct image of modules along a composite morphism
of ringed topoi, followed by the transport of the direct image of modules along Stacks 03G8's
cartesian comparison of the direct images of sheaves of sets.

This is the statement in the `RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules` presentation. The same part key
also sits on `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.SmallEtaleModulePullbackComp`, which states the same
comparison in the library's primary `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward` vocabulary and
is what consumers outside this presentation use; the two are identified by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso_eq_modulePushforwardCompIso'`. A tag carried by
both is correct, not a duplication: each presentation states the clause in its own vocabulary.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardCompIso' (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).pushforwardModules ⋙
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g).pushforwardModules ≅
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (f ≫ g)).pushforwardModules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback
declarations.doc:
The pullback `f^*G = 𝒪_X ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪_Y} f⁻¹G` of `𝒪_Y`-modules along a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`
of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullback (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ⥤ Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackAdjunction
declarations.doc:
Pullback of `𝒪`-modules along a morphism of algebraic spaces is left adjoint to the
pushforward `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward`: there is a bijection
`Hom_{𝒪_X}(f^*G, F) = Hom_{𝒪_Y}(G, f_*F)`, natural in both variables.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackAdjunction (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    modulePullback B S hS f ⊣ modulePushforward B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison `f_* ∘ g_* ≅ (f ≫ g)_*` of direct images of `𝒪`-modules along a
composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces.

Both sides have the direct image of sheaves of sets of the composite as their underlying
sheaf, and the comparison is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphismTypeU_comp`, the
comparison of Stacks 03G2, part (3), on it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardCompIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    modulePushforward B S hS f ⋙ modulePushforward B S hS g ≅
      modulePushforward B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison `f_* ∘ g_* ≅ (f ≫ g)_*` of direct images of `𝒪`-modules along a
composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces.

Both sides have the direct image of sheaves of sets of the composite as their underlying
sheaf, and the comparison is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallToposMorphismTypeU_comp`, the
comparison of Stacks 03G2, part (3), on it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardCompIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    modulePushforward B S hS f ⋙ modulePushforward B S hS g ≅
      modulePushforward B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the composition comparison for direct images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison `g^* ∘ f^* ≅ (f ≫ g)^*` of inverse images of `𝒪`-modules along a
composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces.

Both functors are left adjoint to `(f ≫ g)_*`: the left-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleCompAdjunction`, which composes the two adjunctions and reads
the resulting right adjoint through `modulePushforwardCompIso`, and the right-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackAdjunction`.  The comparison is the uniqueness of a
left adjoint, so it is the mate of the comparison of direct images.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackCompIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    modulePullback B S hS g ⋙ modulePullback B S hS f ≅ modulePullback B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackCompIso
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison `g^* ∘ f^* ≅ (f ≫ g)^*` of inverse images of `𝒪`-modules along a
composite of morphisms of algebraic spaces.

Both functors are left adjoint to `(f ≫ g)_*`: the left-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleCompAdjunction`, which composes the two adjunctions and reads
the resulting right adjoint through `modulePushforwardCompIso`, and the right-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackAdjunction`.  The comparison is the uniqueness of a
left adjoint, so it is the mate of the comparison of direct images.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackCompIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    modulePullback B S hS g ⋙ modulePullback B S hS f ≅ modulePullback B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardIdIso
declarations.doc:
**The unit law of Stacks 03LU for the direct image**: the direct image of `𝒪`-modules along
an identity morphism of algebraic spaces is the identity functor.

The direct image of sheaves of sets along an identity is the identity functor, and the structure
map of the identity is the corresponding identification of the structure sheaves
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.structureSharpSet_id`), which is exactly the input
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModulesIsoId` asks for.

This is the datum that the `idIso` field of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModulePushforwardCoherence` assumes.
declarations.statement:
def modulePushforwardIdIso (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    modulePushforward B S hS (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
declarations.comment: the unit law for the direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIdIso
declarations.doc:
**The unit law of Stacks 03LU**: the inverse image of `𝒪`-modules along an identity morphism
of algebraic spaces is the identity functor.

The inverse image is a left adjoint of the direct image by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackAdjunction`, the direct image along an identity is the
identity functor by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardIdIso`, and a left adjoint of the
identity functor is the identity functor.
declarations.statement:
def modulePullbackIdIso (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) :
    modulePullback B S hS (𝟙 X) ≅ 𝟭 (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
declarations.comment: the unit law: the inverse image of modules along an identity is the identity functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCompIso_assoc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LU, associativity of the composition comparison for direct images.**  For three
composable morphisms `f : W ⟶ X`, `g : X ⟶ Y`, `h : Y ⟶ Z` of algebraic spaces the two ways of
comparing `f_* ∘ g_* ∘ h_*` with `(f ≫ g ≫ h)_*` agree.

This is the `assoc` field of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ModulePushforwardCoherence`, so it is no
longer a hypothesis.  It is the cocycle law at the morphisms of ringed topoi of Stacks 03G8,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardModulesCompAt_assoc`, transported along the identifications
of the two direct images.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePushforwardCompIso_assoc (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) :
    isoWhiskerLeft (modulePushforward B S hS f) (modulePushforwardCompIso B S hS g h) ≪≫
        modulePushforwardCompIso B S hS f (g ≫ h) =
      (associator (modulePushforward B S hS f) (modulePushforward B S hS g)
          (modulePushforward B S hS h)).symm ≪≫
        isoWhiskerRight (modulePushforwardCompIso B S hS f g)
          (modulePushforward B S hS h) ≪≫
        modulePushforwardCompIso B S hS (f ≫ g) h
declarations.comment: the associativity of the composition comparison for direct images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherence
declarations.doc:
**Pseudofunctoriality of the direct image of `𝒪`-modules of Stacks 03LU, with no
hypothesis.**  The identity datum is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardIdIso`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardCoherenceOfIdIso` supplies the associativity coherence
and the two unit laws from it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def modulePushforwardCoherence : ModulePushforwardCoherence B S hS
declarations.comment: the pseudofunctoriality of the direct image, assembled: the identity comparison together with the associativity and the two unit laws of the composition comparison, as one datum with no hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03D6, part (1)**, unconditionally, and the direct-image half of Stacks 03LU: the
direct image of `𝒪_X`-modules along a morphism of algebraic spaces, read as `𝒪_Y`-modules by
restriction of scalars along the structure map.

The inverse-image half of Stacks 03LU is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback`, and the adjunction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackAdjunction`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SmallEtaleModulePullback.lean`).  That adjunction is
stated for the direct image of Stacks 03D6, part (1) attached to the morphism of ringed topoi,
which is this functor up to a comparison that is not yet supplied; see the implementation notes
of that file.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforward (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ⥤ Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.pullbackModulesToposIsoGeneral_hom_app_unit
declarations.doc:
**The two constructions of Stacks 03LU along a morphism of ringed sites agree.**  The
comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.HomGeneral.pullbackModulesToposIsoGeneral` of the two
pullbacks of sheaves of modules carries the corepresentability identification
`Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pullbackModulesObjUnitIso` of `f^*𝒪_Y ≅ 𝒪_X` to Mathlib's
adjoint-transpose one, `SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit` at `f^♯`.

Both are pinned by their transposes along Stacks 03D7, those two transposes are compared by
`homEquiv_pullbackModulesToposIsoGeneral_hom_app_unit`, and they agree because both are the unit
section of `𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HomGeneral.pullbackModulesToposIsoGeneral_hom_app_unit :
    f.pullbackModulesToposIsoGeneral.hom.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (toRingedTopos Y).O)) ≫
        SheafOfModules.pullbackObjUnitToUnit f.toRingedToposSiteHom.fSharpRing =
      (pullbackModulesObjUnitIso f.toRingedToposHom.toRingedToposModulesHom).inv
declarations.comment:
the corepresentability construction of `f^*𝒪_Y ≅ 𝒪_X` for the pullback of the
modules development and Mathlib's adjoint-transpose construction for the site-presented pullback
agree under the comparison of the two pullbacks, for a morphism of ringed sites at independent
universes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleInverseImageStructureSheafIso_hom
declarations.doc:
The forward map of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleInverseImageStructureSheafIso` is the
inverse-image form of the structure map of Stacks 03G8.  This is what makes that isomorphism the
canonical one of Stacks 03LV rather than an arbitrary one.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleInverseImageStructureSheafIso_hom (h : U ⟶ V) (hh : IsEtale B S hS h.hom) :
    (etaleInverseImageStructureSheafIso B S hS h hh).hom =
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS h).fSharpInverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** Along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces, the pullback of `𝒪_Y`-modules
of Stacks 03LU is naturally isomorphic to the inverse image of modules with its scalars
transported along the canonical isomorphism of structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage :
    modulePullback B S hS f ≅ etaleModuleInverseImage B S hS f hf
declarations.comment: pullback of modules is inverse image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** The comparison of the pullback of modules with the inverse image sends the
canonical image of every section of the inverse image to that same section.  This specifies the
comparison, rather than merely asserting that the two functors are isomorphic: a scalar-unit
twist of the natural isomorphism is excluded.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage_unit_app
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (U : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ)
    (m : ((inverseImageModules (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y)).obj G).val.obj U) :
    ((extendScalarsFSharpAdjunction B S hS f).unit.app
          ((inverseImageModules (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y)).obj G) ≫
        (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
          (smallEtaleRingedToposModulesHom B S hS f).fSharpInverseImage).map
            ((modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage B S hS f hf).hom.app G)).val.app U m =
      m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** Pullback of sheaves of modules along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces
is exact.  Through the comparison with the inverse image both halves are the exactness of the
inverse image of modules of Stacks 04JC, restriction of scalars along an isomorphism being an
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePullback_exact :
    exactFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (modulePullback B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Equation 03LW, that is clause (2) of Stacks 03LV.**  Along an étale morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces the pullback of `𝒪_Y`-modules of Stacks 03LU is naturally
isomorphic to étale restriction: `f^*G` is the sheaf whose sections over an étale chart `U` of
`X` are the sections of `G` over the composite chart of `Y`.

The comparison factors through the inverse image of modules by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage`, which is clause (2) of
Stacks 03LV in its inverse-image reading.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback :
    modulePullback B S hS f ≅ etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS f hf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_fSharpInverseImage_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** For an étale morphism of algebraic spaces the inverse-image form
`f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` of the structure map of the morphism of small étale ringed topoi of Stacks 03G8
is an isomorphism.

The proof exhibits it as a universal arrow: composition with it is identified with the inverse
of the composite of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fMapRestrictionEquiv` with the chart correspondence
and the adjunction, and the chartwise formula for the structure map says that the identification
sends the structure map itself to the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_fSharpInverseImage_of_isEtale :
    IsIso (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: the inverse image of the structure sheaf, h⁻¹𝒪_V = 𝒪_U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleStructureSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** For an étale morphism of algebraic spaces the inverse image of the
structure sheaf of the target along the morphism of small étale ringed topoi of Stacks 03G8 is
canonically isomorphic to the structure sheaf of the source.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleStructureSheafIso :
    (Stacks.Sheaves.ToposPushforward.inverseImageCommRingFunctor
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom).obj
      (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Y).O ≅ (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X).O
declarations.comment: inverse image of the structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleStructureSheafIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** The forward map of the canonical isomorphism of structure sheaves along an
étale morphism is the inverse-image form of the structure map; the isomorphism is not an extra
choice.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleStructureSheafIso_hom :
    (etaleStructureSheafIso B S hS f hf).hom =
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).fSharpInverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LV.** Along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces, the pullback of `𝒪_Y`-modules
of Stacks 03LU is naturally isomorphic to the inverse image of modules with its scalars
transported along the canonical isomorphism of structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage :
    modulePullback B S hS f ≅ etaleModuleInverseImage B S hS f hf
declarations.comment: the identification f^*G = f_small^{-1}G along an étale morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleInverseImageIsoEtaleModulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks' Equation 03LW**, the outer identification `G|_{X_étale} = f_{small}^{-1}G`: the
inverse image of `𝒪_Y`-modules along an étale morphism, read over `𝒪_X` through the canonical
isomorphism of structure sheaves, is étale restriction of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleModuleInverseImageIsoEtaleModulePullback :
    etaleModuleInverseImage B S hS f hf ≅ etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS f hf
declarations.comment: the inverse image of modules is étale restriction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Equation 03LW, that is clause (2) of Stacks 03LV.**  Along an étale morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces the pullback of `𝒪_Y`-modules of Stacks 03LU is naturally
isomorphic to étale restriction: `f^*G` is the sheaf whose sections over an étale chart `U` of
`X` are the sections of `G` over the composite chart of `Y`.

The comparison factors through the inverse image of modules by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage`, which is clause (2) of
Stacks 03LV in its inverse-image reading.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback :
    modulePullback B S hS f ≅ etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS f hf
declarations.comment: pullback of modules along an étale morphism is étale restriction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Equation 03LW, canonicity.**  The comparison of the pullback of modules with étale
restriction sends the canonical image of a section of the inverse image of modules to the
comparison of Stacks 03LQ applied to that section, so it introduces no twist of its own: it is
the canonical identification and not merely some natural isomorphism of the two functors.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModuleInverseImage_unit_app`, which pins
the extension-of-scalars half, followed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleInverseImageIsoEtaleModulePullback_val_app`, which pins the
transport half.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback_unit_app (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (U : (SmallEtale B S hS X.1)ᵒᵖ)
    (m : ((inverseImageModules.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
      (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y)).obj G).val.obj U) :
    ((extendScalarsFSharpAdjunction B S hS f).unit.app
          ((inverseImageModules.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
            (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).toToposHom
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS Y)).obj G) ≫
        (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
          (smallEtaleRingedToposModulesHom B S hS f).fSharpInverseImage).map
            ((modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback B S hS f hf).hom.app G)).val.app U m =
      ((etaleModuleInverseImageIsoRestrictionTransport B S hS f hf).hom.app G).val.app U m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_moduleEtaleBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LX for the ordinary direct image, read as a statement about the canonical map, in
the étale case.**  For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces whose bottom arrow `g` is étale,
the canonical base-change comparison

`(f_*F)|_{Y'} ⟶ f'_*(F|_{X'})`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleEtaleBaseChangeComparison` is an isomorphism.

This is what `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ModuleHigherPushforwardBaseChangeCanonical.lean`
records as the single underived statement the canonical reading of Stacks 03LX and Stacks 071Z
was owed.  It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_moduleBaseChangeMap_of_isEtale` conjugated into
the étale-restriction spelling by Stacks 03LW,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackIsoEtaleModulePullback`, which is canonical, so the
conjugation introduces no twist.

**This is the étale case and not Stacks 073K, part (1).**  Stacks 073K, part (1) asserts base
change for `g` merely *flat* and `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated; `hg` here is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale`, and étale is strictly stronger than flat.  So this is a
special case of that tag and carries no attribute for it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleEtaleBaseChangeComparison (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    IsIso (moduleEtaleBaseChangeComparison B S hS i f' f g sq hg)
declarations.comment:
the ordinary direct image, for the CANONICAL comparison map and for an ÉTALE
square: g étale, not merely flat, so this is a special case of Stacks 073K part (1) and not
that tag.  The existing 03LX attributes carry isomorphisms with the right endpoints that are
not identified with the canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleHigherPushforwardEtaleBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
Let

```
X' --i--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --g--> Y
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` with `g` étale.  Then for every `n` the
`n`-th higher direct image of `𝒪_X`-modules commutes with restriction along the étale base
change,

`R^n f'_*(F|_{X'}) = (R^n f_*F)|_{Y'}`

in `Mod(𝒪_{Y'})`, naturally in the `𝒪_X`-module `F`. The morphism `f` is not assumed
representable, quasi-compact or quasi-separated, and `F` is not assumed quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleHigherPushforwardEtaleBaseChangeIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (n : ℕ) :
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X'.1 X'.2
    etaleModulePullback B S hS i (isEtale_of_isPullback B S hS f' i g f sq.flip hg) ⋙
        (modulePushforward B S hS f').rightDerived n ≅
      (modulePushforward B S hS f).rightDerived n ⋙ etaleModulePullback B S hS g hg

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackSquareIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LX, the footnote.** For a commutative — in particular a cartesian — square

```
X' --i--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --g--> Y
```

of algebraic spaces, the inverse image of modules around the square agrees:
`(f')^*(G|_{Y'}) = (f^*G)|_{X'}` for every `𝒪_Y`-module `G`, naturally in `G`.

**Both restrictions are read as the inverse image of modules**, so all four functors in the
statement are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback` — the source's `G|_{Y'}` is `g^*G` and
its `(-)|_{X'}` is `i^*`.  That is the reading of Stacks 03LW, which the source's own footnote
invokes to derive this identity, and which this development does **not** supply: no comparison
of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback` with the étale restriction
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModulePullback` used elsewhere in this file is proved anywhere,
and the two are different functors (the tensor inverse image of Stacks 03D6, part (2) against
restriction along `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp`).  So what is proved here is the
footnote in the inverse-image reading, not in the restriction reading, and the attribute says so.

No étaleness is used: as in the source, the comparison is the Stacks 03LU composition
isomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackCompIso` for the two factorizations of the
diagonal `X' ⟶ Y` of the square, glued by the commutativity `sq.w` of the square; only `sq.w`
is consumed, so the cartesian hypothesis is stronger than the proof needs.  The module universe
is the universe `u` of the structure rings, which is the only one at which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback` exists.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackSquareIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g) :
    modulePullback B S hS g ⋙ modulePullback B S hS f' ≅
      modulePullback B S hS f ⋙ modulePullback B S hS i
declarations.comment:
the footnote, with both restrictions read as the inverse image of modules
  (Stacks 03LW)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardEtaleBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LX, the ordinary direct image, unconditionally.**  Let

```
X' --i--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --g--> Y
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site `B`,
with `g` étale.  Then for every `𝒪_X`-module `F`

`f'_*(F|_{X'}) = (f_*F)|_{Y'}`

in `Mod(𝒪_{Y'})`, naturally in `F`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardEtaleBaseChangeIsoOfStructureSharp` with its
hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangeStructureSharp_comp_baseChangeRingMap`.  The higher direct
images of Stacks 03LX are not treated, so the attribute carries a part string; the footnote is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackSquareIso`.

The restriction `(-)|_{X'}` is read here as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModulePullback`,
restriction of modules along small étale postcomposition, which is the reading of the ordinary
clause; the footnote is proved in the inverse-image reading instead, for the reason recorded in
its own docstring.

Inherited caveat.  The source asserts an equality, and this isomorphism has the right endpoints
but is **not** proved to be the adjunction mate of the inverse-image identification around the
square: that is already the standing in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SmallEtalePushforwardBaseChange.lean`, whose
implementation notes record it for
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePushforwardBaseChangeIso`, and the same applies to the
`Type u` instance of Stacks 03LR, part (1) that this isomorphism is built from.

The module universe is the universe `u` of the structure rings, which is the only one at which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforward` exists.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardEtaleBaseChangeIso (sq : IsPullback i f' f g)
    (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) :
    etaleModulePullback B S hS i (isEtale_of_isPullback B S hS f' i g f sq.flip hg) ⋙
        modulePushforward B S hS f' ≅
      modulePushforward B S hS f ⋙ etaleModulePullback B S hS g hg

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LY.** The pullback of `𝒪`-modules of Stacks 03LU along the morphism of algebraic
spaces represented by a morphism of étale scheme charts of `X`.  This is the functor
`f_{small}^*` in which the source states the transition isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartModuleInverseImage {V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS (chartSpace B S hS X U).1 (chartSpace B S hS X U).2 ⥤
      Modules.{u, u} B S hS (chartSpace B S hS X V).1 (chartSpace B S hS X V).2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleInverseImageComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LY.** The canonical comparison of successive chartwise pullbacks of modules with
the pullback along the composite morphism of charts: it is the composition comparison of
Stacks 03LU, read through the equality `chartMap g ≫ chartMap f = chartMap (g ≫ f)`.

It is this comparison that makes the cocycle condition
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsChartModuleCocycle` a statement rather than a type error.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartModuleInverseImageComp {W V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (g : W ⟶ V) :
    chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X f ⋙ chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X g ≅
      chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X (g ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleRestrictionComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LY.** Restriction of a module to a chart commutes canonically with further
chartwise pullback along a morphism of charts: the composite of the structure morphism of the
larger chart with the morphism of charts is the structure morphism of the smaller chart.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartModuleRestrictionComp {V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U) :
    chartModuleRestriction B S hS X U ⋙ chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X f ≅
      chartModuleRestriction B S hS X V
declarations.comment: compatibility of chart restriction with the chartwise pullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartModuleGlueingData
declarations.doc:
**The data of Stacks 03LY**: a sheaf of `𝒪_U`-modules on the small étale site of every étale
scheme chart `U` of `X`, transition isomorphisms along the chartwise pullbacks of modules, and
the cocycle condition relating them.
declarations.statement: structure ChartModuleGlueingData
declarations.comment: the data (1), (2) and the cocycle condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleRestrictionComp_cocycle_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LY, the cocycle condition for the chartwise restrictions.**  For composable
morphisms `g : W ⟶ V` and `f : V ⟶ U` of étale scheme charts of `X` and an `𝒪_X`-module `F`, the
transition `c_g` of the restriction family after the chartwise pullback `g^*c_f` of the
transition `c_f` is the transition `c_{g ≫ f}`, read through the canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleInverseImageComp`.

This is the condition that `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsChartModuleCocycle` names, written out at
the family of restrictions; see the discussion in the module documentation of why the term of
that predicate's type does not follow.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartModuleRestrictionComp_cocycle_app (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    {W V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U) (g : W ⟶ V) :
    (chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X g).map
          ((chartModuleRestrictionComp B S hS X f).app F).hom ≫
        ((chartModuleRestrictionComp B S hS X g).app F).hom =
      (chartModuleInverseImageComp B S hS X f g).hom.app
          ((chartModuleRestriction B S hS X U).obj F) ≫
        ((chartModuleRestrictionComp B S hS X (g ≫ f)).app F).hom
declarations.comment: the cocycle condition for the chartwise restrictions of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isChartModuleCocycle_chartModuleRestrictionTransitionFamily
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle condition of Stacks 03LY for the chartwise restrictions of an `𝒪_X`-module, as
a term of the predicate.**  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleRestrictionTransitions_cocycle` transported from the
spelling in which it is proved to the one the predicate's instantiation produces, by
`CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp_eq_comp_of_heq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isChartModuleCocycle_chartModuleRestrictionTransitionFamily
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    IsChartModuleCocycle B S hS X (chartModuleRestrictionFamily B S hS X F)
      (chartModuleRestrictionTransitionFamily B S hS X F)
declarations.comment: the cocycle condition for the chartwise restrictions, as a term of the predicate

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalChartModuleGlueingData
declarations.doc:
**The chartwise glueing datum of an `𝒪_X`-module**: its restrictions to the étale scheme
charts of `X`, the comparisons `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleRestrictionComp` as the
transition isomorphisms, and the cocycle condition they satisfy.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalChartModuleGlueingData (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    ChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X
declarations.comment: the chartwise glueing datum of a module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleGlueingFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical chartwise description of `𝒪_X`-modules**: the functor sending an
`𝒪_X`-module to the family of its restrictions to the étale scheme charts of `X`, with the
comparisons `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleRestrictionComp` as transitions.  That this
functor is an equivalence is Stacks 03LY.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartModuleGlueingFunctor :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ⥤ ChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X
declarations.comment: the canonical chartwise description of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleGlueingEquivalence
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules on the small étale site of an algebraic space `X` is the same thing
as a family of `𝒪_U`-modules `F_U` on the small étale sites of the étale scheme charts `U` of
`X`, together with isomorphisms `c_f : f^*F_U ≅ F_V` for the morphisms `f : V ⟶ U` of charts
satisfying the cocycle condition `c_g ∘ g^*c_f = c_{g ≫ f}`: an equivalence of categories, given
by sending a module to the family of its restrictions to the charts.
declarations.statement:
def chartModuleGlueingEquivalence :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ≌ ChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X
declarations.comment: the equivalence of modules with chartwise glueing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_chartModuleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LZ.** The chartwise pullback of modules preserves quasi-coherence: a morphism of
étale scheme charts of `X` represents an étale morphism of algebraic spaces, along which the
pullback of Stacks 03LU is restriction of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_chartModuleInverseImage {V U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (chartSpace B S hS X U).1 (chartSpace B S hS X U).2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((chartModuleInverseImage B S hS X f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_chartModuleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03LZ.** An `𝒪_X`-module is quasi-coherent exactly when its restriction to every
étale scheme chart of `X` is quasi-coherent: the chartwise family of restrictions of a module
satisfies datum (1) of Stacks 03LZ precisely for the quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_chartModuleRestriction
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∀ U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        ((chartModuleRestriction B S hS X U).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of a module is quasi-coherence of its chartwise restrictions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isChartwiseQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Datum (1) of Stacks 03LZ**: the module of a chartwise glueing datum is quasi-coherent on
the small étale site of every étale scheme chart of `X`.
declarations.statement: def isChartwiseQuasicoherent : ObjectProperty (ChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X)
declarations.comment: datum (1): the chartwise modules are quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentChartModuleGlueingData
declarations.doc:
**The data of Stacks 03LZ**: a quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-module on the small étale site of every
étale scheme chart `U` of `X`, transition isomorphisms along the chartwise pullbacks, and the
cocycle condition relating them.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev QuasicoherentChartModuleGlueingData
declarations.comment: the data (1), (2) and the cocycle condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The canonical chartwise description of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules**: the functor of
Stacks 03LY cut down to the quasi-coherent objects on both sides, so that composing it with the
inclusion of the chartwise quasi-coherent data is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleGlueingFunctor` on the nose.  It is well defined because
the restriction of a quasi-coherent module to a chart is quasi-coherent, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_chartModuleRestriction`.  That this functor is an
equivalence is Stacks 03LZ, proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor_isEquivalence` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/SmallEtaleChartQuasicoherentGlueingEquivalence.lean`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ⥤ QuasicoherentChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X
declarations.comment: the canonical chartwise description of quasi-coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingEquivalence
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module on the small étale site of an algebraic space `X` is the same
thing as a chartwise quasi-coherent glueing datum: a *quasi-coherent* `𝒪_U`-module `F_U` on the
small étale site of every étale scheme chart `U` of `X`, transition isomorphisms
`c_f : f^*F_U ≅ F_V` along the chartwise pullbacks of Stacks 03LU for the morphisms `f : V ⟶ U`
of charts, and the cocycle condition `c_g ∘ g^*c_f = c_{g ≫ f}` — an *equivalence of categories*,
given by sending a quasi-coherent module to the family of its restrictions to the charts.

It is the equivalence `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartModuleGlueingEquivalence` of Stacks 03LY,
cut down to the quasi-coherent objects on both sides.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingEquivalence :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ≌ QuasicoherentChartModuleGlueingData B S hS X
declarations.comment: quasi-coherent modules are the chartwise quasi-coherent glueing data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The canonical chartwise description of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor` — restriction to the étale
scheme charts — is an equivalence onto the chartwise quasi-coherent glueing data.
declarations.statement:
instance quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor_isEquivalence :
    (quasicoherentChartModuleGlueingFunctor B S hS X).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the canonical chartwise description of quasi-coherent modules is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_over_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M0, conditions (1) and (3).** A sheaf of `𝒪_F`-modules on the small étale site
of an algebraic space `F` is quasi-coherent if and only if its restriction along one étale
chart whose structure morphism is surjective on points is quasi-coherent.

The restriction is restriction to the slice of the small étale site at the chart; see the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_over_of_isSurjective (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS U.1.hom) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔ (M.over U).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_affine_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M0, conditions (1) and (4).** A sheaf of `𝒪_F`-modules on the small étale site
of an algebraic space `F` is quasi-coherent if and only if its restriction along every étale
chart whose underlying scheme is affine is quasi-coherent.

The restriction is restriction to the slice of the small étale site at the chart; see the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_forall_affine_over (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C,
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS F).obj U)) →
        (M.over U).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_etaleModulePullback_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M0, conditions (1) and (2).** A sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules on the small étale site
of an algebraic space `X` is quasi-coherent if and only if its pullback along an étale
morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces which is surjective on points is quasi-coherent.

The forward implication needs no surjectivity: quasi-coherence of a module is inherited by
every étale pullback, because a covering of the composite chart of `X` lifts to a covering of
the chart of `Y` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale.smallEtalePostcomp_cover_lift`) and
global presentations transfer by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasGlobalPresentation_over_postcomp_iff`.  The converse is where
surjectivity enters: an étale chart of `Y` surjective on points composes with `f` to an étale
chart of `X` surjective on points, which covers the final object of the small étale site of
`X` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SmallEtale.coversTop_of_isSurjective`, so every chart of `X`
is covered by charts that map to it; those are, up to isomorphism, the composites
of the charts of `Y`, which carry global presentations by hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_etaleModulePullback_iff (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ((etaleModulePullback B S hS f hf).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_exists_etale_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M0, conditions (1) and (2), in the existential form of the source.** A sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules on the small étale site of an algebraic space `X` is quasi-coherent if and only
if there is an étale morphism `f : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces, surjective on points, whose
pullback of the module is quasi-coherent.

The witness for the forward implication is the identity of `X`, which is étale because
precomposing an étale chart with it returns the chart, and surjective on points because
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_id` is the identity.  No comparison of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtalePostcomp` with the identity functor is needed: the pullback
along the identity is quasi-coherent because
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_etaleModulePullback_iff` applies to every étale
morphism, the identity included.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_exists_etale_surjective
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : Z ⟶ X) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom),
        IsSurjective B S hS f.hom ∧
          ((etaleModulePullback B S hS f hf).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallEtaleInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1, the internal Hom.**  Let `F` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let
`M`, `N` be quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-modules with `M` of finite presentation, Stacks 03DL(7).  Then
the internal Hom `𝓗om_{𝒪_F}(M, N)` is quasi-coherent.

The internal Hom is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleInternalHom`, formed on the small étale
ringed site of `F`; its sections over an étale chart `U` are the morphisms `M|_U ⟶ N|_U`, so they
lie in `u + 1` even though those of `M` and `N` lie in `u`.

The proof is the source's.  Quasi-coherence is local on a covering of each object
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_locally_over`), the finite-presentation
hypothesis supplies for each étale chart a covering on whose members `M` has a finite global
presentation, and on such a member the conclusion is
`isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallEtaleInternalHom_over_of_hasFiniteGlobalPresentation`: restriction
to an étale chart is a localization and formation of internal Hom commutes with localization
(Stacks 04M1 and 0E8H), so the chart case is the globally presented case
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallEtaleInternalHom_of_presentation'` on the
small étale site of the chart.

The quasi-coherence of `M` is one of the source's hypotheses and is listed; the proof does not
use it, since finite presentation already implies it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_smallEtaleInternalHom (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hMfp : M.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    (smallEtaleInternalHom B S hS F hF M N).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: (6) internal hom out of a module of finite presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_left_of_shortExact'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 for short exact sequences, left term, at `m := u`, with nothing assumed.**  The
kernel term of a short exact sequence of `𝒪_F`-modules on an algebraic space is quasi-coherent if
the other two terms are.

No instance of Stacks 03DW occurs, because sections of a short exact sequence are left exact;
this is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_left_of_shortExact` with its `h03DX` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_left_of_shortExact'
    (T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (hT : T.ShortExact)
    [T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: clause (4), left term, for the small étale site of an algebraic space, at module universe u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_middle_of_shortExact'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 for short exact sequences, middle term, at `m := u`, with nothing assumed.**  An
extension of quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-modules on an algebraic space is quasi-coherent.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_middle_of_shortExact` with its `h03DX` supplied
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` and its
`T.g`-specific instance of Stacks 03DW by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_g_val_app_of_shortExact_of_isCartesian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_middle_of_shortExact'
    (T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (hT : T.ShortExact)
    [T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: clause (4), middle term, for the small étale site of an algebraic space, at module universe u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_right_of_shortExact'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 for short exact sequences, right term, at `m := u`, with nothing assumed.**  The
quotient term of a short exact sequence of `𝒪_F`-modules on an algebraic space is quasi-coherent
if the other two terms are.

Its two hypotheses are supplied as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherent_middle_of_shortExact'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_right_of_shortExact'
    (T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)) (hT : T.ShortExact)
    [T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: clause (4), right term, for the small étale site of an algebraic space, at module universe u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit_cofan
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (1).**  Any direct sum of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules on an algebraic space
`X` is quasi-coherent: the vertex of a colimiting cofan on a family of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules, indexed by an arbitrary type, is quasi-coherent.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit_cofan_of_h03DX` with Descent,
Proposition 03DX(2) supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit_cofan {ι : Type w}
    {G : ι → Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (c : Cofan G) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hG : ∀ i, (G i).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    c.pt.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: (1) any direct sum of quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-modules is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_quasicoherentSheaves_of_essentiallySmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (2).**  Any colimit of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules on an algebraic space `X`
is quasi-coherent: quasi-coherence is closed under colimits of every small shape `K`.

The shape `K` is replaced by its small model, for which this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_quasicoherentSheaves_schemeUniverse`: a
colimit is the cokernel of a map between two direct sums, and clauses (1) and (3) apply.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_quasicoherentSheaves_of_essentiallySmall (K : Type w)
    [Category.{w'} K] [EssentiallySmall.{u} K] :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape K
declarations.comment: (2) any colimit of quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-modules is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_kernel_and_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (3).**  The kernel and the cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-modules on an algebraic space `X` are quasi-coherent.
declarations.comment: (3) the kernel and the cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-modules are quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_twoOutOfThree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (4).**  Given a short exact sequence `0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` of `𝒪_X`-modules
on an algebraic space `X`, if two out of the three terms are quasi-coherent then so is the
third.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_twoOutOfThree
    {T : ShortComplex (Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)} (hT : T.ShortExact) :
    (T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite → T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite → T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
      (T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite → T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
      (T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite → T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
declarations.comment: (4) in a short exact sequence of 𝒪_X-modules, if two of the three terms are quasi-coherent so is the third

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorModule_schemeUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (5).**  The tensor product of two quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules on an algebraic
space `X` is quasi-coherent.

The tensor product is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorModule`, the sheafified objectwise tensor
product on the small étale ringed site; the two sheafification conditions it uses hold at the
universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorModule_schemeUniverse (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (tensorModule.{u, u, u} B S hS F hF M N).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: (5) the tensor product of two quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-modules is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheafSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1 (6).**  Let `𝓕`, `𝓖` be quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules on an algebraic space `X`
with `𝓕` of finite presentation (Stacks 03DL(7)).  Then the internal Hom
`𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(𝓕, 𝓖)` is quasi-coherent.

The internal Hom is the one of Stacks 03EM in `Mod(𝒪_X)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.internalHomSheafSmall`; see the module documentation.  The
quasi-coherence of `𝓕` is part of the source's statement; the argument does not use it, a module
of finite presentation being quasi-coherent.  Quasi-coherence is local on the members of a
covering family (Stacks 03DN), the charts over which `𝓕` has a finite presentation cover `X`, and
over each of them
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_over_internalHomSheafSmall` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheafSmall (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (_hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hfp : M.IsFinitePresentationOnSite) :
    letI := smallEtaleRingedSite_essentiallySmall B S hS F hF
    (RingedSite.internalHomSheafSmall (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF) M
      N).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: (6) the internal Hom 𝓗om(𝓕, 𝓖) of two quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-modules with 𝓕 of finite presentation is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M1, tensor products.**  The tensor product of two quasi-coherent `𝒪_F`-modules on
an algebraic space is quasi-coherent.

The tensor product is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorModule`, formed on the small étale ringed
site of `F`; the sections of the two factors may lie in independent universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorModule (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    (N : Modules.{u, n} B S hS F hF) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (tensorModule B S hS F hF M N).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.quasicoherentModuleOfBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M3**, the descent datum.  For a quasi-coherent module `ℱ` on a scheme `X` and a
morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` from the object scheme of a groupoid with `t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ`, the pullback
`φ^*ℱ` together with its canonical descent morphism is a quasi-coherent module on the
groupoid.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentModuleOfBase (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) :
    QuasicoherentModule G
declarations.comment: the canonical descent datum on φ^*ℱ and the two conditions of Stacks 03LI, for a target which is a scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.quasicoherentModuleOfBaseFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M3**, the functor.  Pullback along `φ` together with the canonical descent
morphism is functorial in the quasi-coherent module on the base.
declarations.comment: the functor ℱ ↦ (φ^*ℱ, α), for a target which is a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentModuleOfSpaceBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M3**, the descent datum, for a target which is an algebraic space.  For a
quasi-coherent module `ℱ` on an algebraic space `X` and a morphism `φ : U ⟶ X` from the
object space of a groupoid in algebraic spaces with `t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ`, the inverse image `φ^*ℱ`
together with its canonical transition morphism is a quasi-coherent module on the groupoid.
declarations.comment: the canonical descent datum on φ^*ℱ and the two conditions of Stacks 0441, for a target which is an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_quasicoherentFromSpaceBase
declarations.doc:
The functor `ℱ ↦ (φ^*ℱ, α)` from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules to the quasi-coherent
modules on `(U, R, s, t, c)` is an equivalence of categories, for `φ : U ⟶ X` étale with
`t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ`, `{φ}` a surjective étale covering of `X`, `φ` relatively representable, and the
arrow space the kernel pair `R = U ×_X U` with `t`, `s` the two projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_quasicoherentFromSpaceBase
    (hcov : IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun _ : Unit => G.objects.1) (fun _ => φ.hom))
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable φ.hom)
    (hpb : IsPullback G.target.hom G.source.hom φ.hom φ.hom) :
    (quasicoherentFromSpaceBase B S hS G φ hφ).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the functor QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c) is an equivalence of categories, for a target which is an algebraic space: full faithfulness and essential surjectivity at the hypotheses of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.equivalenceQuasicoherentFromSpaceBase
declarations.doc:
The equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)` whose functor is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentFromSpaceBase`, under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_quasicoherentFromSpaceBase`.
declarations.statement:
def equivalenceQuasicoherentFromSpaceBase
    (hcov : IsEtaleCovering B S hS (fun _ : Unit => G.objects.1) (fun _ => φ.hom))
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable φ.hom)
    (hpb : IsPullback G.target.hom G.source.hom φ.hom φ.hom) :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.obj X.property ≌ QuasicoherentModule B S hS G
declarations.comment: the equivalence QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c) itself, for a target which is an algebraic space, at the hypotheses of the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentFromSpaceBase
declarations.doc:
**The functor `QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)` attached to an étale `φ : U ⟶ X` with
`t ≫ φ = s ≫ φ`**: it sends a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` to `φ^*ℱ` with its canonical
transition morphism, and a morphism to its inverse image along `φ`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentFromSpaceBase :
    QuasicoherentSheaves.{u, u} B S hS X.obj X.property ⥤ QuasicoherentModule B S hS G
declarations.comment: the functor QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c) of the equivalence, for a target which is an algebraic space; this declaration is the functor itself, that it is an equivalence being proved in QuasicoherentFromSpaceBaseEquivalence.lean

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedImmersion_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M4 for closed immersions**, unconditionally.

A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion exactly when every one of its base
changes to a representable presheaf is, exactly when every one of its base changes to an affine
object of the site is, exactly when its base change along one surjective étale scheme chart of
the target is, and exactly when its base changes along the members of some Zariski covering of
the target are.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheaf_tfae` at the closed immersions, whose descent
hypothesis — Stacks 03I2 for the closed immersions of schemes — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isClosedImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_tfae
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS f,
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G),
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor G),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧
        ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f (U i).ι))
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_tfae_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an immersion exactly when every one of its base
changes to a representable presheaf is, exactly when every one of its base changes to an affine
object of the site is, exactly when its base change along one surjective étale scheme chart of
the target is, and exactly when its base changes along the members of some Zariski covering of
the target are.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isImmersion_tfae` with its hypothesis `hdesc` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isImmersion_tfae_of_isAlgebraicSpace
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsImmersion B S hS f,
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          IsImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G),
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        IsImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor G),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧
        ∀ i, IsImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f (U i).ι))
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_tfae_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M4 for open immersions**, unconditionally.

A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is an open immersion exactly when every one of its base
changes to a representable presheaf is, exactly when every one of its base changes to an affine
object of the site is, exactly when its base change along one surjective étale scheme chart of
the target is, and exactly when its base changes along the members of some Zariski covering of
the target are.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpenImmersion_tfae` with its hypothesis `hdesc` — Stacks 03I2
for open immersions — supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenImmersion_tfae_of_isAlgebraicSpace
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsOpenImmersion B S hS f,
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ G),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ G),
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) g ∧
        IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)),
      (∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor G),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧
        ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f (U i).ι))
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isVeryReasonable_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc: A quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is very reasonable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVeryReasonable_of_isQuasiSeparated (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsVeryReasonable B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isVeryReasonable_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M5, representable implies very reasonable.** A representable morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` is very reasonable: each of its represented base changes is again a
representable algebraic space, hence Zariski locally quasi-separated by the implication
`(θ) ⇒ (ζ)` of Stacks 03JX and very reasonable by `(ζ) ⇒ (ε)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isVeryReasonable_of_relativelyRepresentable (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) : IsVeryReasonable B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_of_isReasonable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M5, reasonable implies decent.** A reasonable morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` is decent: each of its represented base changes is a reasonable algebraic space,
hence satisfies property `(γ)` of Stacks 03JX by the implication `(δ) ⇒ (γ)`, which is
decency.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isReasonable (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsReasonable B S hS f) :
    IsDecent B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasPropertyBeta_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M5, decent implies property `(β)`.** A decent morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` has property `(β)`: each of its represented base changes is a decent algebraic
space, hence satisfies property `(β)` of Stacks 03JX by the implication `(γ) ⇒ (β)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPropertyBeta_of_isDecent (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsDecent B S hS f) :
    HasPropertyBeta B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonable_of_isVeryReasonable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M5, very reasonable implies reasonable.** A very reasonable morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` is reasonable.

Both conditions of Stacks 03KZ are conditions on the represented base changes of the morphism,
each of which is an algebraic space, so this is the implication
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_isVeryReasonableSpace` applied base change by
base change.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_iff_valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M6.** A quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is decent as a
morphism is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative
criterion.

A valuative square for `f` has its bottom edge `Spec R ⟶ Y`, so it is a valuative square for
the base change `X ×_Y Spec R ⟶ Spec R`, which is quasi-compact and has decent source; that
base change is universally closed, hence satisfies the existence part by Stacks 03KJ, and a
dominating extension solving the square there solves the original one after composing the lift
with the projection to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_iff_valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isDecent
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hdecent : IsDecent B S hS f) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f ↔ ValuativeCriterion.Existence f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exact_moduleChartDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M8.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `U` be a
surjective étale scheme chart of `X` with structure morphism `τ`, let `R = U ×_X U` (the
cartesian square `hR` in the spaces-étale site of `X`) with its two projections `t, s : R ⟶ U`
and structure morphism `ρ`, and put `a = τ ≫ f`, `b = ρ ≫ f`.  For every `𝒪_X`-module `F` the
sequence

`0 → f_*F → a_*(F|_U) → b_*(F|_R)`

of `𝒪_Y`-modules, whose first arrow is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleChartDirectImageUnitArrow`
and whose second arrow is the difference `t^* - s^*` of the two arrows
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleChartDirectImageParallelArrow`, is exact: the short complex is
exact and its first arrow is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_moduleChartDirectImage (hU : IsSurjective B S hS U.1.hom) {t s : R ⟶ U}
    (hR : IsPullback ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map t) ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map s)
      ((SpacesEtale.isTerminal_idObj B S hS X).from ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U))
      ((SpacesEtale.isTerminal_idObj B S hS X).from ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U)))
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (ShortComplex.mk
        (moduleChartDirectImageUnitArrow B S hS f ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U).2 F)
        (moduleChartDirectImageParallelArrow B S hS f ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U).2
            (isEtale_chartMap B S hS X t) ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj R).2
            (Over.w ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map t).hom) F -
          moduleChartDirectImageParallelArrow B S hS f ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U).2
            (isEtale_chartMap B S hS X s) ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj R).2
            (Over.w ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).map s).hom) F)
        (moduleChartDirectImage_comp_sub_eq_zero B S hS f t s F)).Exact ∧
      Mono (moduleChartDirectImageUnitArrow B S hS f ((comparisonFunctor B S hS X).obj U).2 F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M9 along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.**  The direct image `i_*G` of a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module along a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` is quasi-coherent.

A closed immersion is representable and affine, so its direct image is computed on base-changed
charts by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePushforwardChartIso` and that one is cartesian on affine
charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1 Z.2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePushforward B S hS i).obj G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the direct image along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03M9.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`.  Then the direct image `f_*F` of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` is
quasi-coherent.

Quasi-coherence of `f_*F` is tested on the affine étale charts `V` of `Y`, over which `f_*F`
restricts to the direct image along the base change `V ×_Y X ⟶ V` of the restriction of `F`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforward_isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_forall_affine_chart`); that base
change is quasi-separated with quasi-compact source, and the affine-base case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_affine_target`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_qcqs (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (quasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (F_qcoh : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closedImmersion_quasicoherentIdeal_correspondence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MB.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`.

1. For every closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces the direct image `i_*𝒪_Z` is a
   quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, the map `i♯ : 𝒪_X ⟶ i_*𝒪_Z` is surjective — locally surjective as
   a map of sheaves of rings, and an epimorphism of `𝒪_X`-modules — and its kernel is a
   quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.
2. The rule `Z ↦ 𝓘_Z = Ker(𝒪_X ⟶ i_*𝒪_Z)`, with `i` the inclusion of `Z`, is an
   inclusion-reversing bijection from the closed subspaces of `X` onto the quasi-coherent sheaves
   of ideals of `𝒪_X`.
3. If `Z` corresponds to `𝓘 = 𝓘_Z`, a morphism `h : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces factors through
   `Z` if and only if the map `h^*𝓘 ⟶ h^*𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedImmersion_quasicoherentIdeal_correspondence :
    (∀ {Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (i : Z ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom →
      (structureSheafPushforward B S hS i).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (structureSharp B S hS i) ∧
        Epi (pushforwardStructureProjection B S hS i) ∧
        (SheafOfModules.Submodule.ker
          (pushforwardStructureProjection B S hS i)).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
    (∀ Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z = SheafOfModules.Submodule.ker
        (pushforwardStructureProjection B S hS (ObjectProperty.homMk Z.1.ι :
          (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ X))) ∧
    Set.BijOn (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X) Set.univ
      {I | I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite} ∧
    (∀ Z W : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1,
      Z ≤ W ↔ definingIdealSheaf B S hS X W ≤ definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z) ∧
    ∀ (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (h : Y ⟶ X),
      (∃ g : Y ⟶ (⟨Z.1.toFunctor, Z.2.1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS),
          g ≫ ObjectProperty.homMk Z.1.ι = h) ↔
        (modulePullback B S hS h).map (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z).ι ≫
          (modulePullbackUnitIso B S hS h).hom = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.surjective_iff_pointsMap_surjective_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MD.** A representable morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is
surjective — surjective after every representable base change — if and only if the induced map
on points is surjective.

No algebraic-space hypothesis is needed: representability of the morphism, which is part of
surjectivity in the relative sense, is the only one used.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_iff_pointsMap_surjective_of_representable
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ↔
      Function.Surjective (pointsMap B S hS F f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSurjective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *surjective* when the induced map `|X| → |Y|` on
their sets of points is surjective.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsSurjective (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsSurjective B S hS f,
        ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
          ∀ g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y, IsSurjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧
            IsSurjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
          IsSurjective B S hS φ ∧ IsEtale B S hS φ ∧ IsSurjective B S hS (φ ≫ f),
        ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (ψ : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y)
            (h : yoneda.obj U ⟶ yoneda.obj V),
          φ ≫ f = h ≫ ψ ∧ IsSurjective B S hS φ ∧ IsEtale B S hS φ ∧
            IsSurjective B S hS ψ ∧ IsEtale B S hS ψ ∧ IsSurjective B S hS h,
