        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧
          ∀ i, IsSurjective B S hS (pullback.snd f (U i).ι)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_comp
declarations.doc: A composite of morphisms surjective on points is surjective on points.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a morphism of algebraic spaces surjective on points is surjective on
points.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.presheafImpliesHoldsOnEveryEtaleChart_of_etale_precomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MJ, condition (1) from the represented base changes.** A property `P` of scheme
morphisms which survives composition with an étale morphism in front of it holds on every étale
chart of a morphism of presheaves all of whose represented base changes have `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem presheafImpliesHoldsOnEveryEtaleChart_of_etale_precomp (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hP : ∀ {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ Y) (p : Y ⟶ Z), Etale i → P p → P (i ≫ p)) :
    PresheafImpliesHoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P
declarations.comment: condition (1) from the represented base changes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_surjectiveChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MJ**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2). A property of morphisms of
schemes which is étale local on the source and target holds on every commuting square of étale
charts of a morphism of algebraic spaces exactly when it holds on one such square whose chart
of the source is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_surjectiveChart
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G) :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f ↔ HoldsOnSurjectiveEtaleChart B S hS P f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MJ** for a morphism of representable presheaves: a property of morphisms of
schemes which is étale local on the source and target holds on every commuting square of étale
charts of the morphism exactly when it holds of the morphism of schemes read off the canonical
representations of source and target.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_representable
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    [F.IsRepresentable] [G.IsRepresentable] (f : F ⟶ G) :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f ↔
      P ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
        (yoneda.preimage (F.reprW.hom ≫ f ≫ G.reprW.inv)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_relative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MJ** for a representable morphism of algebraic spaces: when `P` is in addition
stable under base change and local on the base for the fppf topology, the every-chart condition
is exactly the relative morphism property of the inverse image of `P`, that is, `P` holds of
every represented base change of the morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_iff_relative
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange]
    [P.IsLocalAtTarget Scheme.fppfPrecoverage]
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f) :
    HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f ↔
      (P.inverseImage (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f

declarations.name: RingHom.Flat.faithfullyFlat_of_isLocalHom
declarations.doc: A flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_of_isLocalHom {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsLocalRing S] {f : R →+* S} (hf : f.Flat) [IsLocalHom f] : f.FaithfullyFlat
declarations.comment: section tag: a flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.faithfullyFlat_etaleLocalRingMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical homomorphism of étale local rings `𝒪_{G, f ∘ x} ⟶ 𝒪_{F, x}` induced by a flat
morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of algebraic spaces at a geometric point `x` of its source is faithfully
flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_etaleLocalRingMap {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS F) :
    (etaleLocalRingMap hF f x).FaithfullyFlat
declarations.comment: section tag: the étale local ring map of a flat morphism is faithfully flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlat
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *flat* when the morphism of schemes underlying every
commuting square of étale scheme charts of it is flat.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlat (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFlatAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03ML, part (2).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *flat at* a point `x`
of its source when the morphism of germs it induces in every pointed étale scheme chart at `x`
is flat on local rings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFlatAt (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) (x : points B S hS F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_tfae
declarations.doc:
Nine criteria for a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` to be flat: pointwise flatness,
flatness of every base change to a scheme or to an affine scheme or to one surjective étale chart
of the target, flatness of the composite with one surjective étale chart of the source, flatness
of the morphism of schemes in every — or in one surjective — commuting square of étale charts, or
over a pair of Zariski coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsFlat B S hS f,
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, IsFlatAt B S hS f x,
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) → IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y),
        IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ IsEtale B S hS g ∧ IsFlat B S hS (pullback.fst g f),
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS p ∧ IsFlat B S hS (p ≫ f),
      ∀ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS q → p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q →
          IsFlat B S hS (yoneda.map a),
      ∃ (U V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X) (q : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y) (a : U ⟶ V),
        IsEtale B S hS p ∧ IsEtale B S hS q ∧ IsSurjective B S hS p ∧
          p ≫ f = yoneda.map a ≫ q ∧ IsFlat B S hS (yoneda.map a),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (Yopen : I → Subfunctor Y) (J : I → Type u)
        (Xopen : ∀ i, J i → Subfunctor (pullback f (Yopen i).ι)),
        IsZariskiCover B S hS I Yopen ∧ (∀ i, IsZariskiCover B S hS (J i) (Xopen i)) ∧
          ∀ i j, IsFlat B S hS ((Xopen i j).ι ≫ pullback.snd f (Yopen i).ι)
    ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_comp
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03MN.** A composition of flat morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_comp
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hH : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS H)
    (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ H)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g) :
    IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03MO.** Flatness of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` is stable
under base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_isStableUnderBaseChange :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) => IsFlat B S hS f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFpqcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MQ.** A family of flat morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with common
target `Y` is an *fpqc covering* when, for every affine object `T` of the big fppf site of
`S` and every morphism `h : T ⟶ Y`, there is a finite family of affine objects over `T`
which is an fpqc covering of `T` and refines the family pulled back along `h`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFpqcCovering {I : Type v} {X : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFpqcCovering_pullback
declarations.doc:
Pulling an fpqc covering family of algebraic spaces over `S`
back along a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces gives an fpqc covering of `X`: the second
projections of the fibre products of Stacks 02X2 form an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFpqcCovering_pullback
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} {Y X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Yi : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (g : ∀ i, Yi i ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hg : IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i => (g i).hom)) :
    IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i => pullback.snd (g i).hom f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFpqcCovering_of_isIso
declarations.doc:
An isomorphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, regarded as a family indexed by a
point, is an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFpqcCovering_of_isIso
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G) [IsIso f] :
    IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun _ : PUnit.{v + 1} => f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFpqcCovering_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MR**, the composition clause. Composing an fpqc covering of an algebraic space
over `S` with fpqc coverings of each of its members gives an fpqc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFpqcCovering_comp
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type v} {J : I → Type w}
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {Xi : I → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {Xij : (Σ i, J i) → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXi : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i))
    (hXij : ∀ (i : I) (j : J i), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xij ⟨i, j⟩))
    (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (g : ∀ (i : I) (j : J i), Xij ⟨i, j⟩ ⟶ Xi i)
    (hf : IsFpqcCovering B S hS f)
    (hg : ∀ i, IsFpqcCovering B S hS (g i)) :
    IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun ij : Σ i, J i => g ij.1 ij.2 ≫ f ij.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFpqcCovering_iff_pullback_atlas
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with target `X` is an
fpqc covering exactly when its pullback along a surjective étale morphism `a : U ⟶ X` from a
scheme in the site is an fpqc covering of `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFpqcCovering_iff_pullback_atlas
    {I : Type v} {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Xi : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj)
    (ha_surj : IsSurjective B S hS a) (ha_etale : IsEtale B S hS a) :
    IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i ↦ (f i).hom) ↔
      IsFpqcCovering B S hS (fun i ↦ pullback.fst a (f i).hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_iff_injective_on_field_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MU.** A representable transformation is universally injective if and only if
its maps on field-valued points are injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_iff_injective_on_field_points
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : F ⟶ G) (ha : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable a) :
    (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyInjective : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)) a ↔
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (T : BigFppfOver B S hS),
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T ≅ Spec (.of K)) →
      Function.Injective (a.app (Opposite.op T)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.UniversallyInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MV.** A morphism is universally injective if every base change along an
algebraic space induces an injective map on points.
declarations.statement: abbrev UniversallyInjective {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MW.** A base change of a universally injective morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` is universally injective.

Nothing is needed beyond unwinding the definition: a base change of `Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` along
`k : W ⟶ Z` is a base change of `X ⟶ Y` along `k ≫ g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hf : UniversallyInjective B S hS f) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS (pullback.fst g f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MW** for an arbitrary cartesian square: if `IsPullback a b g f` and `f` is
universally injective, then so is `a`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_pullback` composed with the
identification of the given square with the canonical fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_isPullback (hC : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS C)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T) (f : C ⟶ T) (g : Z ⟶ T)
    (hf : UniversallyInjective B S hS f) {a : A ⟶ Z} {b : A ⟶ C}
    (hpb : IsPullback a b g f) : UniversallyInjective B S hS a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MX.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` the
following are equivalent: `f` is universally injective; the base change `Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` of `f`
along every morphism from a scheme over `S` is universally injective; the same for every
morphism from an affine scheme over `S`; the same for one morphism from a scheme over `S`
which is surjective; and the base change of `f` along each member of some Zariski covering of
`Y` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_tfae {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyInjective B S hS f,
        ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
          UniversallyInjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∀ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
          IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Z) →
            UniversallyInjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∃ (Z : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Y),
          IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ UniversallyInjective B S hS (pullback.snd f g),
        ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → Subfunctor Y), IsZariskiCover B S hS I U ∧
          ∀ i, UniversallyInjective B S hS (pullback.snd f (U i).ι)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyInjective_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03MY.** A composition of universally injective morphisms of algebraic spaces over
`S` is universally injective.

The base change `W ×_Z X ⟶ W` of the composite along `k : W ⟶ Z` is identified by the pasting
isomorphism `W ×_Z X ≅ (W ×_Z Y) ×_Y X` with the composition of a base change of `X ⟶ Y` and a
base change of `Y ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_comp (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : UniversallyInjective B S hS f) (hg : UniversallyInjective B S hS g) :
    UniversallyInjective B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_isOpen_preimage_eq_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03N0.** Let `{f i : X i ⟶ T}` be an fpqc covering of schemes and let `W i` be an
open subset of `X i` for each `i`, such that the two projections of `X i ×_T X j` pull `W i` and
`W j` back to the same open subset for all `i` and `j`. Then there is a unique open subset `V`
of `T` whose inverse image in `X i` is `W i` for every `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isOpen_preimage_eq_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage {I : Type v} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (X : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T)
    (W : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
    (hW : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (f i) (f j) ⁻¹ᵁ W i = pullback.snd (f i) (f j) ⁻¹ᵁ W j) :
    ∃! V : T.Opens, ∀ i, f i ⁻¹ᵁ V = W i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_isOpen_preimage_eq_of_flat_of_quasiCompact_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**An open subset descends along a surjective flat quasi-compact morphism.** Let
`f : T' ⟶ T` be a surjective, flat, quasi-compact morphism of schemes and let `W' ⊆ T'` be open
with `pr₀⁻¹(W') = pr₁⁻¹(W')` in `T' ×_T T'`. Then there is a unique open `W ⊆ T` with
`W' = f⁻¹(W)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isOpen_preimage_eq_of_flat_of_quasiCompact_of_surjective {W' : Set T'}
    (hW' : IsOpen W')
    (hcompat : (pullback.fst f f).base ⁻¹' W' = (pullback.snd f f).base ⁻¹' W') :
    ∃! W : Set T, IsOpen W ∧ f.base ⁻¹' W = W'
declarations.comment: covering by a single surjective flat quasi-compact morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_opens_preimage_eq_of_flat_of_quasiCompact_of_surjective
declarations.doc:

`f : T' ⟶ T` surjective, flat and quasi-compact, an open subscheme `W'` of `T'` whose two
preimages in `T' ×_T T'` agree is the preimage of a unique open subscheme of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_opens_preimage_eq_of_flat_of_quasiCompact_of_surjective (W' : T'.Opens)
    (hcompat : (pullback.fst f f).base ⁻¹' (W' : Set T') =
      (pullback.snd f f).base ⁻¹' (W' : Set T')) :
    ∃! W : T.Opens, f ⁻¹ᵁ W = W'
declarations.comment: covering by a single surjective flat quasi-compact morphism, as open subschemes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.FamilyPlusValue
declarations.doc: The colimit of zeroth Čech cohomology over covering families of `U`.
declarations.statement: abbrev FamilyPlusValue

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.familyPlusEquiv
declarations.doc:
The covering-family colimit is canonically equivalent to the value of Mathlib's
covering-sieve plus construction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def familyPlusEquiv :
    FamilyPlusValue J F U ≃ (J.plusObj F).obj (op U)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.familyPlusPresheaf
declarations.doc: The presheaf whose values are the covering-family colimits of zeroth Čech cohomology.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def familyPlusPresheaf : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.familyPlusEquiv_mk
declarations.doc:
On every representative, the comparison sends a matching family to the same matching
family on the generated covering sieve, and then to its colimit class. This characterizes the
comparison independently of any choices made in extending a family to its generated sieve.
declarations.statement:
theorem familyPlusEquiv_mk
    (E : J.toPrecoverage.ZeroHypercover.{u} U)
    (s : PreZeroHypercover.H0 F E.toPreZeroHypercover) :
    familyPlusEquiv J F U
        (Quotient.mk (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (FamilyPlusRelated J F U)) ⟨E, s⟩) =
      GrothendieckTopology.Plus.mk (familyMatchingFamily J F U E s)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.familyPlusPresheaf_map_mk
declarations.doc:
Restriction is induced by pulling back matching families. Any morphism of covering
families over the base morphism computes the same restriction; thus this includes the
canonical fibre-product covering without requiring a choice of fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem familyPlusPresheaf_map_mk {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U)
    (E : J.toPrecoverage.ZeroHypercover.{u} U)
    (G : J.toPrecoverage.ZeroHypercover.{u} V)
    (φ : G.toPreZeroHypercover.HomOver E.toPreZeroHypercover f)
    (s : PreZeroHypercover.H0 F E.toPreZeroHypercover) :
    (familyPlusPresheaf J F).map f.op
        (equivShrink (FamilyPlusValue J F U)
          (Quotient.mk (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (FamilyPlusRelated J F U)) ⟨E, s⟩)) =
      equivShrink (FamilyPlusValue J F V)
        (Quotient.mk (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (FamilyPlusRelated J F V))
          ⟨G, PreZeroHypercover.H0.mapOver F φ s⟩)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_common_refinement
declarations.doc: Covering families form a directed system under refinement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_refinement
    (E G : J.toPrecoverage.ZeroHypercover.{u} U) :
    ∃ H : J.toPrecoverage.ZeroHypercover.{u} U,
      Nonempty (H.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom E.toPreZeroHypercover) ∧
        Nonempty (H.toPreZeroHypercover.Hom G.toPreZeroHypercover)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.smallFamilyPlusEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc: The comparison commutes with restriction maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallFamilyPlusEquiv_naturality {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (familyPlusPresheaf J F).map f ≫ (smallFamilyPlusEquiv J F Y.unop).toIso.hom =
      (smallFamilyPlusEquiv J F X.unop).toIso.hom ≫ (J.plusObj F).map f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.toFamilyPlusNatTrans_app
declarations.doc: The canonical presheaf map is pointwise the map defined by the identity covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem toFamilyPlusNatTrans_app (x : F.obj (op U)) :
    (toFamilyPlusNatTrans J F).app (op U) x = toSmallFamilyPlus J F U x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.singleton_specMap_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03NY.** The singleton family of affine schemes induced by a
ring homomorphism is an fpqc covering if and only if the homomorphism is faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem singleton_specMap_mem_fpqcPrecoverage_iff_faithfullyFlat
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) :
    Presieve.singleton (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f)) ∈
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (Spec (.of A)) ↔ f.FaithfullyFlat

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03NY.** The family `{D(x) ⟶ 𝐀²_k, D(y) ⟶ 𝐀²_k,
Spec k[[x, y]] ⟶ 𝐀²_k}` is an fpqc covering of the affine plane.
declarations.statement:
theorem presieve₀_affinePlanePowerSeriesCover_mem_fpqcPrecoverage :
    (affinePlaneCover k ⟨Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k)))⟩).presieve₀ ∈
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.presieve₀_affinePlaneLocalRingCover_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03NY.** The family `{D(x) ⟶ 𝐀²_k, D(y) ⟶ 𝐀²_k,
Spec 𝒪_{𝐀²_k, 0} ⟶ 𝐀²_k}` is an fpqc covering of the affine plane.
declarations.statement:
theorem presieve₀_affinePlaneLocalRingCover_mem_fpqcPrecoverage :
    (affinePlaneCover k
        ⟨Spec ((Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k))).presheaf.stalk
            (affineOrigin k 2)),
          (Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k))).fromSpecStalk
            (affineOrigin k 2)⟩).presieve₀ ∈
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage (Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_and_surjective_sigmaFromSpecStalk_polynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03NY.** The morphism `φ : ∐_{x ∈ 𝐀¹_k} Spec 𝒪_{𝐀¹_k, x} ⟶ 𝐀¹_k`,
where `k` is a field, is flat and surjective. This is the positive half of the example; the

      Surjective (sigmaFromSpecStalk (Spec (.of (Polynomial k))))

morphism is flat and surjective.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isSheaf_fpqc_iff_zariski_and_affine_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03O1.** A presheaf on schemes over `S` is an fpqc
sheaf if and only if it is a Zariski sheaf and satisfies the singleton sheaf
condition for faithfully flat morphisms between affine schemes over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_fpqc_iff_zariski_and_affine_singleton
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) F ↔
      (Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S) F ∧
        ∀ {R T : CommRingCat.{u}} (f : R ⟶ T) (g : Spec R ⟶ S)
          [Flat (Spec.map f)] [Surjective (Spec.map f)],
          Presieve.IsSheafFor F
            (.singleton (Over.homMk (Spec.map f) rfl :
              Over.mk (Spec.map f ≫ g) ⟶ Over.mk g)))

declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDifferentialsPresheaf_not_isSheaf_fpqc (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    ¬ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over (Spec (.of (ZMod p))))
      (relativeDifferentialsPresheaf (Spec (.of (ZMod p)))).functor

**The syntomic comparison of Tag 03O4.** The fpqc topology is finer than the syntomic
topology.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_zariski_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** An fpqc sheaf on the schemes over `S` is a Zariski sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_etale_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** An fpqc sheaf on the schemes over `S` is an étale sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_smooth_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** An fpqc sheaf on the schemes over `S` is a smooth sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_smooth_of_isSheaf_fpqc (S : Scheme.{u}) (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf
      ((Scheme.grothendieckTopology (@Smooth : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})).over S) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_syntomic_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** An fpqc sheaf on the schemes over `S` is a syntomic sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_syntomic_of_isSheaf_fpqc (S : Scheme.{u}) (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf
      ((Scheme.grothendieckTopology (@Syntomic : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})).over S) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fppf_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** An fpqc sheaf on the schemes over `S` is an fppf sheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_chosenSmallEtale_of_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03O4.** Restriction of an fpqc sheaf to a chosen small étale site is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_chosenSmallEtale_of_isSheaf_fpqc
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
      ((SmallEtale.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Over.post (X := B.obj S hS) B.inclusion).op ⋙ F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.etaleTopology_le_fpqcTopology
declarations.doc: The étale topology is coarser than the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleTopology_le_fpqcTopology :
    Scheme.etaleTopology.{u} ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupBaseChangeYonedaIsoBigStructurePresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03O5.** The natural bijection `Mor_S(T, 𝐆_{a,S}) ≃ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`, as an isomorphism
of presheaves of sets on the schemes over `S`: the presheaf represented by the additive group
scheme over `S` is the presheaf of global regular functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveGroupBaseChangeYonedaIsoBigStructurePresheaf (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    yoneda.obj (Scheme.asOver (additiveGroupBaseChange S) S) ≅
      Scheme.bigStructurePresheaf S ⋙ forget CommRingCat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqc_bigStructurePresheaf_forget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03O5.** The presheaf of sets `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` on the schemes over `S` satisfies
the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology: it is represented by the additive group scheme over
`S`, and the fpqc topology on the schemes over `S` is subcanonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fpqc_bigStructurePresheaf_forget (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    Presieve.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u}.over S)
      (Scheme.bigStructurePresheaf S ⋙ forget CommRingCat)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isSheaf_fpqc_bigStructurePresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03O5.** The presheaf of *rings* `𝒪 : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Rings`, `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`,
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology on the schemes over `S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_Γ` restricted along the forgetful functor
`Sch/S ⥤ Sch`, which is continuous from the localized fpqc topology to the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.isSheaf_fpqc_bigStructurePresheaf (S : Scheme.{u}) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u}.over S) (Scheme.bigStructurePresheaf S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A quasicoherent descent datum is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent
datum of a quasicoherent module on the target.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEffective (D : QuasicoherentDescentData f) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentDescentData.isEffective_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
Every quasi-coherent descent datum for an fpqc covering family of an arbitrary scheme is
effective, at an arbitrary index universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_fpqcPrecoverage {S : Scheme.{u}} (𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{v} S)
    (h𝒰 : 𝒰.presieve₀ ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S) (D : QuasicoherentDescentData 𝒰.f) :
    D.IsEffective
declarations.comment: effectivity of all quasi-coherent descent data for an fpqc covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023M.** For a faithfully flat algebra `A` over a commutative ring `R` and an
arbitrary `R`-module `M`, the extended Amitsur cochain complex
`M → A ⊗[R] M → (A ⊗[R] A) ⊗[R] M → ⋯`
is exact in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.Descent.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023M.** For a faithfully flat algebra `A` over a commutative ring `R` and an
arbitrary `R`-module `M`, the extended Amitsur cochain complex
`M → A ⊗[R] M → (A ⊗[R] A) ⊗[R] M → ⋯`
is exact in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 023M**, and **Stacks Lemma 03OA**.  The extended Amitsur cochain complex of a
faithfully flat algebra is exact for every module of coefficients.  Exactness of the extended
complex `M → A ⊗[R] M → A ⊗[R] A ⊗[R] M → ⋯` says both that the unaugmented complex is exact in
positive degrees and that its degree-zero cohomology is `M`, which is the form 03OA states.
declarations.statement:
theorem amitsurExtendedCochainComplex_acyclic_of_faithfullyFlat
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) (M : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R A] :
    (amitsurExtendedCochainComplex R A M).Acyclic

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData
declarations.doc:
A descent datum for modules for an `R`-algebra `A`.

The transition is bundled as an `A ⊗[R] A`-linear equivalence, and `cocycle` is the equality
`φ₁₂ ∘ φ₀₁ = φ₀₂`.
declarations.statement: structure DescentData
declarations.comment: descent datum for a module along a ring map

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData.IsEffective
declarations.doc:
A module descent datum is effective if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum
obtained by extending scalars from an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
abbrev DescentData.IsEffective (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R A] (D : DescentData.{u, v, w} R A) : Prop
declarations.comment: effectivity of a module descent datum

declarations.name: ModuleCat.DescentData.isEffective_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 023N, part (1).** Every descent datum for modules along a faithfully flat ring map
`R → A` is effective: it is isomorphic, as a descent datum, to the canonical datum on the
extension of scalars of an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem DescentData.isEffective_of_faithfullyFlat
    (D : DescentData.{u, u, max u w} R A) : D.IsEffective R A
declarations.comment: descent data for modules along a faithfully flat ring map are effective

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.fpqcAssociatedPresheafOfModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OG**, first assertion.  The presheaf
`Fᵃ : (f : T ⟶ S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺ F)` attached to a quasi-coherent module `F` on `S` is a module over
the structure presheaf `𝒪` of the big fpqc site of `S`: the sections of `f⁺ F` over `T` form a
module over `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`, and the restriction maps of `Fᵃ` are semilinear over those of `𝒪`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fpqcAssociatedPresheafOfModules :
    PresheafOfModules.{u} (fpqcStructurePresheaf S)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isSheaf_fpqcAssociatedPresheafOfModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OG**, second assertion.  The presheaf
`Fᵃ : (f : T ⟶ S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺ F)` attached to a quasi-coherent module `F` on `S` satisfies the
sheaf condition for the fpqc topology on the schemes over `S`.
declarations.comment: the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_of_isTerminal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03OI.** On a site with a final object `S`, the defining condition of Stacks 03OH
for quasi-coherence of a sheaf of modules need only be checked at `U = S`: the module is
quasi-coherent if and only if some covering of `S` admits a global presentation of the module
on each of its members.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_of_isTerminal (M : SheafOfModules.{m} R)
    {S : C} (hS : IsTerminal S) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ S),
        Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J S ∧ ∀ i, (M.over (V i)).HasGlobalPresentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.isSheaf_structurePresheaf_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**The presheaf `𝒪` is a sheaf on a site of schemes over `S` whose coverings are fpqc
coverings of schemes.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_structurePresheaf_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf K.toGrothendieck (structurePresheaf S toOver)
declarations.comment: the structure presheaf is a sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.isSheaf_structurePresheaf_and_exists_iso_siteAssociatedModule
declarations.doc:
Let a site of schemes over `S` be presented by a precoverage `K` on a category
`C` and a functor `toOver : C ⥤ Over S`, satisfying the site axioms of Stacks 00VH (isomorphisms,
composites and base changes of coverings are coverings, the base changes being fibre products in
`C` along covering arrows) and the four conditions of the tag: (1) `toOver` is fully faithful and
`C` is essentially small; (2) every Zariski covering of the underlying scheme of an object is
refined by a covering of the site; (3) `S/S` is an object of the site; (4) every covering of the
site is an fpqc covering of schemes.  Assume that the fibre products of the site along covering
arrows are fibre products of schemes.  Then the presheaf `𝒪` is a sheaf, and every quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-module `M` is isomorphic to `Fᵃ` for a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_structurePresheaf_and_exists_iso_siteAssociatedModule
    (hTerminal : ∃ T : C, Nonempty (toOver.obj T ≅ Over.mk (𝟙 S))) :
    ∃ hR : Presheaf.IsSheaf K.toGrothendieck (structurePresheaf S toOver),
      ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (siteStructureSheaf S toOver K.toGrothendieck hR)),
        M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite →
        ∃ (F : S.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent),
          Nonempty (M ≅ siteAssociatedModule S F toOver K.toGrothendieck hR
            (isSheaf_associatedPresheaf_of_preservesCoveringFibreProducts K toOver hfpqc hpres
              F))
declarations.comment: both assertions: O is a sheaf and every quasi-coherent O-module is F^a for a quasi-coherent F on S. Corrected form: the source's statement is false when the fibre products of the site along coverings are not fibre products of schemes (not_isSheaf_structurePresheaf_counterexample), so that is assumed (PreservesCoveringFibreProducts), as the source's sites of schemes form fibre products in Sch/S. Condition (1) is fullness, faithfulness and essential smallness; the site axioms are Stacks 00VH

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplex
declarations.doc:
The Čech complex associated to an additive presheaf and a family of morphisms with fixed
target whose finite nonempty fibre products exist.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev cechComplex
    {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [HasProducts.{w} A] [Preadditive A]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))]
    (F : CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ A) : CochainComplex A ℕ
declarations.comment: the Čech complex of an abelian presheaf along a family with fixed target

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology
declarations.doc:
The degree-`n` Čech cohomology object of a presheaf with respect to a family of morphisms
with fixed target. For abelian-group-valued presheaves this is the Čech cohomology group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev cechCohomology
    {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] [HasProducts.{w} A] [Abelian A]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))]
    (F : CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ A) (n : ℕ) : A
declarations.comment: the Čech cohomology groups, as the cohomology of the Čech complex

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexFunctor_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OM.** The Čech complex functor of Stacks 03OL is exact on the
category `PAb(C)` of abelian presheaves on `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechComplexFunctor_exact
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀),
      HasProduct (fun a ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i a)))] :
    exactFunctor
      (CategoryTheory.Functor Cᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb})
      (CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb} ℕ)
      (cechComplexFunctor (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max w uAb}) E)

registrations.name: PresheafOfModules.freeObj
registrations.comment: Z_G(U) = Z[G(U)]: the free presheaf of modules on G, over the constant presheaf of rings Z (Z_U is the case G = h_U)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.homIntegralCechComplex_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03OP.** The differential of the complex of maps out of the integral Čech complex is
the alternating sum of the maps induced by the face maps of the simplicial formal coproduct of
fibre products, that is, of the maps which repeat one of the indices.
declarations.statement:
theorem homIntegralCechComplex_d (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a}) (n : ℕ) :
    ((homComplexFunctor (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E)).obj F).d n (n + 1) =
      ∑ j : Fin (n + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) •
        (preadditiveYoneda.obj F).map
          ((integralCechRealization.{w, v, u, a} (X := X)).map
            ((cechSimplicialObject E).δ j)).op

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexIsoHomIntegralCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03OP.** The Čech complex of an abelian presheaf `F` is the complex of maps out of
the integral Čech complex of Stacks 03OQ, naturally in `F`. This is the second of the two
displays of 03OP, and it is the Hom identification of Stacks 03AS; the values of the Čech
complex are lifted to the universe in which maps of abelian presheaves live.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechComplexIsoHomIntegralCechComplex :
    liftedCechComplexFunctor.{w, v, u, a} E ≅
      homComplexFunctor (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E)
declarations.comment: the identification of the Čech complex with maps out of the integral complex

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.homIntegralCechComplexXIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03OP.** The degree-`n` term of the complex of maps out of the integral Čech complex
is the product, over `(n+1)`-tuples `i` of indices, of the groups of maps from the free abelian
presheaf on the fibre product `U_{i 0} ×_U ⋯ ×_U U_{i n}` to `F`. This is the first of the two
displays of 03OP.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homIntegralCechComplexXIso (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max v a}) (n : ℕ) :
    ((homComplexFunctor (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E)).obj F).X n ≅
      ((∏ᶜ (fun i : Fin (n + 1) → E.I₀ ↦ AddCommGrpCat.of
        (freeAbelianYoneda.{v, u, a}.obj ((∏ᶜ (fun b ↦ Over.mk (E.f (i b)))).left) ⟶ F)) :
          AddCommGrpCat.{max u v a}))

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexIsoHomIntegralCechComplexObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03OP.** When the coefficient universe contains the universe of objects of `C`, so
that the groups of maps of abelian presheaves lie in the coefficient universe too, the Čech
complex of `F` itself -- and not merely a universe lift of it -- is the complex of maps out of
the integral Čech complex.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechComplexIsoHomIntegralCechComplexObj
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v a}) :
    cechComplex E F ≅
      (homComplexFunctor (integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, max u a} E)).obj F
declarations.comment: the identification for the Čech complex itself

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.integralCechComplex_homology_isZero
declarations.doc:
The homology presheaves of the integral Čech chain complex vanish in every positive degree:
the complex of abelian presheaves is exact in all degrees except `0`. The degree-`0` term of
`integralCechComplex` is `⊕_{i₀} Z_{U_{i₀}}`, so the hypothesis `0 < n` is exactly "all degrees
except `0`", and nothing is asserted at `n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem integralCechComplex_homology_isZero (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((integralCechComplex.{w, v, u, a} E).homology n)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.injective_presheaf_cechCohomology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OR.** The positive-degree Čech cohomology of an injective
presheaf of abelian groups vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_presheaf_cechCohomology_isZero (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (cechCohomology E I p)

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyIsoRightDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AU.** For each `n`, the natural isomorphism `ČH ⁿ(E, -) ≅ R ⁿ(ČH ⁰(E, -))` of
functors on abelian presheaves.

This is also [Stacks Project, Tag 03OS], the Étale Cohomology chapter's form of the same
statement: on abelian presheaves the functors `Ȟ ᵖ(U, -)` are the right derived functors of
`Ȟ ⁰(U, -)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechCohomologyIsoRightDerived (n : ℕ) :
    cechComplexFunctor E ⋙
        HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max w u v a} (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n ≅
      cechCohomologyRightDerived.{w, v, a, u} E n

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.existsUnique_cechCohomologyDeltaFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03AU.** Čech cohomology is canonically isomorphic, as a cohomological δ-functor, to
the higher right derived functors of degree-zero Čech cohomology. The isomorphism is unique with
its prescribed degree-zero component.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_cechCohomologyDeltaFunctorIso :
    ∃! e : (cechCohomologyDeltaFunctor.{w, v, max u v a, u} E).1 ≅
        (rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E).1,
      e.hom.app 0 = (cechH0IsoRightDerivedPlusZero.{w, v, a, u} E).1.hom ≫
        eqToHom ((rightDerivedCechDeltaFunctor.{w, v, a, u} E).2.1 0).symm

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.sheafToPresheaf_preservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.doc: The inclusion of sheaves into presheaves preserves injective objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafToPresheaf_preservesInjectiveObjects {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type u') [Category.{v'} A] [HasSheafify J A] :
    (sheafToPresheaf J A).PreservesInjectiveObjects
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor from sheaves to presheaves preserves injectives

declarations.name: Stacks.CechComparison.exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_pageTwo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OW: the Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence, with its second
page.**  For a covering family `𝒰 = E` of an object `U` of a site `C` and an abelian sheaf `F`
there is a cohomological spectral sequence whose second page is

```
E₂^{p,q} ≅ Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F)),
```

the Čech cohomology of the covering with coefficients in the cohomology presheaves
`H^q(F) : V ↦ H^q(V, F)`, and which abuts to `R^{p+q}(Ȟ⁰(𝒰, -) ∘ i)(F)`.

The abutment is the cohomology of the right derived functor of the composite
`Ȟ⁰(𝒰, -) ∘ i`, which is the group [Stacks, Tag 03OW] calls `H^{p+q}(U, F)`; the identification
of the two is **not** part of this statement, which is why the tag carries a clause.  See the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_pageTwo (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    ∃ S : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0,
      (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty ((S.page 2 zero_le_two).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅
        Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology E (F.cohomologyPresheaf q) p)) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S
        (fun n => (((sheafIncl J) ⋙ cechZeroFunctor E).rightDerivedPlus n).obj F)
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence and its second page

declarations.name: Stacks.CechComparison.exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_abutsTo_sheafCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03OW.**  Let `C` be a site, `𝒰 = E = {U_i → U}_{i ∈ I}` a covering of
`U ∈ Ob(C)` (the family generates a covering sieve of `U`) and `F` an abelian sheaf on `C`.  There
is a cohomological spectral sequence, zero outside the first quadrant, with second page

```
E₂^{p,q} ≅ Ȟ^p(𝒰, H^q(F)),
```

the Čech cohomology of the covering with coefficients in the abelian presheaf
`H^q(F) : V ↦ H^q(V, F)`, and abutting to `H^{p+q}(U, F)`: the graded family abutted to is
`n ↦ H^n(U, F)` in degrees `n ≥ 0` and is zero in negative degrees, where no term of the
spectral sequence contributes.

The spectral sequence is the Grothendieck spectral sequence of `Ȟ⁰(𝒰, -) ∘ i` of
`exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence`; its abutment `R^n(Ȟ⁰(𝒰, -) ∘ i)(F)` is identified with
`H^n(U, F)` by `Stacks.CechSite.rightDerivedPlus_cechZero_obj_iso_cohomologyPresheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechToCohomology_spectralSequence_abutsTo_sheafCohomology
    (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U) (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    ∃ S : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0,
      (∀ p q : ℕ, Nonempty ((S.page 2 zero_le_two).X ((p : ℤ), (q : ℤ)) ≅
        Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology E (F.cohomologyPresheaf q) p)) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, p < 0 ∨ q < 0 → IsZero ((S.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q))) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo S (fun n : ℤ ↦
        if n < 0 then ⊥_ AddCommGrpCat.{u} else (F.cohomologyPresheaf n.toNat).obj (op U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.isAffine_sigmaObj
declarations.doc:
The disjoint union of the members of a standard `τ`-covering is an affine scheme: the index
type is finite and every member is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.isAffine_sigmaObj (τ : CoveringTopology) {T : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine T] {I : Type w} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ T)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ U f) :
    letI : Finite I := h.finite_index
    IsAffine (∐ U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.isAffine_left_sigmaObj
declarations.doc:
The scheme underlying the disjoint union, in the big site over `S`, of the members of a
family whose underlying morphisms form a standard `τ`-covering is affine. The disjoint union is
computed on underlying schemes, since the forgetful functor to schemes preserves it.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.isAffine_left_sigmaObj (τ : CoveringTopology) (S : Scheme.{u})
    {T : Over S} [IsAffine T.left] (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ (fun i ↦ (E.X i).left) (fun i ↦ (E.f i).left)) :
    letI : Finite E.I₀ := h.finite_index
    IsAffine (∐ E.X).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsStandardCovering.isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_bigSite
declarations.doc:
For an abelian sheaf on the big `τ`-site over `S` and a standard `τ`-covering of an affine
object of that site, the canonical refinement of the covering by the morphism from the disjoint
union of its members induces an isomorphism of Čech complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsStandardCovering.isIso_cechComplexMap_coproductRefinement_bigSite
    (τ : CoveringTopology) (S : Scheme.{u}) {T : Over S} [IsAffine T.left]
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{w} T)
    (h : IsStandardCovering τ (fun i ↦ (E.X i).left) (fun i ↦ (E.f i).left))
    (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{v})
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf
      ((Scheme.grothendieckTopology (coveringMorphismProperty τ)).over S) F) :
    letI : Finite E.I₀ := h.finite_index
    IsIso (Stacks.CechSite.cechComplexMap E
      (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} (Sigma.desc E.f))
      (Stacks.CechSite.coproductRefinement E) (F ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor.{w, v}))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.PreZeroHypercover.nonempty_hom_singleton_sigmaDesc
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms with fixed target whose members have a coproduct is a **refinement of
the one-member family** given by the morphism from that coproduct.
declarations.comment:
the covering `𝒰` is a refinement of `𝒱 = {∐ Uᵢ ⟶ U}`, the direction of
  Stacks 03FI (2) that does hold

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpecIntCovering.isEmpty_hom_singleton_sigmaDesc
declarations.doc:
**The one-member family given by the disjoint union of a covering need not refine it**: for
the covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic opens of `2` and of `3`, the one-member family given by
the morphism from the disjoint union of its members is not a refinement of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_hom_singleton_sigmaDesc :
    IsEmpty ((PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} (Sigma.desc covering.{u, w}.f)).Hom
      covering.{u, w})
declarations.comment:
`𝒱 = {∐ Uᵢ ⟶ U}` is not a refinement of `𝒰`, witnessed by the standard Zariski
  covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic opens of `2` and of `3`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpecIntCovering.isEmpty_hom_singleton_of_mem_precoverage
declarations.doc:
**No one-member covering of `Spec ℤ` refines the covering by the basic opens of `2` and of
`3`**, for any topology whose coverings are jointly surjective families of morphisms with a
given property.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_hom_singleton_of_mem_precoverage {P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}}
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (g : V ⟶ target.{u})
    (hg : Presieve.singleton g ∈ Scheme.precoverage P target.{u}) :
    IsEmpty ((PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{w} g).Hom covering.{u, w})
declarations.comment:
no covering of the form `{V ⟶ U}` is a refinement of `𝒰`, witnessed by the
  standard Zariski covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic opens of `2` and of `3`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SpecIntCovering.not_initial_isSingletonCovering_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**The one-member coverings of an object do not form an initial subcategory of its category
of coverings**: for the covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic opens of `2` and of `3` there is no
one-member covering mapping to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_initial_isSingletonCovering_inclusion (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hP : (@IsOpenImmersion : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ≤ P) :
    ¬ (isSingletonCovering.{u, w} (Scheme.precoverage P) target.{u}).ι.Initial
declarations.comment:
coverings of the form `{V ⟶ U}` are not an initial subcategory of the category
  of all coverings of `U`, witnessed by the standard Zariski covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic
  opens of `2` and of `3`; the remark's further assertion that Čech cohomology can nonetheless
  be computed from the coverings `{V ⟶ U}` is not proved, the source leaving it unformulated

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyOfObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P0: Čech cohomology of an object.** The colimit, over the opposite of the category
of all coverings of `U`, of the Čech cohomology groups of `ℱ` with respect to each covering.
declarations.statement:
def cechCohomologyOfObject (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (n : ℕ)
    [HasColimit (cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)] : A
declarations.comment:
`Ȟⁿ(U, ℱ)`, defined as the colimit over the opposite of the category of coverings
  `𝒰` of `U` of the Čech cohomology groups of `ℱ` with respect to `𝒰`

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.isColimitWhiskerSingletonCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P0, the assertion the source leaves unformulated: Čech cohomology of a sheaf is
computed from the one-member coverings.** For an additive presheaf `ℱ` turning `w`-indexed
coproducts into products, on a category whose `w`-indexed coproducts are universal, the cocone
on the diagram of Čech cohomology groups restricted to the opposite of the full subcategory of
*one-member* coverings `{V ⟶ U}`, obtained by restricting the universal cocone on all coverings,
is still a colimit cocone. That is: `Ȟⁿ(U, ℱ)` is the colimit over the one-member coverings
alone — even though, as the standard Zariski covering of `Spec ℤ` by the basic opens of `2` and
of `3` witnesses, those coverings are not an initial subcategory of all coverings of `U`.

The hypotheses are the source's own. `huniv` is the infinitary extensivity of the site, the
disjointness of the coproducts that the proof of Stacks 03OZ invokes; and
`PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) ℱ` is the sheaf condition for the covering of a coproduct by
its summands, the equality Stacks 03OZ (3) rests on, which the paragraph before the remark
observes to be "false for a general presheaf". Together they are what the remark means by "it
only works for sheaves".

Because the cocone whose legs are tested is the universal cocone on *all* coverings, the
statement contains its own canonicity: the comparison is the restriction of the identity.
declarations.statement:
def isColimitWhiskerSingletonCovering
    (huniv : ∀ {I : Type w} {D : Discrete I ⥤ C} {d : Cocone D},
      IsColimit d → IsUniversalColimit d)
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [∀ I : Type w, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F] (n : ℕ)
    [HasColimit (cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)] :
    IsColimit ((colimit.cocone (cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)).whisker
      (singletonCoveringInclusion.{w} J U).op)
declarations.comment:
Čech cohomology `Ȟⁿ(U, ℱ)`, the colimit over all coverings of `U`, can still be
  computed in terms of the coverings `{V ⟶ U}`: the universal cocone restricted to the one-member
  coverings is again a colimit cocone, for a coefficient presheaf turning arbitrary coproducts
  into products, which is the source's "it only works for sheaves"

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.ι_cechCohomologyOfObjectIsoColimitSingleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P0.** The comparison of
`Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomologyOfObjectIsoColimitSingleton` is the canonical one: on each
one-member covering `{V ⟶ U}` it is the leg, at that covering, of the colimit over all
coverings.
declarations.statement:
theorem ι_cechCohomologyOfObjectIsoColimitSingleton
    (huniv : ∀ {I : Type w} {D : Discrete I ⥤ C} {d : Cocone D},
      IsColimit d → IsUniversalColimit d)
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [∀ I : Type w, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F] (n : ℕ)
    [HasColimit (cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)]
    [HasColimit ((singletonCoveringInclusion.{w} J U).op ⋙
      cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)]
    (V : (SingletonCovering J U)ᵒᵖ) :
    colimit.ι ((singletonCoveringInclusion.{w} J U).op ⋙
          cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n) V ≫
        (cechCohomologyOfObjectIsoColimitSingleton.{w} J U huniv F n).hom =
      colimit.ι (cechCohomologyCoveringFunctor.{w} J U F n)
        ((singletonCoveringInclusion.{w} J U).op.obj V)
declarations.comment:
the computation of `Ȟⁿ(U, ℱ)` from the coverings `{V ⟶ U}` is the canonical
  comparison: it restricts on each one-member covering to the leg of the colimit over all
  coverings

declarations.name: Stacks.CechComparison.exists_cover_restriction_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03P1.** Cohomology is local: for an abelian sheaf `F` on a site `C`,
an object `U`, a degree `p > 0` and a class `ξ ∈ H^p(U, F)`, there is a covering
`{U_i → U}` of `U` such that `ξ|_{U_i} = 0` for every member `i` of the covering.

Here `H^p(U, F)` is `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H' F p U`, the value over `U` of the cohomology
presheaf of `F`, and the restriction maps are the functoriality of that presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_restriction_eq_zero (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (U : C) (ξ : Sheaf.H' F p U) :
    ∃ S : J.Cover U, ∀ g : S.Arrow, (F.cohomologyPresheaf p).map g.f.op ξ = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**Zariski cohomology of a quasi-coherent module agrees with its big `τ`-site cohomology**:
for a quasi-coherent module `F` on a scheme `S` and a degree `p`,

  `H^p(S, ℱ) ≅ H^p_τ(S, Fᵃ)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIso` at the whole scheme.  The object it
is taken over on the right, `(opensBelowToOver hS).obj ⊤`, is a final object of the big site by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_opensBelowToOver_top`, so the right-hand side is `τ`-cohomology of
`S` itself.

**This is [Stacks, Tag 03P2] in the case `𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ`**, for all five `τ` at once.  Together
with `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso`, which is the case
`𝒞 = S_étale`, it is the covering set of the tag: the source lets `𝒞` be either of the two, and
these are one declaration per case.
declarations.statement:
public def bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj F) p ⊤ ≅
      Sheaf.H' (bigOverAssociatedSheaf S F τ B hS) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff τ B) hS).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: the case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ: τ is a bound variable, so this one declaration covers all five of fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale and Zariski. The object the right-hand side is taken over, (opensBelowToOver hS).obj ⊤, is a final object of the site, so that side is τ-cohomology of S itself. The case 𝒞 = S_étale is smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-coherent module `F` on a scheme `S` and a degree `p`, Zariski cohomology of `F`
agrees with small étale cohomology of its associated module:

  `H^p(S, ℱ) ≅ H^p(S_étale, Fᵃ)`.

The right-hand side is taken over `(opensToEtale S).obj ⊤`, a final object of the small étale
site, so it is étale cohomology of `S` itself.
declarations.comment: the case 𝒞 = S_étale.  The object the right-hand side is taken over, (opensToEtale S).obj ⊤, is a final object of the small étale site, so that side is étale cohomology of S itself. The case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ, for all five τ at once, is bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.QcohSiteCohomology.cohomologyAtFinalObjectIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P3, first assertion.**  The scheme `S` is a final object of the site `C` of
schemes over `S`, so the groups `H^p_τ(S, F^a)` on the right-hand side of Theorem 03P2 are the
right derived functors of the global sections functor of the site, that is Mathlib's global
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.
declarations.comment: since S is final in C, the right-hand side of 03P2 is derived global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.QcohSiteCohomology.zariskiCohomologyIsoCohomologyAtObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P3, second assertion.**  For **any** object `f : Y ⟶ S` of the site `C` of
schemes over `S`,

`H^p(Y, f^*F) = H^p_τ(Y, F^a)`,

the left-hand side being the Zariski cohomology on `Y` of the pullback module `f^*F` and the
right-hand side the `τ`-cohomology of the associated sheaf `F^a` over the object `f` of `C`.
The object of `C` in question is `u t`, and `objAtFinalObjectIso` identifies it with
`f : Y ⟶ S`.

Theorem 03P2 is not available in this repository and is carried as the hypothesis `h03P2`, in
the form in which that theorem is stated: the comparison for the scheme `Y`, the quasi-coherent
module `f^*F` on it and the final object `t` of a site `D` of schemes over `Y`.  Everything
else is proved: `cohomologyAtObjectIso` moves the right-hand side of `h03P2` from the final
object of `D` to the object `u t` of `C`.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiCohomologyIsoCohomologyAtObject (e : u ⋙ πC ≅ πD ⋙ Over.map f) (p : ℕ) (t : D)
    (h03P2 :
      Sheaf.H'.{u, u, u} ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf Y.ringCatSheaf).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)) p (⊤ : Y.Opens) ≅
        Sheaf.H' (associatedSheafPullback f F πD J hFaPullback) p t) :
    Sheaf.H'.{u, u, u} ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf Y.ringCatSheaf).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)) p (⊤ : Y.Opens) ≅
      Sheaf.H' (associatedSheaf F πC K hFa) p (u.obj t)
declarations.comment: H^p(U, f^*F) = H^p_tau(U, F^a) at an arbitrary object f : U ⟶ S of the site, with Theorem 03P2 at the final object carried as the hypothesis h03P2 and the sheaf conditions of 03OG as hFa and hFaPullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03P3], second assertion, for `𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ`:** for **any** object `Z` of a
localized big `τ`-site of `S`, with underlying scheme `U = Z.left.obj` and structure morphism
`f = Z.hom.hom : U ⟶ S`,

  `H^p(U, f^*F) ≅ H^p_τ(Z, Fᵃ)`,

the left-hand side being the Zariski cohomology on `U` of the pullback module `f^*F` and the
right-hand side the `τ`-cohomology of the associated module `Fᵃ` over the object `Z` of the
site.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAlong` at the whole of `U`, whose
image is `Z` by `AlgebraicGeometry.objAtTopIso`.  Nothing is assumed: the source's own proof of
Tag 03P2 is what is run, over `Z` instead of over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public def bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject (p : ℕ) (Z : Over (base B S hS)) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Z.left.obj).ringCatSheaf).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback Z.hom.hom).obj F)) p (⊤ : (Z.left.obj).Opens) ≅
      Sheaf.H' (bigOverAssociatedSheaf S F τ B hS) p Z
declarations.comment: second assertion, the case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ: H^p(U, f^*F) = H^p_τ(U, Fᵃ) at an ARBITRARY object Z of the site, not only at a final one. τ is a bound variable, so this one declaration covers all five of fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale and Zariski. Nothing is assumed: the sheaf condition of Tag 03OG is already carried by bigOverAssociatedSheaf, and Tag 03P2 is not invoked either — the collapse its proof runs along opensBelowToOver is run here along opensBelowToOverAlong, which lands at the object Z. The case 𝒞 = S_étale is smallEtaleQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03P3], second assertion, for `𝒞 = S_étale`:** for **any** object `Z` of the
small étale site of `S`, with underlying scheme `U = Z.left` and étale structure morphism
`f = Z.hom : U ⟶ S`,

  `H^p(U, f^*F) ≅ H^p(Z, Fᵃ)`,

the left-hand side being the Zariski cohomology on `U` of the pullback module `f^*F` and the
right-hand side the cohomology of the associated module `Fᵃ` on the small étale site of `S`,
taken over the object `Z` of that site.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAlong` at the whole of `U`, whose
image is `Z` by `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleObjAtTopIso`.  Nothing is assumed: the source's own
proof of Tag 03P2 is what is run, over `Z` instead of over `S`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject (p : ℕ) (Z : S.Etale) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf Z.left.ringCatSheaf).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback Z.hom).obj F)) p (⊤ : Z.left.Opens) ≅
      Sheaf.H' (smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf S F) p Z
declarations.comment: second assertion, the case 𝒞 = S_étale: H^p(U, f^*F) = H^p(U, Fᵃ) at an ARBITRARY object Z of the small étale site of S, not only at a final one. Nothing is assumed: the sheaf condition of Tag 03OG is already carried by smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf, and Tag 03P2 is not invoked either — the collapse its proof runs along opensToEtale is run here along opensToEtaleAlong, the composite of opensToEtale over U with composition along the étale structure morphism of Z, which lands at the object Z. The case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ is bigOverQuasiCoherentCohomologyIsoAtObject

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03P3], first assertion, for `𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ`:** the scheme `S` is a final
object of a localized big `τ`-site of `S`, so the groups `H^p_τ(S, Fᵃ)` on the right-hand side
of [Stacks, Tag 03P2] are the right derived functors of the global sections functor of the site,
that is Mathlib's global `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`.

The object on the left is `(opensBelowToOver hS).obj ⊤`, which is exactly the object
`AlgebraicGeometry.bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso` takes its right-hand side over, and
it is final by `AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_opensBelowToOver_top`.
declarations.statement:
public def bigOverAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' (bigOverAssociatedSheaf S F τ B hS) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff τ B) hS).obj ⊤) ≅
      AddCommGrpCat.of (Sheaf.H.{u} (bigOverAssociatedSheaf S F τ B hS) p)
declarations.comment: first assertion, the case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ: since S is final in 𝒞 the right-hand side of Tag 03P2 is derived global sections. The object is the very one bigOverQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso lands at, and it is final by isTerminal_opensBelowToOver_top; τ is a bound variable, so all five topologies are covered. The case 𝒞 = S_étale is smallEtaleAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03P3], first assertion, for `𝒞 = S_étale`:** the scheme `S` is a final object
of its small étale site, so the groups `H^p(S_étale, Fᵃ)` on the right-hand side of
[Stacks, Tag 03P2] are the right derived functors of the global sections functor of the site.

The object on the left is `(opensToEtale S).obj ⊤`, which is exactly the object
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso` takes its right-hand side over,
and it is final by `AlgebraicGeometry.isTerminal_opensToEtale_top`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso (S : Scheme.{u}) (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' (smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf S F) p ((opensToEtale S).obj ⊤) ≅
      AddCommGrpCat.of (Sheaf.H.{u} (smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf S F) p)
declarations.comment: first assertion, the case 𝒞 = S_étale: since S is final in S_étale the right-hand side of Tag 03P2 is derived global sections. The object is the very one smallEtaleQuasiCoherentGlobalCohomologyIso lands at, and it is final by isTerminal_opensToEtale_top. The case 𝒞 = (Sch/S)_τ is bigOverAssociatedSheafGlobalCohomologyIso

declarations.statement: noncomputable def additiveGroupSheaf : Sheaf (topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: part (1), Gₐ on the small étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.additiveGroupSheaf
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleConstantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMapsAb
declarations.doc:
The constant sheaf of abelian groups with value `A` on the small étale site of a scheme `X`
has as its sections over an étale `X`-scheme `V` the group of locally constant `A`-valued maps
on `V`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtaleConstantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMapsAb (X : Scheme.{u})
    (A : Type (max (u + 1) v)) [AddCommGroup A] :
    ((constantSheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of A)).obj ≅
      smallEtaleLocallyConstantMapsAb.{u, max (u + 1) v} X A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleConstantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMapsAb_unit
declarations.doc:
The identification of the constant abelian sheaf on the small étale site with the locally
constant maps sends the sheafification-unit image of `a : A` to the constant map with value
`a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleConstantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMapsAb_unit (X : Scheme.{u})
    (A : Type (max (u + 1) v)) [AddCommGroup A] (T : (X.Etale)ᵒᵖ) (a : A) :
    ((smallEtaleConstantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMapsAb.{u, v} X A).hom.app T)
      ((toSheafify (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X)
        ((Functor.const (X.Etale)ᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of A))).app T a) =
      LocallyConstant.const T.unop.left a
declarations.comment: constant sections on Scheme.smallEtaleTopology, AddCommGrpCat coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantGroupSheafRepresentedByConstantGroupScheme
declarations.doc:
The constant sheaf of groups on the schemes over `S` is represented by the constant group
scheme `G_S`, compatibly with the constant-presheaf unit, for every topology between the
Zariski and the fpqc topology.
declarations.statement:
public def constantGroupSheafRepresentedByConstantGroupScheme (S : Scheme.{u})
    (G : Type (max (u + 1) v)) [Small.{u} G] [Group G] (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S))
    (hZ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) (hF : J ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) :
    GroupSheafRepresentation S (𝟭 (Over S)) J G
declarations.comment: group-valued representation on the big over-site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMaps
declarations.doc:
The sheafification of the constant presheaf on the schemes over `S` has the locally
constant `G`-valued maps as its sections, for every topology between the Zariski and the fpqc
topology.
declarations.statement:
public def constantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMaps (S : Scheme.{u}) (G : Type (max (u + 1) v))
    [Small.{u} G] [Group G] (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S))
    (hZ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) (hF : J ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) :
    ((constantSheaf J (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj G).obj ≅
      (locallyConstantMapsOver G S ⋙ forget GrpCat)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMaps_unit
declarations.doc:
The identification of the constant sheaf with locally constant maps sends the
sheafification-unit image of `g` to the constant map with value `g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem constantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMaps_unit (S : Scheme.{u})
    (G : Type (max (u + 1) v)) [Small.{u} G] [Group G] (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S))
    (hZ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) (hF : J ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S)
    (T : (Over S)ᵒᵖ) (g : G) :
    ((constantSheafIsoLocallyConstantMaps S G J hZ hF).hom.app T)
      ((toSheafify J ((Functor.const (Over S)ᵒᵖ).obj G)).app T g) =
      LocallyConstant.const T.unop.left g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantSheafComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
On the schemes over `S`, the canonical comparison from the Zariski sheafification of the
constant presheaf to its `J`-sheafification is invertible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem constantSheafComparison_isIso (S : Scheme.{u}) (G : Type (max (u + 1) v))
    [Small.{u} G] [Group G] (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S))
    (hZ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) (hF : J ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S)
    [HasWeakSheafify (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S) (Type (max (u + 1) v))]
    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type (max (u + 1) v))] :
    let P : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v) := (Functor.const (Over S)ᵒᵖ).obj G
    IsIso (zariskiSheafToTauSheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S) J hZ P)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constantSheafIsoConstantGroupSchemePoints
declarations.doc:
The constant sheaf of sets is naturally the underlying functor of points of the constant
group scheme. The isomorphism is the composite through the group-valued functor of locally
constant maps.
declarations.statement:
public def constantSheafIsoConstantGroupSchemePoints (S : Scheme.{u})
    (G : Type (max (u + 1) v)) [Small.{u} G] [Group G] (J : GrothendieckTopology (Over S))
    (hZ : Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S ≤ J) (hF : J ≤ Scheme.fpqcTopology.over S) :
    ((constantSheaf J (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj G).obj ≅
      ((yonedaGrp.obj (constantGroupScheme G S) ⋙
        GrpCat.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v}) ⋙ forget GrpCat)
declarations.comment: representation of the constant sheaf by the group scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.additiveGroupPresheafIsoPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6, the identification of `Gₐ`.**  The additive group sheaf of a site of
schemes over `S` is the functor of points of the additive group scheme `Gₐ,S` of
[Stacks, Tag 022V], restricted to the site along `toOver`.

The comparison is stated after the forgetful retyping of `AddCommGrpCat` into `GrpCat`, which
is the shape in which `AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupBaseChangePointsIsoGlobalSections`
records that the group law on sections is addition of functions.  It is a whiskering of that
natural isomorphism and assumes nothing about the topology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveGroupPresheafIsoPoints :
    toOver.op ⋙ yonedaGrpObj (Scheme.asOver (additiveGroupBaseChange S) S) ≅
      additiveGroupPresheaf S toOver ⋙ forget₂ AddCommGrpCat AddGrpCat ⋙ AddGrpCat.toGrp
declarations.comment: Gₐ is the functor of points of the additive group scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.additiveGroupSheaf_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6, the notation `H^p_τ(X, 𝒪_X)`.**  The underlying presheaf of `Gₐ` is the
structure presheaf of the site read additively.  So the cohomology of `Gₐ` on a site of
schemes over `S` and the cohomology of the structure sheaf `𝒪_S` of [Stacks, Tag 04HS] on that
site are cohomology of one and the same abelian sheaf, which is what lets the two notations of
the remark be used interchangeably.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveGroupSheaf_obj (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (toOver.op ⋙ globalSectionsOver S)) :
    (additiveGroupSheaf S toOver J h).obj =
      structurePresheaf S toOver ⋙ forget₂ RingCat AddCommGrpCat
declarations.comment: Gₐ is the structure sheaf of Stacks 04HS read additively

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.sheafHZeroAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6 in degree zero.**  On a site of schemes over `S` with a terminal object `X₀`,
the degree-zero cohomology of `Gₐ` is the additive group of global functions on the scheme over
`S` that `X₀` names.  This is the degree-zero case of the remark's chain of equalities, and it
holds for every topology at once with no input from [Stacks, Tag 03P2]: degree-zero sheaf
cohomology is sections over a terminal object, and the sections of `Gₐ` are the global
functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHZeroAddEquiv (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (toOver.op ⋙ globalSectionsOver S))
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    {X₀ : C} (hX₀ : IsTerminal X₀) :
    Sheaf.H (additiveGroupSheaf S toOver J h) 0 ≃+
      (additiveGroupPresheaf S toOver).obj (op X₀)
declarations.comment: degree zero: H⁰ of Gₐ is the additive group of global functions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6, the big fppf site.**  `Gₐ` as an abelian sheaf on `(Sch/S)_{fppf}`.  Its
underlying presheaf is the structure sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 04HS] of that site read additively,
so its cohomology is the group the remark also writes `H^p_{fppf}(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def additiveGroupSheaf : Sheaf (topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: Gₐ on the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sheafHZeroAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6 in degree zero, fppf.**  `H^0_{fppf}(S, Gₐ) = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`: the big fppf site
over `S` has `S` itself for a terminal object, and degree-zero sheaf cohomology is sections
over a terminal object.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHZeroAddEquiv [HasSheafify (topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
    Sheaf.H (additiveGroupSheaf S B hS) 0 ≃+ Stacks.Sites.globalSectionsAddCommGrp S
declarations.comment: degree zero on the big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleOver.additiveGroupSheaf
declarations.doc:

underlying presheaf is the structure sheaf of [Stacks, Tag 04HS] of that site read additively,
so its cohomology is the group the remark also writes `H^p_{étale}(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def additiveGroupSheaf : Sheaf (topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: Gₐ on the big étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleOver.sheafHZeroAddEquiv
declarations.doc:

declarations.doc:

declarations.comment: Gₐ on the big Zariski site

declarations.doc:

site over `S` has `S` itself for a terminal object, and degree-zero sheaf cohomology is
