declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfEtaleAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6 in degree zero, fppf against étale.**  `H^0_{fppf}(S, Gₐ) =
H^0_{étale}(S, Gₐ)`: both are the additive group `Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` of global functions.  This is one
leg of the remark's chain of equalities, in the degree in which it needs nothing from
[Stacks, Tag 03P2].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfEtaleAddEquiv :
    Sheaf.H (BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bf hSf) 0 ≃+
      Sheaf.H (BigEtaleOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Be hSe) 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfZariskiAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03P6 in degree zero, fppf against Zariski.**  `H^0_{fppf}(S, Gₐ) =
H^0_{Zar}(S, Gₐ)`: both are the additive group `Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` of global functions.  Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfEtaleAddEquiv` this is the remark's whole chain
of equalities in degree zero, the rightmost term `H^0(S, 𝒪_S)` being `Γ(S, 𝒪_S)` as well.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfZariskiAddEquiv :
    Sheaf.H (BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bf hSf) 0 ≃+
      Sheaf.H (BigZariskiOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bz hSz) 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
For a scheme `S` below the cutoff of a big `τ`-site and every `p`,
`H^p(X, 𝒪_X) ≅ H^p_τ(X, Gₐ)`: the left-hand side is the cohomology of the structure sheaf on the
underlying topological space of `S`, the right-hand side the `τ`-cohomology of `Gₐ` over the
final object `(opensBelowToOver hS).obj ⊤` of the localized big site.
declarations.statement:
public def additiveGroupSheafCohomologyIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf S.ringCatSheaf).obj (Scheme.unitModule S)) p ⊤ ≅
      Sheaf.H' (overAdditiveGroupSheaf S τ B hS) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff τ B) hS).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: all degrees p ≥ 0: H^p_τ(X, Gₐ) = H^p(X, 𝒪_X), the specialization of Theorem 03P2 to ℱ = 𝒪_S. τ is a bound variable, so this one declaration is the comparison for all five big sites at once, in particular for the fppf, étale and Zariski sites the remark names. The left-hand side is cohomology of the structure sheaf on the site of opens of the underlying topological space of S, which is this repository's spelling of H^p(X, 𝒪_X), so the rightmost equality of the chain needs no further comparison. The missing ingredient supplied here on top of 03P2 is Gₐ = (𝒪_S)ᵃ, namely overAdditiveGroupSheafIsoAssociatedSheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafCohomologyFppfEtaleIso
declarations.doc: `H^p_{fppf}(X, Gₐ) ≅ H^p_{étale}(X, Gₐ)` for every `p`, both being `H^p(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public def additiveGroupSheafCohomologyFppfEtaleIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' (BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bf hSf) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff .fppf Bf) hSf).obj ⊤) ≅
      Sheaf.H' (BigEtaleOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Be hSe) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff .etale Be) hSe).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: all degrees p ≥ 0: H^p_fppf(X, Gₐ) = H^p_étale(X, Gₐ), the first leg of the chain, obtained by composing additiveGroupSheafCohomologyIso at τ = fppf with its inverse at τ = étale. The sheaves are BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf and BigEtaleOver.additiveGroupSheaf themselves, by overAdditiveGroupSheaf_fppf and overAdditiveGroupSheaf_etale. The degree-zero case is additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfEtaleAddEquiv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveGroupSheafCohomologyFppfZariskiIso
declarations.doc: `H^p_{fppf}(X, Gₐ) ≅ H^p_{Zar}(X, Gₐ)` for every `p`, both being `H^p(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public def additiveGroupSheafCohomologyFppfZariskiIso (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H' (BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bf hSf) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff .fppf Bf) hSf).obj ⊤) ≅
      Sheaf.H' (BigZariskiOver.additiveGroupSheaf S Bz hSz) p
        ((opensBelowToOver (κ := cutoff .zariski Bz) hSz).obj ⊤)
declarations.comment: all degrees p ≥ 0: H^p_fppf(X, Gₐ) = H^p_Zar(X, Gₐ), the second leg of the chain. With additiveGroupSheafCohomologyFppfEtaleIso and additiveGroupSheafCohomologyIso this completes the chain H^p_fppf = H^p_étale = H^p_Zar = H^p(X, 𝒪_X) for all p ≥ 0. The sheaves are BigFppfOver.additiveGroupSheaf and BigZariskiOver.additiveGroupSheaf themselves, by overAdditiveGroupSheaf_fppf and overAdditiveGroupSheaf_zariski. The degree-zero case is additiveGroupSheafHZeroFppfZariskiAddEquiv

declarations.name: Stacks.Kummer.etaleH1MultiplicativeAddEquivPicard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03P8, the étale identification.** For any scheme `X`, the first étale
cohomology of the multiplicative group is the Picard group: `H¹_étale(X, 𝐆_m) = Pic(X)`.

The identification is the composite of the canonical ones: restriction to a size-bounded small
étale site (Tag 00XU), the identification of `H¹` of the units of the small étale ringed site with
its Picard group (Tag 040E), and the identification of that Picard group with `Pic(X)` by
`𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` (Tag 03DX (2)); the coefficient universe of `𝐆_m` is immaterial for `H¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def etaleH1MultiplicativeAddEquivPicard
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    Sheaf.H.{w} (multiplicativeSheaf.{u, v} S) 1 ≃+ Stacks.Picard.ofScheme S
declarations.comment: the étale identification H¹_étale(X, 𝐆_m) = Pic(X), for every scheme X; the fppf, syntomic and smooth identifications are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.AllTopologies.identifications
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03P8.** For any scheme `X` there are canonical identifications

`H¹_fppf(X, 𝐆_m) = H¹_syntomic(X, 𝐆_m) = H¹_smooth(X, 𝐆_m) = H¹_étale(X, 𝐆_m)
  = H¹_Zar(X, 𝐆_m) = Pic(X) = H¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)`.

The five big-site groups are identified with `Pic(X)` by
`Stacks.Picard.AllTopologies.baseH1UnitsAddEquivSchemePicardGroup`, which is Tag 040E on the big
`τ`-site followed by clause (1) of Descent, Proposition 03DX at `τ` read on Picard groups; the
last link is Tag 040E on the site of opens of `X`,
`Stacks.Picard.ZariskiSite.zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup`.

Every identification is normalized on invertible modules:
`Stacks.Picard.AllTopologies.baseH1UnitsAddEquivSchemePicardGroup_symm_classOf` and
`Stacks.Picard.ZariskiSite.zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf` send the class of an
invertible module to the first cohomology class of its torsor of local generators, and the six
`identifications_*` lemmas below express each field in those terms.
declarations.statement: public def identifications : Identifications.{t} B X hX

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.ZariskiSite.zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03P8, the Zariski identification.** For any scheme `X` there is a
canonical isomorphism of abelian groups `H¹_{Zar}(X, 𝐆_m) = Pic(X)`.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup :
    Sheaf.H (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (schemeRingedSite X)) 1 ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup (schemeRingedSite X).O.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (schemeRingedSite X).O).2
declarations.comment: the identification H¹_Zar(X, 𝐆_m) = Pic(X); the four comparisons of H¹_fppf, H¹_syntomic, H¹_smooth and H¹_étale with H¹_Zar are not covered

declarations.name: Stacks.Picard.ZariskiSite.zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03P8, the Zariski identification is the canonical one.** Its inverse
sends the class of an invertible module to the first cohomology class of its torsor of local
generators.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (schemeRingedSite X).O))
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (schemeRingedSite X).O.obj
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (schemeRingedSite X).O).2 L) :
    (zariskiH1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup X).symm
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf (schemeRingedSite X).O.obj
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (schemeRingedSite X).O).2 L hL) =
      Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1
        (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (schemeRingedSite X))
        (Quotient.mk (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorSetoid
            (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.unitsAddSheaf (schemeRingedSite X)))
          (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.Generators.generatorTorsor (schemeRingedSite X)
            (schemeRingedSite_isLocallyRinged X) L hL).torsor)
declarations.comment: the Zariski identification is the canonical one, normalized on line bundles

registrations.name: Stacks.Picard.FirstCohomology.h1UnitsAddEquivPicard_symm_classOf
registrations.comment: the identification Pic(X) = H¹(X, 𝒪_X^*) is the canonical one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_flat_and_fibers_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC, part (2), (a) ⟺ (b).** A morphism of schemes is étale if and
only if it is locally of finite presentation, flat, and all of its fibres are étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_flat_and_fibers_etale
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Etale f ↔ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ Flat f ∧
      ∀ s : S, Etale (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_pullback_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC, part (6), fibre products.** Let `i₁ : X ⟶ X'` and
`i₂ : Y ⟶ Y'` be morphisms of schemes over a base `S`. If both are étale, then so is the
induced morphism `X ×_S Y ⟶ X' ×_S Y'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_pullback_map {S X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : Y ⟶ S}
    {f' : X' ⟶ S} {g' : Y' ⟶ S} {i₁ : X ⟶ X'} {i₂ : Y ⟶ Y'} [Etale i₁] [Etale i₂]
    (e₁ : f = i₁ ≫ f') (e₂ : g = i₂ ≫ g') :
    Etale (pullback.map f g f' g' i₁ i₂ (𝟙 S) ((Category.comp_id _).trans e₁)
      ((Category.comp_id _).trans e₂))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_prod_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC, part (6), products.** The product of two étale morphisms of
schemes is étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_prod_map {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ X') (g : Y ⟶ Y')
    [Etale f] [Etale g] : Etale (prod.map f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativeDimension_zero_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC, part (7).** An étale morphism of schemes has relative
dimension `0`: it is locally quasi-finite, and a locally quasi-finite morphism is exactly one
of relative dimension `0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeDimension_zero_of_etale {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] :
    RelativeDimension f 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRegular_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC, part (8), the regular case.** The source of an étale morphism
with regular target is regular, an étale morphism being smooth.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_iso_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PC (over a field).** A morphism to the spectrum of a field is
étale if and only if its source is, over that spectrum, a coproduct of spectra of finite
separable field extensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etale_iff_iso_coproduct_spectra_finite_separable
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {U : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Etale f ↔
      ∃ (I : Type u) (K : I → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k (K i))
        (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k (K i))
        (e : U ≅ ∐ fun i ↦ Spec (.of (K i))),
        e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (K i)))) = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSmallEtaleSheafCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03YX, étale case.** Big étale cohomology over `S` agrees, naturally in the abelian
sheaf, with the cohomology of its restriction to the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSmallEtaleSheafCohomologyIso
    (F : Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS) Ab.{u + 1})
    [HasSheafify (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS) Ab.{u + 1}]
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) Ab.{u + 1}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS) Ab.{u + 1})]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) Ab.{u + 1})]
    (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} F p ≃+
      (((SmallEtale.inclusion B S hS).sheafPushforwardContinuous
          Ab.{u + 1} (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
          (BigEtaleOver.topology B S hS)).obj F).H p
declarations.comment: big-site cohomology over S agrees with that of the restriction to S_etale

An étale neighborhood of a geometric point consists of an étale scheme over the base together

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover.exists_etaleNeighborhood_lift
declarations.doc:
Let `s : Spec Ω ⟶ S` be a geometric point of `S`, with `Ω` separably closed, and let
`(U, u)` be an étale neighborhood of `s`, that is `f : U ⟶ S` is étale and `u ≫ f = s`. Then
for every étale covering `𝒰` of `U` there are an index `i` and a lift `uᵢ` of `u` to `𝒰.X i`,
so that `(𝒰.X i, uᵢ)` is an étale neighborhood of `s` and `𝒰.f i` is a morphism of étale
neighborhoods `(𝒰.X i, uᵢ) ⟶ (U, u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleNeighborhood_lift {S U : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (f : U ⟶ S) [Etale f] (u : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U) (hu : u ≫ f = s)
    (𝒰 : U.Cover.{v} etalePrecoverage) :
    ∃ (i : 𝒰.I₀) (uᵢ : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ 𝒰.X i),
      Etale (𝒰.f i ≫ f) ∧ uᵢ ≫ 𝒰.f i ≫ f = s ∧ uᵢ ≫ 𝒰.f i = u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_ab_exact
declarations.doc:
**The stalk functor on abelian presheaves is exact.** For a geometric point `s` of `S`, the
stalk functor `PAb(S_et) ⥤ Ab`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕_s̄`, commutes with finite limits and finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_ab_exact :
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits
        ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}))
declarations.comment: (1) the stalk functor on abelian presheaves is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify
declarations.doc:
**Stalks of a presheaf of sets and of its sheafification agree.** For a geometric point `s` of
`S` and a presheaf of sets `𝓕` on `S_et`, the map `𝓕_s̄ ⟶ (𝓕^#)_s̄` induced by `𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕^#` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify
    (F : S.Etaleᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) :
    IsIso ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber.map (toSheafify (smallEtaleTopology S) F))
declarations.comment: (2) the stalk of a presheaf of sets equals the stalk of its sheafification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify'
declarations.doc:
**Stalks of a presheaf of sets and of its sheafification agree**, for presheaves of sets in
`Type (max (u + 1) v)`. For a geometric point `s` of `S` and a presheaf of sets `𝓕` on `S_et`, the
map `𝓕_s̄ ⟶ (𝓕^#)_s̄` induced by `𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕^#` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_map_toSheafify'
    (F : S.Etaleᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v)) :
    IsIso ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber.map (toSheafify (smallEtaleTopology S) F))
declarations.comment: (2) the stalk of a presheaf of sets equals the stalk of its sheafification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale_sheafFiber_ab_exact
declarations.doc:
**The stalk functor on abelian sheaves is exact.** For a geometric point `s` of `S`, the stalk
functor `Ab(S_et) ⥤ Ab`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕_s̄`, commutes with finite limits and finite colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSmallEtale_sheafFiber_ab_exact :
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}))
declarations.comment: (3) the stalk functor on abelian sheaves is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_type_exact
declarations.doc:
**The stalk functor on presheaves of sets is exact and commutes with colimits.** For a
geometric point `s` of `S`, the stalk functor `PSh(S_et) ⥤ Sets`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕_s̄`, commutes with
finite limits, with finite colimits, and with colimits of any size.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSmallEtale_presheafFiber_type_exact :
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber (A := Type (max u v))) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber (A := Type (max u v))) ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{w₁, w₂}
        ((pointSmallEtale s).presheafFiber (A := Type (max u v)))
declarations.comment: (4) the stalk functor on presheaves of sets is exact and commutes with colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale_sheafFiber_type_exact
declarations.doc:
**The stalk functor on sheaves of sets is exact and commutes with colimits.** For a geometric
point `s` of `S`, the stalk functor `Sh(S_et) ⥤ Sets`, `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕_s̄`, commutes with finite limits,
with finite colimits, and with colimits of any size.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointSmallEtale_sheafFiber_type_exact :
    PreservesFiniteLimits ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := Type (max u v))) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := Type (max u v))) ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{w₁, w₂}
        ((pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber (A := Type (max u v)))
declarations.comment: (4) the stalk functor on sheaves of sets is exact and commutes with colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_of_forall_isZero_etaleStalk_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU for sheaves of modules, the vanishing case.** A sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the
small étale site of `S` whose stalk at every geometric point of `S` vanishes is zero.

The zero map from the zero sheaf is surjective on every geometric stalk, the target of each of
those maps being a zero module, so it is locally surjective by Tag 03PU and therefore an
epimorphism; an epimorphism out of a zero object forces the identity of its target to
vanish.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_of_forall_isZero_etaleStalk_module (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (h : ∀ t : GeometricPoint S, IsZero (etaleStalk B S hS t F.obj)) :
    IsZero F
declarations.comment: module coefficients, the vanishing case of the isomorphism criterion: a sheaf of modules whose geometric stalks all vanish is zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_bijective_etaleStalkMap
declarations.doc:
A morphism of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of `X` which is bijective on the stalk
at every geometric point of `X` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_of_bijective_etaleStalkMap (α : F ⟶ G)
    (h : ∀ s : GeometricPoint X, Function.Bijective
      ((etaleStalkFunctor.{u, u + 1} B X hX s).map α)) :
    IsIso α
declarations.comment: sheaves of sets, the isomorphism case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint.mono_iff_forall_injective_stalkFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PU.** A map of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of a scheme
is injective if and only if it is injective on the stalk at every geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_forall_injective_stalkFunctor (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    Mono φ ↔ ∀ s : GeometricPoint S, Function.Injective (s.stalkFunctor.map φ)
declarations.comment: injectivity on stalks at geometric points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint.epi_iff_forall_surjective_stalkFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03PU.** A map of sheaves of sets on the small étale site of a scheme
is surjective if and only if it is surjective on the stalk at every geometric point.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_iff_forall_surjective_stalkFunctor (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    Epi φ ↔ ∀ s : GeometricPoint S, Function.Surjective (s.stalkFunctor.map φ)
declarations.comment: surjectivity on stalks at geometric points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_of_surjective_etaleStalkMapOfCoefficients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU** for an arbitrary concrete coefficient category. A map of sheaves on the small
étale site of `S` which is surjective on the stalk at every geometric point of `S` is locally
surjective.

A section over `V` is, near every point of `V`, the image of a section: its germ at the geometric
point attached to that point is the image of a germ, germs are computed on étale neighbourhoods,
and two sections with the same germ agree on an étale neighbourhood of the point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallySurjective_of_surjective_etaleStalkMapOfCoefficients
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) A} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (h : ∀ s : GeometricPoint S, Function.Surjective
      ((etaleStalkPresheafFunctor B S hS s A).map α.hom)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) α.hom
declarations.comment: local surjectivity from surjectivity on geometric stalks, arbitrary coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleStalkMap_of_isLocallySurjective_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU for sheaves of modules.** A locally surjective map of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on
a small étale site is surjective on the stalk at every geometric point: the stalk is the fiber of
the point of the site attached to the geometric point, and a point of a site turns local
surjectivity into surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_etaleStalkMap_of_isLocallySurjective_module
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (α : F ⟶ G)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) α.hom]
    (s : GeometricPoint S) :
    Function.Surjective
      ((etaleStalkPresheafFunctor B S hS s (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).map α.hom)
declarations.comment: surjectivity on geometric stalks, module coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_of_surjective_etaleStalkMap_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU for sheaves of modules.** A map of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale
site of `S` which is surjective on the stalk at every geometric point of `S` is locally
surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallySurjective_of_surjective_etaleStalkMap_module
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (h : ∀ s : GeometricPoint S, Function.Surjective
      ((etaleStalkPresheafFunctor B S hS s (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).map α.hom)) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) α.hom
declarations.comment: local surjectivity from surjectivity on geometric stalks, module coefficients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyFaithful_etaleStalkSheafFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU.** The stalk functors at the geometric points of `S` are jointly faithful on
abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `S`: two morphisms of sheaves inducing the same map on
every stalk are equal.

Two morphisms with the same germ at every geometric point agree, over each object of the site, on
the sieve of arrows along which the two sections become equal; that sieve is covering because
every point of the object carries a geometric point lifting to it, and a sheaf is separated for a
covering sieve.
declarations.comment: the geometric stalks are jointly faithful on abelian étale sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exact_iff_etaleStalk_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU.** A short complex of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `S` is exact
exactly when its short complex of stalks at every geometric point of `S` is exact.

A stalk is a filtered colimit, so the stalk functors are exact and the condition is necessary;
it is sufficient because the stalk functors are jointly faithful, so a sheaf whose stalks all
vanish vanishes, applied to the homology of the complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_iff_etaleStalk_exact
    (T : ShortComplex (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})) :
    T.Exact ↔ ∀ s : GeometricPoint S,
      let Φ := sheafToPresheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} ⋙
        etaleStalkPresheafFunctor B S hS s AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}
      ∀ b : Φ.obj T.X₂,
        ((Φ.map T.g).hom b = 0 ↔ ∃ a : Φ.obj T.X₁, (Φ.map T.f).hom a = b)
declarations.comment: exactness of abelian étale sheaves is checked on geometric stalks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_etaleStalkMap_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03PU.** A locally surjective morphism of abelian sheaves on a small étale site is
surjective on the stalk at every geometric point: the stalk is the fiber of the point of the
site attached to the geometric point, and a point of a site turns local surjectivity into
surjectivity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_etaleStalkMap_of_isLocallySurjective
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (hY : B.Contains Y)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Y hY) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}} (α : F ⟶ G)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology B Y hY) α.hom]
    (s : GeometricPoint Y) :
    Function.Surjective
      ((etaleStalkPresheafFunctor B Y hY s AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).map α.hom)
declarations.comment: surjectivity on stalks at geometric points, abelian sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePresheafPushforward
declarations.doc:
The direct image `f_*𝓕` of a presheaf of sets `𝓕` on the small étale site of `X` along
`f : X ⟶ Y`: the presheaf on the small étale site of `Y` sending `V/Y` to `𝓕(V ×_Y X / X)`.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePresheafPushforward {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ((X.Etale)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) ⥤ ((Y.Etale)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleBaseChange_isCovering
declarations.doc:
Pulling an étale covering family of `S` back along `f : T ⟶ S` yields an étale covering
family of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleBaseChange_isCovering {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (E : Covering (SmallEtale B S.obj S.property))
    (hE : SmallEtale.IsCovering B S.obj S.property E) :
    SmallEtale.IsCovering B T.obj T.property
      ⟨(smallEtaleBaseChange B f).obj E.1, E.2.map (smallEtaleBaseChange B f)⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheafFor_baseChange_iff
declarations.doc:
The sheaf condition for a presheaf on the small étale category of `T`, tested against the
base change of a covering family of `S`, agrees with the sheaf condition for its direct image
tested against the original family.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheafFor_baseChange_iff {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (P : (SmallEtale B T.obj T.property)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v)
    (E : Covering (SmallEtale B S.obj S.property)) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor ((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).op ⋙ P) E.2.presieve₀ ↔
      Presieve.IsSheafFor P (E.2.map (smallEtaleBaseChange B f)).presieve₀

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**The direct image, or pushforward, `f_*` along `f : X ⟶ Y`** on sheaves of sets of the
small étale sites: the sheaf `f_* F` on `Y_étale` sends an étale `Y`-scheme `V` to `F(V ×_Y X)`,
that is, `f_*` is precomposition with base change along `f`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev smallEtaleDirectImage :
    Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ⥤
      Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology Y) (Type (max (u + 1) v))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1.** Pullback of an étale sheaf commutes naturally with taking stalks at a
geometric point.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePullbackStalkIso (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) (x : GeometricPoint T.1) :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.1 T.property) ⋙
      etaleStalkFunctor.{u, u + 1} B T.1 T.property x ≅
    etaleStalkFunctor.{u, u + 1} B S.1 S.property (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackStalkIso_germ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1.** The comparison sends the germ of a section pulled back to a pointed
étale neighborhood to the germ of the original section.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePullbackStalkIso_germ (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) (x : GeometricPoint T.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B T.1 T.property x).Elements)
    (V : (geometricPointFiber B S.1 S.property
      (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))).Elements)
    (a : U.1 ⟶ (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).obj V.1)
    (ha : U.2.1 ≫ (SmallEtale.toScheme B T.1 T.property).map a ≫
        B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst V.1.obj.hom f) = V.2.1)
    (t : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op V.1)) :
    ((smallEtalePullbackStalkIso B f x).hom.app F)
      ((colimit.ι
        ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B T.1 T.property x)).op ⋙
          (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
            (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property)
            (SmallEtale.topology B T.1 T.property)).obj F).obj)
        (Opposite.op U)) (pullbackSectionAlong B f F V.1 U.1 a t)) =
      (colimit.ι
        ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B S.1 S.property
          (x.map (B.inclusion.map f)))).op ⋙ F.obj)
        (Opposite.op V)) t

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackSheafFiberIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1** for arbitrary coefficients. Inverse image of a sheaf on the small étale site
commutes naturally with the stalk at a geometric point.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePullbackSheafFiberIso (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) (x : GeometricPoint T.obj)
    (A : Type uA) [Category.{vA} A] [HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} A] [HasProducts.{u} A]
    [((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous A
      (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)).IsRightAdjoint] :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback A
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property) ⋙
      (geometricPointSitePoint B T.obj T.property x).sheafFiber ≅
    (geometricPointSitePoint B S.obj S.property (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))).sheafFiber

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackSheafFiberIso_germ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1** for arbitrary coefficients, on germs: the comparison of the stalk of an
inverse image with the stalk at the image point sends the germ of a pulled-back section to the
germ of the original section.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePullbackSheafFiberIso_germ
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property) A)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B T.obj T.property x).Elements)
    (V : (geometricPointFiber B S.obj S.property
      (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))).Elements)
    (a : U.1 ⟶ (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).obj V.1)
    (ha : U.2.1 ≫ (SmallEtale.toScheme B T.obj T.property).map a ≫
      B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst V.1.obj.hom f) = V.2.1) :
    pullbackSectionAlongHom B f A F V.1 U.1 a ≫
        colimit.ι ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B T.obj T.property x)).op ⋙
            (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback A
              (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
              (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)).obj F).obj) (op U) ≫
          (smallEtalePullbackSheafFiberIso B f x A).hom.app F =
      colimit.ι ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B S.obj S.property
        (x.map (B.inclusion.map f)))).op ⋙ F.obj) (op V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkSmallEtalePullObjIso_germ
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03Q1** for arbitrary coefficients, on germs and on a single sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleStalkSmallEtalePullObjIso_germ
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property) A)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B T.obj T.property x).Elements)
    (V : (geometricPointFiber B S.obj S.property
      (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))).Elements)
    (a : U.1 ⟶ (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).obj V.1)
    (ha : U.2.1 ≫ (SmallEtale.toScheme B T.obj T.property).map a ≫
      B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst V.1.obj.hom f) = V.2.1) :
    pullbackSectionAlongHom B f A F V.1 U.1 a ≫
        colimit.ι ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B T.obj T.property x)).op ⋙
            (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback A
              (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
              (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)).obj F).obj) (op U) ≫
          (etaleStalkSmallEtalePullObjIso B f x A F).hom =
      colimit.ι ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B S.obj S.property
        (x.map (B.inclusion.map f)))).op ⋙ F.obj) (op V)
declarations.comment: pullback_stalk on germs, arbitrary coefficients, single sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackStalkIsoModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1 for sheaves of modules.** Inverse image of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on small
étale sites commutes with taking stalks at a geometric point: the stalk at `x` of the inverse
image along `f` is the stalk of the original sheaf at the image geometric point, naturally in the
sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public def smallEtalePullbackStalkIsoModule {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S)
    (x : GeometricPoint T.1) :
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.1 T.property) ⋙
      etaleStalkFunctorModule B T.1 T.property Λ x ≅
    etaleStalkFunctorModule B S.1 S.property Λ (x.map (B.inclusion.map f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafPullback_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
Inverse image along `f : T ⟶ S` between the small étale topoi preserves finite limits:
being a morphism of sites, base change has an exact left adjoint on sheaves, and that left
adjoint is the sheaf pullback.
declarations.statement:
public instance smallEtaleSheafPullback_preservesFiniteLimits {S T : B.Scheme} (f : T ⟶ S) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleAbSheafPullback_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q1.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, the inverse image functor
`f⁻¹ : Ab(Y_étale) ⥤ Ab(X_étale)` between the categories of abelian sheaves on the small
étale sites is exact: it preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso
declarations.doc:
For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y`, the inverse image on the small étale sites carries the
sheaf represented by an étale `Y`-scheme `V` to the sheaf represented by the base change
`X ×_Y V`, naturally in `V`: `f⁻¹ h_V ≅ h_{X ×_Y V}` as functors of `V`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso_app_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
Under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and the Yoneda bijections for sheaves,
precomposition with the component of `smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso` at `V` is the
identity on sections over `X ×_Y V`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso_app_hom_comp (V : Y.Etale)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (g : (smallEtaleTopology X).uliftYoneda.{max (u + 1) v}.obj
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange f).obj V) ⟶ F) :
    (smallEtaleTopology Y).uliftYonedaEquiv
        ((((smallEtaleBaseChange f).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type (max (u + 1) v))
          (smallEtaleTopology Y) (smallEtaleTopology X)).homEquiv _ _)
            (((smallEtalePullbackRepresentableNatIso.{u, v} f).app V).hom ≫ g)) =
      (smallEtaleTopology X).uliftYonedaEquiv g

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous_obj_obj_obj
registrations.comment:
for a continuous functor `u : C₂ ⥤ C₁` the direct image on sheaves is given
  by `f_* F (V) = F (u V)`

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_isTerminal
registrations.comment:
a continuous `u` carrying a final object to a final object and preserving
  fibre products has an exact left adjoint `f⁻¹` of `f_*`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_Γ_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q5.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. For every degree `p`
and every filtered system `F` of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the canonical map

> `colim_i H^p_étale(X, F_i) ⟶ H^p_étale(X, colim_i F_i)`

is an isomorphism: taking cohomology of the étale site of `X` commutes with filtered colimits.

Étale cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections, which is sections over the final
object `X ⟶ X` of the small étale site; that object is quasi-compact and separated over `X`, so
this is the case `U = X` of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_sheafSections_smallEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_Γ_smallEtale (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (p : ℕ)
    {I : Type (max (u + 1) v)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F
      ((Sheaf.Γ X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerived p))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap_app_constantComplex_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q5 for the canonical map of Tag 0GJN on constant coefficients.** The locus where
the canonical map `α_{K,x,t}` is an isomorphism on constant coefficients is closed under filtered
colimits of the coefficient group: if `M` is the colimit of a filtered system `N` of abelian
groups and `α` is invertible on the constant complex with value `N i` for every `i`, then it is
invertible on the constant complex with value `M`.

A map of `D(Ab)` is invertible as soon as it is so on cohomology in every degree, and in each
degree both sides are functors of the coefficient group commuting with filtered colimits: below
degree zero both vanish, and in degree `p ≥ 0` the stalk side is `M ↦ (constant sheaf M)_x` placed
in degree zero while the sections side is `H^p_étale(F_{x,t}, -)` of the inverse image of the
constant sheaf. The variety of vanishing cycles is affine, hence quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so [Stacks, Tag 03Q5] on its small étale site applies.

See the module docstring for why this is not phrased as preservation of filtered colimits by
`α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap_app_constantComplex_of_isColimit
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X S : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (f : X ⟶ S) (x : GeometricPoint X)
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f)))
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (N : I ⥤ Ab.{u + 1})
    (c : Cocone N) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hi : ∀ i, IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app
      (smallEtaleConstantComplexAb X (N.obj i)))) :
    IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app
      (smallEtaleConstantComplexAb X c.pt))
declarations.comment: for the canonical map of Tag 0GJN at a variety of vanishing cycles, in the unbounded derived category: the locus where the map is invertible on constant coefficients is closed under filtered colimits of the coefficient group

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.ColimitBaseChange.isIso_colimitDesc_algebraCohomologyCocone
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a ring, `(B_i)` a directed system of `A`-algebras with colimit `B`, `f : X ⟶ Spec A`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and `F` an abelian sheaf on `X_étale`. With
`Y_i = Spec B_i ×_{Spec A} X`, `Y = Spec B ×_{Spec A} X` and `G_i`, `G` the inverse images of `F`,
the restriction maps exhibit `H^p(Y, G)` as `colim_i H^p(Y_i, G_i)`, for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimitDesc_algebraCohomologyCocone [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (hcB : IsColimit cB) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso (colimit.desc (algebraCohomologyDiagram A B f F n)
      (algebraCohomologyCocone A B cB f F n))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BaseChangeAlgebraSystem.etaleCohomologyColimit_baseChange_systemLimit_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q6 for an affine `X`, at the canonical limit.** This is
`etaleCohomologyColimit_baseChange_isColimit`
instantiated at `cY = systemLimitCone T X Z`, so that the scheme the cohomology on the left is
taken over is the honest `Y = (lim_i Z_i) ×_T X`: with `T = Spec A`, `Z_i = Spec B_i` and
`B = colim_i B_i` this is `Spec B ×_{Spec A} X`, by Stacks 01YW
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.affineLimitCone`, through `overLimitCone_pt_iso`).
declarations.statement:
def etaleCohomologyColimit_baseChange_systemLimit_isColimit
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (X : Over T) (Z : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over T)
    [IsAffine T] [IsAffine X.left] [∀ i, IsAffine (Z.obj i).left]
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (hD : ∀ i, B.Contains ((baseChange T X Z).obj i))
    (hY : B.Contains (systemLimitCone T X Z).pt)
    (F : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.AbelianSheafSystem.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (bcSys T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY))
    (𝒢 : Sheaf (bcPrecoverage T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z)
      (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY).toGrothendieck Ab.{u + 1})
    (ι : ∀ j, (F.obj j).obj ⟶ (bcToLimitSmall T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z)
      (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY j).op ⋙ 𝒢.obj)
    (hcolim : IsColimitPresentation.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (bcSys T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcToLimitSmall T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcToLimitSmall_transition T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z)
        (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcPrecoverage T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY) F 𝒢 ι)
    (i : (bcSys T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY).I) (p : ℕ)
    (E : CohomologyCocone.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (bcSys T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcToLimitSmall T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcToLimitSmall_transition T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z)
        (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY)
      (bcPrecoverage T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z) (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY) F 𝒢 ι i
      (bcLevelTerminal T X Z (systemLimitCone T X Z)
        (isLimitSystemLimitCone T X Z) B hD hY i) p) :
    IsColimit E.cocone
declarations.comment: the case of an AFFINE `X`: the source allows `X ⟶ Spec(A)` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the passage from an affine `X` to a general qcqs one is the Cech descent along a finite affine cover, which this library does not carry. The system is geometric rather than ring-level: `T`, the `Z_i` and `X` are affine schemes over `T`, and `A`, `B_i`, `B = colim B_i` are reached through `Spec(colim B_i) = lim Spec B_i` of Stacks 01YW, no `CommRingCat`-level wrapper taking a ring and a functor `I ⟶ CommRingCat` being stated. The base change is written `Z_i ×_T X`. The cohomology is the right-derived `sheafSections` of Stacks 09YP on the small AFFINE etale sites, inherited from `etaleCohomologyColimit_isColimit_of_affine`, and is NOT yet identified with the mainstream `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleCohomologyFunctor`: the 04HR half of that identification is supplied here by `affineEtaleCohomologyFunctorIso`, but transporting cohomology across `AsSmall.equiv` onto the universe-raised site Stacks 09YP is stated on does not exist in this library

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleCohomology_specBaseChange_colimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03Q6].** Let `A` be a ring, `I` a nonempty directed set, `(B_i)` a system of
`A`-algebras over `I` (a functor `B : I ⥤ Under A`) and `cB` a colimit cocone of it, with vertex
`B = colim_i B_i`. Let `g : X ⟶ Spec(A)` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `F` an abelian
sheaf on `X_étale`. Write `Y_i = Spec(B_i) ×_{Spec A} X`, `Y = Spec(B) ×_{Spec A} X` and `G_i`,
`G` for the inverse images of `F` along the projections to `X`. Then for every `p`,

`H^p_étale(Y, G) = colim_i H^p_étale(Y_i, G_i)`,

the colimit taken along the restriction maps of the morphisms `Y_j ⟶ Y_i` (for `i ≤ j`) and
`Y ⟶ Y_i`. The colimit is stated elementwise, which over a directed index and with abelian
groups is the assertion that the cocone is a colimit: every class on `Y` comes from some `Y_i` (the
inverse image of `G_i` on `Y` identified with `G` by the composition isomorphism of inverse
images), and a class on `Y_i` which dies on `Y` already dies on some `Y_j`, `j ≥ i`.

The proof is the source's: this is [Stacks, Tag 09YQ] at the inverse system of the `Y_i`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleCohomologyBaseChangeColimit`), the limit `Spec(B) = lim Spec(B_i)`
being the image of the colimit `B` under `Spec`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomology_specBaseChange_colimit (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (I : Type u) [Preorder I]
    [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (B : I ⥤ Under A) (cB : Cocone B) (hcB : IsColimit cB)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (g : X ⟶ Spec A) [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (p : ℕ) :
    (∀ η : Sheaf.H.{u + 1}
        ((etaleAbelianInverseImage.{u, 0} (pullback.snd (Spec.map cB.pt.hom) g)).obj F) p,
      ∃ (i : I)
        (ξ : Sheaf.H.{u + 1}
          ((etaleAbelianInverseImage.{u, 0} (pullback.snd (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g)).obj F) p),
        (etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, u + 1}
          (pullback.map (Spec.map cB.pt.hom) g (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g
            (Spec.map (cB.ι.app i).right) (𝟙 X) (𝟙 (Spec A))
            (by rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, Under.w]; rfl) (by simp)) _ p ξ).comp
          (Ext.mk₀ ((etaleAbelianInverseImageCompIso'.{u, 0}
            (pullback.map (Spec.map cB.pt.hom) g (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g
              (Spec.map (cB.ι.app i).right) (𝟙 X) (𝟙 (Spec A))
              (by rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, Under.w]; rfl) (by simp))
            (pullback.snd (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g) (pullback.snd (Spec.map cB.pt.hom) g)
            (by simp only [pullback.map, pullback.lift_snd, Category.comp_id])).app F).inv)
          (add_zero p) = η) ∧
    (∀ (i : I)
        (ξ : Sheaf.H.{u + 1}
          ((etaleAbelianInverseImage.{u, 0} (pullback.snd (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g)).obj F) p),
        etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, u + 1}
          (pullback.map (Spec.map cB.pt.hom) g (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g
            (Spec.map (cB.ι.app i).right) (𝟙 X) (𝟙 (Spec A))
            (by rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, Under.w]; rfl) (by simp)) _ p ξ = 0 →
        ∃ (j : I) (a : i ⟶ j),
          etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, u + 1}
            (pullback.map (Spec.map (B.obj j).hom) g (Spec.map (B.obj i).hom) g
              (Spec.map (B.map a).right) (𝟙 X) (𝟙 (Spec A))
              (by rw [Category.comp_id, ← Spec.map_comp, Under.w]) (by simp)) _ p ξ = 0)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, at the source's hypotheses: a ring `A`, a directed set `I` (nonempty, as directed sets are in the source), a system of `A`-algebras `B : I ⥤ Under A` with a colimit cocone `cB` (so `B = colim B_i` is `cB.pt`), a quasi-compact and quasi-separated `g : X ⟶ Spec A`, an abelian sheaf `F` on Mathlib's small etale site of `X` and every degree `p`. `Y_i` and `Y` are the fibre products `Spec B_i ×_{Spec A} X` and `Spec B ×_{Spec A} X` (the factors in Mathlib's `pullback` order), `G_i`, `G` the inverse images of `F` along their projections to `X`, and the cohomology is the library's etale cohomology `Sheaf.H` on the small etale sites, with coefficients in `AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}`, the first universe in which these sites have sheafification. The equality of the source is stated as the elementwise form of a filtered colimit of abelian groups along the restriction maps: joint surjectivity of the maps `H^p(Y_i, G_i) to H^p(Y, G)` and eventual vanishing of a class killed on `Y`, which over a directed index is exactly the assertion that the cohomology cocone is colimiting. The proof is the source's, Tag 09YQ at the inverse system of base changes.

declarations.name: Stacks.HigherDirectImage.higherDirectImageComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q8 for abelian sheaves.** The higher direct image `R^p f_*` is the sheafification
of the presheaf `V ↦ H^p_ét(X ×_Y V, F)`, by a natural isomorphism whose components are the
counit-normalized objectwise comparison `higherDirectImageSheafificationIso`, and whose
cohomology presheaf has the derived restriction maps of sections.
declarations.statement:
public def higherDirectImageComparison (p : ℕ) :
    HigherDirectImageComparison.{u, w} B f p

declarations.name: Stacks.HigherDirectImage.derivedPushforwardComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q8, unbounded complexes.** The canonical comparison of `Rf_*` with the sheafified
derived presheaf of sections over the étale base changes is invertible, evaluating the derived
presheaf of sections at `V` is the total right derived functor of sections over `X ×_Y V`, and
the restriction maps of the hypercohomology presheaf are the derived restriction maps of
sections.
declarations.statement: public theorem derivedPushforwardComparison : DerivedPushforwardComparison.{u, w} B f

declarations.name: Stacks.HigherDirectImage.higherDirectImageStalkCohomologyPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q8 at a geometric point.** The stalk at `s` of the `p`-th higher direct image of
`F` along `f` is the stalk at `s` of the cohomology presheaf `V ↦ H^p_ét(X ×_Y V, F)`, which by
definition of the stalk is the colimit of that presheaf over the étale neighbourhoods of `s`.

This is the objectwise comparison of Stacks 03Q8, `higherDirectImageSheafificationIso`, followed
by the invariance of a stalk under sheafification,
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkSheafificationIso`.
declarations.statement:
public def higherDirectImageStalkCohomologyPresheafIso
    (F : Sheaf (JX B (X := X)) AddCommGrpCat.{w}) (p : ℕ) :
    etaleStalk B Y.obj Y.property s (((pushforward.{u, w} B f).rightDerived p).obj F).obj ≅
      etaleStalk B Y.obj Y.property s (preimageCohomologyPresheaf.{u, w} B f F p)
declarations.comment: the stalk form: the stalk at a geometric point `s` of `R^p f_* F` is the stalk at `s` of the cohomology presheaf `V ↦ H^p(X ×_Y V, F)`, hence the colimit of that presheaf over the étale neighbourhoods of `s`. This is the first display in the source's proof of Stacks 03Q9, which the source attributes to this tag. The base, the morphism `f` and the geometric point are arbitrary. It is NOT Stacks 03Q9: that tag identifies the colimit with the cohomology of the base change of `X` to `Spec(O^{sh}_{Y,s})`, which is Stacks 03Q6 and is not available in a consumable shape

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.higherBaseChangeStalkHom_comp_higherDirectImageStalkIso_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q9, compatibility with base change along a commutative square.** Write
`θ = AlgebraicGeometry.higherDirectImageStalkIso` for the isomorphisms
`(R^q g_* F)_{f(x)} ≅ H^q(T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}), F)` and
`(R^q h_* e⁻¹F)_x ≅ H^q(Y ×_X Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}), e⁻¹F)`. For a commutative square
`h ≫ f = e ≫ g` with `g`, `h` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `θ` at `x` after the stalk `b` at
`x` of the base change map `f⁻¹ R^q g_* F ⟶ R^q h_* e⁻¹ F` is `θ` at `f(x)` followed by the pull
back `ρ` along `κ = AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationBaseChangeSquareMap`, the morphism
`Y ×_X Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}) ⟶ T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)})` given by `e` and by the morphism `m`
of strict henselizations: `θ ∘ b = ρ ∘ θ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherBaseChangeStalkHom_comp_higherDirectImageStalkIso_hom (q : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1}) :
    ((higherBaseChangeStalkHom f g h e w x.hom).app q).app F ≫
        (higherDirectImageStalkIso B₁ hX h x q ((smallEtalePullbackAb e).obj F)).hom =
      (higherDirectImageStalkIso B₂ hS g (x.map f) q F).hom ≫
        AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (etaleCohomologyPullback
          (strictHenselizationBaseChangeSquareMap B₁ B₂ hX hS w x m hm)
          ((strictHenselizationBaseChangeSquarePullbackHom B₁ B₂ hX hS w x m hm).app F) q)
declarations.comment: compatibility of the isomorphisms with the base change map of a commutative square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkHigherDirectImageIso
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `s` a geometric point of `S` and
`p : X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ X` the projection,
`(R^n f_* F)_s ≅ H^n_ét(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)` for every abelian sheaf `F` on `X_étale`
and every `n`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkHigherDirectImageIso (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (n : ℕ) :
    (smallEtaleStalkAb s.hom).obj (((smallEtalePushforwardAb f).rightDerived n).obj F) ≅
      ((Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s))
          Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerived n).obj
        ((smallEtalePullbackAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)).obj F)
declarations.comment: first assertion, for an abelian sheaf `F` on `X_étale`: `(R^n f_* F)_s = H^n_ét(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p^{-1}F)`, with `R^n` Mathlib's right derived functors of direct image and of global sections on the small étale sites; the strict henselization is taken inside a big étale site `B` containing `S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkDerivedPushforwardHomologyIso
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `K` in `D⁺(X_étale)` and `n : ℤ`,
`(R^n f_* K)_s ≅ H^n(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K)`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkDerivedPushforwardHomologyIso
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1})) (n : ℤ) :
    (smallEtaleStalkAb s.hom).obj ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
        ((smallEtalePushforwardAb f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj K)) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor Ab.{u + 1} n).obj
        ((Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s))
          Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
          ((smallEtalePullbackAb
            (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K))
declarations.comment: second assertion, for `K` in `D^+(X_étale)` and `n` in `ℤ`: `(R^n f_* K)_s = H^n_ét(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p^{-1}K)`, the cohomology objects of the right derived functors on the bounded below derived categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkDerivedPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
For `f : X ⟶ S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated,
`(Rf_* K)_s ≅ RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K)` in `D⁺(Ab)`, naturally in `K ∈ D⁺(X_étale)`.
declarations.statement:
def stalkDerivedPushforwardIso :
    (smallEtalePullbackAb
        (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)).mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙
        (Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s))
          Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ≅
      (smallEtalePushforwardAb f).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        (smallEtaleStalkAb s.hom).mapDerivedCategoryPlus
declarations.comment: third assertion: `(Rf_* K)_s = RΓ_ét(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p^{-1}K)` in `D^+(Ab)`, as an isomorphism of functors on `D^+(X_étale)`, the stalk and `p^{-1}` acting degreewise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.higherDirectImageStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q9: the stalks of the higher direct images.** Let `g : T ⟶ S` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, `F` an abelian sheaf on `T_étale` and `s`
a geometric point of `S`. Then `(R^n g_* F)_s = H^n_étale(T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)`,
where `p : T ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ T` is the projection. The isomorphism is natural in `F`,
compatible with the connecting morphisms (it is the component of
`AlgebraicGeometry.higherDirectImageStalkComparison`), and in degree zero it is the canonical map
`AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb`.

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyHenselian.higherDirectImageEtaleStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03Q9 over a strictly henselian base.** The stalk at `s` of the `n`-th higher direct
image of `F` along `f : X ⟶ Spec R` is the `n`-th étale cohomology group of `X` with
coefficients in `F`.
declarations.statement:
public def higherDirectImageEtaleStalkIso
    (hs : s.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)) (n : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    etaleStalk B (Spec (.of R)) hS s ((higherDirectImage B R hS f n).obj F).obj ≅
      ((smallEtaleGlobalSections B X).rightDerived n).obj F
declarations.comment: conditional on the base being `Spec R` for a strictly henselian local ring `R` and the geometric point lying over its closed point, so that the strict henselization is `R` and the base change of the source is `X` itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_cechCohomology_isZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QB.** The direct image of an injective abelian sheaf on the small étale site of
`X` has vanishing positive-degree Čech cohomology for every family of morphisms in the small
étale site of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforward_injective_cechCohomology_isZero
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (I : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    [Injective I]
    (E : Covering.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (SmallEtale B Y.obj Y.property))
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (Stacks.CechSite.cechCohomology E.2
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj I).obj p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_pushforward_of_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QB, with no homological-algebra side condition.** The direct image of an injective
abelian étale sheaf is acyclic for a further direct image.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_pushforward` with all three of its
instance binders discharged, exactly as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_sections_of_smallEtale`: sheafification
comes from Mathlib's plus construction at the coefficient universe `u + 1` and the enough
injectives from `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_succ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_pushforward_of_smallEtale
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (I : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    [Injective I] :
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
      (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)).rightAcyclic
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_sections_of_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QB, with no homological-algebra side condition.** The direct image of an injective
abelian étale sheaf is acyclic for sections over any object of the small étale site of the
target.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_sections` with both of its instance
binders discharged: abelian presheaves on the small étale site of a scheme in `Scheme.{u}` have a
sheafification with coefficients in `AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}` by Mathlib's plus construction, the
site having its objects in `Type (u + 1)`, and the resulting abelian category of sheaves has
enough injectives because `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_succ` makes it
Grothendieck abelian at that coefficient universe.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforward_injective_rightAcyclic_sections_of_smallEtale
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (I : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    [Injective I] (V : SmallEtale B Y.obj Y.property) :
    ((sheafSections (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (Opposite.op V)).rightAcyclic
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_abutsTo_leraySpectralSequence_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**The Leray spectral sequence for the small étale site** (Stacks 03QC). Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be
a morphism in a big étale site and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X`.
There is a cohomological spectral sequence with second page

```
E₂^{p,q} ≅ H^p_ét(Y, R^q f_* F),
```

the étale cohomology of `Y` with coefficients in the higher direct images of `F`, which abuts
to the graded family `n ↦ H^n_ét(X, F)` of étale cohomology groups of `X`: some finite
decreasing filtration of each `H^n_ét(X, F)` has the terms `E_∞^{p,n-p}` as its graded pieces.

Both the second page and the abutment are taken in the derived-functor form of étale
cohomology, `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedPlus` of global sections, and `R^q f_*` is the
`q`-th right derived functor of direct image.

This is `exists_abutsTo_leraySpectralSequence_smallEtale_sections` for the final object of the
small étale site of `Y`, whose base change is a final object of the small étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_abutsTo_leraySpectralSequence_smallEtale
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    ∃ E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} 0,
      (∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty ((E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (p, q) ≅
        ((smallEtaleGlobalSections B Y).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
          ((Stacks.HigherDirectImage.pushforward.{u, u + 1} B f).rightDerivedPlus q |>.obj
            F))) ∧
      SpectralSequence.AbutsTo E
        (fun n => ((smallEtaleGlobalSections B X).rightDerivedPlus n).obj F)

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_etale_finite_factors_positiveDim_remainder
declarations.doc:
After an étale base change preserving the residue field at `p`, a finite type
algebra splits into finitely many finite factors, each with exactly one prime
over `p'`, and a factor whose fibre has no zero-dimensional irreducible
component.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_finite_factors_positiveDim_remainder
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : Algebra.Etale R R')
      (p' : Ideal R') (_ : p'.IsPrime) (_ : p'.LiesOver p)
      (n : ℕ) (e : Fin (n + 1) → R' ⊗[R] S)
      (_ : CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents e)
      (r : Fin n → Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S))
      (_ : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime) (_ : ∀ i, (r i).LiesOver p'),
      Function.Bijective (Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p p' (Algebra.ofId _ _) (p'.over_def p)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, Module.Finite R' (Localization.Away (e i.castSucc))) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, e i.castSucc ∉ r i) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin n) (q : Ideal (R' ⊗[R] S)), q.IsPrime → q.LiesOver p' →
        e i.castSucc ∉ q → q = r i) ∧
      (∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents
          (PrimeSpectrum (p'.Fiber (Localization.Away (e (Fin.last n))))),
        1 ≤ topologicalKrullDim Z)

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.henselian_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QH.** The five standard characterizations of a henselian local ring:
henselianness, coprime factorization lifting, decomposition of module-finite algebras,
splitting the finite part of finite type algebras, and splitting pointed étale
algebras.
declarations.statement:

    List.TFAE [HenselianLocalRing R,
      HasCoprimeFactorizationLifting R,
      FiniteAlgebrasSplitIntoLocalFactors.{u, v} R,
      FiniteTypeAlgebrasSplitOffFiniteLocalFactors.{u, v} R,
      PointedEtaleAlgebrasSplit.{u, v} R]

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_algEquiv_pi_puncturedKummerAlgebra
declarations.doc:
Every étale algebra over `ℂ⟦t⟧` is a finite product of trivial factors and
punctured Kummer extensions of positive degree.
declarations.statement:

    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Algebra (PowerSeries ℂ) A]
    [Algebra.Etale (PowerSeries ℂ) A] :
    ∃ (ι κ : Type*) (_ : Finite ι) (_ : Finite κ) (n : κ → ℕ),
      (∀ j, 0 < n j) ∧
      Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[PowerSeries ℂ]
        (ι → PowerSeries ℂ) × (∀ j, puncturedKummerAlgebra (n j)))

maps into `D(t)`.
