declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleCover_has_section
declarations.doc:
An étale covering of `Spec ℂ⟦t⟧` has a member whose structure morphism
admits a section, so the identity cover refines it.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCover_has_section
    (𝒰 : (Spec (.of (PowerSeries ℂ))).Cover Scheme.etalePrecoverage) :
    ∃ i : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ s : Spec (.of (PowerSeries ℂ)) ⟶ 𝒰.X i,
      s ≫ 𝒰.f i = 𝟙 (Spec (.of (PowerSeries ℂ)))

declarations.name: exists_algEquiv_pi_henselianLocalRing_of_module_finite
declarations.doc:
A finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a finite product of
henselian local rings, each finite over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algEquiv_pi_henselianLocalRing_of_module_finite
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HenselianLocalRing R]
    (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Module.Finite R A] :
    ∃ (ι : Type v) (_ : Finite ι) (B : ι → Type v)
      (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (B i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra R (B i))
      (_ : ∀ i, HenselianLocalRing (B i)),
      (∀ i, Module.Finite R (B i)) ∧ Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[R] ∀ i, B i)

declarations.name: StrictlyHenselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
A commutative ring is strictly henselian if it is a henselian local ring and its
residue field is separably closed.
declarations.statement:
class StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop extends
  HenselianLocalRing R, IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R)

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.henselizationTower
declarations.doc:
The canonical henselization/strict-henselization tower associated to a local ring and a
chosen separable closure of its residue field.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def henselizationTower (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep] : HenselizationTower R κsep
declarations.comment: existence, flat local maps, and parts (1), (2), and (4)

declarations.name: HenselianLocalRing.existsUnique_isLocalHom_of_ind_etale
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the henselization, in existential form** (Stacks 04GS). Let
`(R, 𝔪, κ)` be a local ring, let `Rh` be a local `R`-algebra with `R → Rh` local which is a
filtered colimit of étale `R`-algebras and has residue field `κ`, and let `Sh` be a henselian
local ring with `R → Sh` local. Then there is exactly one `R`-algebra map `Rh → Sh` that is a
local ring map. This is what makes the maps `R → R^h → R^{sh}` of Tag 03QL canonical: applied
to `Rh = R^h` and `Sh = R^{sh}` it pins the map out of the henselization uniquely.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HenselianLocalRing.existsUnique_isLocalHom_of_ind_etale
    {R : Type u} {Rh : Type v} {Sh : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing Rh] [CommRing Sh]
    [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsLocalRing Rh] [HenselianLocalRing Sh] [Algebra R Rh] [Algebra R Sh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Rh)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Sh)]
    (hind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{max u v} R).ind.{max u v}
      (CommAlgCat.of R (ULift.{u} Rh)))
    (hres : Function.Surjective (ResidueField.map (algebraMap R Rh))) :
    ∃! f : Rh →ₐ[R] Sh, IsLocalHom f
declarations.comment: canonicity of the map from the henselization

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyHenselian.subsingleton_etaleCohomology_smallEtaleTopology
declarations.doc:
Positive-degree étale cohomology of an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of the
spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_etaleCohomology_smallEtaleTopology
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (Spec (.of R)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of R)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} F p)
declarations.comment: vanishing of positive-degree étale cohomology, on the small étale site

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyHenselian.isIso_globalSectionsToEtaleStalk
declarations.doc:
For a strictly henselian local ring, the canonical global-sections-to-stalk
map is an isomorphism for every sheaf of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSectionsToEtaleStalk
    [StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    (hs : s.LiesOver (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R))
    [HasWeakSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      (Type (u + 1))]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      (Type (u + 1))) :
    IsIso (globalSectionsToEtaleStalk B R hS s F)
declarations.comment: global sections equal the closed geometric stalk

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyHenselian.globalSections_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
Global sections of abelian étale sheaves on a strictly henselian local
scheme are exact. As a right adjoint, this functor already preserves limits.
declarations.statement:
public instance globalSections_preservesFiniteColimits
    [StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}] :
    PreservesFiniteColimits
      (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyHenselian.subsingleton_etaleCohomology
declarations.doc:
Positive-degree étale cohomology of an abelian sheaf over a strictly
henselian local scheme vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_etaleCohomology
    [StrictlyHenselianLocalRing R]
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of R)) hS)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} F p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.etalePushforward_exact_of_isFinite
declarations.doc: Direct image of abelian étale sheaves along a finite morphism is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etalePushforward_exact_of_isFinite :
    exactFunctor _ _ (etalePushforward.{u, u + 1} B fbar)
declarations.comment: exactness of direct image along a finite morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePushforwardStalkToProduct_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QP, part (1), sheaves of sets.** For a finite morphism the
comparison map from the stalk of a direct image to the product of the stalks over the lifts of
the geometric point is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePushforwardStalkToProduct_bijective
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)] (y : GeometricPoint Y.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (Type (u + 1))) :
    Function.Bijective (finitePushforwardStalkToProduct B f y F)
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePushforwardStalkEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QP, part (1), sheaves of sets.** The stalk at a geometric point `y`
of the direct image of a sheaf of sets along a finite morphism is the product of the stalks of
the sheaf over the lifts of `y`.
declarations.statement:
public def finitePushforwardStalkEquiv
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)] (y : GeometricPoint Y.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (Type (u + 1))) :
    etaleStalk B Y.1 Y.property y
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.1 Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).obj F).obj ≃
      (∀ x : {g : y.source ⟶ X.1 // g ≫ B.inclusion.map f = y.hom},
        etaleStalk B X.1 X.property
          (geometricPointLift (B.inclusion.map f) y x) F.obj)
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePushforwardStalkEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QP, part (1), sheaves of sets.** Each component of the product
decomposition of the stalk is the canonical stalk map at the corresponding lift.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finitePushforwardStalkEquiv_apply
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)] (y : GeometricPoint Y.1)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (z : etaleStalk B Y.1 Y.property y
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B Y.1 Y.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).obj F).obj)
    (x : {g : y.source ⟶ X.1 // g ≫ B.inclusion.map f = y.hom}) :
    finitePushforwardStalkEquiv B f y F z x =
      finitePushforwardStalkComponent B f y F x z
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum
declarations.doc:
The stalk of a finite direct image is canonically the direct sum of its
stalks at the geometric lifts.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalk B Y.1 Y.property y
        (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (SmallEtale.topology B Y.1 Y.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).obj F).obj ≅
      ∐ fun x : GeometricLifts B f y =>
        AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalk B X.1 X.property
          (geometricPointLift
            (B.inclusion.map f) y x) F.obj
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum_germ
declarations.doc:
On each component, the finite direct-image stalk decomposition takes a
section over a neighborhood of `y` to its germ at a lift `x`, after pulling
the neighborhood back to `X`. The auxiliary neighborhood `V` is any étale
neighborhood of `x` mapping to that pullback and carrying the specified point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum_germ
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (x : GeometricLifts B f y)
    (U : (geometricPointFiber B Y.1 Y.property y).Elements)
    (V : (geometricPointFiber B X.1 X.property
      (geometricPointLift
        (B.inclusion.map f) y x)).Elements)
    (t : V.1 ⟶ (smallEtaleBaseChange B f).obj U.1)
    (hU : V.2.1 ≫ (SmallEtale.toScheme B X.1 X.property).map t ≫
        B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst U.1.obj.hom f) = U.2.1)
    (hX : V.2.1 ≫ (SmallEtale.toScheme B X.1 X.property).map t ≫
        B.inclusion.map (pullback.snd U.1.obj.hom f) = x.1) :
    colimit.ι
        ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B Y.1 Y.property y)).op ⋙
          (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
            AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
            (SmallEtale.topology B Y.1 Y.property)
            (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).obj F).obj)
        (op U) ≫
      (stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum B f y F).hom ≫
      (by classical exact Limits.Sigma.π _ x) =
    F.obj.map t.op ≫
      colimit.ι
        ((CategoryOfElements.π (geometricPointFiber B X.1 X.property
          (geometricPointLift
            (B.inclusion.map f) y x))).op ⋙ F.obj)
    (op V)
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum_natural
declarations.doc: The finite direct-sum decomposition is natural in the abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum_natural
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)]
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}}
    (α : F ⟶ G) :
    etaleStalkMap B Y.1 Y.property y
        (((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (SmallEtale.topology B Y.1 Y.property)
          (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).map α) ≫
        (stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum B f y G).hom =
      (stalkPushforwardIsoDirectSum B f y F).hom ≫
    Limits.Sigma.map (fun x : GeometricLifts B f y =>
          etaleStalkMap B X.1 X.property
            (geometricPointLift
              (B.inclusion.map f) y x) α)
declarations.comment: part (1): the stalk of a finite pushforward, for abelian sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_smallEtalePushforwardAb_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**The positive higher direct images along an integral morphism vanish.** For a finite
morphism this is the acyclicity half of Stacks Project Tag 03QP, finiteness implying
integrality.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_rightDerived_smallEtalePushforwardAb_of_isIntegralHom
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero (((smallEtalePushforwardAb f).rightDerived q).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (2): vanishing of the positive higher direct images

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QP, part (2), at the coefficients of the proper base change development.** The
positive higher direct images of an abelian sheaf along an integral morphism of schemes vanish:
an integral morphism — a finite morphism, for instance — is acyclic for étale cohomology.

Direct image is exact, and applying an exact functor degreewise to an injective resolution
gives a resolution again, so the homology of the image complex vanishes in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage_of_isIntegralHom
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegralHom f]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero (((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, v} f).rightDerived q).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (2) at the coefficients of proper base change

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QP, part (2), for sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale sites of Stacks
021B.** For `f` with integral underlying morphism of schemes — a finite morphism, for instance —
the higher direct images of a sheaf of `Λ`-modules along `f` vanish: `R^q f_*ℱ = 0` for every
`q > 0`. The direct image is exact by `modulePushforward_exact_of_isIntegralHom`, and the higher
right derived functors of an exact functor vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isIntegralHom
    [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (ℱ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w r} Λ))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero (((modulePushforward.{u, max w r} B Λ f).rightDerived q).obj ℱ)
declarations.comment: part (2), for sheaves of Λ-modules on the small étale sites of Tag 021B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleEquivalenceContinuousGSet
declarations.doc:
If `L` is a separable closure of `K`, schemes étale over `K` are
equivalent to discrete continuous `Gal(L/K)`-sets. The underlying set of the
image of `X` is naturally the set of morphisms `Spec L ⟶ X` over `Spec K`,
and the action of `σ` is precomposition by `Spec.map σ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleEquivalenceContinuousGSet
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] [IsSepClosure K L] :
    ∃ E : (Spec (.of K)).Etale ≌ ContinuousGSet.{u, u} Gal(L/K),
      ∃ e : ∀ X,
        (E.functor.obj X).obj.obj.V ≃
          (separableClosureGeometricPoint K L ⟶
            (Scheme.Etale.forget (Spec (.of K))).obj X),
        (∀ {X Y} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x),
          e Y ((E.functor.map f).hom x) =
            e X x ≫ (Scheme.Etale.forget (Spec (.of K))).map f) ∧
        (∀ X (σ : Gal(L/K)) (x),
          (e X (ConcreteCategory.hom ((E.functor.obj X).obj.obj.ρ σ).asHom x)).left =
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ.toAlgHom.toRingHom) ≫ (e X x).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleSheafStalkEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03QT.**  For a geometric point of the spectrum of a field, taking stalks is an
equivalence from the small étale topos to the category of continuous sets over the absolute
Galois group, naturally identified with the stalk functor, and the Galois action on a germ
changes the geometric lift of the étale neighborhood by precomposition.
declarations.statement:
def etaleSheafStalkEquivalence :
    Σ e : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max u v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK ≌
        AlgebraicGeometry.ContinuousGSet.{u, max u v}
          (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar),
      { α : e.functor ⋙ AlgebraicGeometry.ContinuousGSet.forget
            (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) ≅
          etaleStalkFunctor.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar //
        ∀ (F : smallEtaleTopos.{u, max u v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK)
          (σ : GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar),
          letI := GeometricPoint.residueFieldAlgebra sbar
          ∀ (τ : Gal(sbar.residueField /
              (Spec (.of K)).residueField (sbar.hom default)))
            (_hτ : ∀ a : GeometricPoint.separableClosure sbar,
              (σ a : sbar.residueField) = τ (a : sbar.residueField))
            (U : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).Elements)
            (q : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).obj U.1)
            (_hq : q.1 = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom τ.toRingHom) ≫ U.2.1)
            (t : ((sheafToPresheaf _ _).obj F).obj (op U.1)),
            let V : (geometricPointFiber B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar).Elements := Functor.elementsMk _ U.1 q
            ConcreteCategory.hom (α.app F).hom
                (ConcreteCategory.hom ((e.functor.obj F).obj.obj.ρ σ).asHom
                  (ConcreteCategory.hom (α.app F).inv
                    (etaleStalkGerm.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar F U t))) =
              etaleStalkGerm.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar F V t }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field, let `sbar` be a geometric point of `Spec K` with absolute Galois group
`G`, and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `Spec K` corresponding to the
`G`-module `M`.  Then the degree-zero étale cohomology of `Spec K` with coefficients in `F` is
the group `M ^ G` of Galois invariants.
declarations.statement:
def etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})] :
    Sheaf.H.{w, max u v} F 0 ≃+ ↥(etaleStalkGaloisInvariants.{u, v} B K hK sbar F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants_coe
declarations.doc:
The identification of degree-zero étale cohomology with the Galois invariants is taking
germs at the geometric point: a cohomology class is sent to the germ of the global section which
represents it.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants_coe
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})]
    (x : Sheaf.H.{w, max u v} F 0) :
    (etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants B K hK sbar F x).1 =
      etaleGlobalSectionGerm.{u, v} B K hK sbar (abelianEtaleSheafOfSets.{u, v} B K hK F)
        (Sheaf.H.equiv₀ F (SmallEtale.finalIsTerminal B (Spec (.of K)) hK) x)
declarations.comment: part (2), the comparison is taking germs at the geometric point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants_abelianEtaleStalkGerm
declarations.doc:
Read in the abelian-group-valued stalk, the identification of degree-zero étale cohomology
with the Galois invariants sends a cohomology class to the germ, at the final pointed étale
neighbourhood, of the global section which represents it.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants_abelianEtaleStalkGerm
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v})]
    (x : Sheaf.H.{w, max u v} F 0) :
    etaleGaloisModuleAddEquivStalk.{u, v} B K hK sbar F
        (etaleH0AddEquivGaloisInvariants B K hK sbar F x).1 =
      abelianEtaleStalkGerm.{u, v} B (Spec (.of K)) hK sbar F
        (finalPointedNeighborhood B K hK sbar)
        (Sheaf.H.equiv₀ F (SmallEtale.finalIsTerminal B (Spec (.of K)) hK) x)
declarations.comment: part (2), the comparison in the abelian stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.additiveSheafHAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QU, part (3), at `𝐆_a`.**  For a field `K`, a geometric point `sbar`
of `Spec K` and every degree `q`,

`H^q_étale(Spec K, 𝐆_a) ≅ H^q(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/κ), Kˢᵉᵖ)`,

`κ` being the residue field at the image of `sbar` and `Kˢᵉᵖ` the Galois module with addition as
group law.  This is the general comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology` with its Galois
module identified at `𝐆_a` by `AlgebraicGeometry.additiveContinuousGModuleIso`.
declarations.comment: part (3) at 𝐆_a, in every degree: the degree-q étale cohomology of the spectrum of a field with coefficients in the additive group is the degree-q continuous group cohomology of the absolute Galois group with coefficients in the separable closure under addition. This is the general objectwise form of part (3) on Mathlib's small étale site, smallEtaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology, with its Galois module computed at 𝐆_a by additiveContinuousGModuleIso -- the stalk computation additiveStalkIsoSepClosure packaged with its germwise Galois equivariance additiveSectionEval_galoisFiberAction into an isomorphism of discrete Galois modules. Nothing is assumed of the field and nothing is carried. NOT proved here: parts (1) and (2) of the tag, which are separate registrations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleRightDerivedGammaIsoContinuousGroupCohomologyFunctor
declarations.doc:
In every degree `q`, the `q`-th right derived functor of the global sections functor
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Γ` of the small étale site of `Spec K` is the stalk equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence` followed by the `q`-th continuous group
cohomology functor of the absolute Galois group.
declarations.comment: part (3), as an isomorphism of functors, with étale cohomology as the right derived functor of global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleSheafCohomologyIsoContinuousGroupCohomologyFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field, let `sbar` be a geometric point of `Spec K` and let `G` be the absolute
Galois group at `sbar`. For every `q`, Mathlib's degree-`q` sheaf cohomology functor
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.functorH` on the small étale site of `Spec K` is the stalk equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence` followed by the degree-`q` continuous group
cohomology functor of `G`.
declarations.comment: part (3), in every degree, as a natural isomorphism of functors: sheaf cohomology on the small étale site of the spectrum of a field is the stalk equivalence of 04JQ followed by the continuous group cohomology functor of 04JR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field, let `sbar` be a geometric point of `Spec K` with absolute Galois group `G`,
and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `Spec K`, corresponding to the
`G`-module `M` under `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence`. Then for every `q`

`H^q_étale(Spec K, F) = H^q(G, M)`.
declarations.statement:
def etaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} F q ≃+
      continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1} (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) q
        ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj F)
declarations.comment: part (3): in every degree q, the degree-q étale cohomology of the spectrum of a field with coefficients in an abelian sheaf is the degree-q continuous group cohomology of the absolute Galois group with coefficients in the sheaf's module of 04JQ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleDerivedGlobalSectionsIsoDerivedGaloisInvariants
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field, let `sbar` be a geometric point of `Spec K` with absolute Galois group `G`,
let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `Spec K` and let `M` be the discrete
`G`-module it corresponds to under `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence`. Then in
the derived category of abelian groups there is a canonical isomorphism

`RΓ(Spec K, F) ≅ RΓ_G(M)`

between the derived global sections of `F` and the derived `G`-invariants of `M`, both computed
on bounded below derived categories and mapped to the unbounded one by `DerivedCategory.Plus.ι`.
declarations.statement:
def etaleDerivedGlobalSectionsIsoDerivedGaloisInvariants
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
        ((Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK)
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
        ((continuousGModuleInvariants.{u, u + 1}
          (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar)).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
              ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj F)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafCohomologyIsoContinuousGroupCohomologyFunctor
declarations.doc:
For every `q`, Mathlib's degree-`q` sheaf cohomology functor on its small étale site of
`Spec K` is the restriction `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafRestriction` to the site
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology`, followed by the stalk equivalence
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence` and the degree-`q` continuous group
cohomology functor of the absolute Galois group.
declarations.comment: part (3), in every degree, on Mathlib's small étale site of the spectrum of a field: sheaf cohomology there is restriction to the site of 021B followed by the stalk equivalence of 04JQ and the continuous group cohomology functor of 04JR

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
declarations.doc:
For every abelian sheaf `F` on Mathlib's small étale site of `Spec K` and every degree `q`,

`H^q_étale(Spec K, F) = H^q(G, M)`,

`M` being the Galois module of the restriction of `F` to the site
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.topology`.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
    (F : Sheaf ((Spec (.of K) : Scheme.{u})).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (q : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} F q ≃+
      continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1} (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) q
        ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj
          ((smallEtaleSheafRestriction B K hK).obj F))
declarations.comment: part (3) on Mathlib's small étale site, objectwise: the degree-q étale cohomology group of the spectrum of a field with coefficients in an abelian sheaf is the degree-q continuous group cohomology of the absolute Galois group with coefficients in the sheaf's Galois module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGlobalSectionsIsoInvariants
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QU, part (2), as an isomorphism of functors.**  Over a field, global
sections of an abelian étale sheaf and the Galois invariants of its module of Tag 04JQ are
isomorphic functors to abelian groups, by taking germs at the geometric point.
declarations.comment: part (2), as a natural isomorphism of functors, in the abelian-group encoding of discrete Galois modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGlobalSectionsIsoContinuousGModuleInvariants
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QU, part (2), as an isomorphism of functors, in the vocabulary of
continuous group cohomology.**  Global sections of an abelian étale sheaf over a field are the
`continuousGModuleInvariants` of the discrete Galois module of Tag 04JQ.
declarations.comment: part (2), as a natural isomorphism of functors, in the coefficient category of continuousGroupCohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGammaIsoGaloisInvariants
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QU, part (2), functorially, for the global sections functor of the
site.**  The global sections functor `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Γ` of the small étale site of the
spectrum of a field is the functor of Galois invariants of the module of Tag 04JQ, in the
abelian-group encoding of discrete Galois modules.  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGlobalSectionsIsoInvariants` with sections over the final object
rewritten as global sections.
declarations.statement:
def etaleGammaIsoGaloisInvariants
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}] :
    Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} ≅
      (abelianEtaleStalkEquivalence.{u, v} B K hK sbar).functor ⋙
        continuousGAddCommGrpInvariants.{u, max u v}
          (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar)
declarations.comment: part (2), as an isomorphism of functors on the global sections functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleGammaIsoContinuousGModuleInvariants
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QU, part (2), functorially and in the module encoding, for the global
sections functor of the site.**  The global sections functor `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Γ` of the
small étale site of the spectrum of a field is the stalk equivalence of Tag 04JQ followed by the
functor of `G`-invariants of discrete modules over the absolute Galois group.
declarations.statement:
def etaleGammaIsoContinuousGModuleInvariants
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}] :
    Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B (Spec (.of K)) hK) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} ≅
      (etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, v} B K hK sbar).functor ⋙
        continuousGModuleInvariants.{u, max u v}
          (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar)
declarations.comment: part (2), as an isomorphism of functors with the module invariants

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.multiplicativeSheafHAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology
declarations.doc:
For a field `K`, a geometric point `sbar` of `Spec K` and every degree `q`,

`H^q_étale(Spec K, 𝐆_m) ≅ H^q(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/κ), (Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ)`,

`κ` being the residue field at the image of `sbar`.
declarations.comment: part (3) at 𝐆_m, in every degree: the degree-q étale cohomology of the spectrum of a field with coefficients in the multiplicative group is the degree-q continuous group cohomology of the absolute Galois group with coefficients in the units of the separable closure. This is the general objectwise form of part (3) on Mathlib's small étale site, smallEtaleSheafCohomologyAddEquivContinuousGroupCohomology, with its Galois module computed at 𝐆_m by multiplicativeContinuousGModuleIso -- the stalk computation multiplicativeStalkIsoUnits packaged with its germwise Galois equivariance multiplicativeSectionEval_galoisFiberAction into an isomorphism of discrete Galois modules. Nothing is assumed of the field and nothing is carried. NOT proved here: parts (1) and (2) of the tag, which are separate registrations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stacks03QV
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03QV, whole.**  Sheaves on `Spec(K)_étale` for `K` a field, with
`G = Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)` the absolute Galois group.

Under the equivalence of Tag 04JQ between abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `Spec K` and
discrete `G`-modules: (1) the constant sheaf `𝐙/n𝐙` corresponds to `𝐙/n𝐙` with the trivial
`G`-action, (2) `𝐆_m` corresponds to `(Kˢᵉᵖ)^*`, (3) `𝐆_a` corresponds to `(Kˢᵉᵖ, +)`, and
(4) `μ_n` corresponds to `μ_n(Kˢᵉᵖ)`, each with its `G`-action.  Moreover

  `0 = Pic(Spec K) = H¹_étale(Spec(K)_étale, 𝐆_m) = H¹(G, (Kˢᵉᵖ)^*)`,

which is Hilbert's 90 theorem, and, for every `i ≥ 1`,

  `0 = H^i(Spec K, 𝒪) = H^i_étale(Spec(K)_étale, 𝐆_a) = H^i(G, Kˢᵉᵖ)`.

The module docstring lists the declaration proving each component.
declarations.statement:
public def stacks03QV :
    ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj
        (constantEtaleSheaf B K hK (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))) ≅
      constantGModule K sbar (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n))) ×
    ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj
        (multiplicativeSheafRestriction B K hK) ≅ sepClosureUnitsGModule K sbar) ×
    ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj
        (additiveSheafRestriction B K hK) ≅ sepClosureAddGModule K sbar) ×
    ((etaleContinuousGModuleEquivalence.{u, u + 1} B K hK sbar).functor.obj
        (rootsOfUnitySheafRestriction B K hK n) ≅ sepClosureRootsOfUnityGModule K sbar n) ×
    (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) 1 ≃+
      continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1} (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) 1
        (sepClosureUnitsGModule K sbar)) ×
    (∀ i : ℕ, Hgroup (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).ringCatSheaf ⊤ (i + 1)
          (Scheme.unitModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) ≃+
        Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
          (Stacks.ArtinSchreier.additiveSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) (i + 1)) ×
    (∀ q : ℕ, Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
          (Stacks.ArtinSchreier.additiveSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) q ≃+
        continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1} (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) q
          (sepClosureAddGModule K sbar)) ×
    PLift (Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).picardGroup ∧
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) 1) ∧
      IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1}
        (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) 1 (sepClosureUnitsGModule K sbar)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (Hgroup (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).ringCatSheaf ⊤ i
        (Scheme.unitModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))))) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
        (Stacks.ArtinSchreier.additiveSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u + 1}
        (GeometricPoint.absoluteGaloisGroup sbar) i (sepClosureAddGModule K sbar))))

Central simple algebras of degree `d` are classified by nonabelian
`PGL_d`-valued Galois cohomology.

public noncomputable def centralSimpleAlgebraClassEquivPGLH1
    (K : Type u) [Field K] (Ksep : Type v) [Field Ksep] [Algebra K Ksep]

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDelta
declarations.doc:
**The map `δ : Br(K) → H²(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K), (Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ)`.** The Brauer class of a central simple
algebra `A` of degree `d` is sent to the class of the scalar two-cocycle
`(σ, τ) ↦ g̃_σ⁻¹ g̃_{σ τ} σ(g̃_τ⁻¹)` of a lift `g̃` of the projective cocycle of a splitting of
`Kˢᵉᵖ ⊗ A`.
declarations.statement: def brauerDelta : BrauerGroup.{u, v} K → TwoCohomology K Ksep

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDelta_mul
declarations.doc:
**The map `δ` of tag 03R7 is a group homomorphism**: it takes the group law of the Brauer
group, which is tensor product, to the group law of the second cohomology group.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerDelta_mul (x y : BrauerGroup.{u, v} K) :
    brauerDelta K Ksep (x * y) = brauerDelta K Ksep x * brauerDelta K Ksep y

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDelta_surjective
declarations.doc:
**`δ` is surjective.** Every class in `H²(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K), (Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ)` is the class of a locally
constant cocycle, that cocycle is the scalar defect of a projective cocycle, and the
classification of tag 03R6 realises the projective class by a central simple algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerDelta_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (brauerDelta K Ksep : BrauerGroup.{u, v} K → TwoCohomology K Ksep)

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDelta_injective
declarations.doc:
**`δ` is injective.** If two central simple algebras have the same class then `A ⊗ Bᵐᵒᵖ` has
trivial class, hence is a matrix algebra over `K`, and that exhibits a Brauer equivalence between
`A` and `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerDelta_injective :
    Function.Injective (brauerDelta K Ksep : BrauerGroup.{u, v} K → TwoCohomology K Ksep)

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDelta_bijective
declarations.doc: **The map `δ` of tag 03R7 is bijective.**
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerDelta_bijective :
    Function.Bijective (brauerDelta K Ksep : BrauerGroup.{u, v} K → TwoCohomology K Ksep)

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.brauerDeltaEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03R7.** The map `δ : Br(K) → H²(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K), (Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ)` is an
isomorphism of groups. As for `brauerDeltaHom`, the commutative group structure on the Brauer
group is available for central simple algebras in the universe of the ground field, so this
bundling is stated with `Kˢᵉᵖ` in that universe too; `brauerDelta_injective` and
`brauerDelta_surjective` are the two halves without that restriction.
declarations.statement: def brauerDeltaEquiv : BrauerGroup.{u, u} K ≃* TwoCohomology K Ksep

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_forall_brauer
declarations.doc:
Let `Ω` be a separably closed Galois extension of a field `K` and assume `Br(K') = 0` for
every finite extension `K'/K`. Then `H^q(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ) = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`, the group being
the continuous group cohomology of the discrete Galois module
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.unitsContinuousGModule`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_forall_brauer (K Ω : Type u) [Field K]
    [Field Ω] [Algebra K Ω] [IsGalois K Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
    (hBr : ∀ (K' : Type u) [Field K'] [Algebra K K'] [Module.Finite K K']
      (y : BrauerGroup K'), y = 1)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) q (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω))
declarations.comment:
part (1) IN FULL, for the DERIVED-FUNCTOR groups continuousGroupCohomology of
Stacks 04JR: H^q(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ) = 0 for EVERY q ≥ 1, where Ω is any separably closed field Galois
over K, so at Ω = K^sep this is exactly the tag's part (1). The Brauer hypothesis is the source's
own -- Br(K') = 0 for every finite extension K'/K -- and the degree range is the source's.
Degrees one and two are the two earlier registrations in
MultiplicativeGroupVanishingCriterion (Hilbert 90 through the degree-one comparison, and the
crossed-product argument through the degree-two comparison, the latter needing only Br(K) = 0).
Degrees q ≥ 3 are part (2), the registration in TorsionGaloisVanishing, through
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_of_forall_isAddTorsion: multiplication by a positive integer n
on a discrete module has kernel and cokernel killed by n, so part (2) and two passes of the long
exact sequence of the δ-functor of Stacks 010Q make it injective on H^q for q ≥ 3, while every
class is killed by some positive integer by Stacks 0DV3 part (1). This registration is part (1);
part (2) is the registration in TorsionGaloisVanishing and the degree-one and degree-two
statements keep their own registrations in MultiplicativeGroupVanishingCriterion

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauerGroup_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03R8, part (1) in degree two**, in explicit cocycle form and with no
carried hypothesis: if `Br(K) = 0` then every locally constant `2`-cocycle on `Gal(Ω/K)` with
values in `Ωˣ` is a coboundary, which is the vanishing of `H^2(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ)`. At `Ω = Kˢᵉᵖ` this
is the degree-two case of the tag.

The hypothesis is weaker than the tag's, which asks for the Brauer group of every finite
extension of `K`: only `Br(K) = 0` is used, because it already makes every relative Brauer group
`Br(L/K)` vanish, which is the premise of
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauer` at each finite Galois subextension `L` of
`Ω`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauerGroup_eq_one (hBr : ∀ y : BrauerGroup K, y = 1)
    (f : Gal(Ω/K) × Gal(Ω/K) → Ωˣ) (hloc : IsLocallyConstant f) (hf : IsMulCocycle₂ f) :
    IsMulCoboundary₂ f
declarations.comment:
part (1) in degree two, in explicit cocycle form, UNCONDITIONAL -- nothing is
carried. Under the tag's Brauer hypothesis every locally constant 2-cocycle of the Galois group
with values in the units is a coboundary, which is the vanishing of H^2(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ); at
Ω = K^sep this is the tag's degree-two case. Proved from
isMulCoboundary₂_of_forall_finiteGalois fed with the crossed-product argument
isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauer, whose premise the tag's hypothesis discharges at once since
Br(K) = 0 forces every relative Brauer group Br(L/K) to vanish. The hypothesis used here is only
Br(K) = 0, which is weaker than the tag's, and Ω is an arbitrary Galois extension rather than
the separable closure, so this is more general than the tag's degree-two case rather than
narrower. NOT proved here: the other degrees of part (1), for which see
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units, and part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03R8, part (1).** Let `K` be a field with `Br(K) = 0` and let `Ω/K` be
a Galois extension. Then

`H^q(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ) = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`,

the groups being this library's continuous group cohomology of Stacks 04JR evaluated at the
discrete Galois module `Stacks.GaloisCohomology.unitsContinuousGModule`. At `Ω = Kˢᵉᵖ` this is
part (1) of the tag.

Three inputs are carried. `h03QU₁` and `h03QU₂` are the comparison, in degrees one and two,
between the cocycle description of Galois cohomology and the derived-functor description: the
vanishing of the cocycle quotient implies the vanishing of `continuousGroupCohomology`. The two
descriptions are not related anywhere in this library above degree zero. `hhigh` is the
vanishing in degrees `q ≥ 3`, which the source deduces from part (2) of the tag through the
four-term sequence `0 → A → M → M ⊗ 𝐐 → B → 0`; part (2) is not formalized here.

What is proved is degrees one and two: in degree one the cocycle premise of `h03QU₁` is Hilbert's
theorem 90 for an infinite Galois extension,
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isLocallyConstant_of_isMulCocycle₁`, which needs no
hypothesis at all; in degree two it is
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauerGroup_eq_one`, which consumes the Brauer
hypothesis. So the Brauer hypothesis is genuinely used, and the tag's content in degrees one and
two is established rather than assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units (hBr : ∀ y : BrauerGroup K, y = 1)
    (h03QU₁ : (∀ f : Gal(Ω/K) → Ωˣ, IsLocallyConstant f → IsMulCocycle₁ f →
          IsMulCoboundary₁ f) →
        IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) 1 (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω)))
    (h03QU₂ : (∀ f : Gal(Ω/K) × Gal(Ω/K) → Ωˣ, IsLocallyConstant f → IsMulCocycle₂ f →
          IsMulCoboundary₂ f) →
        IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) 2 (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω)))
    (hhigh : ∀ q : ℕ, 3 ≤ q →
      IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) q (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω)))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) q (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω))
declarations.comment:
part (1), the full degree range q ≥ 1, over three carried hypotheses, and for an
arbitrary Galois extension Ω/K rather than only the separable closure. CARRIED as `h03QU₁` and
`h03QU₂`: the comparison in degrees one and two between the explicit cocycle description of
Galois cohomology and the derived-functor description continuousGroupCohomology of Stacks 04JR
-- the two are not related anywhere in this library above degree zero, where the comparison is
invariantsIsoZerothCohomology; this is the standard comparison of the standard complex with the
right derived functor and not a Stacks tag of its own. CARRIED as `hhigh`: the vanishing in
degrees q ≥ 3, which is the one part of part (1) assumed wholesale; the source gets it from part
(2) of this tag together with the four-term sequence 0 → A → M → M ⊗ Q → B → 0, whose
divisible-coefficient input IS proved (isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_of_module_rat, Stacks
0DV3 part (2)) but whose remaining ingredients -- part (2), the construction of M ⊗ Q as a
discrete Galois module, and the long exact sequence of continuousGroupCohomology -- are not.
PROVED: degrees one and two, where the cocycle premises of `h03QU₁` and `h03QU₂` are discharged
from proved results -- Hilbert 90 for an infinite Galois extension
(isMulCoboundary₁_of_isLocallyConstant_of_isMulCocycle₁, which needs no hypothesis) and the
crossed-product argument (isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauerGroup_eq_one above), the latter consuming the
Brauer hypothesis. So the hypothesis is genuinely used and the tag's content in degrees one and
two is established, not assumed. Also PROVED, and new: the coefficient module itself,
unitsContinuousGModule, the units of Ω as a discrete Galois module in the sense of Stacks 04JP,
together with the continuity of the Galois action on them. NOT proved: part (2) of the tag, for
which the library has none of the inputs -- see this file's module documentation

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_one
declarations.doc:
For a Galois extension `Ω/K`, the continuous group cohomology `H¹(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ)` of the
discrete Galois module `Stacks.GaloisCohomology.unitsContinuousGModule` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_one :
    IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) 1 (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω))
declarations.comment:
part (1) at q = 1, for the derived-functor groups H^q(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ) of
Stacks 04JR, with NO HYPOTHESIS WHATSOEVER -- STRONGER than the proposition at q = 1 in two
independent ways. First, the proposition assumes Br(K') = 0 uniformly over every finite extension
K'/K and this assumes nothing about Brauer groups at all: the cocycle statement at q = 1 is
Hilbert 90 for an infinite Galois extension, namely
isMulCoboundary₁_of_isLocallyConstant_of_isMulCocycle₁, which is unconditional, so the
proposition's hypothesis is not used and is not needed. Second, Ω is an arbitrary Galois extension
rather than the separable closure; at Ω = K^sep this is exactly the tag's q = 1 case. Nothing is
carried: the comparison between the cocycle and derived-functor descriptions is
Stacks.GroupCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_one_of_forall_isCoboundary, which
is a theorem, not a hypothesis. NOT proved here: the degrees q ≥ 2 of
part (1) -- q = 2 is isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_two just below, over the tag's own
hypothesis in the weaker form Br(K) = 0, and the degrees q ≥ 3 are
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_fourTerm and
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_annihilated, which still carry part (2) -- and
part (2) itself

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_two
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field with `Br(K) = 0` and let `Ω/K` be a Galois extension. Then the continuous
group cohomology `H²(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ)` of the discrete Galois module
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.unitsContinuousGModule` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_two (hBr : ∀ y : BrauerGroup K, y = 1) :
    IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(Ω/K) 2 (unitsContinuousGModule K Ω))
declarations.comment:
part (1) at q = 2, for the derived-functor groups H^q(Gal(Ω/K), Ωˣ) of
Stacks 04JR. Nothing is carried: no comparison between the cocycle and derived-functor
descriptions is assumed, and the only hypothesis is Br(K) = 0. That is STRICTLY WEAKER than the
proposition's own hypothesis, which assumes Br(K') = 0 uniformly over every finite extension
K'/K -- Br(K) = 0 is one instance of it, and it already forces every relative Brauer group
Br(L/K) to vanish, which is what the crossed-product argument needs at each finite Galois
subextension. Ω is an arbitrary Galois extension rather than the separable closure, so this is
more general than the tag's degree-two case in that respect too; at Ω = K^sep it is exactly that
case. The cocycle input is isMulCoboundary₂_of_brauer, assembled by
exists_isLocallyConstant_isMulCoboundary₂_of_forall_finiteGalois (which records that the
trivialising 1-cochain, being inflated from a finite level, is locally constant -- strictly more
than Mathlib's IsMulCoboundary₂ gives, and exactly what the comparison consumes); the comparison
itself is Stacks.GroupCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_two_of_forall_isCoboundary, which
is a theorem, not a hypothesis. NOT proved here: q = 1 of
part (1), which is isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_one above and needs no Brauer
hypothesis at all; the degrees q >= 3, which are
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_fourTerm and
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_annihilated and still carry part (2); and part (2)
itself

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_and_torsion_of_forall_brauer
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03R8.** Let `K` be a field with separable algebraic closure `Kˢᵉᵖ`,
and assume that `Br(K') = 0` for every finite extension `K'/K`. Then

1. `H ^q(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K), (Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ) = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`, and
2. `H ^q(Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K), M) = 0` for every torsion discrete `Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)`-module `M` and every
   `q ≥ 2`,

the groups being this library's continuous group cohomology of Stacks 04JR, and the module of
the first conjunct being the discrete Galois module
`Stacks.GaloisCohomology.unitsContinuousGModule`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_and_torsion_of_forall_brauer (K : Type u)
    [Field K]
    (hBr : ∀ (K' : Type u) [Field K'] [Algebra K K'] [Module.Finite K K']
      (y : BrauerGroup K'), y = 1) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, u} Gal(SeparableClosure K/K) q
        (unitsContinuousGModule K (SeparableClosure K)))) ∧
      ∀ (M : ContinuousGModule.{u, max u v} Gal(SeparableClosure K/K)),
        IsAddTorsion M.obj.obj.V → ∀ q : ℕ, 2 ≤ q →
          IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, v} Gal(SeparableClosure K/K) q M)
declarations.comment:
the WHOLE proposition at Ω = K^sep: part (1) and part (2) together, as one
statement, under exactly the source's hypothesis -- Br(K') = 0 for every finite extension K'/K.
The first conjunct is H^q(Gal(K^sep/K), (K^sep)ˣ) = 0 for every q ≥ 1, at the discrete Galois
module unitsContinuousGModule; the second is H^q(Gal(K^sep/K), M) = 0 for every torsion discrete
Galois module M and every q ≥ 2. Both are values of the derived-functor groups
continuousGroupCohomology of Stacks 04JR. This is an assembly of the two theorems of this chapter
that each prove one part in full: isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_units_of_forall_brauer, in
StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleCohomology.GaloisCohomology.MultiplicativeGroupVanishingAllDegrees,
which takes the same Brauer hypothesis verbatim and gives every degree q ≥ 1; and
isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_of_isAddTorsion, in
StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleCohomology.GaloisCohomology.TorsionGaloisVanishing, which
gives every degree q ≥ 2 for every torsion discrete module, and whose hypothesis -- Br(L) = 0 for
the intermediate fields L of K^sep/K finite over K -- is an instance of the source's at K' = ↥L,
every such L being a finite extension of K. Every clause of the proposition is established here.
The per-part registrations elsewhere in the chapter are retained: part (1) in every degree in
MultiplicativeGroupVanishingAllDegrees, part (2) in TorsionGaloisVanishing, and the degree-one
and degree-two statements of part (1) in MultiplicativeGroupVanishingCriterion

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_of_isAddTorsion
declarations.doc:
If the Brauer group of every finite subextension of a separably closed Galois extension
`Ω/K` vanishes, then `H^q(Gal(Ω/K), M) = 0` for every torsion discrete `Gal(Ω/K)`-module `M` and
every `q ≥ 2`, the groups being the continuous group cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_continuousGroupCohomology_of_isAddTorsion (K Ω : Type u) [Field K] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra K Ω] [IsGalois K Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
    (hBr : ∀ L : IntermediateField K Ω, FiniteDimensional K L → ∀ y : BrauerGroup L, y = 1)
    (M : ContinuousGModule.{u, max u v} Gal(Ω/K)) (hM : IsAddTorsion M.obj.obj.V)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (continuousGroupCohomology.{u, v} Gal(Ω/K) q M)
declarations.comment:
part (2) in full, for the DERIVED-FUNCTOR groups continuousGroupCohomology of
Stacks 04JR: H^q(Gal(Ω/K), M) = 0 for EVERY torsion discrete Galois module M and EVERY q ≥ 2,
where Ω is any separably closed field Galois over K, so at Ω = K^sep this is exactly the tag's
part (2). The Brauer hypothesis is the one the source states, and in fact less: only the finite
SEPARABLE extensions of K inside Ω are used, whereas the tag asks for every finite extension, so
this statement implies the tag's rather than specialising it. The proof is the source's dévissage
carried out on locally constant cochains. A locally constant 2-cocycle on a profinite group takes
finitely many values, so it is a cocycle with values in a finite submodule; a finite module is
reduced to a module killed by a prime p along its p-torsion subgroup; a finite module killed by p
is handled over an open subgroup of index prime to p -- the preimage of a p-Sylow subgroup of a
finite quotient -- where the action factors through a p-group and the module is filtered by
copies of Z/p with trivial action, and the restriction-corestriction identity cor o res = n,
written out on cochains, carries the trivialization back to the whole group; and Z/p with trivial
action is the Kummer sequence of Stacks 03PL away from the characteristic and the Artin-Schreier
sequence of Stacks 0A3J in the characteristic, each fed by the two degrees of part (1) proved in
MultiplicativeGroupVanishingCriterion. Degrees above two come from dimension shifting along the
module of locally constant functions into a torsion divisible hull, which is an injective object
of the category of Stacks 04JP whose cokernel is again torsion. This registration is part (2);
part (1) has its own three registrations in MultiplicativeGroupVanishingCriterion

declarations.name: IsCField
declarations.doc:
A field `K` is a \(C_r\) field if every homogeneous polynomial of degree
`d ≥ 1` in `n` variables has a nonzero solution when `d ^ r < n`.

The degree bound is `0 < d`, not `0 < d ^ r`. The two agree for every `r ≥ 1`, but at `r = 0`
they do not: `d ^ 0 = 1` even for `d = 0`, so `0 < d ^ r` is satisfied by the constant
polynomial `1`, which is homogeneous of degree `0` and has no nonzero root. With that spelling
`IsCField K 0` is false for every field, which is not what \(C_0\) means.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCField (K : Type*) [Field K] (r : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: exists_nonzero_common_zero_of_isHomogeneous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RB.** Over an algebraically closed field, a family of `s < n`
homogeneous polynomials of positive degree in `n` variables has a common nonzero zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_nonzero_common_zero_of_isHomogeneous
    (k : Type*) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {s n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin s → ℕ) (f : (i : Fin s) → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)
    (hd : ∀ i, 0 < d i) (hf : ∀ i, (f i).IsHomogeneous (d i)) (hsn : s < n) :
    ∃ α : Fin n → k, α ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval α (f i) = 0
declarations.comment: an algebraically closed field is `C_r`: the one-polynomial case `s = 1`

declarations.name: exists_nonzero_common_zero_of_isHomogeneous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RB.** Over an algebraically closed field, a family of `s < n`
homogeneous polynomials of positive degree in `n` variables has a common nonzero zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_nonzero_common_zero_of_isHomogeneous
    (k : Type*) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {s n : ℕ}
    (d : Fin s → ℕ) (f : (i : Fin s) → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)
    (hd : ∀ i, 0 < d i) (hf : ∀ i, (f i).IsHomogeneous (d i)) (hsn : s < n) :
    ∃ α : Fin n → k, α ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, MvPolynomial.eval α (f i) = 0

declarations.name: brauerGroup_eq_one_of_isCField
declarations.doc: Every Brauer class over a C₁ field is trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerGroup_eq_one_of_isCField (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (hK : IsCField K 1) (x : BrauerGroup K) : x = 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCField_functionField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RD (Tsen's theorem).** The function field of a variety of dimension
`r` over an algebraically closed field `k` is a \(C_r\) field.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0A23.** A curve over a field is a variety of Krull dimension one.
declarations.statement:
public class IsCurve (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop
    extends IsVariety k f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety
declarations.doc:
A scheme over a field is a variety when it is integral and its structure morphism is
separated and of finite type.
declarations.statement:
class IsVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) : Prop
    extends IsIntegral X, IsSeparated f, LocallyOfFiniteType f, QuasiCompact f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.brauerGroup_functionField_eq_one
declarations.doc:
The Brauer group of the function field of a curve over an algebraically closed field is
trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerGroup_functionField_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f]
    (y : BrauerGroup X.functionField) : y = 1

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_spec_of_trdeg_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RG.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field and `K/k` a field
extension of transcendence degree one. Then

`H^q_étale(Spec K, 𝐆_m) = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`.

The criterion of Stacks 03R8 read through Stacks 03QU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_of_forall_brauer`, reduces this to
the triviality of the Brauer group of every finite extension `K'/K`; such a `K'` has
transcendence degree one over `k`, so `Br(K') = 0` by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.brauerGroup_eq_one_of_module_finite_of_trdeg_eq_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_spec_of_trdeg_eq_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (hK : Algebra.trdeg k K = 1)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec (.of K))) q)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_of_trdeg_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RG**, under its earlier name: an alias of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_spec_of_trdeg_eq_one`. Let `k`
be an algebraically closed field and `K/k` a field extension of transcendence degree one. Then
`H^q_étale(Spec K, 𝐆_m) = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement: alias subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_of_trdeg_eq_one
declarations.comment:
vanishing of the positive-degree étale cohomology of 𝐆_m over a
transcendence-degree-one extension of an algebraically closed field, over Tag 03R8 and Tag 03QU
as the hypothesis h03RG

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.epi_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI is an epimorphism**, for a
smooth curve over a field:
`j_* 𝐆_{m,η} ⟶ ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 ⟶ 0`
is exact. This is the right-hand exactness of the source, with the algebraically closed base
field of the source weakened to an arbitrary field.

It is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.epi_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve_of_forall_imageSieve_ι_mem` with its
hypothesis discharged by `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.imageSieve_ι_mem_of_isCurve`.

Together with the left end,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_genericPointInclusion`, and the
vanishing of the composite,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve`,
what remains of Stacks 03RI is the exactness in the middle,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exact_divisorSequenceOfCurve`; the four together are the short exactness
of the sequence, `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.shortExact_divisorSequenceOfCurve`, which is what
discharges the short exactness hypothesis of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve`.
declarations.comment:
the right-hand exactness of the sequence for a smooth curve over a field: the
second map, as constructed here, is an epimorphism of étale sheaves; the exactness in the middle
is proved separately, as Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exact_divisorSequenceOfCurve

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exact_divisorSequenceOfCurve
declarations.doc:
For a smooth curve `X` over a field, the fundamental exact sequence
`0 → 𝐆_{m,X} → j_* 𝐆_{m,η} → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 → 0` is exact in the middle: the kernel of
the divisor map `j_* 𝐆_{m,η} ⟶ ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙` is the image of `𝐆_{m,X}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_divisorSequenceOfCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] :
    (ShortComplex.mk
      (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X))
      (divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve.{u, u + 1} g)
      (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve.{u, u + 1}
        g)).Exact
declarations.comment:
the exactness in the middle of the sequence for a smooth curve over a field: a
section of j_* G_m killed by the divisor map is étale locally an invertible global function

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.shortExact_divisorSequenceOfCurve
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a smooth curve over a field `k`, let `η` be its generic point with inclusion
`j : η ⟶ X`, and let `X_0` be its set of closed points with inclusions `i_x`. Then

`0 → 𝐆_{m,X} → j_* 𝐆_{m,η} → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 → 0`

is a short exact sequence of étale sheaves on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_divisorSequenceOfCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] :
    (ShortComplex.mk
      (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X))
      (divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve.{u, u + 1} g)
      (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve.{u, u + 1}
        g)).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
the fundamental exact sequence for a smooth curve over a field, as a short exact
sequence of étale sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSections
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence
`0 → 𝐆_{m,X} → j_* 𝐆_{m,η} → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 → 0`, on sections over an arbitrary étale
`X`-scheme `U`**: an invertible global function on the generic fibre `η ×_X U` is sent to the
finitely supported family of its orders of vanishing in `⨁_{x ∈ X_0} ((i_x)_* 𝐙)(U)`, the member
at a closed point `x` being the locally constant `𝐙`-valued map on the fibre `x ×_X U` recording
the order of vanishing at each point of `U` over `x`.
declarations.statement:
def closedPointDivisorSections :
    Additive ((Γ(pullback U.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) →+
      DirectSum ↥(closedPoints X)
        fun x : closedPoints X => (integerSkyscraper.{u, v} X x.1).obj.obj (op U)
declarations.comment:
the second map on sections over an arbitrary étale X-scheme, for X integral and
normal

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSections_restrict_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The fundamental exact sequence is a complex on sections over an arbitrary étale
`X`-scheme `U`**: the restriction to the generic fibre of an invertible global function on `U` has
zero family of orders of vanishing.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPointDivisorSections_restrict_eq_zero (a : (Γ(U.left, ⊤))ˣ) :
    closedPointDivisorSections.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
      (pullback.fst U.hom (genericPointInclusion X)).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a)) = 0
declarations.comment:
the sequence on sections over an arbitrary étale X-scheme is a complex, for X
integral and normal

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.integerSkyscraperDivisorOfPoint_map
declarations.doc:
**The `x`-component of the second map of the fundamental exact sequence is compatible with
restriction along a morphism of the small étale site**, read in the sections of `(i_x)_* 𝐙` over an
étale `X`-scheme. Neither object is assumed irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem integerSkyscraperDivisorOfPoint_map {X : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral X]
    [IsNormal X] {U V : X.Etale} [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian V.left]
    (x : X) (φ : U ⟶ V) (a : (Γ(pullback V.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) :
    ((integerSkyscraper.{u, v} X x).obj.map φ.op).hom
        (integerSkyscraperDivisorOfPoint.{u, v} V x (Additive.ofMul a)) =
      integerSkyscraperDivisorOfPoint.{u, v} U x
        (Additive.ofMul (Units.map (etaleGenericFibreMap φ).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a))
declarations.comment:
the x-component of the second map is compatible with restriction along a morphism
of étale X-schemes, read in the sections of i_{x,*} Z, for X integral and normal

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorPresheafSection_map
declarations.doc:
**The second map on sections is compatible with restriction**, read in the coproduct of the
underlying presheaves of the skyscrapers: restricting the section attached to a unit on the generic
fibre of `V` along a morphism `φ : U ⟶ V` of the small étale site gives the section attached to the
restricted unit. Neither object is assumed irreducible.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPointDivisorPresheafSection_map {U V : X.Etale} [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left]
    [NoetherianSpace U.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian V.left] [NoetherianSpace V.left]
    (φ : U ⟶ V) (a : (Γ(pullback V.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) :
    ((∐ fun x : closedPoints X ↦ (closedPointSkyscraper.{u, v} X x).obj).map φ.op).hom
        (closedPointDivisorPresheafSection.{u, v} V (Additive.ofMul a)) =
      closedPointDivisorPresheafSection.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
        ((smallEtaleBaseChange (genericPointInclusion X)).map
          φ).left.appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a))
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence is compatible with restriction along a morphism of
étale X-schemes, read in the coproduct of the underlying presheaves of the skyscrapers, for X
integral and normal

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorPresheafSection_restrict_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**An invertible global function on `U` has trivial image under the second map**, read in the
presheaf coproduct: the sequence is a complex on sections over an étale `X`-scheme with Noetherian
space, with no irreducibility hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPointDivisorPresheafSection_restrict_eq_zero (U : X.Etale)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left] [NoetherianSpace U.left] (a : (Γ(U.left, ⊤))ˣ) :
    closedPointDivisorPresheafSection.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
      (pullback.fst U.hom (genericPointInclusion X)).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a)) = 0
declarations.comment:
the sequence is a complex on sections over an arbitrary étale X-scheme, read in the
coproduct of the underlying presheaves of the skyscrapers, for X integral and normal

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSheafSection
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI over an arbitrary étale
`X`-scheme with Noetherian space, valued in the sheaf `⨁_x (i_x)_* 𝐙` itself.** This is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSections` followed by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSheaf.sheafSectionOfDirectSum`.

No irreducibility hypothesis is carried on `U`, which is the generality of the source.
declarations.statement:
def closedPointDivisorSheafSection (U : X.Etale) [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left]
    [NoetherianSpace U.left] :
    Additive ((Γ(pullback U.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) →+
      (closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, v} X).obj.obj (op U)
declarations.comment:
the second map on sections over an étale X-scheme with Noetherian space, valued
in the sheaf ⨁_x i_{x,*} Z, for X integral and normal; no irreducibility is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSheafSection_map
declarations.doc:
**The commuting square that makes the second map of Stacks 03RI a map of presheaves**, read in
the sheaf `⨁_x (i_x)_* 𝐙`: restricting the section attached to a unit on the generic fibre of `V`
along a morphism `φ : U ⟶ V` of the small étale site gives the section attached to the restricted
unit.

It is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSections_map` together with the naturality of the
passage from the direct sum of the groups of sections to the sections of the sheaf,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSheaf.map_comp_sheafSectionOfDirectSum`. Neither object
is assumed irreducible, so this is the square at the generality of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPointDivisorSheafSection_map {U V : X.Etale} [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left]
    [NoetherianSpace U.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian V.left] [NoetherianSpace V.left]
    (φ : U ⟶ V) (a : (Γ(pullback V.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) :
    ((closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, v} X).obj.map φ.op).hom
        (closedPointDivisorSheafSection.{u, v} V (Additive.ofMul a)) =
      closedPointDivisorSheafSection.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
        ((smallEtaleBaseChange (genericPointInclusion X)).map
          φ).left.appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a))
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence is compatible with restriction along a morphism of
étale X-schemes with Noetherian spaces, read in the sheaf ⨁_x i_{x,*} Z, for X integral and
normal; no irreducibility is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorSheafSection_restrict_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**An invertible global function on `U` has trivial image under the second map of Stacks 03RI
read in the sheaf `⨁_x (i_x)_* 𝐙`**: the sequence of the source is a complex over an arbitrary
étale `X`-scheme with Noetherian space, with no irreducibility hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedPointDivisorSheafSection_restrict_eq_zero (U : X.Etale)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left] [NoetherianSpace U.left] (a : (Γ(U.left, ⊤))ˣ) :
    closedPointDivisorSheafSection.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
      (pullback.fst U.hom (genericPointInclusion X)).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a)) = 0
declarations.comment:
the sequence is a complex on sections over an étale X-scheme with Noetherian
space, read in the sheaf ⨁_x i_{x,*} Z, for X integral and normal; no irreducibility is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleDivisorRestricted
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI on the affine étale site**,
as a morphism of presheaves of abelian groups. Its component at an affine étale `X`-scheme `W` is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleDivisorApp`, and its commuting square is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleDivisorApp_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
def affineEtaleDivisorRestricted :
    (Scheme.AffineEtale.Spec X).op ⋙ ((genericPointDirectImage.{u, v} X).obj
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, v} (Spec X.functionField))).obj ⟶
      (Scheme.AffineEtale.Spec X).op ⋙ (closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, v} X).obj
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence on the affine étale site, as a morphism of
presheaves, for X integral, normal and locally Noetherian

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMap
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI, as a morphism of abelian
sheaves on the small étale site of `X`:**
`j_* 𝐆_{m,η} ⟶ ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙`.

It is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleDivisorRestricted` transferred along the inclusion of the
affine étale site, which is cover dense and full and hence locally full, so
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCoverDense.restrictHomEquivHom` is a bijection. The source states the
sequence for a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field; the hypotheses carried here —
integral, normal, locally Noetherian — are all weaker, and are discharged in that setting by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isCurve` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isNormal_of_isCurve_of_smooth`.

Being data, this definition is not pinned down by its type: the zero morphism inhabits it too.
What pins it down is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.whiskerLeft_divisorSequenceSecondMap` together with
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMap_hom_app` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleDivisorApp_apply`, which say that on sections over an affine
étale `X`-scheme it is the family of orders of vanishing, and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMap_eq_of_whiskerLeft`, which says that no other
morphism of sheaves does so.
declarations.statement:
def divisorSequenceSecondMap :
    (genericPointDirectImage.{u, v} X).obj
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, v} (Spec X.functionField)) ⟶
      closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, v} X
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence, as a morphism of étale sheaves, for X integral,
normal and locally Noetherian; the exactness of the sequence is not proved at this generality

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMap
declarations.doc:
**The two maps of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI compose to zero**, so that
`0 → 𝐆_{m,X} → j_* 𝐆_{m,η} → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 → 0`
is a complex of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`.

Both composites are morphisms into the sheaf `⨁_x (i_x)_* 𝐙`, so restriction to the affine étale
site is injective on them and it suffices to compare them there, where
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.comparison_app_comp_affineEtaleDivisorApp` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMap :
    multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, v} (genericPointInclusion X) ≫
        divisorSequenceSecondMap.{u, v} X = 0
declarations.comment:
the sequence is a complex: the two constructed maps compose to zero, for X
integral, normal and locally Noetherian; the exactness of the sequence is not proved at this
generality

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI for a smooth curve over a
field**, which is the setting of the source. The three hypotheses of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMap` are discharged there: a curve is integral by
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety` and locally Noetherian by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isCurve`, and a smooth curve is normal by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isNormal_of_isCurve_of_smooth`.
declarations.statement:
def divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] :
    (genericPointDirectImage.{u, v} X).obj
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, v} (Spec X.functionField)) ⟶
      closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, v} X
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence for a smooth curve over a field, as a morphism of
étale sheaves; the short exactness of the sequence is proved in the MiddleExactness file of this
directory

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve
declarations.doc:
**The two maps of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI compose to zero for a smooth
curve over a field.** This is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMap` with
the hypotheses of that statement discharged as in
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve`.
declarations.statement:
theorem multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_comp_divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve {k : Type u}
    [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] :
    multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, v} (genericPointInclusion X) ≫
        divisorSequenceSecondMapOfCurve.{u, v} g = 0
declarations.comment:
the sequence is a complex for a smooth curve over a field: the two constructed maps
compose to zero; the short exactness of the sequence is proved in the MiddleExactness file of
this directory

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.fundamentalSequence_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RI.** Let `X` be a smooth curve over a field, let `η = Spec k(X)` be
its generic point with inclusion `j : η ⟶ X`, and let `X_0` be the set of closed points of `X`
with inclusions `i_x : Spec κ(x) ⟶ X`. Then

`0 ⟶ 𝐆_{m,X} ⟶ j_* 𝐆_{m,η} ⟶ ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} (i_x)_* 𝐙 ⟶ 0`

is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`. The first map is the
comparison morphism `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison` along `j`, which
restricts an invertible global function on an étale `X`-scheme `U` to the generic fibre
`U ×_X η`; the second is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.closedPointDivisorMap`, the family of orders of
vanishing.

Exactness at `𝐆_{m,X}` is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.mono_multiplicativeDirectImageComparison_genericPointInclusion`: the
generic fibre is scheme-theoretically dense. Exactness in the middle is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exact_fundamentalSequence`, which rests on algebraic Hartogs on the
normal scheme `U`. Exactness on the right is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.epi_closedPointDivisorMap`: a divisor on a nonsingular curve is locally
the divisor of a rational function, and the pullback of that function along an étale morphism has
the prescribed orders of vanishing.
declarations.statement:
theorem fundamentalSequence_shortExact :
    (ShortComplex.mk (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, v} (genericPointInclusion X))
      (closedPointDivisorMap.{u, v} fX)
      (comparison_comp_closedPointDivisorMap.{u, v} fX)).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.injective_restrict_genericFibre
declarations.doc:
**Exactness of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI at `Γ(U, 𝒪_U^*)`, read on
sections over an étale `X`-scheme `U`.** On an integral scheme the generic fibre `η ×_X U` is
scheme-theoretically dense in `U`, so an invertible global function on `U` is determined by its
restriction to it.

This is the injectivity of the first map of the sequence
`0 → Γ(U, 𝒪_U^*) → Γ(η ×_X U, 𝒪^*) → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} Γ(x ×_X U, 𝐙)`
displayed in the proof of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_restrict_genericFibre :
    Function.Injective (Units.map
      (pullback.fst U.hom (genericPointInclusion X)).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom)
