declarations.comment: exactness at Γ(U, 𝒪_U^*) of the sequence on sections over an étale X-scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.genericFibreDivisorSections
declarations.doc:
**The second map of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI, on sections over an
irreducible étale `X`-scheme `U`**: an invertible global function on the generic fibre `η ×_X U`
is sent to the family of its orders of vanishing, the member at a closed point `x` being the
locally constant `𝐙`-valued map on the fibre `x ×_X U` recording the order of vanishing at each
point of `U` over `x`.

The family has finite support, a rational function having finitely many zeros and poles, so it is
an element of the direct sum `⨁_{x ∈ X_0} ((i_x)_* 𝐙)(U)`, the third term of the sequence
displayed in the proof of the source.
declarations.statement:
def genericFibreDivisorSections :
    Additive ((Γ(pullback U.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) →+
      DirectSum ↥(closedPoints X)
        fun x : closedPoints X => (integerSkyscraper.{u, v} X x.1).obj.obj (op U)
declarations.comment: the second map on sections over an irreducible étale X-scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.genericFibreDivisorSections_restrict_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**The sequence of Stacks 03RI is a complex, read on sections over an irreducible étale
`X`-scheme `U`**: an invertible global function on `U` restricts to an invertible function on the
generic fibre with no zeros and no poles, so its family of orders of vanishing is zero.

Together with `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.injective_restrict_genericFibre` this is the sequence
`0 → Γ(U, 𝒪_U^*) → Γ(η ×_X U, 𝒪^*) → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} Γ(x ×_X U, 𝐙)`
displayed in the proof of the source, exact at its left end and a complex at the middle.
declarations.statement:
theorem genericFibreDivisorSections_restrict_eq_zero (a : (Γ(U.left, ⊤))ˣ) :
    genericFibreDivisorSections.{u, v} U (Additive.ofMul (Units.map
      (pullback.fst U.hom (genericPointInclusion X)).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a)) = 0
declarations.comment: the sequence on sections over an irreducible étale X-scheme is a complex

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleGenericFibreOrd_appTop
declarations.doc:
**The order of vanishing of an invertible global function on the generic fibre is compatible
with restriction along a morphism `φ : U ⟶ V` of the small étale site of `X`:** restricting along
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleGenericFibreMap φ` and taking the order of vanishing at a point `y`
of `U` gives the order of vanishing at `φ.left.base y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleGenericFibreOrd_appTop {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X] {U V : X.Etale}
    [IsIntegral U.left] [IsIntegral V.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian U.left]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian V.left] (φ : U ⟶ V) (y : U.left)
    (a : (Γ(pullback V.hom (genericPointInclusion X), ⊤))ˣ) :
    etaleGenericFibreOrd U y
        (Additive.ofMul (Units.map (etaleGenericFibreMap φ).appTop.hom.toMonoidHom a)) =
      etaleGenericFibreOrd V (φ.left.base y) (Additive.ofMul a)
declarations.comment:
the second map of the sequence is compatible with restriction along a morphism of
étale X-schemes, read on the order of vanishing at a point

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_trdeg_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RJ.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field, let `X` be an
integral scheme whose function field `K = k(X)` has transcendence degree one over `k`, and let
`j : Spec K ⟶ X` be the inclusion of the generic point. Then

`R^q j_* 𝐆_{m,K} = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`.

A smooth curve over `k` satisfies the hypotheses, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_functionField_eq_one`, so this is more general than the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_trdeg_eq_one
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] (hK : Algebra.trdeg k X.functionField = 1)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X)).rightDerived q).obj
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RJ.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field, `X` a smooth curve
over `k` with structure morphism `g`, `η = Spec k(X)` its generic point and `j : η ⟶ X` the
inclusion of the generic point. Then

`R^q j_* 𝐆_{m,η} = 0` for every `q ≥ 1`.

No hypothesis is carried. The higher direct image is killed on the étale neighbourhoods by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_field`,
which leaves the vanishing of `H^q_étale(Spec L, 𝐆_m)` at each finite separable extension `L` of
`k(X)`. That is Stacks 03RG, since `L` has transcendence degree one over `k`.

Smoothness is in the statement because the source assumes it. The proof does not use it: the
curve hypothesis is enough.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X)).rightDerived q).obj
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RK.** Let `X` be a curve over an algebraically closed field `k`,
with structure morphism `g`, let `η = Spec k(X)` be its generic point and `j : η ⟶ X` the
inclusion of the generic point. Then

`H^p_étale(X, j_* 𝐆_{m,η}) = 0` for every `p ≥ 1`.

The source assumes `X` smooth; the proof does not use smoothness, so it is not assumed and the
statement is more general than the tag. The smooth case, with the source's hypotheses verbatim,
is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve`.

The source argues by the Leray spectral sequence `E₂^{p,q} = H^p(X, R^q j_* 𝐆_{m,η})`, whose
`q ≥ 1` rows vanish by Stacks 03RJ and whose abutment `H^{p+q}(η, 𝐆_m)` vanishes for
`p + q ≥ 1` by Stacks 03RG. The proof here is the edge isomorphism of that spectral sequence,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_isZero_rightDerived`,
with both inputs proved: Stacks 03RJ is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_trdeg_eq_one`,
whose premise is `AlgebraicGeometry.trdeg_functionField_eq_one`, and Stacks 03RG at the function
field of `X` is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_spec_functionField`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} ((genericPointDirectImage.{u, u + 1} X).obj
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField))) p)
declarations.comment:
vanishing of the positive-degree étale cohomology of the direct image of 𝐆_m
along the generic point of a curve over an algebraically closed field

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RK.** Let `X` be a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field
`k`, let `η = Spec k(X)` be its generic point and `j : η ⟶ X` the inclusion. Then

`H^p_étale(X, j_* 𝐆_{m,η}) = 0` for every `p ≥ 1`.

This is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf`,
the collapse of the Leray spectral sequence to its edge isomorphism, with Stacks 03RJ and
Stacks 03RG proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g] (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} ((genericPointDirectImage.{u, u + 1} X).obj
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField))) p)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_sigma_closedPointPushforward_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RL.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme locally of
finite type over an algebraically closed field — a smooth curve over an algebraically closed
field, for instance. For every `q ≥ 1` the degree-`q` étale cohomology of
`⨁_{x ∈ X₀} (i_x)_* ℤ` vanishes, the sum being over the closed points `X₀` of `X` and `i_x` the
inclusion of a closed point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_sheafH_sigma_closedPointPushforward_smallEtale {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
      (∐ fun x : closedPoints X ↦
        (smallEtalePushforwardAb (X.fromSpecResidueField x.1)).obj
          ((constantSheaf (smallEtaleTopology (Spec (X.residueField x.1))) Ab.{u + 1}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} ℤ)))) q)
declarations.comment:
vanishing of the positive-degree étale cohomology of the direct sum over the
closed points of the pushforwards of the constant integer sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RM.** Let `X` be a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field
`k`, let `η = Spec k(X)` be its generic point and `j : η ⟶ X` the inclusion of the generic
point. Then

`H^q_étale(X, 𝐆_m) = 0` for every `q ≥ 2`.

The proof is the long exact sequence of étale cohomology attached to the divisor sequence
`0 → 𝐆_{m,X} → j_* 𝐆_{m,η} → ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} i_{x,*} 𝐙 → 0` of Stacks 03RI: the segment
`H^{q-1}(X, ⨁_x i_{x,*} 𝐙) → H^q(X, 𝐆_{m,X}) → H^q(X, j_* 𝐆_{m,η})` has both outer groups
zero, the left one by Stacks 03RL since `q - 1 ≥ 1`, the right one by Stacks 03RK.

Stacks 03RL is used from the library, as
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_sigma_closedPointPushforward_smallEtale`, and
the vanishing of `H^q(X, j_* 𝐆_{m,η})` is the edge argument
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_genericPointDirectImage_multiplicativeSheaf_of_isZero_rightDerived`
(which is how Stacks 03RK is proved above), applied to the hypotheses `h03RJ` (Stacks 03RJ) and
`h03RG` (Stacks 03RG) carried here. The
divisor sequence itself is carried as its second map `d` with `hzero` and `hSE` (Stacks 03RI);
its first map is the comparison morphism
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.multiplicativeDirectImageComparison` along `j`, which restricts an
invertible global function on an étale `X`-scheme `U` to the generic fibre `U ×_X η`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_smoothCurve {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g]
    (d : (genericPointDirectImage.{u, u + 1} X).obj
          (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField)) ⟶
        closedPointDivisorSheaf.{u, u + 1} X)
    (hzero : multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X) ≫ d = 0)
    (hSE : (ShortComplex.mk
      (multiplicativeDirectImageComparison.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X)) d
      hzero).ShortExact)
    (h03RJ : ∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q →
      IsZero (((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, u + 1} (genericPointInclusion X)).rightDerived q).obj
        (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField))))
    (h03RG : ∀ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1}
      (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} (Spec X.functionField)) q))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} X) q)
declarations.comment:
vanishing of the degree ≥ 2 étale cohomology of 𝐆_m on a smooth curve over an
algebraically closed field, over Tag 03RI, Tag 03RJ and Tag 03RG as hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_of_smoothCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RM.** Let `X` be a smooth curve over an algebraically closed field
`k`. Then

`H^q_étale(X, 𝐆_m) = 0` for every `q ≥ 2`.

The long exact sequence of the fundamental exact sequence of Stacks 03RI,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.shortExact_divisorSequenceOfCurve`, places `H^q(X, 𝐆_m)` between
`H^{q-1}(X, ⨁_{x ∈ X_0} i_{x,*} 𝐙)`, zero by Stacks 03RL, and `H^q(X, j_* 𝐆_{m,η})`, zero by
Stacks 03RK; the latter rests on Stacks 03RJ and Stacks 03RG, supplied here.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_multiplicativeSheaf_of_smoothCurve {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k g] [Smooth g]
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton
      (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} (Stacks.Kummer.multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} X) q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.IsAbelianVariety
declarations.doc:
A group scheme over a field is an abelian variety if its structure morphism makes its
underlying scheme a proper, geometrically integral variety.
declarations.statement:
class IsAbelianVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A] : Prop
    extends IsProperVariety k A.hom, GeometricallyIntegral A.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RO.** A group scheme over a field is an abelian variety if its
structure morphism makes its underlying scheme a proper, geometrically integral variety.
declarations.statement:
class IsAbelianVariety (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [GrpObj A] : Prop extends IsProperVariety k A.hom, GeometricallyIntegral A.hom

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.etale_torsion_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RP, part (6).** Let `A` be an abelian variety over a field `k` and
`n` an integer.  The `n`-torsion group scheme `A[n] = Ker([n] : A → A)` is étale over `k` if and
only if `n` is invertible in `k`, or `A` is zero-dimensional.

The second alternative is a correction of the source, which omits it: for the zero abelian
variety `A = Spec k`, every `A[n]` is `Spec k`, hence étale, also when `n = 0` in `k`.  For a
nonzero abelian variety the statement is the source's.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_torsion_iff (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelianVariety k A] (n : ℤ) :
    Etale (GrpObj.torsion A n).X.hom ↔ topologicalKrullDim A.left = 0 ∨ IsUnit (n : k)
declarations.comment: part (6), with the zero-dimensional case added

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.surjective_zpow_id
declarations.doc: Multiplication by a nonzero integer `n` on an abelian variety is surjective.
declarations.statement: theorem surjective_zpow_id (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : Surjective ((𝟙 A : A ⟶ A) ^ n).left

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.exists_pow_eq
declarations.doc:
If `k` is algebraically closed, the group `A(k)` of rational points of an abelian variety is
divisible: for every `n ≥ 1`, every rational point is an `n`-th power.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_eq [IsAlgClosed k] (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (x : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ A) : ∃ y : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ A, y ^ n = x

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_torsion
declarations.doc:
For a nonzero integer `n`, the `n`-torsion group scheme `A[n] = Ker([n] : A → A)` of an
abelian variety `A` of dimension `g` is finite locally free of degree `|n| ^ 2g` over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_torsion (n : ℤ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (GrpObj.torsion A n).X.hom
      (n.natAbs ^ (2 * abelianVarietyDimension A))

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.nonempty_torsionBy_addEquiv_of_isUnit
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian variety of dimension `g` over an algebraically closed field `k`, and `n`
a natural number invertible in `k`. Then the `n`-torsion `A(k)[n]` of the group of rational points
is isomorphic to `(ℤ/nℤ) ^ 2g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_torsionBy_addEquiv_of_isUnit [IsAlgClosed k] (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) :
    Nonempty (AddSubgroup.torsionBy (Additive (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ A)) n ≃+
      (Fin (2 * abelianVarietyDimension A) → ZMod n))

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.exists_torsionBy_char_pow_addEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian variety of dimension `g` over an algebraically closed field `k` of
characteristic `p > 0`. There is an integer `0 ≤ f ≤ g` such that `A(k)[p ^ m] ≅ (ℤ/p^mℤ) ^ f` for
every `m` (for `m = 0` both sides are trivial).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_torsionBy_char_pow_addEquiv [IsAlgClosed k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ f ≤ abelianVarietyDimension A, ∀ m : ℕ, Nonempty
      (AddSubgroup.torsionBy (Additive (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ A)) ((p ^ m : ℕ) : ℤ) ≃+
        (Fin f → ZMod (p ^ m)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleCohomology_rootsOfUnity_smoothProjectiveCurve_of_genus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RQ.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve of genus `g` over an
algebraically closed field `k` and let `n ∈ k^*`. Then
`H⁰_ét(X, μ_n) = μ_n(k)`, `H¹_ét(X, μ_n) = Pic⁰(X)[n] ≅ (𝐙/n𝐙)^{2g}`,
`H²_ét(X, μ_n) ≅ 𝐙/n𝐙` (by the degree), `H^q_ét(X, μ_n) = 0` for `q ≥ 3`; and the same groups
for the constant sheaf `𝐙/n𝐙`: `𝐙/n𝐙`, `(𝐙/n𝐙)^{2g}`, `𝐙/n𝐙` and `0` for `q ≥ 3`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomology_rootsOfUnity_smoothProjectiveCurve_of_genus (hn : IsUnit (n : k)) :
    Function.Bijective (baseRootsToEtaleH0 E k X hX f n) ∧
      Function.Bijective (etaleH1RootsOfUnityToCurvePicardDegreeZeroTorsion k X f E hX n hn) ∧
      (∃ e : Sheaf.H (kummerSmallEtale E X hX n).X₁ 2 ≃+ ZMod n,
        ∀ x, e (etaleH2RootsOfUnityFromPicard k X f E hX n hn x) = picardDegreeZMod k X f n x) ∧
      (∀ q, 3 ≤ q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H (kummerSmallEtale E X hX n).X₁ q)) ∧
      Nonempty (Sheaf.H (smallEtaleConstantZModSheaf E X hX n) 0 ≃+ ZMod n) ∧
      Nonempty (Sheaf.H (smallEtaleConstantZModSheaf E X hX n) 1 ≃+
        (Fin (2 * genus f) → ZMod n)) ∧
      Nonempty (Sheaf.H (smallEtaleConstantZModSheaf E X hX n) 2 ≃+ ZMod n) ∧
      ∀ q, 3 ≤ q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H (smallEtaleConstantZModSheaf E X hX n) q)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03RQ], the case `q = 2`.**  Let `X` be a smooth proper curve over an
algebraically closed field `k` and let `n` be invertible in `k`.  Then `H²_étale(X, μ_n)` is
cyclic of order `n`.

The Kummer coboundary presents `H²_étale(X, μ_n)` as the quotient of `H¹_étale(X, 𝐆_m)` by its
`n`-th multiples — it is onto because `H²_étale(X, 𝐆_m) = 0` ([Stacks, Tag 03RM]) and its kernel
is the `n`-th multiples because the preceding map of the long exact sequence is multiplication by
`n` — and the degree identifies that quotient with `𝐙/n𝐙`, by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.ker_curveKummerCoboundary_eq_ker_sheafHOneMultiplicativeDegreeMod`.

The normalisation of this isomorphism is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_curveKummerCoboundary`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod :
    Sheaf.H.{u + 1} (rootsOfUnitySheaf.{u, u + 1} X n) 2 ≃+ ZMod n
declarations.comment: the q = 2 clause, that H^2_etale(X, mu_n) of a smooth proper curve over an algebraically closed field is cyclic of order n, normalised by the degree through sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_curveKummerCoboundary; the q = 0 clause is AlgebraicGeometry.baseRootsToEtaleH0_bijective_of_isCurve and the q > 2 clause is subsingleton_sheafH_rootsOfUnitySheaf_of_smoothCurve, while the q = 1 clause awaits Stacks 03P8 for the small etale site

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_curveKummerCoboundary
declarations.doc:
**The normalisation of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod`**: the
coordinate of the Kummer coboundary of a class in `H¹_étale(X, 𝐆_m)` is the degree of that class
modulo `n`.  Together with
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_curveKummerCoboundary_eq`, which says that every class in
`H²_étale(X, μ_n)` is a coboundary, this fixes the isomorphism and not merely its existence.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_curveKummerCoboundary
    (a : Sheaf.H.{u + 1} (multiplicativeSheaf.{u, u + 1} X) 1) :
    sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod g hn (curveKummerCoboundary g hn a) =
      sheafHOneMultiplicativeDegreeMod g n a
declarations.comment: the normalisation of the q = 2 clause by the degree: the coordinate of the Kummer coboundary of a class of H^1_etale(X, G_m) is the degree of the corresponding divisor class modulo n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseRootsToEtaleH0_bijective_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RQ, the case `q = 0`.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over an
algebraically closed field `k` and let `n` be invertible in `k`. Pullback along the structure
morphism is a bijection from the `n`-th roots of unity of `k` onto `H⁰_étale(X, μ_n)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseRootsToEtaleH0_bijective_of_isCurve
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k f] [Smooth f] [IsProjectiveVariety k f] (n : ℕ) (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
    Function.Bijective (baseRootsToEtaleH0 B k X hX f n)
declarations.comment: the q = 0 clause, H^0_etale(X, mu_n) = mu_n(k); the clauses for q = 1, q = 2 and q >= 3 need Stacks 03P8 and 03RM, which the library does not have

declarations.name: Stacks.Kummer.subsingleton_sheafH_rootsOfUnitySheaf_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RQ, the clause `q ≥ 3`.** Let `X` be a smooth projective curve over
an algebraically closed field `k` and let `n ≥ 1` be invertible in `k`. Then
`H^q_étale(X, μ_n) = 0` for every `q ≥ 3`.

The Kummer sequence places `H^q(X, μ_n)` between `H^{q-1}(X, 𝐆_m)` and `H^q(X, 𝐆_m)`, both zero
by Stacks 03RM since `q - 1 ≥ 2`. Projectivity is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_rootsOfUnitySheaf_of_isCurve (q : ℕ) (hq : 3 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1, u + 1} (rootsOfUnitySheaf.{u, u + 1} X n) q)
declarations.comment: the clause q >= 3: H^q_etale(X, mu_n) = 0 for every q >= 3

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleCohomology_rootsOfUnity_affineSmoothCurve_of_compactification
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleCohomology_rootsOfUnity_affineSmoothCurve_of_compactification (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    [IsAffine X] {Xbar : Scheme.{u}} (fbar : Xbar ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k fbar] [Smooth fbar]
    [IsProjectiveVariety k fbar] (j : X ⟶ Xbar) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hj : j ≫ fbar = f)
    (r : ℕ) (hr : Nat.card ↥(Set.range j.base)ᶜ = r) :
    Function.Bijective (baseRootsToEtaleH0 E k X hX f n) ∧
      Nonempty (Sheaf.H (kummerSmallEtale E X hX n).X₁ 1 ≃+
        (Fin (2 * genus fbar + r - 1) → ZMod n)) ∧
      ∀ q, 2 ≤ q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H (kummerSmallEtale E X hX n).X₁ q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleH0EquivRootsOfUnitySections_val
declarations.doc:
The comparison is the canonical evaluation of degree-zero cohomology at the final
étale object, followed by the inclusion of the kernel into the units sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleH0EquivRootsOfUnitySections_val
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X)
    (n : ℕ)
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (x : Sheaf.H.{w, u}
      (rootsOfUnitySheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX)
        (SmallEtale.toScheme B X hX)
        (unitsPresheaf_isSheaf_smallEtale B X hX) n) 0) :
    (etaleH0EquivRootsOfUnitySections B X hX n x).1 =
      Additive.toMul
        ((Limits.kernel.ι
          (powerSheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX)
            (SmallEtale.toScheme B X hX)
            (unitsPresheaf_isSheaf_smallEtale B X hX) n)).hom.app
          (Opposite.op (SmallEtale.final B X hX))
          ((Sheaf.H.equiv₀
            (rootsOfUnitySheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX)
              (SmallEtale.toScheme B X hX)
              (unitsPresheaf_isSheaf_smallEtale B X hX) n)
            (SmallEtale.finalIsTerminal B X hX)) x))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.rootsOfUnitySections_bijective_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
Roots of unity in global sections of an integral scheme over an algebraically
closed field are precisely the constants.
declarations.statement:
theorem rootsOfUnitySections_bijective_of_isIntegral
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    Function.Bijective
      ((rootsOfUnitySections n).map f.op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.baseRootsToEtaleH0_bijective_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
The canonical pullback from the field's roots of unity to degree-zero étale
cohomology is bijective over an algebraically closed field.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseRootsToEtaleH0_bijective_of_isIntegral
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (hX : B.Contains X)
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    [HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X hX) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
    Function.Bijective (baseRootsToEtaleH0 B k X hX f n)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RT.** Let `X` be a scheme of finite type and of dimension at most one
over an algebraically closed field `k`, and let `F` be a torsion abelian sheaf on `X_étale`. Then
`H^q_étale(X, F) = 0` for every `q ≥ 3`.

No separatedness is assumed. The source's "dimension 1" is the case of equality of the bound
`topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_of_three_le (q : ℕ) (hq : 3 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w} F q)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RT.** Let `X` be an affine scheme of finite type and of dimension at
most one over an algebraically closed field `k`, and let `F` be a torsion abelian sheaf on
`X_étale`. Then `H^2_étale(X, F) = 0`.

An affine scheme is separated over `k`, so this is Theorem 03SC (2), Tag 0A54.
declarations.statement: theorem subsingleton_sheafH_two_of_isAffine [IsAffine X] : Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w} F 2)
declarations.comment: H^2(X, F) = 0 if X is affine

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093Q (2).** A sheaf is locally constant if every object of the site has a covering
on each member of which its restriction is a constant sheaf.
declarations.statement: class IsLocallyConstant [∀ U : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) D] (F : Sheaf J D) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves of sets and of abelian groups

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093Q (3).** A sheaf with values in a concrete category is finite locally constant
if every object of the site has a covering on each member of which it is a constant sheaf with
finite underlying value. For `Type` and `Grp`, this is respectively the source's notion for
sheaves of sets and sheaves of groups.
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves of sets and of abelian groups

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsConstant
registrations.comment: constant sheaves of sets, of abelian groups and of Lambda-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finiteEtaleRepresentable_of_descent
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X` is finite locally constant if and only if it is
represented by an object of the site whose structure morphism is finite, that is, by a scheme
finite étale over `X`. It takes a binder `hdesc : EtaleDescentForFiniteEtaleRepresentability B`,
which defaults to the theorem `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleDescentForFiniteEtaleRepresentability`,
so the statement applies to `B X F` alone.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finiteEtaleRepresentable_of_descent
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hdesc : EtaleDescentForFiniteEtaleRepresentability B :=
      etaleDescentForFiniteEtaleRepresentability B) :
    Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyConstant (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) F ↔
      ∃ U : SmallEtale B X.1 X.property,
        IsFinite (B.inclusion.map U.obj.hom) ∧
          Nonempty (F ≅
            (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property)).obj U)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finiteEtaleRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03RV.** A sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X` is finite
locally constant if and only if it is represented by an object of the site whose structure
morphism is finite — that is, by a scheme finite étale over `X`.

The reverse implication is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isFiniteLocallyConstant_of_finiteEtaleRepresentable`. The forward one is
the étale-local representability of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_sliceRepresentatives_of_isFiniteLocallyConstant` followed by
effective descent for schemes affine over the base along an fpqc covering, Stacks 0245, in the
form `AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_isAffineHom_of_anyIndex`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finiteEtaleRepresentable
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.2) (Type (u + 1))) :
    Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyConstant (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.2) F ↔
      ∃ U : SmallEtale B X.1 X.2,
        IsFinite (B.inclusion.map U.obj.hom) ∧
          Nonempty (F ≅
            (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.2)).obj U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantFiniteEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between the finite locally constant sheaves of sets on the small étale site
of `X` and the finite étale covers of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteLocallyConstantFiniteEtaleEquivalence :
    FiniteLocallyConstantSheaf B X ≌ FiniteEtaleOver X.1
declarations.comment: the equivalence of categories; the object-level statement is Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finiteEtaleRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleSetSheaf
declarations.doc: A constructible sheaf of sets on the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleSetSheaf (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf
declarations.doc: A constructible sheaf of abelian groups on the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    [∀ (S T : B.Scheme) (f : T ⟶ S),
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w}
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)).IsRightAdjoint]
    [∀ (T : B.Scheme) (V : SmallEtale B T.obj T.property),
      HasWeakSheafify ((SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property).over V) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{w}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
A constructible sheaf of modules over a Noetherian ring: on a finite
constructible stratification of every affine open, it is locally constant of
finite type.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleModuleSheaf (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (R : Type r) [Ring R]
    [∀ (S T : B.Scheme) (f : T ⟶ S),
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange B f).sheafPushforwardContinuous (ModuleCat.{w} R)
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property)).IsRightAdjoint]
    [∀ (T : B.Scheme) (V : SmallEtale B T.obj T.property),
      HasWeakSheafify ((SmallEtale.topology B T.obj T.property).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} R)]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{w} R)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleAbelianEtaleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RW (2).** A sheaf of abelian groups `F` on the small étale site of `X` is
constructible if for every affine open `U ⊆ X` there is a finite decomposition `U = ∐ᵢ Uᵢ` into
constructible locally closed subschemes such that `F|_{Uᵢ}` is finite locally constant for
all `i`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleAbelianEtaleSheaf
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w}) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleModuleEtaleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RW (3).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring. A sheaf of `Λ`-modules `F` on the small
étale site of `X` is constructible if for every affine open `U ⊆ X` there is a finite
decomposition `U = ∐ᵢ Uᵢ` into constructible locally closed subschemes such that `F|_{Uᵢ}` is of
finite type and locally constant for all `i`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleModuleEtaleSheaf (Λ : Type r) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_limit_colimit_and_isWeakSerreClass_abelian_and_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RZ.** Let `X` be a scheme of a big étale site and `Λ` a Noetherian ring. Then

1. a finite limit and a finite colimit of constructible sheaves of sets on the small étale site
   of `X` are constructible;
2. the constructible abelian sheaves on that site form a weak Serre subcategory of all abelian
   sheaves on it; and
3. the constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules on that site form a weak Serre subcategory of all
   sheaves of `Λ`-modules on it.

This is the whole tag in one statement, under no hypothesis on `X` and none on `Λ` beyond the
source's own Noetherianness, which part (3) alone uses. Each part is proved by the theorem that
states it alone: `AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_limit` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_colimit` for part (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.constructibleAbelianSheaf_isWeakSerreClass` for part (2), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isWeakSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf` for part (3). Those
four registrations are retained, each stating its own part.

The three parts are independent facts and not a chain: part (1) is about sheaves of sets and is
not used for parts (2) and (3), which reduce to Tag 093U (2) and Tag 093U (3) respectively, so
the conjunction asserts strictly more than any one of them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_limit_colimit_and_isWeakSerreClass_abelian_and_module
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] :
    (∀ (I : Type v) [SmallCategory I] [FinCategory I]
        (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))),
        (∀ i, IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (F.obj i)) →
          IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (limit F) ∧
            IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (colimit F)) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
        (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} =>
          IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X F) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
        (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
          (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ) => IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ F)
declarations.comment:
the whole tag: part (1) finite limits and finite colimits of constructible sheaves
of sets are constructible, part (2) the constructible abelian sheaves are a weak Serre
subcategory, part (3) the constructible sheaves of modules over a Noetherian ring are a weak
Serre subcategory. Unconditional: no hypothesis on the scheme and no instance the source does not
name; part (3)'s ring is a Ring rather than a CommRing, which is more general than the source,
and its Noetherian hypothesis is used by part (3) alone. The four component registrations are
retained.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_limit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RZ for sheaves of sets, finite limits.** A finite limit of constructible sheaves
of sets on the small étale site of a scheme is constructible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_limit
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (F.obj i)) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (limit F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RZ for sheaves of sets, finite colimits.** A finite colimit of constructible
sheaves of sets on the small étale site of a scheme is constructible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_colimit
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : ∀ i, IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (F.obj i)) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X (colimit F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isWeakSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RZ (3).** For `Λ` a Noetherian ring, the constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules on
the small étale site of a scheme form a weak Serre subcategory of all sheaves of `Λ`-modules on
that site. There is no hypothesis on the scheme.

The proof is the five term form of the weak Serre condition,
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakSerreClass_iff_prop_obj₂_of_exact`. Given an exact
`ℱ₀ ⟶ ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂ ⟶ ℱ₃ ⟶ ℱ₄` with the four outer terms constructible, fix an affine open and
stratify all four of them on one constructible stratification of it with
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_stratification_isStratifiedSheaf_forall`. Inverse image to a stratum is
exact by `AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteLimits_smallEtaleSheafPullback_moduleCat`, so the
restricted five term sequence is still exact, and on a stratum constructibility is local
constancy of finite type, which is a weak Serre condition by Tag 093U (3). Hence the restriction
of `ℱ₂` to each stratum is locally constant of finite type, which is constructibility of `ℱ₂`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem SmallEtale.isWeakSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ) => IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.constructibleAbelianSheaf_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03RZ for abelian sheaves.** The constructible sheaves of abelian groups on the small
étale site of a scheme form a weak Serre subcategory of all abelian sheaves on that site.
declarations.statement:
public instance constructibleAbelianSheaf_isWeakSerreClass :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} =>
        IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_constructible_partition_finite_etale
declarations.doc:
Let `f : U ⟶ X` be an étale morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes. Then `X`
has a partition into constructible locally closed subschemes over each of which the base change
of `f` is finite étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_constructible_partition_finite_etale
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace U] [QuasiSeparatedSpace U]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (f : U ⟶ X) [Etale f] :
    ∃ P : Set (Set X), IsTopologicalPartition P ∧
      (∀ S ∈ P, Topology.IsConstructible S) ∧
      (∀ S ∈ P, ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (i : Y ⟶ X),
        IsImmersion i ∧ Set.range i.base = S ∧
          IsFinite (pullback.fst i f) ∧ Etale (pullback.fst i f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_preimage_singleton_iff_exists_affine_open_isFinite_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02NW, condition (4).** For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
morphism locally of finite type, finiteness of the fibre over a generic point of an
irreducible component is equivalent to finiteness over some affine neighbourhood of the
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_preimage_singleton_iff_exists_affine_open_isFinite_restrict
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [QuasiSeparated f] (η : Y) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints Y) :
    (f ⁻¹' {η}).Finite ↔
      ∃ V : Y.affineOpens, (η ∈ V.1) ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V.1)
declarations.comment: forward direction over an affine open

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.extensionByZeroDirectSumAdj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03S4.** Extension by zero, defined as the sheafification of the
presheaf `j_{p!}` whose sections over a scheme `V` étale over `X` are the direct sum
`⨁_{φ : V → U} F(V →^φ U)` of Stacks Tag 0F4K, is a left adjoint of the restriction functor
`j^{-1}` on abelian sheaves of the small étale sites of an étale morphism `j : U ⟶ X` of
schemes.
declarations.statement:
def extensionByZeroDirectSumAdj :
    sheafToPresheaf U.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} ⋙
        extensionByZeroDirectSum j (A := AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) ⋙
        presheafToSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} ⊣
      etaleRestriction.{u, v} j
declarations.comment: the sheafification of the direct-sum presheaf j_{p!} is a left adjoint of j^{-1}

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03S5** for module coefficients: extension by zero of sheaves of
`Λ`-modules on small étale sites preserves finite limits.  It is additive, preserves
monomorphisms and preserves all colimits, hence preserves homology, hence finite limits.

instance etaleModuleExtensionByZero_preservesFiniteLimits :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (etaleModuleExtensionByZero.{u, r} Λ j)

Extension by zero along an étale morphism of schemes is an exact functor on
abelian sheaves of the small étale sites.

    [HasSheafify U.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}] :
