        (Fin r →₀ PadicInt ℓ) ×
          DirectSum (Fin t)
            (fun i => PadicInt ℓ ⧸ (PadicInt ℓ) ∙ ((ℓ : PadicInt ℓ) ^ e i)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.IsTorsion
declarations.doc:
A torsion ℓ-adic sheaf is annihilated by a single power of ℓ, uniformly
at all finite levels.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev LAdicSheaf.IsTorsion [IsNoetherian X.1] [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.torsionSheaves
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03UR.** The torsion `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves, as a property of objects of the abelian category
of `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves.
declarations.statement: public abbrev torsionSheaves : ObjectProperty (LAdicSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RationalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03UR.** The abelian category of `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaves on `X`: the quotient of the abelian
category of `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves by the Serre subcategory of torsion sheaves. Its objects are the
`ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves on `X`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev RationalSheaf
declarations.comment: the category of Q_ℓ-sheaves as the quotient by the torsion sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.rationalization
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03UR.** The quotient functor `F ↦ F ⊗ ℚ_ℓ` from `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves to `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaves.
declarations.statement: public abbrev rationalization : LAdicSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ ⥤ RationalSheaf B X ℓ
declarations.comment: the quotient functor F ↦ F ⊗ Q_ℓ

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.RationalSheaf.abelian
declarations.doc: **Stacks 03UR.** The category of `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaves on `X` is abelian.
declarations.statement: public instance RationalSheaf.abelian : Abelian (RationalSheaf B X ℓ)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.rationalStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03UR.** The stalk at a geometric point `x` of the `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf `F ⊗ ℚ_ℓ`, for `F` a
`ℤ_ℓ`-sheaf: the `ℤ_ℓ`-module stalk of `F` (Tag 03UQ) tensored up to `ℚ_ℓ`. Every `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf is
of this shape, the objects of the quotient category being the `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves themselves.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev LAdicSheaf.rationalStalk (F : LAdicSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ)
    (x : GeometricPoint X.1) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the stalk of F ⊗ Q_l is the stalk of F tensored with Q_l

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.isTorsionObject_isSerreClass
declarations.doc:
The `ℓ`-power torsion objects of an abelian category form a Serre class: they contain the
zero object and are closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions. For `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves this is
the Serre subcategory of torsion sheaves of Stacks 03UR.
declarations.statement:
public instance isTorsionObject_isSerreClass (ℓ : ℕ) :
    (isTorsionObject (C := C) ℓ).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: torsion sheaves are a Serre subcategory

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.isLocalizedModule_mapIntLinearMap
declarations.doc:
**The hom-groups of a Serre quotient at the `ℓ`-power torsion objects.** The localization
functor exhibits `Hom (L.obj X) (L.obj Y)` as the localization of the abelian group `Hom X Y` at
the powers of `ℓ`: multiplication by `ℓ` is invertible on the target, every element of the target
is a power of `ℓ` away from the image, and two morphisms have the same image exactly when a power
of `ℓ` equalizes them. For `ℤ_ℓ`-sheaves this is the formula
`Hom_{ℚ_ℓ}(F, G) = Hom_{ℤ_ℓ}(F, G) ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} ℚ_ℓ` of Stacks 03UR, since every integer prime to `ℓ`
is already a unit of `ℤ_ℓ`.
declarations.statement:
public instance isLocalizedModule_mapIntLinearMap (X Y : C) :
    IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (ℓ : ℤ)) (mapIntLinearMap L X Y)
declarations.comment: Hom_{Q_l}(F,G) = Hom_{Z_l}(F,G) localized at the powers of l

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.cohomology
declarations.doc:
**The ℓ-adic cohomology of an ℓ-adic sheaf.** For an ℓ-adic sheaf `F = {Fₙ}` on `X` and a
degree `i`, this is `Hⁱ(X, F) = limₙ Hⁱ(X, Fₙ)`.
declarations.statement: public def LAdicSheaf.cohomology (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (i : ℕ) : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.compactlySupportedCohomology
declarations.doc:
**The compactly supported ℓ-adic cohomology of an ℓ-adic sheaf.** For an ℓ-adic sheaf
`F = {Fₙ}` on `X` and a degree `i`, this is `Hⁱ_c(X, F) = limₙ Hⁱ_c(X, Fₙ)`.
declarations.statement:
public def LAdicSheaf.compactlySupportedCohomology (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (i : ℤ) :
    ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ_[ℓ]

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.rationalCompactlySupportedCohomology
declarations.doc:
**The compactly supported ℓ-adic cohomology with `ℚ_[ℓ]`-coefficients.** For the rational
ℓ-adic sheaf `F ⊗ Q_ℓ` attached to an ℓ-adic sheaf `F`, this is the extension of scalars of
`Hⁱ_c(X, F)` along `ℤ_[ℓ] → ℚ_[ℓ]`, that is `Hⁱ_c(X, F ⊗ Q_ℓ) = Hⁱ_c(X, F) ⊗_{ℤ_[ℓ]} ℚ_[ℓ]`.
declarations.statement:
public def LAdicSheaf.rationalCompactlySupportedCohomology (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (i : ℤ) :
    ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℚ_[ℓ]
declarations.comment: H^i_c(X, F' ⊗ Q_ell) = H^i_c(X, F') ⊗_{Z_ell} Q_ell

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.geometricCompactlySupportedCohomology
declarations.doc:
**The compactly supported ℓ-adic cohomology of the geometric fibre**,
`Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F) = limₙ Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, Fₙ)`, as in [Tag 03UT](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03UT)
for the restriction of `F` to `X_k̄`.
declarations.statement:
public def LAdicSheaf.geometricCompactlySupportedCohomology (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (i : ℤ) :
    ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℤ_[ℓ]
declarations.comment: H^i_c(X_kbar, F) = lim_n H^i_c(X_kbar, F_n), on the geometric fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology
declarations.doc:
**`Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F ⊗ Q_ℓ) = Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F) ⊗_{ℤ_[ℓ]} ℚ_[ℓ]`**, the cohomology of the rational
ℓ-adic sheaf `F ⊗ Q_ℓ` that [Tag 03V2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V2) is about.
declarations.statement:
public def LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ)
    (i : ℤ) : ModuleCat.{u + 1} ℚ_[ℓ]
declarations.comment: H^i_c(X_kbar, F' ⊗ Q_ell) = H^i_c(X_kbar, F') ⊗_{Z_ell} Q_ell, on the geometric fibre

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.lFunctionOfConstructibleFlat
declarations.doc:
**The L-function of a constructible flat `Λ`-module.** It is the Euler product over the
closed points of `X` of the inverse local factors `det(1 - π_x^* T ^ (deg x) |_{ℱ_x̄}) ⁻¹` of the
geometric Frobenius acting on the stalks of `ℱ`.
declarations.statement: public def lFunctionOfConstructibleFlat [QuasiCompact f] : PowerSeries Λ
declarations.comment: the definition of L(X, F) for a constructible flat Λ-module F: the local factors are the local factors of the geometric Frobenius on the stalks of F, whose finiteness and projectivity are derived from constructible flatness rather than supplied

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.constructibleFlatLFunction
declarations.doc:
The L-function `L(X, ℱ) = ∏_{x ∈ |X|} det(1 - π_x^* T ^ (deg x) |_{ℱ_x̄}) ⁻¹ ∈ Λ⟦T⟧` of a
constructible flat `Λ`-module on `X_étale`, for a scheme of finite type over a finite field and an
arbitrary commutative coefficient ring `Λ`, in particular any finite ring. Its local factors are
the projective determinants of the geometric Frobenius on the finite projective stalks.
declarations.statement:
public def constructibleFlatLFunction [QuasiCompact f]
    (hF : IsConstructibleFlatModuleSheaf B X Λ F) : PowerSeries Λ
declarations.comment: the definition of L(X, F) for a constructible flat Λ-module F over an arbitrary finite (indeed commutative) coefficient ring Λ, not necessarily local: the local factors are the projective determinants of the geometric Frobenius on the finite projective stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FrobeniusMatrices.lFunction
declarations.doc:
The L-function `∏_{x ∈ |X|} det(1 - π_x^* T ^ (deg x)) ⁻¹` of a family of Frobenius
matrices on a scheme `X` over `k`, as an element of `Λ⟦T⟧`.
declarations.statement: public def lFunction [Finite k] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : PowerSeries Λ
declarations.comment: the Euler product over the closed points of a scheme of finite type over a finite field, for a given family of Frobenius matrices rather than one derived from a constructible flat sheaf; the positivity of the residue degrees and the finiteness of the closed points of bounded degree are proved, not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.EulerSystem.coeff_eulerProduct_eq
declarations.doc:
The Euler product converges: the coefficient of `T ^ j` of the Euler product is the
coefficient of `T ^ j` of the product over any finite set of indices that contains all the
indices of degree at most `j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem coeff_eulerProduct_eq {j : ℕ} {t : Finset ι} (ht : E.support j ⊆ t) :
    PowerSeries.coeff j E.eulerProduct = PowerSeries.coeff j (∏ i ∈ t, E.factor i)
declarations.comment: the convergence of the Euler product: it is stated for an arbitrary coefficient ring, so it specializes to the Q_ell case of this tag

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction
declarations.doc:
The L-function of a `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf `F` on a scheme `X` of finite type over a finite field `k`:

`L(X, F) = ∏_{x ∈ |X|} det(1 - π_x^* T ^ (deg x) | F_x̄) ⁻¹ ∈ ℚ_ℓ⟦T⟧`,

the product over the closed points `|X|` of `X` of the inverse characteristic series of the
geometric Frobenius `π_x^*` acting on the rational stalk `F_x̄` at a geometric point over `x`,
where `deg x = [κ(x) : k]`.  The factor at `x` is identified with
`det(1 - π_x^* T ^ (deg x) | F_x̄) ⁻¹` by `localFactor_frobeniusMatrices`, and the product
converges in the sense of `coeff_rationalLFunction_eq`: there are finitely many closed points of
any given degree, so each coefficient is already computed by a finite subproduct.
declarations.statement:
public def LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (f : X.1 ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] : PowerSeries (Padic ℓ)
declarations.comment: the definition of L(X, F) for a Q_ell-sheaf F, as the Euler product over the closed points of the inverse characteristic series of the geometric Frobenius on the rational stalks

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.coeff_rationalLFunction_eq
declarations.doc:
The convergence of the defining product: the coefficient of `T ^ j` of `L(X, F)` is computed
by the product of the local factors over any finite set of closed points containing all those of
degree at most `j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LAdicSheaf.coeff_rationalLFunction_eq (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ)
    (f : X.1 ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    {j : ℕ} {t : Finset (closedPoints X.1)}
    (ht : (LAdicSheaf.frobeniusMatrices B X ℓ F f).eulerSystem.support j ⊆ t) :
    PowerSeries.coeff j (LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction B X ℓ F f) =
      PowerSeries.coeff j
        (∏ x ∈ t, (LAdicSheaf.frobeniusMatrices B X ℓ F f).localFactor x)
declarations.comment: the product converges since there are finitely many points of a given degree

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.lFunction_eq_inv_charSeries_compactSupport
declarations.doc:
**The cohomological interpretation of the L-function with finite coefficients.** Let `X` be a
separated scheme of finite type over a finite field `k`, `k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`, `Λ` a
finite commutative ring of order prime to the characteristic of `k`, and `F` a constructible flat
`Λ`-module on `X_étale`. Then `X` has a compactification, and for every compactification `j`
(through which `RΓ_c(X_k̄, -)` and `π_X^*` are computed) and every presentation `#k = p ^ q`,
`RΓ_c(X_k̄, F)` is perfect and `L(X, F) = det(1 - π_X^* T | RΓ_c(X_k̄, F))⁻¹` in `Λ⟦T⟧`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lFunction_eq_inv_charSeries_compactSupport
    [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k kbar] (Λ : Type) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (hΛ : ((Nat.card Λ : ℕ) : k) ≠ 0)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hF : IsConstructibleFlatModuleSheaf B X Λ F) :
    Nonempty (CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) ∧
      ∀ (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
        (hcard : Fintype.card k = p ^ q),
        LFunctionCharSeriesIdentity B X Λ f kbar F hF j p q hcard

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FrobeniusMatrices.lFunction_eq_alternatingCharSeries
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03V0**, Theorem 64.20.2 (Adic sheaves).  The L-function is the
alternating product of the characteristic series of geometric Frobenius on compactly supported
cohomology,
`L(X, ℱ) = ∏_i det(1 - π_X^* T |_{H_c^i(X_k̄, ℱ)}) ^ ((-1) ^ (i + 1))`.
The coefficient ring is only required to have torsion-free additive group, which holds for
`ℚ_ℓ`; this is the hypothesis behind the source's "since `ℚ_ℓ` has characteristic `0`, it
suffices to prove the equality after taking logarithmic derivatives".
declarations.statement:
public theorem lFunction_eq_alternatingCharSeries [IsAddTorsionFree Λ] {ι : Type w} [Fintype ι]
    (deg : ι → ℤ) (rk : ι → ℕ) (B : ∀ a : ι, Matrix (Fin (rk a)) (Fin (rk a)) Λ)
    (htrace : D.TraceFormula deg rk B) :
    D.lFunction = alternatingCharSeries deg rk B
declarations.comment: the determinant identity, with the trace formula of Tag 03V2 over the finite extensions of k carried as the explicit hypothesis `TraceFormula`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FrobeniusMatrices.lFunction_eq_alternatingCharSeries_iff
declarations.doc:
**The cohomological interpretation of the L-function, as a criterion.**
Over a coefficient ring with torsion-free additive group the determinant identity
`L(X, ℱ) = ∏_i det(1 - π_X^* T |_{H_c^i(X_k̄, ℱ)}) ^ ((-1) ^ (i + 1))`
holds if and only if the trace identity
`∑_{d ∣ n} d ∑_{deg x = d} tr((π_x^{n / d})^* |_{ℱ_x̄}) = ∑_i (-1) ^ i tr((π_X^n)^* |_{H_c^i})`
holds for every `n ≥ 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem lFunction_eq_alternatingCharSeries_iff [IsAddTorsionFree Λ] :
    D.lFunction = alternatingCharSeries deg rk B ↔ D.TraceFormula deg rk B
declarations.comment: the determinant identity, equivalent to the trace identity in the proof

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction_eq_gradedCharSeries_compactSupportFrobenius
declarations.doc:
**The L-function of a `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf.** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a
finite field `k` with `p ^ q` elements, `k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`, `ℓ` a prime with `ℓ ≠ p`
and `F` a `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf on `X`. Then
`L(X, F) = ∏ᵢ det(1 - π_X^* T | Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F))^{(-1)^{i+1}}` in `ℚ_ℓ[[T]]`.

`X` is separated because `Hⁱ_c` is defined for separated schemes only (Definition 03UT).
`ℓ ≠ p` is the chapter's standing convention; the statement is false for `ℓ = p`
(`L(𝔸¹_k, ℚ_p) = 1/(1 - p ^ q T)` while the alternating product is `1`).
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction_eq_gradedCharSeries_compactSupportFrobenius (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p)
    (F : LAdicSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ) :
    LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction B X ℓ F f =
      gradedCharSeries
        (fun i => LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i)
        (fun i => (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f j kbar p q
          hcard F i).hom)
declarations.comment: the determinant identity for a Q_l-sheaf, l invertible in k

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.adicLFunction_eq_inv_charSeries_compactSupport
declarations.doc:
**The ℓ-adic cohomological interpretation of the L-function.** Let `X` be a separated scheme
of finite type over a finite field `k`, `k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`, `ℓ` a prime invertible
in `k`, and `F = (Fₙ)` an ℓ-adic sheaf on `X_étale` whose levels are flat over `ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺¹ℤ`. Then `X`
has a compactification, and for every compactification `j` and every presentation `#k = p ^ q`:
* the complexes `RΓ_c(X_k̄, Fₙ)` are perfect and the ℓ-adic L-function `L_{ℤ_ℓ}(X, F)` reduces
  modulo every `ℓⁿ⁺¹` to `det(1 - π_X^* T | RΓ_c(X_k̄, Fₙ))⁻¹`;
* for every `c ∈ ℤ_ℓ⟦T⟧` with these reductions, `L_{ℤ_ℓ}(X, F) = c` if and only if
  `L(X, F ⊗ ℚ_ℓ) = ∏ᵢ det(1 - π_X^* T | Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F ⊗ ℚ_ℓ)) ^ ((-1) ^ (i + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LAdicSheaf.adicLFunction_eq_inv_charSeries_compactSupport (hℓ : (ℓ : k) ≠ 0) :
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f
    ∀ (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (hF : ∀ n, PowExact ℓ (n + 1) (F.level n)),
    Nonempty (CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) ∧
      ∀ (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
        (hcard : Fintype.card k = p ^ q),
        ∃ hP : ∀ n, StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect.{0, u + 1, u + 2} (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
            (compactSupportFrobeniusCohomology.{u, 0} (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1))) f j kbar
              (LAdicSheaf.levelComplex B X ℓ F n))),
          (∀ n : ℕ, PowerSeries.map (PadicInt.toZModPow (n + 1))
              (LAdicSheaf.adicLFunction B X ℓ F hF f) =
            (((CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.perfectDerivedCharSeries.{u + 2, 0, u + 1}
              (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))
              ((LAdicSheaf.geometricPerfectTower B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard F
                (LAdicSheaf.powExact_etaleLevel B X ℓ F hF) hP).obj n) (hP n)
              ((LAdicSheaf.geometricPerfectTower B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard F
                (LAdicSheaf.powExact_etaleLevel B X ℓ F hF) hP).endo n))⁻¹ :
                (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))⟦X⟧ˣ) : (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))⟦X⟧)) ∧
          ∀ c : ℤ_[ℓ]⟦X⟧, (∀ n : ℕ, PowerSeries.map (PadicInt.toZModPow (n + 1)) c =
              (((CategoryTheory.FilteredDerived.perfectDerivedCharSeries.{u + 2, 0, u + 1}
                (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))
                ((LAdicSheaf.geometricPerfectTower B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard F
                  (LAdicSheaf.powExact_etaleLevel B X ℓ F hF) hP).obj n) (hP n)
                ((LAdicSheaf.geometricPerfectTower B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard F
                  (LAdicSheaf.powExact_etaleLevel B X ℓ F hF) hP).endo n))⁻¹ :
                  (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))⟦X⟧ˣ) : (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1)))⟦X⟧)) →
            (LAdicSheaf.adicLFunction B X ℓ F hF f = c ↔
              LAdicSheaf.rationalLFunction B X ℓ F f =
                gradedCharSeries
                  (fun i =>
                    LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i)
                  (fun i => (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f j kbar
                    p q hcard F i).hom))
declarations.comment: the identity for Z_l coefficients is the l-adic limit of 03UZ at the levels, and it is equivalent to 03V0 for F ⊗ Q_l since Z_l has no l-torsion

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.isZero_rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology_of_neg
declarations.doc:
**`Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F ⊗ Q_ℓ) = 0` for `i < 0`**, for every ℓ-adic sheaf `F` on a separated scheme of
finite type over a field, every extension field `k̄` and every compactification: the lower half
of the statement of [Tag 03V2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03V2) that
`Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F)` is nonzero for `0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim X` only.
declarations.statement:
public theorem LAdicSheaf.isZero_rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology_of_neg
    (F : LAdicSheaf B X ℓ) (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0) :
    IsZero (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i)
declarations.comment: the lower half of the degree bound: H^i_c(X_kbar, F) = 0 for i < 0

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.traceFormula
declarations.doc:
**The trace formula for a `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf.** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a
finite field `k` with `p ^ q` elements, `k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`, `ℓ` a prime with `ℓ ≠ p`
and `F` a `ℚ_ℓ`-sheaf on `X` (an ℓ-adic sheaf, tensored with `ℚ_ℓ`). Then
* `Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F)` is a finite dimensional `ℚ_ℓ`-vector space for every `i`,
* it is nonzero only for `0 ≤ i ≤ 2 dim X`, and
* `∑_{x ∈ X(k)} Tr(π_x | F_x̄) = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ Tr(π_X^* | Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, F))`, the rational points being the
  closed points of residue degree one.

`ℓ ≠ p` is the chapter's standing convention; the statement is false for `ℓ = p`
(`X = 𝔸¹_k`, `F = ℚ_p`: the right hand side is `0`, the left hand side `p ^ q`).
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.traceFormula (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p) (F : LAdicSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite ℚ_[ℓ]
      (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i)) ∧
    (∀ i : ℤ, Nontrivial
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i) →
      0 ≤ i ∧ ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim X.1 = d ∧ i ≤ 2 * (d : ℤ)) ∧
    ∑ᶠ (x : closedPoints X.1) (_ : residueDegree f x.1 = 1),
        LinearMap.trace ℚ_[ℓ] _
          (LAdicSheaf.rationalStalkFrobenius B X ℓ F x.1 (finite_residueField f x.1 x.2)) =
      ∑ᶠ i : ℤ, (if Even i then (1 : ℚ_[ℓ]) else -1) *
        LinearMap.trace ℚ_[ℓ]
          (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f j kbar F i)
          (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard F
            i).hom
declarations.comment: finiteness, the degree bounds 0 <= i <= 2 dim X and the trace formula

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isPerfect_compactSupport_and_sum_stalkTrace_eq_compactSupportLefschetzNumber
declarations.doc:
**The trace formula ([Stacks, Tag 03V3]).** Let `k` be a finite field with `p ^ q` elements and
`k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`, let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over `k` (of any
dimension), let `Λ` be a finite ring whose cardinality is invertible in `k`, and let
`K ∈ D_ctf(X, Λ)`. Then `X` has a compactification over `k`, and for every compactification
`j : X ⟶ X̄` the complex `RΓ_c(X_k̄, K) = RΓ(X̄_k̄, (j_! K)|_{X̄_k̄})` lies in `D_perf(Λ)`, and

`∑_{x ∈ X(k)} Tr(π_x | K_x̄) = Tr(π_X^* | RΓ_c(X_k̄, K))`

in `Λ^natural`, where the stalks `K_x̄` at the rational points are perfect (so that their traces
are defined), `π_x` is the geometric Frobenius acting on `K_x̄` and `π_X^*` is the canonical
Frobenius action on `RΓ_c(X_k̄, K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_compactSupport_and_sum_stalkTrace_eq_compactSupportLefschetzNumber
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (Λ : Type) [Ring Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Fintype k] (kbar : Type u) [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    [Algebra k kbar] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k kbar] (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    [CharP kbar p] (hcard : Fintype.card k = p ^ q)
    (hcop : Nat.Coprime (Nat.card Λ) (Fintype.card k))
    (X : B.Scheme) (f : X.obj ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] (K : CochainComplex.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X.obj))
    (hK : IsCtf B X Λ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj)) :
    Nonempty (CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) ∧
      ∀ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f),
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
          (compactSupportFrobeniusCohomology.{u, 0} Λ f j kbar K)) ∧
        ∃ (hX : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
            (compactSupportFrobeniusCohomology.{u, 0} Λ f j kbar K)))
          (hs : ∀ x : rationalPoints f, StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (rationalPointStalkComplex.{u, 0} Λ kbar x.1 K))),
          ∑ᶠ x : rationalPoints f, perfectDerivedTrace Λ ⟨_, hs x⟩
              (DerivedCategory.Q.map (rationalPointStalkFrobenius.{u, 0} Λ kbar p q hcard x.1 K)) =
            canonicalCompactSupportLefschetzNumber.{u, 0} Λ f j kbar p q hcard K hX
declarations.comment: `Λ : Type` (universe 0); X in a big étale site; K ∈ D_ctf(X, Λ) represented by a bounded below complex; RΓ_c(X_k̄, K) through any compactification (one exists by 0F41)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.perfectDerivedTrace_canonicalCompactSupportFrobenius_eq_sum_of_isCtf_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 03V3]: the trace formula for `D_ctf`.** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite
type over the finite field `k` with `p ^ q` elements, lying in the big étale site `B`, with a
compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄` (which defines `RΓ_c`), and `k̄` an algebraic closure of `k`; let
`Λ` be a finite ring (possibly noncommutative) with `#Λ` invertible in `k`, and `K` a bounded
below complex of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale` whose class lies in `D_ctf(X, Λ)`. Then
`RΓ_c(X_k̄, K)` is perfect, the stalks `K_x̄` at the rational points are perfect, and
`Tr(π_X^* | RΓ_c(X_k̄, K)) = ∑_{x ∈ X(k)} Tr(π_x | K_x̄)` in `Λ^♮`.

`X` is separated and of finite type over `k` as in the setting of Tag 03UG ("`X/k` as above"),
where `RΓ_c` is defined (Definition 03UT); the instance `Fintype (rationalPoints f)` always holds
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.finite_rationalPoints`).
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectDerivedTrace_canonicalCompactSupportFrobenius_eq_sum_of_isCtf_of_isSeparated
    (hΛ : (Nat.card Λ : k) ≠ 0) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [Fintype (rationalPoints f)] (J : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (K : CochainComplex.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)) (hX : B.Contains X)
    (hK : IsCtf B (B.obj X hX) Λ (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.obj)) :
    ∃ (hKs : HasPerfectStalks Λ K) (hperf : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj (compactSupportFrobeniusCohomology.{u, 0} Λ f J kbar K))),
      perfectDerivedTrace Λ ⟨_, hperf⟩ (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.map
          (canonicalCompactSupportFrobenius.{u, 0} Λ f J kbar p q hcard K)) =
        ∑ x : rationalPoints f, perfectDerivedTrace Λ ⟨_, hKs (rationalGeometricPoint kbar x.1)⟩
          (DerivedCategory.Q.map (rationalPointStalkFrobenius.{u, 0} Λ kbar p q hcard x.1 K))
declarations.comment: RGamma_c(X_kbar, K) is perfect and the trace formula, for K in D_ctf(X, Lambda)

declarations.name: Stacks.InverseSystem.perfectTower_padicTrace_eq_alternating_trace_limitCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 03V4.** Let `ℓ` be a prime.  Suppose we have `Kₙ ∈ D_perf(ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺¹ℤ)`,
`πₙ : Kₙ → Kₙ` and isomorphisms `φₙ : Kₙ₊₁ ⊗ᴸ_{ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺²ℤ} ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺¹ℤ → Kₙ` compatible with `πₙ₊₁`
and `πₙ` — that is, a `PerfectTower ℓ`.  Then

1. the elements `tₙ = Tr(πₙ | Kₙ) ∈ ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺¹ℤ` form an element `t_∞ = {tₙ}` of `ℤ_[ℓ]`, namely
   there is exactly one `t_∞ ∈ ℤ_[ℓ]` reducing to `tₙ` modulo `ℓⁿ⁺¹` for every `n`;
2. the `ℤ_[ℓ]`-module `Hⁱ_∞ = limₙ Hⁱ(Kₙ)` is finite and is nonzero for finitely many `i`
   only; and
3. the operators `Hⁱ(πₙ) : Hⁱ(Kₙ) → Hⁱ(Kₙ)` are compatible with the transitions of the
   inverse system, hence define a unique `πⁱ_∞ : Hⁱ_∞ → Hⁱ_∞` lying over them, and every such
   family satisfies `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ Tr(πⁱ_∞ | Hⁱ_∞ ⊗_{ℤ_[ℓ]} ℚ_[ℓ]) = t_∞`.

Levels are indexed so that level `n` carries coefficients in `ℤ/ℓⁿ⁺¹ℤ`, avoiding the zero
ring; `(-1)ⁱ` for `i : ℤ` is written as `if Even i then 1 else -1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem perfectTower_padicTrace_eq_alternating_trace_limitCohomology
    {ℓ : ℕ} [Fact ℓ.Prime] (T : PerfectTower.{v} ℓ) :
    -- (1) the traces `tₙ` form an element `t_∞` of `ℤ_[ℓ]`
    (∃! t : ℤ_[ℓ], ∀ n : ℕ, PadicInt.toZModPow (n + 1) t = traceAtLevel T n) ∧
    -- (2) each `Hⁱ_∞` is a finite `ℤ_[ℓ]`-module, and only finitely many are nonzero
    (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite ℤ_[ℓ] (limitCohomology T i)) ∧
    {i : ℤ | Nontrivial (limitCohomology T i)}.Finite ∧
    -- (3) the `Hⁱ(πₙ)` are compatible with the transitions of the inverse system
    (∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ), levelCohomologyEndoHom T i (n + 1) ≫ levelCohomologyTransition T i n =
        levelCohomologyTransition T i n ≫
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{v} (levelCast ℓ n)).map (levelCohomologyEndoHom T i n)) ∧
    -- (3) and so define a unique family `πⁱ_∞` of endomorphisms of the `Hⁱ_∞`
    (∃! π : ∀ i : ℤ, limitCohomology T i →ₗ[ℤ_[ℓ]] limitCohomology T i,
        ∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (a : limitCohomology T i),
          limitCohomologyProjection T i n (π i a) =
            levelCohomologyEndoₗ T i n (limitCohomologyProjection T i n a)) ∧
    -- (3) which satisfies `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ Tr(πⁱ_∞ | Hⁱ_∞ ⊗ ℚ_[ℓ]) = t_∞`
    (∀ t : ℤ_[ℓ], (∀ n : ℕ, PadicInt.toZModPow (n + 1) t = traceAtLevel T n) →
      ∀ π : ∀ i : ℤ, limitCohomology T i →ₗ[ℤ_[ℓ]] limitCohomology T i,
        (∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (a : limitCohomology T i),
            limitCohomologyProjection T i n (π i a) =
              levelCohomologyEndoₗ T i n (limitCohomologyProjection T i n a)) →
          ∑ᶠ i : ℤ, (if Even i then (1 : ℚ_[ℓ]) else -1) *
              LinearMap.trace ℚ_[ℓ] (ℚ_[ℓ] ⊗[ℤ_[ℓ]] limitCohomology T i)
                (LinearMap.baseChange ℚ_[ℓ] (π i)) =
            (t : ℚ_[ℓ]))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.isRational_constantLFunction_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03V8, part (1).** The L-function `L(X, ℚ_ℓ) = ∏_{x ∈ |X|} (1 - T^{deg x})⁻¹` of a smooth,
projective, geometrically irreducible curve over a finite field is a rational function: its
product with a polynomial whose value at `0` is nonzero is a polynomial. (The polynomials are
`(1 - T)(1 - qT)` and `det(1 - π_X^* T | H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ))`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.isRational_constantLFunction_of_smoothProjectiveCurve (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p) :
    ∃ P Q : Polynomial ℚ_[ℓ], Q.eval 0 ≠ 0 ∧
      constantLFunction f ℚ_[ℓ] * (Q : PowerSeries ℚ_[ℓ]) = (P : PowerSeries ℚ_[ℓ])
declarations.comment: part (1): L(X, Q_ell) is a rational function, for X a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over a finite field and ell a prime different from the characteristic; its product with (1 - T)(1 - qT) is det(1 - pi_X^* T | H^1(X_kbar, Q_ell))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.exists_integral_curveNumerator_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03V8, part (2), independence of `ℓ`.** `dim H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ) = 2g`, and for every basis of
`H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ)` the polynomial `det(1 - π_X^* T | H¹)` is the image of one integral polynomial of
degree at most `2g` with constant coefficient `1`: the numerator `L(X, ℤ)·(1 - T)(1 - qT)` of the
zeta function of `X`, in which `ℓ` does not occur.
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.exists_integral_curveNumerator_of_smoothProjectiveCurve (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p) :
    Module.finrank ℚ_[ℓ] (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f
        (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) =
      2 * genus f ∧
    ∀ bV : Module.Basis (Fin (2 * genus f)) ℚ_[ℓ]
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f
          (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)),
      ∃ P : Polynomial ℤ, P.natDegree ≤ 2 * genus f ∧ P.coeff 0 = 1 ∧
        (P : PowerSeries ℤ) = integralCurveNumerator f (Fintype.card k) ∧
        P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ_[ℓ]) = localCharPolynomial (LinearMap.toMatrix bV bV
          (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f
            (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar p r hcard (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ)
              ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom) 1
declarations.comment: part (2), independence of ell: dim H^1(X_kbar, Q_ell) = 2g and the characteristic polynomial det(1 - pi_X^* T | H^1) is the image of the integral numerator of the zeta function of X, a polynomial over Z determined by the Euler product of X, in which ell does not occur

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.isIntegral_curveEigenvalue_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03V8, part (2), integrality.** The eigenvalues `α_1, …, α_{2g}` of `π_X^*` on
`H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ)` are algebraic integers.
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.isIntegral_curveEigenvalue_of_smoothProjectiveCurve (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p)
    (bV : Module.Basis (Fin (2 * genus f)) ℚ_[ℓ]
      (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f
        (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)))
    {Ω : Type*} [CommRing Ω] (φ : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* Ω) (α : Fin (2 * genus f) → Ω)
    (hα : (localCharPolynomial (LinearMap.toMatrix bV bV
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f
          (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar p r hcard (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ)
            ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom) 1).map φ =
      ∏ i, (1 - Polynomial.C (α i) * Polynomial.X))
    (i : Fin (2 * genus f)) : IsIntegral ℤ (α i)
declarations.comment: part (2): the eigenvalues alpha_1, ..., alpha_{2g} of pi_X^* on H^1(X_kbar, Q_ell) are algebraic integers, being the reciprocal roots of the integral numerator of the zeta function, of constant coefficient 1

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.natCard_fieldValuedPoints_eq_one_sub_sum_add_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03V8, part (3).** The number of points of `X` with values in an extension `k_n` of `k` of
degree `n ≥ 1` is `#X(k_n) = 1 - ∑_{i=1}^{2g} α_i^n + q^n`, `α_i` the eigenvalues of `π_X^*` on
`H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.natCard_fieldValuedPoints_eq_one_sub_sum_add_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
    (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p)
    (bV : Module.Basis (Fin (2 * genus f)) ℚ_[ℓ]
      (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f
        (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)))
    {Ω : Type*} [CommRing Ω] (φ : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* Ω) (α : Fin (2 * genus f) → Ω)
    (hα : (localCharPolynomial (LinearMap.toMatrix bV bV
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f
          (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar p r hcard (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ)
            ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom) 1).map φ =
      ∏ i, (1 - Polynomial.C (α i) * Polynomial.X))
    {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Finite K]
    (hK : Module.finrank k K = n) :
    (Nat.card (fieldValuedPoints f K) : Ω) = 1 - ∑ i, α i ^ n + (Fintype.card k : Ω) ^ n
declarations.comment: part (3): #X(k_n) = 1 - sum_{i=1}^{2g} alpha_i^n + q^n for every extension k_n of k of degree n >= 1, alpha_i the eigenvalues of pi_X^* on H^1(X_kbar, Q_ell)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.norm_curveEigenvalue_lt_of_smoothProjectiveCurve
declarations.doc:
**Tag 03V8, part (4).** Every eigenvalue `α_i` of `π_X^*` on `H¹(X_k̄, ℚ_ℓ)`, read in `ℂ` along
a ring map `ℚ_ℓ → ℂ`, has `|α_i| < q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.norm_curveEigenvalue_lt_of_smoothProjectiveCurve (hℓp : ℓ ≠ p)
    (bV : Module.Basis (Fin (2 * genus f)) ℚ_[ℓ]
      (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X ℓ f
        (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ) ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)))
    (φ : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* ℂ) (α : Fin (2 * genus f) → ℂ)
    (hα : (localCharPolynomial (LinearMap.toMatrix bV bV
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f
          (CompactificationOf.ofProper f) kbar p r hcard (LAdicSheaf.constantSystem B X ℓ)
            ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).hom) 1).map φ =
      ∏ i, (1 - Polynomial.C (α i) * Polynomial.X))
    (i : Fin (2 * genus f)) : ‖α i‖ < (Fintype.card k : ℝ)
declarations.comment: part (4): |alpha_i| < q for every eigenvalue alpha_i of pi_X^* on H^1(X_kbar, Q_ell) read in C; it follows from the Riemann hypothesis |alpha_i| = sqrt q, which the source states right after the lemma

declarations.name: Stacks.TraceFormula.exists_pow_mem_sector
declarations.doc:
**Exercise 03V9.** For complex numbers `α 1, …, α n` and a conic sector
`C_ε = {z | |arg z| < ε}` with `ε > 0` about the positive real axis, there is an integer `k ≥ 1`
with `α 1 ^ k, …, α n ^ k` all in `C_ε`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_mem_sector (α : ι → ℂ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ ∀ i, α i ^ k ∈ {z : ℂ | |z.arg| < ε}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup.IsOpenSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03VE.** A subgroup of the étale fundamental group is open if it is
the stabilizer of a point of the geometric fibre of some finite étale cover.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsOpenSubgroup {X : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) (H : Subgroup (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tags 0BND (1) and 03VF (3).** Finite étale covers of a connected scheme `X`
are equivalent to finite sets with a continuous action of `π₁(X, x)`, by an equivalence whose
underlying finite sets are the geometric fibres at `x` and whose action is evaluation of natural
automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtaleEquivalence (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    ∃ E : FiniteEtaleOver X ≌ ContAction FintypeCat.{u} (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x),
      ∃ α : E.functor ⋙
          forget₂ (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x))
            FintypeCat.{u} ⋙ FintypeCat.incl ≅ finiteEtaleFiberFunctor x,
        ∀ (Y : FiniteEtaleOver X) (σ : EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)
          (y : (E.functor.obj Y).obj.V.obj),
          (α.hom.app Y) (ConcreteCategory.hom ((E.functor.obj Y).obj.ρ σ).asHom y) =
            (σ.asIso.app Y).hom ((α.hom.app Y) y)
declarations.comment: (3) the functor sending a finite étale Y/X to F_x(Y) with its natural action is an equivalence onto the finite discrete continuous π₁(X, x)-sets; (1) and (2) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup.isOpen_coe_of_isOpenSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03VF (1), openness.** An open subgroup of the étale fundamental group
is an open subset for the canonical topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_coe_of_isOpenSubgroup {H : Subgroup (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)}
    (hH : IsOpenSubgroup x H) : IsOpen (H : Set (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x))
declarations.comment: (1) the open subgroups are open subsets; that they are a neighbourhood basis of the identity is `nhds_one_hasBasis_isOpenSubgroup`, and (2) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup.nhds_one_hasBasis_isOpenSubgroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03VF (1).** For the canonical topology on the étale fundamental group
of a connected scheme, the open subgroups — the stabilizers of points of geometric fibres — form
a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem nhds_one_hasBasis_isOpenSubgroup (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    (nhds (1 : EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)).HasBasis (IsOpenSubgroup x)
      fun H ↦ (H : Set (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x))
declarations.comment: (1) the open subgroups are a neighbourhood basis of the identity; that each of them is an open subset is `isOpen_coe_of_isOpenSubgroup`, and (2) and (3) are not covered here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProfiniteTop_etaleFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 03VF, part (2).** With its canonical topology the étale fundamental
group of a connected scheme at a geometric point is a profinite group: it is a topological group
by `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFundamentalGroupIsTopologicalGroup`, and its underlying space is
compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProfiniteTop_etaleFundamentalGroup (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (x : GeometricPoint X) :
    Stacks.Chapter05.Tag_0BR1.IsProfiniteTop (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
declarations.doc:
The residue-field Galois action on the geometric fibre functor at `sbar`.
Its action is specified below, independently of any isomorphism of groups.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup
    [ConnectedSpace X] :
    Gal(sbar.residueField / X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) →ₜ*
      AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup X sbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension
declarations.doc:
The étale fundamental group is the Galois group of the maximal extension
unramified over the scheme, with canonicality specified below.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleFundamentalGroup X sbar ≃ₜ*
      Gal(maximalEtaleExtension X sbar / X.residueField (sbar.hom default))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension_apply
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification sends the generic-point homomorphism to
restriction of absolute Galois automorphisms to the maximal étale extension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension_apply
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X) :
    letI : Normal (X.residueField (sbar.hom default))
        (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) :=
      normal_maximalEtaleExtension X sbar hs hgeneric
    ∀ σ : Gal(sbar.residueField / X.residueField (sbar.hom default)),
      fundamentalGroupIsoGalMaximalEtaleExtension X sbar hs hgeneric
          (absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup X sbar σ) =
        (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar)) σ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup_apply
declarations.doc:
A generic-field automorphism acts on a finite étale geometric fibre by
precomposition with the induced automorphism of the geometric point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup_apply
    [ConnectedSpace X]
    (σ : Gal(sbar.residueField/X.residueField (sbar.hom default)))
    (Y : FiniteEtaleOver X)
    (p : finiteEtaleFiber sbar Y) :
    ((((absoluteGaloisToFundamentalGroup X sbar) σ).asIso.app Y).hom p).1 =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ.toAlgHom.toRingHom) ≫ p.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.maximalEtaleExtension
declarations.doc: The compositum of all finite extensions giving finite étale normalizations.
declarations.statement:
public def maximalEtaleExtension :
    IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normal_maximalEtaleExtension
declarations.doc: The maximal finite-étale extension is normal over the function field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem normal_maximalEtaleExtension
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X) :
    Normal (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) (maximalEtaleExtension X sbar)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.le_maximalEtaleExtension
declarations.doc:
The extension is largest among extensions with finite étale normalizations of all finite
subextensions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem le_maximalEtaleExtension
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X)
    (M : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField)
    (hM : ∀ L : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField,
      L ≤ M → FiniteDimensional (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) L →
        FiniteEtaleNormalization X sbar L) :
    M ≤ maximalEtaleExtension X sbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteEtaleNormalization_of_le_maximalEtaleExtension
declarations.doc: Every finite subextension of the maximal extension gives a finite étale normalization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteEtaleNormalization_of_le_maximalEtaleExtension
    [IsIntegral X] [IsNormal X]
    (hs : GeometricPoint.IsAlgebraic sbar)
    (hgeneric : sbar.hom default = genericPoint X)
    (L : IntermediateField (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) sbar.residueField)
    [FiniteDimensional (X.residueField (sbar.hom default)) L]
    (hL : L ≤ maximalEtaleExtension X sbar) :
    FiniteEtaleNormalization X sbar L

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.IsMixedOfWeightLE.of_exact
declarations.doc:
Mixedness of weight at most `i` propagates along an exact sequence: in the excision
sequence `H^i_c(U) → H^i_c(X) → H^i_c(Z)` of an open-closed decomposition `X = U ⊔ Z`, if the
Frobenius actions on the two outer terms are mixed of weight at most `i`, then so is the
Frobenius action on `H^i_c(X)`, whose eigenvalues are therefore algebraic numbers of absolute
value `q ^ (w / 2)` with `w` an integer at most `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsMixedOfWeightLE.of_exact {A B C : Type*} [AddCommGroup A] [Module K A]
    [AddCommGroup B] [Module K B] [AddCommGroup C] [Module K C] [FiniteDimensional K A]
    [FiniteDimensional K B] {fA : Module.End K A} {fB : Module.End K B} {fC : Module.End K C}
    {j : A →ₗ[K] B} {p : B →ₗ[K] C} (hA : IsMixedOfWeightLE q ι i fA)
    (hC : IsMixedOfWeightLE q ι i fC) (hj : ∀ a, j (fA a) = fB (j a))
    (hp : ∀ b, p (fB b) = fC (p b)) (hexact : LinearMap.ker p ≤ LinearMap.range j) :
    IsMixedOfWeightLE q ι i fB
declarations.comment: the weight bound: the eigenvalues on H^i_c are algebraic numbers of absolute value q ^ (w / 2) with w an integer at most i. The weight datum is the cited theorem of [WeilII]; it is carried here for the two outer terms of the excision sequence of an open-closed decomposition of X and propagated to H^i_c(X)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isPureOfWeight_of_duality
declarations.doc:
Poincaré duality turns mixedness into purity: if the Frobenius action `f` on `H^i_c` is
mixed of weight at most `i`, the action `g` on the cohomology of the dual sheaf in degree
`2 * d - i` is mixed of weight at most `2 * d - i`, and duality matches each eigenvalue `α` of
`f` with the eigenvalue `q ^ d / α` of `g`, then `f` is pure of weight `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPureOfWeight_of_duality {d : ℤ} {g : Module.End K W}
    (hf : IsMixedOfWeightLE q ι i f) (hg : IsMixedOfWeightLE q ι (2 * d - i) g)
    (hdual : ∀ α : K, f.HasEigenvalue α → g.HasEigenvalue ((q : K) ^ d / α)) (hq : 1 < q) :
    IsPureOfWeight q ι i f
declarations.comment: the final assertion, that w = i when X is smooth and projective of dimension d: proved from mixedness in degree i and in the dual degree 2 * d - i together with the Poincare duality matching of the two spectra

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.weightBound
declarations.doc:
**Weil II** ([Tag 03VH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03VH); Deligne, *La conjecture
de Weil II*). Let `k` be a finite field with `p ^ q` elements, `k̄` an algebraic closure, `ℓ ≠ p` a
prime, `X` connected and separated of finite type over `k` with a compactification `j`, and
`ρ : π₁(X, x̄) → GL_r(ℚ_ℓ)` continuous, satisfying the conclusions of Deligne's conjecture
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.HasDeligneConclusions`) along every embedding `ι : ℚ_ℓ → ℂ`. Then for
every `i` the eigenvalues of `π_X^*` on `Hⁱ_c(X_k̄, ℱ_ρ ⊗ ℚ_ℓ)` (finite dimensional) are algebraic
numbers of absolute value `(p ^ q) ^ (w / 2)` along `ι` with `w ∈ ℤ`, `w ≤ i`; and if `X` is smooth
and proper over `k` (the source asks for projective), then `w = i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem LAdicSheaf.weightBound
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Fintype k] (kbar : Type u) [Field kbar] [Algebra k kbar]
    [IsAlgClosure k kbar] (p q : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hcard : Fintype.card k = p ^ q)
    (hℓ : ℓ ≠ p) (X : B.Scheme) [IsNoetherian X.1] [ConnectedSpace X.1] (f : X.1 ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (x : GeometricPoint X.1) {r : ℕ} (ρ : EtaleFundamentalGroup X.1 x →* GL (Fin r) ℚ_[ℓ])
    (hρ : Continuous ρ)
    (hD : ∀ ι : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* ℂ, HasDeligneConclusions (geometricFrobeniusFamily f x) p ι ρ) :
    (∀ (i : ℤ) (ι : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* ℂ),
      haveI : FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X
        ℓ f j kbar (LAdicSheaf.representationSheaf B X x ρ hρ) i) :=
        LAdicSheaf.finiteDimensional_rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B ℓ kbar p q
          hcard hℓ X f j _ i
      IsCharpolyMixedOfWeightLE (p ^ q) ι i
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard
          (LAdicSheaf.representationSheaf B X x ρ hρ) i).hom) ∧
    (IsProper f → Smooth f → ∀ (i : ℤ) (ι : ℚ_[ℓ] →+* ℂ),
      haveI : FiniteDimensional ℚ_[ℓ] (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B X
        ℓ f j kbar (LAdicSheaf.representationSheaf B X x ρ hρ) i) :=
        LAdicSheaf.finiteDimensional_rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedCohomology B ℓ kbar p q
          hcard hℓ X f j _ i
      IsCharpolyPureOfWeight (p ^ q) ι i
        (LAdicSheaf.rationalGeometricCompactlySupportedFrobenius B X ℓ f j kbar p q hcard
          (LAdicSheaf.representationSheaf B X x ρ hρ) i).hom)
declarations.comment: the whole tag: the eigenvalues of pi_X^* on H^i_c(X_kbar, F_rho) are algebraic numbers of absolute value q^(w/2) with w <= i an integer, and w = i for X smooth and proper (the source says projective), for rho satisfying the conclusions of Deligne's conjecture along every embedding of Q_ell in C
